source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Opening Words of Introduction Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij-Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj Sacred Journey; Sacred History; Sacred Road; Sacred Rite Mythopoetic Aesthetics: Great Good; Pure Truth; Primordial Beauty

Here then is where we shall begin the telling of this Sacred Narrative formed from Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij to be shaped into the Ancestral Account-Ojer Tzij of this Council Book known as the Popol Wuj. The Ancient Word; the Ancestral Account that carve the Ancient Paths and create the Ancestral Roads of this Mythic Journey that is the Sacred Journey we are about to take up as we step into this Ancient Book of Ancestral Advice. Let us enter the mythic time and mythic space of the Imaginal Realm in order to enter the Imaginal World by engaging our imagination with the Ancient Word that bring to life the Ancestral Account written out on the pages of this Noble Book of Noble Counsel known as Popol Wuj. It is our capacity to imagine this Imaginal World or Mundus Imaginalis through our ancestral soulʼs desire to know the depth and heights of the Maya Cosmos.

So let us enter that Cosmos of Maya on its own terms and in its own language whenever possible. This is an English Translation of the Original Maya Kʼicheʼ Mythopoetic Language that calls upon us to open our imagination to magical mythical transforming World know to the Maya as the Sky-Earth; Kaj- Ulew. This Mythic World is mirrored reflection of the Natural World of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Highlands and Lowlands just this Mythic World creates an echo of the Cultural World of the Kʼicheʼ Maya People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Popol Wuj then must be understood as Maya Myth that reveals the essential nature of the Kʼicheʼ Maya People who formed and shaped themselves through mythic words and mythic metaphors that form and shape the Sacred History written out here in the Ancient Word to be told as the Ancestral Account that reveals as it expresses all that was brought to fruition by the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ. The Popol Wuj then must be taken up as the complete revelation of the ʼrise and fallʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Kingdom that begins with a Cosmogony that tells of the forming and shaping of the Sky-Earth-Sea to then move through the various Ages or Suns of Creation and Destruction in which the Former, the Shaper known as Bearer, Begetter and Mother, Father attempt to form and shape their Providers and Sustainers. This relationship of providing thanks and gratitude to oneʼs Former and Shaper while sustaining them with sacrificial gifts of sacred sustenance is the story told here in the Popol Wuj; a story in which the Former and Shaper failed to bring about their Providers and Sustainers until they use maize as the sacred substance to mold and model their flesh.

This Book of Council tells us the Sacred Story of an Aesthetic Culture and Artisan Society in which its women and men are dedicated to the creative arts as artists and artisans. Perhaps it is this desire to create beauty in the world that makes the mythopoetic language of the Popol Wuj such beautiful writing to read and contemplate.

body: This Book of Council known as the Popol Wuj is a sublime literary work that was formed and shaped over thousands of years until it was written down in the ʼLatinateʼ by the Kʼicheʼ Maya Scribes. I have told this story of Introduction in great detail yet placed it at the end of this Translation and Interpretation of the Popol Wuj for those who want to ʼenter the wordʼ through an Introductory Essay written for those who need more cultural context and historical understanding of the Maya People and Mesoamerican World in which the Popol Wuj came to life as Ancient Indigenous Americaʼs most beautifully written and perfectly designed Mythological Text. Popol Wuj is a Sacred Literary Masterpiece that was formed and transformed over thousands of years until it was written out to reveal the Mythic Lifecycle of the Maize People from the Primordial Origins of the Maya World with formation of the Earth from the Sea and Sky to the Cataclysmic End with the complete destruction of the Kʼicheʼ Maya World embodied by the ʼburningʼ of the Last Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ along with their Capital City known and named ʼBroken-Down Caneʼ or ʼQʼumaraq Aajʼ the perfect name to express the devastations of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Kingdom that came with fall of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Sun.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It is ʼas ifʼ Maize itself had written the Popol Wuj as the lifecycle of Maize by entering the Maya consciousness so completely that it called upon the People of Maize-Ixim Winaq to tell the interwoven narrative of Maize and Humans who lived out their lives nurturing and nourishing one another as they told the story of the Maize Lords as the Story of the Sun and Moon generation after generation until it was written down in glyphic and pictorial form by the Maya Civilization that developed alongside the Olmec and Xicalanca People who are named here in the Popol Wuj. This Maya form of writing with glyphs alongside pictographic images is what was transcribed into the Latinate text of the Popol Wuj by the Noble Maya Scribes who were taught to write in the ʼLatinateʼ by the Dominican Friars. This is the original mythopoetic text of the Popol Wuj that is translate and interpreted here in this English Translation of the Popol Wuj.

People of Maize; the Pueblo of Maize: Ixim Winaq Formed and Shaped by the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account Wayebʼ: the Five Acts of the Five Nights of Popol Wuj Changing Face of the Sun; Transforming Face of the Earth

This is the Sacred Book of the Kʼicheʼ Maya written down by the Noble Council of Noble Scribes that gathered together to invoke the remembrance of their Divine Ancestors who carried out the Sacred Journey of the Kʼicheʼ People;

Kʼicheʼ Pueblo; the People of Maize; the Pueblo of Maize as they knew themselves from beginning to end of this Sacred History that is a Mesoamerican Myth of Maize and those who named themselves the Maize People: Ixim Winaq. For it is this Book of Council that was written by the Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word as the Book of Counsel that provided their lives with Ancestral Advice on the Ancestral Path of Being and Becoming Perfect Replacement of the Divine Ancestors whoʼs Ancestral Words and Ancestral Ways are formed and shaped into the Ancestral Account that is inscribed in the pages of this Noble Book of Noble Council known as Popol Wuj.

Popol Wuj then tells of the many Sacred Journeys on the many Paths of Initiation walked in Rites of Passage where Young Initiates and their Spiritual Guides were carried across the abyss of insecurity and incertitude on the mythic bridge of the Popol Wuj.

Popol Wuj as the Myth of the Maize People bore the Young Initiates across the void of uncertainty brought on by the fear and anxiety caused by the many Roads of Transformation that were taken up in the lives of the Kʼicheʼ Maya and found here in the Myth of Maize People that forms that mythic path to pass over the trouble times that the Young Initiates faced as they made their way through the Houses of Ordeal encountered in the Underworld passage on their Ritual Initiation into the noble lives that awaited them as Engendered Sons of Noble Mothers and Noble Fathers whose deep understanding and ancestral knowledge is revealed here in the Popol Wuj through its Ancient Word that tells the Ancestral Account of those who Divine Ancestors and Ancestral Divinities who walked the Paths of Initiation to face the fears of the ordeals that challenged them in every way. This is the way of Storytelling and Myth-making that calls upon our Ancestral Soul to feel what the Ancestors once felt in order to intuit what they once imagined as they engaged their mythic imagination in ancient, ancestral ways.

body:
Now it is we who are called to enter the Imaginal World of the Mundus Imaginalis in order that we might also experience the mythic events and mythic ways of the mythic speech and mythic metaphors that are brought to life through our sowing the Ancient Word in our mythic imagination so that we might experience this Ancestral Account as the sacred passage that carries across times of insecurity as we live through an epic; an era; an age that is defined by a deep sense of unknowing. The Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj creates a profound sense of understanding as we shoulder the Blowguns of the Hero Twins to take-up the Road of Initiation just as they had done long, long ago when they walked their Path of Transformation. Let us then ʼenter the wordʼ to ʼenter the roadʼ to ʼenter the wayʼ of being and becoming a perfect replacement of the Divine Ancestors whoʼs ʼperfect words, perfect waysʼ are expressed throughout this Noble Book of Noble Counsel that is a Noble Book of Ancestral Advice.

Let us ʼenter this Ancestral Accountʼ to ʼenter the Ancestral Worldʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom; a Mesoamerican Realm that reveals as it tells how the Maya once lived out their lives on the Face of the Earth.

Let us ʼenter this Ritual Worldʼ of the Popol Wuj where the Ritual Ways of Ancestral Lives were marked out by Two Sacred Calendars that came together to create a threshold time that was crossed on this bridge of space and time known as the Popol Wuj. This Myth of the Maize People carried the Maya across these Dangerous Five Days and Nights of Liminal Space and Time. Popol Wuj formed the ritual space as it shaped the ritual narrative that bore the Maya across this sacred space and time that was borne as a ʼsacred burden; sacred bundleʼ embodied by the Ritual Drama of Popol Wuj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Popol Wuj is best thought of as the Ritual Renewal of the Sky-Earth through the Re-Enactment of the Forming and Shaping of the Ancient Ancestral World of the Maize People; the World of the Sky-Earth with its Four-Corners and Four- Sides that are seen in the constellations directly overhead of the Night-Sky when the Popol Wuj was performed at the Mid-point of the Dry and Rainy Seasons. It is here in this Mid-most place that exists between the Dry Winds and Cloudy Rains that the Popol Wuj was performed by the Kʼicheʼ Maya in order to renew their world and its time.

Popol Wuj is bridge that once bore the Kʼicheʼ Maya across the uncertain and insecure movement of the Sun and Moon; Planets, Stars, and Constellations during the Five Dangerous Days of the Wayebʼ when time slept in order that the ancestral soul might dream to bring forth new images of the New Year with is new imagination of space and time. The Two-Hundred and Sixty Day Divinatory Calendar and the Three-Hundred and Sixty Day Agricultural-Solar Calendar came together to create Five-Day; Five-Night Ritual Period of Time when a New Year- bearer was placed on his road for the coming year to govern the world as the embodied face of both Sacred Space and Divine Time. This period of time is when the Popol Wuj was played-out on the Great Plaza of Kʼicheʼ beneath the Great Temples and Ballcourt of Kʼicheʼ.

This Long Performance; this Long Recitation of Popol Wuj is what is being ʼsown and rootedʼ here at the beginning of this Sacred Narrative that brings to life the Sacred Lifecycle of the Earth, Sun, Moon, and Stars whose ritual death will end the ʼOut-going Yearʼ to then begin the ʼIn-coming Yearʼ at its rebirth through the Long Performance of the Popol Wuj with its Five Acts played out on the Five Days and Five Nights of the Sacred Five Days of the Wayebʼ. This volatile unstable time was when time and space slept in order that the Ancestral Soul of Maya Day- keepers could dream in order to ʼseeʼ in order to ʼknowʼ as they ʼdivinedʼ what the New Year held for the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ.

body:
This insecure time was carried as a sacred burden that was borne up in myth and ritual by the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo who became completely engaged in the ʼParticipation Mystiqueʼ of the Popol Wuj that completely engaged the mythic imagination of its Original Audience as it told of the Sowing of the Maize People and the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Sun. We too must engage our imagination as we enter the Imaginal Realm of Myth where our participation is the utmost importance if we are to ʼenter the wordʼ to ʼenter the worldʼ as we ʼenter the mythʼ of the Maize People by entering the Mundus Imaginalis of Popol Wuj.

It is up to us to bring the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj to life as our soul hungers to be fed by its images while being formed and shaped by its mythic words and metaphors. Our mythic imagination must become one with the Ancient Word as we enter the imaginative state known as ʼparticipation mystiqueʼ in which we transcend the present to enter into ʼin illo temporeʼ or ʼin those timesʼ in order that these mythic events become ancestral experiences of the soul.

It is up to us and our imagination to enter the Popol Wuj as the Sowing of the Maize as Sacred Sustenance and the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Sun as the Age and Era of the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo who formed and shaped the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom through all they said and did to bring their Ancient World to fruition. This is the Sacred Story told here.

body:
Mundus Imaginalis of Popol Wuj The Sowing of Sacred Sustenance The Dawning of the Sun of the Maize People The Maya Myth of the Maize People Grandmotherʼs Home and Milpa; Grandfathers Ballcourt and Quest This Sowing; this Dawning is what is brought to life here throughout the Popol Wuj in order to bring harmony and balance to the Sky-Earth so the Maize would come to fruition while the power and sovereignty of the Kʼicheʼ Lords and Nobles would continue to rule and govern the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom with its Ancestral Realm filled with Ancestral Soul that cried out to be invoked and remembered as it clamored to be recalled through the remembrance of the Ancient Ways of Ancestral Walking in Quest of living in a World where one was guided and protected by Divinities-Kabʼawil whose ways of being and becoming are revealed right here in the Popol Wuj .

Popol Wuj is best understood as a mythical bridge on the path of transformation; a mythical bridge of initiation upon which one crosses from the death and decay of the Old Year that calls out for its complete destruction and annihilation so a New World can be created where it once rose-up. This is what the Kʼicheʼ Maya did at the end of each and every year when they broke their pots and plates to then build up the sides of their altar places. A New World was created from the broken elements of the Old World and in this way the World and its Time was renewed through the Long Performance of the Ancient Word that was once accompanied by the Long Recitation of the its Ancestral Account of Popol.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This New World was created by the Kʼicheʼ Maya becoming something new through its Young Nobles Initiates who took up the Ancestral Path to the Sacred Center of the Mesoamerican World. This is the story told here in the Popol Wuj to inaugurate and initiate a New Life in a New Year; a New Year with a New Year- Bearer with ways of their own that would be brought forth into being through the ritual performance of this ritual drama of Popol Wuj; this is the story told here. This is the Sacred Narrative of life, death, and rebirth that begins right here with the sowing and seeding of the Ancient Word that leads to the rooting-down and rising-up of the sacred sprouts of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

This translation provides the reader with the Original Maya Kʼicheʼ Mythopoetic Language in order to ʼName of the Namesʼ as a means of ʼdecolonizingʼ this Translation and Interpretation of Popol Wuj. This ritual act of ʼnaming the namesʼ asks us to enter this Mythic Masterpiece of the Maize People on its own terms and in its own cultural contexts. This is why I have added ʼInterpretive Interludesʼ in a smaller font in order that the reader recognizes these interpretations as ʼcultural contextʼ and ʼinterpretive understandings of the natural worldʼ in which this Myth of the Maize People takes place.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Kʼicheʼ Maya knew the Ancient Word by heart as they are said to have suckled it as Sacred Sustenance of the Soul. The Maya lived this Myth of the Maize Lords yet we need addition understanding and interpretation to be able to appreciate many of it ingenious mythic plays with word and metaphor. This is why I feel obligated to provide the extra interpretive insights in order that the reader might better understand the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj. We will only come to deep appreciation of this Book of Counsel after many readings and recitation of its words and phrases which is the ʼway of mythʼ when ʼmyth claimsʼ us like the Popol Wuj will claim you through the sheer beauty of its mythopoetics and the way it builds on itself from beginning to end to cultivate a complete understanding of the Mesoamerican World through this Maya Myth of the Maize People.

I hope the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj awakens you to the Mesoamerican World with all its Transforming Magic and revelation of the Ancestral Soul of the Ancient Ones known as the Nawales. Popol Wuj is the Sacred Script that brought forth the Nawal that waited to be awoken by this Masterful Myth of the Maya known as Popol Wuj.

May its words and metaphors awaken your soul as it stimulates you mind and invigorates your feeling for others in the Santo Mundo-Sacred World that only comes to life when we fire ourselves up through the magic of myth and its ability to awaken our Ancestral Soul; the Ancestral Soul Ancient Indigenous America. In this way we no longer are forced by the dominant culture to live as ʼdisplaced Europeansʼ when we can develop a deep connection the Sacred Landscape and all the Many Generations of Indigenous People who have lived here.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Popol Wuj is the Sacred History of the Indigenous Pueblos who lived as One with the Maize Beings who they eventually became through their being formed by the Popol Wuj as Ritual Drama to be shaped by its being performed as Ritual Sacrifice. This is the Sacred Narrative told here to awaken your heart and mind to the Ancestral Ways of Indigenous America while feeding your body and soul with the mythic images that come to life as you engage your mythic imagination.

This is it. This is the Seeding and Sowing of the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj. It begins here at the root of this Flowering Cane of Maize that will come to fruition as we make our way word by word through this Mythic Masterpiece of the Maya People; Maya Pueblo known as the Kʼicheʼ.

I have lived with the Maya for Forty Years now and I have yet to meet a Maya who wants to return to the Popol Wuj because they have been taught by the dominant society and its Christian Culture of Christian Religion that tells them that the Popol Wuj is the work of the devil and filled with only lies and deceit. It is excruciating for me at times to live with Native American People who are taught to feel ʼas ifʼ the Popol Wuj were not theirs at all. And this is because of the way they have been severed from the roots, trunk, branches, limbs, flowers, and fruit of your lineages.

The Maya are like all of us in the sense of being a ʼdismemberedʼ people who are made to feel that in truth they come from the Ten Lost Tribes of Israel and so it goes. There is so much work to be done but it is dignified work filled with human integrity as we seek to reconnect with the Past in the Present to transform our Future filled with connection made through ancestral communication. All this connection and communication can be re-formed and re-shaped through re-telling the Ancestral Accounts found in Ancient Indigenous Mythology especially such as those found in this Mythic Masterpiece of the Popol Wuj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
We humans have a way back to our origins; we have a way back to the ʼtreeʼ from where we fell as the fruit of extraordinarily magnificent human lineages. All of us are special fruit yet all of us have been made to feel as if there were something inherently wrong with us and because of that in deep need of being saved. Life doesnʼt have to be lived with ideas like this. Life can be lived completely fired up by myths like the Popol Wuj that give our lives meaning while making us feel completely at home in the world.

We live in a world where the Maya are made to feel their Ancestorsʼ most imaginative and ingenious Literary Masterpiece is of no value at all for it is said to be nothing but lies and deception in almost every free Spanish translation found on-line; lies and deception; imagine the fury and gall of those who want to keep the Maya oppressed for all time. Worse still is that this oppressive force of culture and society; myth and religion wish only to keep the Maya illiterate in their Original Kʼicheʼ Maya Language so that the Maya are unable to read one of this worldʼs most significant literary works of Indigenous Mythopoetic genius. So that the Original Maya Kʼicheʼ Text is only read by those few foreign scholars who specialize in Philology in their study of Ancient Literature and Language like the Popol Wuj. It is one great big mess but at least we know now that it is all a big mess; and, fortunately human beings are quite good about cleaning up our messes. Just look at the way we destroy cities and towns to build them up again in no time at all.

The Maya will come to recognize the tremendous literary and cultural inheritance that has been left to them in the form of the mythopoetic beauty and imagination of Popol Wuj. This extraordinaire moment of decolonization that we now live in has come to free our minds and bodies; spirits and souls in order to renew our World of the Sky-Earth so that the transformation of our ritual and mythic life has begun in earnest.

We must allow our souls to be claimed by this Maya Myth of the Maize People and its playful Maize Deities whose trickster ways have much teach us about stand-up against bullies who want nothing more than to humiliate and belittle us. So let us enable our Ancestral Imagination to live again in order to recognize our lives as being those that live in an extraordinarily imaginative and inventive world where this Sacred Narrative once thrived along with its People and their Place. Myths exist like seeds that come back to life once you seed them but one must seed them if they are to live again. Let us break the chains of our soulsʼ enslavement to those old and new stories that come from far across the Sea that do not speak of this Indigenous Place nor of its Indigenous People nor of its Indigenous Pueblos. The time has come to say what cries out to be said; for we can no longer wait to say what lays so heavy on our Heart; on our Soul as that which goes un-spoken and un-performed in a world as oppressed and oppressive as it has ever been.

body:
With the writing of this Translation and Interpretation of Popol Wuj I have only done what I was born to do knowing there is a much greater movement and motion of Myth and Ritual that must be brought to life. What will happen? What will we do next? This is the question asked throughout the Popol Wuj as the Formers and Shapers create and destroy one Sun after the next to begin one Age after the next. A New Sun awaits us on the horizon where it will rise-up and out of the Coming Up Place of the Sun in the West. Our waiting and watching for the Sun of the next Age has come to its end; it is time to act by gathering together in Noble Council to begin our Ritual Walking again. The time of Transformation is here. We must sweep away the debris in order to begin again. This is what the Hero Twins do when they sweep-out their sacrificed Fathers Ballcourt to begin playing again; it is time to sweep the ballcourt clean so we can begin to play again.

Let us ʼenter the wordʼ to ʼenter the wayʼ to ʼenter the worldʼ of the Ancient Ones whose ancestral voice cries out to heard again. A voice that calls out to remind us that it is time to suckle the sacred sustenance of the sacred word; sacred metaphor of this sacred myth; it is time to suckle the sweet nectar of ancestral knowledge that flows from the exquisite beauty of the Popol Wuj. It is time for us to listen to the ancestral voice that reminds us that our Ancestral Soul will only feel true satisfaction when it is fed with these authentic mythic images that awaken our collective, communal consciousness and its collective mythic memory of the mythic archetypes brought to life here in the Popol Wuj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Popol Wuj is formed and shaped around an essential ancestral essence that when we partake of it acts as a magic elixir of life that opens our heart to transform our soul through the profound feelings and deep sensations that are released through the mythopoetic genius of this Mesoamerican Myth of the Maya. Popol Wuj when taken with a deep desire to change and transform is soul medicine; Popol Wuj is an Elixir of Life, Death, and Rebirth calls upon us to fully engage our soul and its imagination to release the mythic energy that gets us moving again. In many ways we are stuck in a World we no longer wish to participate in because it is not a world where the human soul is fed by the genius and beauty of authentic Indigenous Myth.

This is why the Popol Wuj is so valuable in our life and times because of the way it ignites our imagination in the crucible of our changing and transforming lives. Popol Wuj gets us moving again as it releases energies within us we might not even know exist. This why I am writing this so that you know for certain that this Ancient Maya Myth of Indigenous America is capable of transforming our existence when we allow it to claim and by doing so ʼenter the wordʼ to ʼenter the worldʼ of Indigenous America instead of feeling out of place as displaced Europeans who cannot find our way home. Popol Wuj makes us feel at home as it reveals the Ancient Ancestral Stories of this place so that we come to know this place in Indigenous Terms and in Indigenous Ways.

One of the Popol Wujʼs greatest strength is to make us feel at home again in the world; a world in which we are made feel a deep sense of belonging by our becoming one with the People; Pueblos, and Places that are brought to life through our recitation of the Popol Wuj. We are made to feel ʼas ifʼ we were the ʼnatural enemiesʼ of the Indigenous People of the America because of the history we are fed through our education. What if we were taught the Popol Wuj in Elementary School and that we were the ʼnatural alliesʼ of the Indigenous Nations? What then?

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
How would our perspective change if we were taught the Popol Wuj as the guiding myth of the Sacred Landscape of Maize Sowers and Milpa Growers? This is the attitude I ask you to take towards your reading of the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

The Original Maya Kʼicheʼ Mythopoetics of the Popol Wuj is said to be a Sacred Text that defies translation and I could not agree more to this truth. But this doesnʼt mean we shouldnʼt try to bring forth a translation that brings our the natural beauty of its mythopoetics so we can develop a Maya Perspective of Life, Death, and Rebirth that comes from this Sacred Text that is dedicated to the continual Creation and Destruction of the Age or Suns that provide warmth and heat to all of those who live on the Face of the Earth. Popol Wuj is a beautiful text and it can be translated while at the same time acknowledging that its original language is one of humanities creates creations by an Aesthetic Culture dedicated and devoted to bringing beauty into the World; Beauty that manifests the Truth; Beauty that expresses the Good; Beauty that reveals a Maya sense of Transcendence through which the Ancestors return through their Descendants to continue with the sacred work of forming and shaping the Beauty of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea.

I can only ask that you to do your all to take in the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Accountʼs for the ingenious mythopoetic play that it offers us through its mythic words and mythic metaphors as something that is not ʼstrange and foreignʼ much less as ʼexoticʼ as most translations have done in the past. These past translations have wished to make its mythopoetic language seem more alien and exotic than it actually is by translating its Five Acts ʼas ifʼ they were something so different that there is no way to understand them much less hold them close to oneʼs heart in order that they flower and fruit in oneʼs soul.

Mythic Masterpieces of Mythopoetic Literature Imaginal Realm; Imaginal World; Mundus Imaginalis Ancient America; Ancient American Indigenous Scripture

body:
Popol Wuj is as Ancient Indigenous Myth formed and shaped with an enchanting mythopoetics that is as easy to understand as any Myth in a world where all Myths seem to be strange until we make them our own. Let us make the Popol Wuj our own as the precious indigenous myth that is; a myth that is human myth that is able to ʼclaim usʼ as any other of humanityʼs many masterful myths.

So let the Popol Wuj in to all of us who are a people and pueblo that was born and raised in this place that we now call las Américas. Let yourself feel at home in this Imaginal Realm of this Imaginal World of the Mundus Imaginalis in order to develop a deep sense of belong in the Mythic Realm of this Book of Counsel; this Book of Ancient Ancestral Advice. We need not feel like displaced Europeans in Indigenous America when we learn to speak Indigenous Languages and learn to read Indigenous Myths to then come to practice Indigenous Ways of Being and Becoming in the World. Some of the first Spaniards, French, Dutch, and English want to assimilate their lives to Indigenous Ways of Living. The Native Americans may have found great pleasure when they saw and heard Europeans appropriating Indigenous Ways of Living on the Land. Most certainly there have been thousands of Euro-Americans who chose Indigenous Ways of Live by adapting to the Indigenous World while learning to speak Indigenous Language to then adopt Indigenous Myths and Stories to guide their new lives lived in Indigenous ways.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
We are who we are yet it always surprises me how Euro-Americans continue to expect Indigenous People to assimilate Euro-American ways of living out their lives when looking upon Euro-American as ʼstrangeʼ if not worse for assimilating Indigenous Ways of Life into the ways of growth and development. Popol Wuj asks us to ʼenter the worldʼ of the Maya to be able to walk step and step with the Hero Twins and the First Four Fathers and their Sons as they make their way walking down the road of transformation on their ritual path of initiation. Needless to say we can learn a great of wisdom while attaining a tremendous amount of knowledge about the Mesoamerica World by reading the Popol Wuj with as much care and concern as we can muster.

The days of living our lives guided by Greek and Norse Myths must come to an end if there is any hope to feel at home here in las Américas. There is nothing like the Popol Wuj for opening up our hearts to engage our souls in a myth that tells us the ways of Indigenous America. It is our choice; it is our life and so it is up to us to choose the myths that support our lifeʼs quest to live out meaningful and purposeful lives. Why read European Myths when no longer live in Europe? Why practice Middle Eastern Religions when we no longer live in the Middle East? My Ancestors left Italy and Ireland; England and Germany to come to the Americas it is only natural that a grandson of migrants should continue migrating to where one can live out a life deeply influenced by the People and Place I chose to live. I came to the Maya to learn from the Maya and now that my life comes to its inevitable end it is up to me to give back all that I have learned while living with the Maya in an act of reciprocity in which and where the Mythopoetic Language of the Popol Wuj is t most valuable gift I have received by living up here on this mountain with the Maya.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is why I have dedicated my life to this Translation of the Popol Wuj. A translation that has taught me to perfect the way I understand and speak Maya Languages. This long process of translation and interpretation has generated as great love for the Maya People; their Language; and their Mythic, Metaphorical ways of living life in the footsteps of their Ancestors which has created a path of deep human connection through the communication one becomes capable of with the Maya through speaking their Maya Languages to cross-over and into the Cultural World of the Maya People.

My life has been blessed by the Beloved Language of Maya as their Sacred Speech while at the same time being somewhat cursed by never feeling like I will ever get speaking Maya just right. And so it goes with this Translation and my years of doing my all to get it just right. Well this is it; as good as it gets so I certainly hope you can appreciate the sacrifice; a willing self-sacrifice but a sacrifice all the same.

We who live in the Americas and were born and raised in the Americas can enter into the Indigenous Myths of the America with great ease because we know the Natural World in which this myth takes place while at the same time recognizing the ways of the mythic actors as being similar if not the same as the ways of the Maya who live out their lives formed by the mythic language and mythic metaphors that originate in the Popol Wuj.

Once again: Myth makes us feel at home in this world in order to give us as sense of belonging that only walking across the Face of the Earth comes close to replicating; which is why Sacred Journeys and Sacred Myths bring out one another in order to increase their ability to provide us with a sense of belonging. After all Myths like the Popol Wuj come from this land and its sacred landscape just as myths arise from the lived experience of the Indigenous People and the ways of living of the Indigenous Pueblos of the land and its sacred landscape.

body:
These are those People who are made and molded from this sacred landscape and its myths that have been formed and shaped by the People and Place from which they originate; these People and these Places are those who formed and shaped the myths we can once again live and grow by. So letʼs enter the Popol Wuj with the idea that it is meant to form and shape us as it feeds our starving soul with images that have moved the Maya to take action in their World for thousands of years.

Sacred Journey; Sacred History; Maya Myth In Quest of Knowing: What is ours to bring to Fruition? The Mythic Quest; the Search for Purpose and Belonging So let us enter the Popol Wuj in quest of coming back into contact with our purpose in life and the meaning that purpose provides us in our quest to live deeply fulfilling lives. After all the Popol Wuj tells of one Sacred Journey after the next of Young Men and Young Men in search of ʼwhat is theirs in lifeʼ to bring to fruition. These mythic figures move from being lost souls who have no idea what their true destiny is to the authors and actors of the destiny as the take up what is theirs to bring to fruition.

We humans need to see success before we experience success and this is one of the great beauties of the Popol Wuj that shows the Hero Twins success; just as it shows their Mothers success; just as it shows their Fatherʼs success; and on down the line it goes as once story of mythic story of mythic failure being transformed into mythic success. This is why it is said we humans need myth to in order envision our own triumph against all odds. These are the kinds of sacred stories you are about to enter here.

Myth is the bridge that carries us over the deep abyss of ʼunknowing and uncertaintyʼ and this Maya Myth of the Maize Lords known as the Popol Wuj is a truly magnificent myth that forms a truly magnificent bridge to our origins and all that is found there in the depths our initiatory descent into the underworld where our Ancestors await our return.

body:
This is the Dark Night-Sky with its ʼancestral starsʼ that make up the ʼWhite- Road-Saq Bʼey of the Milky-Way where our Ancestors shimmer and shine in the starlight of the darkness of the calm quiet night. This is where the Maya go in their ritual fires to converse with their dead and deceased.

This is where we are called to return again in order to create connection through the ease of our human inheritance that is the simple sacred act of communication as we raise our eyes to the bright stars in the dark night to invoke the names of our Ancestors in order to remember them again.

We are here, they are there but in this moment of soulful communication and connection we are together blankets by the velvet mantle of Night and its divine darkness. This is the primordial darkness of our human origins that we are about to enter as we ʼenter the ancient wordʼ to ʼenter the darkʼ where the spark of creation and formation awaits our invocation; our incantation of the sacred words to bring forth the Primordial Earth up and out of the Primordial Waters of the Sea and Sky.

It is time to engage our mythic imagination through our Long Performance; Long Recitation of Popol Wuj. So without further ado let us take of the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

Popol Wuj: Book of Counsel; the Council Book Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij-Ancestral Account

This is the root of the Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij; this is the origin of the Ancestral Account-Ojer Tzij here in this place known as Kʼicheʼ; this Place; this Pueblo; these People known and named Kʼicheʼ; Place of the Many Trees; People of the Many Trees; Pueblo of the Many Trees-Kʼi Cheʼ: Kʼicheʼ by name. Here we shall inscribe it; here we shall implant it as the Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij-the Ancestral Account. This then is its being seeded as the Ancient Word; this then is its being sown as the Ancestral Account; here at the beginning of the telling of the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

This, then, was when they gave a full account of everything that was done in the Perfection of Existence; in the Perfection of Being; in the Perfection of the Word; in the Perfection of Way as they are known: Saqil Kʼolem, Saqil Tzij.

Here we shall write it out in these days, in these times that are spoken of as the Word of God-Uchʼabʼal Dios; the Word of God known and named as the next Age of Christianity; as the next Era of Christendom-Christianoil chik; as the next Sun to come known as Christianity; the Age of Christianity as it is named.

body:
We shall bring it forth in the Perfection of Being, in the Perfection of the Word-Saqil Kʼolem, Saqil Tzij, in this place, in these times, for no longer can we look upon the Precious Painted Picture Books of Counsel-Saq Ilbʼal re Popol Wuj to ponder their Sacred Pictorial Histories that come from Beside the Sea known as Ilbʼal Saq petenaq Chʼaqa Palo; no longer are there the Sacred Images to gaze upon to Enliven the Imagination; for the Precious Painted Pictographic Histories that came from Beside the Sea can no longer be contemplated for they no longer exist in these days; in this place; in these times; in this space.

We shall just bring it forth here in writing because there is no longer a place to see Our Ancestral Story; Our Ancient Account that was once shown to be seen in the Painted Pictographic Histories known as the Ilbʼal; for those Pictorial Histories that came from Beside the Sea-Ilbʼal Saq petenaq Chʼaqa Palo no longer exist.

For our Painted Pictorial Histories-Ilbʼal with their ancient writing and painted pictures that were formed and shaped on the Pounded-Poj Paper-Wuj of the Wild Fig Tree-Poj no longer exist.

Ilbʼal re Popo Wuj Mythic Maps of Meaning Painted Pictorial Pictographic Histories Pounded Pages of Paper; Painted Books of Ancestral Memory

These were our Painted Pictographic Histories that are spoken of as Ilbʼal re Popo Wuj; those Precious Pictorial Histories that were painted on the Pounded Paper Lienzos-Ilbʼal re Poj- Poj-Wuj that are said to no longer exist to be contemplated; those that no longer can be seen to be known; those Ilbʼal re Popo Wuj that are no more to be found to be pondered as the Painted Books of Ancestral Memory that were gazed upon as Mythic Maps of Meaning that once showed the Way of Divine Ancestors as they walked their Roads of Migration on Ancestral Paths of Transformation that are drawn and painted on road covered with footprints that pass by Sacred Mountains and cross-over Mystic Rivers where scene are illustrated telling of Ancestral Events that have become Mythic Experiences.

body:
These Great Lienzos can be seen to be pondered as the Mapa de Cuauhtinchan Dos and el Mapa de Cuauhtinchan so we know quite well what these Ilbʼal re Popo Wuj through Mesoamerican Scholarship that has opened our perspective and understanding of the Mesoamerican Cosmos that was illustrated and painted on these ʼpounded Amate-Poj paper lienzos or Poj-Poj-Wuj or Popo Wujʼ with their glyphic script and iconographic naming of the names of the Ancient World of the Ancestral People of Ancestral Pueblos.

This is the Sacred History told here in the Popol Wuj that was transcribed by Noble Scribes who listen to the Ilol-Seers and Naʼol-Knowers that revealed their Divine Ancestors mythic lives that were contemplated by those who were Ponderers-AjBʼis and those who were Knowers-AjNaʼoj whose names will be named here.

According to the Noble Scribes those Painted Pictorial Histories of those Mythic Maps of Meaning no longer exist to be seen to invoke the names of the People and Place; to remember the Events and Experienced illustrated on these Ancient Maps filled with Mythic Meaning and Historical Consequence.

Those Ilbʼal re Popo Wuj that once formed our imagination and shaped our intuition are no longer to be seen to tell the story of our living in darkness when we searched to find the ʼOne- Junʼ who would come to guide and protect us as we made our way wondering across the Face of the Earth. Those Pictorial Histories that were painted on the Pounded ʼPoj-Amateʼ Paper Lienzos are no longer to be seen; for they are hidden away in the shadows where they no longer speak to tell the stories of where we come from and where we have been; what we did and what was done to us as those who came from a People; a Place; and a Pueblo that were once seen in a Painted Pictorial History that showed in order to reveal our Ancient Ancestral Account that tells of when we lived in the Shadows; when we lived in the Dark with no One to lead and defend us against those who only wanted sacrificial death for us.

Our Shadows-Qamujibʼal New Castilian Sun; New Age; Kristianoil New Word; New Maize Lord; Uchʼabʼal Tiox; Jesukristo Perfection of Being; Perfection of the Word: Saqil Kʼolem; Saqil Tzij

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so it is that we will write out our Ancient Word here; we will write out our Ancestral Account here to tell of our lives lived in the shadows-qamujibʼal when we lived in ʼour darknessʼ before the Perfection of Existence; before the Perfection of the Word of God- Saqil Kʼolem; Saqil Tzij uchʼabʼal Tiox; the Perfect Life of Christianity-pa Kristianoil-the Precious Life of Christendom as it is said and seen in the Painted Pictures of the Sacred Life; the Divine Life:

Ilbʼal Saq Kʼaslem. We will tell of all that happened before in the Perfection of Being; in the Perfection of the Word: Saqil Kʼolem; Saqil Tzij. These Ancient Words could not be more ambiguous in their need to protect the ʼWord of God and Age of Christianityʼ while setting the scene in order to begin telling of the Divine Ancestors lived in the Perfection of Being; in the Perfection of the Word that will be revealed here in the telling of the Ancient Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

These Noble Scribes wish to elevate their Ancestors through high regard and deep respect for remembrance while at the same time acknowledging that life has changed with the New Language known as the Word of God and the New Age that has come into existence that is ruled by the New Christian Sun of Christendom where and in which the body and blood of Jesukristo are perceived to be the Sacred Sustenance of the Maize People.

And so it is that Jesukristo has become the Maize Deity who will be sacrificed between Twins who like Junajpu, IxBʼalamkej will sacrifice their lives to become the Great Star-Venus and the Moon who will accompany Jesukristo as he makes his way across the Sky alongside his Father the Sun. This is where the Book of Council will leave the New Sun behind to tell the Ancient Ancestral Account with very little influence coming from the Dominican Priests who taught the Noble Maya Scribes how to write in the Latinate.

The Four Corners; the Four Sides as it is said by those known as the Former, the Shaper; as it is spoken by those who Form the Corners; by those who Shape the Sides known as Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol.

Four-fold Cornering; the Four-fold Siding Four Corners; Four Sides of the Sky-Earth Great Square in the Night Sky: Great Plaza of Kʼicheʼ Great Rectangle of Orion: Ballcourt Let us invoke the Four-fold Cornering; the Four-fold Siding; the Measuring of the Four Corners; the Measuring of the Four Sides of the Great Square in the Night Sky and on the Earth as the Great Plaza and Milpa were the Popol Wuj will be performed; we have invoked the Rectangle of Orion as the Ballcourt by halving the measuring-chord to stretch it into the Sky and down to Earth. We have invoked the Form and Shape of the Four-fold Cornering; the Four-fold Siding of the Sky-Earth in order to bring the Forming; the Shaping of the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew to Completion. Let us enchant the Four-Corners; the Four-Sides through the Original Maya Kʼicheʼ invocation; incantation of the Four- fold Cornering; Four- fold Siding of the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew.

Ukaj Tzʼuq, Ukaj Xukutaxik; retaxik; Ukaj Cheʼxik, Umej Kʼaʼmaxik Upa Kaj, Upa Ulew; Kaj Tzʼuq, Kaj Xukut, chuchaʼxik rumal Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol

These are those known as Contemplator: AjBʼis. These are those known as Wonderer-AjBʼis-Worrier of all that must be brought forth into the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea. These are those who are the Sagacious Sage-AjNaʼoj-the Knowledgeable Knower who are the Sublime Seer-Ilol of all that was; all that is; and all that would come to be on the Face of the Earth.

These are those known as the Sagacious Knower-AjNaʼoj-Sensitive Thinker who gatherer their thoughts together in council with One-an-Other to arrive at an understanding of all that can be felt to be known through the intuitive sense of the engaged intuition and immersed imagination.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These who are Ponderer; Knower; AjBʼis, AjNaʼoj are named here as those who come together to think and imagine in order to consider and contemplate all that can be understood in order to know what to do next as the Former; as the Shaper of the Sky-Earth.

For these who are AjBʼis-Contemplator and AjNaʼoj-Knower are those who must think upon the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea in order to envision what must be brought forth into existence on the Face of the Earth. It was they who pondered and considered; thought and contemplated to know what would be needed in and upon the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew; in and upon the Lake-Sea; Cho-Palo.

Forming and Shaping the Mythic Bridge of Popol Wuj Footsteps on this Mythic Path of Transformation Feeling at Home in the World Belonging to a People and Place Entering the Word to Enter the Ancestral Account Enter the Imaginal Realm of Change and Transformation Now that we have ʼnamed the namesʼ of the Former, the Shaper; Grandmother, Grandfather; Mother, Father; Bearer, Begetter; Daughters, Sons and all of the many forms and shapes they take it is time to begin the Forming; the Shaping of the Primordial Earth. We have Formed and Shaped the Four-Fold Cornering; Four-Fold Siding of the Sacred Space where this Long Performance and Long Recitation of the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account will be played out.

This Introductory invocation and incantation has opened up our way into the Five Acts of the Popol Wuj that will be performed during the Five Days and Five Nights in which the transforming face of space and time can begin as we enter the Wayebʼ with its ʼSleeping and Dreamingʼ through which the mythic imagination is brought to life. All is prepared for the performance of the recitation of this Sacred Narrative.

body:
This sacred threshold period of ending and beginning has begun out of which the movement of forming and shaping of the Sky-Earth can begin in the Maya Cosmos where being and becoming are invoked to be repeated over and over again. The Maya Time and Space braid itself together through the Two-Hundred and Sixty Day Divinatory Calendar and the Three- Hundred and Sixty Day Solar Calendar coming together to reveal the Year-Bearer who will carry the Sun on his back as a Sacred Burden for the next Three Hundred and Sixty Days. The ʼchanging faceʼ of the Lord of Five Days known as the Year-Bearer or Cargador del Tiempo or Mam has been invoked as: the Grandfather; the Ancient One; the Ancestor.

The time has come to enter the ritual performance of renewal that brings about the change and transformation of the Ancestral Face of Sun; the Sun understood and imagined as the Face of Time known as Kinich Ajaw: the Sun-faced Lord. This Sun-faced Lord is the face of the Sun that is the face of time. And this dear reader is the ritual context in which the myth of the Popol Wuj was performed in order to renew time and space; the Sun and World in a Cosmos that repeated itself ʼtime and againʼ in ways that could be nurtured and nourished to bring forth great abundance on the Face of the Earth.

Rites of Passage Essence of the Wayebʼ Changing Face of the Sun Transforming Face of Time Rituals of Initiation Sacred Journeys of Ancestral Peregrination This is the essence of the Popol Wuj that you must understand in order to ʼenter the wordʼ to ʼenter the worldʼ of the Ancestors in order to ʼenter the wayʼ of transformation and change. And not to confuse things but this was also the time of year when the Young Women and Men; Nobles and Vassals were initiated through Rites of Passage that are played out metaphorically here in the Popol Wuj.

Myth and Ritual are woven together here in the Popol Wuj in order that we are given an intimate view of the Maya Cosmos that provides us with a perspective that enables us to see through the eyes of Maya Priests and Priestesses whoʼs sacred burden in life was to bring fruition all that existed on the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea in order that the People of the Pueblos lived in abundance and prosperity. The Year-bearer; the Cargador del Año; the Mam; the Ancestor; the Face of the Sun has been awoken through our incantation of his many names as the Transforming Face of Time.

This is the essence of the Wayebʼ which is the essence of the Ritual Performance; Ritual Recitation of the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj. It is time to begin the Incantation of the Forming and Shaping; Molding and Modeling of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
When the Maya entered the Five Days; Five Nights of the Wayebʼ they entered in the Myth and Ritual of Popol Wuj in order to pass-over the ʼliminal or thresholdʼ state between the Old Year and New Year. This is the same time for the Rites of Passage and the Rituals of Initiation that carry its Youth through the passage of Older Girls and Older Boys into the Young Adult Life of Young Women and Young Men to the transform Older Children into the life ways and responsibilities of Young Adults where Young Women and Young Men find what is theirs in Life to bring to fruition. This is the time for a quest to be given vision through Ancestral Advice and Noble Counsel that comes from the Popol Wuj. The Popol Wuj that speaks to us metaphorically of the Noble Entitlements of the Noble Women and Noble Men who find out who they are and what is their destiny to fulfill in life as the Sacred Burden-Patan that they will bear as members of Noble Lineage and the deep sense of belonging that leads to a feeling connect to oneʼs People and Place to feel at Home in the World. Popol Wuj expressed all of these changes and transformation through the Five Acts of the Five Section of Popol Wuj where there is a different form of natural and cultural passage from one Stage of Life to the next. This you will come to experience as you move through the Popol Wuj as a Sacred Journey of Ancestral Peregrination that is the Path of Initiation told of here in the Popol Wuj.

We know from studies of Indigenous Pilgrimage that the Popol Wuj was watched and listened to as a Sacred Ritual Performance that fed the heart and soul of the Young Initiates who then took-up the Sacred Road or Saq Bʼey that was the same Sacred Path of Pilgrimage known as Peregrination. The Initiates and their Leaders walked in the footsteps of their Divine Ancestors to receive the sacred knowledge that would influence their lives all lifelong.

body:
For on this Path of Peregrination many ʼsignsʼ would be given just as many experiences would be had that provide great meaning and significance. So you see the stories found the Popol Wuj were listened to be experienced as the mythic images and mythic metaphors that guided oneʼs experience in life.

And so it is that the invocation of the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj enables us to ʼcross- overʼ on this transcendent passage that is formed by myth and shaped by ritual. A mythic bridge is formed through the ritual performance of the Popol Wuj; and, it will be on that mythic bridge that the Maya crossed-over these ʼFive Danger Daysʼ of the Wayebʼ that was a period of ʼpass- overʼ in which a profound experience of transcendence was experienced as the Present entered the Past to reveal the Future.

When we engage our imagination fully in the reading of the Popol Wuj we also experience this transcendence as the Mythic Past becomes the Mythic Present. Through our souls complete engagement in the mythic imagination we also enter ʼin illo temporeʼ when this Myth of the Maize People was and is brought to life through the ritual performance of the Popol Wuj.

For it is well known that Myth always is although it never was; and so it is that we will bring this myth to life as we fully engage our imagination by ʼentering the wordʼ of this Sacred Narrative in order to enter into the ancient time and ancestral space of Popol Wuj during this time of the Wayebʼ as we enter this period of Transformation that comes to fruition in the Renewal of the Year and Rebirth of the Face of the Earth. The time of our soulʼs complete participation in the enchantment of the Sky-Earth has come with the articulation of the Ancient Word as the incantation of the Ancestral Account that will bring the Ancestral Soul and its collective memory to life. Great quantities of psychic energies will be released as we engage our imagination causing us to feel profound feelings will intuiting deep meaning as we participate in this Long Performance; Long Recitation of Popol Wuj.

body:
When we ʼenter the wordʼ a particular quality of existence is experience as the collective unconscious or collective memory awakes within us to release tremendous energy that we must then direct to our own sense of transformation in the life so that we come to feel at home in the world; a world in which we belong; a world in which we share empowering memories and experiences that are awakened only through our experience of myth. These ancestral remembrances are experienced one after the next as we move through the Popol Wuj. And so it is that the moment of mythic transcendence has arrived as our opportunity to fully participate in the transcendent function of ʼparticipation mystiqueʼ as we ʼenter the wordʼ of this Ancestral Account enabling our Ancestral Soul to return to the Ancestral World of that is formed and shaped by the mythopoetic genius of Popol Wuj. It is time to cross the great abyss of time and space on this mythic bridge that carries us back before the mythic erasure and religious annihilation of those fanatic Europeans who wished to eradicate the Popol Wuj from the Face of the Earth by burning the vast libraries of the Maya Pueblos while exterminating its Priest and Priestess; Noble Women and Noble Men and all those who participated in performing the Ancestral Accounts found in the Books of Council known as Popol Wuj.

This Ancient Myth of the Maya is an Ancestral Being that refuses to be eradicated from the Face of the Earth and so it was that it found a way to be written down in the Latinate by the Last Noble Lords and Scribes of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Kingdom. The Ancient Word of this Popol Wuj found a way to survive so that it would live again when its time came to come back to life.

It is time to bring this precious Maya-Mesoamerican Myth back to life by entering the sleeping and dreaming of the transforming time of the Wayebʼ when and where the mythopoetic genius of the Popol Wuj can be performed and recited by Maya Speakers and Singers; Dancers and Musicians; Actors and Acrobats; Performers and Ballplayers.

body:
This is it; the time has come; the Grand Stage of this Long Performance has been cordoned-off on the Great Plaza that has been measured-out and staked-off on the Four Corners; on the Four Sides.

The torches are lit; the stars burn bright in the deep darkness of the Night Sky as we enter this transforming time that lays calm and quiet; still and silent between the Dry Season and the Rain Season when the dew covers the Earth to water the Maize sprouts in the Milpa that has been sown all across the Mountain-Plain.

With the work of sowing seeds and building houses come to completion it is time to remember the origins of the words and ways that the People and their Pueblo come from in order to give thanks to the Ancestors while asking what must be done next to bring the Sky-Earth to fruition. Myth and Ritual have become one in the Wayebʼ where lifeʼs renewal and transformation fills the hopes and desires of the Descendants whoʼs Ancestral Souls call out to be remembered by being invoked through the sacred act of ʼnaming the namesʼ.

The Pueblo gathers together as ʼOnly One-Xa Junʼ to participate in the Ritual Performance of the Popol Wuj where the ritual purpose and mythic intention focuses in on the renewal of life through the forming of clouds and the shaping of mist as this mythic summons for rain comes with the performance of ritual sacrifice. And so it is that myth and ritual become one through ritual performance of Popol Wuj.

This is it; it is time to end in order to begin again; it is time to renew life through the invocation of myth; through the performance of ritual; through ritual song and ritual dance; through mythic longing and mythic trance.

Popol Wuj as Our Mythic Bridge of Our Crossing-over Unspoken Pain and Suffering The time has come to begin again by crossing-over the unspoken pain and suffering caused by the cultural dismemberment and religious dislocation that nobody talks about yet feels like a broken pot; an open schism that is felt as a tribal rupture; as a shattering of lineages; as a scattering of jade; a spilling of blood; a debt that remains unpaid.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The erasure of the Popol Wuj among the Maya began not so very long ago which makes its wound felt to be very fresh in a People who have lived as a Pueblo for over Three Thousand Years. But those who inflicted the wound know how to keep it open and unhealed while salting it with every opportunity so that it always feels real.

This began just a few hundred years ago with the erasure of Maya Ritual and Maya Myth by the Dominican and Franciscan Orders through their close association with the Spanish Inquisition. But this oppression of the Popol Wuj continued through the violence of the 1980ʼs and 1990ʼs and then strengthened with the Millennium in 2000 to then end in 2012 with the Return of the Maya in 2012 and the Oxlajuj Baqtun event. Times are changing and this translation is intended to be an agent of change so let us allow it to act in that way. The future of las Américas asks us to return to the Ancestral Past to collect and recollect all that was erased from American lives. We must return to ʼrememberʼ all that was ʼdismemberʼ from the American Experience in American lives that were denied the Indigenous Experience of speaking Indigenous Languages to participate in Indigenous Myths and Rituals.

We cannot return to the Past but we can return to the Mythic Imagination of the Past and this is what we shall be doing here in the Mythic Act of Return to the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj .

THIS then is its narration; here then is its recitation: all is in suspense; all is calm; all is at rest; all is silent; all is quiet; not a murmur; not a ripple in the vast vacant void of the empty expanse of Sky.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
A Mythopoetic Translation THIS then is its narration; here then is its recitation: all is suspense; all is calm; all is at rest; still and silent; calm and quiet; motionless, immobile; no murmur; no mumble; not a hum; nothing to rumble; nothing to churn; not a wave; not a ripple; nothing moves for all is serene stillness as silence echoes silence in the constant calm; in the continuous quiet; no motion, no movement; not a sigh; not a sound in the unbroken silence; in the incessant stillness; nothing to stir that might make an echo in the vast vacant void; in the infinite expanse of empty, empty Sky- Kaj. Kʼakatzʼininoq; kʼakachamamoq;

Kʼakatzʼinonik; Kʼasilanik; Kʼakalolinik; Katolona Kʼakatzʼininoq-suspense; kʼakachamamoq-calm; kʼakatzʼinonik-rest; kʼasilanik-silence; kʼakalolinik-murmur-hum; katolona-empty, vacant, void, vacuous; I write these Maya Kʼicheʼ words so that you might receive a sense of the primordial sound of the calm quiet silence in this incantation of the motionless murmur of the vast vacant void of the still silent solitude of the empty expanse of the Primordial Sky.

Here, then, is the First Word; the First Speech-Nabʼe Tzij; Nabʼe Uchan when it was first spoken there was not yet a single being; not a single creature since there was nothing yet named; nothing yet known.

For there was not yet a One Person-Jun Winaq;

Nor was there yet a being that was named; that was known as: One Animal-Jun Chikop Bird-Tzʼikin Fish-Kar Crab-Tap Tree-Cheʼ

Rock-Abʼaj-Stone Cave-Jul-Hole Ravine-Siwan-Canyon Grassland-Kʼim-Thatch Forest-Kʼichelaj-Place of the Many Trees

Just all alone is the Sky; the Face of the Earth cannot be seen for the Face of the Earth has yet to be revealed.

There, all alone, is the still silent Sea; settled, calm and quiet; it alone is wombed over by the vast, vacant void of the empty vault of Sky; separate are the Two who are pooled together as One; a perfect reflection; the One over the Other; the Two seen as just One-xa Jun; a mirrored void of vacant Sky reflected in the shinny shimmer of the silent solitary Sea.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The serene, silent Sky floats upon the placid, pool of Sea; its silent stillness echoes in the emptiness of reflected quiet; the ʼOneʼ reveals the ʼOtherʼ in the mirrored Sky; on the mirrored Sea.

Nothing yet is there to be gathered together; nothing yet there to sound out; not-a-thing to rise-up; nothing to move around; nothing to move about, for everything is at rest; everything held in place; for there is just nothing at all to stand-up; nothing at all to stand-out; just nothing at all to climb-up and out to move all about in the silence; upon the Water; beneath the Sky.

There is just nothing there that might come into being that which might shoot-up to sprout-out; for there is just nothing at all that might rise-up and straighten out: xa ma kʼo wi naki laʼ kʼolik yakalik. Just pooled Water; just the flat Sea; just they alone are pooled and placid; calm and collected; for all that might exist has yet to come into being; for that which might be has yet to come into existence; for all that might be has simply not yet come into being.

Just calm quiet; just still silence is all there is in the nocturnal darkness; there in the dark; there in the night; there in the darkness of night where all is filled with silence; the silence of the night; there where all is quiet darkness in the calm silence of night; in the silent darkness of the calm quiet of the still silent night. They are there; there they are; in the darkness; in the night.

They who are there are those who are all alone yet together; together as one in the calm; in the quit; in the stillness; in the darkness of the Night.

All alone are they who are those who are known as:

Former, Shaper-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol;

Sovereign Plumed Serpent-Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz;

Bearer, Begetter-Alom, Kʼajolom.

It is they who are those who are there in the shimmering shine of the sparkling light of the jade green waters; hidden yet there is he who is enveloped in the glistening glimmer; in the glossy gleam of the glittering light-saqtetoj; saqtetoj-the sparkling splendor that emanates from the precious turquoise bundle of resplendent quetzal feathers and lovely blue cotinga plumage.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Sovereign Plumed Serpent-Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz is there with Former; is there with Shaper; Mother-Father as they are known; as they are named Tzʼaqol- Bʼitol; Alom-Kʼajolom; Molder-Modeler; Bearer-Begetter.

These are those who are there in the Water; there in the Night; the Maker- Tzʼaqol; the Modeler-Bʼitol they are just out of view enveloped in jade-green feathers of the resplendent quetzal; bundled in the precious plumage of the lovely- blue cotinga; awash in the sparkling light of the turquoise waters.

There in the Turquoise Sea they just shimmer; they just shine; their divine jade beads; their sacred golden seeds; they just flash; they just flare as they flicker making the water glisten as it glimmers; glimmers as it glitters; glitters as its gleams; this sparkling light just shines as it shimmers there in the blue-black stillness in the silent darkness of the Sky. There they are cloaked in the lovely blue-green mantel of the calm quiet of the Primordial Night; there in the dark womb of the Primordial Sea are they who come together to form; to shape the Water-Sky as the Turquoise-Blue Sea begins to move about as its Primordial Waters are called to give birth in the Jade-Green Darkness of the engendering Night.

There they are; they are there amidst the Primordial Waters where starlight sparkles in the starlit night that shines as it shivers silver slivers of scintillating light that shimmers as it shines bright straight overhead in the Middle of the Night at that sacred most time known as Mid-Night. Deep down below the Sacred Golden Seeds and Divine Jade Beads begin to twitch as they twitter in their Sacred Bundle of Plumage and Feathers. There in the Ancestral Water are the Ancestorsʼ Ancestral Seeds accompanied by their Eternal Jade Beads that are now shifting and shaping; shaping and shifting in the Ancestral Waters all of which causes a resplendent kind of Primordial Light to begin escaping out of the Sea and into the Night.

body:
This Ancient, Ancestral Light glitters as it gleams; gleams as it glimmers; glints as it glows as it begins to shimmer and shine; and so, the Sacred Bundle flashes as it flickers; shakes as it shivers to then quake and quiver all-about. This is the Sacred Bundle of his Majesty, Sovereign Plumed Serpent Lord Quetzalcoatl; Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz who now is enclosed, encased in a resplendent green cloak of iridescent green feathers. This jade-green cloak; this emerald-green mantel flutters as it floats like cypress bows that ripple in the breeze to envelop the Precious Twin ʼas ifʼ embraced by the arms of the Cypress Tree.

The Feathered Serpent; Quetzalcoatl is now bundled in a plumed mantel as the Mythic and Magical Nawal Serpent whose scales have transformed into feathers leaving Quetzalcoatl wrapped in the soft embrace of the feathery fluff of these fine florescent feathers; twinned and coupled; paired and doubled; complementary and complete; now completely covered; blanketed beneath the Spirit of the Sky; the Soul of the Sea gather together to be the Two in the One who greet one-an-other as the Divine Twins they are and forever will be braided strands of Sky and Sea.

These Two who are One are bundled and bound together in the precious plumage of the Resplendent Quetzal-Qʼuqʼ and Lovely Blue Cotinga-Raxon; emerald green, turquoise blue as two become one in an ancient ancestral embrace that envelops as it embodies the everlasting life of the Jade Green Bead of Lifeʼs Eternal Return seen and experienced as the Sacred Golden Seed that shimmers and shines as the Great Star Venus who as the Nawal of Lord Quetzalcoatl changes and transforms into the Maize Peopleʼs Sacred Sustenance to provide and sustain the Maya from ʼNow to Eternityʼ which is to say ʼForever Moreʼ which is exactly where this Myth of the Maya begins and ends to tell you what lays in store for all of us who have ʼentered the wordʼ to know what the Maya always knew which is there is no Death without Rebirth just as there is no Life without Death.

body:
And so we begin at the end with Lifeʼs Eternal Return; Deathʼs undying renewal; and, Rebirthʼs desire to be nourished and nurtured to fruition in the Descendantʼs Face with its Ancestral Smile that shines bright in the Eyes, Nose, and Mouth of the Maya People who beloved countenance blooms and blossoms forth as an Ancient Ancestral Flower. This is the Sacred Story that will come to fruition here in this Translation and Interpretation of the Popol Wuj written for you.

This is the way Qʼuqʼkumatz received his name Quetzalcoatl which was bestowed upon him because of this Sacred Bundle of Quetzal Feathers preciously twinned with Lovely-Blue Cotinga Plumage; perfect complements of one-an-other.

Earth-Sky; Water-Sky Sea-Earth; Sky-Sea It is this ʼsacred bundle of feathersʼ that bears within its embrace the essence of creation as the resplendent jade green jewel of the maize kernel; the luminous blue mask of watery wet light; emerald reed, the jade seed, the turquoise bead that will soon to be brought forth from the shadowy darkness and into the resplendent light of the Soil, Sky, and Sea; Earth, Air, and Water; the dusty red dirt of the Earth, the rich resinous Cypress bows potent and powerful and explosive when put to the torch to create Ritual Altar Places where the Immolation of the Gods burn as the transforming essence of the Sacred Fire.

Earth-Sky; Water-Sky; Sea-Earth; Sky-Sea are all paired with one another just as the iridescent green, red, and white Feathers of the Resplendent Quetzal that complements golden amber, earthen brown, and obsidian black of Rattlesnakeʼs Serpent Scales to symbolize and signify the reciprocal relationship of Sky-Earth-Sea that will inform the telling of the Ancient Word from beginning to end.

body:
These Two beings of Earth and Sea; Sky and Earth; Sky and Sea form as they shape this Precious Twin of blue and green; turquoise and jade; gold and obsidian; silver and corral red; emerald and gold forms and shapes that are molded and modeled together to bring forth the Feathered Serpent; the Plumed Serpent; Quetzalcoatl; Qʼuqʼ-Kumatz whose Eternal Return will never come too early and whose rising as the Morning Star will never come too late.

Quetzalcoatl is a Creator Deity who also destroys as Heart of the Lake-Sea-Ukʼuʼx Cho- Palo just as his Divine Twin-Heart of the Sky is a Destroyer who will also create as Creator who is known and named as the One-Jun; the One-Footed-One known as the Smoking Mirror- Tezcatlipoca-the One-Footed-One-Jun Raqan-Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj spoken of here as Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

The Popol Wuj is their sacred narrative of Creation and Destruction who Form in order to Shape; Mold in order to Model; Make in order to Refine; Carve in order to Create; Sculpt in order to Shape in an Artist and Artisan World and Culture where the Aesthetic Drive is to create the Good and the True by forming and shaping the Beautiful all of which lead to Transcendence.

This Transcendence comes from a People of Maize who lived as a Pueblo of Maize People. The People of Maize of this Pueblo of Maize lived their lives formed and shaped by the Popol Wuj that is the Myth of the Maize People. This Myth of the Maize People known as Popol Wuj is what molded and modeled the lives of the Maize People whose Ancestors molded and modeled the Myth of Maize that they lived by forming and shaping this Myth of the Maize from the lives they lived; lives that were formed and shaped by Popol Wuj; the Popol Wuj that was formed and shaped by the these People of Maize that is a Pueblo of Maize People. I once asked the Maize growing in the Milpa where the Popol Wuj came from.

body:
This Milpa of Maize was in full bloom with its corn tassels and corn silk covered in bees and wasps of all kinds; little turquoise beetles and ants as well birds and hummingbirds were feeding off the bugs and the bugs feeding off the flowers. This Milpa of Maize was fully alive and so I asked it: where does the Popol Wuj come from since it is a Mythic Metaphors that tells the Sacred Story of your Life, Death, and Rebirth? And sure enough this living being known as la Milpa said very clearly under the bright sun and the buzzing bees: the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj comes from us the Maize Plants that are sown together to grow together as the Pueblo of the Maize People.

I was not surprised by I was overjoyed at the answer as our conversation deepened and deepened as the Milpa told the story of where the Popol Wuj came from and how it was written. This is the Way of the Maya who live their lives as ʼOneʼ with their Sacred Sustenance: Maize or Ixim which mean that which comes from-Ix the Nipple-Im of Motherʼs Breast. Ixim is the Sacred Sustenance of the Motherʼs Breast and all the many metaphorical plays that arise from this relationship between Sacred Sustenance of the Maya and the Maya who understood Kakawa- Cacao as Sacred Sustenance and Maize-Ixim as Sacred Sustenance.

Popol Wuj was formed and shaped by the Milpa; the Milpa that formed and shaped the Life Ways of the Maya; the Life Ways of the Maya that formed and shaped the genius of the Popol Wuj that was formed and shaped over Thousands of Years of the Maya living as One with their Milpa. We could speak of Cacao as well because Cacao is also spoken of as well in the Popol Wuj through mythic words and mythic metaphor. So realize from the beginning the Popol Wuj is grounded in the Sacred Reciprocal Relationship of the Maya and their Maize and their Sacred Relationship with the Divinities of the Sky, Earth, and Sea as well as all the different Deities that fruit forth from the ʼinter- connectednessʼ of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea or Kaj-Ulew; Cho-Palo from which the clouds are formed from which the rain falls and so on and so forth.

We are beginning at the beginning in the Primordial Water and the Dark Night Sky in which the Primordial Essence of Golden Seeds of Sustenance and Jade Beads of Life are bundled and bound in the Sacred Bundle of Quetzalcoatl. Now we will move towards bringing forth the Mountain-Earth from the Lake-Sea to rise-up and climb-out into the Heart of the Sky to form the Heart of the Earth out of the Heart of the Water known as the Heart of the Lake-Sea. We are deep into the Creation of the Maya Cosmos which tells as it reveals the Principal Metaphor of the Popol Wuj which is ʼRising-Upʼ to ʼClimb-Outʼ in order to Fruit and Flower into Abundance and Prosperity.

This is known as a Cosmogony because it is the Creation of the Cosmos out of ʼNothingʼ as we have already been told in beautiful mythopoetic ways. Without this Interpretation it would be ʼliterallyʼ impossible to understanding what is going on here unless you suckled the Popol Wuj from your Motherʼs Breast as the Motherʼs Milk that sustained and provided your life with Sacred Sustenance. The Maya knew the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account by heart so let us not pretend we can understand without understanding it within the Cultural Context in which it was lived.
