body:
The beauty of the Popol Wuj is that the more you read it and the more you allow it to ʼclaim your soulʼ then the more fascinating it becomes since every reading brings out different relationships depending on oneʼs age in life and the life passage one is moving through in life. Popol Wuj is meant to be read and recited; performed and played out year after year throughout life in order that it is entered as the Imaginal Realm where the Divine Ancestors are invoked and remembered all lifelong because the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj has something to say to all human beings; Women and Men; throughout life from the infant who suckles their Motherʼs Milk to the Great-Great Grandmother who prepares for Death by asking to be told a story from the Popol Wuj. Popol Wuj talks to us about life, death, and rebirth in ways that its Ancient Words always are meaningful for those who seek meaning through a profound connection through this Maya Myth of the Maize People that tells the story of the Pueblo of Maize and all that they said and did...

Popol Wuj is a manifestation of humanityʼs capability to create an artistic masterpiece that opens one soul to feeling all human, divine, cultural, spiritual, natural, and social relationship more and more while invigorating oneʼs life heart and soul; body and mind. Popol Wuj is true imaginative genius and you must know this from the very beginning; right here from the very start.

Great Knowers-E Nimaq Etaʼmanel-Great Sages were they, great was their genius; great too was their imagination for they were Great Thinkers-E Nimaq AjNaʼoj-Great Knowers whoʼs knowing thoughts and ingenious imagination were truly great.

For they were Great Seers who were Great Diviners who saw all there was to be seen to divine all there was to be divined; for they were Great Sages-AjNaʼoj- Great Sages who were Great Knowers who knew all there was to be known to do all there was to be done.

body:
Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Heart of the Sky Deity; Divinity; Kabʼawil Rain Beings; Lightning Beings; Thunder Beings Divine Storm Beings; Tojojila Divine Triplets who embody Heart of the Sky He who is the One-Footed-One known as Hurricane; the One spoken of as One-Footed- Hurricane Rain known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja who is the First of the Three Ancestral Deities of the Heart the Sky known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja who is accompanied by the Second and Third Divinities of the Heart of the Sky the Second of Three Deities of the Heart of the Sky is known as Mist Rain; Cloud Rain-Chʼipi Kaqulja; and, the Third of Three Deities of the Heart of the Sky is named Sudden Thunderbolt Rain or Green Lightening Thunderbolt Rain spoken of as Raxa Kaqulja. Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja is the most powerful Creator and Destroyer who is the Maya equivalent of the Toltec Deity known as Tezcatlipoca; the Smoking Mirror who will reveal when his essence and nature; condition and qualities are needed on a need to know basis as all other interpretive explications and understanding will be revealed.

These are the names you will come to speak in order to know as we step onto the path of ʼdecolonizingʼ our speech by adapting and adopting new ways of speaking in order to feel at Home in the World; a World known as Ancient Indigenous America where we will eventually come to live in a deep sense of belonging when we slow-down enough to allow ourselves to learn Native American ways of speaking Native American Language in order to invoke and enchant the Ancestral Soul of Native American World. This is the opportunity provided to the Reader; Reciter of this Translation and Interpretation of the Popol Wuj; a Mythopoetic text that names all of the Sacred Names of the Popol Wuj with both the English and Original Maya Kʼicheʼ Language.

If you wish to learn articulate the Maya Kʼicheʼ Mythopoetics then sound the Ancestral Names by following the Academia de Lengua Mayas Guatemaltecas pronunciation protocol and soon you will feel the strength of connection and beauty of communication as you connect with the Soul of the Maya Word to communicate with Soul of the Maya World through the articulation of the Maya Kʼicheʼ Language.

Decolonizing our speech takes effort but the effort made is extraordinarily gratifying especially because there is so much support at the tip of your fingers with the powers of the Internet and its many Kʼicheʼ Maya Language Learning tutorials. Best of luck and most of all enjoy the experience as we move forward towards a New World in which we will learn to assimilate Native American Languages into our lives to feed our Ancestral Soul with the authentic archetypal images brought to life through your speaking them into existence.

This is it; this is the applied art of decolonization in action as we open up to the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account in completely new ways.

This then was when his Word-Tzij; the Word of Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj came together here where Sovereign Plumed Serpent-Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz was in the Darkness-chi Qʼequmal; was in the Night-chi Aqʼabʼal.

This was when Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj spoke with Sovereign Plumed Serpent-Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz; this was when they brought their Word-Tzij together in Council; when they gathered together their thoughts to ponder their thinking; when they contemplated their ideas and imagination; when they considered their plans and possibilities.

Concerned then were they when they contemplated their imagination; when they consulted the thinking of their thoughts; there, where they came together as One in deliberation; there in the dark; there in the night when they found one another in the nocturnal darkness.

body:
These are those who are known as Heart of the Sky-Ukʼux Kaj; Heart of the Lake-Sea-Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo; these are those who are named the One-Footed-One Hurricane-Jun Raqan; Sovereign Plumed Serpent; Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo.

Divine Twins; Complementary Compare; Primordial Pair Ancestral Rivals; Ancient Adversaries; Divine Duality

These are those known as Heart of the Sky-Earth; Heart of the Lake-Sea; the One- Footed-One Hurricane; and he who is known as the Sovereign Plumed Serpent; those who are named Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja; those who are named Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz; spoken of a Heart of the Sky One-Footed-One Hurricane Rain Thunder- Lightening; invoked as Heart of the Lake-Sea Sovereign Plumed Serpent.

These are Two Principal Deities; the Two Primary Divinities; Kaʼibʼ Kabʼawil who will be the Creators and Destroyers of the Forming; of the Shaping that will be with us from beginning to end as the Ancient Ancestral Formers and Shapers of Creation and Destruction that will accompany us as the Divine Twins; as the Complementary Companions; as the Primordial Pair through all the Ages; all the Suns; all the Ages.

These Divine Twins are known in Mesoamerica as Quetzalcoatl and Tezcatlipoca who are Precious Twins that reflect One-an-Other as the Inverse Image of each other in order to act as rivals and adversaries in a relationship of complementary duality. The Smoking Mirror- Tezcatlipoca creates an obscure obsidian reflection of Quetzalcoatl whose name signifies Precious Twin.

These Twins are always act as Playful Tricksters but Tezcatlipoca is easily offended by those who do not show him high regard and great respect despite his rule breaking; boundary- crossing disruptive ways of creating the chaos that only he can bring to order in order to win a boon or reapportion sacrifice.

body:
These Two Divinities act as rule makers who are rule breakers in pursuit of creating a new order in the World of the Sky-Earth of their Creation and Destruction. They are always on the edge; on the margins; just out of sight yet looking in to watch everything that is going on while hearing all that is said in order to judge and justify what needs to be done next.

And so here they are contemplating their ideas and imagination to consider what must be done next to form the Earth to then shape the Sea and Sky. Here we are at the Cosmogonic Origin of the Popol Wuj with these complementary forces of Creation and Destruction whose desire and intention is to bring forth Providers to provide them with the sacred sustenance to then create Sustainers to sustain them with worship and reverence; regard and respect; prayers and sweet smelling gifts sacrifice that will be offered up to them through properly performed rituals of sacrifice on their Altars of Sacrifice.

These Divine Twins need their Sacred Days to be kept in proper ways in order to receive the worship and praise that they so hunger for as Divinities-Kabʼawil of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq. They are the most important Kabʼawil in the Popol Wuj so get comfortable with them since they will be our constant companions as they shape-shift as Nawales throughout the telling of the Popol Wuj.

So realize from the beginning these Primordial Mesoamerican Twins will act as disruptive Tricksters who will bring about the Great Reversals that change and transform one Sun of One Age to the next by acting as rivals who complement one another by collaborating in Creation to then cooperate in Destruction.

These are those ʼPrimordial Godsʼ of the Maya and Mesoamerican People who you will come to know exceedingly well so let us introduce them little by little until you know them as the Precious Twins they are who need one-an-other like the Night needs the Day; like the Sun needs the Rain; like the Sky needs the Sea; like the Earth needs the Clouds; like Maize needs Humanity; like Humanity needs Maize; like the Men need Women; like Arrogance needs Humility; like Kindness needs Acknowledgement; like Sacrifice needs Remembrance; like Descendants need Ancestors; like Ancestors need Descendants; like Princes need to be Tested; like Nobles need to be Mocked; like Youth needs Initiation; like Curious Young Women need Cunning Craftiness and Creativity; like the Ocean needs the Shore and so on and so forth.

body:
And so then it was made clear to them, just as it was revealed to them; when their hearts were made one amidst the light was when they took council together. This was when they became ʼOneʼ with the ʼOtherʼ; just the ʼTwoʼ of them there in the Dark; the two of them there in the Night; in the Water, in the Light; when their ʼTwoʼ became Just One: Xa Jun. This then was when the sprouting forth of People-Winaq was revealed to them; and so it was seen by them just how those Humans-Winaq would be brought forth into being-tzʼuqik; these Human Beings-Winaq were those who would be ʼbrought forth into being-winaqirikʼ as People-Winaq who would Populate- Winaqirik the Face of the Earth.

They knew as they thought; just as they saw as they imagined the way in which their creation would be brought forth into being through the clarity of their thinking. They thought in order to know; just as they imagined in order to see the way in which their creation would be brought forth into being through the transforming genius of their imagination through which-and with which-they were to bring life- kʼaslem to fruition through the creation of human beings-winaqirem.

This then was when they thought upon their ideas while they contemplated their imagination to bring the generation of human beings to fruition in order to bring the creation of life to completion.

For it was they, the two Kabʼawil known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj; named Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz who came to an accord as their ʼhearts became oneʼ there before the light of dawn-ta xkikʼuxlaj kibʼ xeʼ wi saq.

This then was when their imagination of the creation of humanity appeared to them as a clear image of the generation of life; a clear image of the generation of life that was revealed to them through the genius of their imagination; their imagination that revealed to them just exactly what they had to do to bring forth the creation of humanity on the Face of the Earth.

The image that was revealed to them through the contemplation of their thoughts and ideas was the image that they saw in their thoughts and imagination that showed them how to bring about the generation of life; the generation of life that brought about the creation of humanity: utzʼuquxik kʼaslem, winaqirem!

This was when their hearts where made one through their genius thinking- xkinaʼojij; their hearts were made one through their creative imagination- xkinaʼojij to reveal just how to bring about sprouting-forth of life to bring about the formation and generation of the trees and vines-utzʼuqik, uwinaqirik cheʼ, kʼaʼm.

This was made known to them through their nawal genius as the sprouting- forth of life that was the generation of existence that led to the creation of human beings who would come to fruition with the generation of the human lineages; human lineages that would come to fruition through the peopling and populating the face of the earth-utzʼuquxik kʼaslem, winaqirem.

This is what was being brought into being through the thinking of thoughts and planning of ideas by the Kabʼawil who were there in the dark; who were there in the night.

It is there, in the dark; there, in the night, when and where it was done by Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja-the One Footed One, the One Legged One; Hurricane who was the First-Nabʼe of the three Voices of the Thunder; of the Lightning; of the Water; of the Rain; Kaqulja as they are known; those who are divine aspects of the Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj who is known as the Roar of the Storm-Kaqulja; Cry of the Water-Kaqulja; Call for the Rain: Kaquljaʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The first of the three forms of Thunder and Lightning that called down rain was known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja. This was the first of the three shapes taken by Heart of the Sky that was the first form that Thunder and Lightening took as the first shape of the Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj; so that the first name of the First of Thunderers- Nabʼey Tojojila that was taken by Heart of the Sky was that which was known as One Footed One Hurricane Thunder-Bolt Lightening known as Call of the Rain; Voice of the Rain; Cry of the Rain: Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

Kaqulja his Voice-Kaqul; Rain-Water-Jaʼ his throat-kaqul; his cry-kaqul of water-Jaʼ; rain-Jaʼ so that his roar of the storm; his cry for water; his call for the rain; his shouting-out for a downpour-Raxa Kaqulja.

This is the lightning and thunder that always announce the arrival and the departure of the rainstorm that enters with Thunder-Lightning-Kaqulja and exits with Thunder-Lightning- Kaqulja thus the ʼnaming of the namesʼ of the Three Types of Thunder-Lightning: First-Nabʼey Jun Raqan Kaqulja, One-Footed Hurricane Rain; Second-Ukabʼ Chʼipi Kaqulja, Misty Drizzle Rain; Third-Rox Raxa Kaqulja Surprise Green-Lightning Downpour Rain.

Then came the Second-Ukabʼ who is known as Chʼipi Kaqulja-Misty Rain or Heat-Lightning Rain that accompanied the thick drizzle rain known as ʼChʼipi, Chʼipiʼ with its long drawn out waves of thunder-lightning spoken of as Chʼipi Kaqulja: call of misty water; cry of drizzle rain; howl of foggy storm; shout of the rolling-thunder that moves as a thick heavy wave of wet-watery-air over and across the Mountain-Plain; Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj.

Chʼipi Kaqulja, is the Second-Ukabʼ of the three Rain Beings, Lightning Beings, who are Thunder Beings that is the second-ukabʼ form rain-jabʼ, lightning-qoyopa, and thunder-kaquljaʼ takes as the shape that Storm takes as the roar of the downpour; of the weeping rain; or of the song of showers that fall upon the Face of the Earth all of which are known as the Three Faces of the Heart of the Sky-Oxibʼ Uwach rech ri Ukʼuʼx Kaj; spoken of as the Thunderers: Tojojilila.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Next came the last of the three forms of the Heart of the Sky; the Third-Rox shape of the naming of the names of thunder-lightning known and named Raxa Kaqulja.

This third one of three is just a blast out of the blue as an urgent invocation that is an astonishing annunciation of the sudden arrival of Storm Lightning with its downpour rain and massive thunderbolts that strikes as a bedazzling blaze of Green Lightning-Raxa Qoyopa. This type of thunder-lightning is known this Raxa Kaqulja because of its resplendent roar of this most powerful sort of Rainstorm Rain known as Tojil with its severe thunder and lightning that burst out of the Heart of the Sky to explode behind the house or on the road or under the Torch-Pine Tree as an explosion of Blue-Green Lightning to give Raxa Kaqulja his name.

Raxa Kaqulja then is a ʼbrilliant-raxaʼ, ʼshining-raxaʼ, ʼsparkling-raxaʼ sort of ʼsudden- raxaʼ ʼsurprise-raxaʼ lightning that leaves one trembling with the fear of death before these terrifying thunderbolt that is always experienced as a jolt of lightning leaving one with the feeling of just having confronted death through the immense power of life expressed by the vitality of the Heart of the Sky in this form of Raxa Kaqulja. Raxa Kaqulja, is the third-rox of the three-oxibʼ forms, three shapes that the call and cry for water takes that can sound like a weeping and wailing for rain that is often accompanied by the streaks and shrieks of lightning on the mountain tops that can be heard in the canyons and ravines the howl and roar; moan and groan that thunder can take when the Heart of the Sky wants to announce the coming of the rain by through the voice Nawales of Rain known as the Rainmakers spoken of also as Achijabʼ-Rain-Warriors; Rain-Men known as the Heart of the Sky- Ukʼuʼx Kaj.

body:
All three forms of the Heart of the Sky, Ukʼuʼx Kaj, descended down to celebrate council with Sovereign Plumed Serpent, Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz. It was they who came to think upon and imagine the Divine Life, the Sacred Life, the Pure Life-Saq Kʼaslem. For the time had come to bring forth the Dawn of Life-Saq Kʼaslem; for it was they who were called upon to bring forth the emergence of the Pure Life; Sacred Life; the Divine Life: Saq Kʼaslem.

Three Divine Forms of Lightning-Thunder Three Divine Names of Falling Water And so it was the Three forms of Lightning-Thunder that descended down into the Primordial Water where the forming and shaping of the jade green bead of the emerald green seed would be engendered by the Three Divine Forms; Three Sacred Shapes of Thunder that were the Three Divine Embodiments of Lightning-Thunder that wept and cried; called and summoned; screamed and shouted; roared and howled for all kinds of Rain: Hurricane Rain of Jun Raqan Kaqulja; Misty Drizzle Rain known as Norte of Chʼipi-Chʼipi; and, Sudden Green Lightning Downpour Rain of Raxa Kaqulja.

These then are the three names of the three sacred rains that are announced by the Thunder and Lightning of Jun Raqan Kaqulja; Chʼipi Kaqulja; Raxa Kaqulja. This is the ʼSky- Waterʼ that will come together in the Settled Water of the Lake-Sea to bring the Sacred Life-Saq Kʼaslem into being as the ʼSprouting Forth of Life-Tzʼuqik Kʼaslem and the ʼGeneration of the Trees and Vines-Winaqirik Cheʼ, Kʼaʼmʼ that will transform into the ʼGeneration of Men-Trees and Women-Vinesʼ that Sprouts Forth as the Peopling and Populating of the Sacred Life: Tzʼuquxik Winaqirem ri Saq Kʼaslem.

Saq Kʼaslem:

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Sacred Life; Divine Life; Precious Life; Hallowed Life; Holy Life For this was when the Kabʼawil known as Heart of the Sky Hurricane Thunderer- Hurricane Lightning-Misty-Wind Thunder-Lightning; and Sudden-Green Lightning that was the Thunder-Lightening of Downpour Lightning-Thunder. These Three Sacred Forms of Lightning and Thunder came together as those known and named Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja; Chʼipiʼ Kaqulja and Raxa Kaqulja; and it was they who gathered together in Noble Council. It was those three forms of ʼSky-Waterʼ that gathered together there in the dark, in the night; there in the Primordial Waters of the Lake-Sea where they talked to one another, gathering their thoughts, summoning their imagination, invoking their feelings for it was they who felt what they imagined as they imagined what they thought upon and contemplated as the emergence of the Dawn of Life: Saq Kʼaslem. Saq Kʼaslem is the Dawning of Sacred Life that would be experienced as that which is known as ʼCreationʼ yet spoken of here in Popol Wuj as the ʼForming and Shapingʼ of ʼthe Former, the Shaper-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitolʼ who would continuously ʼForm and Shapeʼ the Sacred Life- Saq Kʼaslem through the continuous movement of ʼCreation and Destructionʼ to bring ʼLife- Death-Rebirthʼ into existence. This is the Sowing and Dawning of all that is brought to fruition on the Face of the Earth as the manifestation, revelation, and expression of the Blessed Life, Holy Life, Sacred Life: Saq Kʼaslem.

Saq Kʼaslem would be experienced as the Peopleʼs Holy Life, as the Puebloʼs Hallowed Life; as the Vassalsʼ Loyal Life; as the Subjectsʼ Sacred Life; as the Noble Scribesʼ Pure Life; as the Oratorsʼ Enlightened Life; as the Writersʼ Enthused Life; as the Painterʼs Precious Life; as the Poetsʼ Inspired Life; as the Musiciansʼ Enchanted Life; as the Noble Lords Divine Life; as the Rulersʼ Beloved Life; as the Prayer-Makerʼs Blessed Life; as the Sacrificial Priests Pure, Pious, Perfect Life; as the Day-Keepersʼ Divined-Destined Life; as the Matriarchs and Patriarchsʼ Precious, Perfect, Pure Life; as the Divine Life of the Kabʼawil: Saq Kʼaslem.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so they thought upon their work of bringing forth their generation of life as they gathered together in council with one another to ponder; to wonder as they thought about the Dawn of Life-Saq Kʼaslem and how that Sacred Life-Saq Kʼaslem would be brought forth into being through their forming and shaping that would come to fruition in their formation; in their generation of the Precious Life: Saq Kʼaslem. This then was when they thought upon it to imagine it; imagine it to see it as they considered it and contemplated it with care and concern as which they were called upon to bring forth into existence as the Dawn of Life: Saq Kʼaslem.

How should the Dawn of Life be conceived? How should we imagine it; how should we see it to know it; this that is the Sacred Life; this that is the Divine Life; how should it be brought forth into Being as Precious Life: Saq Kʼaslem?

How should the emergence of this Precious Life-Saq Kʼaslem-that is the Prized Life to be conceived? How shall we think upon it so that we might bring it forth into being?

How shall we think upon it as that which must be thought upon? How shall we know it as that which must be known by thinking upon our thoughts of formation and germination of creation?

How shall we imagine it through our imagination so that we might imagine it as something to be brought forth into being as the formation of life; as the germination of life; as the creation of life?

How shall we come to see it through our seeing? How shall we come to know it through our knowing? How shall we come to imagine; how shall we come to see it; how shall we come to know it as that which is to be known and named as the Sowing, the Dawning: Ewaxibʼal, Saqiribʼal?

For is it not the Sacred Life that is the Divine Life that is the Precious Life known as Saq Kʼaslem that calls out to be formed by the Former-Tzʼaqol; that cries out to be shaped by the Shaper-Bʼitol? Is this not then when we must bring forth that which is known as the Forming and the Shaping of the Dawn of Life: Saq Kʼaslem?

And so it was that he, Sovereign Plumed Serpent known as Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz, asked Heart of the Sky known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj:

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“How shall it be done? What must be said to bring forth the Sowing; to bring forth the Dawning: Chawaxoq, Saqiroq?” “Who shall be the Provider? Who shall be the Sustainer?”

“Who shall provide for us as our Provider? Who shall sustain us as our Sustainer? Who will nourish us as our Nourisher? Who will nurture us as our Nurturer? Who then will be the Feeder; who then will become the Maintainer; who then are they who will be those that will do all that must be done to provide and sustain us?”

“Who then must we formed and shaped to be those who become our Provider and Sustainer? How shall they be composed to be completed; how shall they be molded and modeled to be made? How shall they be formed to be finished as our Keepers and Care-takers? Who then are they? Who then are they and how shall they be made?”

“How shall they be formed and shaped as those who will be known and named as Provider; those who will be known and named as Sustainer; Supporter, Maintainer; Nourisher, Nurturer: Tzuqul, Kʼool?”

And so then he thought; so then he pondered; the One who was known as Heart of Sky he wondered; he who was named Heart of the Sky Hurricane Rain Lightning Thunderer-Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

This then is when he spoke, when he said: “So be it! Ta Chuxoq! May that which calls be brought forth: Come Forth!”

“Imagine it so, think upon it like this: the water that is here, just take it away, just empty it out so that the Earth may sprout forth from a place that is flat; this place here that is flat like a plate; like a bed that is level; let it be leveled out flat.” “Like a bed then, just even it out, lay it like this, just lay it out flat; like a bed, make it like that; just even it up, flatten it out; flatten it out just so, so that we can bring forth the Sowing and the Dawning; the Sowing, the Dawning of the Sky- Earth: Chawaxoq, Saqiroq, Kaj-Ulew!”

body:
This then was when the Kabʼawil Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz; Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja; Chʼipiʼ Kaqulja; Raxa Kaqulja invoked as they enchanted their work of incantation as they brought forth their work of enchantment as the calling forth of the Sowing and the Dawning; there at the Dawn of Life with the Emergence of the Sky-Earth: Kaj-Ulew.

“Is this not the place?” “Is this not the place of our being shown high regard and great respect? Will this not be the place of our worship; the place of our veneration where we will be shown adoration by being remembered through rituals of remembrance; rituals of recollection through prayers of invocation and rites of incantation?” “Is this not where we will be shown thanks and praise through reverential acts performed in reverential ways? Is this not the place where we will be receive acts of reconciliation that are rituals of veneration performed with grace in ancient, ancestral ways through the ritual keeping and counting of the days by those who will be known as keepers and counters of our Sacred Days?”

“Will this not be the hallowed place where we will be given praise in sacred ways on our altar of sacrifice-uqʼijilabʼal; there before our ancestral throne-uqʼalaʼibʼal beside our altar place made of ancient stone there before of Great House that is our lineageʼs home where we will be nourished and nurtured; provided and sustained by those who are known as the Providers and Sustainers; by those who are named Nourisher, Nurturer who will be brought forth into being as the Formed Ones; as the Shaped Ones by those who are the Formers; by those who are the Shapers?”

“Is this not this Place? Are these not these People? Is this not the Place of Our Ancestral Throne-qʼalaʼibʼal-Our Place of Adoration? Are these not the People who will be the keepers of our Altar of Sacrifice; our Altar of Divination; Our Sacred Place of Keeping the Days-Qʼijilabʼal?”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Are not these the People who will be the care-takers of our throne place-qʼalaʼibʼal where we will receive of our veneration; where we will receive of our adoration by being shown high regard and deep respect for what we have done to be bring forth their existence through our formation and our germination of that which is known as Our Forming and Our Shaping of Sacred Life-Saq Kʼaslem?” “Will this place that we must bring forth into being and becoming not be the place of our Altar of Sacrifice that will be kept and cared for by our keepers and care-takers who well keep our lineage shrines-uqʼijilabʼal and maintain our ancestral throne-uqʼalaʼibʼal where we will receive our loyal subjects and beloved vassals known as our Divine Daughters, Sacred Sons; Saqil Al, Saqil Kʼajolom who will come bearing us great gifts of gratitude to nurture and nourish us with sacred sustenance?” “Is this not that place? Are these not the people? The Forest People of the Many Trees; the Forest People of the Many Vines; who have been brought forth into being; who will be brought forth into becoming through Our Forming, Our Shaping of the Great Trees, Great Vines; the Great Men; the Great Women who will be those who will be those known and named as the Provider; the Sustain: Tzuqul, Kʼool?”

“Let us bring them forth, let us bring them out; let us form them, let us shape them; let us craft and create them. Let us begin then with the conception and creation of the Forming; of the Shaping of the Formed Beings; of the Shaped Beings: AjTzʼaqʼ AjBʼit!”

This then was what was said by those known as the Divinities-Kabʼawil who were the Former; the Shaper of all that was brought forth into being to Provide and Sustain as the Providers; as the Sustainers; Nourishers; Nurturers; Supporters, Maintainers.

This then was when the Earth was made to sprout-forth; to sprout-out by them; by those known as Former, as Shaper; the Maker, the Molder of all that was brought forth into existence. Just their words alone caused it to sprout-forth; to sprout-out into being. To bring forth the Earth, they said: “EARTH!”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Chiwinaqir Ulew: “ULEW!” Xecha!ʼ Immediately, it sprouted out; instantly, like a cloud, like the mist, it blew-up, it erupted; into the Sky it did rise when the Earth rose-up it just climbed; up and up into the Sky.

This then was when the Earth sprouted-out of the Sea; immediately, it shot-up; like a Great Mountain the Earth sprouted-out of the Primordial Waters. It was then that it began climbing when it climbed-up and up into the Sky.

This then is the origin of the Face of the Earth-Uwach Ulew were the Sowing-Ewaxibʼal and Dawning-Saqiribʼal will be brought forth into being by the Kabʼawil who will act as the Former, Shaper who will embody the ways of the Creator and Destroyer of the multiple Ages and their many Suns that will ʼRise and Fallʼ through their ʼCreation and Destructionʼ of the Formed People; Shaped People who will brought into being and becoming through ʼCreationʼ

known as the ʼComing Forthʼ of the Forming; of the Shaping.

This is the Ancient Ancestral Account of the Maize People that begins here with the Sowing and Sprouting of the Earth that was sown in the blue-green waters of the Lake-Sea to ʼrise-upʼ in the Primordial Sky as the Great Mountain-Nima Juyubʼ.

It was just their Nawal-xa Nawal; it was just their ancestral powers of transformation; it was just their ritual performance of sacrifice-xa Pus that made it so.

Truly, it was just the way they thought upon the ʼsprouting-forth-xwinaqirikʼ of the Earth that made it sprout forth-winaqirik the way it was made to shoot-up- tzʼuqik and climb out of the Primordial Waters of the Lake-Sea. This was the way the ʼemergence of the Earthʼ was imagined to be by the Kabʼawil the Deities.

This then was the way it was brought forth into being to continue on to climb-up into becoming the Earth-Sky that is the name of the World in Mayaʼs understanding of the cosmogonic origins of the of Earth-Ulew and Sky-Kaj as well as the settled waters of the Lake-Sea known as Cho-Palo.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It was their nawal imagination of their magical formation-nawal- magical creation as that which they brought to fruition through their Forming; though their Shaping of that which they brought to completion through their Molding; through their Modeling of the Mountain-Plain: Juyub-Taqʼaj.

All of the sudden, just like that, the Face of the Earth was covered with Cypress Groves and blanketed with Pine Groves-ukisisil, upachajil-for Cypress Trees and Pine Trees sprouted forth across the mountainside. And so it was that a mantle of Cypress Trees was made to cloak the mountainside just as a mantel of Pine Trees covered the Mountain-Plain: Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj.

This then was when the Earth was made to sprout forth by them; those known to us as Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Lake-Sea; Ukʼuʼx Kaj; Ukʼuʼx Cho- Palo. Just their word alone caused it to sprout forth into being.

Sign, Symbols, and Signification of Secret Sacred Speech Myth and Religion; Twins and Twinship Creation and Destruction of the Forming and Shaping Every single word in the Popol Wuj extremely important and that is why I am ʼbringing them outʼ in this translation in order that the reader experience its Mythic Metaphors and Ethno- Botanical in ways that accentuate and ensoul our understanding of its Ancient Words as Mythic Metaphor. These are two of the most emblematic trees of the Many Trees People and so it is that they are the Nawales or Arborous Transforms that are the ʼTree Companionsʼ of these two major deities of the Popol Wuj: Quetzalcoatl as the Cypress Grove and Tezcatlipoca as the Pine Grove.

The Cypress Trees whose jade-green bows embody the long feathery limbs of the Cypress Groves-Kʼisisil. The Pine Tree whose golden-red resin of its ʼfat-wood or chajʼ is the very embodiment the Kʼicheʼ Deity-Kabʼawil known and named Tojil: he of the Torch; he of the Sacrificial Payment; he of the Torch-Pine Wood-Chaj. His name Tojil originates from Taj-Torch and Toj-Payment as in the Sacrificial Payment of the Sacrificial Debt: Toj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The debt of fire paid with fire; fire that comes from the Pine tree! This is the torch that will come up time and again as the main metaphor for the creation and maintenance of Burning Fire-Qʼaqʼ and Burning Coals-Qʼaqʼal that symbolize Power-Qʼaqʼal. This is the Mesoamerican World of the Sky-Earth in which Fire is Power and Power is Fire. Cypress groves are the embodiment of Qʼuqʼkumatz; Quetzalcoatl whose long tail feathers speak to us of the long cypress bows that bring the Sky-Earth to life while filling it with meaning through this metaphor of the Cypress Tree whoʼs emerald green limbs never die. And so we develop a deep, deep sense of belonging to a place where the Mountain Trogon and Resplendent Quetzal perch on the extended arms of Cypress limbs of Cypress Groves that flourish in Cloud Forests where mist and clouds embody Water and Rain.

The Pine Trees of the Pine Groves embody the Sun with its shimmering and shiny needles and resin that runs like blood from any tree that is left scored in order to be tapped. Here is where this Myth of the Kʼicheʼ Maya speak to us of the Natural World that form and shapes the Cultural World in which the Popol Wuj was formed and shaped to form and shape the Kʼicheʼ Maya who lived beside the Pine Groves and Cypress Groves with their Many Trees known as Kʼicheʼ to form the name of the Forest: Kʼicheʼlaj.

It is through living oneʼs myth that human beings live with a profound sense of feeling at home in the world; a world in which one is given a sense of belonging that is brought to life through the imagination of the imaginal world that one lives in. In this way myth comes alive through the connection and communication one develops with the Natural World and Cultural World as lived reality that is brought to life through the mythic words and mythic metaphors of the mythic experiences that are formed and shaped through the expression of the Mythic Imagination of Popol Wuj.

body:
The Kʼicheʼ Maya live with a deep sense of belonging to the Highland Forests of Pine and Cypress; Oak and Alder; Cherry and Elderberry; Corral and Willow Trees where their Ancient Word is brought to life by being brought into play so that those who live among the Pine and Cypress Groves instantly feel at home in the Imaginal Realm of this Ancestral Account of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ; Many Tree People; Many Tree Pueblo.

Myth is not something that symbolizes something else; Myth is that which creates purpose and meaning in life by creating connection and communication with Imaginal World that is a reflection of Culture and Nature as well as everything that lives there that brings to mind the Imaginal Realm of the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj. Myth then is the Imaginal World that brings the Natural World to life in meaningful and purposeful ways. In this way a person lives out their myth in a world that is ensouled by the Ancient Word and its ability to ʼensoulʼ the Anima Mundi-Ensouled World by ʼanimatingʼ it through mythic narratives; narratives that are the means of further soul-making of the myth-making Kʼicheʼ People of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo whose epic myths and mythic legends populated the Sky-Earth and Lake-Sea with Ancestral Soul.

And so it is that the World resounds with Ancestral Soul that is sown as the ancestral seed of creation here at the very origins of the sprouting-forth of the Earth; Ulew that comes into being through the ʼwordʼ of ʼcreationʼ.

This is the ʼforming and shapingʼ of the Former; of the Shaper that will ensoul and animate everything that comes into being from the very first beginnings; from the origin of a World that ʼsprouts forthʼ into being to continue on into becoming that Mountain Place and Canyon Country of the Kʼicheʼ Nation and their Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

This is how the Ancient Word of the Book of Council will ʼensoulʼ the Sky-Earth; Kaj- Ulew as it is brought into ʼbeingʼ through the ʼforming and shapingʼ of the Ancient Word and that Ancient Wordʼs transformative power to form and shape all that exists on the Face of the Earth.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This ʼnaming of the namesʼ is how the Kʼicheʼ myth-makers ʼanimatedʼ everything that existed when they brought forth the recitation of the Ancient Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj that was performed every year to renew the original essence of the Ancestral Soul that was first brought to life to be placed in the World of the Sky-Earth and all its beings through the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj. It is the ʼnameʼ that ensouls the being; it is the ʼnaming of namesʼ that ensouls all that exist whose Ancestral Name is filled with Ancestral Soul.

And so it goes ʼround and roundʼ as the ʼForming and Shapingʼ animates the World with Ancestral Soul through the Ancestral Words of the Ancestral Names that ʼForm and Shape; Mold and Model; Craft and Createʼ an Ancestral World fully animated with Ancestral Soul.

Qʼuqʼkumatz-Tojil Quetzalcoatl-Tezcatlipoca Jade Green Feathers of the Cypress Bows Torch-Pine Resin; Golden-Red Blood of the Sun Metaphor of metaphors; the long wispy feather-like bows of the Cypress Trees of the Cypress Groves speak of the long wispy tail feather of the emerald-green Resplendent Quetzal. These emblematic feathers embody the emblematic image of Qʼuqʼkumatz-Quetzalcoatl- Kukulkan that takes the form of the Maize Deity who is adorned with a Resplendent Headdress of jade-green leaves of Maize Leaves; Leaves of Maize that are embodied by a Headdress of Quetzal Feathers.

These Cypress Bows that wave in the wind call down the Rain Deity-Chak who is the principal ally of Quetzalcoatl. The Quetzal Feathers of Quetzalcoatl are ensouled in order to be embodied by a host of mythic images such as those mentioned here as: the Divine Feathers of Noble Maya Lords; Sacred Feathers of Divine Maize Deities; Noble Feathers of the Corn Tassel Headdress of the ʼwell adorned, well dressedʼ First Four Lords; First Four Fathers of the Maize People.

body:
And so it is that the Ancestral Soul of Quetzalcoatl animates the Cypress Bow filling it with Ancestral Soul so that Quetzalcoatlʼs soul lives on amongst the Maize People of the Pueblo Maize. And so too with Tezcatlipoca who take the form of Tojil who lives in the soul of the Torch-Pine Tree whose animate essence lives in the flowing golden sap or qʼol that is beheld by the Maya as the beloved blood of the Sun. This is what ensouling the animate world with Ancestral Soul feels like and it feels like it smells; and, it smells sweet. When one finds oneself amongst the Pine and Cypress Groves one feels the presence of Divinity as myth speaks the language of the soul so that instantaneously the world and one are filled with a profound sense of Ancestral Soul to enter the Ancestral Presence of the very Origin of the Formation and Generation of the Pine and Cypress Groves that cloaked the Face of the Earth with a fine Mantel of Trees in a Great Forest that is blanketed with a great multitude of trees; these Many Trees known as Kʼicheʼ provide us with a name filled with Ancestral Soul with a particular form of power that burns hot with beauty and strength.

Jade Green bows of Cypress; Emerald Green needles of this long-needled Torch-Pine that cloaks the Face of the Earth of the Maya Highlands from the Great Southwest of El Norte over to the Huaxteca of Northeastern Mexico to Copan Honduras Cypress and Pine climb up and out of Highland Mesoamerica all along the Valleys and Mountains of Central Mexico so that one feels at home in these resplendent forest cloaked in fresh smelling groves that remind one of where one comes from as a merchant-warrior or a messenger-ambassador who traveled on journeys that took them far from home yet made familiar by the forest groves of Pine and Cypress that grew all along the paths and roads of Mesoamerica.

body:
These Pine Groves that form Pine Mantles offer ʼlong flexible pine needlesʼ that are used for ritual adornment and ritual dress to blanket the floors and altar places; plazas and shrines of all Kʼicheʼ Maya ritual performance. These Cypress Groves and Pine Forests speak straight to the Mayan soul of ritual sacrifice and the living mythic metaphors that live on in the life ways of the Maya as Mesoamericans. The living Maya Kʼicheʼ language and the metaphors it forms and shapes act as a Mobius Strip to turn this forming and shaping inside out as the mythic language that was formed and shaped from ancient myth that forms and shapes the life ways of the Mayaʼs mythically informed lives.

Traditional Maya Lives that are formed and shaped by their Natural World that forms and shaped that language and its metaphors that form and transform the way the Maya live in the Natural World. And so it goes that the language of myth speaks to the realities of the Traditional Maya lives; lives that speak about the world through mythic metaphor that tell of the Ancient World and its creation and that creationʼs forming and shaping of Ancestral Lives that have been inherited as the traditional lives and world that are lived out as a reflection of Ancestral Myth and its metaphorical language within which the Maya have always lived.

The Maya Kʼicheʼ language transforms the Face of the Earth into a Sacred Landscape that speaks to the Kʼicheʼ Maya to make them at home in the world that is ʼensouledʼ and ʼanimatedʼ with the Ancestral Souls of the Ancient Ones known as los Nawales. These Ancestral Beings live in everything that exists in a Sacred Landscape that is completely alive and filled with Nawal Souls that communicate with their Descendants.

body:
This is how the Maya had always lived deeply meaningful lives; lives that were enveloped in the living soul of the Nawal Ancestors that lived in everything that existed up in the Sky, down in the Water and upon the Earth. This is why living out oneʼs life guided and protected by the Popol Wuj is a profound way to live oneʼs life for a Kʼicheʼ Maya lucky enough to live a Traditional Maya life formed and shaped by the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj. And so it goes as the language of mythos continues to be found in the Eternal Return of the Cypress Groves of Lord Quetzalcoatl and Pine Groves of Lord Tojil; Pine Groves of Jun Raqan Kaqulja; Pine Groves of Heart of the Sky who is the divine embodiment of the Sun.

Cypress Groves and Pine Groves continue to influence the Maya way life and its way of thought as the Kʼicheʼ language continues to structure the life ways of the Kʼiche Maya who continue to grow cypress and pine as the most favored trees for a Maya to grow in their familial forests.

Cypress Groves-Pine Groves Many Trees of the Kʼicheʼ Forest Many Groves of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom

The Kʼicheʼ Maya may no longer read the Popol Wuj but its mythic language and metaphor continues to exist within the Maya Kʼicheʼ language. Just as the Pine and Cypress continue to thrive throughout the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom as the principal trees who provide sacrificial offerings and ritual adornment for all the major rituals that are performed by the Maya in the Highlands and Lowlands as well as throughout the Cities and Towns of Mesoamerica were the Long Pine Needles and Resplendent Green Cypress Bows adorn all forms of Maya ritual and worship.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Without the ancestral presence of their refreshing scent Maya ritual lacks the essence of renewal and rebirth that emanates from the refreshing presence of Pine needles and Cypress bows. A Maya ritual cannot take place if it lacks this natural embodiment and archetype of synesthesia that springs from the revitalizing scent; regenerating look; refreshing feel; revitalizing taste, and restorative remembrance of Cypress and Pine as the ʼnawalʼ embodiment of the Ancestral Deities, the Divine Ancestors, and their transformative power to renew and restore life in order to revive and rejuvenate the world. Popol Wuj reveals as it expresses the way in which Qʼuqʼkumatz and Jun Raqan are made manifest in and upon the Face of the Earth as the Pine and Cypress Trees through their being Formed and Shaped by these primordial acts of creation of the Cypress Groves-Kisisil and Pine Groves-Pachajil. These two Ancestral Trees animate the Face of the World with Ancestral Soul that is then gathered to form rituals of sacrifice as they shape the rites of passage where Initiates enter ʼritual spaceʼ created with adornment bound and bundled; enveloped and embraced by Cypress Bows and Pine Needles.

The language of Popol Wuj brings forth sweet scents here to open its audience to sacred scents that shimmer and shine with resplendence will lofting ancestral smells that awaken our Ancestral Soul to those ancient ancestral times when these ritual acts of creation took place long, long ago. Pine trees with their long luscious sweet scented emerald green needles and Cypress trees with their richly perfumed flexible and fragrant jade green bows bring forth the experience of synesthesia that in turn brings forth the sense of renewal of the eternal return to a paradisiacal past of the Forest Dwellers. This provides the sense of the Pure Life that maintains the feeling of the Perfect Life-Saq Kʼaslem that comes through most strongly through the experience of synesthesia created through the invocation of these Primordial Beings of the Forest known as Kisisil and Pachajil.

body:
Ancient Ancestral Beings Kisisil-Cypress Groves and Pine Groves-Pachajil Qʼuqʼkumatz-Quetzalcoatl and Tojil-Tezcatlipoca These Ancient Ancestral Beings are the First Beings of the Forest of the Kʼicheʼ Maya who this Sacred Scripture specifically names through its naming of these evergreen trees of evergreen groves that ʼinstantlyʼ cover the body of the Earth with its green mantle. This cloaking and clothing of the living body of the Mountain-Plain with this cloak of Evergreen Trees is what wraps as it envelops the imagination with a sense of the Eternal Life that is created by these forever green Pine and Cypress trees of the Forests of the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo.

This is the newly born body of the Earth that has just been made to rise-up out of the Primordial Waters through the invocation of the sacred word. This incantation of the Sky-Earth and its being Formed and Shaped brings forth the Mountain-Plain that instantly calls out to be clothed and cloaked; dressed and adorned; ornamented and embellished with the Pine and Cypress tree covered groves of the Forest People of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. It is not their voice of enchantment that brings forth this magnificent green cape; green cloak over the Territory; the Kingdom of both the real natural reality and imaginal realm of the Sacred Body of the Sacred Landscape of the Many Tree People; Many Tree Pueblo of the Many Tree Place; known by the Kʼicheʼ as Kʼicheʼ by name: Place of the Many Trees. What is important to realize here is that this sacred text speaks of sacrifice in subtle yet straightforward ways through its words stating specifically that it was ʼjust their nawal powers of transformation, just their giving of sacrifice that made so; xa kinawal, xa kipus xbʼanataj wiʼ to then move immediately to the intimation and indication of the ʼMountain-Plainʼ being covered with Pine and Cypress Grove of Pine and Cypress Trees. These Cypress Trees provide the cypress bows of the long tail feathers of Quetzalcoatl of the Cypress Groves.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Whereas the Pine Groves with its Pine Trees provide the ʼtorch-pineʼ wood of the ocote or ʼrichly resinous fat-woodʼ of the Sacrificial Fire and Ritual Torch of Tojil, the Sacred Nagual- the Divine-Transform of Tezcatlipoca who takes the form of Heart of the Sky-Hurricane-Lord Storm-Tojil. These are those who are the transform or nagual of the One-Jun known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Jun Raqan-Tojil-Kʼawil who as an archetypal mythic trickster mocks all of those who attempt to define, thus control, his infinitely changing and transforming ways.

All of these Classic and Post-Classic Maya Divinities are always shown with a ʼtorchʼ burning forth from the center of their forehead. It is the Deity One-Footed-One Thunderer known as the Kabʼawil Jun Raqan Kaqulja who goes by the name Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj that will take on Four Divine Forms of the Four Directions of the Sky-Earth. And so it will be that the expression of the Principal Kabʼawil will become Tojil-Awilix-Jaqawitz-Nikʼaj Taqʼaj when we come to the Fourth Act; Fourth Section of Popol Wuj. Yet this future transformation is invoked here in ways that integrate the Five Acts of Popol Wuj in ritualistic ways to create unite where past Translations and Interpretations created separation.

These Pine Trees and Cypress Trees of the Pine Groves and Cypress Groves created ʼSacred Spaceʼ in which the Popol Wuj was once played-out as a Long Performance; Long Recitation that took place in a ritual space formed and shaped by Pine Needles and Cypress Bows in which the incense made from the Pine Tree transformed the mind while it woke the body and soul to Ancient Ancestral World of Myth and the Imaginal Realm in which it was brought to life through its Ritual Performance and Ritual Recitation enveloped in Cypress Bows and Pine Arbors that formed and shaped the Kʼicheʼ Maya sacred ritual space.

body:
Is this not the Place of our receiving worship? Is this not the Place of our being given thanks and praise? It is, it is, it is the place of the pine needles and cypress bows enveloped in clouds of pine incense that billow forth from the pine pitch and round balls of pine incense… This then is when the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account reveals as it tells of the ʼguidance and protectionʼ of Kʼicheʼ Maya Kabʼawil Tojil known as the ʼTorch-Chaj or Taj or Tojʼ to create the sacred name of Tojil who is the Lord of Fire-Qʼaqʼal-Power. Just as the sacrificial torch embodies the burnt offerings of sacrificial reciprocity that is given as a reciprocal payment of sacrifice-Toj that is given through the rich resinous pine-pitch offerings of Torch Pine that is offered up in rituals of sacrifice to pay the ritual debt that must be paid in order to bring about the ritual transformation of the Sky-Earth.

So realize these Pine Trees must have once been seen as the Nawal embodiment of Tojil whose golden blood is the golden sap; golden blood of the Sun that runs down from Pine Trees that were and continue to be cut open to be tapped for the rich Torch-Pine wood known as Chaj or Ocote and Sap-Qʼol that is so extremely important to Maya Fire Ceremonies. These are the sacrificial gifts that are given to the Kʼicheʼ Deities-Kabʼawil known as Tojil and Awilix when they must be provided with sacrifice in the specific form of ʼjust Resin-xa Qʼol; just Pine Beetle Casting-xa Rachaq Noʼj which is to say this Torch-Pine Tree is the embodiment of the Sun Deity from whoʼs wounds are gathered the pine beetle castings of the Pine Tree that are known as Rachaq Noʼj which are the ʼtailing of the Earth; leftovers of Geniusʼ that sustains the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew.

body:
Then there are the Cypress Bows as Nawal embodiment of Quetzalcoatl-Qʼuqʼkumatz which hopefully will help you realize that every single name and every single word that is found written in this Ancient Ancestral Account were transcribed in order to form and shape the Kʼicheʼ Maya mythic imagination and the imaginal realm that was formed and shaped by the Natural World of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom in which Pine Groves and Cypress Groves were Groves filled with Divinity that gave its blood and body as sacred sustenance to provide and sustain the constant transformation of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea. Thus this Great Mountain was enveloped in a great green mantel of Many Trees: Kʼi Cheʼ. This then was when the Mountain-Plain of the Kʼicheʼ was blanketed with a mantel of Cypress Groves-Kisisil that embodied the ʼNawal or Tree Companionʼ of the Maize Lord Quetzalcoatl known as Sovereign Lord Quetzalcoatl-Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz.

At the same moment of Forming and Shaping the Mountain was when the Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj; Mountain-Plain was cloaked with a mantel of Torch-Pine Trees that formed the Pine Groves- Pachajil of Tojil. These are the Torch-Pine of the Sun Deity known as Tojil who was named Lord Torch-Ajaw Tojil-Lord Lightning-Bolt; Lord Thunderbolt; Lord Storm: Tojil.

Cypress Trees and Torch-Pine Trees formed and shaped the bright green groves of Cypress and Pine that covered the Face of the Earth with a thick mantel of verdure to cloak the mountainside with resplendent emerald and jade green perfection. In this way the two Kabʼawil were made present in the form of their Nawal Transforms of Cypress and Pine leaving the Sky- Earth prepared for the forming and shaping of the Providers and Sustainers.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These Providers and Sustainers were those and are those who harvest the Torch-Pine by scoring its bark to tap its blood to impregnate its wood with golden-red sap. This is the sap and the ʼfat-wood or chajʼ known as ocote that is chopped away slice by slice without ever killing the tree. In this way the Maya make the incense that is burnt as ʼsacred sustenanceʼ in ritual fires in the round stone altars of sacrifice. Long ago the Cypress Trees gave-up their emerald green bows to form the arbors in which ritual sacrifice was performed on the stone altars of sacrifice. And so it was that Qʼuqʼkumatz-Quetzalcoatl the Plumed Serpent and Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Heart of the Sky were made to be forever present on the Face of the Earth. The Divine Twinʼs eternal presences was embodied and ensouled in the Cypress Groves and Pine Groves that blanketed the Mountains and covered the Plains of the Ancestral Realm of the Many Tree People. The Cypress Groves and Pine Groves grew in importance as the Forests of the Kʼicheʼ who know themselves as the Forest People or Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ. Now the Kʼicheʼ Forests are protects all across the realm of the Kʼicheʼ.

What is fascinating that those Ancestral Forests are spoken of right here in the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj where the Imaginal Realm Myth brings to life the fresh smell and fresh look of eternal emerald green of the Kʼicheʼ Highlands of Guatemala. Right here in the Imaginal Realm of the Mythic Imagination we see and we smell as we imagine the perpetual green of Cypress Bows and Pine Needles of Cypress Groves and Pine Groves of the Many Tree Pueblo those who are named Kʼicheʼ Winaq; those who are known to this day as the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ known as Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ for it is they who are those of the Kʼicheʼlaj: the Forest of Many Trees of the Mountain-Plain of Kʼicheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It is here at the very beginning of the forming and shaping of the Sacred Landscape that the Popol Wuj ensoul the Sky-Earth with the forest that cloaks the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom with Cypress Groves and Pine Groves that envelop the Popol Wuj in a mantel of verdure to invoke the eternal life of their Principal Deities: the Feathered Serpent and Heart of the Sky; Qʼuqʼkumatz and Ukʼuʼx Kaj.

So, then indeed it was Qʼuqʼkumatz who was made content for he felt great joy and so he spoke to Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj: “Is it not good that you have come, you Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj; You, Jun Raqan Kaqulja; and You-Chʼipi Kaqulja; and You, Sudden Green Lightning?” “Our Forming, our Shaping has turned out well,” they replied. And so it did; their Forming and their Shaping did turn out well. First, then was the Earth made to rise-up as the Mountain-Plain; Juyubʼ Taqʼaj so that next the natural course of the water found its way down through the mountainside to form the rivers and create the streams that wound their way down through the Great Mountain-Nimaʼq Juyubʼ when it appeared.

Double-Entendre:

Secret Sacred Speech Mythic Speech of Initiation of the Gourd Head People Secret Sacred Speech of the Tulan Tzuy-Wa Xchʼobʼochʼox ubʼe Jaʼ: xbʼinijeʼik kʼole je raqan xoʼl taq Juyubʼ xa chʼobʼol chik xekʼoje wi Jaʼ, ta xkʼutunijeʼik Nimaʼq Juyubʼ.

This is a fascinating sentence that tells us in a secret sort of sacred way about how the Mountain Tribes-Chʼobil Juyubʼ set the boundaries to their Ancestral Realms by following the natural course of the Water Ways of the rivers; Xchʼobʼochʼox ubʼe Jaʼ to set the limits of the Ancestral Lands of the Great Houses-Nim Ja.

Whenever a sentence is as ʼoddʼ as this sentence is to translate because of the way its ambiguous words and their meaning meander about it is almost always a sign that something else is being said on top of the surface reading.

Which in this case is a sentence that tells us of how the Ancestral Water Ways found their natural course by the way the water wound its way down the Great Mountain to show the natural course that the rivers and streams would take.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Which can be read as the waterways that course through the mountain showed the way that different groups who lived on the mountain were divided up according to the natural path of the water that delineated the borders that wound down the mountainside.

The mountainside that was ʼdivided-upʼ amongst the ʼgroups or divisionsʼ of Tribes that found their natural land boundaries by following the natural way the water wound its way down the mountainside.

In the Maya Highlands and Lowlands it was always the Rivers-Bʼe Jaʼ and Streams- Raqan Jaʼ that demarcated the boundaries of the Great Houses-Nim Ja. Nim Jaʼ meaning river which is a homonym to Great House-Nim Ja or Lineage that the Maya Scribes seemed to be playing with in a most serious way. This section continues on to make another double-entendre that plays on the verbal act of xwinaqirik to populate or to people and to create by saying the following: This is how the Earth; Ulew was peopled-xwinaqirik when it was populated- xwinaqirik by the Deity-Kabʼawil known as the Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Earth.

Which is a fine play on: This is how the Earth was created-xwinaqirik when it was created-xwinaqirik by the Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Earth.

The Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj was and is formed and shaped from a secret sacred language that initiates were initiated into to be able to read and understand it on its various levels of meaning; meaning we are just being able to understand today.

Let us continue with the surface reading to not complicate the meaning for non-initiated reader and translator.

Thus the Earth was created-uwinaqirik when it was made to sprout-up; when it was made to sprout-out-xwinaqirik of the Water by Heart of the Sky, Heart of the Earth-Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew as they are known.

They were the first to imagine it so: Sky was brought forth into being; Earth too was brought forth into being to then be placed in the Water.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Allow us to bring forth two alternative translation of this secret sacred speech of mythic incantation so that we might bring forth the original idea of ʼplacing the Sky-Earth-Water in their proper place that is brought forth from this sacred text that defies translation in every way.

A Multiplicity of Possible Translation of this Secret Sacred Language They were the first to think upon it like this: Sky was sidled-up to one-side; Earth was sidled-up upon the other-side to then be placed amongst the Waters. They were the first to imagine it like this: Sky was brought forth into being; Earth too was brought forth into existence to then be placed amidst the Water. They were the first to think upon it so: Sky was put in its place; Earth put in its place there amidst the Water. They were the first to imagine it so: the Sky existed; and so too did the Earth; the Earth that existed was placed in the Water. They were the first to have imagined it so; this then was when they rounded out the Sky; to then round out the Earth; to then place it there amidst the Water.

They were the first to think of it so; they separated the Sky and then they separated the Earth; to then place the Earth there within the Water.

These then where their thoughts; this then was their thinking when they reflected upon their work, their work of creation; when they pondered their work; when they considered all they had done; when they thought upon all they had brought to completion. This then was when they contemplated all they had done to bring their work to conclusion. This then was when their work of creating the Sky- Earth was brought to fruition by them.

Then came that which was called to be done next when they were called to bring their work to fruition through their Forming, their Shaping; their Molding, their Modeling of the Ancient Animal Ancestors who were called forth into Being as those that were to be Formed; as those that were to be Shaped by the Former, by the Shaper; by the Molder, by the Modeler.

body:
This then was when they thought upon their bringing forth of the Wild Animals of the Mountain Wilderness-Uchikopil Juyubʼ when they imagined; when they envisioned populating the mountainside with the Animals; when they thought upon their bringing forth of the Forest Guardians-Chajal re Kʼichelaj; when they considered and contemplated their populating of the Forest with the Keepers and Care-takers of the Mountain Wilderness-Uwinaqil Juyubʼ.

This was when they imagined the forest beings; when they thought upon all the animals of the mountains, the guardians of the forest, in this, their first attempt to populate the mountainside with the Animals; in this, their first attempt to populate the wilderness with Guardians of the Forest; Caretakers of the Wilderness who they imagined to be the many Animals Companions that would come to people and populate the Wild Mountain-Plain; Animals who would come to populate the Mountain Wilderness: Animals of the Mountain-Chikopil Juyubʼ- Mountain Animals, Care-takers of the Forest-Chajal re Kiʼchelaj-Guardians of the Forest; People of the Mountain-Winaqil Juyubʼ-Mountain People.

Before long their imaginative thoughts inspired their nawal thinking so that it brought forth images of Animal Protectors who as Animal Companions would come to reside among the Trees and Vines.

These would be those who they imagined would come to inhabit the Forest there upon the Mountain-Plain known as the Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj. This then is how these Guardians of the Mountain were named: The Deer; ri Kiej Bird; Tzʼikin Puma; Koj Jaguar; Bʼalam Serpents; Kumatz Rattlesnake; Sochoj Bushmaster; Kanti Protectors of the Vines; Chajal Kʼaʼm These would be the Guardians of the Forest-Chajal re Kiʼchelaj-Guardians of the Wild Mountain Places-Juyubʼal as well as the Valleys and Plains-Taqʼajal. It was then that the Bearer-Begetter-Alom, Kʼajolom spoke:

“Should there just a din of silence; should their only be a deafening quiet under the Trees and Vines? If so, then it would be best that they have Guardians- Chajal to watch over them!” said the Mother-Fathers; Alom, Kʼajolom.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Should there be such a din of silence; nothing more than this tranquil rustling of savage serene quiet; that incessant sort of horrendous hush in the bush amongst the brush; just the relentless roar of stillness beneath the branches of the fruiting trees and flowering vines with all their spiny thorns and many stinging leaves; was this the only speech that would ever be spoken here on this Earth that had yet to be awoken to life by ʼnaming the namesʼ of those who would become the Provider; the Sustainer; the Nourisher, the Nurturer of all that called to be fed and maintained there on the Mountain; there on the Plain?”

And so they imagined them ʼjust soʼ with hoofed footed ones and feathered winged ones; this then was when they spoke-up to then speak-out; their speech made it so, immediately these Forest Beings were brought forth there on the Mountain; instantly, just like that-jusukʼ-they were made to appear: Deer-Kej; Bird-Tzʼikin; the Four-Footed Ones, the Feathery Winged-Ones.

They instantly came into being there in the Mountains; there in the Canyons; down in the Ravine among the Trees and upon the Vines.

Then they were given their abode; the Deer, the Birds, they were given their homes:

“You, Deer, go down there by the river; go sleep in the ravines, in the canyons; there you shall live.” “Here is where you shall be, in the grasslands, among the wild fruit trees; up in the branches; out on the vines; in the forest, this is where you will grow and multiply. On all four you will move about; on all four you will make your way; this is how it will be,” this is what was said to them; this is what they were told.

So then next, they chose the living places that would become their mountain abode; a place down in the valley to build the homes of the Small Birds; Big Birds:

body:
“You, you Birds, get on up in the trees; there up above in the branches; up, up, on-top of the vines, make your nests; build your homes. There, there is where you will multiply to become many. There, there is where you will grow and increase; there on the limbs, there on the branches of the trees; out on the vines is where you shall be,” this is what they were told when they were spoken to; the Deer, the Birds; the Four-Footed Ones and those of the Feathered-Wings.

Tzʼikin the Birds that ʼCalled-out to the Sun-Sikʼij Kin as the Dog of the Sun; Tzʼi-Kin; Tzʼikin a Bird that cried out like a Dog-Tzʼi when the Sun-Kin rose-up at Dawn and fell-down at Dusk. Kiej the Four-footed one Kajibʼ Raqan or Kejebʼ to form the name of the Deer: Kiej or Kej.

Then they did what was theirs to do; while being given their sleeping places; their burrows; their dens; gathering what was there to build their abode; to design their dwellings, to fashion their houses; to finish their homes.

There in their forest they went to live; there in the wilderness is where they fixed-up their nests; burrowed their dens, and laid-out their lairs; some slept together, others slept alone; some lived with one another, others lived on their own.

This was the way the Animals of the Wilderness; Animals of the Earth were each given a home by Alom, Kʼajolom-Bearer, Begetter as they are known.

Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol-Former, the Shaper Alom, Kʼajolom-Bearer, Begetter Kej, Tzʼikin; Deer, Bird Alom, Kʼajolom were those who were the Mother of Descendants; those who were the Father of Descendants; Giver of Girls; Giver of Boys; Alom, Kʼajolom; Maker of Sprouts; Maker of Seeds; Alom-Maker of Sprouts-Conceiver of Children; Bearer of Children; Kʼajolom-Maker of Skull-Seeds known as ʼEngenderer or Sons-Kʼajolom; Begetter of Sons. And so it was they who were those known as Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom who completed their work of generating the Deer, the Birds; the Four-Footed Ones, those of the Feathered Wing Ones as they are known; as they are called; when they are invoked by name; the name that names them until this very day: Kej, Tzʼikin; Deer, Bird.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
When their work was complete; when their work was finished the Former, the Shaper; Bearer, Begetter-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom called upon the Deer and the Birds to do what they were Formed to do; what they were Shaped to do which was to invoke their Former; which was to invoke their Shaper; ʼTheyʼ who Formed the Deer and Birds were the Formers just as ʼTheyʼ who were Shaped the Deer, the Birds were ʼThoseʼ who were the Shapers.

The Former-Tzʼaqol, the Shaper-Bʼitol were those who Formed; were those who Shaped those who were the Formed Ones; those who were the Shaped Ones; AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit. Now Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom wanted to be remembered by being invoked by those they had Formed; they wanted to be remembered by those they had Shaped.

Now those who were the Former, Shaper; Mother, Father; Bearer, Begetter wished only to hear, in order to feel, their ʼnames being namedʼ by the Animals who they created; these who were the Deer-Kej; Bird-Tzʼikin who were those that were called upon to perform the sacred task of invoking their Former; their Shaper to remember their Mother, Father by ʼnaming their namesʼ of their Former, their Shaper; Bearer, Begetter-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom. And so they ordered the Animal People to do just this when the Animal People were called upon to invoke their Formers; their Shapers by ʼnaming their namesʼ to invoke those who Formed them and those who Shaped them as Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom!

This then was when they spoke to the Deer-Kej, the Birds-Tzʼikin; they were spoken to by Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom: “Speak out! Call out! Donʼt just squawk. Donʼt just warble. Invoke us: each one of you one by one; according to your class, according to your kind; according to your group, your order; go ahead now just Name our Names!” This then is what was said to them:

ri Kej-the Deer Tzʼikin-Birds Koj-Puma Bʼalam-Jaguar Kumatz-Serpent “Name then our names; show us reverence, show us respect; invoke us, name us: We, your Mother; We, your Father-Oj Ichuch; Oj Iqajaw!” “Go ahead; get right to it; you can do it; nowʼs the time for you to prove it! Go ahead, just do it!”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Go ahead; just do what youʼve been asked to do; name our names just like you have been shown to do:”

Jun Raqan, Chʼipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol Alom, Kʼajolom “Speak forth, speak out! Kixchaʼwoq!” “Invoke us; remember us; revere us; show us respect; show us regard; worship us in our way; this is all we ask you to say; just give us thanks; just show us praise; Kojiqʼijila!” “Go ahead, just do what youʼve been called on to do: Name our Names! That is all we ask of you!” they were told when they were spoken to-Xeʼuchaʼxik.

They couldnʼt do it; they could not speak like Former, Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol asked of them to; they just mimicked the sound and speech of others.

And so it was that when they began to speak they just squawked and screeched instead of making proper speech they just shrieked.

They just whined, they just whimpered; they just chittered, they just chattered; they just howled and yowled when they wanted to speak and so it was that they only growled.

They just kept up their shrill squeaking and sharp squawking acting as if they were really talking; they could only moan and groan each one all alone instead of calling out together the names as required of their Former; their Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol as was desired by their Mother-Father; Alom, Kʼajolom. So now it was known as it was clearly shown that the Animals could not and would not speak with one voice in one tone like their Bearer, Begetter had shown them to say: Alom, Kʼajolom.

The Animals could not speak amongst one another as they were asked to do: when they were asked to speak a common language that sounded true to the original form of speech that they were asked to articulate as a group; as a class; as an order with a single sort of speech that enabled them to communicate together as ʼOneʼ who could speak with an ʼOtherʼ to then ʼName the Namesʼ of those who formed and shaped them; their Former, their Shaper; their Maker, their Molder; their Crafter, their Creator.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
For it was no longer clear as to the nature of the language they spoke since each one of them cried out as they called out in different ways; each one with their own form of speech that was as difficult to understand as it was to speak as way of speech that one could repeat. The expression, the character, the nature of their language never came out clearly. Each one of them cried out as they called out in different ways; each according to their kind; all according to their group; each speaking the speech that was theirs and theirs alone to speak on their own; each in their own way.

When Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol heard them, they knew their work had not turned out so good, for the Animals could not speak as Alom, Kʼajolom wished they would and thought that they should if only they could do what they were ask to do; but they could not do what they were asked to do; as hard as they tried the Animalsʼ attempt to speak one language was just no good. So Former, Shaper talked it over together as they spoke with One-an-Other to then say what they said:

“The Naming of our Names by the Formed Beings we formed; by the Shaped Beings we shaped did not turn out well; this is just not right; just as it is just no good,” said Alom, Kʼajolom speaking together as close companions of One- an-Other; chi Kibʼil Kibʼ.

So, then, they said: “You must be transformed; you must be transfigured, for you did not turn out the way we imagined you to be configured: as those who would speak together in one form of speech. But you cannot speak one sort of speech together; you cannot speak with one another; like we speak as your Father, as we speak like your Mother; so why try anymore, why even bother.” “Now we must change our Word as to what is your Sustenance-Iwechaʼ- Food; your Nourishment-Ikʼuxun-your Edibles; your Sleeping Places-Iwarabʼal- your Hideaways; your Lairs-Iyakalibʼal-your Dens,” is what the Animals were told.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Now you have forced us to bring you down; we must change our word all around; we must change what we said about the way you are to live in the woods; the way you live in the forest must be changed for your own good.” “We must change your life ways, we must change your sustenance, your sleeping places, your homes, yours lairs; your dens; your nests and all the rest of your earthly abodes; we must change the very living spaces we gave to you as your dwelling places; your earthly homes; your residence here in the world on the Face of the Earth,” they were told.

“All that is yours will come from the Canyons-Siwan-Ravines and from the Forest-Kʼicheʼlaj because you could not show us respect and regard through the ritual keeping and counting of Our Sacred Days,” they were told. “Nor could you worship us by showing us praise through the veneration that is shown through the reverence and remembrance that comes with the sacred act of ʼNaming our Namesʼ as you were formed and shaped to do,” when they were scold by Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol. “You could not invoke us, nor summons us by calling upon us as we formed and shaped you to do.”

body:
“There are those who will come to do what we ask of them; those who will show us reverence through the orderly practice of our Ancestral Ways; the orderly naming of our ordered names; Ancestral Names named in perfectly ordered ways. There will be those who show us reverence by giving us praise in Ancient Ancestral Ways by keeping the sacred count of our numbered and named days,” said the Bearer, spoke the Begetter: Alom, Kʼajolom. “For there will be those who will provide for us with sacrificial offerings; offerings sacrificed to us that will provide and sustain us with sacred sustenance.” “So just bear your fate; this shall be your destiny for the rest of your days: let your flesh be eaten!” “Ta chuxoq! May it come to pass! Let it be so! This, then, is your burden to bear; this is your ancestral debt to pay; your divine duty to perform; your sacred service to be given by you to all those who will live from your being hunted till death to thrive from your flesh,” as it was said so they were told. This then was when the Small Animals, the Big Animals were instructed as to what was their fate when they were given counsel as to what their destiny was to be for all eternity here on the Face of the Earth.

This then was when they met their defeat; when their flesh became meat to feed the hunger; to satisfy the appetite of those who would eat their flesh as a sweet sort of treat.

This was their divine destiny; this was the sacred burden of the Animal People here on the Face of the Earth where the fate of the flesh of Small Animals and the fate of the flesh of the Big Animals was to be hunted and killed to be eaten as meat; meat to be eaten as the sacred sustenance of those ate flesh; of those who ate meat on the Face of the Earth; Chuwach Ulew.
