body: SO IT WAS THEN THAT ANOTHER EFFORT WAS MADE to bring forth the Formed People, the Shaped People-Winaq Tzʼaq, Winaq Bʼit; by Former, by Shaper; by Bearer, by Begetter-Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom. “Let us just try again; let us make another attempt; for is not the Sowing, the Dawning soon upon us?” “Xa kʼu tija chik mixyopij rawexik, usaqirik?” “Let us make a Formed Being that provides for us; let us make a Shaped Being that sustains us; one who nourishes us; one who nurtures us as Our Provider, as Our Sustainer; those spoken of as Nourisher, those named as Nurturer; those who are named Tzuqul, Kʼool as they will be known.” “If not, then who; who will ʼName our Namesʼ through our invocation; who then will remember us through the recollection; the remembrance of our ways here upon the Face of the Earth?” “Did we not already try with our First Forming, with our First Shaping? Did we not already complete our Molding and Modeling of those who would worship us by being and becoming those who would come forth to count and keep our Divine Days; those who would venerate us in beautiful benevolent ways; those who would regard and respect us by showing us thanks and praise as those who would become our Keeper and Counter of Days-qaqʼijiloxik?” “Did we not already finish the work of ʼCrafting and Creatingʼ those who would become our Prayer-makers and Worshippers to bring about Our Glorification before our Throne where we were placed to receive their adoration and their adulation; where we were placed on Our Altar Place to receive our worship and our admiration-qaqʼalajxik” “Did we not already bring forth those who would glorify and worship us with their adoration and glorification of us as our Prayer-Makers and Worshippers who would invoke us and remember us through showing us thanks and praise- qaqʼalajxik in ancestral ways through their worship and remembrance of us by Keeping the Sacred Count of Our Sacred Days in sacred, sacrificial ways?” “Did we not already attempt to make an Obedient One-AjNim who was a Humble One-AjXobʼ who was a Respectful One-AjXobʼ who was a Devout One- AjNim who would be those known as Our Provider; Our Sustainer those named: Tzuqul;

body:
Kʼool,” they cried out as they invoked the Forming; the Shaping of those who would become their Nourisher; their Nurturer.

A Second Attempt by Ancestral Deities A Second Try by Imperfect Divinities A Second Effort; Another Endeavor To Make another Effort; to Create in a New Way To Model, to Mold Mud; To Form, to Shape Earth; To Craft, to Carve Clay

Those who are calling out to make another attempt to Form and Shape the Formed Ones; the Shaped Ones who will become the Providers; the Sustainers are those Formers and Shapers known as the Divinity; those named Kabʼawil.

This is the Deity known as Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo. This is the Divinity named Jun Raqan Kaqulja Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ulew. These are those who are the Heart of the Lake-Sea; Heart of the Sky-Earth. Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz is spoken of as the Precious Twin-Quetzalcoatl- Sovereign Plumed Serpent and his Divine Twin-the One-Footed-One; Hurricane; Trickster Lord of the Great Reversal; Changer-Transformer of All.

These are those who are known a Creator and Destroyer that will continue on with the Forming of the Formed Being and the Shaping of the Shaped Beings whoʼs being formed and being shaped is invoked here in this next attempt; new attempt to Form and Shape Obedient Beings who are Respectful Beings.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
A Muddy Section of Weak Translation Soft Clay; Wet Earth without the Heat of the Sun They are not hard; They will come undone This next section of the Popol Wuj has the most diverse translations of anywhere in the entire work because of the slippery kinds of muddy adjectives and their sticky clay-like meanings purposefully chosen by the Scribes to receive a feeling and sense of this creation that perfectly describes this ʼfailed, faulty, and fallenʼ earthen man whose body is made of mud; this one man who is a creature whose flesh is created from mud and clay both known as xoqʼol that come from the earth; ulew. So this is an apparently simple section yet filled with complex meaning telling us what it takes to be a finely-formed and well-shaped ʼhumanʼ being. These extraordinarily ambiguous descriptive words have caused translators endless anguish and anxiety; worry and consternation because wherever one looks in the dictionaries you will find a multiplicity of meaning. The result being such that when you consult the translation you will find a great variety of difference which all meant to reveal something, I think.

I think, because I am not sure but I feel like our beloved Maya Scribes are trying to show us how failed these being are by finding words that fail straight-forward sense and understanding they are all words that can be used in a great variety of context to signify all kinds of different meanings. That takes a great deal of genius on the part of the Scribes; genius that they say this Man of Mud does not have.

Once again we are involved in ʼserious playʼ that is ʼserious word playʼ to bring about meaning by creating confusion and uncertainty around these failed and faulty clay beings from the Earth-Ulew where the Maya found ancient mounds along the Gulf and Pacific Coast filled with Clay Figurines that remind one of the simple clay beings described here.

So when you read the descriptions it is not at all inappropriate to think upon the millions and millions of clay figurines that the Mesoamerican World produced from the mud and the clay of the flesh of the Earth!

body:
“So then, shall we not try again?” “Let us just try again then to form and shape Obedient Beings-AjNim who are Humble Beings-AjXobʼ. Let us mold and model Respectful Beings who are Reverential Beings; let us make Devoted Beings who are Dedicated Beings; letʼs just shape Righteous Beings who are Reverent Beings; letʼs just form Dutiful Beings who will provide for us as our Providers; letʼs just shape Reliant Beings who will sustain us as our Sustainers: AjNim, AjXobʼ; Tzuqul, Kʼool.

This then was when they formed his body from Ulew-Earth. His flesh was made of mud-xoqʼol for it was mud that was the clay-xoqʼol that they molded and modeled the flesh-utyoʼjil of this formed being shaped from Earth-Ulew; this created creature fashioned from clay-xoqʼol; this Earthen-Man made of mud- xoqʼol. So then it was that it didnʼt look so good; Ma ku utz xkilo So then they didnʼt like the way it looked; Ma ku utz xkilo So then they didnʼt look upon it with contentment; Ma kʼu utz xkilo

Just lop-sided, deformed, incoherent, inconsistent; xa chi yojomanik Just soft, spongy, squishy, squashy, without character; xa tzubʼulik Just soggy, saturated, sopping wet, it could not move; xa nebʼelik Just so weak, without strength, limp, it just crumbled; xa lubʼanik Just one to come undone, it fell apart, it fell to pieces, it fell over; xa wulanik

And so it just dissolved in water when it got wet; xa pu chiʼumarik And so it just melted away; it became soft; it was weak; xa pu chiʼumarik

body:
His head was not round so it drooped to one-side; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom His head sagged so that he couldnʼt hold it up; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom Not being round his skull would never roll; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom His head could not swivel around; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom He could not turn his head; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom He could not move his head about; Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom Just in one direction could he face; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach He could just look in one direction; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach Just lop-sided was his deformed face; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach He just faced in one direction; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach His face was just immovable; fixed; motionless; Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach His face was still; stiff; stuck in one place: Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach He could only walk straight-ahead because he only looked in one direction! Just blanketed was his vision; Xa kuʼl uwach Just covered-up was his sight; Xa kuʼl uwach Just veiled was his face; Xa kuʼl uwach He could not see behind him; Mawi chi mukun chirij He couldnʼt see backwards into the past; Mawi chi mukun chirij He couldnʼt see what was coming up from behind; Mawi chi mukun chirij He couldnʼt look back; Mawi chi mukun chirij Chi chʼaw nabʼe maja bʼi unaʼoj; xa jusukʼ chiʼumar pa jaʼ.

He spoke at first but he had no genius; just right away he dissolved in water.

He spoke at first but without any intelligence; all at once he just crumbled; he just came to pieces; he just fell apart when he was placed in the water.

In the beginning he could speak in but without any insight; he had no genius; he just softened up; he just fell apart; he just immediately dissolved in the water.

At first he could converse but without understanding; he just immediately fell to pieces; instantaneously, he simply dissolved in water.

He spoke at first but without any genius; he just immediately disintegrated in the water!

“Heʼs not hard; he will not endure!” said the Former; said the Shaper. “Mawi Ko!” xechaʼ chi ku ri AjTzʼaq; AjBʼit.

“He will never last; he just isnʼt strong enough,” said Former, said Shaper.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
A Hard People; A Hard Life; A Hard Seed To Live is to Endure; To Endure is to Live Life is a Struggle: La Vida es una Lucha One can find remnants of this age of the Clay People buried in the soil everywhere one digs on the Face of the Earth. And many of the oldest ones from the La Costa Sur look just like the clay figurines described here with lopsided heads; looking in one direction; with no way to move their head; their vision blanketed; but very few of them fall apart in the rain or they wouldnʼt still be here after Three Thousand Years sleeping underground. If one is to survive a Maya Life one must be ʼHard-Koʼ because for the Traditional Maya life is a struggle: la Vida es una Lucha!

Yes, ʼla Vida es una Luchaʼ is something one hears all the time living among the Maya because anything of value is that which has been ʼwonʼ or ʼgainedʼ or ʼearnedʼ through ʼla Pura Lucha que es la Vidaʼ which is to say the ʼPure Struggle that is Lifeʼ and that is why one must be ʼhardʼ to ʼendureʼ which is a mythic metaphor that I feel as the Translator and Interpreter of this complicated text could not be more appropriate in describing the struggle it has been to bring forth this work of Translation and Interpretation as all struggle in life must be if one is live with the Maya with any sort of sincere solidarity leading to a deep sense of camaraderie and companionship.

“Just straight away, in an instant, the clay man became soaked and soggy when drenched in wetness to then quickly fall to pieces; it just dissolved in water. It was not hard; it would not endure.”

Endurance and being ʼHard-Koʼ embody the most important characteristic of all the important characteristics of a People and Pueblo who are milpa planting, maize-tending, temple- building, road-constructing, ball-playing, captive-taking, long-distance walking and paddling merchant culture. A human being had to be ʼhardʼ or ʼkoʼ in order to endure the water drenched ritual-performing, initiation-suffering, artisan-crafting, culture-creating, hard-working Maya people!

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
To be a strong Maya woman or man one must be hard and enduring like maize plants that must be able to endure massive amounts of water at the beginning of the rainy season and again when the hurricanes pour down on the world. Or enduring the heat and dryness of the early part of the growing season of the milpa when no rain falls yet the seed has been sown in the dry, hard grown.

Maize is a resilient plant that is known to be ʼmuy duro porque aguanta todoʼ since Maize is ʼvery hard, very tough because it can endure everything: drought, flood, wind, hail, insects, heat, cold, weeds, bad treatment but then when you help Maize she-he responds to come back to life in order to leave his-her replacements behind to live on as a Nawal Ancestor.

A Nawal Ancestor whose magic powers of transformation always enable the Maize Being to survive: ʼporque es muy, muy duro y aguanta todo lo que pasa en la Milpa donde nunca muere porque siempre aguanta todo, todo, todo lo que le pasa en la Vida que siempre es una Lucha!” Which is to say: “Maize never dies no matter what because Maize endures everything that happens to it in La Milpa; no matter what happens one must be ʼduroʼ because Life requires that Humans and their Maize are Hard-Ko-Duro in a Life that is always a Struggle!” Being hard and enduring is the essence of the Maya who never look back to dwell on what they suffered as a people in a world and way of life in which the Maya look forward to the future. Maya experience the present as the place to give thanks for all that ʼGodʼ or ʼKabʼawilʼ have given to them as ʼel plan de Diosʼ. This is a world in which ʼasí esʼ is heard all of the time: ʼthat is just the way it isʼ as it is said.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
One must be ʼhardʼ or ʼkoʼ like kernels of maize, like nibs of cacao, like long distant merchants and long-suffering initiates in the life and death struggle to survive rites of passage and rituals of investiture. These rites and rituals took a great deal of time and effort in which those who were involved in these ʼrites of passageʼ moved over long distant trade routes that cross the jungle, over mountain passes, to drop down into the cave world before continuing on through sweltering lowland jungles where those who found themselves in these life and death rituals of transformation were expected to walk in the elements no matter what they were; the freezing cold or roasting heat and most obviously through cold rain, sleet and hail that one might meet up with on the way.

This pilgrimages that were rites of initiation is what the Popol Wuj is moving towards and this is where we learn what is needed to take up the road of initiation on the path of young noble lords who walked the ʼSaq Bʼey or Sacred Pathʼ that lead to Lord Quetzalcoatl who sat upon his jaguar throne to greet Highland and Lowland ʼPrincesʼ who sought out the signs and symbols of Noble Power and Rulership found in the emblems of investiture. This is that story told here; a story in which Noble Princes needed to be ʼhard-koʼ to survive the rigors of the road. This was a road of initiation where sleep was difficult to find and taken under leaky palm roof huts during the relentless deluge of tropical monsoon rains. The lowland jungles were and are places were blood sucking gnats, mosquitoes, biting flies, ticks of all sorts, leeches, vampire bats and voracious beetles, biting wasps and buzzing bees, hairy caterpillars that brand one skin as bad as any burning iron.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This lowland forest where the Classic Maya Civilization thrived is where poisonous serpents and deadly vipers slither on vines and moved about like jungle roots to end the life of those who failed to pay proper attention. And all of this biting and stinging takes place in less than a heartbeat. One must be ʼhardʼ to ʼendureʼ a place with such a predatory nature such as that found all across the Limestone Jungle of the Petén, Tabasco, Campeche, Belize, Vera Cruz, the Huaxteca, and Yucatan. This predatory place includes by nature all the many wild groups of marauding warriors who enjoyed nothing more than raiding others. Now you are able to imagine this metaphor of needing to be ʼhard-koʼ in order to endure as a human being.

“It is just a sign of what not to do; itʼs just a warning of further failures that lie up ahead for this fallen creature crafted from clay; this earthen being molded from mud is just an indication of whatʼs to come! So be it!” “It is just an omen; he canʼt even walk; it is best that he never be allowed to multiply to become a great many more mistaken creations of clay.” “This man made of mud; this creature crafted from clay is just no good; this fallen formation is formed from a substance whoʼs essence is flawed by its very nature; using the earth to form its flesh is just a mistake; it will never endure.” “It is just another test; itʼs just been another attempt of our ʼforming and shapingʼ that has come to a bad end; itʼs just another flop; itʼs just another flawed and fallen work of our crafting creation; itʼs just another failure; that is all that it is.” “It is just a mistake; itʼs just an omen is what it is; just a sign; a premonition: xa labʼeq! So be it! We will just have to think it over again,” they said.

This then was when they destroyed him; this is when they threw him down; his Molders; his Modelers; they just took their clay creation up in their hands and brought him crashing down on the ground.

This was when they smashed him to pieces; this was when they laid him low on the Earth below! It was over; their second attempt had come to its end; they could begin again.

body:
And they did just that by asking: “What should we do now? ¿Jupa cha ki chiqabʼano?”

Third Try; Third Attempt; Third Endeavor To Carve Obedient Ones-AjNim; To Create Respectful Ones-AjXobʼ

To Form the Providers-Tzuqul; To Shape the Sustainers-Kʼool

This then was when they began again; when they wondered; when they pondered; when they thought; when they contemplated upon what was to be done next to bring their work of forming to completion; to bring their work of shaping to conclusion; to bring their Forming; their Shaping to Fruition. “What shall we do to finish our work to form, our work to shape those who will name our names; those who will keep our Sacred Count of the Days; those who will remember us; to worship us; and honor us in Ancient Ancestral Ways?”

This is what they said when they thought on it again; when they imagined it just so; just so they could bring forth Formed Beings who were Shaped Beings who would worship and venerate them by giving them praise by keeping their days while remembering them by invoking their names.

This was what they said when they thought on it again; when they imagined it so; this then was when they saw in order to known just how to carve and create beings who would invoke them by name.

This then was when they saw them again so that they would know how to form and shape those who would remember their Former; their Shaper and recollect their Maker, their Molder in Ancestral Ways of remembrance by ʼNaming their Namesʼ and giving them praise while keeping their Sacred Days.

This then is when they thought on their ʼFormingʼ and on their ʼShapingʼ again so that their Providers; their Sustainers would be brought to Completion; so that their Formation of the Sacred Life-Saq Kʼaslem would be brought to Conclusion; so their Generation of the Bright Life-Saq Kʼaslem would be brought to Fruition.

And so they went to the see the Seers who were the Diviners of Destiny. These were those who formed the Golden Maize Seeds-Ixim and those who shaped the Corral Red Beans-Tzʼiteʼ of Divination; these Diviners were Day-Keepers who were Seers who were Knowers who were known; who were named: Xpiyakok, IxMuqane; Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw.

What must be done to divine the fortune and fate of our Carving and Creating the Carved Ones, the Created Ones?” “Letʼs just do what we must do to consult to order of the Count of Days; to consult the order of the Ancient Ways; to consult the Forming of the Tzʼite Beans, to consult the Shaping of the Maize Seeds.” “Let us take up that which is the casting of the Sacred Seeds of Sacred Sight; let us take up that which is the casting of the Divine Beans of Divine Divination.” “Which is to say: we must cast the consultation of beans; the divination of seeds to see what shape the forming takes; to see what form the shaping makes so that we can know the form our casting takes; to know the shape our divination makes.” This then was when those who are known as the Ancient Ancestral Ones: Xpiyakok, Xmuqane; Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw cast and counted the Golden Seeds of the Maize Tree-Ixim Cheʼ, the Red Beans of the Coral Tree-Tzʼite Tree, this is when they said: “With kernels, with beans let us cast our divine-destiny; let us count our future-fate so that we may see the form, so that we may see the shape of the ʼfaceʼ

that our divination takes with the corral red beans of the Tzʼiteʼ Tree; with the golden yellow kernels of Maize Tree-Ixim Cheʼ.”

“Let us, let them make another attempt to see what there is to be seen through their sacred forming; to know what there is to be known through their sacred shaping.” “Let us, let them make another attempt to bring forth their Divine Count of Days; the Formation of its Ancestral Ways to see in order to know what form their Sacred Count of Days takes.” “Let us, let them form and shape their Divination to see what we seek to see; to know what we need to know; so that we come to see and come to know what we need to do to form and shape Our Forming; Our Shaping to Carve and Craft Our Creation of the Formed Ones; of the Shaped One; of the Carved Ones; of the Crafted Ones. Let it be done so it can be brought to fruition and fulfillment.”

“Let us; let them make another effort to bring forth their insight and imagination through their divination; through their counting of the divine count and through their shaping of their sacred shape that their divination takes.”

“Let us; let them mold and model their Ancestral Divination to reveal what is to be known through their powers of revelation that comes through those who are the Diviners-AjQʼij-Day-Keepers; the Knowers-AjNaʼoj-Wise Ones; the Mid- Most Seers-e Nikʼ Wachinel-Sages, those who are known as the Grandmother of the Day, Grandmother of the Dawn-Ratiʼt Qʼij, Ratiʼt Saq as they are invoked by Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; as they are remembered by Alom, Kʼajolom.” Grandmother of the Day, Grandmother of the Dawn-Ratiʼt Qʼij, Ratiʼt Saq those who are the Diviners-AjQʼij; the Knowers-AjNaʼoj; the Mid-Most Seers-e Nikʼ Wachinel; those who are known and named the Keeper of Days: the Nawal Ones; the Sagacious Ones; the Knowers; the Seers; the Diviners are those who are they keep the Sacred Count in the Divine Ordering of the Days upon which to offer Ritual Sacrifice is Ancient Ancestral Ways.

Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane: the Ancestral Couple Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw: the Primordial Pair Diviners; Formers; Knowers; Mid-Most Seers; Sages AjQʼij; AjBʼit; AjNaʼoj; e Nikʼ Wachinel; Ilol; Nawales; Nawinaq Realize dear reader that a great deal of exoteric knowledge is provided here in these names that are introduced without any explanation. So let us introduce again these Nawal Winaq, these Magically Transforming Ancestors known also as Nawinaq who take the form and shape of their Animal Companions, their Animal Souls, their Animal Guides, Spirit Guides of the Dead, Guides of the Dawn, Seers of the Dark, Knowers of the Night and its Darkness.

body:
These are those who ʼFeel-Naʼ in the World of the Sky-Earth where Feeling-Naʼoj is the Knowing-Naʼoj of the Knower-Naʼol who is the Seer-Ilol while those who ʼcast the golden maize seeds and corral red beansʼ are those who are AjQʼij-those of the Sun and AjBʼit-those of the Formation-Bʼit of the Divination. In this sense the Popol Wuj tells us of Divination being the means of Knowing what must be done next to Form and Shape the Providers and Sustainers. These are those Diviners and Day-keepers who come from the Ancient Age of the Animal People where ʼanima-soul-psycheʼ is the very ʼheart and soul of the words ʼanima and animalʼ which we must understand through our development of a Maya sense of the words ʼAnima-Soul-Nawalʼ and ʼAnimal-Companion-Nawalʼ if we are to understand how Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane work together as diviners who are connected to the Ancestral Soul and its Vision and Knowledge to find out what will be the ʼessenceʼ of the ʼsubstanceʼ from which they will form and shape the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings.

This is the Third Attempt at forming and shaping the ʼFormed Ones; Shaped Onesʼ with which to ʼpeople and populateʼ the Face of the Earth. For these Ancestral Mother-Fathers; Grandmother-Grandfathers work in pairs just as they work together as an Ancestral Couple. Xpiyakok will act as the ʼpillar-raqanʼ that stands beside the Diviner to support their Sacred Act of Divination and this goes on today amongst the Kʼicheʼ Maya where Mother-Fathers or Chuch- Qajaw continue to work together at their altar places where they do the ʼworkʼ of ʼforming and shapingʼ the knowledge and insight that guide and protects the People of their Pueblo.

Xpiyakok is the ʼpillar or raqanʼ and Ixmuqane acts as the Diviner-AjQʼij who is the former and shaper of destiny who scatters the seeds and shapes their formation to then count and form the seeds and beans in small mounds of seeds or small mounds of beans to create the ʼFormʼ that ʼDivinationʼ takes in this ancient practice of divination that the Maya have practiced since ʼtime immemorialʼ.

body:
These two Ancestral Diviners will be introduced and named as ʼGrandmother of the Day, Grandmothers of the Dawn or Ratiʼt Qʼij, Ratiʼt Saq and it is they who divine through their Ancient Ancestral Animal Soul, Animal Spirit that is their Animal Companion or Nagual-Nawal- Nahual who is known and named here as Junajpu Uch; Junajpu Utiw; One Hunter Possum; One Hunter Coyote.

IxMuqane is also known as Jun AjPu Utiw or Ancient One Grandmother Coyote; Ixmuqane as Jun AjPu Utiw comes from the Ancient Ancestral Place of the Reeds spoken of as Jun AjPu, Ancient Ancestral Place Thick with Abundance, Ancient Ancestral Place Thick with Reeds; IxMuqane in this section we are entering here is known as the Ancient Grandmother Diviner, Grandmother Coyote of the Dusk. Jun Ajpu Utiw is known as Ancient Ancestral Coyote Grandmother, Ruler and Authority of the Night, She feeds off of Death, she transforms as she wishes for she is the Trickster Deity Extraordinaire with Magical Powers of Transformation that when understood are at the very center of the Popol Wujʼs sacred narrative.

Xpiyakok, IxMuqane as the Primordial Couple of Ancient Ancestral Trickster Diviners are those who know everything there is to know because they come from the Ancient Age, Ancient Sun of the Animal People and this is what makes them such powerful diviners. As the Primordial Couple or Ancient Ones they are rulers of the knowledge of divination that is given to those who see in the ʼdarkʼ and live in the ʼnightʼ while resting in the Light of Day when the Sunʼs power overtakes the powers of diviners who cannot ʼseeʼ when there is so much ʼlightʼ. The Ancient Word says, “Let us speak with them that they might speak through their divination to know what we most need to know.” This is what is said of them; those who are Xpiyakok, IxMuqane who are Junajpu Wuch; Junajpu Utiw; Ancient Ancestral Possum Hunter; Ancient Ancestral Coyote Hunter who are connected to the Past Ages of the Past Sun.

body:
It is through the remembrance of the Past Suns of the Past Ages through which the Day- keepers and Diviners; Seers and Knowers communicate to know all there is to be known by seeing all there is to be seen in order to divine the knowledge they need to know to be able to do as they are called to do. This is the knowledge that will tell them what the Former and Shaper must use as the Ancestral Essence of all their Forming and Shaping of their Providers and Sustainers.

It was there where they looked with their ancestral vision to know and reveal what was asked of them by those who sought to see what they saw to know what they knew with their powers of divination.

These were those who were known as the Mid-Most Seers-Nikʼ Wachinel whose divinatory vision saw what there was to be seen in order to know what there was to be known to reveal what their was to be revealed. What they saw and knew was what they revealed as the knowledge they sought with their ancestral seeds and ancestral stones.

What they wanted to know could only be seen with their ancestral beans and ancestral bones that formed and shaped the form and shape of their divination. There divination that told them of all they could see and all they could know in order to reveal all they divined that was all that they was known.

All this knowledge was revealed with the casting and counting of the red corral beans and golden yellow seeds; ancient stones and ancestral bones that spoke to them in order to reveal all that knew in order to tell all that was known.

Day-Keeper; the Former of Divination Mid-Most Seer of Ancestral Revelation AjQʼij; AjBʼit; e NikʼWachinel This is what they revealed to Heart of the Sky; the One-Footed-One known as Jun Raqan and Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz; Sovereign Plumed Serpent when they were spoken to by the Day-Keeper; the Former of Divination; the Mid-Most Seer of Ancestral Revelation: AjQʼij; AjBʼit; e NikʼWachinel.

body:
These are those who are known as: AjQʼijabʼ-Day-Keepers; these are those who are the counters and keepers of the Sacred Days as well as those who reveal their revelations in Sacred Ways; these are those who are the Seers and Diviners of days that see and divine through their ancient ancestral powers of divination. These are those known as: AjBʼit-the Former of Divination; the Shaper of Divination; those who formed the shape of the small mounds of Maize Seed and small heaps of Tzʼiteʼ Bean that formed and shaped their formation of their divination that revealed the essence of the flesh of their creation of the Formed Beings; of the Shaped Beings.

These are those Formers of Divination-AjBʼit who form and shape small mounds of Tzʼiteʼ Beans-Palo de Pito-the Corral Tree with its bright red beans that were formed and shaped into small heaps; heaps that were mounds that brought forth their formation of divination; their divination that revealed to them what would be the essence of the flesh in their forming of the Formed Beings; in their shaping of the Shaped Beings.

It is just Golden Yellow Kernels of Maize and Corral Red Beans of Tzʼiteʼ that provided the Knowledge that sustained their Understanding of what they needed to know to form the body and soul of the Formed Beings; to shape the heart and mind of the Shaped Beings. These are those who are known as e NikʼWachinel those who are the Mid- Most Seers of divinatory imagination that is seen to be known as the inner-most vision of the seeing and knowing in the Ancestral Art of Divination.

These are those known as e NikʼWachinel who were the Mid-Most Seers that could see to the very core of the divinatory revelation that was formed and shaped by their revelatory divination. It was they who saw into the very ʼHeart of Divinationʼ to bring forth the Revelation that was seen there to be known there as that which was revealed as the Ancient Word that told just what was needed to carve and craft their next attempt at carving and crafting; forming and shaping the Formed Ones, the Shaped Ones; AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit who would become their Providers, their Sustainers; Tzuqul, Kʼool.

body:
Providers, Sustainers: Tzuqul, Kʼool. These Providers and Sustainers were those who would be brought to life by those who were the Formers, the Shapers of the Formed Ones, the Shaped One. These were those who were the Carvers, the Creators of the Carved Ones; the Created Ones who would do all that had to be done as the Providers and Sustainers; the Nourishers and Nurturers of their Formers and Shapers who were the Carvers and Creators of the Carved Ones, the Created Ones.

Divination alone was the Ancestral Way to be shown that which was known to be the essence of the flesh of the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings who would be Formed and Shaped by the Former; by the Shaper who would bring their forming and shaping to completion by first bring their divination to fruition through the forming and shaping of its ancestral kernels and divinatory seeds into formed mounds of ancestral bones and divinatory beans.

This then was when the two Kabʼawil; the twin Divinities known and named Jun Raqan and Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz spoke when they said what they said to the Day-Keepers and Diviners; Formers and Mid-most Seers:

“Just gather it together; gather the knowing that is the knowledge of what can be seen; just find the wood that we need to form Our People-Qawinaq who are the Shaped People-Qawinaq Bʼitoj those who are the Formed People-Qawinaq Tzʼaqoj-Our People the Sculpted Ones, Our People the Carved Ones, who will be our Providers; who will be our Sustainers-Tzuqul, Kʼool.”

body:
Invoke Us; Remember Us Maya Prayer-Making; Kʼicheʼ Day-keeping Midwife, Matchmaker-Iyom, Mamom “Invoke us so that we might be invoked by our Descendants; Remember us so that we might be remembered by those who are the Reverent Ones; by those who are the Worshipful Ones; by those who are the Loyal Ones; those who the Faithful Ones, by those who are the Devout; the Devoted Ones; by those who are the Dedicated Ones, Dutiful Ones so that we might be remembered; so that we might be revered and respected by those who are Our Providers; Our Sustainers.” Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane: these are those who are the Grandmother, Grandfather-Qatiʼt, Qamam who are also known as the Midwife, Matchmaker-Iyom, Mamom who are the Ancestral Couple; Primordial Pair who bring their Granddaughters; Grandsons into the world as their Descendants known as Iweey-their Descendants; their Teeth!

Iyom comes from Eeyʼom: Grandmother; Mid-wife who brings forth her Descendants; her Road-Bʼey or ʼEey which is the metaphorical essence of Destiny; Destiny-Eeyʼ that is Oneʼs Road-Bʼey or ʼEey that is Oneʼs Teeth-Eey; the Teeth of the Grandmother-Eeyʼom-Iyom-Mid- Wife. Eeyʼ then are the Teeth that are the Maize Seed buried within the Mother Earth.

These are the Ancestral Teeth; Ancestral Skulls sown as the Ancestral Seed in the Body of the Earth to bring forth the next generation of Maize that is harvested as a magical abundance of Maize Seed to feed those who must be fed.

This is how the Divine Ancestors of the Maize People bring forth their Descendants of Maize who are the Remembrance of their Ancestral Seed that was ground into the ʼAncestral Fleshʼ with which was formed and shaped; molded and modeled the First Four Fathers of Maize by IxMuqane! The First Four Mothers are formed from dreams; the First Four Mothers are shaped from sleep where and when the ancestral imagination crafts and creates dreams. IxMuqaneeyʼ is the Grandmother of Maize; Ix-She of; Muq-Burial; Kan-Maize-Eeyʼ-Seed or Teeth or Road or Destiny or Descendant. IxMuqane is also known among the Kʼicheʼ as IxMuqʼanil-Ix-She of; Muq-Burial; Qʼanil-Mazorca of Maize or She of the Buried Head of Maize; She of the Buried Mazorca of Maize.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is elemental etymology of the Ancestral Name of the Grandmother of Maize IxMuqane is more than enough to place you on the road-bʼey or eeyʼ of understanding her great destiny-bʼey here in the Popol Wuj where she will ʼbury the maize seedʼ in order to ʼDeify- Kabʼawilaxʼ Maize by planting maize after the Hero Twins Junajpu, IxBʼalamkej rise-up out of the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa to become the Sun and Moon of the Maize People. IxMuqane will bring the Sowing of the Popol Wuj to fruition with her ʼDeification of Maizeʼ with her first ʼFour Sowings; Four Seedingsʼ of Maize in her House and in her Patio in order to form and shape the sanctification of maize with which ends the Third Act-Third Section of Popol Wuj known as the Sowing; the Sowing that will open the path to the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Sun.

The Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Sun that will be watched and waited for by these First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom who will be the First Four Men molded and modeled in the hands of IxMuqane.

IxMuqane must be thought of a the Mother Goddess of Maize and the Grandmother of the Maize People; Matriarch of the Maize People who sow their ʼseedʼ in the sacred soil of the Mother Earth; the Body of IxMuqane. Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane are the Grandmother, Grandfather of their Grandchildren who are their Descendants-Ketal-Kitzijel who are the Replacements-Kʼexel of their Grandmother, Grandfather-Qatiʼt, Qamam of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq those who are the People-Winaq and the Pueblo-Amaqʼ of Maize; these then are the People of Maize; the Pueblo of Maize: Ixim Winaq, Amaqʼ Ixim: .

The People of Maize; the Pueblo of Maize-Ixim Winaq; Amaqʼ Ixim are those who live together in their Pueblo of the Maize People that is a Pueblo likened to a Milpa of Maize; a Corn Field whose ancestral story is told here in this mythopoetic incantation of mytho-metaphorical- mythopoetics that is a most sacred sort of secret speech known as the Ancient Ancestral Account-Ojer Tzij of Popol Wuj.

This is secret sacred speech I want me reader to understand to decolonize our minds in order to decolonize our soul by entering the word of Maya-Kʼicheʼ. The Maya Kʼicheʼ Language is that Sacred Secret Speech written as the Mythopoetic of the Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij that reveals as it tells of those who are known as the Ixim Winaq-Maize People whose Ancient Word- Ojer Tzij we bring forth here as a remembrance of their Ancient Ancestral Grandmother, Grandfather-Qatiʼt, Qamam; who are none other than Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane who are none other than those known as the Mid-Wife, Matchmaker; Matriarch; Patriarch-Iyom, Mamom of the Ixim Winaq.

This is their story and it is they who are the Diviners and Day-keepers who bring about this entire myth so it is best you develop a deep understanding of them here and now! Ixmuqane will form and shape the First Four Ancestors of the Kʼicheʼ Maya in her hands; the same hands that will now perform the forming and shaping of the divination that is about to happen in this difficult to understand section of the Divination of the Essence of the Substance from which the Formed People; Shaped People will be formed and shaped.

What will the Former and Shaper use to form and shape the Provider and Sustainer; what wood will they use to carve and craft this ʼnext attemptʼ of Forming and Shaping Obedient Beings who are Respectful Beings.

So now you are well prepared with ancestral knowledge that tells of IxMuqaneʼs divine hands that move over and about the Golden Kernels of the Maize Tree-Ixim Cheʼ and Corral Red Beans of the Tzʼite known as the Corral Tree with which she will form and shape her divination from the ruby red divining beans of the Corral Tree-Tzʼite; the Painted Tree-Tzʼajtel known as the Erythrina Corallodendron: Tzʼiteʼ.

This then is our invocation and remembrance; that is our incantation and recitation of the Ancient Truth; Ancestral Tradition known as ʼEntering the Wordʼ which we have entered here by ʼNaming the Namesʼ of the Grandmother and Grandfather of the Maize People who are the Principal Pair of Ancient Ancestors whoʼs Familial History is told right here.

body:
“Pass your hands over the Golden Kernels of Maize; pass your hands over the Corral Red Beans of the Tzʼite; just show how it is to be done; just make it so it comes out right; just reveal how to chisel it; just reveal how to carve its side, the side of the wooden plank; just tell us how to sculpt its face; sculpted face carved of wood; just reveal the way to sculpt its mouth; reveal the way to carve it out; its mouth; its face; the side of the plank; the face of the board-uchiʼ; uwach cheʼ; the mouth, the face of the wooden people; the mouth, the eyes-uchiʼ; uwach cheʼ of these wooden works of wood to be formed; to be shaped by the Former; by the Shaper.” This is what was said by those who asked the Ancestral Diviners; Ancient Seers; Primordial Knowers to reveal how to bring forth their Forming and their Shaping of these Beings of Wood who would be known as the Wooden Beings; the Wooden People; the People of Wood; the Wooden Works of Wood who were the Wooden People of worked wood; just whittled-works of worked-wood.

How would this wood work be done? How would they bring forth the Wooden Beings, these Beings of Wood who would be sculpted and shaped; scored and scraped; carved, cut, and crafted; fashioned, formed, and finished from the soft knotless amber wood of the Tzʼiteʼ Tree; the Corral Tree; the Whistling Tree known as Palo de Pito.

Palo de Pito; Whistling Tree Ancestral Tree: Mam, the Old Man, the Eternal One Spiny-Backed One; Caiman-Backed One; Crocodile Tree This is the Ancestral Tree from whoʼs wood is formed the Ancient One-the Ancestor, the Mam, the Grandfather whoʼs essence is embodied and ensouled in this Tzʼite; this Talking Tree who divines the future through the knowledge of the past. This Ancestral Tree that ʼnever diesʼ nor can be killed stands with its ʼcaiman spines on its backʼ at the very Center of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Cosmos of the Highlands while the Ceiba stands with its ʼcrocodile spines on its backʼ at the very Center of the Maya Cosmos of the Lowlands.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This then is the Sacred Tree that stands at the Center of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea where life repeats itself in cyclical ways; ways that can be known to be revealed through the cyclical turn and return of the Sacred Count and Keeping of the Days; the Sacred Count and Keeping of the Suns as they turn round and round to repeat the Sacred Cycles of Life, Death, and Rebirth on the Face of the Earth as is mirrored in the Face of the Sky.

These bright iridescent corral red seeds of the Tzʼiteʼ are the ʼblood dropsʼ of the Sun; the Ancestor; the Ancient One; the Old Man who walks his road across the Sky from Dawn to Dusk. It is then at Dusk that he ʼEnters the Waterʼ to be paddled across the Underworld Sea across the Night Sky on the White Road of the Milky Way. It is then at Dawn that he rises up again. It is here at Dawn with its Sacrificial Altar and Sacred Throne where his Day-keepers await the Sun as the Old Man.

These Day-Keepers who are Prayer-makers enchant the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew Lake-Sea; Cho-Palo with their prayers of invocation and fires of incantation that ʼname the nameʼ of the Day that will be taken up as a Sacred Road. This Sacred Road has been walked before on other Sacred Days just exactly the same as this day being named on this day in the Sacred Count of Days. This is the story being formed and shaped here through the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

This is a repetition of the original text to form and shape the divination a second time. This first part was the divination of ʼhowʼ the worked wood would be worked by carving and crafting the ʼwoodʼ to create ʼwooden works of woodʼ to then divine next what would be the essence of the substance that would be the ʼfleshʼ of the ʼwooden peopleʼ who would be crafted and carved from wood.

So let us repeat this ʼTranslation-Interpretationʼ as it was understood in ʼTwin-Waysʼ by those who were initiated into this Ancient Ancestral Cult of the Days that formed the Mythopoetic Basis of the Sacred Practice of Keeping the Count of the Divine Days through which the Art and Science of Divination arose to guide and protect the Maya.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This Sacred Calendar provided guidance and protection to the Maya as they made their way from one day to the next through the seeing and knowing that came from divination that revealed in order to tell what needed to be done next.

This Ancestral Practice of the Count of Days and the Art of Divination that is revealed here in the Popol Wuj is as alive and well as it may ever have been only now everyone and anyone who is called to this practice is allowed to take-up this ʼAncestral Roadʼ of the ʼKeeping and Counting of the Daysʼ.

The Popol Wuj will become a great fount of knowledge for Day-Keepers when they return to its mythic words and mythic metaphors in the Years to come and this is why I have added so much Interpretation to this Translation of the Ancient Word. Let us continue as the Ancient Word reveals the essence from which the Wooden People will be formed and shaped.

“Let it be done; let it be known; let the revelation be revealed through the work of divination; let the golden seeds of maize be thrown; let the corral red beans of Tzʼite be scattered to reveal just how these formed being that are shaped being that are carved being that are crafted being will be brought forth into being!”

“Let it be done, let it be finished by passing your hands over the scattered Maize kernels. So let it be done; just pass your hands over the scattered Tzʼite; …the corral red Tzʼite beans; the golden yellow Maize seeds…let it be seen; let it be known…” “Let it be done, let it be finished; may the golden kernels be thrown; may the corral red beans be scattered to reveal the essence of their nature; to divine the nature of their essence. What then is the nature of the flesh of their body; their body, their flesh; the essence of their being?”

“What will be the essence of the substance of the flesh of these molded beings; these modeled beings of molded and modeled matter. From what then shall they be made?”

Let it be done: “Let us let them perform their forming and shaping in order to divine the work of the Formers, the Shapers in their work forming the Formed Beings; in their work shaping the Shaped Beings.”

body:
“Let us let them try their luck; let us let them consult their Way of Seeing; their Way of Knowing; their Way of Divining; through the casting and scattering of the seeds; casting and scattering of the beans; the forming and shaping of the seeds; the forming and shaping of the beans; the counting of the seeds; the counting of the beans through which to perform our divination and all that it reveals.”

“Let them make another attempt at bring forth the knowledge; to bring forth the knowing that comes forth from the seeing and knowing of divination; in our effort to reveal what will be revealed through our revelation of our divination with it seeing and knowing of that which must be done.” “Let it be known; let it be revealed; let it be divined so that we may know what will be the essence of their flesh; the essence of the flesh of their bodies; the bodies of those who will be Formed; the bodies of those who will be Shaped into those who will be known as the Formed Beings; those who will be known as the Shaped Beings.”

They scattered a handful of Golden Maize Kernels of the Maize Tree, then they cast a handful of Corral Red Tzʼite beans from the Tzʼite Tree; then they began shaping the count from which they could mound-up the little mounds of counted seeds and counted beans. This is how they gave form and shape to their divination without knowing exactly what shape their divination would take. They performed their work by passing their hands over their work in perfectly Ancestral Ways to assure their vision was clear through which to see their divination to then listen to what its destiny said by revealing all that their divination showed; by showing all that their formation revealed.

body:
“Destiny, Formation; Qʼij, Bʼit!” called out the One Grandmother, One Grandfather; Jun Atiʼt, Jun Mamaʼ as they were named, those Old Ones, those Ancient Ones who implored and pleaded; beseech and entreated the golden kernels, the red seeds to reveal what was there to be revealed of the Forming, of the Shaping of the Wooden People. This then was when they spoke out to the seeds and beans to begin their divination of what they needed to find and to know; to go out into the ʼmany treesʼ of ʼthe forestʼ to bring home the wood they would work through their forming and shaping of the Formed Beings; of the Shaped Beings by the Former, the Shaper; Bearer, Begetter: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom.

Invocation; Incantation; Enchantment Speak; Speak-Out; Just Say It Make it; Mold it; Form it; Shape it Carve it; Craft it; Create it Here then, are the invocations revealed to form and shape these archetypal divination to get a sense of divination in English of a Maya Kʼicheʼ incantation of divination.

“Just go find it; just go feel it; to see it; to touch it; to hear it; to reveal it. Speak, speak out; speak out loud so we can hear it; to hear what you say as to what is the way we must go to see it; to then find it; to then go get it; to cut it, to carve it, to create it; to mold it, to model it, to make it.” “Go ahead and say it; just relay it; just feel it to reveal it so we can know it; to see it; to find it; so we can go get it; go on now and get with it; just do what is yours to divine where to find it so we can go get it; to cut it; to carve it; to create it so we can finish the work we first started.”

“Just tell us where to go so we will know just where to see that special sort of tree with this special sort of wood from which we will form and shape the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings; AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit who will be formed; who will be shaped by us who are the Formers; who are the Shapers of those who will be known as the Formed Ones; the Shaped Ones; those who will act out the Ancestral Ways of the Providers, the Sustainers; Tzuqul; Kʼool at the time of Our Sowing, at the time of Our Dawning; Ewaxibʼal; Saqiribʼal.”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“You, Maize; you, Tzʼite; you, Destiny; you, Formation be useful, be helpful by telling us what we need to know to finish our work; our work of forming; our work of shaping that we must bring to fruition; the work we must bring to completion.”

This is what was said to the Maize Seeds; the Tzʼite Beans to bring forth the Divination; the Formation; Qʼij; Bʼit as it is known to those who are the Day- Keepers who are the Diviners; the Diviners who are the Shapers of Divination: AjQʼijʼ AjBʼit.

And so it was that the Men were formed from the wood of the Tzʼiteʼ Tree where as the Women were shaped from bundles of Reeds that were gathered amongst the Rushes-Sibʼaq as there are known; the Reeds that grow in the Rushes beside the Lakeshore of the Great Water; Nim Ya; Nim Jaʼ.

The Wooden People were now called forth as they were invoked as Men carved from Worked Wood-Ajam Cheʼ; as Women crafted from Bundled Reeds- Poy-Scarecrow Beings. These Men of Wood and Women of Reeds were known together as Adorned Decoys-Poy and Worked-Wood or Ajam Cheʼ translated here as the Wooden People.

Xpiyakok: AjTzʼite Old Man: Ancestral Grandfather of the Maize People Ixmuqane: AjQʼiij Old Woman: Ancestral Grandmother of the Maize People

That Grandfather was known as an AjTzʼite, a Diviner, a Seer, the Old Man-Mam of the Tzʼite Tree; his name Xpiyakok, the First Father-Grandfather of the Maize People. His complement and companion who was his primordial partner was the one known as Our Grandmother-Qatiʼt and it is she who was an AjQʼiij, a Diviner, a Day-keeper who is spoken of as the Old Woman, Atiʼt; the First Mother-Grandmother of the Maize People: Ixmuqane. Yet here she is known and named as the Pillar-Raqan-Post of their divination. Ixmuqane, she is designated as the One Foot-Raqan-One Leg that stands strong next to her partner the Former, Shaper of this Divination known as AjTzʼite-He of Authority, Rule, Insight, Knowledge;

body:
He of the Tzʼiteʼ; He of the Talking Tree: Tzʼi Teʼ for this tree is a tree that speaks to its owner like a Dog-Tzʼi who speaks through the bark, leaves, wood, flowers, and seeds of this magical transforming tree Tzʼite by name; known by the Traditional Maya as both Friend-Enemy; Amigo-Enemigo.

This Ancestral Tree of Speaking Wood is known as Tzʼite in Maya Kʼicheʼ; in Maya Tzʼutujil this Palo de Pito or Whistle Tree is known as Tzʼajtel the ʼPainted Tree for its brilliant red bean. Its elongated flowers call in the Hummingbird making it the House of the Sun. Those same flowers are transformed into whistles just as its beans are said to ʼwhistle in order to speakʼ when thrown in the fire. Its leaves can be eaten in times of hardship while its bark produces a sedative effect to induce sleep and dreams to guide Seers and reveal knowledge to Diviners who seek visions and insights in their Tzʼite induced dreams. The Tzʼiteʼ is truly an Ancestral Tree that is a Nawal Cheʼ a Magical Transforming Tree indeed.

Tzʼite signifies the Canine Tree or Dog Tree who manifests a natural sense of Rule and Authority over the Land. The Maya domesticated the ʼdog as canineʼ as in the taking of the ʼpupsʼ of the wolf and coyote and fox and escuintle and other canine we no longer know as ʼwild dogsʼ who lived on the threshold of the Maya Villages and their Milpa and its Forests and Fields. These canines embodied the ways of the People of the Pueblo they lived alongside of just as they enacted the thoughts of their ʼdueñosʼ in nawal ways which is to say humans and canines communicate with one another to provide and sustain one another with sustenance in all the many forms sustenance takes.

body: Canines and Human Beings formed a bond early on in the Mesoamerican World where they spoke to one another through the whistle speech of the Tzʼiteʼ Tree. All the many forms and shapes that canines take were important to the Maya as they lived their lives beside the Forest and inside their beloved Milpa where dogs were used to protect the Mayaʼs sacred sustenance of maize, bean, squash, and chili. Canines were known as Ancestral Beings or Nawales who embodied the Principal Deities of the Mesoamerican Cosmos. Especially the Coyote-Utiw who is the Nagual or Animal Transform of Tezcatlipoca; the Smoking Mirror known here in Popol Wuj as the One-Footed-One-Hurricane-Jun Raqan Kaqulja, the Very Heart of the Sky; el Mero Corazón del Cielo; the Very Heart of Heaven as some folks name the name of this ʼCelestial Mindʼ whoʼs divine voice guided and protected his people as they made their way through life lived on the Face of the Earth. Junajpu Utiw you might remember is one of the ancestral patriarchs of the First Sun of the Animal People; it is he who can devour sustenance that is both living and dead.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Spiny Tree: Pillar of the Sky-Earth Heart of the Sky-Heart of the Earth Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ukʼuʼx Ulewʼ Tzʼite: Tree of Authority Junajpu Coyote; Junajpu Utiw So realize that this Tzʼite Tree is the Tree of Authority just as it is the embodiment of the spirit and soul of Ukʼuʼx Kaj as Junajpu Coyote; Junajpu Utiw. This is to say, ʼthe Tzʼiteʼ Tree is the embodiment and ensoulment of the Heart of the Earth; Heart of the Sky just as the Reeds and Rushes are the embodiment and ensoulment of the Heart of the Lake-Heart of the Sea. In this way the Primordial Deities of the Popol Wuj are lived out through their forming and shaping of themselves through the embodiment of themselves in nature as the Worked-Wood of the Tzʼiteʼ Tree and the Bundled Reeds of the Lakeshore Rushes known as Sibʼaq here in the Popol Wuj. All of which provides ʼHeart of the Sky-Heart of the Earth; Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ukʼuʼx Ulewʼ with great authority over the Sky-Earth as well as the ʼcreation and destructionʼ that will happen there. This First Sun of the Popol Wuj is the Sun of Quetzalcoatl with its Animal People in which Junajpu Wuch-Ancient Ancestral Possum is the Nagual of Quetzalcoatl who is the Precious Twin of Tezcatlipoca who is known in Popol Wuj as Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja who comes to life through his Ancestral Nagual Junajpu Utiw the Ancient Ancestral Coyote; Coyote who is the Nagual of Tezcatlipoca.

Popol Wuj is a magical transforming myth of the Maya that is formed and shaped with endless plays of its Principal Deities transforming from one entity into another. So I am trying my best to awaken this transformative play right here so you come to understand the ʼacts of creation and destructionʼ as the ʼdivine playʼ of the Divinities known to you well by now as Kabʼawil who change and transform in infinite and endless ways. Possum is the Lord of the Dawn; Coyote is the Lord of the Dusk and it is they who are called upon here to participate in the divination of Xpiyakok and Ixmuqane that seeks to see in order to know in order to reveal where they must go to find the essence of the substance of the flesh from which will be carved and crafted the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This search here will be taken up again when the Former; Shaper known as Tzʼaqol; Bʼitol seek out the knowledge that reveals to them what substance must be used to mold and model the Beings of Wood; Beings of Reeds; Beings of Clay; Beings of Animal Flesh all of which are failed and fallen creations that must be destroyed. It is only when the Yellow Maize; White Maize are found that the flesh of the Maize Beings is formed and shaped out of ground maize. Ixmuqane will be guided by the Fox and Coyote; Parquet and Crow to the Mountain of Sustenance known as Meʼawan where the treasure chest of sweet sustenance is found in the two Mountain Places known as Pan Paxil; Pan Kayala where they will find the Maize that will be ground nine times to then be used as the flesh of the Maize People. This divination that seeks to find the essence of Human Flesh begins right here with Junajpu Wuch; Junajpu Utiw who assist Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane in their Forming and Shaping of their Divination. The Wooden Men of this Third Age of Formed Beings; Shaped Beings will be carved and crafted out of Tzʼiteʼ wood because the Tzʼiteʼ is a tree that communicates extraordinarily well as a Nawal or Nagual of the Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Earth. Tzʼite is a Tree with sharp senses that gives ʼhimʼ the power of ʼknowingʼ like all Canines that live in Packs; Canines that must be understood as the Wolf, the Fox, the Coyote, the Escuintle, and any number of other Indigenous Canines of the Americas we have no idea of anymore since all that sort of knowledge of Indigenous America has been erased through the destructive powers European Conquest and Colonization of Indigenous American. The Dog-Tzʼi is a nawal animal that was painted by the Maya as life-loving companions of human being. The dog like the tree named after it was deeply revered by the Maya because of their ingenious way of being able to understand the thoughts and intentions; as well as the gestures and language of Human Beings.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This most ingenious ancestral being known as the ʼDog-Tzʼiʼ is both a friend and an enemy of human beings; a kind and affectionate companion; a faithful and loyal friend or can be a bitter foe, a vicious rival; a fierce and ferocious adversary. But it is here in the Popol Wuj that ʼheʼ acts as trusty companion who ʼguidesʼ and ʼprotectsʼ one on the road; who ʼdefendsʼ and ʼleadsʼ one in the dark of night and the foggy drizzle of the mountainside.

Dogs are a Huntersʼ guide and protector; Dogs are the Merchantsʼ guide and protector; Dogs are the guides and protectors of Grandmother, Grandfather; Granddaughter, Grandsons so that in this sense of being guide and protector a Dog is exactly like a Kabʼawil so that a Dog must be seen as exactly like the Nagual of the Kabʼawil because the Dog is the Animal Transform; Animal Companion of who acts divine in the prescient way it knows what will happen next.

Dogs act just as divinity and humanity act when they communicate with one another through their intuitive intelligent sort of ancestral genius so much so that the Divine Ancestors and their Human Descendants work together in complementary companionship as Divine Twins; not unlike Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz and Jun Raqan Kaqulja; not unlike the Wooden Women formed from bundled reeds and rushes; not unlike the Wooden Men shaped from the carved wood of the Tzʼiteʼ Tree.

There is more going on here amongst the Kabʼawil as Divinities who seek to complement one another through their magical powers of transformation known as being ʼnawalʼ in every way. But these Kabʼawil cannot ʼseeʼ to ʼknowʼ in order to ʼrevealʼ what must be done next and so it is that the Original Maya Kʼicheʼ text of Popol Wuj repeats itself in a most interesting yet puzzling kind of way as Xpiyakok, IxMuqane are called upon by the Kabʼawil to ʼshape their divinationʼ in an ancient ancestral way; a way of forming and shaping a divination that is followed to this very day.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
So let us follow this mythic speech to find our way through this masterful play on the sacred act of divination known as the Formation of the small mounds of seeds and beans; kernels and stones known as the blood and bones of the Ancient Ones. Realize right now that this story that tells of the search for the essence of the flesh of the Providers and Sustainers of the Kabʼawil is the story of the quest for the magical transforming kernels of maize that will come to fruition with the molding and modeling of the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Lineages in the hands of IxMuqane. IxMuqane who will transform maize kernels by cooking them in ʼlime and ashʼ in a process known as nixtamalization known to the Kʼicheʼ Maya a Tziya! This process of cooking maize kernels in wood-ash or white-lime is what created the Mesoamerican Civilization through this alchemical transformation of maize into a highly nutritive and nourishing form of sacred sustenance.

Needless to say the ʼword-playʼ that takes place here takes us deep into the esoteric world of the Maize People whoʼs great Matriarch IxMuqane acts as the Former; the Shaper of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq and their Sacred World where maize is named as it is sown in order to deify the Face of the Earth where IxMuqane buries the sacred seeds of her Descendants who will be seen as the Replacements-Kʼexel that come back to life through the sowing of the ʼtiny-skullsʼ of the Divine Ancestors. These Divine Ancestors live out eternal lives through their ʼeternal returnʼ as the Descendants of the First Four Sowings of Maize.

This eternal cycle of sowing and sprouting embodies the never-ending life of renewal through the sowing of seed; sowing of the ʼtiny-skullsʼ of the Divine Ancestors. These ʼtiny- skullsʼ are the skulls that are the seeds that are sown as the essence of the First Fathers of Maize. This is the living essence of the Maize People that sprouts forth from the seeds sown in the Earth by IxMuqane: the Great Matriarch of the Maize People.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Maya knew all of this when they participated in the performance of the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj but you need to be taught this so you understand the word-play performed in this quest to find the ʼperfect essenceʼ of those who will become the Maize People-Ixim Winaq who will act out their Rituals of Sacrifice as the Providers of Sacred Gifts of Sacrifice and the Sustainers of the Sacred Days in Ancient Ancestral Ways.

This mythic quest to find the Sacred Seeds of Sacred Sustenance has begun right here with this divinatory search for the special wood from the special tree. You must know this to be able to ʼenter the wordʼ of Popol Wuj in meaningful ways that enlighten your understanding of this ancestral act of divination that is also the keeping and counting of the Sacred Days in Ancient Ancestral Ways.

This is it; these are those Ancient Ancestral Ways of forming and shaping the form and shape of Divination in order to find what is hidden; in order to see that which will be shown to know that which must be known; in order to do what must be done to bring the Ancient Word to Fruition.

This is it; this is the sowing of the sacred seeds of knowing the origins of the Wooden People; the Wooden People who will bring about a deeper understanding of what it takes to be in order to become a ʼPerfect People, Perfect Pueblo-Saqil Winaq, Saqil Amaqʼ.

This carving and crafting of the Wooden People anticipates the sowing and sprouting of the Maize People told in their Ancestral Account of being and becoming a Perfect Pueblo of Perfect People who will be molded and modeled in the hands of IxMuqane after she grinds down the Yellow Maize, White Maize found by the Fox and Coyote; Parakeet and Crow.

We are walking the Sacred Road of Transformation in this Ancestral Quest to become the Ixim Winaq: Maize People. This is their Myth of Maize; this is their Sacred Story of the Creation and Destruction of the multiple Ages; many Suns of the Maize People as they make their way on the Ancestral Path of Being and Becoming the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo whoʼs story is told here through the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

body:
Now you know where we are moving on this Sacred Journey known as the Mythic Quest to become the perfect replacements of perfect ancestors. Let us take up that road to enter those ancient ancestral times when the ancient ways of the Divine Ancestors guided and protected their Beloved Descendants all along the Sacred Path of Initiates in their Ancestral Quest to be and become the Perfect Replacements of their Perfect Ancestors.

Popol Wuj manifests the perfect speech and perfect acts of the Ancestral Way of speaking and acting as the Divine Ancestors which makes the Myth of the Maya told here in the Popol Wuj to royal road to knowing just exactly how to act and speak as the Noble Women and Noble Men of the Ancient Maya.

This is the Sacred Path that protects and guides one on the Sacred Journey of Transformation and Change. So let us take up this Ancient Ancestral Road of the Maya of Mesoamerica assured that it is the original authentic Path of Initiates whose time had come to perform their part in this Long Performance and Long Recitation known as Popol Wuj.

Let us engage our imagination in order to enter the transcendent mystery of participation known as ʼparticipation mystiqueʼ through which we become ʼoneʼ through the transcendent function of mythic speech and mythic acts. This is it; this is our opportunity to step into the Imaginal World of Popol Wuj in order to transcend time and space by entering the mythic words and mythic ways of the many mythic metaphors of Popol Wuj: sowing and sprouting; forming and shaping; creating and destroying; rising and falling; sowing and dawning... Come, let us ʼenter the ancient wordʼ to ʼenter the ancestral wayʼ to ʼenter the ancient worldʼ to ʼenter the ancestral wisdomʼ to ʼenter the ancestral road of knowingʼ that is found when we ʼenter the ancient, ancestral road of Popol Wuj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Come, let us ʼenter the wordʼ to become the Divinities known as the Kabʼawil to know what it is like to create and destroy the Many Ages of the Many Suns of the Many Worlds that were formed and shaped by the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj. Come, let us ʼenter the Ancient Wordʼ like never before by participating with our mythic imagination like the Maya once did when they participated with their active imagination when they were called to sacred act of remembrance through the invocation of the sacred word. This is it; this that you are about to bring to life here.

“You Maize-Ixim, you Tzʼite-Bean; you Destiny-Qʼij, you Formation-Bʼit make yourself useful, do what must be done; speak; reveal to us how it will be made,” they said to the Maize-Ixim kernels; when they spoke to the Tzʼiteʼ the bright red corral beans.

This is when the Kabʼawil spoke to one another; those known as Jun Raqan and Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz.

“Be self-sacrificing in your way; be sacrificial in your support; show pity, show remorse, show humility but of course you who are the Heart of the Sky- Ukʼuʼx Kaj do not chastise; do not belittle the spoken word of the mouth; do not mock the genuine ways of speech nor bring low the divine countenance of Quetzalcoatl; mock not the revered presence of Sovereign Plumed Serpent; do not ridicule the sacred essence of Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz, ” they said, speaking straight to the truth when the Maize Kernels and Tzʼiteʼ Beans spoke clearly through their Divination of what must be performed next; at the Formation of the Knowing; at the Shaping of the Seeing; upon their Expression of the Truth; upon their Revelation of the Word that told them exactly what had to be done to bring the Wooden People to life.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Sovereign Plumed Serpent, Quetzalcoatl; One-Footed-One, Hurricane Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz; Jun Raqan Kaqulja Heart of the Lake-Sea; Heart of the Sky-Earth Quetzalcoatl-Precious Twin; Tezcatlipoca-Smoking Mirror Divine Twins; Rival Complements of One-an-Other This was when ʼHeʼ was spoken to there before the divine powers of the Ixim-Maize Seed; Tzʼite-Red Corral Bean; Sun-Qʼij; Formation-Bʼit or Sustenance-Ixim; Authority-Tzʼite; Destiny-Qʼij; Existence-Bʼit; who are there to speak with the ʼOneʼ known as Heart of the Sky- Ukʼuʼx Kaj. The beauty of this mythopoetic language is found in the open and ambiguous way it brings forth many meanings through its polysemic way of forming feelings while shaping the senses that provide the reader or listener of this Long Performance, Long Recitation of the Ancient Words with many meanings and significations.

This one phrase: ʼKatkʼix la uloq at Ukʼux Kaj, ma-qajisaj uchi, uwach Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatzʼ speaks to us of ʼcarving the mouth and eyes; the face and countenance of Quetzalcoatl which is to say ʼdonʼt belittle the speech and countenance of Lord Quetzalcoatl in order to speak of the Heart of the Sky and his being asked not to ʼre-workʼ the wood-work of Quetzalcoatl.

At the same time this tight little play on words embodies as it ensouls the archetypal names of Ancestral Ways of Divination: Ixim, Tzʼite, Qʼij, Bʼit. While at the same time this sacred text invokes the Sowing and Dawning; ta Chawaxoq, ta Saqiroq of the Provider and Sustainer; Tzuqul, Kʼool through the Invocation and Divination of At Ixim; At Tzʼite; At Qʼij; At Bʼit asking them to be useful by telling the Heart of the Earth, Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Lake; Heart of the Sea what they need to know in order to do what they need to do to bring forth the next attempt at Forming and Shaping the Providers and Sustainers.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is where the transforming genius of the Nawal Scribes is brought forth through the subtle significations of the mythic meanings and foundational feelings that are woven together through the ingenious sensibility of the intuition and the imaginative genius of feeling that is brought out through the sensation of carving and sculpting these Wooden Beings who are bound to the sentiment of humiliation and disgrace that comes to fruition in their inevitable death, downfall, and demise. This Divination-Qʼij and Formation-Bʼit speaks through the Maize Kernels-Ixim and Tzʼiteʼ Corral Red Beans who call out to the Kabʼawil asking the Heart of the Sky-Earth not to destroy the carving and crafting of Heart of the Lake-Sea. But this of course is exactly what the Heart of the Sky-Jun Raqan Kaqulja-Hurricane will do when he is not remembered by the Wooden People when they are asked to ʼname the nameʼ of their Former and Shaper; something they cannot do.

We are asked to ask ourselves what is it within ourselves that will be the cause of our being brought low? What is it that we must do to not disgrace our own speech in order not to humiliate our own being and becoming in this World of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea where everything means more than it appears to mean in a World of sign, symbols, and significations where polysemic interpretations take us deeper and deeper into the straight-talking truth of who we really, truly are. What do the Sacred Seeds of Sustenance say? What do the Bright Red Beans of Blood tell us?

The multiple meanings and symbolic significations found in this sacred secret speech causes the reader to ponder in order to wonder to then contemplate what these Maya Scribes want to say with: Qʼij; Bʼit other than Divination and Formation. And what this is; is something major; something of great importance because it is an invocation that calls upon the Sun-Qʼij to provide the warmth and light with which to embrace our Destiny-Qʼij; while calling on Formation-Bʼit to invoke and remember the Divine Powers of Creation and Destruction.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These are the Cosmic Forces of the Kabʼawil that are invoked as the Forming and Shaping; Molding and Modeling; Carving and Creating of everything that must be brought into being in the World of the Sky-Earth to Provide and Sustain the Formers and Shapers with the knowledge they need to divine the essence of the sacred substance from which the flesh of the Formed Beings, Shaped Beings will be brought forth throughout the Creation and Destruction of the Ages.

The last of these Ages was imagined by the Maya as the Age of Maize. Maize that was sown in the Milpa to grow and grow as the canes that flowered and fruited into the ʼheads of the Maize Lordsʼ who ʼtasseled-upʼ on top to ʼhead-upʼ down below, just so. Just so that the People of Maize would be provided and sustained by the Maize that they-the People of Maize-provided for and sustained as their Maize that was sown to be grown in the Milpa.

In this way the People of Maize were just like the Maize just as the Milpa was just like the Pueblo of the People of Maize. The Maize growing in the Milpa needs the People of the Pueblo to provide and sustain them care and attention throughout their lifecycle lived out in the Milpa just as the Kabʼawil need the People to provide and sustain them with sacrifice in order that the Kabʼawil provide the Milpa with rain from the clouds and warmth from the Sun.

This reciprocal relationship between all the Providers and Sustainers is what is told in the Popol Wuj in which all the Actors act as Providers and Sustainers. Remember: Quetzalcoatl is the Mesoamerican Maize Lord who in a Nahua Story descends down into the Land of the Dead to bring back the bones of the Ancestors that will be used as maize seed to be sown in the Milpa. Just as the Lords of Death here in the Popol Wuj are those who do everything they can to keep the Maize Lords from living by cutting their lineage off at the ʼtrunkʼ by decapitating the Maize Deity-Jun Junajpu. But the Maize Lord; Maize Deity cannot be killed just as Quetzalcoatl here cannot be destroyed by Hurricane and so it is that the ʼeternal returnʼ of the Maize Lords is the very essence of the soul of the Maize People who will live on to see another day dawn on the horizon at the threshold of life and death. This is the story that is told here; the story of providing and sustaining to be provided for and sustained by those who one has nourished and nurtured to fruition. This is also a story of the lifecycle of Maize and the Milpa that begins like all Ages with a great deal of hope that is embodied in the sprouts shooting up and out of the Earth with vim and vigor only to end up dying in the end after flowering and fruiting with great beauty only to end life being complete destroyed through the utter chaos of wailing winds under a desiccating Sun.

This is the Sun at the end of the lifecycle of maize when the seeds dries out in the husk as the head of maize holds on tight to the cane before being ʼbent down lowʼ to protect the seeds from being eaten by the Bird Deity Wuqubʼ Kaqix who is none other than another Nagual embodiment of the One Footed One Jun Raqan Kaqulja who is of course the very Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj. This is the magical transforming world of myth in which the Lords of Life and the Lords of Death take on one form after another to shape-shift as one Nawal-Nagual-Nahual Being or another.

body:
So realize this Nawal Truth of Mesoamerica is what governs this mythic world and its mythic landscape and by doing so you will be able to enjoy the changing and transforming ways of this sacred mythic script know as Ancient Word of Popol Wuj that tells the Ancestral Account of the People of Maize and their Maize Deities who play out the mythic metaphor of the Maize and its lifecycle that is played out through the life and death struggle of the Hero Twins and their descent into the Underworld of Death where they face and overcome the test, trials, and ordeals that await them there in the Imaginal Realm of the Death Lords known as Xibʼalbʼa: Place of Fear; Place of Intimidation; Place of Initiation.

This is the story initiated here with the Divine Twins; Twin Deities known as the Kabʼawil who embody the Creative and Destructive Forces of the Maya Cosmos where Maize is sown in the Milpa by the People of Maize who are the Pueblo of Maize who live out their lives formed and shaped by the Sacred Lifecycle of Maize.

Popol Wuj embodies the lifecycle of the Milpa just as it is ensouls the way of each and every Age with its New Sun and New Moon filled with hope and intention to create great beauty and prosperity only to end up completely destroyed at the inevitable fall into death, destruction, and demise at the end of every Age; like the end of every Day; like the end of every season of Maize; like the end of every Culture and Society with their foreseeable end that begins with some sort of dynastic decline that leads to some kind of cataclysmic collapse of a Nation of People that comes to some type of destructive fall at the end of every Civilization.
