source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This is the Destruction that can only be held in check through constant efforts to bring forth Creation through providing sacrifice in order to sustain the Kabʼawil with worship and exaltation; reverence and adoration. Popol Wuj tells us that the Divine Powers of Creation take continual self-sacrifice and this is what the text is telling us here as the Divination asks Heart of the Sky to sacrifice himself to the creative cause of Quetzalcoatl in order not to bring about the disgrace and downfall of this Deity whose essence is Creation. This is the One known as Qʼuqʼkumatz; Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo; He who is the Former of the Turquoise-Blue Bowl; He who is the Shaper of the Emerald-Green Plate; He of the Aqua-Marine Sea; He of the Jade-Green Earth; known as AjRaxa Laq; AjRaxa Tzel; the Molder of Precious Blue-Green Sea; the Modeler of the Precious-Green Earth. This Divine Power of Creation is named in order to be invoked as Sun-Qʼij while Formation-Bʼit is invoked to be remembered as Creation by Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja who is called upon to give sacrifice. And so it is that these Divine Twins give their own blood through their own self-sacrifice. Apparently they bleed themselves with maguey spines or kʼix. So that from now on out blood sacrifice will be given by the Providers and Sustainers to provide and sustain the Kabʼawil with sacred sustenance who will provide and sustain the Maize in the Milpa with light and warmth of the Sun; moisture and rain from the Clouds; lightning and thunder from the Three Forms and Shapes of the Heart of the Sky who will provide and sustain the Maize People of the Pueblo of Maize with their Sacred Sustenance in the form of Maize and Cacao.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Maize People will bleed themselves and others to provide and sustain the Kabʼawil with their sacred sustenance which is the heart and blood of human beings. The Kabʼawil are those divine beings who will provide their Milpa with the warmth and rain that is needed to sustain the Maize sown in la Milpa that will grow when fed by the dew that falls during the night at the end of the Dry Season and then the rain that falls during the day in the Rainy Season. Around and around the reciprocal acts of sacrifice go as they provide and sustain the Providers and Sustainers with sacred sustenance; Providers and Sustainers who provide and sustain those who provide and sustain others who must be fed by those who are the Providers and Sustainers; Nourishers and Nurturers; Feeders and Maintainers. This sacred story of reciprocity is told here.

Human Sacrifice; Kabʼawil Tojil; Lord Storm Mountain People; Canyon Country; Drops of Blood; Drops of Rain Nahua Kingdom of Lord Nakxitl Quetzalcoatl And so it is that all those who are Providers and Sustainers will give Blood Sacrifice to provide and sustain creation through Human Sacrifice which means the Providers and Sustainers will give blood sacrifice through Human Sacrifice. Rain will fall as drops of blood are given on the altar stones of sacrifice so that a ʼgreat rainʼ will fall when the Kʼicheʼ Kabʼawil Tojil known as Lord Storm demands to ʼsuckle the chestsʼ of all those Mountain People who have agreed to give Tojil sacrifice by allowing themselves to be ʼsuckledʼ by this ʼhummingbirdʼ Warlord Tojil of the Kʼicheʼ; Tojil who has guided his Kʼicheʼ Warlords to subjugate the Mountain Tribes to the rule of Ukʼuʼx Kaj and Qʼuqʼkumatz. Qʼuqʼkumatz is also known as Nakxitl Quetzalcoatl the Four-footed Deer Lord and Conqueror of the Nahua People of Tollan Tzuy-Wa of Chichen Itzaj that is the Place Beside the Cenote of the Itzaj People. This is where the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom go to receive their Kabʼawil that will ʼguide and protectʼ them all along the way.

body:
The Kʼicheʼ Kingdom grows in power and strength as their sovereignty and majesty grows in proportion to their subjugation of the Mountain People and Canyon Country who will provide the blood that calls the rain so the maize and cacao comes to fruition in order to pay the tribute required from Ajaw Nakxitl Quetzalcoatl who sits upon his Jaguar Throne in the Council House of the Sacred Reed Mats of Tollan Tzuy-Wa.

This story is being set-up right here through this Ancient Ancestral Divination and Formation that calls out to Heart of the Sky asking him not to disgrace the face of Quetzalcoatl in order not to bring in shame on word spoken by the Sovereign Plumed Serpent. The Warrior Deity Jun Raqan Kaqulja will transform into the Storm Deity of the Kʼicheʼ known as Tojil; Tojil is gifted to the First Father Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ of the First Kʼicheʼ Lineage known as the Kaweq but this is getting far too far ahead of the story despite being a premonition of that story of human sacrifice being told here through this secret sort of sacred speech that demands to be interpreted in ingenious imaginative ways as it performed here through the full engagement of our intuition and intelligence; feelings and sensations; imagination and inventiveness. Popol Wuj is an Ancient Ancestral Myth that tells of the reciprocal relationships that are played-out and performed by the Providers and Sustainers; Tzuqul, Kʼool. So it is best you understand this relationship of Creation and Destruction; Forming and Shaping; Feeding and Maintaining; Providing and Sustaining that is told right here.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This relationship of sacrifice that is created between the Providers and Sustainers of Creation and Destruction is being formed and shaped right here through the sacrificial acts of the Kabʼawil Ukʼuʼx Kaj and Qʼuqʼkumatz; for it is they who are called upon to give their own blood for the creation of these Men of Wood and Women of Reeds. Wood and Reeds play significant roles in the Maya World. Never-the-less this Mythic Masterpiece of the Popol Wuj leaves the reader quite confused through the words it has used unless one knows the story by heart as the Maya once knew this Myth of the Maize People that is known today as Popol Wuj.

This Myth of the People of Maize wish to use its mythopoetic words to disguise ʼblood sacrificeʼ in mythopoetic plays that leave ʼfirst time readersʼ completely dazed and perhaps confused too in no uncertain way. But for those who known the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account there is no question that this Sacred Scripture of the Ixim Winaq is ʼsetting the sceneʼ for the blood sacrifice that will call down the rain on the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This rain will provide and sustain the Mountains and Valleys of the Kʼicheʼ in order to transform the Kʼicheʼ Realm into the prosperous place of maize and cacao that it will become through the sacred acts and sacred speech of Kʼicheʼ Lords and their Noble Vassals who will subjugate the Mountain Places and Canyon Country to the rule of the Heart of the Sky-Earth and Heart of the Lake-Sea known as the One-Footed-One, Hurricane and the Sovereign Lord Quetzalcoatl. This section tells us of their giving blood sacrifice to bring the Wooden Men and Reed Women to life. For was it not ʼHe-Ukʼuʼx Kajʼ who was the ʼOne-Jun Raqan Kaquljaʼ that was called upon to give blood sacrifice-katkʼix la uloq to feed the forming, the shaping that was brought to completion by Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz through his creation of the New Sun, New Age of the Wooden People. Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz is called upon by Former and Shaper to participate with Jun Raqan Kaqulja in the Forming and Shaping of the Wooden Men of Tzʼiteʼ and the Reed Women of Sibaqʼ in order that their collaborative and complementary Twinship comes to fruition but as you will come to see something is lacking in the essence of their wooden flesh and reed bodies of these two formed and shaped creations known as the Wooden People.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: They will fail to remember Jun Raqan Kaqulja and their inability to invoke the remembrance of the One-Footed-One Hurricane will bring down a great flood of destruction from the Heart of the Sky: Ukʼuʼx Kaj. And so the Beloved Descendants learn how not to act by learning through the Wooden People how one must invoke oneʼs Former and Shaper in order to remember them in proper ways as the Provider and Sustainer of the Kabʼawil through sacred secret speech and by giving self-sacrifice with maguey spines and obsidian blades. These sacred acts of speech and blood sacrifice of the Providers and Sustainers begins here. This is why Quetzalcoatl is begging Jun Raqan Kaqulja to sacrifice himself in their carving and crafting of the Wooden People; Quetzalcoatl calls on his Precious Twin to give sacrifice in order that their work of forming and shaping turns out well. But their work does not turn out well. The Wooden People donʼt turn out well because they cannot remember the Heart of the Sky; Ukʼuʼx Kaj as their Creator. It is because of this failure to invoke and remember Ukʼuʼx Kaj that Heart of the Sky-Hurricane turns against the Forming and Shaping of Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz as Creator. And so it is that Ukʼuʼx Kaj becomes the Great Destroyer known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja or Hurricane. Creation and Destruction is the way of the Ages or Suns of the Animal People; the Clay People; the Wooden People; and then the Maize People who are the Kʼicheʼ People. The Animals are brought into existence by Lord Quetzalcoatl as Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo the Primordial Waters of Creation of the Heart of the Lake-Sea to then be destroyed by Heart of the Sky known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj and his obsidian blade that feeds upon the flesh of the Animal People. Then the Clay People are created by being molded out of Earth and Water to end up too wet making them not ʼhardʼ enough to live out their lives on the Face of the Earth. They are wet because of the Essence of the Heart of the Lake-Sea and so they are completely eradicated through the total destruction of Heart of the Sky who brings down this man made of mud who Ukʼuʼx Kaj lays low by smashing him down upon the Earth below.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And now we have the Wooden People who are carved from wood and bundled from reeds only to be completely destroyed by the Heart of the Sky as you will come to see while being transformed into Spider Monkeys who are the Nagual of Quetzalcoatl known as Kʼoy. Kʼoy this is a most bothersome trickster animal who disrupts the peace of the jungle forest in every way as he embodies the reversal of what Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz intended with his formal forming and shapely shaping of Wooden Men and Reed Women.

Katkʼix la uloq at Ukʼux Kaj; Ma qajisaj uchiʼ, uwach Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz Sacrifice your Blood with the Maguey Spine Bleed your Blood with Obsidian Blade Donʼt Shame the word; donʼt disgrace the face of Lord Quetzalcoatl Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz, Quetzalcoatl, the Creator and Jun Raqan, the One Footed One, Tezcatlipoca the Destroyer, Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj were together again Forming and Shaping the next Age of Sibaqʼ Reed Women and Tzʼiteʼ Tree Men. This polysemic phrase ʼsacrifice yourself-katkʼix la uloqʼ is difficult to translate with precision since it could mean: give self-sacrifice with maguey thorns; humble yourself; mock yourself; sacrifice yourself to the work of forming and shaping of these Wooden Works of Wood known as Poy and Ajam Cheʼ. Poy signifies: Manikins; Scarecrows; Dolls; Puppets; whereas Ajam Cheʼ means ʼWorked Wood or Woodworks; literally: Wooden Works of Wood; Ajam Cheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
those People Sculpted from Wood as Crafted Wood-works of Worked Wood known as Ajam Cheʼ . Let is us ʼenter the wordʼ of these Wooden People in order to watch the way their Age rises-up through the powers of Creation to be brought down low through the powers of Destruction for this is the Forming and the Shaping of those Deities known as Qʼuqʼkumatz and Jun Raqan Kaqulja; Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo; Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ulew spoken of as the Precious Twins Quetzalcoatl and the One-Footed-One who are the Divine Twins of the Heart of the Lake-Sea; Heart of the Sky-Earth.

This is their story of the Creation and Destruction of the Wooden People in which the Men were carved from the wood of the Tzʼiteʼ Tree and the Women were bundled and bound together as Formed Beings shaped from the Reeds and Rushes of the Lakeshore or Sibʼaq as these abundant beings of the Mesoamerican World are known to this very day.

Here begins the telling of the Wooden People formed and shaped from the wood of Tzʼite Trees and the Reeds and Rushes of the Sibaqʼ that grow thick beside the water of the lakeshore overflowing with natural abundance and prosperity.

They came out well those who were the Wooden Beings-Poy those who were the Wood-worked Works of Wood-Ajam Cheʼ.

They came out well because of their speech and because of the way they spoke with one another there on the Face of the Earth. So be it! They said then: May it be so! Let them be as they were formed and shaped to be by their Former; by their Shaper. When they spoke their name; in a stroke the Wooden Beings were made; known as the Poy-Manikins is what they were these Wooden Beings that were ʼakin to menʼ known and named Ajam Cheʼ: Wooden Works of Wood.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They looked just like People; they spoke just like People as well. And so then it was that the Face of the Earth became populated by the Wooden Ones who now peopled the Face of the Earth. They multiplied and became many; they conceived and delivered Daughters; they begot and engendered Sons; they sired and gave birth to Children. This then was when they were there on the Face of the Earth these who were known as Wooden Manikins-Poy-Wooden Figurines; those who were known as Ajam Cheʼ-Wooden People; those People of Wood who were just Wooden Works of Worked-Wood. But they had no heart; they had no courage; they had nothing that one could call feelings much less a touching thought of the heart; for nothing moved their soul.

They had no intelligence; they had no genius; they had no thoughts nor ideas; they had nothing that might be called imagination much less remembrance; all of which made them about as caring and concerned for others as the timber planks of wood that they were. But being made of boards that wasnʼt the worst of it because they couldnʼt remember who formed and shaped them; they couldnʼt name the names of their Former or their Shaper who was their Carver; who was their Creator. They walk about rather poorly, more or less lost and without direction; they crawled about on all fours. They had no remembrance, no recollection of the Heart of the Sky their Kabʼawil: their Deity; their Divinity known as: Ukʼuʼx Kaj. Because of this they were judged; and this then was their downfall there on the Face of the Earth. And so it was seen as just another attempt; just another demonstration of the human condition; just another attempt at making and molding a Provider; a Sustainer: they did not turn out well.

At first they spoke; but their faces were just so dry; their arms, their legs had no consistency, no uniformity.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
No blood flowed in their veins; no vital fluids ran through their limbs, the branches of their desiccated bodies were just so very parched; their arms dry to the bone. They did not perspire thus sweat did not drip from their pores; no oily fat greased their skin to give them a nice chubby complexion; they were just so very, very dry; just dried up and dried out is what they were.

Dry were there cheeks giving them firm façades that were as rigid as wooden masks. Just ʼwoodpecker-stiffʼ were their unbending legs and inflexible arms so that their flesh squeaked whenever they moved their boney bodies about.

And so it was that they felt nothing before their Former, Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Bearer, Begetter; Alom, Kʼajolom; Giver of Breathe, Giver of Heart; Alay Qech, Kʼuxlay Qech; Inspirer and Heartner of the Bright Life; Inspiration;

Encourager of the Divine Life-Saq Kʼaslem.

They were the First People to grow thick and abundant here on the Face of the Earth. Let us continue on with the end of the Wooden People and their downfall, death, and demise.

This then was when they were finished off; when they were eliminated- kimaʼixik; eradicated-kimaʼixik; they were just erased from the Face of the Earth; because it was those who were known and named the Manikins-Poy along with the Wooden Works of Wood-Ajam Cheʼ who were swept clean as they were swept clear from where they had started out so well to end up eliminated as those who were decimated there on the Face of the Earth; for it was they who were the Poy and the Ajam Cheʼ that were definitively destroyed by those who had formed and shaped them not so very long ago.

They were just ground down-kikʼutuxik before being completely ground out- kikʼutuxik as those who were killed off-xekamisax. The end had come for these Woodwork Beings ʼAjam Cheʼ who were just Wooden Works of Wood.

These were those who were Poy that had been dressed up and adorned to be seen as Manikins in order to be known as Manikins that were finished-off.

body: Those who were known as Puppet People who were seen as Doll People: Poy were ground-out-xekʼutuxik like chili ground-down on a grinding stone. These Wooden People who began their existence with such promise were all killed-xekamisax just finished off because they did not invoke the name of Ukʼuʼx Kaj who had formed and shaped them; they could not remember Heart of the Sky because they had no remembrance of those who were their Former; their Shaper and so it was they were exterminated-xekamisax by the One-Jun known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj who was the One-Jun named: Heart of the Sky. This then was when Heart of the Sky thought of flooding the Face of the Earth with a deadly deluge of water; this was when a Great Rain were imagined by Ukʼuʼx Kaj; a torrential rain that became a ferocious flood to bring about the definitive destruction of the Wooden People. For it was He who was the One-Jun named Heart of the Sky who thought-up the Great Flood-Nimaʼ Bʼutik that came as a Great Rain-Nimaʼ Jabʼ that was imagined by ʼHimʼ to bring about the ʼEndʼ of those who could not remember their Former; their Shaper known as Heart of Sky. This was the One-Jun named Jun Raqan Kaqulja-the One-Footed-One of Thunderbolt Lightning; he who was the Hurricane-Jun Raqan that brought about the Great Flood-Nimaʼ Bʼutik there on the Face of the Earth. And so it was that this Nimaʼ Bʼutik-Great Flood; Great Hurricane was made to fall upon the Wooden People-Ajam Cheʼ and the Puppet People-Poy-who were the Manikin Pueblo made-up of the Manikin People who had been formed and shaped just a short time before the creation of the Nimaʼ Bʼutik that was the Great Flood that had been imagined as the thought of the Heart of the Sky.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This Nimaʼ Bʼutik, this Great Flood was made to fall atop the thoughtless Poy and the mindless men made of Worked Wood-Ajam Cheʼ whose forming and shaping came to no good. It was just Tzʼiteʼ wood from the Tzʼiteʼ tree that was worked as the wooden essence; the wooden substance used for the flesh of these Wooden Men formed by the Former; shaped by the Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol. This was the wood used to form and fashion; sculpt and shape the wooden bodies of these Beings of Wood; this worked-wood came from the Divining Tree: Tzʼiteʼ.

Lakeshore reeds growing amongst the rushes-known as Sibʼaq-were used to bind and bundle the body of the Reed Women in this Age; in this Sun; in this Era of the ʼWooden Peopleʼ that would be remembered as the Age of the Wooden Beings.

Divine Powers of Destruction To End the Age To Devour the Sun To Destroy the Moon This was the Sun that would be invoked as the Sun of the Wooden-Works of Worked- Wood; this then was the Era that would be invoked to be remembered as the Age of the Sun of the Wooden People.

These Wooden People came to a swift and deadly end in which the destructive forces of creation would finish the Wooden People off in truly deadly ways that were as creative as they were destructive; ways of destruction that would inhabit the Face of the Earth with a deadly hunger.

For it was then that Gouger of Eyes descended on the People; then the Killer Bats dropped out the Sky; to then open the way to the Devouring Jaguars to rise-up as the living forces of Death and Destruction that always appear at the End of a Sun; End of an Age that came to life in the devastating destruction and devouring consumption of the Wooden Men and Reed Women. This was brought to fruition through the powers of destruction that were embodied by the Jaguar Warriors of Night and Eagle Warriors of Day who were accompanied by the Killer Bats who flew about from Dusk to Dawn as they fluttered and flittered all about throughout the calm quiet darkness found in the shadowy stillness of the long quiet Night.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
There was no escape the Wooden People would be devoured by Death and if not they would be transformed into their remnants known as the Spider Monkeys or Kʼoy who will be introduced when their time comes at the end of the telling of the Death and Demise of the Wooden Men and Reed Women who are told of here as the Creation and Destruction of the Heart of the Lake-Heart of the Sea; Heart of the Sky, Heart of the Earth.

So let is tell their story in order to complete the telling of the First Forming, First Shaping of the First People; First Pueblos on the Face of the Earth: the Trees and Vines; the Deer and Birds; the Snakes and Serpents; the Puma and Jaguar all of who are known together as the Animal People of the Wilderness. Then came the Clay Creature, the Man made of Mud, the Soft Being formed from Wet Earth, this was the Dude made of Dirt; and now the Wooden People known as the Men of Tzʼiteʼ and the Women of Sibʼaqʼ. This is the story told here.

This, then, is the way they were killed: they were just drowned; they just drowned in the dark rain. This was a heavy rain of black resin that fell from the dark sky of storm that drowned out the Wooden People: Ajam Cheʼ; Poy.

There came a ʼDark Rain of Resinʼ known as ʼNimaʼ Qʼol-Great Resinʼ that fell thick; that fell dark; that fell heavy from a tarred Sky.

And with that dark rain of resin there appeared the Monster Destroyers known by their names; names that are named here:

Kʼotkʼowach: Eye-Gouger; Gouger of Eyes; xkʼotin ubʼaqʼ kiwachʼ, it was this gouger of eyes that gouged out in order to carve out the eyes of those they ate as Eagles-Kʼot who gouge out the eyes of their prey.

Kamalotzʼ Kama Sotzʼ: Killer Bat; Death Bat, this one decapitated the heads of their victims; these Killer Bats just lopped off the skulls of those who were found sleeping out in the dark; known as a ʼDecapitator of Headsʼ this one named Kamalotz or Kama Sotz sliced-off the heads of their prey like a ʼfruit batʼ slicing off their sustenance with their razor sharp teeth that sliced through the neck in less than a heart-beat; this Killer Bat just decapitated the heads that were skulls-xqupin ula kijolom.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Kotz Bʼalam: Crushing Jaguar; Crunching Jaguar; Devourer of Flesh this Jaguar chomped and chewed to eat his prey whole; by crunching and crushing their skulls and bones these Devouring Jaguars just finished off their meals leaving nothing behind; not even the skull and bones.

Tukum Bʼalam: Dismembering Jaguar; Scattering Jaguar; shredder of bone and sinew, this Jaguar just tore his victim to pieces. Just grinding-up to ground- down the bones of those who fell into his merciless clasp; the pitiless grip of this Jaguarʼs fangs and claws made sure nothing ever made it passed his demolishing grasp.

And so it was that the names of these devouring giants were named in order that everyone came to know who these giants were that finished off the Wooden Beings who were formed from Tzʼiteʼ and shaped from Sibʼaq. This is the telling of their eradication from the Face of the Earth. So let us tell their story so it becomes crystal clear as to the way of Destruction in the World of Creation.

There came the One named Kʼotkʼowach who gouged out the eyes his victimʼs face.

There came Kama Sotzʼ the Killer Bat known as Kamalotzʼ or he who dropped down out of the Heart of the Sky to lop-off the heads of those who had no idea they were about to die.

There came Kotz Bʼalam who crushed and crunched the flesh and bone; tendons and nerves; grist and gristle that he devoured as he finished off his prey as the One who gulp down everything that came his way.

There came Tukum Bʼalam who dismembered the quarry he hunted as the one who caught what he ate to then make his way through his prey piece by piece; limb from limb. For he ripped his victims to pieces just as he tore them apart; shredding their muscles and tendons; thrashing and slashing their ligaments and veins; as he rip through the sinew that is known as the grist of the gristle.

In this way Tukum Bʼalam left the bodies of his victims dismembered; to leave the bones of his prey scattered all about leaving his victim in tatters as is the way of the Jaguar Lords of the Mountain Places and Canyon Country in the Ancestral Realm of the Mythic Imagination known as the Imaginal Realm of Kʼicheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These Wooden People were ground up to be ground down; their body and bones were smashed to pieces, split apart; they were punished to be made examples of because they expressed no feeling; no care; no concern for their Mother; no remembrance for their Father; no recollection for the One-Jun known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Juraqan. And so it was that Ukʼuʼx Kaj created a Great Flood of Black Rain to end the days of the destiny of the failed and fallen; flawed and faulty Wooden People. Their disregard and disrespect for their Former, Shaper caused the Face of the Earth to darken; and so it was that the frightening Sky announced the arrival of the Black Rain. The Black Rain began to fall as a Dark Rain and this is how it fell; it fell as Day Rain just as it fell as Night Rain.

The Black Rain, the Dark Rain never stopped falling so that it rained all day; just as it rained all night. This then was the Dark Rain; Black Rain that ended the age of the Wooden People with a Great Flood: Nima Bʼutik.

The Small Animals, the Big Animals they just entered the houses where the Wooden People hid. The Small Animals, the Big Animals were those who just cut- away at their faces of the Wooden People; this then was when the faces of the Wooden People were slashed by the limbs of the Trees when the branches of the Trees slashed the limbs of the Wooden People.

This then was when they-the Wooden People-were pounded by the rocks that watched and waited to catch the Wooden People wherever they ran; but there was no escape, there was nowhere for Wooden People to hide from the blows that were there to take them down from the destructive mind that descended from the Heart of the Sky. Their cooking pots; their cooking utensils just spoke up as they spoke out against their owners-their dueños-kajawal for the lack of respect and regard they showed them despite all the service they provided; this lack of care and concern for those who worked for them day and night was now taken to heart in order to be punished.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Now it was time for them to make their point and have their say; to accuse them in order to condemn them for the infinite ways they mistreated them night and day. Those, those who had done so much for them, the Women of Reeds who had used their kitchen utensils and cooking pots without the least bit of care and even less concern for the painful sort of pitiful condition in which they left them scalded, scratched, and scorched; burnt, blistered, and blackened so that they ended up chipped and charred; busted and broken.

This was no way to treat those clever creations of crafted clay who were put to use every day, to be taken up again beside the hearthʼs fire that burned through the wee hours of the night, to be brought back to life as the fire that was made to blaze in the cool quiet time before the dawn.

Those who came forth were kiqʼebʼal, kixot, kilaq, kibʼoʼj, kitzʼia, kikaʼ all of whom were know well as their clay water jars-kiqʼebʼal; their clay comal-kixot; their clay plates-kilaq; their clay cooking pots-kibʼoʼj; their special clay vessels used to boil maize in wood-ash or white-lime known as nixtamal-kitzʼia that always stood beside the kitchen wall beside their grinding-stones: kikaʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were those who only wanted to be remembered for all they done to create the Wooden Peopleʼs sacred sustenance. These hard clay creations of the Ancestral Kitchen had gone through so much fire and flame at the hands of those Wooden Men and Reed Women whoʼs faulty forming of their Ancestral Ways and flawed shaping of the tasks of their Days and Nights of transforming hard kernels into soft sustenance had left the clay utensils of their kitchen failed and fallen. Those clay creation who they had used, abused, and misused now cried out to be heard when they told of the great anguish; the great affliction they were made to endure because of the scorching heat of their red-hot cooking fires that blazed as they burned within the sacred triangle that was formed by their Three-Stone-Hearth shaped by the ʼThree Hearth Stonesʼ known as the Xkʼubʼ upon which their clay cooking utensils were placed over their fire. It was here atop the ʼThree Hearth Stonesʼ that the Reed Women kneeled on their small reed mats to perform their sacred burden of cooking the sacred sustenance of the Wooden People.

It was then that their heavy grinding stones told their story of how they were never given a moment of rest by those who didnʼt feel a thing for their endless grinding of maize and cacao across their sensitive stone face. The many instruments, implements, tools, and utensils of the Wooden People that were used to prepare their sacred sustenance that fed those who had to be fed now cried out to be heard as those who now called-out to speak their word.

It was they-the clay pots and clay comal-who were constantly put to use by the Reed Women who were given the task of feeding the Wooden People. It was they-the Women of Reeds-who caused the clay pots and clay comal constant pain by setting them there upon the Xkʼubʼ that were set beside the fire that blazed before those who knelt before their scotching flames that burned within the Three Hearth Stones that were set within the kitchen and its open fire.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These clay creations came before these Wooden Works of Wood to let it be shown that theyʼd been neglected and abused for much too long and now it was time for that truth to be known.

It was time to judge them, to then castigate them by making the Wooden People endure the same pain as they had caused their charred pots, plates, ladles, and bowls; their burnt comal, their ground down grinding stones, scorched hearth stones, and lime-caked nixtamal which was everything there was in their ancestral kitchen that had been treated with neglect and disrespect by those who had not a care or concern for those clay beings whoʼd always been left much too long in the burning hot fire and its scorching flames.

Immediately they threw themselves upon the Wooden People to cut into their flesh; they jumped on them to cut and carve-up their faces. But it wasnʼt just their kitchen utensils and cooking pots that attacked them there.

No, no, no it was their domestic animals that came after them to let them know all they had done to make their lives miserable; leaving them always on the edge of starvation in an intolerable existence where they always went hungry.

Now it was time for their animals to rise-up to give them some of the same. These were their dogs-kitzʼi and their turkeys-kakʼ that were eaten as soon as they fattened up. That was just the way it was for those who were the dogs-kitzʼi and turkeys-kakʼ of the Wooden People; dogs and turkeys who joined in now with the Clay Cooking Utensils to take it to the Wooden People who had caused them suffering whenever they could.

They just let the Wooden People have what they had coming to them for the cruel neglect they were made to suffer when they were made to endure hunger; when they were driven to the brink of starvation; what else could they do?

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The end of their days had arrived for the Wooden People so that something new could come through; now it was time for the truth to be spoken; it was time to come true about who the Wooden People grew to become and how they came to treat those who they were given to take care of there on the Face of the Earth. And so their Dogs and their Turkeys spoke-up as they spoke-out against those who were there to give them care and show them concern as their providers and sustainers; nourishers and nurturers:

“You really made us suffer, you truly caused us harm, you bit into us, so now we will bite into you; you chewed on us, so now it is time we chewed on you,” growled their Dogs-Kitzʼi, gobbled their Turkeys-Kakʼ.

Then it was their old grinding stones who spoke: “On our faces you ground down maize until it was fine and silky; cacao too. You did this every day, day after day; from dawn to dusk, your grinding never stopped; grinding-down endless kernels of maize; grinding-up infinite nubs of cacao; you just ground down our face with your endless grinding that was never enough.”

Sacred Secret Speech: Joli, Joli; Jukʼi, Jukʼi Letʼs go girl! Letʼs go girl!

Letʼs go gal! Letʼs go gal! Our One Ground Drink of Maize;

Our One Ground Drink of Maize Now it was time for them to continue speaking-out now that everyone was listening to these ancient, ancestral Grinding-Stones who finally were able to speak their piece; to say what they had to say: “After nightfall; before sunrise, it didnʼt matter, it was always the same for us; always the same sound of grinding maize, grinding cacao, on your grinding stones, upon our face: scrape, scrape, grind, grind; the same orders spoken over and over: joli, joli, jukʼi, jukʼi; letʼs go girl-jo ali, jo ali; letʼs go gal-jo ali, jo ali; our one ground drink of maize-jun ukʼej; our one ground drink of maize-jun ukʼej; letʼs go girl get our ground maize drink; letʼs go girl get our ground maize drink.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Joli, Joli, Jukʼi, Jukʼi was all you ever said because that was all we ever heard you say because that was all you ever said; over and over: joli, joli; jukʼi, jukʼi. And knowing this was our sacred burden to be paid as the tribute that was asked of you; so we just kept up our grinding from sun-up to sun-down like good girls are taught to do grinding maize and cacao over our Grinding-Stones from Dawn to Dusk as Maidens are taught to do by those who call out for the ground drink of maize known as jun ukʼej, jun ukʼej; jukʼi, jukʼi.”

Jukʼi, jukʼi; Joli, joli; Jo ali, jo ali Sounds that Signify; Sounds that Sings This play on the sound of grinding maize-joli, joli; jukʼi, jukʼi-is just as much as play on words as it is a play on sound that tell of the Women and Girls who grind their Peopleʼs Sweet Drink of Ground Maize. This play on sound that is a play on words says everything about how sound speaks to us in order to say something vital about the relationship between the grinding stone and the ʼstrong, hardʼ Women and Girls who must work in the patios and kitchens of their Female Lords or Ixqi Ajaw who are responsible for the feeding of their Great Houses.

This is an Imaginal World that mirrors the Real World of Noble Women who learned the sacred ways of grinding maize and grinding cacao on their Grandmothersʼ Grinding-Stones-Ka. This is the Ancestral Work of Women just as is they Ancestral Art of spinning cotton thread with their Great-Grandmotherʼs Spindle-whorls-Bʼatzibʼal for it was the Bʼatzibʼal that was placed in the cradle of the Infant Girl as magical invocation of a Noble Womanʼs vocation. Weaving was the inherited vocation of all Maya Woman that began with the spinning of cotton thread to then dye those threads in order to then weave them into the sacred cloth that became to ancestral clothing that gave both cultural identity and magical protection to the family members and relatives who wore those threads as cloths that clothed one in Ancestral Protection and Divine Guidance.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Maya wore Ancestral Clothing that guided and protected those who wore the cloths that cloaked them in ancestral ways of being and becoming a Nawal Replacement of Nawal Ancestors. And so goes this incantation that says so much about the Ancestral World of the Maize People.

Jo ali jo! Joli, Joli; Jukʼi, Jukʼi! Our sweet drink; our sweet-kʼi drink; our one sweet drink that is our one ground drink-jun ukʼej of maize that is ground down to satisfy the Mayaʼs appetite for sacred sustenance. Jukʼi, Jukʼi is the drink that is first ground down to be taken up as their most roasty-toasty ancestral sweet drink there is: joli, joli; jukʼi, jukʼi. Let us listen to what the Grinding Stones say.

This then was when the Grinding Stones spoke up to tell of their plight before those who left them with constant work grinding maize; work that never ended since the sacred sustenance of the Ixim Winaq asked to be transformed from hard kernels of maize to the soft sustenance that could be either drank or eaten.

This transformation of hard grains into sweet food was brought to fruition through the continual work of Maya Women and Girls who were called upon to feed their people four times a day: twice with maize drink-once at dawn, once before sleep and twice during the day with tamales and tortilla.

And so it was that this endless work of women and girls is remembered here in mythic ways; this continuous work of cooking corn in clay pots of nixtamal water everyday-juta qʼij; to then strain and rinse it in their clay sieves; to then grind it on the grinding stone xqʼek-dusk; saqirik-dawn in order to then cook it up again in great big pots-kukubʼ as tamales or on a hot comal-xot as toasted tortilla.

body:
Truly, the work of Maya women to feed the People of their Pueblo knows no end in the Traditional World of the Maya in which the work of Women and Girls of the Maize People knows no end: Jo ali jo! Joli, Joli; Jukʼi, Jukʼi! This little tune says it all. The maize that will be ground tomorrow must be cooked tonight in white-lime over a fire that is not too hot and not too cold. Just as the tortilla and tamales that might be left over at the end of the day are given to the Turkeys and Dogs who hunger for something sweet to eat in a world that is fed with Sacred Sustenance known as Maize.

Imagine the endless work of Maya Women and how spinning cotton to weave cloth to then embroider that cloth were never seen as work since they are creative acts of art that Maya Women enjoy in powerful ancestral ways of creation.

Popol Wuj says so much by singing out this refrain that tells one how to treat the Women and Girls called upon to perform the work of grinding maize and cacao for the Great Fiestas that the Maya had to bring to fruition in which feeding a great many people was seen as a divine act of creation of alliances that were formed and shaped through the sharing of sacred sustenance: Joli, Joli; Jukʼi, Jukʼi!

This sacred sustenance had to be created in sacred ways without causing or creating more suffering than was necessary to toast the tortilla or cook up the tamales in the Great Big Tinajones known as Nimaʼ Kukubʼ. This is the story told here in secret sacred forms of speech that sing out: Joli, Joli; Jukʼi, Jukʼi! Jo ali, Jo ali; Jun ukʼej; Jun ukʼej; Jo Ali, Jo Ali; Jun ukʼi Jun ukʼi!

“We were never given any rest, just grinding and grinding is all you gave us to do, maize and cacao, grinding and grinding, night and day. This was our cargo to carry; our debt to life; our burden to bear; that which was ours wear given to us at birth like a sign of pride like the braids we wore in our hair; this was the sacred work we were given to perform for you who watched us from both far and near; we never stopped grinding for fear of never being given another offer to pay our ancestral debt to you like we did here by grinding maize; by grinding cacao.”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Grinding Maize; Grinding Cacao; this was our sacred burden to bear- qapatan; our ancestral office to share; our divine duty of theirs that they set upon us to pay as our tribute-qapatan; grinding and grinding was just our debt, just our tribute to be paid to you when ʼyou were still people-ix ta na winaqʼ who lived here on the Face of the Earth as they say.”

“Now it is you who will try out our strength when we grind you down. Now it is our turn to take a bite out of you, when we grind down your flesh,” said their grinding stones-kikaʼ. Then their dogs-kitzʼi said what they had to say: “Why didnʼt you give us our piece; our portion; just a bit; just a bite, just a taste of all that you ate? You saw us waiting there hungry; you just kept us there watching and waiting; but you kept us waiting like that, waiting patiently; we wanted just a bite to eat but still you ran us out; you just drove us away; always with your stick-yakal at the ready to give it to us while you ate you fill when we went hungry. Is that any way to treat your companion; your buddy; your best friend in life?” “We almost died of hunger because of you. But how could you have known that, when you canʼt feel a thing? Perhaps you might have thought it over; with you as our masters we almost died. Now itʼs time you try out our teeth-qabʼaq just the ʼour bones-qabʼaqʼ here in our mouths-qachiʼ. We are going to take a bite out of you before the end of the day!” growled their dogs before they tore into those who now faced them face to face like never before. Next, it was their comal-kixot; their tortilla-toasting griddles-kixot and cooking pots-kibʼoj who said: “You caused us pain, the way you burnt our mouths, charred our faces; always cooking with us over your blazing fire, could you have not known! You tested us well when you left us on your blistering fire. Why so hot; why so long? You didnʼt think we felt pain? Then you try it. Now we will burn you!” cried-out their pots; called-out their comal. They went after them, they pursued them; they caught up with them and burnt them good as any self- respecting worker of the Wooden People always would.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Their firestones-abʼaj that were their hearthstones-xkʼubʼ that were burning red-hot in the fire just flew up and out of the flames hitting the Wooden Ones in the head.

Those hearthstones of theirs shot right out of the flames to hit them right on their head-jolom as if one had aimed them directly at their skulls-taqal chi kijolom.

That was it! They knew what had hit them before it was over; those Wooden Men, Reed Women werenʼt as innocent as they pretended to be.

It was then when those Wooden People ran as fast as they could run; they just ran and ran to just keep running from all that was now scattered about the ground; that which was thrown at them from all around. And so they were hit from above and below until they were finally knocked down.

They scrambled up on top of their houses to escape but their houses collapsed beneath them when they tried to make their getaway.

It was no use, their destiny was sealed; their fortune that was their fate told them they were destined to die on that very same day.

They tried to climb up in the trees, but they were easily defeated by the limbs and leaves of the branches of the trees that they had never treated with form of respect or regard of any degree. Now the branches of the trees turned against them and began to hit these people formed from wood of the Talking Tree known as Tzʼiteʼ.

But that didnʼt stop them from running through the Many Trees-Kiʼcheʼlaj of the Forest where they were attacked by the limbs and branches that beat them bad and cut them to pieces. Those branches, limbs, and twigs they had cut and chopped now gave them more of the same: the People of Wood; the Wooden People realized now who they were and where they came from leaving them nothing more to do then accept what was theirs; their destiny; their fate; their death that now surrounded them from all sides.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Tree People now remembered and recognized these Men-made of Wood; these trees with their branches, trunks, and limbs who would never forget those who had once wounded them even though they knew what they were doing was no good. Those who were now on the run were those same shameless woodcutters who had once carelessly cut firewood in the forest by chopping down the trees to then cut-up their branches without the least bit of concern for the trees of the forest.

Those who once did whatever they wanted in the wilderness; those who once did whatever they pleased to the vines and trees now received the wrath of the vines and the revenge of the trees.

It was then that they-the Wooden People-tried to hide inside of the caves but the caves slammed shut in their faces leaving them no other option than to receive what was theirs in life: the death and destruction of their flawed lineage with its failed and fallen ways.

This, then, was the destruction of the Formed People, the Shaped People. They were the lost ones; the broken ones; those who suffered the great reversal of their destiny; their luck had changed forever; they were transformed once and for all because they showed no respect or regard for all that surrounded them in life; these Wooden People showed no care or concern for those who they lived life with on the Face of the Earth.

And because of that they learned what it was like to feel hurt by being left to defend for themselves in the dust and dirt of their death and decay; destruction and demise that they live out every day.

The Wooden People are no longer what they once were. They were made examples of by being transformed in their speech and in their looks; for their language and appearance were changed forever. So now, today, it is said that the Spider Monkey-Kʼoy is just a memory of them; a sign, a symbol to remind everyone of their fallen, failed, and flawed ways especially those who act ʼas ifʼ they were their descendants: descendants of the Wooden People known as Kʼoy who we will meet up down the road when they climb-up in the trees.

body:
Those Kʼoy, those Spider Monkey, who live in the forest today live as a remembrance of their sorrowful and sad ways of life; perfect examples of how not to speak and act in order to significant signs on the path of life upon which the Wooden People taught others how not to act through their disastrous and destructive ways of living out a failed and fallen existence.

These Kʼoy live on as the kʼexel-replacements of a lost-sach generation of Formed Beings, Shaped Beings who were failed beings that were fallen beings- sachnaq winaq who made very good examples as very bad examples for their human descendants who would come to learn from the Wooden People through their regret, remorse, and repentance.

Truly, the Wooden People taught those who came after them how to behave like kind and caring, considerate people since bad examples always teach one better how not to fail than good examples show one how to succeed.

It was just soft, knotless wood from a spiny tree full of color known as the Tzʼiteʼ that was used to form and shape their wooden flesh by the Former, the Shaper; the Maker, Molder; the Woodworker, the Whittler of the Wooden People.

Kʼoy: the Spider Monkey; Wooden People Today it is the Spider Monkey that acts like these poorly behaved Wooden People; and so it is they, the Wooden People, who are remembered as the descendants of this lineage of Spider Monkey People; the remembrance of Quetzalcoatl whoʼs Nagual or Animal Companion is the Spider Monkey.

They were just Puppet People; Poy, just Doll People; Poy who were the People of Worked and Whittled Wood known as Ajam Cheʼ who are just Men made of the Wood of the Tzʼite; the Tzʼite and its Magical Talking Wood and Divinatory Beans that are used every day to divine the order and count of the Days. Tzʼite is a knotless wood that is used amongst the Maya to sculpt and shape the many Masks of Mam; the Ancestor; the Grandfather; the Old Man; el Viejito known as Rilaj Mam; the Ancient Old Man who lives on today as a remembrance of this story that is so well told here.

body:
And so too the Women of the Rushes and Reeds-Sibʼaq are remembered and recalled by the great bunches of reeds cut on the lakeshores of the Maya world where they are dried in the Sun to then be gathered up and brought home. Then they are woven in the patios of the lineages of those People who weave reed mats. Reeds that are worked with flat, round stones held in the hand just right to flatten the reeds so they can then be woven into the noble reed mats known as Pop; Pop the root that is the origin of the name Popol Wuj; the Council Book of the Noble Reed Mat of Noble Rule and Authority.

Pop are the embodiment of Female Authority; Female Rule of the Matriarch who was and continues to be the Ruler of the Maize Peopleʼ lives. Pop or Petate are those Reed Mats upon which the Maya enter the world at birth and exit life at death. Maya people were once rolled up in the Pop upon which they died to return again on the Pop upon which they returned to life as their own replacements who would be born into the world as their Descendants: Ketal; Kitzijel. This is the story told here; as it is said: Just the Half of It. The story of the Reed Women is hidden away in the shadows for it is too powerful to be revealed here in the light of the public eye; the public sight; for that story reveals the Ancestral Soul that reveals the Ancient Perspective of the Ancient Ones: los Nawales.

body:
These stories that are written out to be recited here are just revealed stories that demonstrate in order to manifest the truth and tradition; the work and the word; the word and the way of these Mythic Archetypes; Mythic Figures known as Poy as Ajam Cheʼʼ These were those who were just Wooden-Works of Worked-Wood; these were those who were just the Wood- Worked People of Wood. You will see how they reappear in another place down the road on top of the Mountain Jaqawitz; the Open Mountain; the Mountain of Lord Jaqawitz; this is where the Poy, the Ajam Cheʼ will play a most significant role of the Kʼicheʼ Maya when the fight their epic battle with the Mountain People; the People of the Canyon Country who will fall to the Nawal Powers of the Jaguar Lords introduced to you here; Jaguar Lords who will be defended and protected by these Wooden People; Puppet People; the Manikin People known as Poy; spoken of as Ajam Cheʼ: Woodwork People of Worked Wood.

These Wooden People who were whittled works of wood continue to exist until this very day as those people who do not know how to care for others nor have concern for the world they live in with the many things that must be shown respect and regard for like their tools and instruments formed and shaped in the hands of working people.

The Wooden-People never learned to protect the world they lived in, its wild and domestic animals, its people, and all the many tools, art, and things those people made. This is how these disrespectful beings are remembered and known today: as Wooden People with No Heart; No Soul.

They are seen as the fallen ones-sachnaq, poqnaq winaq-the lost ones who experienced the great reversal of their destiny and its fortune, its fate. They are seen today as Spider Monkey swinging through the forest canopy, high, high up in the many trees that grow and multiply in the forest of the Kʼicheʼ.

body: “It is usually during the trauma of initiation that a neophyte hears the most sacred myths of his tribe for the first time. This is an important point. A myth is not a story that can be recited in a profane or trivial setting. Because it imparts sacred knowledge, it is always recounted in a ritualized setting that sets it apart from ordinary profane experience, and can only be understood in the solemn context of spiritual and psychological transformation. Mythology is the discourse we need in extremity. We have to be prepared to allow a myth to change us forever. Together with the rituals that break down the barrier between the listener and the story, which help him to make it his own, a mythical narrative is designed to push us beyond the safe certainties of the familiar world into the unknown. Reading a myth without the transforming ritual that goes with it is as incomplete an experience as simply reading the lyrics of an opera without the music. Unless it is encountered as part of a process of regeneration, of death and rebirth, mythology makes no sense.” A Short History of Myth Karen Armstrong “A myth is a way of making sense in a senseless world. Myths are narrative patterns that give significance to our existence.” Rollo May “It helps to regard soul as an active intelligence, forming and plotting each personʼs fate. Translators use ʼPlotʼ to render the Ancient Greek word ʼMythosʼ in English. The ʼPlotsʼ that entangle our souls and draw forth our characters are the Great Myths. That is why we need a sense of myth to gain insight into our epic struggles, our misalliances, and our tragedies. Myths show the imaginative structures inside our messes, and our human characters can locate themselves against the background of the characters of myth.” James Hillman “We may be closest to hearing the call when we feel alone or in trouble, for genius hides behind the wound and one of the greatest wounds in life is to not know who we are intended to be or what we are supposed to serve in life.” Michael Meade The Genius Myth “Mythic imagination can break the spell of time and open us to a level of life that remains timeless. Myth is not about what happened in past times;

myth is about what happens to people all of the time.” Joseph Campbell “If we spoke a different language, we would perceive a somewhat different world.”

Ludwig Wittgenstein

“But sometimes what we call ʼmemoryʼ and what we call ʼimaginationʼ are not so easily distinguished.” Leslie Marmon Silko

“Myth must be kept alive. The people who can keep it alive are the artists of kind or another.” Joseph Campbell

“Psychology is ultimately mythology, the study of the stories of soul.” James Hillman

“A myth, therefore, is true because it is effective, not because it gives us factual information. If, however, it does not give us new insight into the deeper meaning of life, it has failed. If it works, that is, if it forces us to change our minds and hearts, gives us new hope, and compels us to live more fully, it is a valid myth. Mythology will only transform us if we follow its directives. A myth is essentially a guide; it tells us what we must do in order to live more richly. If we do not apply it to our own situation and make the myth a reality in our own lives, it will remain as incomprehensible and remote as the rules of a board game, which often seem confusing and boring until we start to play.” A Short History of Myth by Karen Armstrong Ukabʼ Second Wuqubʼ Kaqix: Lord Seven Macaw: Great Bird Deity The Big Man and his Giant Sons Seven Macaw Shield Bearer Volcano Boy Earthquake Boys Wuqubʼ Kaqix Chimalmat Sipakna Kabʼraqan Age of the Giants; Sun of the Giants; Era of the Giants Twin Sons Two Sons Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu the Boys, the Sons, the Twins Junajpu Ixbʼalamkej Four Hundred Boys: Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ

body:
When we enter this Second Act of this Five Act Performance of Popol Wuj we have entered the middle of this Sacred History of the Divine Ancestors of the Maize People, which is a story that is already in progress; a story in which the mythic narrative is already moving; En Medias Res as it is known. When enter into this Second Section we enter into the Ancestral Account of the Maize People that the Maya People know by heart yet first time readers have no idea of who the Mythic Figures are or where they have come from. This is why I must introduce you to this traditional Kʼicheʼ Maya narrative of the Maize People that the Kʼicheʼ Maya suckled as the very milk of their motherʼs breast; their motherʼs breast whoʼs Nipple-Im provided and sustained the lives of the Maize People with Sacred Sustenance-Ixim that came from-Ix the Nipple-Im of their Mothers Breast as the Motherʼs Milk-Ixim that fed the Ancestral Soul of the Maya with the sustenance the Mayaʼs Ancestral Soul needed to ʼpass-overʼ this most difficult and dangerous threshold of the Year.

Popol Wuj was performed at the ʼmid-pointʼ of the Ritual Year that lay between the Old Year that was dying and in need of ritual offerings of sacrifice to be brought back to life as the New Year. These Rituals of Sacrifice where performed alongside or within the Long Performance of the Popol Wuj as the Myth of the Maize Lords that was played out as Ritual Drama enacted as a Rite of Passage that enabled the Maya to ʼpass-overʼ this uncertain and insecure passage that fell between the Old and New Year.

It is in this sense that the Popol Wuj is the ʼMyth of the Eternal Returnʼ that is played out as the Ritual Renewal of the Sky-Earth with its Sacred Time and Sacred Space being and becoming renewed through the Mythic Imagination and Ritual Enactment of the Eternal Return of the Divine Ancestors in the lives of their Descendants which is the Mythic Plot of ʼRebirth and Renewalʼ played-out through the Long Performance; Long Recitation here in the Long Revelation of the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj.

Xpiyakok: Grandfather of the Maize Deities Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu: Fathers of the Maize Lords Maize Deities; Maize Lords; Hero Twins; Junjapu, Ixbʼalamkej Soul Capture and Soul Lose of Jun Junajpu in Xibʼalbʼa Soul Retrieval from the Lords of Death: Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame

We have literally and metaphorically entered the ʼMid-Pointʼ in the mythic narrative of the Maize Lords-Junjapu, Ixbʼalamkej and their Fathers known as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who are the direct descendants of the Ancestral Maize Deity: Xpiyakok. We have entered the middle of the Hero Twinsʼ lives when and where Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej must order the natural chaos that reigns on the Face of the Earth. We begin in the middle of this sacred narrative of the Maize People by being introduced to the Ancestral Enemies of the Maize People.

The Maize People cannot begin their lives until the Face of the Earth is ʼset-rightʼ by the Hero Twins-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej-who must put everyone in their place so the next Sun and next Moon of the Maize People can rise-up in the Sky to shine their light and its strength over the Age of the Maize People that will be ordered and ruled by Ancestral Ways of the Maize People. For the World of the Sky-Earth to be ʼset-rightʼ it must be placed in a definitive sense of ʼcosmic orderʼ by placing sacrificial offering in the Four Cosmic Direction: North-South; West-East.

Once this is completed the Hero Twins must descend down into the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa to retrieve the Ancestral Souls of the First Fathers of Maize: Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. This heroic act of ʼSoul Retrievalʼ requires the ʼSacrificial Deathʼ of the Lords of Death-Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame by the Hero Twins-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

These ʼYoung Good-Looking Handsome Menʼ perform ʼXaraxoxinaqʼ which means they practice ʼHuman Sacrificeʼ by opening the chest of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame to then quickly- xaraxoj-rapidly extract the palpitating heart of the Lords of Death; Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: One Death, Seven Death; Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so it is that we experience through myth this Mesoamerican practice that is so well disguised that past translation have not been able to translate the act of Heart Sacrifice as ʼXaraxoxinaq and Xaraxojʼ preferring to leave it at ʼquickly they were killed, the two lords were sacrificedʼ when the text is emphatic in its use of these highly imaginative words that described the lightning like speed with which this heart sacrifice was performed in order that the ʼbeating heartʼ that was a ʼliving heartʼ could be fed to the sacrificial fires pumping with life.

This was the kind of lightning-bolt speed with which the art of human sacrifice was performed in the Mesoamerican World. This Mesoamerican World had now completely enveloped the Maya in the South and East where the Great Empire of Quetzalcoatl embraced all those who embraced the Great Lord Quetzalcoatl on his Jaguar Throne set upon his Noble Reed Mats of Noble Rule and Ancestral Authority that covered the floors of the Council House or Popol Na-Popol Ja of the Nimaʼ Ajaw-Great Lords who was a Nawal Ajaw-Magical Transforming Lord of Tula Tollan; of Tollan Tzuy-Wa. Tollan Tzuy-Wa is where this sacred narrative is headed as we begin this Sacred Journey of Transformation that takes us to the Underworld of Death to the Celestial Sphere where the Heart of the Sky bring Life back to Life through these Rituals of Sacrifice and Mythic enactments of the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj.

This is the story we will enter here at the mid-point of the Old and New Year when ʼMyth and Ritualʼ were braided together to form a binding bond between the living and the dead; the old and the new; the sowing and sprout; the fall and the rise; the descent and ascent; the descendants and the ancestors in a dry and dusty world where the Face of the Earth called up to the Sky to release its waters of renewal to bathe the Maize People who had sown the Maize they would grow in their Milpa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
In this sense the Popol Wuj is a petition for rain and the ʼgood lifeʼ that is the ʼgreen lifeʼ that comes with the rain that falls from the Sky. Popol Wuj is dramatic calling-out to the Heart of the Sky-Earth; Heart of the Lake-Sea to send the falling water from the clouds above so that life might rise-up from down below where the Hero Twins must go to release the powers of life and its renewal that are captured there in the Underworld by the Lords of Death.

In this sense the Popol Wuj is a story of ʼsoul retrievalʼ for all of those who enter it with a fully engaged soul and a highly active mythic imagination. In this sense the Popol Wuj is a myth that awakens our soul by releasing the psychic energies that are captured by our human condition that has us ʼstuckʼ in the past and unable to move forward into a new life on a new path of being and becoming.

Popol Wuj is a Mythic Masterpiece with an inherent power to inspire and encourage us to enter an Imaginal Realm where and in which our Ancestral Soul must find its way to the sacred fire of transformation alongside the Hero Twins who sacrifice their depleted lives to the sacrificial fire in order that they rise again as new creations with powers to change and transform the Sky-Earth into which they have been made anew. In this sense the Popol Wuj is a myth that tells us of the renewal of life in which we become ʼdancers and magiciansʼ with the powers to bring death back to life. Let us ʼenter the wordʼ of the Popol Wuj in the very middle of its being told at the Mid-Point of the Year so that we might take up the road with the New Year-bearer to make our way walking day by day as we name the names of days as the Keepers and Counters of the Sacred Day. In this sense the Popol Wuj is the sacred narrative that teaches us how to be and become well trained Day-Keepers who carry time as Cargadores del Tiempo: Bearers of Time.

Let us introduce you to the Mythic Figures and Mythic Archetypes who the Maya knew as the sacred sustenance they suckled as the Motherʼs Milk of the Mothers who lived out the lives of the Mothers and Grandmothers found here in the Popol Wuj.

body:
The Popol Wuj that tells us the Ancestral Account of the Great Matriarch IxMuqane; the Grandmother of the Maize People who brings IxKikʼ the Moon Maiden-Moon Mother into her home where she will raise the Hero Twins as the Grandsons of IxMuqane.

In this sense the Popol Wuj is the sacred narrative of a single mother who must run for her life to save her life and the life of her twin sons who she bears in her womb.

Popol Wuj is an empowering story that tells of the curious and cunning powers of the Heroine who must use her crafty creativity to transform the World of the Sky-Earth once and for all.

ʼBetwixt and Betweenʼ

World of the Divine Ancestors; World of their Beloved Descendants Saqtetoj: Calm White Light of the Pre-Dawn Sky The Nawal Perspective; Seeing Through the Transcendent Function The Mythic Bridge; Our Passage over Disempowerment

This Second Section of this Second Act of Popol Wuj begins with a dreamy white light that settles over the Sky-Earth to create an atmosphere of being ʼbetween and betwixtʼ the world of the Ancestors and the world of their Descendants. This calm pre-dawn light has a name that expresses a feeling that acts as a presentiment of the sensation that is heard in the pronunciation of Saqnatanoj revealing to us that we have entered a world that exists between the Sun of the Wooden People and the Sun of the Maize People. This Saqnatanoj, then, was when soft-white-light enveloped the Sky-Earth in the calm quiet glow of Dawn; its luminous warmth of smooth silver moon like sort of silent still light blanketed the Face of the Earth in an ancient memory; ancestral remembrance-natanoj recalling sensation of the feeling in the moment when the Ancient Ones, the Divine Ancestors, the Nawales watched and waited for the First Dawn; a memory-natabʼal of an Age; a recollection of a Sun that had come and gone: Saqnatanoj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Saqnatanoj was the time that was the moment just before the arrival of the shimmering, shining sparkle of the bright white light of Dawn. Saqnatanoj; embodiment, ensoulment of the resplendent recollection and remembrance, the radiant recuerdo y recolección of the first rays of sunlight of Sunrise; the glistening gleam of the glossy glow of Dawn, just named, just known as: Saqnatanoj.

So let us take up ʼthe good fightʼ alongside the Two Boys, the Two Sons, the Twin Brothers known as the Hero Twins as they lead us down the road to where we must go to see all there is to see; to know all there is to know; to speak and act as the First Mother-Fathers who showed their Descendants just how to say what must be said and do what must be done in order to know just where to go! This is where we go to see all that is to be seen to know all there is to be known to be all that we can be by becoming the perfect replacement of the Divine Ancestors. This is the ʼWay of the Wordʼ of Popol Wuj that provides us with Noble Counsel while it sustains us with Sacred Sustenance to fed us with the images that our Soul hungers to see and our Spirit hunger to know in order to be who we were born to become in lives we were begotten to bear the bones of our Ancestors in the Sacred Bundle where all that is precious and prized must go to be carried on our back as the Kabʼawil that is ours alone to guide and protect us all along the way as we form our lives by shaping our days by doing what we were born to do in lives that we must find that which is ours by divining the path of our destiny.

This is the Sacred Journey of life found right here in the Popol Wuj that tells of the First Dawn and its Calm White Light known to all as Saqnatanoj; the Sacred Nostalgia for our Home that we forced by destiny to leave so long ago. The Home we were driven from by desire in search of a better way next to brighter fire; in a life that we thought we could find without ever realizing the love we had at Home was the only true love we would ever know.

body:
This is what the Hero Twins come to see in order to know by going where they were invited to go deep down into the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa to play the Rubberball Game with the Lords of Death on their Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice known and named: Pusbʼal Chaaj.

This dangerous place known as Pusbʼal Chaaj is where sacrifice was given and where wagers were made and bets were taken as to who would win and who would lose in a deadly game played to the Death; Death that could be brought back to Life by those who were born with the Emerald Seed-the Jade Bead of the Eternal Return just waiting and watching within them;

just watching and waiting for the moment when their sprouting out would bring their lineage back to life just as is revealed here in the Ancient Ancestral Account of the First Fathers of Maize Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu whose Jade Beads-Emerald Seed came back to life as Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. This is the story told here in the Popol Wuj that you will come to know in perfectly profound ancestral ways. Popol Wuj asks us to invoke the Divine Ancestors and their Kabʼawil by ʼNaming their Namesʼ just as it calls upon us to remember the Ancient Ones known as the Nawal Lords of Tollan Tzuy-Wa who we will come to know extremely well by the time we come to the end of this Sacred History of the Popol Wuj.

This is the Ancestral Account of the Ancient Word we know as the Mayaʼs Myth of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq. Popol Wuj is Ancient Ancestral Indigenous Scripture that asks us to open our hearts in order to clear the vision of our soul to awaken our psyche in order to engage our imagination so that we might see the magic play of mythic words and metaphors that reveal a world we have never gone before.

body:
In this way we are provided with the Nawal Perspective of the Mayaʼs Ancestral Soul through which to see through the Imaginal Realm with Ancestral Insight where we come to know who we are and what we were born to do in our lives lived out here on the Face of the Earth. Popol Wuj is quest to find this Nawal Perspective that is Magical Transforming Perspective of this Trickster People who know what it take to outsmart the Lords of the Underworld who only what Death for us in a world were deception and lies; trickery and cheating are the ways of those who rule the Ancestral Realm.

But this can all be changed and transformed through the Nawal Perspective we gain by becoming ʼoneʼ with the Sacred Word of Popol Wuj in order to ʼsee throughʼ the transcendent function that eliminates the Conquest of the Castilian Sun while erases the Colonizing Powers and all the damage they have do. All of this is eradicated from the Face of the Earth through the Popol Wuj that take us across this Mythic Bridge to the time and place that existed before el Adelantado Pedro Alvarado ever came riding on his Four-Footed Deer to this Ancient Ancestral Place known today as Mesoamerica. It is just our cunning creativity and our curious craftiness that will open the doors to opportunities that we never saw as being available to us before. Popol Wuj shows us the way to pass through the deadly Crossroads to continue on down the road on our passage from the demeaning world of the Colonial Powers to enlighten world of the Hero Twins who beguiling powers of Tricksters Lords know no other way than the Transcendent Function of Myth that bears us beyond to oppression to a world of opportunity in which everything is possible. Just like the magical dances and performances of the Hero Twins who are called upon to perform their Nawal Magic that will end the Lives of Death one and for all in this Ancient Story that tells of the Underworld Lords great fall that ends in the death and demise of the Lords of Death; the destruction and downfall of those scary, scary meanies who are the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. All of this is found right here in the Popol Wuj.

body:
Placing the Constellations in the Night Sky Placing Volcanic Eruption and Earthquake in the Mountains Placing the Boys, the Sons, the Twins on their Path Placing the Reader in the Middle of this Sacred Text

This Nawal Perspective of the Ancestral Soul is what will open up our Mythic Imagination to the Imaginal World of this Maya Myth of the Maize People. Our Ancestral Soul watches and waits within us to reveal the mythic beauty and mythic genius that are ours to be to be seen to be found to be known in this Ancient, Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

Let us take up this Mythic Masterpiece of the Ancient Word of Maize People-Ojer Tzij Ixim Winaq in order that we might also follow in the footsteps of the Hero Twins, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej, as they ʼorderʼ the Sky-Earth as they make their way walking and talking on the Face of the Earth.

These are those Boys who are Sons who Twins who are Grandsons who make their way around the Four Corners; Four Sides of the Sacred World placing their sacrificial offerings in the Northern Quadrant of the Night Sky and then in the Southern Quadrant of the Night Sky. It is then they turn towards the Western Horizon to leave their Sacrificial Offering in the Mountain of Meʼawan-Maize Mountain at the Falling Down Place of the Sun in the West. It is then that they move towards the Eastern Horizon to the leave their Sacrificial Offering in the Mountain of Saqiribʼal-Dawning Mountain there at the Coming-Out Place of the Sun in the East.

This is where we are headed in this Second Act of Creation that is a story of Creative Acts of Destruction as the Boys listen to the Divine Voice of the Heart of the Sky to carry-out Cosmogonic Acts of Ritual Sacrifice that ʼOrder the Face of the Sky to then Order the Face of the Earthʼ in preparation for the Forming and Shaping of the Maize People that comes to fruition in the Multiplying and Growing of the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo in the Fourth and Fifth Act of the Popol Wuj. This then is Sacred History that tells of the defeat and destruction of the Lords of the Death and their playing the ʼGameʼ of Human Sacrifice.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And in a most incredibly paradoxical mythic twist the Popol Wuj tells of the ʼenduring need for human sacrificeʼ that is required for humans beings to bring about the creation of abundance and prosperity. Popol Wuj tells us how the Divine Ancestors of the Kʼicheʼ People showed their First Four Fathers and First Four Mothers how to give ʼblood sacrificeʼ to provide and sustain their Kabʼawil who came from Tollan Tzuy-Wa where they had become accustomed to being feed their sacred sustenance of human blood and human hearts.

This is where the First Four Fathers begin hunting the Mountain People to feed their Kabʼawil. Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam provide sacrifice for Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz, Nikʼaj Taqʼaj.

In this way the Popol Wuj does not attempt to hide their Ancestral Life that is known as Our Shadows-Qamujibʼal. And yet they make it known that Human Sacrifice is the essence and reciprocal condition that the Kʼicheʼ Maya were born into as those who learn to practice Blood Sacrifice in order to live the Good Life: Utzilaj Kʼaslem; the Sacred Life, Saq Kʼaslem.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix is about to be ʼplacedʼ in the Northern Quadrant of the Night Sky as the One-Legged-One; Jun Raqan or the One Legged-Big Dipper of Ursa Mayor; the Four-Hundred Boys-Jobʼ Much Kʼajolabʼ will be placed in the Southern Quadrant of the Night Sky after their death and defeat by Sipakna-Volcano Boy.

body:
Sipakna-Volcano Boy will be placed in the West to become the Mountain of Sustenance known as Meʼawan-Bent-Over; Broken-in-Half Cane where great quantities of Maize are found stored within the Maize Mountains of Pan Paxil, Pan Kayala found here at Meʼawan. Kabʼraqan-Earthquake will be ʼplacedʼ in the East after his ʼsacrificeʼ at the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij to become the Dawn Mountain of Saqiribʼal or Sajribʼal: Dawning Mountain. This Primordial Mountain of the Dawn-Saqiribʼal is where the Sun continues to be welcomed into the World of the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew every New Year on February 19th-20th when the Cargador del Año or Year-Bearer-Mam is set on his Path of Walking the Four Corners; Four Sides of the Sky-Earth during the Solar Year of Eighteen-Twenty Day Months or Eighteen-Months of Twenty-Day Months plus the One Five Day Month of the Five Dangerous Days of the Wayebʼ. This is that story being told here.

Popol Wuj is the Ritual Drama formed from Five Ritual Acts played out on the Five Starlit Nights of the Wayebʼ:
