body:
First Night tells of the Cosmogonic Creation of the Earth-Ulew then the telling of the Animal People, Clay-Creature, Wooden Men, Reed Women… Second Night tells of the Defeat of the Giants Wuqubʼ Kaqix, Jobʼ Much Kʼajolabʼ-Four Hundred Boys; Sipakna and Kabʼraqan by the Hero Twins … Third Night tells of the Hero Twinʼs Descent into Xibʼalbʼa and their Defeat and Destruction of the Lords of Death; Lords of Xibʼalbʼa… Fourth Night tells of IxMuqane Molds and Models the First Four Mother-Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom and the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Sun of the Ixim Winaq, Pilgrimage to Tollan Tzuy-Wa… Fifth Night is the telling of the Invocation and Remembrance of Kʼicheʼ Noble Lineages and their Peregrination through the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom to Settle Mountains to Abandon Mountains; this Ancestral Path of the Kʼicheʼ Realm Comes to it Inevitable End with the Dawn of the Kaxlan Qʼij-Castilian Sun with the Arrival of Don Pedro de Alvarado known as Donadiu-Tonatiuh-Nahua Sun that issues in the Beginning of Krixtianoil- Dominican Catholic Christianity with the New Word-New Story-New Account of God and his Son Jesukristo spoken of as Chʼabʼal Tiox: Word of God.

We have taken up the ʼInvocation and Remembranceʼ of this Ancient Ancestral Account told with the Ancient Ancestral Word known as Ojer Tzij Popol Wuj: the Ancient Word of the Council Book of Ancestral Counsel; Ancestral Advice. Let us pick-up the pace by moving on from where we left off to get ourselves well situated En Medias Res-In the Midst of Things which is to say Amidst its Being Told; in the Middle of its Recitation: Right Here in the Middle of Things that Shine Bright like the Sun and Moon as well as that Great Big Star that Sweeps the Road to Open the Way so the Sun can Rise-Up in order to Walk-On with Wuqubʼ Kaqix who isnʼt as ʼBrightʼ as he imagines himself to be!

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Principle Bird Deity of the Maya Cosmos who is the major opponent and adversary of the Maize People will make his own introduction of himself in the calm white light before Dawn; there in the nostalgic glow of possibility that simmers in the Sky and upon the Earth just before Sunrise. Lord Seven Macaw known as Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kaqix is a False-Face Noble Lord whose name is translated as Lord Seven Macaw; Lord Seven Red Feathers or Wuqubʼ-Seven Kaq-Red Kʼix-Feathers: Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix; Seven Macaw is an ʼarrogant oneʼ and his self aggrandizement gives him a view of himself as a Big Man; Nimalaj Achi. Wuqubʼ Kaqix imagines himself to be the Great Lord which is a name perfectly in sync with the mythic archetype of a Principal Bird Deity; a Noble Lord of the Jungle Forest with a Treetop Throne in mythic Tree of Abundance from which he rules over his Ancestral Sun while gorging himself on its fruit from which ritual drunkenness is rooted in the ʼfermented liquorʼ known as ʼthree day sweetʼ that is potent mind-altering medicine once used in ritual initiation of the rites of passage for which it was once made.

Every element of the Popol Wuj is connected to everything else; and, so it is that the Nance Fruit Tree-Tajpal that provides the Sacred Sustenance of Wuqubʼ Kaqix is also the fruit used to make the liquor that the Four Hundred Boys will come to drink to become drunk to then die crushed here in this Sacred Narrative of Popol Wuj. Once they are drunk the First Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix known as Sipakna brings their initiation hut-kabʼal down on them killing workers, messengers, and advocates of the Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja on the Face of the Earth: Uwach Ulew. This is the Mesoamerican Myth of the Maize People that tells of the movement of the Sky-Earth through mythic figures and archetypes that personify the Forces of Nature spoken of in mythic ways.

Kabʼawil Two Way Seers of the Sky-Earth Kabʼa: ʼNameʼ

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Kabʼawil: The Sacred Naming of the Names Kabʼ: Honey Kabʼawil: Queen of the Hive Kabʼal: ʼFull and Completeʼ Kabʼawil: Twins and Twinship Kabʼawil these are Divine Twins-Kaʼibʼ Kabʼawil who are those whose ʼtwo-kabʼ way vision of the kabʼawilʼ allowed them to ʼsee-ilʼ with two-way vision that allowed them to see everything, everywhere, both near and far; above and below; past and future; truth and deception; they saw-il all there was to see-il on the Face of the Earth; Kabʼan. This two way vision of Kabʼawil is the ʼcapacityʼ that makes Kabʼawil the Two Way Seers of the Sky-Earth: Kabʼawil. Kabʼawil are those who see everything to know everything to be able to do everything they come to do.

The Twins will pull of tremendous acts of magic because they are Kabʼawil who are Nawal Winaq; Nawal Winaq who are of a nature-kʼojeʼik-condition that enables them to transform whatever they wish to transform with the intention of bring some sort of greater transformation in the World.

Kabʼawil need a bit of time and space to understand them because they will be with us and have been with us from the first utterance of this Ancient Account for it kabʼa means ʼnameʼ so that Kabʼawil are those who are named by the naming of their names; which is how Popol Wuj is begun with the naming of the names of the Kabʼawil who I call Divine Ancestors.

These Kabʼawil are those who embody the voice and ensoul the soul of the narrator of the Ancient Word; the voice of the narrator who is omniscient as all Kabʼawil always are. Letʼs take this name as far back as I have been able to do with the compilation of a ʼglyphic dictionary of Classic Chol Maya.

This potent name-kabʼa in the language of Classic Chol or Cholan or Chorti Maya means much more than name-kabʼa for the name Kabʼawil manifests sweet abundance-kabʼ awa a word formed from kabʼ-honey and wa; sustenance which in the case of Kʼabʼawil is seen as the ʼsweet abundanceʼ to provide sweet sustenance for the Queen of the Hive.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Were Maya Queens seen as Queen Bees? Yes, I believe they must have been since Bee Hives are well organized societies that produce sacred sustenance to feed and sustain those who feed and sustain the multiplying and growing of the People of the Pueblo. Bees are vital for the pollenization of the Maize growing in la Milpa so that the more Bees that exist the more honey is produced along with the production of more kernels of corn on each head of maize. In this sense Kabʼawil are those who ʼfill-outʼ in order to complete everything that is made and manufactured in by the Maya People of a Maya Pueblo.

Kabʼawil is said to be the ʼfull and completeʼ abundance of the kingdom that is distributed in perfect reciprocity between the Kabʼawil who provide the Rain and Wind for Maize and Cacao that provides abundant sustenance for the Maize People-Ixim Winaq who provide sacred sustenance to sustain the Kabʼawil through rituals and rites of sacrifice that shape the clouds that form the lightning and thunder that provide rain for the Cacao and Maize.

body: It is then the Sky is cleared of clouds as the North Wind is called in to bring forth the flowering and fruiting of the Maize growing in la Milpa. This is the way of the Kabʼawil, Maize in la Milpa and the Ixim Winaq who form this triangle of reciprocity that creates great abundance in the World… Kabʼawil are Deities that are complete-kabʼal in the sense they are those who are completely filled with sustenance through the reciprocal relation between Divinity; Kabʼawil and Humanity; Winaq and the Earth; Kabʼan-Ulew. Kabʼal signifies the idea of the fullness of abundance; the completeness of an order; the wealth of a people; the richness of a land; kabʼal- complete as in the head of maize replete with grain; the cacao pod filled with seeds; fruit trees burgeoning with fruit; clouds filled with water; nets teaming with fish, shrimp, and crabs. The complete definition of Kabʼawil is more than enough for you to take up a deeper search into the meaning of this most enigmatic name-kabʼa of these Divinities-Kabʼawil-Deities- Kabʼawil. Kabʼawil are those who might best be understood as the ʼNamed Onesʼ who only want to hear their names named through their ritual remembrance and invocation of the ʼNaming of the Namesʼ spoken in divine ways.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These names of the Kabʼawil ask to be pronounced in sacred ways in which the sacred names the Divine Ancestors and Kabʼawil were first pronounced at the very beginning of the Popol Wuj with the ʼNaming of the Namesʼ of the Divine Ancestors and their Kabʼawil known as the Divine Twins: Kabʼawil by having the number Two-Kaʼibʼ being transformed into a ʼdivine agentʼ by adding the suffix-il at the end of the name as in Kabʼawil. Kʼabʼawil are those who are brought into being through the Nawal Powers of Transformation that is one of the divine capacities of the Twins and Twinship that are the Powers of Creation that are experienced as the Nawal Powers of Transformation of Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ukʼuʼx Ulew as Jun Raqan Kaqulja who become Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz, Nikʼaj Taqʼaj and Ukʼuʼx Cho-Ukʼuʼx Palo Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz who become Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatzʼ who becomes Nakxit Qʼuqʼkumatz who becomes Rajawal AjRelebʼal Qʼij Quetzalcoatl of Tollan Tzuy-Wa who becomes a Nim Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz who the Ancient Word says changes and transforms in magical ways as the Nim Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz who is a Kabʼawil who is Nawal Winaq or Nawinaq!

To be a Kabʼawil is to exist through the Nawal Ways of Transformation that are also seen and known as Ancestral Change within Change in order to transform and change the Sky-Earth in divine ways that are magical ways. The prime of example of this is the Maize Plant as it changes on the outside of the husk as the cane, leaves, tassel, corn silk, and roots change to transform on the outside while the heads of maize change and transform in the inside within the husk in which the ʼone seedʼ that was planted has become 800 seeds on each and every head of corn.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This change within change is known as ʼjaloj-kʼexojʼ and is a true manifestation of the divine nature of maize because of the way great abundance is created from just one small spark of life so that ʼone becomes manyʼ which is exactly what essence of being a Kabʼawil is all about! Kabʼawil then emanate a sense of ʼTwo-ness-Kaʼibʼʼ that gives them the sense of ʼcompletenessʼ found in the divine sense of ʼtwinsʼ and complimentary ʼtwinshipʼ as coming from Two-Kaʼibʼ as the Two that is deified to become a Kabʼawil.

Kabʼawil are those who are the very essence from which comes all the Forming and Shaping of Creation through the Formation-Generation that sprouts forth in the Sky-Earth through the balancing and the harmonizing of the Twinning of Duality and all the endless forms it takes in the Sowing and the Dawning of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea; Kaj-Ulew; Cho-Palo.

It is the Two-ness of the Kabʼawil that bring forth the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings into the light of existence out of the darkness of non-existence to bring forth the sprouting out of the Trees and Vine; Men and Women; Maize and Cacao; Sun and Moon; Heat and Moisture; Wind and Rain; Life and Death; Earth and Sky; Sky and Water; Rain and Sun; Dew and Drought; Mother and Father; Word and Story; Song and Dance; Day and Night on and on and on as the manifestation, revelation, and expression of Two-ness of the Kabʼawil with their Dual Powers; Twin Powers found throughout this Book of Counsel; this Council Book with its many names both sacred and profane of the Sacred and Divine that lead to the Creation and Formation of Divinity known as Kabʼawil.

Let us move quickly into a deeper understanding the Divine Twins who are the Hero Twins of Popol Wuj who are named by this Sacred Text as Kabʼawil for it is they who are Two who speak and act as One those making them divine in every way.

Junajpu, IxBʼalamkej Cultural Heroes of the Maize People Maize People: Ixim Winaq Perfect Path-Saqetal-Perfect Way Seven Scarlet Macaw-Wuqubʼ Kaqix-Principal Bird Deity

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Hero Twins as Cultural Heroes of the Maize People must prepare the Sky-Earth for the arrival of the Maize People who are of course led by the First Mother-Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Maya; the Kʼicheʼ Maya who will come to know and name themselves as the Ixim Winaq; the People of Maize; the Maize People: Ixim Winaq.

The Maize People will eventually take over the Forest Kingdom of Wuqubʼ Kaqix but before that takes place the Cultural Heroes of the Maize People, JunAjPu, IxBʼalamKej must take Wuqubʼ Kaqix out of his ʼThrone set upon his Tree of Sustenanceʼ because he prides himself as being a Great Lord while being seen by those below as being a pretentious self-aggrandizing Lord who is an ʼarrogant oneʼ by nature of his red plumage and the ʼfineryʼ of Silver Throne; his Turquoise adornment; his Jade embellishment all of which leads to his self-aggrandizement- nimarisaj rib-self-magnification. Wuqub Kaqix only says he is a Noble Ruler because of the his ʼtrappings and trimmingsʼ that are nothing more a manifestation of material wealth which begs one of the principal questions asked in the Popol Wuj: what does it take to be a Great Lord and Noble Ruler of oneʼs People and Pueblo? The Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Maya will answer that question through their Courageous Acts and Regal Speech; just as they will make themselves out to be perfect examples-saqetal-precious pathway for the People of their Pueblo to follow by becoming the perfect path-saqetal that is exemplified by the divine way the Noble Lords act and speak through their Noble Ways and Noble Words.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Wuqubʼ Kaqix saw himself as a Nawal Winaq which, is the way he wanted to be seen by those who would follow him who embodied and ensouled the Perfect Path-Saqetal-Perfect Way to be copied perfectly; to be followed precisely on his path and mirrored exactly in his way while being imitated flawlessly in his speech as the Perfect Ancestral Exemplum-Saqetal to be followed as a Nawal Winaq who as a Divine Ancestor embodied and ensouled their magical powers of transformation known as ʼancestral geniusʼ that was the very essence and condition of the nawal nature of being of Nawal Winaq who would come to transform the Sky-Earth; Lake- Sea once the Wooden People followed the exemplary path that was what Wuqubʼ Kaqix imagined to be his perfect way of being in the world of the Sky-Earth. Wuqubʼ Kaqix as a Great Lord; Nim Ajaw wanted only that the Wooden People would do as he did; to speak as he spoke; to act as he acted; to think as he thought; to be as he would always be; to become as he always was; to be as he had already become which according to Wuqubʼ Kaqix was a Perfect Example-Saqetal because of the way he spoke and acted; walked and talked; reflected and respond just like a Divine Ancestor.

It was Divine Ancestors who changed and transformed just like a Nawal Winaq who communicated and connected with other with concern and care. These Nawinaq spoke and acted just like the Ancient Ancestral Magician who came to show the Wooden People the sacred way to be in order to become perfect Descendants who would come to transform into the perfect Replacements of the Divine Ancestors.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These Divine Ancestors were those who showed their Replacements; their Descendants the ʼWays of Lifeʼ by expressing their transforming nature, condition as well as their transformative essence and way of being and becoming in the world that was Nawal in every way. This is what Wuqubʼ Kaqix did and said when he showed one and all that he indeed was the ʼSacred Pathʼ that was the ʼSacred Wayʼ of being and becoming: Saqetal in every way. JunAjPu, Ixbʼalamkej will act and speaking in ʼbeautiful waysʼ as the ʼcoincidentia oppositoriumʼ to the ʼugly acting and ugly speakingʼ ways of Wuqubʼ Kaqix. Seven Scarlet Macaw; the Principal Bird Deity will always act and speak alone as a single, solitary lord without a companion; without a complement; without a partner to balance his weakness and correct his mistakes; improve his faults while saving him from his failings.

This arrogant Bird Deity rules without a Co-Regent with who to reign over his Noble Kingdom like all the Kʼicheʼ Lords will come to do. Kʼicheʼ Lords will always rule with a companion who will complement their ways as rulers who will always rule in a regal form of Twinship that is a noble kind of Companionship.

This is something you will come to see in order to know about the Kʼicheʼ Lords who like the Hero Twins will come to their rule and sovereignty in perfectly complementary ways; ways that will strengthen and protect one another like Junajpu is strengthened and protected by Ixbʼalamkej; like Ukʼuʼx Kaj is balanced by Ukʼuʼx Ulew; like the Heart of the Sky is harmonized by the Heart of the Earth; just as Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz is inspired by Jun Raqan Kaqulja so it is that Jun Raqan enlivens the competitive essence of Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz. This Ancient Ancestral Account of Twins and Twinship is formed and shaped by the balance and harmony of the Ancestral Word; Ancestral Way of Ancient Maya who knew their World as a Primordial Pair that brought forth prosperity out of the Divine Twinship of the Sky- Earth; Kaj-Ulew. The Maya Hero Twins come from this Primordial Couple that becomes Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane who are the Grandfather and Grandmother of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
JunAjPu, Ixbʼalamkej are the Original Ones; they are Ancient Ancestral Ones; they are the First Ones; they are those who embody Hunter and Hunted as the Jaguar hunts the Deer; as the Deer is hunted by the Jaguar. Their blowgun is the ancient, ancestral weapon used in their hunting that will cause the world to move and transform as they perform the work of Cultural Heroes by putting the Giants of the Past Fallen Age in their place to order the world of the Ixim Winaq. JunAjPu, Ixbʼalamkej act and speak as hunters who are Cultural Heroes so they can begin their lives with the Sowing and Dawning of their Bright Life; Saq Kʼaslem experienced as the Perfect Life; Saq Kʼaslem lived out as the Divine Life; Saq Kʼaslem in the world known as Kaj-Ulew; Sky-Earth.

This is that story of the Twins and Twinship told here where Jun AjPu and IxBʼalamKej are twinned within themselves as hunter and hunted just as they are twinned with one-an-other as hunter and hunted as Jaguar hunts the Deer; as the Deer hunts the Maize; as the Blowgunner Boys protects their Maize growing in the Milpa where the Jaguar hunts the Deer that devours the Maize that comes to fruition in the Milpa. The symbolic soul and essence of the character of Junajpu is his emblematic ʼcerbatana- blowgun-pubʼ who will protect the Maize flowering and fruiting in the Milpa from all the many Birds and Animals who only want to devour its sweet cane, leaves, and kernels as their own sacred sustenance. This gives us Pubʼ and Pu that come together in the name Jun-Aj-Pu who is from the Noble Reed Place of Abundance and Sacred City of Artists, Priests, Calendars, Observatories, Scholars, Painters, and Rulers known as Tollan or Pu.

So Junajpu might be best thought of as Noble Lord of the Sacred City of Pu known as Ancient One; Noble One of Tollan Tzuy-Wa. But Pu sounds like ʼPuj-Pustuleʼ as Professor Oswaldo Chinchilla Mazariegos says in his interpretive understanding of this ʼancestral nameʼ and the ʼsacred story of sacrificeʼ of the ʼPustule One-AjPuj-Pimply Oneʼ who will throw himself onto the sacrificial fire where he is transformed into the Sun.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Indeed, AjPuj is seen throughout Maya Art and Iconography with round pustules covering his body; pustules that ooze pus. This must come from the ʼother half of the storyʼ not told here in this Popol Wuj that does not tell of these warrior twins who are ball-playing brothers that are hunting companions who may develop pustules from the ʼmosquitoʼ bites spoken of in this story or some other such narrative that tells of the Chechen or Manchineel Tree of the Petén that well leaving ʼweeping woundsʼ of those who do not take care when making their way through the jungle.

AjPubʼ, AjPu, AjPuj, AjPus is a Twin who is born with his brother Ixbʼalamkej to his Mother: IxKikʼ. They are born standing up straight like maize sprouts shoot up and out of the Earth on the Mountain and in the Wilderness as Hunter and Hunted. Jun Aj-Pubʼ as a Blowgun Boy or AjPubʼ giving him his name: Junajpubʼ or One Blowgun Boy; the Ancient One-AjPu who is the Young Hunter who will become the Ancient Old Hunter who will become the Hero and Defender of his ancestral lineage the Junajpu Lineage of the Maize People: Ixim Winaq. Let us turn to his Twin Brother Little Jaguar-Deer Ix-Bʼalam-Kej; he who comes from-Ix the Jaguar- Bʼalam and Kej-Deer who are the Hunter and the Hunted.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These Hero Twins are ʼtwinned from withinʼ as those who go to their Milpa to protect their Maize. There in the Milpa amongst the ʼMaize Treesʼ is where the Grandsons go to carry- out their Ancestral Burden that is theirs to continue to perform as Hunters in the Forested World of the Many Trees of the Kʼicheʼ. This is where the Milpa becomes the ripe green lure for the hungry animals. Maize grows into the sweet temptation that call in the herbivores who want to take what is theirs. These herbivores and omnivores enter that which is no longer theirs for the taking. Yet they take their ancestral sustenance that now grows amongst the rows of the Milpa that was once their Forest Floor. This is the Forest Floor that we are told at the beginning of Popol Wuj is the ʼancestral realm and natural domainʼ of the Animal People that is covered with tasty green herbs that sprout to life in the Rainy Season. But that way of life is no more but that doesnʼt stop the deer and rabbits; the jabali and coati; the puma and jaguar; the coyote and fox; the blue jay and crow; the green parakeet and scarlet macaw; the grackle and doves from entering amongst the sweet leaves and canes of maize to chew-up which is theirs for the taking.

But there waits the Jaguar and Puma who place themselves up on a limb of tree just watching and waiting for a sweet-tasting Animal Being from the First Creation to pass below the branch of their tree to offer-up themselves up as the sacred sustenance of fleshy red meat. This is where our mythic imagination is called upon to complete the other half of the story that is not told here yet so hungry to be brought forth from the depths of our mythic imagination.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Junajpu has a Twin Brother Ix-Bʼalam-Kej or Ix Bʼalam Kiej to form the name Ixbʼalamkej who is known as Little Jaguar-Deer, the Hunter and the Hunted, who is Lord of the Wild Animals; Lord of the Wilderness. Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are both depicted with their Father Jun Junajpu in an iconic image of Maya Art that shows the Three Generations of the Maize Deities. This polychrome painting is brought forth on a Sacrificial Ceramic Plate tells the story of the Maize Deities that is told here in the Popol Wuj.

This is the image just as this is the story of the Hero Twins who bring their Father the Maize Lord back to life as he sprouts forth out of the skull-like seed of Xpiyakok who cracks open on the Tortoise Shell Carapace that is painted on the Resurrection Plate found in Boston Museum of Fine Arts and on the Blom Plate of Museo de Chetumal in Quintana Roo, Mexico.

In one image these Three Generations of the Maize Deities-Xpiyakok; Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej sprout back to life through the Ancestral Soul as the Ancestral Essence of the Mayaʼs Mythic Imagination of the Maize People whose origins begin here with the sprouting forth of the Ancestral Skull-Seed of Xpiyakok: He that Sprouts forth from the Tortoise Shell Carapace.

In this scene IxBʼalamKiej is named by a named glyph as Yax Bʼalam and this is how he is known throughout in the Classic Period. In the image found on the Resurrection Plate Yax Bʼalam-Ixbʼalamkej pours water from his Grandmotherʼs water jug over his Father-Jun Junajpu known as Jun Ixim-One Maize Lord in the Classic Period while his twin brother Jun Ajaw- Junajpu attends to the sprouting image of the Rising Return of the Maize that is the First Father of Maize: Jun Ixim.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This Skull-Seed-Sprout is Grandfather of the Maize Deity known in the Classic Period as Jun Nal Yeey-Xpiyakok who is brought back to life by his Classic Period Grandsons Jun Ajaw, Yax Bʼalam known to the Kʼicheʼ Maya as Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. Imagine how ancient this story of the Maize People is if itʼs illustrated with such detail so long ago and yet Popol Wuj is telling the same mythical narrative in its nawal essence and form it takes. But then again what other form do myths take in Cultures and Civilizations as deeply traditional is the Maya Culture and Mesoamerican Civilization. The two-kabʼ of them are attending the ʼrebirthʼ of the Maize Deity; Jun Ajpu with a ʼhand gestureʼ that speaks of ʼrebirthʼ and Yax Bʼalam with his Tinaja-Qʼebʼal-Water Jug taken from Ixmuqane the Grandmother of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq. This is why the Father and Uncle; Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are named only as their Fathers ʼas ifʼ they were ʼjust one- xa junʼ who rises up out of the skull-seed of their Father-Xpiyakok-Jun Nal Yeey who rises up and out of the tortoise shell earth: Xpi-ya-kok. Xpiyakok the Grandfather of the Hero Twins: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are perfect examples of Nawal Winaq giving them miraculous powers of transformation and it is their powers to transforms the Sky-Earth that continues the work of the Formers and Shapers. This work of Forming, Shaping will then be taken up by their descendants just as the forming, shaping of this translation expresses the molding, modeling of the written word in order that this story can live-on through further transformation of further translation and the necessary interpretation needed for its words to be understood on Maya terms, in Maya context, and in Maya ways of knowing-feeling the Ancient Word.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The name Junajpu suggests a variety of different yet congruent meanings for he is the First One from the Place of Reeds which makes him the Ancient One Blowgun Boy who becomes the incarnation of the last day of the twenty day names of the Two-Hundred and Sixty Day Divinatory Calendar. This divinatory calendar comes to its fruition on the last day of the Two-Hundred and Sixty Day; the day Thirteen Junajpu or Thirteen Ajaw-Oxlajuj Ajaw; Oxlajuj Ajpu; known also as the day Oxlajuj Junajpu. This is the last of the ʼJunajpuʼ lineage of its Thirteen Lineages that are named here in the last pages of the Popol Wuj when it ʼNames the Namesʼ of the Lineages and their Thirteen Generations.

Junajpu as One Blow-gun Boy is a magical hunter who is the ʼfirstʼ of ʼtwoʼ twins. He is the one who gets the two into the right kind of transforming trouble while his brother Ixbʼalankeʼ is their protector, savior who gets them out of their hyper-challenging ordeals that change the world once and for all. IxBʼalamKejʼ uses his miraculous powers as Lord of the Animals which he inherits from his mother IxKikʼ the Moon Maiden, Moon Mother, Goddess of Blood, Gatherer of Rubber, Gatherer of Resinous Sap in all the forms ʼsap or tree blood-kikʼ takes such as Copal Incense and the Red Blood of the Dragon Tree whoʼs sap is used by IxKikʼ to create a cunning escape from the Lords of Death; Lords of the Underworld; Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

Ixbʼalamkej calls on his Moon Mother; Blood Gather; the Moon Goddess IxKikʼ in hidden, magical ways. As you know only too well that Ixbʼalamkiej signifies he-she of the Jaguar-Deer making him the hunter and hunted all at once and all in one mythical figure; one mythical being. As Xbʼalankeʼ this Nawal Being becomes the ʼhidden face of the Lunar Jaguarʼ who looks out upon the world to the South from the perspective Full Moon as she-he sets upon the Western Horizon where the Sun sets at Sunset. In this aspect Xbʼalankeʼ is known as the ʼhidden Sun, Jaguar moonʼ and so it is that Xbʼalankeʼ will become the Night Sun as the Full Moon at the end of their lives and story as Blow-Gun Hunter Boys sent to the World to keep the Sky-Earth from dying dead.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
I have decided to use the name Ixbʼalamkej because of the way it forms a female gender balance with male name of Jun Ajpu which is the proper way of balancing and harmonizing the genders in twins, couples, and pairs. I also asked many, many Maya Day-keepers about the pronunciation of this name in the contemporary world of Maya Day-Keeping and Prayer- Making. All of who were adamant about their pronunciation of IxBʼalamKej in which-as you know with the past examples of poj going to po; and, koj going to ko so that kej moves to ke. Makes sense; sounds right; looks good; feels goods which is enough reason for me to write kej not keʼ in the name written as Ixbʼalamkej; or, even as IxBʼalamkiej as is pronounced and written among Maya Tzʼutujil speakers who live out their Traditional Maya ways by dancing the Jaguar- Deer Dance known as ru Xojo Ixbʼalamkiej.

So it is Ixbʼalamkej that I have chose as the proper way to ʼspellʼ in order to invoke, in order to enchant the Number Two Son, Twin Brother of Number One Son Jun Aj Pu or Jun Aj Pubʼ or Jun Aj Puj. Jun Ajpu who is the Ancient Ancestral One of the Ancient Ancestral Place Thick with the Abundance of the Reeds and Rushes-Jun AjPu who is known as you know as Jun AjPubʼ the One-Jun known as One Hunter-JunAjPubʼ-One Blowgun Son: Jun Aj Pubʼ.

This Jun AjPuj or Jun Aj Pus is he of the ʼOne-Junʼ mark of identified here a pustules that are the ʼmark of deathʼ identifying Jun Aj Puj as the Grandson of his Grandfather from Xibʼalbʼa who is Kuchuma Kikʼ known as Blood Gatherer; Rubber Gatherer; Incense Gatherer of the Underworld Realm of Death and Disease known as Xibʼalbʼa. This then is a partial naming of the names that name these Maya Hero Twins that may have changed in pronunciation depending on the Cultural or Natural Context they found themselves in.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This knowledge that I must provide you with here is the knowledge that all Maya would have known at the opening of this scene. So now you know what you need to know to move down the road with the Boys, the Sons, the Twins known to all as the one set of twins that speak as those who are the One formed; the One shaped by Twin Souls that is suggested in the naming of the names of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej: the hunter and the hunted. Junajpu is pronounced in English as Hoon-ah-pooh and in Spanish as Jun-aj-pu just like it sounds.

The pronunciation of Xbʼalamkej spoken in English is sounded out as Ix Bʼalam keh or Xbʼalankeʼ Ix Bʼa-lan-kay or in Spanish as Ix-Bʼalam-kej or Ix-Bʼalan-keʼ just as it is sounded out phoneme by phoneme. It is important to grasp these names and their pronunciation right from the very beginning because these two will be with us all the way through to the end. It would be a shame to not be saying their names properly as I have heard done so many times in the past.

IxBʼalamKej: He-She of the Jaguar Deer Dance is he who creates the archetypal movement of the hunter and the hunted; as Ixbʼalamkej transforms into the movement of the wind who coaxes the movement of the Wind Jaguar with the Deer Dance that awakens the Wind Jaguar who takes up the chase of an enchanting Deer Women whose beguiling dance entices the sleepy Wind Jaguar to take up the hunt. This then is the mythic metaphor of the Sun chasing the Moon or Venus as the Deer Hunter chasing the Sun as a Deer Women who drops into the Sea as Venus follows the falling celestial sphere; the flaming solar ball plunging into the cosmic chaos of the watery wet world of the Dead Ancestors.

The name Junajpu suggests a variety of different yet congruent meanings for he is the First One from the Place of Reeds which makes him the Ancient One Blowgun Boy who becomes the incarnation of the last day of the twenty day names of the Two-Hundred and Sixty Day Divinatory Calendar that flowers and fruits with this sacred day known as Junajpu; Jun Junajpu; Ajaw Junajpu; or just, Ajaw: Noble Lord.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Junajpu, Xbʼalamkej or Xbʼalamkiej are perfect twins, as one person they act in perfect collaboration with one-an-other to bring about the transformation of the Sky-Earth. These twins act as one, speak as one, shoot as one, and dance as one in a world where twins and twinship, couples and colleagues, pairs and partners form and shape the metaphor of divine collaboration that brings the Sky-Earth to fruition.

Watch the way these two work together just as you watch your spirit and soul, mind and body, persona and anima, conscious and unconscious as they work together with one another to bring about the necessary changes needed to understand this story through reflection and introspection that creates perspective that in turn helps one change and transform through our understanding of ourselves as those who are ʼtwinned from withinʼ this is the Maya perspective known in the Western Tradition as Persona and Shadow, Actor and Anima; Actress and Animus.

There is no end to our revelation of the understanding of these perfectly polysemic names: Jun AjPu; IxBʼalamKiej whose meaning depends on the context in which they are found. You will be drawn to fire-up your own imagination to find other meanings that arise from the mythic metaphors created by different cultural contexts and natural realms in which these Boys find themselves. It is you engage in a dialogue with the Imaginal Realm of the Twins through the mythic imagination as the place of initiation on this mythic journey of self-knowledge and its quest for ancestral transcendence experienced as the unity of psyche and myth.

En Media Res: In the Middle of the Myth Seven Scarlet Macaw-Wuqubʼ Kaqix

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
So let us place ourselves in the middle of this myth that is a plot in order for you to understand where we are before taking up the road with the Hero Twins in the direction they are moving. And where we are moving is down the road with the Hero Twins each shouldering a blowgun on their way to take Wuqubʼ Kaqix out of his Nance Tree; his Tapʼal Tree where he takes his mid-day meal of bitter, tart coastal fruit a top the giant Nance Tree where he is perched upon his throne above the Jungle Kingdom over which he reigns as its Sovereign Lord and Ruler.

This way of Wuqubʼ Kaqix will not do for the noble ethics of the Maize People and their New Sun and Moon under which Noble Lords must prove themselves through hard work and ritual sacrifice; the keeping of the days in the Sacred Calendar, blood-letting and the bleeding of oneself; abstention from the ʼgood-lifeʼ through fasting and long pilgrimages, all which manifest the true mark of a Noble Ruler of the People who over time becomes a Great Lord of the Pueblo. Merit, not material wealth is the way a Noble Ruler should be chosen. And this is where we find ourselves in this story that we enter En Media res, which is to be dropped in to a drama that is in full swing.

In fact we have entered the mythic narrative of the Wooden People; which is to say we have entered the ʼmythic plotʼ of the ʼmythic narrativeʼ we just saw the very end of with the destruction of the Wooden People. But now, here, we are about to find out what that Sun of the Wooden People was like, in order to develop an idea of what it takes to be and become a Cultural Hero who opens the path to the Dawning of the Maize of the People.

We are entering the Myth of the Maya Hero Twins that plays out in the Mythic Age of the Wooden People; an Age that Seven Scarlet Macaw-Wuqubʼ Kaqix says he is the ʼBright Lightʼ of their Sun and their Moon. This is the Myth of the Maize People that is like a ʼDreamʼ where ʼtime and spaceʼ are not well defined yet I feel it important you understand-more or less- where we stand at the opening of this Second Act of Popol Wuj.

body:
It is here in the opening scene of the Second Act in which Wuqubʼ Kaqix cries out that he is the Lord of the Face of the Earth and how he is the ʼPerfect Path-Saqetalʼ to be followed as the ʼPerfect Example-Saqetalʼ that shows his ʼfollowersʼ just how to speak and just how to act as a Noble Lord. The Hero Twins, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej, do not agree nor does the Heart of the Sky who is the true ʼSaqetal-Sacred Pathʼ to be followed on the Path of being and becoming the People of Maize: Ixim Winaq.

This desire to be and become the Perfect Descendants of the Divine Ancestors of the Ixim Winaq is what the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj is all about. Popol Wuj shows us that Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are the Saqetal-Perfect Exemplum who the Young Initiates of Noble Lords are called to follow in their Sacred Speech and Heroic Acts.

Human beings need ʼFine Examplesʼ to follow in lives that require divine protection and divine guidance which is precisely what the Ancient Word and Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj once provided to Kʼicheʼ People in order to sustain the Ancestral Soul of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo. Popol Wuj is the Saqetal of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom which makes it a ʼSacred Pathʼ that is a ʼPerfect Pathʼ that protects and guides all those who are called to is Ancient Word that tells the Ancestral Account in the Book of Counsel that is a Sacred Book of Ancestral Advice.

On the Edge of Ages; On the Threshold of Suns Between and betwixt Past and Future Two Stories: One People, One Grain Two Heroes; One Savior, Crosses and Crossbeams

body:
There is no question that those who read and contemplate the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj will learn how to speak and act as Perfect Replacements of the Divine Ancestors of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. There is no doubt that the legitimacy and authority of the Popol Wuj was destroyed by the Dominican Order in their quest to convert the Maya to Christianity and the Word of God with its many ʼWooden Saints and Wooden Virgins-Maria, Mothers-Ana, and Grandmothers-Saraʼ who became the ʼreplacementsʼ of the Divine Ancestors alongside the Wooden Figure of the Savior who was nailed to a Wooden Cross between Twin-Thieves that were the companions of the Jesukristo who laid in his coffin as the Just Judge or Justo Juez that was the exact definition of the Lords of the Xibʼalbʼa who were Lords of the Death known as Jun Kame-One Death and Wuqubʼ Kame-Seven Death.

These were Lords of the Dead and Judges of the Word-Measurers of the Word just as Jesukristo who was the Justo Juez that was seen carrying his sacred tree on his shoulder just as Sipakna will do all by himself. And on and on one could go as the Dominicans must have done when doing everything they could to transform the Popol Wuj into the Sacred Histories of the Castilian Sun. This is why the Dominican Brothers wanted a ʼperfect exampleʼ of their Ancient Word to be written by the Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word so they could then use translate the Ancestral Account of the Kʼicheʼ Maya into the Maya Kʼicheʼ Language that when heard by the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ sounded very, very similar to the Original Sacred History of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is why the Popol Wuj is so authentically Kʼichean because those who were consigned to write it were given permission to reveal what was truly ʼtheirs in lifeʼ to bring to fruition on the Face of the Earth. And so it is that we can begin the telling of the Second Act of Popol Wuj in which the Hero Twins enter into open conflict with Wuqubʼ Kaqix who is none other than the Nawal of the Heart of Sky whose destructive forces are turned against the Maize People and their sacred sustenance Maize that is sown in their Milpa to be devoured by the Animal People who Wuqubʼ Kaqix says is their Lord and Ruler as the Bright Light of their Sun; Bright Light of their Moon; the Sun and Moon of the Age of the Wooden People.

Remember this because Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej will ascend into the Sky as the Sun and Moon of the Maize People. This is the direction we are moving and it is best you know this since the Maya knew well.

Here then is when the story begins; the story of Wuqubʼ Kaqix and Chimalmat; their Sons Sipakna and Kabʼraqan; and, the Hero Twins: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. This is the story of Wuqubʼ Kaqix and his wife Chimalmat that tells of their two sons: Volcano Boy-Sipakna; Earthquake Son-Kabʼraqan.

Here then begins the ancestral account of their defeat by the Boys; the Sons; the Twins: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. Not yet was there the Sun, but there was the One who puffed himself up ʼas ifʼ he were the Sun; the puffed-up One who was not the Sun was the One known as Wuqubʼ Kaqix; Seven Scarlet Macaw was his name.

It was just ʼself-aggrandizement-nimarisaj ribʼ that created his conceit and it was just his self-aggrandizing conceit that caused him to think upon himself as a Big Man; a Big Man-Nimalaj Achi who saw himself as Big People: Nimaʼ Winaqʼ.

body:
This was the ʼArrogant Oneʼ known as Seven Red Feathers-Wuqubʼ Kaq Kʼix spoken of as Seven Macaw: Wuqubʼ Kaqix. Wuqubʼ Kaqix saw himself as a Great Lord that shone like the calm white light; the soft white light, the quite white light-Saqnatanoj that shone as is shined with a tone like a rich radiant remembrance of the Sun and Moon; Saqnatanoj as the first rays of Sun are known; dawning rays of the Sun that feel like the remembrance of the Sunriseʼs even warmth and the Moonlightʼs balanced perfection: Saqnatanoj.

Saqnatanoj This, then, was when soft white light enveloped the Sky-Earth in the calm quiet glow of the Pre-Dawn Sun; its luminous warmth of smooth golden light blanketed the Face of the Earth in an ancient, ancestral radiance of remembrance recalling the moment when the Ancient Ones, the Divine Ancestors watched and waited for the First Dawn; a memory of an Age; a recollection of a Sun that had come and gone.

Saqnatanoj: the time, the place; the moment; the space just before the arrival of the shimmering, shining sparkle of the bright white light of Dawn: Saqnatanoj.

Saqnatanoj: the embodiment, the ensoulment of the resplendent recollection; nostalgic remembrance of the radiant recuerdo y recolección of the Sunʼs first rays of light at Daybreak; there on the horizon at Sunrise; the glistening glint and glimmer of the silky-smooth glow of Dawn, just named, just known as: Saqnatanoj.

Saqnatanoj: an all-embracing divine white light that envelops the Sky-Earth in the Pre- dawn hour on the Pre-dawn horizon before the Sunrise erupts from below to swallow the Sky with its brilliant bright light that explodes across the Face of the Earth: Saqnatanoj. Saqnatanoj: that subtle nostalgic remembrance of the origins of the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew in the Pre-dawn hour just before the ʼsprouting forth of the Sunʼ showers its bedazzling brilliance and heat that ripples across the Lake-Sea; that murmurs as it echoes over the Earth-Sky illuminating the Sacred World-Santo Mundo-Saq Ulew with its Ancestral Recollection of the Ancestral Soul that emanates from the diffuse white light of Saqnatanoj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so this filtered light from past is brought forth to encourage; to inspire; to invoke; to enchant; charm and beguile the Nawal Intuition; Ancestral Imagination; Primordial Intelligence; Sacred Genius-Saq Naʼoj; the dim recollection of Divine Remembrance-Saq Natbʼal that radiates from the warm glow of Saqnatanoj.

This is the time and place when and where Day-keepers and Prayer-makers rise from sleep and its dreams to kneel before their dusty altars covered in wax and memories. It is there where they light the first candles so that they might burn bright in the dim light of the Dawn. The Ancestors called in; called down by the burning candles and alluring incense offered up to them to invoke their divine powers of miraculous change and magical transformation. It is a simple yet powerful intention to wake before Dawn to ʼname the nameʼ of the Divine Ancestors in remembrance of those who had lived long ago to leave their descendants to continue on their Sacred Road guided and protected by those who had gone before; those who had sown their replacements so that they might flower and fruit with abundance to provide oneʼs Lineage like never before.

It was all decided in the Pre-Dawn hours by those who were born with the strength and daring to become Prayer-makers and Day-keepers who came into this world with a destiny that was pure Ancestral Powers to bring forth health and abundance for those who were theirs to show care and concern for there at the Pre-Dawn time of that which is known as Saqnatanoj.

This then is when Day-Keepers and Diviners; Seers and Knowers all of whom are Prayer- Makers begin their petitionary prayers and pleading-petitions intent on enchanting their Kabʼawil with their beguiling invocations. But before those incantation can be intoned there comes the ʼsing-songʼ cadence of the grateful sound of sweetness as prayerful Women and petitioning Men give thanks to then give praise for all theyʼve been given in difficult lives formed from constant struggle and shaped by endless effort in world where one must be hard just to break even never mind getting ahead.

body:
Maltiox, Maltiox; Gracias, Gracias; Thirteen times Maltiox; Oxlajuj-Thirteen times Thank You as this simple prayer goes; Thirteen Times Thank You as this simple incantation of gratitude is invoked to be heard by all those Deities that inhabit the Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Earth. Gratitude is given by those who now kneel on before their altars enveloped incense while being warmed by candle light in this calm quite time of the Day lit-up by the First Rays of the Sun known and named: Saqnatanoj. This is the time when and where those who are the Mother-Fathers of their Ancestral Lineages beg and beseech the Pre-Dawn Sun for all that must be done and for everything the family needs to do as well as all that the community requires; while mentioning oneʼs rivals and adversaries how they must be taken care of too at Sunrise.

This is when Prayer-makers and Day-keepers address Face of the Day; Face of the Sun as Kinich Ajaw he who is the ʼSun-Faced Lordʼ is named by the name of each and every day of the Divinatory Calendar to then have this Day met at Dawn single out as the One whoʼs characteristic ways of being and becoming a Nawal Lord and Rule of the Sacred Count of Days is spoken to in intimate and familiar kind sort of ways in order that this most Day understands the Day-keeper who speaks knows what She-He is speaking of as Mother-Father; Chuch-Qajaw who is Day-Keeper; a Keeper and Counter of Days known and named: AjQʼij: She of the Sun; He of the Sun.

This is when the Sunʼs Nawal is invoked as the Destiny and Direction of the Day with its Path and its Ways. This is when the Fate and Fortune of Face of the Earth is invoked at the ʼBreak-of-Dayʼ as the names are named of the Twenty Nahuales-Naguales-Nawales of the Twenty Days that are now named as the Noble Lords and Rulers of the ʼMountain-Plain; Juyubʼ- Taqʼajʼ; the Noble Lords and Rulers known as the Sun-Faced Lords-Kinich Ajaw are called down to be called in as those who have always ruled and reigned with the Sovereign Power and Authority over the ʼFace of the Earth-Rajawal Uwach Ulewʼ

body:
Here we are presented with this heartfelt mythic image of the mythic imagination that feeds as it sustains our Ancestral Soul; our Indigenous Soul that is all of our Ancestral Inheritance as those who were born and raised here on the Face of the Earth here in these Américas where the spilt blood of our Ancestors has mixed with the soil creating ʼmudʼ out of the blood given by those who died ignorant of who they truly were. And from that Earth mixed with Indigenous and European Blood was molded and modeled a New Formation; New Creation whose Indigenous Essence live on in Our Indigenous Soul.

We are the Formed One; We, the Shaped Ones who have been formed and shaped by the Myth and History we have lived out here on the Face of the Earth in which the best of Indigenous America and the best of European America has found space to live within through the Sacred Indigenous Word of the Popol Wuj that has molded and modeled; crafted and created us like no generation of Humanity before.

This time of Saqnatanoj awakens us to our New Potential formed from New Intentions of the Ancestral Soul of Indigenous America that was sown within us as young children to sprout forth as we grew-up hungry to change and transform our World so that today the Flowering and Fruiting of the Ancient Word comes to life in this Translation and Interpretation of Popol Wuj in which mythic words like Saqnatanoj are brought forth into the light of Dawn as the mythic metaphors that sprout forth from us after being sown in us so long ago.

body:
These are Words and Metaphors that tell us of the Sun that hungers to be sustained and provided for through our remembrance and recollection of its light and that lightʼs capacity to awaken us to love and light that is the essence of care and concern that exists within our Ancestral Soul that thirsts to be fed by the Mythic Images and Mythic Words found here in Popol Wuj. This is the Sun that warms us with its light in an Age that transforms everyday with a profound sense of hope that is inherent to the rebirth and renewal of lifeʼs possibilities with each New Day; an image known to you well as the Sowing and the Dawning; Ewaxibʼal, Saqiribʼal. This is an ancient ancestral mythic image that sprouts forth from beneath the Earth just below the Horizon from where it rises-up to climb and climb like a cloud; like the mist; like a mountain that erupts like a Volcano with New Life; Life that rises-up and over the Face of the Earth to form and shape the Sacred World; el Santo Mundo. This is the New World we must create by finding our true roots in the authentic original writing of the past like those that are found here in the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj.

So here we are at the beginning of our New Narrative where Wuqubʼ Kaqix has come to meet the Dawn; our meeting the Dawn is a perfect metaphor to begin the telling of a New Story in the cool white light of a New Day; a Day with a Destiny that is well known yet never lived out quite the same. A New Dawn of a New Day with its special certain sort of Sun with a style and way all of its own; a style being and way of becoming that is repeated time and again according to the Sacred Count of Days and the Day-keepers who live out their lives enlightened by the knowledge and wisdom discovered in the keeping and counting of the Sacred Days. This is the story told here so let us tell it, here.

body:
There was the First Sky-Earth; Nabʼe Kaj-Ulew but the light of the Sun and Moon was still quite dim. And so it was Lord Seven Macaw-Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kaqix who spoke forth when he saw himself as the bright light-saqetal-white light of the Wooden People; for Wuqubʼ Kaqix-Seven Macaw saw himself as the ʼsacred way- saqetal-sacred path ʼ that he wanted; that he wished; that he willed the Wooden People to follow; for Seven Macaw saw himself as the ʼdivine sign-saqetal-divine directionʼ to take; the perfect path to be taken-up; the divine example to follow for those who survived the Great Flood-Nim Bʼutik.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix just acted as if he were of the same essence as the Nawal Winaq who were known as the ʼAncient Ones, Ancient Ancestral Peopleʼ who were Magical Transforming Ancestors-Nawal Winaq; known the ʼFirst-born Ones- Nawales-the Ancient Onesʼ that were named as those who were the Ancient Ancestors known as Nawal Winaq also spoken of as Na winaq: Transforming Magicians.

And so it was and so it would come to be that these ʼFirst-born Onesʼ who were the ʼFirst-born Ancestorsʼ were endowed with the magical power of transformation; thus were they named Nawal Winaq: Mythical Ancestors of Magical Transformation.

Nawal Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz Nawal Lord Quetzalcoatl A Seven Day Period: Ju Wuq Kumatz-Serpent; Kʼot-Eagle; Bʼalam-Jaguar Just Pooled Blood Alone-Xa utukel remanik Kikʼ

Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are Nawal Ajaw just as is their Mother IxKikʼ and Grandmother IxMuqane. These Nawal Ajaw or Magical Transforming Lords will come to fruition at the very end of the Popol Wuj. This is when Nawal Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz-Nawal Lord Quetzalcoatl will change and transform into his different Nawal Forms that are his Nawal Transforms.

This will happen during Six Periods of Seven Days each one of those periods of Seven Days being named as of One Seven Day Period-Ju Wuq. Periods of Seven Day in which for ʼSeven-Wuqubʼ Days this Magic Transforming Lord known as Nawal Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz will ascend into the Sky-chi Kaj for Seven Days; to then descend down-qajoq into Xibʼalbʼa for Seven Days.

body:
Then this Nawal Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz will become a Serpent-Kumatz for Seven Days-Ju Wuq by him transforming his essence into the nature and condition of a Serpent-Kumatzil for those Seven Days-Ju Wuq.

Then this Nawal Ajaw will become an Eagle-Kʼot for Seven Days when he transforms his essence into the nature and condition of an Eagle-Kʼotal for those Seven Days.

Lord Quetzalcoatl-Nawal Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz then becomes a Jaguar-Bʼalam for Seven Days when he changes and transforms into the essence of the Jaguar-Bʼalamil for those Seven Days-Ju Wuq.

It is then that Nawal Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz become a Sacrificial Pool of Blood-Remelik chik Kikʼel for Seven Days when he becomes ʼjustʼ Pooled Blood during this changing and transforming period of Seven Days to end this period of Forty-Two days of Six Periods of Seven Days.

This Sacred History of Popol Wuj tells us of the Tribes that came before this Nawal Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz to worship him while showing him awe and reverence; regard and respect. For there had never been a Nawal Ajaw like this Noble Kʼicheʼ Lord who was a Great Lord-Nimaʼ Ajaw who was a Nawal Ajaw-Magical Transforming Lord that the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom adored and revered as their Beloved Lord who was a Nawal Ajaw.

This story is told at the end of the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj when the sacred act of ʼNaming the Namesʼ is performed at the close of this Sacred Book of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. This is when the Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word tell us Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz was a Nawal Ajaw that was followed by the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ and by the Mountain Tribes who worshipped him as a Great Lord-Nima Ajaw who acted as the ʼRetal Nimalʼ or ʼGreat Exampleʼ that he was. The Kʼicheʼ and their Mountain Allies looked-up on Nawal Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz for inspiration and courage.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
But here at the beginning of the Popol we are told of Wuqubʼ Kaqix who is not the ʼSaqetalʼ that he wishes he was because he is not a Nawal Ajaw that he says he is here which truly fascinating for the precision and detail with which the Popol Wuj was transcribed to be written down and inscribed to be remembered as a true Mythic Masterpiece of the Maya Culture and Mesoamerican Civilization. Popol Wuj is a Sacred Book of Literary Genius that I have treasured and enjoyed throughout my life.

My only wish now as I become the age of an Elder and Spiritual Guide or Kʼamol Bʼey is that I might be able to guide others to eat in order that they also come to love and appreciate as I have been able to do while living in the Mountains of the Kʼicheʼ amongst the Kʼicheʼ Winaq of the Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ. There is something precious about being claimed by a Masterful Myth such as is this Masterpiece of the Maya Cosmos with its Sky-Earth and Lake-Sea.

Someday the Popol Wuj will become the beloved mythic treasure that it is but this will only happen if we are able to presented with respect and regard it deserves instead of being ʼsecond guessedʼ and ʼdemeaned and dismissedʼ as an inauthentic work of that was just slapped together in the Mid-Sixteenth Century which couldnʼt be further than the truth.

Popol Wuj is an Ancient, Ancient Maya Myth of the Maize People that is played out here in a Long Performance of Five Acts with their Five Long Recitation that are coming to light here at the Dawn of this Second Section; Second Act of Popol Wuj.

Popol Wuj is a ʼSaqetalʼ so let us read it in this way to be guided and protected by its Nawal Genius; Nawal Imagination as we make our way on this Sacred Journey formed by the Imaginal Realm of Myth and shaped by the Mythic Imagination of the People of Maize.

Saqetal-Perfect Way Magical Transforming Being Nawal Winaq Nawinaq Saqetal was the Perfect Path that was the Perfect Way that Wuqubʼ Kaqix formed and shaped by molding and modeling his perfect way-saqetal of making himself out to be of the same nature-kʼojeʼik-condition that was the essence of those Magical Transforming Beings known as Nawal Winaq or Nawinaq.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Wuqubʼ Kaqix says he is the Perfect Path-Saqetal-Perfect Way to be followed as a Nawal Winaq who would be the perfect Saqetal for the Wooden Beings to follow wherever they went when they wandered across the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea known as Kaj-Ulew; Cho-Palo.

This is what led Wuqubʼ Kaqix to say what he was led to say as the One-Jun who said that he was indeed a Nawal Winaq who must be followed as the Wooden Peopleʼs Nim Ajaw- Great Lord who would serve as the Saqetal of the Wooden People as their Nim Ajaw.

I write this in order that the reader understands that the Popol Wuj is a finely organized literary work that is setting-up the design of the plot in which the true Nawal Winaq will become perfect Ancestral Examples to follow when the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom take- up their quest of finding their way across the Face of the Earth in search of Kabʼawil who will guide and protect them along the way.

These Divinities-Kabʼawil are Saqetal that embody the Perfect Path; Perfect Way upon which to cross freezing Highland Mountaintops and dangerous Tropical Jungles where one must follow a ʼsaqetalʼ or risk dying by being frozen to death or being lost in the Petén without a clue of where to turn next to find a drop of water. Wuqubʼ Kaqix saying he is a ʼsaqetalʼ is saying a lot about those who think of themselves as Great Leaders without having any experience of leading at all.

This continues to plague the Américas in a world where ʼFalse-Face Leadersʼ buy their political positions and those positionsʼ powers to corrupt culture and society through Cartel-cash and Narco-wealth that are tied to money-laundering and wide-scale economic and political corruption.

The Popol Wuj is alerting us of this danger right here through the ʼbad exampleʼ of Lord Seven Scarlet Macaw who is nothing more than an adorned puppet; a decorated doll; a made-up manikin whose bejeweled rule and arrogant reign is mere matter of material wealth and a fancy headdress.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Wuqubʼ Kaqix is the Big Man who is nothing more and nothing less than a puffed-up politico with embellished eyes and tinsel teeth while being ornamented with precious stones so that his sparkles and shines in the light of the Sun and Moon. Meanwhile his resplendent jade necklaces and finely beaded jade bracelets provide him with the feeling that he is forever young filling him with the sensation that his forever the Eternal Boy-Puer Eternus who lives ʼas ifʼ he were immune to death. His feeling of being forever young is founded in his material wealth that gives him a deep-seated sense of immortality as riches always do for those who believe that their privileged and affluent existence always provides him with eternal life that is secured and protected by their wealth and prosperity.

But you already know all of this by now yet wonder if it is true and could ever be the sort of life that one would follow as a good example of a perfect path-saqetal to a meaningful life and valued existence. So letʼs get going so that we might find out just exactly what will happen to this handsome, good-looking Seven Scarlet Macaw-Wuqubʼ Kaqix...

And so it was that Lord Seven Macaw; Wuqubʼ Kaqix said: “My nature, my essence shall shine forth over the Formed People, the Shaped People. For I am their Sun-Qʼij; I am their Light-Saq; I their Moon-Ikʼ; I their Royal Reflection; I their Sacred Sustenance-Rikʼil; for it is they who look to me for their light; for their warmth!” “So be it! Ta Chuxoq! May it come to be! Great is my perfection, great is my reflection; great is my resplendence; great is my resemblance to the light of the Sun; great is my resplendence like the light of the Moon.” “For I am the walkway of the People; and, I too am the pathway of the Pueblo!”

In bʼinibʼal winaq; In pu chakabʼal rumal winaq!

body: “My teeth sparkle just the same, for they are formed from precious turquoise stone, shaped to reflect the Sky, bright and blue; they just mirror the Sea that sparkles as it shines in the beautiful blue reflection of the shimmering Sky. Blue is the essence of my elegant smile set-off by my prized polished teeth that shimmer, as they shine bright from my magnificent mouth revealing to all that I am a Royal Ruler, a Noble Lord whose power and authority are easy to see.” “And with regard to my fine noble nose that is a rather divine type of refined sort of sublime kind of stunning species of beautiful beak that gleams and glimmers with a glint that flickers as it flashes and flares so brilliant and bright that its shimmering shine reaches as far as the luminous light of the Moon.” “Silver then is my noble throne; oh, my sacred silver throne that illumines the Sky as it lights-up the Face of the Earth every time I fly from that bright shining perch of mine.” “This makes my nature and condition of the very same essence as the divine radiance of the Sun; and hallowed glow of the Moon. For I am the sacred light of the Divine Daughters of the Dawn; the Sacred Sons of the Sun; those Born in the Light; Begotten in the Light; Daughters of the Moon, Sons of the Sun: Saqil Al, Saqil Kʼajol; Beloved Vassals, Precious Subjects of Noble Lords.” “And so it is that I am the Sun; I too am the Moon of those who are the Divine Daughters-Venerable Vassals of this Noble Realm; I am the bright light of the Sun; I too am the bright light of the Moon; so then it is I who am the Sun and the Moon of those who are the Sublime Subjects-Sacred Sons of this Noble Realm; Saqil Al, Saqil Kʼajol; Divine Descendants, Sacred Subjects; Devout Daughters of the Regal Realm; Loyal Sons of this noble Kingdom; those Precious Replacements borne and begotten in the bright light of the Eternal Sun; conceived and engendered in the luminous light of the changing, transforming Moon.”

body:
“So be it! Ta Chuxoq! May it come to be! For I am truly divine; for truly sacred am I; my divine light; my radiance is that of a Noble Lord; a Noble Lord whose noble splendor reaches far,” said Wuqubʼ Kaqix. But it was not true that Wuqubʼ Kaqix was the Sun. It was just his conceit; it was just his arrogance that brought forth his own particular kind of puffed-up sort of stuffed-up ways of self importance.

Nawal Ajaw Lord Seven Scarlet Macaw King of the Forest Emperor of the Selva Principal Bird Deity He thought himself to be just like the Sun because of his fiery red feathers that burned in a bright blaze as he made his way across the great green canopy of the Jungle Forest where he was seen as the splendid Lord Seven Scarlet Macaw; King of the Forest; Emperor of the Selva.

It was just his magnificent flight across the bright blue turquoise Sky that made one appreciate is bright scarlet red feathers that were set-off by the yellow and blue that drew one to the obvious truth that this Wuqubʼ Kaqix was a wonder of nature that shined bright against the Sky as he floated in flight just above the outstretched arms of the flowering and fruiting trees that made one realize that this Noble Lord known as Seven Scarlet Macaw was truly the Principal Bird Deity a may well have become a Nawal Ajaw if only he would have shown a little bit of humility that bordered on a most endearing trait known as modesty. But modesty and humility were nowhere to be found in the vocabulary of Wuqubʼ Kaqix who if anything was the Lord of Impropriety. There was just no way anyone could context that firm and feral fact of this most Natural Habitat where this Self-Aggrandizing Braggart had plenty of reason to hold himself in such high regard while showing himself such great respect as Lord of the Jungle and King of the Forest of this Noble Realm of the Many Trees. Let keep moving to see where Wuqubʼ Kaqix lands: up in the tree-top canopy or down on the ground sprawled out in misery.

The bright countenance of the Wuqubʼ Kaqix shone only as far as the pale dim light that his bright red-feathers reflected when he took to flight; so that his whitish moonlit sort of washed-out light only reached as far as where he flew about over the trees of the Jungle Forest. For truly, his resplendent face did not illuminate all that lay beneath the Sky; and so it was that his radiance didnʼt ʼlighten-upʼ all there was to ʼbrighten-upʼ there beneath the sheltering Sky in the shadow of the Sun.

This was before the Face of the Sun, Moon, and Great Star could be seen in the Sky. For the Sun had not yet dawned; the Moon had not yet risen; and the Great Star-Venus had not yet climbed-up in the Sky to carry the Sun across the Earth; not yet, not yet, but still Wuqubʼ Kaqix wished to be revered ʼas ifʼ he were the very light of the Sun and Moon.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix wished only to be named as a Noble Lord; to be known as an Entitled Ruler after being given Sovereign Rule and Authority by being honored and revered with the respect and regard that comes with Noble Entitlement- kukobʼisaj-Noble Investiture that named him-Seven Macaw, Wuqubʼ Kaqix-the direct descendant of the Sun; that named him the direct descendant of the Moon.

The light of the Sun, the light of the Moon had not yet become visible; for not yet had the divine light of Sun and Moon shown their radiance; not yet had the Sun and the Moon revealed themselves to be the Replacements who were the Descendants of the Sunʼs golden radiance; of the Moonʼs bright silver light. For the truth was that Wuqubʼ Kaqix desired only to be named a Noble Lord; he hungered only to be the One whose grandeur surpassed all others; the One who wished to be named by Royal Titles of Noble Entitlement; as One of those Engendered Sons of Noble Lords who wished to be provided with tribute and sustained with service in accord with his noble position. For it was he, Wuqubʼ

Kaqix who wished to be recognized as the One who had earned the right to be fed and maintained; nourished and nurtured because of his royal rank and noble status. This is when a Great Deluge was made fall; when a Great Flood came to pass, the flood that was created to destroy the careless, heartless Wooden People; Tree Beings, Reed Beings, the ones known as Poy, Ajam Cheʼ; those who were just dressed up and adorned Doll People-Poy; those who were they bedecked in shimmering shining finery; just bejeweled Puppet People; these who were those Ancient Ancestral Beings; Wooden Men whittled from the Wood of the Tzʼite Tree; and the Reed Women who were formed and shaped from the bundled and bound Reeds that grew amongst Rushes on the Lakeshore that was known as the Place of Origins thick with abundance, rich with sustenance were they; those who were of Tzʼiteʼ and Sibʼaq from which were carved and crafted Wooden Men of Tzʼiteʼ; Reed Women of Sibʼaq; fashioned swiftly to be finished fast these Formed Being; these Shaped Beings were never made to last.

These were those that were Wooden People whoʼs language and looks; speech and appearance were lost forever when they were transformed into Spider Monkeys-Kʼoy who swung through the treetops speaking their ancient animal speech.

Forest Speech Jungle Language Monkey Talk That speech of theirs sounded more like an ancient ancestral form of forest speech that was more of a shriek that sounded like a screech; a screech that called for a squeal in response to a scream but letʼs face it this was no way the speak. This shrieking and screeching instead of speaking was just like the way those Kʼoy squealed and screamed instead of singing which is a true clue as to how these Monkey Boys acted in most alarming ancient animal ways.

body:
This is to say those Monkey Twins liked nothing more than to do what they were born to do which was to get even with those humans who they blamed for what happened to them not so very long ago. So what they did is what they still do which to piss and pooh in their hand to then throw it at folks like me and you. Folks who are always more than content to stand down below these Kʼoy who were once Elders Brothers who were also Older Boys who should have known better to do what they did which was to act envious and jealous like Wooden People of the Forest always have despite being treated with deference as well as with high regard and deep respect.

But that is the way of Animal People that is a story for latter on in this Ancient Account when the Life Ways of the Spider Monkey-Kʼoy will be sung into life through the singing of the song known as Junajpu Kʼoy. Singing this Ancient Ancestral Song of the Monkey Boys known as Junajpu Kʼoy is always a sure bet on halving them come down from the Forest and out of the Trees to perform their dances by dancing for their Grandmother and her Grandsons.

Grandsons who were fast and furious Pipers who knew how to blow on their flutes while beating out the rhythm on their drums which is what Kʼicheʼ Sons and Grandsons were once taught to do as Flute Players and Drummers and Singers of Ancient Tunes like Junajpu Kʼoy that was always played for those who danced down below in Grandmothers Patio and all over here Sitio where the Kʼoy always put on a hilarious show making everyone laugh even if they didnʼt want to.

And so it goes just as it went with the Wooden People whose speech and ways of acting were changed and transformed forever because they thought they were craftier and cleverer than their Younger Brothers. They just spoke and acted as they were molded and modeled to speak and act which meant they were just another flawed and failed fallen attempt to form formed being and shape shaped beings here on the Face of the Earth.

These Poy and Ajam Cheʼ were just destroyed by a Great Flood and those who survived were transformed into Kʼoy.

But you already know that so letʼs move ahead to learn about what happened to Wuqubʼ Kaqix and his Boys: Sipakna and Kabʼraqan; Volcano Boy and Earthquake Boy.

AND SO WE SHALL TELL NEXT, we shall tell further, of when Wuqubʼ Kaqix died; when he was defeated; when the Former formed the Formed Beings; when the Shaper shaped the Shaped Beings.

The Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings were just formed and shaped by AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit; the Former, the Shaper, known as Molder-Modeler; those who created, those who crafted; those who formed the Formed Beings; those who shaped the Shaped Being. These are the Formers; these are the Shapers who brought their forming and shaping of the Formed Ones; the Shaped One here on the Face of the Earth.

This then was when the Forming and Shaping brought them out as that which was known as the Formation; as that which was seen as the Generation of what is invoked and remembered as the Creation of Life that led to the Peopling; the Populating of the Face of the Earth: utzʼuquxik, uwinaqirik kʼaslem, winaqirem Uwach Ulew. This, then, is the origin, the root, the very beginning of Ancient Word that tells of the defeat and fall of Wuqubʼ Kaqix by the Two Boys, the Two Sons: Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ.

Junajpu is the name of the First One-Jun; Ixbʼalamkej is the name of the Second One-Kabʼ. They were just divinities: e Kabʼawil.

It was the Two Boys-ri Kʼajolabʼ-the Two Sons named and known as Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who saw the ugliness-itzel in the self-magnifying ways of Seven Scarlet Macaw.

Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej saw the ugliness in the self-aggrandizing ways of Wuqubʼ Kaqix; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej saw the ugliness in the self-glorifying ways of Lord Seven Macaw and how his ugly ways of being were acted-out before the Heart of the Sky: Ukʼuʼx Kaj.

body:
This then was when the Sons-ri Kʼajolabʼ-the Boys; said to each other: “This is just no good, no good at all. Surely, the way things are, is not the way they should be and become.” “So then, what would it be but a chance; just a try; just an attempt nothing more, for us to take a shot at him when he lands upon his throne at the top of his Nance Tree where he takes his mid-day meal of golden yellow fruit; the Nance- Tapʼal that is his sacred sustenance; his favorite food-echa-his favorite fruit.” “Let us just fire a shot-jun abʼaj-a stone with a blowgun blast when heʼs perched up in his Tapʼal Tree. Letʼs just shoot one shot; letʼs just blow one stone at him nothing more.” “In this way we might wound him; to perhaps bring illness upon him; maybe causing him sickness that could lead to his decline and downfall that would most certainly end his life in death, demise, and defeat.” “This way we might just finish off his wealth that is his jade and his silver; his precious jewels and precious stones with which he adorns himself for his own glorification; the wealth with which he feeds his pride, vanity, and arrogance.” “If not, this will be the way everyone will act in a world where silver mustnʼt become the foundation of the power and authority of sovereign rule!” “So be it; Chuxoq bʼa la na! May it come to pass!” This is what these companions said to one-an-other as the Two of them took up the road each One of them shouldering his blowgun: ubʼ.

Now this Wuqubʼ Kaqix had Two Sons: the First Son went by the name of Sipakna, the Smoking One, Volcano Boy; he who was known as the Spiny-Backed One, Caiman Boy. Sipakna was the “Maker of Mountains” who was the First One; the First Son of Seven Scarlet Macaw: Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

The Second Son-ukabʼ kʼajolabʼ went by the name of Kabʼraqan; Two- Footed-One, Earthquake Boy. It was he who shook the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew for he was the Shaker who made the Sky shake; he was the Quaker who made the Earth quake.

body:
Kʼabʼraqan was the Second Son who was the Destructive One; the One who was born with the destiny to make the Sky shake for that which was his in life was to make the Earth quake: this was the One known as Two-Foot-Kabʼ Raqan. It was he who was known as the “Destroyer of Big Mountains-Leveler of Small Mountains” thus he was named: Kabʼraqan-Earthquake.

Chimalmat: Shield-bearer Chimalmat then was the name of their Mother, the Woman who was the Wife of Wuqubʼ Kaqix; Shield-bearer-Chimalmat was her name. Chimalmat then was the name of the Mother of Sipakna and Kabʼraqan; who was the Woman who was the Wife of Wuqubʼ Kaqix; Shield-bearer- Chimalmat was her name.

Chimalmat: Shield-bearer Chimalmat-Shield-bearer is the One who is the shield of her Pueblo. Her name comes from chimalli-shield, something laid out flat, like the open hand of divination: chimala. Wuqubʼ Kaqix will fall over backwards from the top of his tree to fall flat on his back or chimalmat.

Chimalmat signifies ʼthe one who is laid-out flat on the backʼ which is a play on the name of the Nahua Woman Chimalmat of Wuqubʼ Kaqix which is her name, a name that comes from the Nahuatl speaking people of the North; a name who portends the downfall of Wuqubʼ Kaqix the archenemy of the Ixim Winaq.

Chimalmat as Shield-Bearer is a warrior-woman who defends her people by wielding the shield-chimalli that she bears in her hand. But this chimalli that is a shield is transformed into a weapon by fixing obsidian blades all around its outer edge to transform Chimalmat into Woman Warrior who leaves her enemy ʼflat on the backs-chimalmatʼ. Saying chimala-chimala is a playful way of talking about doing something else flopped out flat on oneʼs back…but I will leave that up to your imagination to figure out what that is all about… Sipakna:Volcano This then was when Sipakna played about-chaaj on the Face of the Earth by ʼmaking ash-chajʼ with his constant eruptions; it is said that he just ʼplayed-chaajʼ with the Great Mountains-Nimaq Juyubʼ that were the Great Volcanoes known and named as:
