Chi Qʼaqʼ: Mouth of Fire Volcano, Volcán de Fuego Jun Ajpu: One Blow-gun Boy, Volcán de Agua IxPekul Ya: Water Cave of the Landslide Volcano, Volcán de Santo Tomás Yaxkanul: New Volcano, Volcán de Santa María Makamob: Gathered Stone of Molten Lava, Cerro Quemado Julisnabʼ: Tendril-Hair Root of the Cave of Flower Mountain, Volcán Almolonga

Just one night was all that was needed for Sipakna to complete his work; just one night was all that it took for Sipakna to create a mountain. Just one night was time enough for Sipakna to bring forth a Great Mountain-Nima Juyubʼ spoken of today as a Volcano. Ordering of Nature by the Cultural Heroes These are the names given to the Great Mountain-Volcanoes that rose-up to stand before the Dawn of the Maize People at the Dawn of the Kʼicheʼ Sun. This is an ancient world of Mountain-Making Giants and Mountain-Quaking Giants; the Age of the Formers and Shapers who are Creators and Destroyers. This Age; this Era took place during the Ancient Ancestral Sun of the Wooden People who die in a Flood of Qʼol-Black Rain of Thick Dark Resin created by this Volcano Boy known as the Spiny One, the Smoking One: Sipakna.

Volcanic Eruptions create devastating Thunder and Lightning Storms that in turn create devastating floods and landslides from the tremendous quantities of water-vapor released from the Earthquake event. This water-vapor and electrical energy from explodes from beneath the Earth rises up into the Sky through the cataclysmic eruption of the Volcano. This is the Black Rain that is experienced as the Flood-Bʼutik that destroys the Wooden People at the end of their Age; at the end of their Sun.

Sipakna is often portrayed standing-up as the Ceiba Tree that is conflated with the ʼspiny backʼ of Sipakna also known as Cipacatli, the Great Crocodile, Great Caiman Earth Monster Deity known as Tlaltecuhtli. This image of the Great Caiman Earth is easily seen by looking up to the East from the Pacific Ocean shore from the Pacific Coast beach town of Cipacate.

body:
The Spiny Back of the Guatemalan Highlands is seen turning oneʼs back to the Pacific Ocean to look up and across the Volcanic Mountain Range of Guatemala. This is the image created here through the ʼnaming of the namesʼ of the Volcanoes Sipakna ʼplaysʼ with making ʼashʼ with his Mountain-making Ways of Creation.

The Pacific Coast of Guatemala is where larger estuaries are formed by Highland Rivers that feed these Estuaries known as ʼYaloʼ with sweet water to create the perfect environment for Pacific Caiman or Pacific Crocodiles. These primordial animals once thrived off the abundance of marine life that grew and multiplied on the Pacific Coast with its low-lying shoreline formed the perfect landscape for estuaries and mangroves teaming with life. This is where the Caiman- Cipacatli grew into Giants that fed the Mesoamerica imagination with this Ancient Ancestral Narratives of Caiman Sea-Monsters. It is from down beside the sweet and salty waters of Pacific Coast Estuaries that one can look to the East from the Ocean Shore to gaze upon the Spiny Back-Bone of the Volcanic Cordillera of El Salvador, Guatemala, and Chiapas all of which was once imagined to be just One Great Cipacatli; One Great Caiman; One Great Crocodile.

This is also where the most ancient clay, stone, and bone remnants of Mesoamericaʼs earliest human settlements can be found in the primordial mounds that exist all the way up and down the Pacific Coast of Mesoamerica. Great quantities of marine life prospered here to provide and sustain Primordial Mesoamerica with its sacred sustenance. The Maize People would come much later as is told in this mythic metaphor that tells us of the Maize People and their transformation of the Face of the Earth by peopling and populating it with Maize People who would eventual sow Maize in the Milpa that would change the Mountains and Plains forever more.

body:
This is the Primordial Narrative of the Primordial World of Mesoamerica that is being introduced here in mythic metaphorical ways. So let us move on with this Ancient Ancestral Account of the Maize People and their Pueblo of Maize with its Milpa that multiplied and grew magical ways to then grow and multiply in miraculous ways until the Maize that was sown in the Milpa was found everywhere one wondered across the Mountains and Plains.

So let us move towards that sowing and growing of the Maize in the Milpa that brought about the multiplying of the People of Maize and their growing of the Milpa that enable the Pueblos of Maize People to multiply and grow; to grow and multiply until they ended up living- off of the Sacred Sustenance that was the very flesh of the Maize People; the Maize People whoʼs flesh were formed and shaped from ground maize; maize that was understood to be the flesh of the Maize People whose flesh was understood to be in its very essence as being that of maize. And if the flesh of the Maize People was formed from maize then eating human flesh as sacred sustenance was the most sacred of all acts one could participate in ritual that was formed and shaped by myth. This idea would have a profound effect on the Mesoamerican imagination of matter in which matter was imagined to be changing and transforming all the time. Mesoamerica Culture and Civilization would understand its Cosmos as being in its essence and it is core as being Nawal in every way. This means that everything changed and transformed depending on how one imagined matter to be changing and transforming in nawal ways. This is the story that is told here in which Sipakna and Kabʼraqan change and transform the Sky-Earth through the Creation and Destruction of the Mountains.

Kabʼraqan: Earthquake And then there was Kabʼraqan who moved the mountains. He just shook the Face of the Earth making it shutter and shake; causing it to quiver and quake. So that it only took Kabʼraqan to tap, tap his two feet for him to create an earthquake; an earthquake that he made by just tap, tap, tapping is two-kabʼ feet-raqan.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This Kabʼraqan was a real destroyer; for it was he who was the leveler of mountains. The Small Mountains, the Great Mountains-Chʼuti Juyubʼ, Nimaʼ Juyubʼ, they just quivered; they just quaked when he made them shiver; when he made them shake so that in no time these Small Mountains; Great Mountains were leveled to the ground; demolished, destroyed. And so it was that the Mountains were brought down to the ground by the Two-Footed One; to Number Two Son known and named: Kʼabʼraqan.

Sipakna and Kabʼraqan It was they, Sipakna and Kabʼraqan, who made themselves out to be the Big Ones, the Great Ones. That is what the Two Sons; the Two Boys; Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ of Wuqubʼ Kaqix did when out walking across the Face of the Earth. They just did what their Father showed them to do by making a great big deal out of themselves wherever their path and its way lead them to.

This was the direct result of them following the fine example of their Fatherʼs self- aggrandizing ways; to then take-up his path of arrogance and conceit that led to them becoming bragging and boastful beasts all of which resulted in their proud and arrogant ways that grew along with them in giant sorts of ways. This was how they came to be who they had become in the World of the Sky-Earth: Kaj-Ulew. “Look at me, Iʼm the Sun,” boasted Wuqubʼ Kaqix. “Look at me, Iʼm the Maker of the Earth,” erupted Sipakna. “Look at me I shake the Sky; I level the Earth,” quaked Kabʼraqan. They were just-xa the Sons of their Father, Wuqubʼ Kaqix. It was just from him that they brought forth their self-aggrandizement-nimarisaj ribʼ, in order to manifest their own arrogance and conceit that was pure pride and vanity as they followed in the footsteps of their Father-kikajaw on the path of their Lord-kikajaw: Wuqubʼ Kaqix, Lord Seven Scarlet Macaw.

Meanwhile, the other Boys, the other Sons-ri Kʼajolabʼ could clearly see the ways of Sipakna and Kabʼraqan were indeed ugly-itzel. It was crystal clear that their vain and arrogant ways of acting and speaking was no way to be especially for those who thought of themselves as nobility.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej saw arrogance and conceit in the way Sipakna and Kabʼraqan created and destroyed Mountains as if ʼcreation and destructionʼ was some sort of game. If one looked at it like this-as the Blowgun Boy did-then this raising-up of Mountains to then knock them right back down again was nothing less than a direct confrontation; perhaps even an open challenge to the ways of Heart of the Sky, Heart of the Earth; Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew.

For this creating and destroying mountains was not some sort of simple way to pass the day playing particularly for those who formed and shaped the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea as did those known as Former and Shaper; those spoken of as Creator and Destroyer who were those named Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj and Sovereign Plumed Serpent-Qʼuqʼkumatz.

This was long before the forming and shaping of Our First Mother, Our First Father; this was long before the First Mother-Fathers; Nabʼey Chuch-Qajaw had been formed and shaped by the Former, the Shaper: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol. So this then was when they thought about the death-kamik and disappearance-sachik of the three arrogant ones, the three of them were to be finished off by the Boys, the Sons, ri Kʼajolabʼ. They just planned their death and disappearance from the Face of the Earth so that they would be dead and gone once and for all.

This was what the Boys wanted; this is what the Two Boys wished for; the Twins known and named Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who knew how to respect the ancestral ways of the Sky-Earth: Kaj-Ulew.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix Nawal of Tezcatlipoca Big Dipper in the Northern Horizon One-Footed-One; One-Legged-One Wuqubʼ Kaqix sees himself as the light of both Sun and Moon. He imagines himself in this way because of his bright shining affluence and bejeweled adornment that was worn as a means of showing off his wealth and prosperity.

This Noble Lord known to you well as Seven Scarlet Macaw is the Lord of Bling who loves to show off his Silver Nose that shines like the Crescent Moon.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
His Turquoise Eyes shimmer as they shine as the ripple across the splendid pools of turquoise water. His Jade Necklace and Jade Earrings provide him with the resplendent sense of youth and rebirth that are so very necessary for the sense of well-being of Lord Seven Scarlet Macaw-Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

This jade adornment is his most resplendent reminder of his eternal existence as a Noble Lord of a Noble Lineage of Noble Maya Lords who as a Divine Ancestor must do everything in his power to be replaced by Beloved Descendants who hopefully will remember him through their songs of praise; incantations of worship and admiration; and, invocations of adoration, veneration, and remembrance.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix is a much adorned being who is as arrogant and conceited as he is haughty, proud and vain. And who wouldnʼt be with his beautiful bright regal red, golden yellow, and Maya blue feathers; his splendid, spectacular feathers provide him his ornithological name: Scarlet Macaw; Ara Macao. Ara Macao; Scarlet Macaws are the native Lords of the Jungle Canopy and Wuqubʼ Kaqix knows that he is gorgeous to look upon, especially in flight. And he will remind all those who flock about him that that his is beautiful to look upon if they donʼt reminder to do so themselves.

This is the way of the Tropical Wilderness where wild flocks of Scarlet Macaw make it known to all that they are there to be seen and heard by all through their incessant crying out that says: ʼwe are hereʼ ʼwe are hereʼ ʼwe are hereʼ…ʼlookʼ ʼlookʼ ʼlookʼ ʼlook at usʼ…ʼlook at usʼ…ʼAre we not beautiful?ʼ ʼAre we not magnificent?ʼ ʼAre we not glorious?ʼ ʼLook at us!ʼ ʼLook at us!ʼ…ʼlook upʼ…ʼlook upʼ…ʼlook, look, lookʼ…ʼlook, look, look at us flyʼ…ʼlook at us fly as we fly across the Heart of the Skyʼ? “Do we not rival the light of the Sun with our royal radiance; our regal resplendence?”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the way it can be with a large flock of Scarlet Macaw when they are at home in their Jungle Forest where they are safe and sound; free to be who they are by nature; natural braggart by birth and in its natural inheritance; and who they are is how they are expressed here in the Popol Wuj through its Ancient that says: these are those who are the Noble Lords and Native Rulers of the Jungle Forest! Just look at his fine emerald jewels that he wears in his feather headdress that manifests his status as a divinity for he is the Nawal Transform of Ukʼuʼx Kaj; Heart of the Sky. The Ancient Word and in its authors of the Popol Wuj doesnʼt just come out and say it but we know it; we know Wuqubʼ Kaqix is the Nawal of the Heart of the Sky because of way this celestial mythic figure speaks and acts as he sings out that he is the King of the Forest.

As a trickster deity Wuqubʼ Kaqix could not possibly embody the Nawal of Tezcatlipoca more perfectly for the way he falls from grace to end up losing his wealth and power. This is the way of Mesoamerican Lords and Rulers whoʼs Titular Deity is Tezcatlipoca. This is the way of Mesoamerican Trickster Figures who like Wuqubʼ Kaqix are given great power by Heart of the Sky to then lose it all through trickery to then end-up dying dead as it is said because he is not brought back to life on Earth instead he is placed after death in the Night Sky as Celestial Ancestor that takes up the entire Northern Quadrant in the form of the Big Dipper or Ursa Major who is Wuqubʼ Kaqixʼ in the Maya Cosmos as you already know so well.

Lord Seven Macawʼs power and rule are founded only in material wealth with which he adorns himself in as a pretentious ruler whose authority is grounded in his being a boasting braggart that elevates himself over all others through his own self-aggrandizement. This is not the way of Lord Quetzalcoatl who is a hard working conscientious and caring ruler.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the way it must be for those who wish to participate as Noble Lords in the Empire of Quetzalcoatl known as Qʼuqʼkumatz to the Kʼicheʼ Maya and Kukulkan to the Maya of Tollan Tzuy-Wa of the Great Post-Classic Maya World of Chichen Itza, Mayapan, Uxmal, Cobaʼ, Cozumel, Tulum, Chetumal, and the turquoise blue sea from where the Sun rises at Dawn from that sacred most place in the East known as the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij.

Lord Quetzalcoatl requires his Noble Lords to be initiated into the Noble Tradition of Tollan Tzuy Wa by ʼEntering the Wordʼ through the initiatory acts carried out through ritual journeys and ceremonies of initiation that change and transform a Young Noble Prince through ritual fasting and ceremonial practices of self-sacrifice.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix wants attention; he wants to be seen; he wants to create problems; he wants to create conflict; he wants to mock the perfect princely ways of Quetzalcoatl because this is his way to change and transform the world of the Sky-Earth. Wuqubʼ Kaqix adorns himself in his pretentious embellishments of shiny silver and sparkling jewels; resplendent jade and celestial turquoise; bright feathers and superlative exclamations of his grandeur.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
He mocks the ʼperfect pathʼ of self-sacrificing Day-Keepers, Calendars Priests and Priestesses. He mocks their precious and perfect ways; sacred ways that are divine ways but these sublime sorts of articulation that are grandiose elocutions of shameless braggarts are meant to be understood on multiple levels. Nevertheless, this is impossible to understand unless one has been initiated into Mesoamerican Myth and Religion in very profound ways that we can only introduce to you here in the most cursory way that must be both brief and superficial because of the restrictions of time and space. Wuqubʼ Kaqixʼs boasting is a way of mocking the perfection of Lord Quetzalcoatl and those who follow his ʼsaqetalʼ as the ʼperfect wayʼ to follow in a world where everyone knows that if a Noble Rulers doesnʼt know the Art of Self-Aggrandizement through beautiful embellishments and flamboyant adornment the Subjects and Vassals will never be satisfied with Lord and Ruler.

And this is why his pronouncements must be understood in a variety of contexts: “look at me I am the Light of the Sun; my resplendence shines as bright as the Great Star; my Silver Nose is like that of Moon; my light shines bright like the Sun…”

If we only read these as a self-sacrificing Dominican or Franciscan Priest or Protestant Reformer or Leftist Academic we will never understand the mockery of the Trickster Deity that is in full disguise here and enjoying every minute of his play on being a ʼperfect exampleʼ of the self-sacrificing divinity.

This is the Ancient Myth of Quetzalcoatl and Tezcatlipoca who as Precious Twins are also eternal rivals who create and destroy Ages as the Dark Twin and Light Twin; the Good and the Bad; the Beautiful and Ugly. Yet the Christian polarities and dualities of Good and Evil; Kind and Wicked; Moral and Immoral will distort our understanding of the Mesoamerican Worldview and yet Wuqubʼ Kaqix is always said to act in ʼevil kinds of wicked waysʼ when he acts in ugly ways that are not beautiful ways. This is what the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj is playing with here.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Sometimes Noble Rulers must act as Wuqubʼ Kaqix acts in order to create the problems that only he can solve as the Nagual or Nawal or Nahual of Heart of the Sky who here along with Qʼuqʼkumatz as Lord Quetzalcoatl who must bring the Age of the Wooden People to an End so the Age of the Maize People can begin. This is what is going on here in the ways that one can only say are the amoral ways of Trickster who must do what he must do to reapportion sacrifice in order that he receives recognition in exchange for Noble Power and Position although he wants some of that too.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix is identified by these Ancient Words: “look at me I am the Light of the Sun; my resplendence shines as bright as the Great Star; my Silver Nose is like that of Moon; my light shines bright like the Sun…” He wants everyone to be looking at him because he is a Magician who is about to pull a fast-one on everyone.

As everyone looks at him in him in his direction his Nawal Jun Kame-who is his complement-is making sure everything is prepared on the Ballcourt of Xibʼalbʼa where the conflict is going to be moved so the ʼreal actionʼ can take place in the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa on the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice where this Myth of Sacred Sustenance is going to be where the ʼreapportioningʼ of sacrifice will get worked out once and for all.

Popol Wuj is a literary work of vast genius that was created by a Ancient Civilization that worked on this Sacred Narrative for at least Three Thousand Years. Popol Wuj can be read at the Trickster Level that I must make you aware of here otherwise what would be the point of my reading and studying it for over four long and exhausting decades of constant contemplation of its mythic words; mythic word-plays; and mythic metaphors and mythic plays of mythic metaphors.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These Forty Years have been filled with word-play; myth-play; language-play; ritual- play; musical-play; cultural-play; ritual-play; thought-play; image-play; work-play but often enough all this play bringing life into focus to create an open perspective that is influenced by a very serious kind of play known as serio ludare. This serio ludare is what develops the reverence one must show to the Kʼicheʼ Maya and the deep regard for their Sacred Literary Tradition that is the Popol Wuj. Yes, Popol Wuj calls us to play with our imagination of language yet it also invokes our deepest respect for a Mythic Tradition that is as beautiful written and ʼplayed-outʼ that something as monumental as is the Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij of Popol Wuj. Popol Wuj being such a unique creation of mythic imagination and mythic metaphor that reveals as it relates and reveals the ʼnawal geniusʼ that is the ʼtransforming geniusʼ of the Cosmo- Magical Imagination and Thought of Mesoamerica.

Popol Wuj reveals a People and a Place through a mythic expression of the World that says in its own very indigenous way that Beauty is Truth and Truth was Beauty and that is all you really need to know. This Beauty and Truth is perhaps what were most revered by the Maya who want to teach its initiates to show reverence of the Beauty of their Ancestral Tradition so that the Truth of that Ancestral Tradition can guide oneʼs life towards create more Beauty and more Truth in order to live out a Good Life filled with veneration for the Kabʼawil who left signs of themselves throughout life in ʼnawalʼ ways.

There is a need for one being initiated into the Sacred Word of Popol Wuj. It is difficult to understand the Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij but when one was initiated into this Ancestral Tradition by ʼentering the wordʼ and when one found what was oneʼs destiny in life then that precious human life was well worth the suffering involved in its Rites of Initiation that are at the Heart and Soul of the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Popol Wuj is a transformative mythological text in itself yet when woven together with Rites of Passage and Sacred Journey and Rituals of Initiation it must have been experienced as truly transcendent experience. Transcendent in the sense that the Descendant became the Ancestor just as the Ancestor was able to return to life through their Replacement. We no longer seek this type of relationship in life yet the Maya certainly do as Descendants and Ancestors replace one another as they live through one another by ʼentering the word of myth to then enter the road of pilgrimage to then enter the fire of ritual. This is the story told here through the transformative powers of Myth and Ritual.

ʼLord of Looking Goodʼ Saqetal: Sacred Exemplum of Rulership Wuqubʼ Kaqix is the ʼLord of Looking Goodʼ for is the Lord of the Wooden People who are an Adorned People who are an Embellished People as you will come to see when they play a major and massive role in the lives of the First Citadel of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. Dressed up and well adorned Puppet People who are Manikin People can be very important people despite being False-face Peopleʼ in every way. But this is the way of Wuqubʼ Kaqix who truly is the ʼsaqetalʼ

of a People like the Maya who know the importance of lying in a world in which your oppressor lies to you. The Maya know how vital it is to be able to deceive others in a world where oneʼs enemy is always trying to deceive you in the marketplace or on the battlefield or ballcourt. The Maya know like the Hero Twins know the importance of learning to cheat when your opponent will only play if they can cheat because they have no idea of what fair-play means.

The Hero Twins like the Maya have learned to lie, cheat, steal, and deceive because the adversaries do nothing other than lie, steal, cheat, and deceive in a world where the odds are stacked against ʼthe good guys like Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpuʼ who are sacrifice right away because they are so honest and kind; up-standing and righteous. This is not the way of Trickster because Trickster lives in world in which the Old Gods hold all the cards in their hand before the deck has even been shuffled.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
So do realize dear reader that the ʼugly waysʼ of Wuqubʼ Kaqix must be interpreted on many levels and one of the most important levels is the way of the One you already know so well. This is the level of the Trickster Deity Wuqubʼ Kaqix who is Lord of the Mountain who is known as He who makes himself; Lord of Near and Nigh-Close; We who are his Slaves; We who are his Men; He who is the Mocker of Men; Lord and Ruler of the Sky-Earth; Heart of the Mountain; the Young Man-Telpochtli; Night Wind; Ome Acatl-Two Reed-Kaʼibʼ Acatl; The Dark Twin; The Enemy-Yaotl. This is Tezcatlipoca-Jun Raqan-the One Footed One who Wuqubʼ Kaqix embodies as his Nawal. He sows discord in order to promote change and transformation thus he is always there at the ʼendʼ of every age.

One Age; One Sun for Quetzalcoatl One Age; One Sun for Tezcatlipoca Divine Twins in Cycles of Creation and Destruction The Mesoamerican Mythos of Popol Wuj expects us to know this and now we do. Tezcatlipoca as Heart of the Sky-Ukʼux Kaj is said to be ʼhe who creates the problems that only he can solveʼ and this is certainly what is going on here in the Popol Wuj. For doesnʼt this section begin with Ukʼuʼx Kaj being offended by the ʼugly-itzel ways of Wuqubʼ Kaqix. Yet Wuqubʼ Kaqix is the Nawal of Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj who as Jun Raqan the One Footed One is seen in the Night Sky as the One-Footed-One-Tezcatlipoca-Ursa Major-Wuqubʼ Kaqix seen as the Big Dipper with its One Leg that is the One Long Tail Scarlet Tail Feather of Lord Seven Scarlet Macaw. The Big Dipper has one long leg that is the one long tail feather of Seven Macaw that ends in the ʼRed Giant Star Arcturusʼ that stand in the Heart of the Sky at the Mid- Night at the Mid-Point of the Year when the Popol Wuj was performed.

body:
Remember that Mesoamerican Myth and Religion is founded in and upon the mythic metaphor of the magical change and transformation of the Sky-Earth through Deities-Kabʼawil that are Nawales. These Nawales change and transform into whatever it takes to ʼget the job doneʼ which is precisely the way of Wuqubʼ Kaqix and the Hero Twins who must end the life of this Trickster in order to end the Age of the Wooden People and its Sun.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix is not ʼevilʼ and the Hero Twins are not ʼgoodʼ as so many Translators and Interpreters have written in the past myself includes. But this sense of Western Duality is only partially correct in effort to comprehend this Maya Myth of the Maize People. So much more is going on here that I do not completely understand but at least I have brought you as far as I am able of guiding you.

Now you can carry our contemplation and comprehension further afield. Look up in the Night Sky to see the Popol Wuj that occurs here on the Face of the Earth because it is in the Night Sky and our looking up that awakens us to a much more cosmic comprehension of this Mesoamerican Myth of the Maya Culture and Mesoamerican Civilization. The multivalent images of Ursa Major-the Big Dipper-La Carreta-Tojil-Kʼawil seen in the Night Sky of Mesoamerica manifests the polysemic ways of this mythic image of this Trickster Lord Tezcatlipoca who is Heart of the Sky-Jun Raqan-Hurricane-the One Footed One-the Smoking Mirror-Wuqubʼ Kaqix who creates the problems that only he can solve! One of those images is Tezcatlipoca as Tojil ʼdrilling fireʼ on the One-Footed of his One-Footed that ends in the ʼRed Giant Arcturusʼ where the ʼember of fireʼ can be seen set ablaze in the Night Sky.

body:
I just went outside my small writing room on March 9th of 2026 to see Arcturus directly over head here at 14˚41ʼ N in the Kʼicheʼ Highlands as Wuqubʼ Kaqix is seen falling head over tail onto the Western Horizon. It is 3AM which means I must get to bed and to sleep but this kept me awake until now with the writing of these words that have brought me relief knowing how important it has been to interpret this Mythic Masterpiece of Mesoamerica in the Cultural Context of Mesoamerican Mythology. I knew there was something that needed to be said about the multivalent polysemic comprehension of Wuqubʼ Kaqix who is much more complicated than the Western thus Christian dichotomy of Good and Evil. Wuqubʼ Kaqix as Lord Seven Scarlet Macaw creates the problem that you will see will end the Age of the Wooden People. The Hero Twins would have no reason to put the World in Order had Wuqubʼ Kaqix and his Two Sons not drawn a great deal of interest to themselves.

But that is what they want to do; the want to ʼsow discordʼ in order that problems sprout all about them that the Hero Twins are called to put in order; in order that IxMuqane ends up Sowing Maize in order to begin Growing Maize that she will grind on her grinding stone in order to mold and model; form and shape the First Four Fathers of the First Four Lineages of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom that will sprout into being at the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Sun at Origin of the Kʼicheʼ People of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo. They will be the Maize People who will create the problems that only they can solve but they donʼt solve those problems.

body:
The End of One Age is the Beginning of the Next Sun The End of One Sun is the Beginning of the Next Age This is when the Heart of the Sky transforms into el Adelantado Don Pedro de Alvarado who like Lord Quetzalcoatl can transform into the Four Footed Conqueror known as Nakxitl Quetzalcoatl. The Maya interpret el Conquistador Don Pedro de Alvarado as the Sun of Quetzalcoatl who has return to take back his Kingdom from Tezcatlipoca who as the Old Sun is no longer ʼhard or strongʼ and because of this his fire has been made wet and goes out being destroyed by a cold, cold rain and hail storm. Whereas the New Sun of Tonatiuh or Donadiu is so strong it just burns up everything in its path, the Kʼicheʼ Capital Qʼumaraq Aaj or Rotten Cane being already bent over and dried out and ready to be put to the torch along with its Rulers.

But you already know this and about the New Sun of the Kaxlan Winaq who as Donadiu is there at the ʼEnd of the Ageʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom and ʼBeginning of the Ageʼ of the Kaxlan Winaq-the Castilian Kingdom. Once again Quetzalcoatl has transformed there at the Creation of the Kaxlan Winaq just as Jun Raqan is there as Destroyer Deity Tezcatlipoca who transforms into the image of the Kaxlan Winaq. And so it goes the Maya didnʼt become Spaniards the Day-after the Spanish Conquest. Nor did they ever become the Spaniards or Catholics for that matter; except in the ways that empowered them to survive and prosper as a People; as a Pueblo known and named Kʼicheʼ. The Kʼicheʼ Maya adapted to the Kaxlan Winaq incursion of their Lands by adopting their Wooden People known as Santos y Virgines; Madres Divinas y Padres Eternos.

The Kʼicheʼ Maya held close to their Maya Kʼicheʼ Language and whatever empowered them in the Three Hundred and Sixty-Five Day Agricultural Calendar with the Forty Days of the Lenten Season or Two Twenty Day Months and Three Trecenas of Thirteen Days each while holding close to their Sacred Count of Days of the Chol Qʼij by remaining to be Day-keeping Day-Keepers and Prayer-making Prayer-Makers.

body: The Kʼicheʼ did exchange the Popol Wuj for the el Baile de la Conquista and el Baile de los Mexicanos while holding close to the Baile del Junajpu Kʼoy that must be left for another day or dawn as time slips by. So let us end this empowering Interpretation of this provocative section of Popol Wuj that appears to be much simpler than in fact it is. And when the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj seems stark and bare there is always something ingenious to be found there or here as it goes. So let us make a short review before we move forward with the confidence we have done our best to interpret these terse yet rich pages of Mythological Imagination. Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej as the Hero Twins of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq must ʼput Wuqubʼ Kaqix in his placeʼ in order that the Sun, Moon, and Star of the Maize People can Dawn to initiate the Age-the Era-the Epoch of the Sun of the Maize People who are the Kʼicheʼ People. Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej will sow maize in Grandmother IxMuqaneʼ s ʼhouseʼ in order that IxMuqane knows their ʼcondition-ukʼojeʼikʼ-stateʼ. To then plant Four Deified Seeds in Four Sacred Places of her House to Sanctify the Seed. This is the Sowing Half of the Sowing and Dawning that is the Popol Wuj. This Sowing and Dawning of the Sun of the Maize People is being prepared by the Hero Twins of the Maize People. The Boys, the Sons, the Twins Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are the Saqetal to be followed for all those Young Noble Initiates who will watch and wait for the Dawn of their Sun as Noble Lords. Noble Lords who will rule and reign as Co-Regent of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom who are Co-Rulers of the Kʼicheʼ Realm just like the Hero Twins do throughout their struggle ʼwithʼ and not ʼagainstʼ the powers of Death and Darkness so that the Light and Warm of the Sun; and, the Moisture and Pull of Moon of the Maize People can Dawn. This is the struggle of the Divine Powers of Life and Death; Growth and Decline; Sprouting-Out and Dying-Back that is being introduced to you here.

body:
I know this is ʼtoo muchʼ is going on here but you need more support then read the work of Susan Milbrath, Anthony Aveni, Guilhem Olivier, Henry B. Nicholson, Michael Smith, Elizabeth Baquedano, Alfredo López Austín, Oswaldo Chinchilla Mazariegos, Den nis Tedlock, Robert Carlsen, Karl Taube, and Lewis Hyde in order to develop your ideas and understanding of Tezcatlipoca as a Trickster Deity. Come let is shoulder our blowguns and be off on this Sacred Journey of the Popol Wuj.

SO HERE IT IS; THIS IS IT; this is just the Ancient Ancestral Account of the Boys ʼblow-gunningʼ false-face ʼLordʼ Seven Scarlet Macaw. Here then is their shooting-down Wuqubʼ Kaqix; they just blasted him with their blow-gun-uwubʼaxik; they just shot-down the Arrogant One with their blow- gun; they just knocked-down the Proud One with their blow-gunning. This was the Loud One known as Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kaqix, spoken of as Lord Seven Scarlet Macaw, Siete Guacamayo; Seven Papagayo; the Noble Lord named Seven Macaw. This here is the telling of the Twins shooting Wuqubʼ Kaqix with their blow- gun. This was when the Two Boys, the Two Sons-Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ took down Seven Macaw; when they knocked him out of his Tajpal Tree.

Here is the Original Account of Seven Scarlet Macaw being knocked-down with a blow- gun ball; when he was shot-out of his throne that was perched-up high in the forest canopy. Wuqubʼ Kaqix was hit by a blow-gun stone; a blow-gun bone by the Two Boys, Sons who were known as the Twins; the First One was named Hunter; Blow-gun Boy: Junajpu. And his Brother; his Twin; the Second One named He-She of the Hidden Jaguar-Moon; spoken of as Little Jaguar-Deer: Ixbʼalamkej. The Two Boys, the Two Sons, the Twins Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej; they just did it; they just did it with their magical power of transformation; they just did it with their Nawal blast of their breath; the magical way they blew through their blowgun; the way they just ʼpuffedʼ on their blowgun; the blowgun they shouldered everywhere they went.

body:
And so it was they who did it; it was those two who went walking; when they headed out talking; walking in the direction of the Great Tajpal Tree shouldering their blowgun; carrying the essence of their destiny on their shoulder; bearing the burden of their thoughts within; determined to do what was theirs to do as divine twins.

We will tell all three stories of each one of the Arrogant Ones; we will tell all three stories of each one of their deaths and defeats. We will tell of each one of them; each one their stories; each one of their deaths and defeats; the deaths and defeats of the three rivals, three enemies, three adversaries known as the three self- aggrandizing ones-ri nimarisaj ribʼ. For all three of them were taken down one at a time; the three of them were taken down one at a time by the Nawal Powers of the Two Boys, the Two Sons who were Nawal Winaq. It was just their Magical Transforming Powers that brought about the death and defeat of the Three Arrogant One. It was just the Nawal Power of Hero Twins that brought about the downfall and destruction of the Three Self-Magnifying Ones.

Now this Wuqubʼ Kaqix had his One Big Tree-Jun Nimaʼ Cheʼ, where he found his sustenance: rechaʼ.

This One Big Tree was the Nance tree known as a Tapaʼl. Tapaʼl is the proper Maya Kʼicheʼ name given to the Nance tree, just as Tapaʼl is the proper Maya Kʼicheʼ name given to the plentiful yellow fruit that grows on the limbs and amongst the leaves of this massive coastal tree. This Tapaʼl grew ʼas ifʼ it were a World of its own; a World that provided Wuqubʼ Kaqix with a secure sense of plenty in a prosperous and plentiful World that this Big Beautiful Bird ruled over from high up above the Jungle Canopy.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix ruled with a tremendous sense of self-confidence because of the way his Tapaʼl Tree nourished and nurtured him with great quantities of fruit. For Seven Scarlet Macaw was perfectly provided for while being splendidly sustained by the sweet and sour fruit of the Tapaʼl that he devoured each and every Day-jutaʼ Qʼij.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Wuqubʼ Kaqix could always be found perched on his Great Throne-Nimaʼ Qʼalibʼal in his One Big Tree-Jun Nimaʼ Cheʼ where the Sun brightened it branches and ripened the fruit as it passed over and across the Heart of the Sky. Truly, Wuqubʼ Kaqix lived the life of a Great Ruler who was Proud Regent of the World that was his to feed off from Dawn to Dusk.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix landed high up in his Tapaʼl where he took his mid-day meal. He just suckled the rich golden fruit that ripened there in plenty; he just gulped down the sweet sustenance of the Tapaʼl; the fine fruit of the Nance Tree. And so it was that Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej saw that this One Big Tree was the feeding place of the Arrogant One; the Self-Aggrandizing One; Seven Scarlet Macaw: Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

Tapaʼl: Nance Tree Tapaʼl: Nance Fruit The Twins saw him move all around the crown of this Nance Tree; he just fluttered about its limbs; he just flittered about its leaves; he just flapped about its limb; he just flopped about in its leaves; the limb; the leaves of this massively massive Tapaʼl Tree whose golden fruit shimmered and shined like the jewels and gems of a resplendent headdress that it wore like a regal crest; like a royal crown of the Forest Canopy where Wuqubʼ Kaqix ruled the Jungle as if he were the Heart of the Sky-Heart of the Earth.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix sucked the sweet flesh of the fresh fruit; he tested each one to see what tasted best; one after the next; one after the next; each one tasted better than the last; sometimes sweet; sometime tart; some hard; some soft; which one tasted better; which one tasted the best.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix never stopped; he never took a rest; he never calmed his searched in his quest to find the best of the best; on the contrary he just kept it up testing and tasting the endless quantities of fruit this Tapaʼl bore in its branches; he just used his beak to break off one ripened fruit after the next in this fruit-fest of Wuqubʼ Kaqix up high in the Tapaʼl Tree. Verily, verily one had to say that this Wuqubʼ Kaqix was nothing less than blessed because his favorite fruit was for him alone since no other animal dared come anywhere near his throne that was his home that was his nest.

body:
Indeed, the Two Boys just hid out there below; waiting and watching to see where we would go; the two of them there in the branches of the One Big Tree; the Great Nance; Jun Nimalaj Tapʼal. The Boys; the Sons; the Twins were there in the tree sneaking about in its leaves; moving about there in its limbs; hidden in its fruit and foliage waiting for a chance to do what they came to do.

This then was when Wuqubʼ Kaqix arrived there up in his perch, settling down atop his golden sustenance, the yellow fruit of this tremendous tree. It was there that he devoured as he suckled the Tapaʼl fruit of the Tapaʼl tree.

Jun Junajpu enters into Junajpu The Divine Ancestor enters into the Descendant The Soul of the Ancestor becomes the Soul of the Descendant The Ancestral Soul of the Divine Ancestor enters the Soul of the Replacement

The Father of Junajpu who is named Jun Junajpu will now ʼenter the soulʼ of his Replacement who is his Son who is his Descendant in order to get the work done of taking revenge on the Lords of Death. The Lords of Death have sacrificed Jun Junajpu which first time readers do not know but the Maya once knew this Myth of the Maize People backward and forward. So when we engage our imagination we are able to engage our soul in order that it participates in this Mythical Realm of the Imagination that is an Imaginal Realm of Myth.

The Divine Ancestor of the Maize People known as the First Father of Maize who is named Jun Junajpu is going to be ensouled and inspired by Junajpu who is his Replacement as his Descendant through the ʼknowing remembranceʼ of the Divine Ancestor-Jun Junajpu who will live through his Descendent-Junajpu. Popol Wuj calls us to experience the Mayan sense of transcendence through the collective memory and remembrance of the Ancestral Soul. We must engage our imagination but to engage our imagination we must engage our soul in order to enter in the Mythical Relationship between Divinity-Kabʼawil and Humanity-Winaq; Nawales and Divine Ancestors; Divine Ancestors and Descendants; Animals and Human Beings; Human Beings and the Entire Animated World or Anima Mundi.

body: The Popol Wuj calls out to us to ʼenter into the Ensouled World of Myth as Junajpu becomes his Father by him being named through the Nawal practice of ʼNaming the Nameʼ of Jun Junajpu so that Junajpu becomes Jun Junajpu. This becoming the Nawal or Magical Animal Transform is what we feel in order imagine in order to experience the transforming and changing essence of the Popol Wuj when we ʼbecomeʼ a Great Big Bird engaging our soul; engaging our imagination to become the Nawal of this Noble Lord Wuqubʼ Kaqix who in fact is Heart of the Sky who is in fact the Trickster Deity Jun Raqan who is Ukʼuʼx Kaj who is in fact a Nawal Transform of the Principal Divinity or Kabʼawil known as the Heart of the Sky. This is what we might best understand as the Transcendent Function of Myth. Junajpu becomes Jun Junajpu in order for Junajpu to know all that Jun Junajpu learned through his life experience that he lived out when he lived on the Face of the Earth. This lived experience of the Ancestor is passed on through the Descendant so that the Descendant becomes ʼsumamente intelegenteʼ or ʼsuper intelligentʼ or ʼnimalaj unaʼojʼ as well as intuitive with a highly developed feeling function and functioning of the sense. All that the Ancestors learned is passed on to their Descendants who are their Replacements. When one ʼenters the wordʼ of Popol Wuj it is ʼas ifʼ everything is begins to change and transform within our Mythic Imagination. By engaging our soul completely we are able to engage our Mythic Imagination completely to awaken the Mythic Realm that is the Imaginal Realm that has been brought to life through this highly imaginative myth where names are names to bring those named being to life in the Imaginal Realm that is formed and shaped by the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This ʼmagical storyʼ of Wuqubʼ Kaqix and the Hero Twins who are the Sons, the Boys of their Father and Uncle Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who are the Maize Lords that have already been sacrificed although first time readers do not known this. So let us let you in on a little secret as to how we are about to enter into an ancestral form of ʼsympathetic magicʼ by re-naming the First Son who we known as Junajpu by the name of his father: Jun Junajpu. With the ʼnaming of the nameʼ Junajpu has become Jun Junajpu to know what to do. Imagine the connotations this has for human beings who are able to imagine in this way; the knowledge and memory of life experience are able to come through. And so it is that our magically transforming narrative begins to speak of Junajpu as his Father Jun Junajpu which is the Mayaʼs way of enabling the Replacements of the Ancestors known as Descendants to be and become their Ancestors by being and becoming the Replacements of their Ancestors. Suddenly the idea of following oneʼs Divine Ancestors as the ʼsaqetalʼ or ʼdivine bridgeʼ as in ʼdivine pathʼ of one Generation to the next Generation. When the Generations are able to pass from one to the next then we come to live in a World that is ʼinformedʼ by this \ Principal Cultural Idea of the Descendants being and becoming the Replacement of their Ancestors.

body: This can be understood as the Ancestors entering their Descendants in order to experience existence as the being and becoming of the Nawal of their Living and Dead Ancestors by entering into the shared Ancestral Soul of the Descendant and Ancestor. In the Maya Cosmos there is no lineal time line going back and forth on a line of time. Instead it is a circle in which the Ancestors enter into the Descendant while the Descendent enters the Ancestors through the sharing of Ancestral Soul which is to say the Soul of Lineage. And this is when one comes to realize the catastrophe it is for humanity for it to have committed so much genocide and its destruction of life lines of lineages that are soul connections of Ancestors and Descendants. But there is always as solution and we know what that solution is: humans have the capacity to activate the human imagination which is to say humans have the capacity to activate the human-divine soul; the ancestor-descendant soul. In this way the Descendant becomes the Ancestor by acting and speaking through the Ancestral Soul that creates a mythic bridge through the Descendant becoming the Ancestral Replacement of whoever or whatever is needed to bring oneʼs lineage back to life in order that their work on the Face of the Earth can be brought to fruition.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: The Nawal nature and condition of Junajpu is to become the essence and being of his Father Jun Junajpu whose power and strength; seeing and knowing; capacities and capabilities ʼpass-over in order to enter intoʼ his Son Junajpu: Father and Son share Ancestral Soul. Imagine the transcendent capacity and capability of human existence when human beings engage their soul as an Ancestral Soul. Imagine what might be accomplished in the sense of tapping into the ʼtranscendent functionʼ of Ancestor and Descendant that are allowed to follow the sacred path of Ancestral Experience that is known here as the ʼsaqetalʼ that is invoked and remembered in order to be brought back to life as a shared Ancestral Soul. An Ancestral Soul that is ʼnamedʼ in order to be ʼknownʼ to enable the soul to come back into existence in oneʼs descendants by opening up oneʼs body and soul; heart and mind; spirit and imagination to the transcendent experience of being and becoming oneʼs Ancestor or Ancestors. Imagine what kind of possibilities come to life in a life lived like this as is suggested here when Junajpu is named Jun Junajpu. We know this is not a ʼscribal errorʼ because the name of the Father is done with the ʼperfect consistencyʼ of a Day-keeper naming the name of Jun Junajpu exactly ʼseven timeʼ as an invocation of Wuqubʼ Junajpu-Seven Junajpu which is exactly what is expected from a performative tradition such as the ʼkeeping and countingʼ of the days to ʼname and numberʼ the Days in order to name their ʼDestinyʼ or ʼNawalʼ through this sacred naming of the names and counting of the count. This is the way the Maya found the Destiny of a Replacement or Descendant of an Ancestor. They found the Destiny of the Descendant according to the Sacred Count of Days which is the way the Maya speak of the 260 Divinatory Calendar. In this way the Father and Uncle of Junajpu, IxBʼalamkej are made present through the invocation and incantation of their names in a magical sort of mythical kind of mystical way so that the Ancestor is remembered through the ʼnaming of namesʼ that fires up the imagination through this Myth of the Maize People.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: The power of myth is that it creates a bridge upon which human beings are able to cross back and forth across generations in order to activate the Transcendent Function of the Ancestral Soul in the Descendant; in the Replacement and in the Ancestors in order to support them as well in the past and for our descendants in the future. The Maya Scribes call us to participate with them in this magical performance and nawal experience of ancestral transformation through this ritual drama of the ʼhuntʼ of the Blowgunner; AjPubʼ and its incantation of the ancestral name of the ʼFirst Hunter-Jun-Junajpuʼ whose ancestral soul, nawal spirit will enter his son Junajpu. This might best call this ʼparticipation mystiqueʼ because of the way the text enchants us so much so that we want to play along in the mythical action and mythical speech of the Hero Twins: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. The Maya Scribes who transcribed their Ancestorsʼ Popol Wuj want us to participate in their recitation of the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account as ritual participants in the mythic imagination who enter fully in their sacred incantation of their remembrance of the Ancestors. This invocation of the past to remember the past in the present is accomplished through the nawal experience of invocation that calls upon the ancestral powers of transformation that is embodied and ensouled in this nawal act of performative speech that brings forth the magical naming of the Son by the ancestral name of the Father: Jun JunAjPu. This is the Transcendent Function of the Mythic Imagination.

body:
We know the Boys are grown-up and old enough to begin doing the work of performing the tasks of Cultural Heroes of ʼtaking-up the burdenʼ of their Father Jun Junajpu and Uncle Wuqubʼ Junajpu who are already dead for some twenty years. But these Fathers must be brought back to life through their Sons so that their Lineages is not ʼcut-offʼ at the ʼtrunkʼ as the Lords of Death want to do. But they canʼt because these people known as the Maize People are super ʼhardʼ just as they are sumamente ʼtoughʼ. The lineage will not die because the ʼnames are namesʼ in order to active the mythic imagination to bring the Ancestral Soul to life. And so it is that we know Jun Junajpu is dead by the fact that his ʼengendered sonsʼ are alive to complete his work in the world of the Sky-Earth. Jun Junajpu was decapitated long ago yet his Ancestral Soul survives as the guide and protector of his ʼreplacementʼ or ʼkʼexelʼ who we know as Junajpu. The Ancestral Soul of Jun Junajpu enters into the Ancestral Soul of Junajpu so he can do what he was born to do which is to avenge his Fathersʼ death. The death of the Fathersʼ must be avenged so that the lineage is kept alive in an Indigenous World where oneʼs Uncle is oneʼs Father; and where oneʼs Fathersʼ Souls must be kept alive.

So Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej have Fathers who are a Father and an Uncle who are named in order to be known as Fathers which is important in a Cosmos where Fathers die all of the time. And when a Father dies before leaving Descendant-Replacements behind then there is a create danger that the entire experience of the lineage will be ʼcut-offʼ at the trunk. This is what Junajpu as Jun Junajpu want to avoid at all costs because they want to bring the soul of the Fathers-Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu back to life. The Divine Ancestors of the Popol Wuj will be brought back to life through their Descendants who are their Replacement s of their Ancestors.

body:
The Hero Twins give of themselves completely so that their lineage comes back to life which is the essence of Popol Wuj. The essence of the Popol Wuj which is the nature and condition of the Popol Wuj is to bring the Ancestral Soul back to life so the Lineage doesnʼt ʼdie deadʼ once and for all and forever. So when we ask the questions: Where we are the Descendants? Where we are the Replacements? We can say: the Descendants to be found in the invocation of the Divine Ancestors; the Replacements are in the remembrance of the Divine Ancestors?

And this is precisely what the Popol Wuj asks the Providers and Sustainers to do: invoke the Ancestors; remember the Ancestors; Invoke; Remember; Incantation and Invocation of Memory and Remembrance of the Ancestors as the Lineage Holders of the Lineage and their Ancestors and Descendants. Imagine the connotation of living in a world such as this that is formed and shaped right here in the Popol Wuj.

Seven Naming of the Name Jun Junajpu In the Toppling of Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kaqix This then was when Jun Junajpu (1) blew hard on his blowgun ball making it fly as it flew just as he planned to do so his shot hit Wuqubʼ Kaqix smack on his jaw to bring about the fall of Lord Seven Macaw. Wuqubʼ Kaqix cried out as he fell from his perch; he was knocked backwards to end-up falling down to the ground where he landed all sprawled out;

flat on his back-chimalmat beneath the Tapaʼl Tree. The Boys went running towards Seven Macaw who was now down on the ground knocked out flat beneath his One Big Nance Tree. Quickly, Jun Junajpu (2) ran to grab hold of Wuqubʼ Kaqix. But it didnʼt go as the Boys wished because it was the arm of Jun Junajpu (3) that was torn away like a branch of tree by Wuqubʼ Kaqix who grabbed hold of the severed limb of the Twin to then bear it away from beneath the Great Big Tree of Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

Wuqubʼ Kaqix had acted real quick when he picked-up the dismembered limb like a big stick to then throw it over his shoulder so he could carry it away like a doubled-up stalk of maize; like bent and broken cane.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It was only by losing his arm that Jun Junajpu (4) had let go of the tight grip with which he held hold of Wuqubʼ Kaqix, allowing the Big Bright Bird to make his escape.

Nevertheless, the Two Boys; the Two Sons; ri Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ had done well for themselves; for they had not been defeated at first by Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

It was then that the arm of Jun Junajpu (5) was carried away by Wuqubʼ Kaqix as he made his way back home cradling his broken jaw.

He walked in this way arriving to where his woman was while holding his jaw tenderly with one hand while carrying something bent and broken over his shoulder with the other. “What have you brought back with you there?” asked Chimalmat, the wife, the woman of Wuqubʼ Kaqix. “Indeed, what could it be? Those two tricksters-kaʼibʼ kʼaxtokʼ just shot me with their blowgun ball, dislocating my jaw as you can see. Now all my teeth are just loose causing me this dreadful pain from which I now suffer so very, very terribly,” said Wuqubʼ Kaqix before Chimalmat, to then give her instructions while cradling his broken jaw the pitiable way he did. “First, this arm here that I carry must be hung over the hearth. Just tie it up there with a lasso; just bind it up there over the fire until they come for it. We will see then if those Two Boys really are the Tricksters they appear to be,” said Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

It was then that Chimalmat hung the arm of Jun Junajpu (6) over the embers of her three-stone hearth with its three-stone fire burning within. So this then was when they thought it over again, Jun Junajpu (7), Ixbʼalamkej.

Pu-Tula-Tollan Place of Origins Tula; Tollan; Cholula; Chollan Ancient Ancestral Place of Reeds and Rushes Here ends the passage of the ʼSeven Blowgun Hunter-Wuqubʼ Junajpu-Seven Ancient Ancestor of the Place of Origins known as Pu-Place of Reeds; Tula; Tollan; Cholula; Chollan. This has been a perfect example-saqetal of the ʼNaming of the Namesʼ of the First Father of Maize-Jun Junajpu-Ancestral Deity of the Maize Lineage.

This has been the invocation and remembrance of the Ancestral Soul of the First Father that is the Ancestral Soul of the Descendant; of the Replacement who is named to be known as the First Son-Junajpu-One Hunter; the Ancient One from the Ancient Ancestral Place of Pu- Reeds; Original Place of the Reeds and Rushes; the Ancient Ancestral Place of Pu; Place Reeds; the Primordial Place of Abundance; Original Place Thick with Primordial Prosperity known as Pu.

Here is where we ʼenter the Nawal Nameʼ that is the ʼMagical Transforming Nameʼ that magically transforms the ʼFace of the Ancestor; Face of the Descendantʼ by ʼnaming the nameʼ of the ʼAncestral Soulʼ as the ʼOriginal Soulʼ that is the ʼLineage Soulʼ that is passed down from the Ancestor to the Descendant who is the Replacement of the ʼOriginal Faceʼ of the ʼOriginal Faceʼ of those who ʼsprouted forthʼ from the Original Place of Reeds and Rushes known to us as: Tula; Tollan; Cholula; Cholan best known place of the Lakeshore Place that Grows Thick with Abundance: Pu. Thus sprouts forth the origin of the naming of the Original Name of the Original Ancestors known by the Ancestral Name: Jun-Aj-Pu: Ancestral One from the Primordial Place known and named as Pu.

This is ʼNaming of the Namesʼ is a magnificent invocation and remembrance of the Nawal Powers of Transformation of the Jun-Aj-Pu Lineage and its continuance as the Life- Loving Lineage and Line of the Maize People; the Life Perpetuating Lineage and Line of Pueblo of Maize with their Life-Giving Light; Life-Sustaining Warmth whose essence is embodied and ensouled in the Eternal Return of Life; Eternal Return of Maize; Eternal Return of Ancestral Soul; Eternal Return of the Ancestral Face through the Rebirth of the Emerald Seed of Life-Jade Green Bead of Eternity of those who live in the warmth and light of the Sun and beneath the sparkling souls of the Ancestors seen shining in the calm quiet darkness of the Infinite and Eternal Night.

body:
This is the ʼNaming of the Namesʼ of those who the Ancestor and Descendant; Original Face and Replacement for ʼAll-Timeʼ in the ʼEverlasting Lightʼ of the People and Pueblo for Eternity: Saqil Amaqil. This is as it is said; this is as it was heard through the ʼNaming of the Namesʼ forever more to the End of Time-Saqil Amaqil as it is spoken in the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

Saqi Nim Aq; Saqi Nima Tziz Great White Peccary; Great White Coati Ancient Old White-Haired Jabali; Ancient Old White-Haired Coati Ancient Old Grandfather; Ancient Old Grandmother This then is when they spoke there to an ancient-looking Grandfather. Truly ʼwhite-hairedʼ was the head of this Old Man, he was there alongside the ancient- looking Grandmother. Truly humble was the Grandmother.

They were just bent over like corn stalks, just doubled over were they like maize; like broken canes were those who had lived to see so many days. They were just bent down low because of their age; truly ancestral looking were these elderly old people indeed, and that is just how these two Ancient Ones appeared when they, the Boys, addressed them with great regard and respect; reverence and admiration. Saqi Nim Aq was the name of the Grandfather. Saqi Nima Sis was the name of the Grandmother.

It was then that the Two Boys, the Two Sons, spoke with them as their Grandmother; when they spoke with them as their Grandfather; the Two Boys address to the Old Woman just as they address the Old Man when they greeted them there beside the road, beneath the tree. And this is what they said:

“We wish you would accompany us when we go over there to bring back our arm that is hanging there on the hearth of Chimalmat; the fire that burns alongside Wuqubʼ Kaqix. We shall just follow along behind you there so we can bring back what is ours; ours that is now theirs; ours that is theirs hanging over the fire of their hearth,” said the Boys before continuing on in their reverent way:

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: “Perhaps you will say: ʼThese here are our Grandsons who accompany us; dead is their Mother; dead is their Father; these Two Boys just tag along with us, they circle about us all day, they just run around us as they play while we make our way down the road looking for where our luck might lay. We might just give them away since our work is nothing more than removing worms-chikopil- animalitos from peopleʼs teeth everyday; people who have nothing to pay. This is what we do; this is our work; this our lifeʼs way,ʼ this is what you will say,” said the Boys to the White-Haired Ones; their Ancient Ancestors: Saqinim Aq, Saqinimʼa Sis. “You must say this as though we were mere children, as if we were just Young Boys in the eyes of Wuqubʼ Kaqix. We will tell you what you need to know so you know what to say when the time comes to do what needs to be done. Donʼt worry, we will help you; we will tell you just what you need to say so you know just what to do,” said the Two Sons, the Two Boys when they gave their instructions to the Old Woman, the Old Man. “Utz bʼa la! Very well, then,” they said. So this then was when they went over to where Wuqubʼ Kaqix was lying on his ʼside-tzamalʼ, right there before his throne; uqʼalibʼal. This is when the Old Grandmother, Old Grandfather who were spoken of as Atiʼt, Mamaʼ came passing by on the road. Just playing along behind them were the Two Boys. Just following the Old Man; the Old Woman; Mamaʼ, Atiʼt, were the Two Sons running about as Grandchildren always do when circling around behind their Grandfather, Grandmother.

As you will see, these Grandsons-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are ʼReplacements-Kʼexelʼ of these Ancestral Grandmother-Grandfather whoʼs Grandsons are born on the Face of the Earth- Uwach Ulew as the Replacements-Kʼexel of Fathers-Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who were tricked through lies and deceit into being sacrificed on the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice through the deception of the Lords of Death. This is the ancestral experience of trickery the Hero Twins-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej learn from to defeat the Lords of Death to then rise-up above all the rest to become the Sun and the Moon that move across the Face of Earth as the Heart of the Sky. Popol Wuj is a Myth of Trickster Twins who must bring about the ʼgreat reversalʼ of Trickster Lords of the Underworld; Trickster Lords of Death who only want ʼdeathʼ for ʼlifeʼ where as the Lords of Life; the Maize Lords; Maize Deities; Kabʼawil only want to bring their ʼdeadʼ Ancestors back to life.

That was when they passed right below the House of the Noble Lord- Rochoch Ajaw where the Great Chief; Great Lord; Nima Ajaw was lying on his side. Just then, the one named Wuqubʼ Kaqix cried out, he just howled in pain, all because of his loose teeth; his teeth that were loose where he was hit in the jaw by the blow-gun ball.

It was right then when Wuqubʼ Kaqix saw the Grandfather, the Grandmother, Mamaʼ, Atiʼt accompanying one-an-other on the road while their Grandsons circled around them like little birds as they played about them; now in front, now behind; round and round the Boys swirled as they twirled around them as they whirled about them; circling them as they played about ʼas ifʼ they were nothing more than children. “Where are you coming from Our Grandfather-Qamam?” asked he who was seen to be a Noble Lord-Jun Ajaw.

“We are just out searching for what is ours-xa oj tzuqubʼey qibʼ-we are just out looking about for our sustenance,” they said. “What then is your sustenance? Who, then, are your providers? Are not these children here that accompany you the ones who sustain you?” asked Wuqubʼ Kaqix. “No, no, not at all, it is not that way, you Our Noble Lord-Lal Ajaw; these Boys here are just our Grandsons-Qamam. It is we who take pity on them. We are those who provide for them; we are those who take care of them. It is just us who give them a portion of what is given to us, oh Noble Lord, Lal Ajaw,” said the Grandmother, the Grandfather; Atiʼt, Mamaʼ. By now Wuqubʼ Kaqix was finished off by the great pain he received from his loose teeth and so it was that only with great pain that he spoke:

“I would like to ask a favor from you; for you to take pity on me; please, I let me ask you that perhaps you might show me a kindness. What sort of medicine do you make; what poison to you cure? What illness do you treat; what sickness do you heal!” asked Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

body:
“It is just worms that we extract from peopleʼs teeth; little animalitos are all that we pull from peopleʼs teeth-xa chikopil eyaj chiqelesaj; that is what is ours. Just eyes do we heal, just sight do we cure. Just bones do we set, you, oh Noble Lord-Lal Ajaw, this is what we do; this is what is ours,” said the Old Man, the Old Woman-xechaʼ kʼut ri Atiʼt; Mamaʼ. “Utz bʼa la! Very well, very well indeed, would you not do that for me; maybe just cure my teeth a little? Truly, they just ache all day; truly unbearable is the pain they give me. I donʼt get any sleep because of them; because of them and my eyes. The little bastards, they shot me with their blowgun; those tricksters they hit me right here on my jaw. Ever since it began, I havenʼt eaten a thing. So please, do me the favor; just show me a kindness! I am in agony because my teeth; they just torment me.” “Very well, Lal Ajaw, it is just the little worms, those tiny little worms that eat away at your teeth. They are those that are there to cause you pain. It is just replacements that must go in, since your loose teeth must come out,” they said; those who are known as the Old Woman, the Old Man.

Ancestral Pair Old Woman, the Old Man AjKun: Healer; Curandera; Curandero Healers of eyes, curers of teeth; bone-setters, just ancient old healers were they, specialists is what they were; spider bite and scorpion bite were what was theirs to cure; snake bite and poisonous spines and infectious thorns that is what they healed. This Ancient Couple were real specialist; this Ancestral Pair were just Curanderos; Hueseros is who they were.

They just worked for what the People could give them; their food; their sustenance; nothing more; the Pueblo had no more to give. Just feathers, jade beads, Tzʼite beans, pretty little shiny things, ancient clay figurines found in the ground; buried beneath the earth; these are the Ancestral Remembrances received from the Milpa; this is what the AjKun; Curanderos; Curanderas received for their sustenance.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were the only things that most ailing people had to give; with cacao and maize they were given what was theirs to live on day after day; cacao and maize were the hard, hard beans and perfect, precious seeds with which they were compensated for the healing they gave to those who were in need; these Healers of Eyes, Ears, Nose, and Teeth were given what was found in abundance in exchange for their healing work they gave to the People of the Pueblo in the most generous way; most of all it was by saying thanks; by showing gratitude; by being receiving deep feelings of appreciation through the deepest sense of grace that come with beans and maize; cacao and canela; vanilla and candela; copal and panela; this is the way to balance to giving and receiving of healing.

This is how they were paid when they were paid with ʼhard, hardʼ seeds and beans that they could use little by little as they made their way down the road watching and waiting to see what destiny provided them in lives sustained by the misfortune of those who sought their special favors in the ancient art of healing ʼdis-easeʼ that was the curing of illness brought on by accidents that were encountered as unfortunate incidents that were inevitably stumbled upon on the path of life.

But this pain of Wuqubʼ Kaqix was no accident in this Myth of the Maize People; but the Old Woman; Old Man who are the Healers of Teeth make it seem like the ʼanimalitos-chikopilʼ are eating away this Big Birds Teeth; this is the way that the terrible pain suffered is made out to be. These Old Folks are Tricksters who reverse this sacred narrative to ʼit is because of the ʼLittle Wormsʼ eating your teeth that we must extract them in order to replace them with ʼnew teethʼ that will be made into the ʼreplacements-kʼexelʼ of the loose teeth of Wuqubʼ Kaqix that must come out to ends his suffering and agony…And so Wuqubʼ Kaqix speaks to say what only an Arrogant Self-Aggrandizing Lord and Ruler could say; which is when he gives the following speech.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Noble Lord, Jun Ajaw Look Like a Lord; Act Like a Lord; Speak Like a Lord “But it might not be so good that my teeth should be taken out. It is just because of them that I am a Lord-Jun Ajaw-a Ruler. It is because of my adorned eyes and adorned teeth of precious metal and shimmering silver that make me who I am; my adornment is what makes me a Noble Lord-Jun Ajaw,” cried Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

“Truly, my beauty, my finery, my elegance comes from the embellishment of my teeth and the adornment of my eyes. The source of my power and authority lies in my fine feathers; it shines from my resplendent jade necklace; it shimmers from my glittering emerald jewelry; it speaks through my stunning turquoise mask; my royal adornment, my regal embellishment are what make me who I am,” confessed Wuqubʼ Kaqix. “Donʼt worry; itʼs not like that; we will put replacements in; replacements made of ground bone is what we will exchange them with, bright white bone is what we will put back in!” said the Old Ones, the Ancient Ones.

But the ground bone they said they would use as replacements was just white maize; finely ground white maize-saq ixim-was what they prepared to set in the mouth of Seven Macaw in exchange for the adorned teeth they pulled from his mouth. “Very well, take them out! Just do what you have to do to cure me! Just help, just heal me if you will!” he then said when he spoke. This then was when the loose teeth of Wuqubʼ Kaqix came out. Just white maize was put back in to replace the teeth they pulled out. And it was just those white kernels of maize that shined bright from his mouth. But then, suddenly, his face fell. No longer did he look like a Lord. No longer did he appear to be an Ajaw. This was when they finished taking out his jade teeth that once glittered and gleamed bright in his mouth, the resplendent jade smile of Wuqubʼ Kaqix was no longer there where it had been. Then they turned to healing his eyes; those well adorned eyes of Wuqubʼ Kaqix. They just fixed his eyes by getting them back in order. This was when they took out the silver. They just extracted the precious metal without him feeling a thing.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This then was the beginning of the end of his self-aggrandizement; the beginning of the end of his self-magnification; the beginning and end of his self- glorification; all of which came to their inevitable end; none of it was allowed to deceive others anymore.

It was just their ingenious thoughts; it was just their imaginative thinking; just their transformative kind of ancestral intelligence that was the root of their intuitive knowing known as ʼnaʼojʼ that revealed to them what they had to do and where they had to go no matter where they were; no matter who they were with. It was just their Nawal Way being twinned from within that magically transformed their Nawal Intelligence; and, Nawal Way of being and becoming Jun AjPu; IxBʼalamKej and their acting and speaking like Nawal Ajaw; those who were known as Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej-xawi kinaʼoj, kinawal Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

Death and Disappearance of Wuqubʼ Kaqix Death of Chimalmat; Mother Sipakna and Kabʼraqan

This then was when he died, the one named Wuqubʼ Kaqix: Seven Macaw as he is known. It was then that Junajpu took back his arm and set it back in place.

Soon after that Chimalmat died, she was the wife Wuqubʼ Kaqix; Shield- Bearer was the women of Wuqubʼ Kaqix she died too; Chimalmat died along with her man Seven Scarlet Macaw.

It was in this way that the wealth of Wuqubʼ Kaqix was lost. It was just a healer-AjKun-who carried it all away; the resplendent jade necklaces-ri kuwal; the precious emerald jewelry-yamanik-the precious gems.

All that made Wuqubʼ Kaqix the False-face Lord that he was; was taken away; all that made him what he was; was taken all away. Everything that he wore to embellish himself to make him the proud and arrogant ruler he became here on the Face of the Earth was carried away by just-xa Jun AjKun; un Curandero.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Those who brought this about are named here as Nawal Atiʼt, Nawal Mamaʼ for it is they who accomplished it all; the Ancient Old Woman, the Ancient Old Man. They are those who did it with their Nawal powers of transformation; their miraculous powers of transformation that gave the Grandmother, Grandfather their magical powers of transformation. This was the Magical Transforming Strength- Nawal Chuqʼabʼ of the Nawal Atiʼt, Nawal Mamaʼ for they are those known as Nawal Winaq. The Boys, the Sons had already taken back ʼtheirʼ arm to then plant it back in its place; the place from where it had been torn out and taken away.

Their work had come out well; Junajpu could to do all that he had done before. They did what they did to bring about the death of Wuqubʼ Kaqix whoʼs arrogant kinds of self-aggrandizing ways were seen as ugly-itzel to them; the Boys.

And so it was that the two of them walked on; down the road they went. It was just the word of the Heart of the Sky-utzij Ukʼux Kaj that was their doing.

It was they who listened to the word of Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj that was their calling; the calling of the Two Sons; the Sacred Word of Heart of the Sky was the doing of the Two Boys-Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ those who were spoken of as Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

Now we shall tell of another arrogant one; another self-magnifying one; Sipakna is his name. This then is the Ancient Word; the Ancestral Account that tells of all that was done by the Two Boys; the Two Sons-Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ those who are known as Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej, by names. Let us tell of their defeat and destruction of Sipakna the First Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqixʼ.

Sipakna: the Spiny One; the Smoking One He who was the First born Son of Lord Seven Scarlet Macaw Nabʼe Kʼajol Wuqubʼ Kaqix “I am Maker of Mountains!” “In Bʼanol Juyubʼ!” . These are the deeds; these are doings of Sipakna, the First born Son of Seven Scarlet Macaw-unabʼe Kʼajol Wuqubʼ Kaqix. “I am maker of mountains!” Said Sipakna.

“In bʼanol juyubʼ!” Kachaʼ ri Sipakna. “I am he who makes mountains!” Cried the one named Sipakna.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is what Sipakna said so let us tell his story of his making mountains. Let us tell of his work there on the river alongside the Four Hundred Boys-Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ those who are known as the Four Hundred Star-Boys of the South: Centzon Huitznahua. Sipakna: Nabʼe Kʼajol-First Born Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix; Caiman Son, Volcano Boy, the Spiny One; and, the Four Hundred Boys, Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ

Here then we shall tell of the ʼdeedsʼ; the ʼdoingsʼ of the First-born Son- Nabʼe Kʼajol of Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

“In bʼanol juyubʼ! I am the maker of mountains,” roared Sipakna.

The First Born Son, Caiman Boy named Sipakna was bathing there in the water when the Four-Hundred Boys-Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ went walking by on the bank of the river-chuchiʼ jaʼ. The Four Hundred Boys were dragging a Great Big Tree-Jun Nima Cheʼ when Sipakna saw them. The Great Big Tree the Four Hundred Boys-Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ were dragging along was the Post-Raqan that they were going to use as the Pillar of their Hut-Kikabʼal. It was there in the River where Sipakna was swimming that the Four- Hundred Boys passed by; they passed by where Sipakna was bathing in the Water- Jaʼ of the River-Jaʼ.

Those Boys had cut down another Great Big Tree; this one was for the Crossbeam of their hut-Uwapalil Kikabʼal; the Hut-Kikabʼal of the Four Hundred Boys. The Hut they were building; the Hut they were raising with the Post-Raqan that was the Pillar they were going use for their hut. The other Great Big Tree they cut for their Hut they would use as the Crossbeam-Uwapalil Kikabʼal known as ʼla Madre or Soleraʼ of their Initiation Hut: Kikabʼal.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
So, then, Sipakna who was a Caiman Boy that was a Crocodile Boy was known as Volcano Boy; the Spiny One, the Smoking One who was the One that noticed the Four Hundred Boys dragging a Great Big Tree that was a Great Big Post and so he asked them, “What are you doing you Boys? What are you making you who are Sons-Naki pa kibʼano Ix Kʼajolabʼ?” “Itʼs this tree, this log. We just canʼt pick it up. We just canʼt lift it up. We canʼt shoulder it; we canʼt shoulder it to carry it over there where we are building our Hut,” said the Four Hundred Boys-Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ. “I can shoulder it! Iʼll carry it for you,” said Caiman Boy-Sipakna. “Where does it go? What do you need for it?” “Itʼs just the Crossbeam of our Hut-xa uwapalil qakabʼal,” they said.

“Very well! Utz bʼa la!” he said.

So then right away Sipakna dragged their Great Big Tree-Jun Nima Cheʼ over to where he could pick it up and shoulder it over to where the Boys were building their Hut: the Hut of the Four Hundred Boys-kikabʼal Omuch Kʼajolabʼ- the Hut of the Four Hundred Sons.

“Just stay here with us, Boy; you can stay right here with us, you Son-at Kʼajol,” they said.

“Do you have a Mother, a Father?” they asked. “None to speak of,” he said. “Let us then press you into our service so that you might carry another tree for us tomorrow. We just need your help lifting the Post for our Hut; we just need you to help raise the Pillar for Our Hut-Raqan Qakabʼal.” “Fine!” he said.

This then was when they gathered together their thoughts; this was when they gathered together to talk it over; the Four Hundred Boys just celebrated Council with one another to listen to what One-an-Other had to say.

“He is only a Boy! What should we do about him? Shouldnʼt we just kill him? For what he does is just no good. He alone lifts up our great big wooden posts; posts we cannot lift ourselves. He lifts those great big trees of ours all by himself and he is just a Boy!” This then was when they came up with an idea that soon would become a plan to end the days of Sipakna. “Letʼs just dig a great big hole over there where we can throw him down in it to then bury him there,” they said to one another.
