source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“We will just say: ʼSon, go down into this hole and bring up the earth,ʼ this is what we will say,” said the Four Hundred Boys when they thought upon their idea; their idea of what they would say to Sipakna in order to tell him what to do.

“This will be when Sipakna is bent over his work down deep in the hole. When he is digging down deep in the hole and while he is digging still we will throw our Great Big Tree down on him so that he dies deep down in the hole,” said the Four Hundred Sons, the Four Hundred Boys: Omuch Kʼajolabʼ. So then they dug it out; they just carved it out; they just excavated one big hole that descended deep down below; they dug and dug until they had dug a deep, deep hole.

This then is when they called for Sipakna: “We are quite pleased with you; perhaps you could keep digging deep down for we can go no further; we just canʼt reach down deeper; deeper down in the hole,” said the Four Hundred Sons.

“Utz bʼa la!” said Sipakna.

So then he descended down into the hole and began digging. “Call up to us when you have dug out all the dirt,” they said to him.

“Fine!-We!” he called up to them above while he just kept digging. But the hole he began digging was the hole that would be his salvation because he knew they wanted to kill him. So he dug a second hole over to one side where he could save himself from being killed. “How much farther do you have to go?” asked the Four Hundred Boys.

“I am still digging but I will call out to you when I have finished the digging-out of this hole,” cried out Sipakna from down deep in the hole.

He wasnʼt digging his own grave; he wasnʼt digging his place of burial- umuqikil. Quite the contrary, he was digging out his own salvation-kʼolbʼal ribʼ. Finally, Sipakna called out to them from down below where he was safely tucked away in his hole carved out to one side.

body:
This was when he called up to the Four Hundred Boys: “Come on down and take away the dirt I have dug-up down here; itʼs all dug-out. Truly, I have dug down deep; can you not hear me calling? Your calls sound like echoes so that your words repeat themselves so that they sound as if they were one level; two levels away so that I can hear where you are calling from,” said Sipakna who was calling out from inside his hole deep down below. This then was when the Four Hundred Boys dragged their Big Tree-Ki- Nimaʼ Cheʼ over to the hole and then listened for Sipakna. “Heʼs not there! He says nothing!”

“Ma kʼo! Ma Chʼawik!” “Letʼs listen when he calls out; letʼs listen for him to die!” They said to one another in a silent sort of secret way so not a word could be heard. “Quiet! Donʼt say a thing! Letʼs wait until we hear him scream; letʼs listen for his cry when he comes to die deep down below…” they said to one another in a whisper; this then was when they covered their faces before throwing their Big Tree down their deep, deep hole... They waited for him to cry-out but all remained silent and still; they listened when they threw the Big Tree-Nimaʼ Cheʼ down to kill the Boy; but they heard nothing; nothing was said; nothing was heard; not a word...

An Alternative Translation

This then was when they called for Sipakna to do as they had planned for him to do. And what they planned for him to do was to keep digging down deeper in their hole because they said they could dig no further; they could reach no farther down digging their deep, deep hole.

So then they came to where Sipakna lay to say what they had planned to say which was their way to ask Sipakna to do what they asked him to do: “We want you to keep going; we want you to keep digging down; to just keep digging deep down so you go deeper and deeper down below; just dig down as far as you can possibly go. We canʼt dig down any deeper. We just canʼt dig any farther down below in our hole; but you can; you can dig down deeper if you keep digging down in this hole,” he was told by the Four Hundred Boys.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Call up to us when you have all the dirt dug out and we will help you up. Call out when you have gone as far as you can go; when you have dug as deep as you can dig down in our hole” they told this one big Boy; the One known as Crocodile Caiman Boy; the Spiny One; the Smoking Volcano Boy. “Very well!” is all Sipakna said as he descended down into the hole; the hole they had already dug deep down below. But before digging down any deeper in the hole that they had dug for him to be buried in Sipakna decided to dig out another hole; another hole to be saved from being buried deep down below by the Four Hundred Boys.

And so he dug that hole of his to the side so that he could continue their work digging a deep, deep hole; the hole down into which they would drop the center post that was the pillar of their hut; the post that was the pillar of their hut that they planned to raise on their own. The hole that Sipakna now dug was just a side hole; a side hole that he dug off to one side to save him from being buried by the Boys, the Four Hundred Boys-Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ who only wanted one thing for Sipakna. What those Boys wanted for Sipakna was death; nothing less, nothing more just death was wanted for this One who was so much stronger than all the rest; so much better than the best of them all put together.

Sipakna knew the Boys wanted to kill him; he knew they wanted him dead. Sipakna knew they wanted to bury him down in their deep, deep hole where they had led him to kill him dead. “How far along are you? How much further do you have to go?” asked the Four Hundred Boys as they ʼthrew downʼ their words so they could be heard by Sipakna. “I am still digging fast, Iʼll call up when itʼs all dug out as deep as I can go then Iʼll call up from down here deep down in this hole,” Sipakna called up to the Boys who could see by all the dirt that he was digging that he was digging deep down below to dig out a deep, deep hole.

body:
But Sipakna was not digging a deep, deep hole in which he was to be killed by their pole; he was digging out a hole to the side where he could hide; he was digging a hole into which he could stay out of the way in order to make his escape; this was the safety hole dug to one side that he was digging out for his own salvation. So this then was when Sipakna called up to the Boys. He was safely dug into the side; dug-in to the side of the deep, deep hole when Caiman Boy called up to them from the side but this time he lied when he said:

“Come on down so you can gather up and take away the last of the earth from down here in the hole; it is all dug-up; itʼs all dug out; itʼs all ready to go. Truly, I have dug a deep, deep hole that goes deep down below. Canʼt you hear me calling out to you from deep down below? As for your calls, they only sound like echoes, as if you were ʼone or two levelsʼ away,” cried Sipakna when he called up to the Boys from deep down below.

Sipakna, he was just hidden away in his hole, he was now safe to the side; he was just safely out of the way well prepared for his escape. This was when he called up from down below where he waited in the cavern he dug out to the side of the deep, deep hole that descended deep, deep down below. Meanwhile, the Four Hundred Boys dragged their great-big-tree-kinimacheʼ over to where they set it into place above the hole where Sipakna was now waiting for their plan to fall into place; just waiting far down below was Sipakna who was now completely in the know that the Four Hundred Boys were about to lift their great-big tree to then throw it deep down below.

They, the Four-Hundred Boys, prepared themselves just right so they could send down their great-big-tree; ki-nimaʼ-cheʼ with all their strength and all of their might; they wanted to throw-down their Center Post all at once so that it shot straight down; down deep to the bottom of this deep, deep hole where it would be left standing as the Center Pole of their Hut..

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They listened but they heard nothing, not a word, silence was all that came up from down below; suddenly nothing could be heard from the Caiman Boy who had been digging-up the dirt by digging deep, deep down in the earth. “Be still. Be quiet, donʼt speak. Letʼs listen for him screams; letʼs listen for his cries when the Center Post hits him and he dies,” they said to one another in a hush, just whispering to each other in a silent sort secretive speech.

But Sipakna heard it all from where he lay silent and still completely out of the way of the Great Post that was the Pillar they were about to send his way to kill him on this most sacrificial sort of day. This then was when they covered their faces with their head-cloths before throwing their Great Big Post that was their Center Pole down to the bottom of their deep, deep hole… It was then that he called out, letting out a single cry when he died. Just one call is all they heard when he let out a cry when the Four Hundred Boys let him die down below; when they let the Great Tree go; that Great Big Tree they sent flying down as fast and far as it could go; down to the bottom of the hole; the hole Sipakna had dug so deep down below.

“Okʼa! It Entered! It Entered! Okʼa! Perfecto! Eso! We did it! Didnʼt we do well? Is he not dead? Mixkamik!” they said.

“What was he up to entering here among us? What was he trying to do; by doing all that he did by coming here to show us he was stronger and better than the best of all the rest of us; us the Four Hundred Boys-Omuch Kʼajolabʼ?” “Who sent him here, anyway?”

body:
“It was just a sign; a sign, a sign of him and his doing; it was just a sign; this doing all that he did here to get in-between of us!” “What he was doing was just no good? So be it!” they said then there, there above the hole where their Center Post of perfectly worked wood now stood as a perfectly centered Pillar that now rose-up directly overhead. “To begin with it, it didnʼt start out well; it all began when he came here to make his way in between us; us, the Four Hundred Boys!” they said, contented now with what they had done to him, Sipakna-Caiman Boy-the Spiny One-the Smoking One: Cipacatli. “Letʼs make our strong three day drink of fermented maguey; our three-day fermentation of the bitter juice of maguey-ki; our three day sweet-ki drink; our Three Day Maguey-Oxij Ki as they say; the Three Day Fermentation of Maguey as it is called; so we can celebrate and make a toast on the Third Day-Oxibʼ Qʼij.” “When those three days pass, we will toast; we will drink to the completion of ʼOur Hut-Qakabʼal. This is what we will do, we who are ʼWeʼ we who are ʼUsʼ the Four Hundred Boys; la Oj Omuchʼ chi Kʼajolabʼ.” “So, then, tomorrow we shall look; and the day after tomorrow we shall look too; we will look to see if the ants donʼt just come up and out of the Earth to show us the truth of his death. When we know he is rotten; when we see that he is dead at the bottom of the hole all decomposed under the great tree sent down deep in the ground. When we see signs of his death and decomposition then our hearts will be consoled and our souls contented.” “Then we shall drink our sweet-ki-bitter fermentation; then we will drink our poison-ki-medicine; our three day sweet-ki drink will be ours with which to make a toast; maybe even boast about what we did when we raised our Center Post up overhead; the Pillar of our Hut,” they said as they planned to celebrate the sacrifice of Sipakna with the completion of their Hut.

Every single word was heard by Sipakna from where he was safely hidden away in his cavern; the cave he made as the path to his salvation.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Sipakna listened to all that was said by the Four Hundred Boys. After all, their talk resounded down and around until it reached deep below where he waited for the days to pass so the Ants could do their duty; so they could perform their role.

This then was when Sipakna heard the Four Hundred Boys talking amongst themselves, which was when he heard what they had to say which he heard quite well; so that when he heard them say: “the Next Day” he knew it was time to put his plan into action.

It was their words that he heard on the Second Day is when he sent the Ants flooding-up from below as a sign that signaled it was time to start the show so that everyone would know Sipakna was now dead after being buried deep down below.

Sipakna had been sacrificed for the good of the whole by the Four Hundred Boys- Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ who buried him alive beneath their Great Pillar that had been sent down to kill him deep down deep in their hole that they had begun digging before Sipakna came along to play a most significant role as ʼsacrificial offeringʼ that would end one period to initiate another.

This aspect of the Popol Wuj most certainly has to do with ritual initiation of the Young Men known as the Four Hundred Boys who may have once gone out beside a river to dig a deep hole where a great caiman or crocodile was lured in to be sacrificed to then be eaten as the ʼsacred sustenanceʼ of this ritual of initiation that was performed as the Rite of Passage that took place in the Initiation Hut of the Young Men.

This then is the telling of a myth that we no longer know its original ritual in the Mesoamerican World where ʼMyth and Ritualʼ twinned one another to bring transformation to the life of the Pueblo; the lives of the People; and, the Natural World at the Mid-Point of the Year.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Ants swarmed over the Pillar; they swarmed over the Post; like a whirlwind this moving mass of Ancient Ancestors swarmed over the Great Center Post that the Four-Hundred Boys had sent to the bottom of their hole just a few days ago. Some of the Ants carried off his hair, some of them carried off his nails; his hair, his nails were carried up and out of there; up from below they did go to pour out from where Sipakna now decomposed deep down below.

This was when the Four-Hundred Boys watched the Ants as they made their parade carrying their banners up from down below in a great show of death so that all could know that Sipakna was buried dead deep down below.

Those who were watching now felt a great sense of relief knowing their idea had worked and this giant boy was stopped from growing any more by being safely buried deep, deep down below in the hole he had dug for himself:

“Isnʼt that trickster-kʼaxtoqʼ-finished off now? Just look at the Ants. Havenʼt they already gathered together? Havenʼt they already swarmed all about? The Ants carry his hair; they bear his nails. Didnʼt we do right by him who wished to outdo us all by doing that which we could do our self?” And so it was that they congratulated one another on their defeat of Sipakna.

But Sipakna was still very much alive. He cut the hair from his head, he chewed his nails with his teeth, and then he gave the hair and the nails to the Ants so they could do what they did best by carrying them off to make their own next. Sipakna did this so that his death would be known to Four Hundred Boy who waited above for his death to flower up from deep down below. Sipakna did what he did with the Ants so that his dying would be felt in the hearts of the Four Hundred Boys, the Four Hundred Sons: Omuch Kʼajolabʼ. And when all of them were certain Sipakna was dead they began toasting with their ʼsweet drink-kikiʼ of the three days; their ritual drink that was known as the Third Day: Roxij. Roxij: the Third Day Drink that was the fermented drink now ready to be drunk. This was when the Four-Hundred Boys prepared to drink their ritual drink to then drink and drink until one and all were completely ritually drunk.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This was when the Four Hundred Sons-Omuch Kʼajolabʼ drank and drank until they were drunker than drunk; they were so drunk that they didnʼt feel a thing when their perfect plan was flipped on its head; their well thought out plot to kill Sipakna suddenly wasnʼt going their way.

There was nothing more to think, plan, or say when their hut came crashing down on their head and this reversal of destiny left them all deader than dead.

Not even ʼone or twoʼ of the Four-Hundred Boys survived, they were all killed by the ʼNawal Geniusʼ of Sipakna; it was just the ʼNawal Knowingʼ of the First Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix that did it.

This then ends the telling of the death of the Four Hundred Boys who are said to have entered the Sky as the Stars-Chʼumilal known as Motz-Pleiades but that could just be a play on words: xa saqbʼal tzij-a play on words; xa tzaqbʼal tzij- words thrown into play; xa tzʼaqbʼal tzij-formed words better known as a lie!

ʼPlay-on Words-Saqbʼal Tzijʼ

This ʼplay-on words-saqbʼal tzijʼ brings out a metaphorical kind of beauty that has never been fully acknowledged as a ʼserious playʼ on metaphor through the metaphorical imagination of myth and those metaphorical plays of the imagination of matter. In this case the Four Hundred Boys are said to have become the Heart of the Sky; the Heart of the Sky being inhabited by the Pleiades at the time of this New Year construction of an Initiation Hut for the Young Men at the Mid-Point of the Year who were called to ʼlistenʼ to the voice of Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Heart of the Sky; Ukʼuʼx Ulew-Heart of the Earth.

body:
Perhaps the Heart of the Earth was sought out deep down below the Face of the Earth where the Center Post was to be sown to ʼrise-upʼ as the Sacred Pillar of the Palo Volador where the Monkey Boys-Kʼoy was sent swinging round and round like the Sun and Moon with their separate Sacred Counts of Nights and Days that spin round and round like the nights and days of the Years; all of whom are known as the Sacred Year Count of Four Hundred Days of Twenty Months of Twenty Day Months to create a Four-Hundred Day Year known as a Tun or Stone that is often confused or conflated to the Abʼ or Year of Three Hundred and Sixty-Five Days of Eighteen Twenty Day Months plus the Wayebʼ Period of Five Dangerous Days. So these Four Hundred Boys of the South-Centzon Huitznahua of the Nahua People of Nahuatl Language seem to be the very same Four Hundred Boys who make-up the Sacred Count of the Days of a Four-Hundred Day Ritual Year; as well as the Sacred Count of the Four Corners; Four Sides of the Milpa. They could easily be Warriors formed in Twenty Groups of Twenty Warriors to create a Four-Hundred Count of Twenty Columns of Twenty Warriors per Column to create a Company of Four Hundred Warriors.

Changing and Transforming World of the Sky-Earth Life and Death; Clouds and Rain; Dust and Dirt; Sprouts of Maize A great deal is going on here that is left to us to bring back life through our ʼremembrance and recollectionʼ of the Mesoamerican World and its Cosmo-Magical Thinking and Thought of Myth and Ritual at this passage of the Agricultural and Ritual Year when the Milpa is sown and the House thatched so that ritual can be performed in order to call down the rain by calling up the clouds to form Thunder and Lightning Storms where the Rain Warriors enter the Sky to throw their thunder-bolts and lightning-bolts down on the Face of the Earth to ʼbreak it openʼ so that life can come flooding out from below like the Ants that rise up and out of Death to bring Sipakna back to Life in mythic metaphorical ways.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These are the energies of Life and Death that are being played with here through myth and ritual. This is when the dew falls from dusk to dawn to fill the ʼtwisted cupsʼ created by the leaves of maize as they twist-up an out of the dry dirt of the Dry Season Earth. This is when the Hero Twins must change and transform the World of the Sky-Earth so that hard-kernels of maize seed can be ʼcracked-openʼ by the thunder and lightning that announces the return of the rain clouds and their life-giving thunder, lightning, and rain. This ritual time of the year when the Popol Wuj was performed was when the Maize was already sown in the Milpa and the construction completed by the thatch-grass being cut and bundled before being bound and ʼtwistedʼ up on the top of the old houses that needed new thatch or new huts that required thatch grass to be bound and bundled to the canes that formed the roof and its scaffold. So letʼs do our best to bring this magical transforming genius into focus; letʼs bring forth an understanding of this nawal genius so that the mythic imagination of the Ancient Word can come to reality.

This ʼserio ludareʼ of changing and transforming nawal words is an aspect of the ʼserious playʼ of the Popol Wuj that calls upon us to ʼenter the wordʼ to ʼenter the metaphorʼ to ʼenter the night skyʼ to ʼenter the transcendence of mythʼ to ʼenter the beautyʼ of divinity and humanity becoming one through our engaged imagination of myth that comes to life through the engaged imagination of our soul.

Once again the Ancestral Soul cries out to us to slow down in order to open up the ʼMundus Imaginalisʼ of Popol Wuj. So let us do this by bring out these mythic metaphors through the ʼnawal geniusʼ of our changing and transforming mind and body; body and soul; soul and spirit; spirit and mind; mind and body…by looking up into the Heart of the Night Sky.

Southern Quadrant of the Night Sky The Four Hundred Boys Enter the Night Sky as those who are the Four Hundred Star Boys of South Centzon Huitz Nahua: Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ

body:
Once again our Ancient Ancestral Account presents a lethal reversal of destiny that comes to life here in the case of the Four Hundred Boys, Four Hundred Sons. Their desire to take control of strength and power ends up meaning that they are undermined from Sipakna who is buried deep down below while being crushed by their own Pillar and Crossbeam from high up above. This shamanic reflection of the above and below is mirrored in their Initiation Hut being brought down on their head; the head of the Boys; the skull of the Sons by the trickster son- Sipakna of a trickster father-Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

This reversal of destiny ʼup-endsʼ the fortune and fate of the Boys; the fortune and fate that ʼends-upʼ becoming the destiny of the Four Hundred Sonsʼ that is a manifestation of destiny being flipped upside-down from deep down below. This flipping of fate that is a reversal of destiny tells us we are walking in a world that Trickster makes by creating the problems that he alone can solve. This world of the Trickster and the lives of those who live in it is governed by destiny and controlled by fate that is ordered by ritual sacrifice.

This is the myth that is told here in innovative and imaginative ways that tells of some sort of ʼritual sacrificeʼ that once occurred in which sacrificial victims met their death beneath a great pillar or post that was brought down upon them from up above to leave the Sacred Post of the Initiation Hut holding up the Sky above from the Earth below. And so it was that the Four Hundred Boys came to their inevitable end. This then is the revelation and recitation of the defeat and destruction; death and disappearance of the Four Hundred Boys, Four Hundred Sons: Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Which as we will come to see will have cosmic repercussions so that they end up in the Southern Quadrant of the Night Sky opposite of Wuqubʼ Kaqix and Chimalmat in the North. This placing of the Four Hundred Boys in the South is where their Pillar and Crossbeams form the False Cross and Southern Cross where the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds cover the Southern Horizon of the South Sea. This is where the bright stars of Alpha and Beta Centaur may well have been seen as the Hero Twins Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej, in the Sacred World of the Sky- Earth where life and death existed in a constant play of change and transformation. The Southern Quadrant of the Kʼicheʼ Cosmos is where the Pacific Coast of Guatemala was once covered in Caiman and Sea-Turtles where early humans lived off of the estuaries teaming with shellfish to create purple murex dye for sacred purple cloth. This is where enormous quantities and all kinds of different species of shrimp and crab, langoustine and mollusks, minnows and fish; sharks and rays; animals and birds of every type and kind fed and clothed the early hunting and gathering people and pueblos of tuber planting and gourd growing Matriarchal societies and cultures of the Pacific Littoral.

These are where the Boys, the Sons of the Great Mother gave sacrifice in rites of initiation from which they emerged as warriors of their Mothers and Grandmothers; keepers and caretakers of their hunting and gathering grounds on the Costa Sur, Boca Costa, and way up into the Highlands. This is where Great Ceiba Tree stood as Pillars; as Posts of the Sky-Earth.

These Giant Ceiba Trees of the Pacific Coast were where Early Mesoamericans lived in homes made among the massive buttress of the Ceiba Trees under palm frond roofs in rooms formed and shaped beneath these Pillars of the Heavens.

This is the remembrance of those mythic times and epic ancestral spaces. It would be from these pillars that great dug-out canoes would be hued and burned into shape to then be dragged out into the Pacific upon which the Maya would paddle their way North and South; East and West in great paddling expeditions we no longer remember.

body:
Saqbʼal tzij; Tzʼaqbʼal tzij; Tzaqbʼal tzij

We know the Four-Hundred Boys enter the Night Sky as the Great Many Stars of the Southern Sphere of the Celestial Firmament when Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej enter the Sky as the Sun and the Moon so something is going on here that requires initiation by ʼentering the wordʼ with the Chuch-Qajaw Ojer Tzij; Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word but until the Kʼicheʼ Maya are able to re-form and re-shape to re-create these folks we must attempt to understand what is happening through our own education in the field.

A great, great word play; a playful as words can be in a ʼword playʼ known as saqbʼal tzij heard also as tzʼaqbʼal tzij formed words that are lies; and, tzaqbʼal tzij thrown down words such as those thrown down by the Four Hundred Boys who threw them down the hole to Sipakna.

This is a play on play on a play on words-saqbʼal tzij; words thrown down like the rubber ball was thrown down into play; and, bone dice were thrown down in games of destiny that showed onesʼ connection with the Heart of the Sky; Trickster and Gamer who played with Destiny at the Crossroads of Life.

This Mocker of Men is said to live in the bounce of the ball; in the fall of the dice; in the drop of a hat; in the path one chose at the Crossroads. It is we who are his slaves; just as it is he who begrudgingly gives the gift of fortune that he then quickly takes away. This Lord of Crossroads, this Lord of the Rubberball and White Dice was there with every play of Fortune and Fame thrown down to make his presence known through the luck and the loss of each and every toss of each and every game of the Noble Lords and their playing and their playing and their playing of games. These two noble games are played by the Fathers who are the Lords of the Twins. Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who play ball and dice all day; the ʼwhite-saq bone-baq dice gameʼ known as ʼsaqbʼalʼ that is one of the many games the Maya once played.

body:
When they played games that were play by throwing dice down into play; when they threw the rubberball down in the rubberball game where the ball was ʼthrown down into playʼ as you will most certainly see. The metaphor always that of being ʼthrow down into playʼ whatever it is that is being throw-down into play; the decapitated heads of sacrificial victims heads being thrown down the temple stairs to roll out on to the plaza is very, very much included. This was when Noble Lords played all-day long when playing dice and playing ball was what Noble Lords did when they lived out lives marked by and identified with serious play; in lives marked by tempting fate in order to play with destiny; the destiny of oneʼs life that was played out each and every day on the Sacrifice Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice or Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Play: Pusbʼal Chaaj the name of the Ballcourt of Xibʼalbʼa; Pusbʼal Chaaj a name that is a metaphor that is word play that defies translation in playful sorts of playful kinds of ways; ways we will come to play with as we enter the Ballcourt where the ball will be ʼthrown down into playʼ as it is said; as they will come to say.

So yes saying the Four Hundred Boys is a Tzʼaqbʼal Tzij that is a lie that is a Saqbʼal Tzij that is a Play on Words that is a Tzaqbʼal Tzij a throwing down of words which is to say words are thrown down into play in order to make a challenge to play ball with and through word-play is the sort of serious play our Maya Scribes are engaged with here as they challenge us to play with them in serious play-serio ludare with the Ancient Word in this Ancient Ancestral Account.

This word play that is going on here is indeed is a very serious sort of play that is going on here with mythic words and mythic metaphors are grounded in word play that is founded in our playing with the ideas Mesoamerican Stargazers who took their play with both words and stars seriously; and what a play on words and with words this is! Someday we will understand this play or we already but have not agreed on what we understand for now it is enough to see the Mid-most Place in the Sky of Pleiades as the Heart of Sky.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
But here is the thing: the Heart of the Sky is embodied by the Four Hundred Boys who are known as ʼWe who are the Vassals of Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan; We who are the Boys of Heart of the Skyʼ so that the Four Hundred Boys who are the ʼHandful of Seeds or Motzʼ transform into the story just told of the Southern Cross being raised up in the Southern Quadrant where the Twins take on the form of the Two of the Brightest Stars in the Sky: Alpha and Beta Centaur who are joined by their companions the Four Hundred Boys of Centaur and then Great Milky white atole of the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds of the Southern Quadrant with its False Cross and Southern Cross that Sipakna helps the Boys raise up to build their Initiation Hut known as Kabʼal which might well have been a Divine House of Initiation as in Kabʼawil….but this is hard to know for certain.

What is known for certain is kabʼal means ʼcompletionʼ in the sense of some ʼthingʼ or some ʼsoulʼ coming to fruition: kabʼal meaning ʼits completeʼ; ʼits correctʼ; ʼitʼs all hereʼ; which is the place where initiation took place protected from the sun and rain. What different life human beings much have lived when they found their vocation through rites of passage that showed them what was truly theirs in life to bring to fruition in order to feel ʼkabʼalʼ with oneʼs destiny by feeling ʼcompleteʼ with oneʼs ancestry. Walking the road of initiation placed Young Men and Young Women in the footsteps of oneʼs Ancestors in order to feel assured of oneʼs fortune and fate in life. Let us take up the road to feel complete: Kabʼal.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the story that is being told through mythic metaphor in which the ʼhandful of seeds plantedʼ thrown down within the ʼheart of the Sky-heart of the Earthʼ which is say the seeds planted in Pleiades straight-up overhead in the Heart of the Sky at Mid-night known a ʼtikil aqʼabʼ or ʼplanted in the darkʼ as the seeds that are ʼthrown-down in the soil dug down in the Heart of the Earth to be sown at Mid-day known as ʼtikil qʼijʼ or ʼplanted in the sunʼ to form and shape a metaphor of planting above in the Middle of the Nightʼs dark to mirror the sowing below in the Middle of the Day in the light of the Sun.

This image of sowing and seeding; shooting and sprouting; growing and transforming to come to flowering and fruiting completion is the story being told here. This is the story that once fed and sustained the Soul of the Maize People who lived by its mythic metaphors in seamless soul sustaining ways known as Nawal Ways of being and becoming one with the Sacred Sustenance that formed and shaped Oneʼs body and soul. This is where we are moving as we make our way down the road on this mythic journey of el Pueblo de Maize.

This is the Sacred Narrative of the Moonʼs embrace and Sunʼs warm that nourish and nurture the ʼsprouting seeds of maizeʼ who as the Four Hundred Boys die to be planted in the Sky where they will come back to Life on the Face of the Earth where they will enter the ʼstruggleʼ as ʼhard, hardʼ seeds sown in the womb of the Earth to eventually flower out in the bright, light of the Sun at the Heart of the Sky in the Middle of the Day to be pulled up into Middle of the Night by the Moonlight whoʼs power and strength remind us: ʼas above so belowʼ the Sun and Moon of Night and Day tell us so.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the Nawal Powers of the Hero Twins who as the Sun and Moon of the Age of the Maize People will guide and protect their People who as a Pueblo will grow and transform to become the Kʼicheʼ Maya who prosper today like never before. This is their Ancient Ancestral Account that tells their story of changing and transforming ways of life, death, and rebirth of the Maize People and their Sacred Sustenance sown as seed in la Milpa. And that story of the Maize People is told best by beginning back before maize was planted in those small settlements of sedentary Matriarchal Rule of Early Horticultural People when they were Hunters and Gatherers who wandered across the Earth searching beside the ʼwater-waysʼ for fish and crab.

This is the Primordial World of those who hunt and those who gather beside and within the ʼrivers and streamsʼ we have entered here by entering the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj that tells of Sipakna and Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who find one another walking beside the river for sustenance; searching beside the water for that which is theirs; theirs feed their hunger; theirs to eat as their flesh and bone; that which is found in the rivers and streams that flow down the Highland Mountains to then cross the Great Coastal Plain. These river-ways and streams were once crawling the crabs and filled with fish; they waterways teeming with turtles where iguanas and lizards lived long lives alongside caiman and crocodile that sought and caught fish and crab that were their primordial nourishment. This is the story told here where hunters hunt hunters in their quest to fulfill their destiny and fate.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Sipakna First Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix Ancient Ancestral One; Caiman Boy; Crocodile Son Spiny One; Smoking One KABʼ Second out of Three Let us tell next of the defeat of Sipakna by Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. Here then begins the story of the death and disappearance of Sipakna by the Twins; the story that tells of the First Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix: the Ancient Ancestral One; Caiman Boy; Crocodile Son; the Spiny One; the Smoking One; the One known and named after his ʼlineageʼ and its ʼhouseʼ known as Sipak Na Ceiba House; First House of the Ancient Ones; the Ancestral Ones...

This is the story that tells of the defeat of Sipakna; the story that tells of when he was brought down by the Two Boys; when he was defeated by the Two Sons known and named Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej; for truly, it was a blow to their hearts that the Four Hundred Boys-Omuchʼ Kʼajolabʼ were killed by Sipakna.

For truly the story must be told of those Boys who were named the Sons of Heart of the Sky known as Omuch Kʼajolabʼ who were finished off-one and all-by Sipakna when he brought their ʼHouse-Kabʼal-Hutʼ down on them.

So let us tell then the story of Sipakna and how his power and might was brought to an end by the clever thinking; by the cunning thought of the nawal genius borne within the Hero Twins; JunAjPu, IxBʼalamKej who were Nawal Winaq in every way.

This is it then; here it is; look and listen close to see and hear all that will sprout forth from the past.

Just Fish, Just Crab-Xa Kar, Xa Tap Hunterʼs Hunger; Appetiteʼs Trap Predator and Prey; When We Wish for More

Just fish, just crab-xa kar, xa tap-were what Sipakna wished for when he fished for fish; in his quest for crab when he went wandering alongside the river where he made his way in search of prey; prey he sought throughout the night and during the dawn and dusk of the comings and goings of the day.

Just these alone were his sustenance; just fish, just crab-xa kar, xa tap; just these alone were his quest and quarry; just these alone were what he ate; these alone were his fortune; his fate; day after day. At Night he raised Mountains; Mountains that climbed into the Sky.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This then was when a ʼlook-a-like replicaʼ of a great big crab was formed and shaped by Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej, who then brought that ʼlook-a-likeʼ crab to life by animating it with ancestral soul; by ensouling it with animate life.

They used the long shiny red flowers of the forest bromeliads known as turkey foot-raqan ekʼ to shape its claws. The Boys gathered the big red flowery ones, ʼpa jaqʼ the ʼopen onesʼ that they found flowering in the forest; the ʼbudding onesʼ that bloomed and blossomed ruby red in the trees.

These they fashioned ʼjust soʼ to form the claws of the crab, while they put into place the open shoots of bamboo grass to imitate the forearms of their decorated decoy; the replica ʼlook-a-likeʼ so that by the time they finished forming and shaping their crab it would pulse as it pulsated with life.

They used a round stone-shaped gourd to replicate the clattering body armor of the crabʼs body and shell; which, once their work was complete, even they were surprised by the lively feel of their formation; how animate their creation felt; how real their creation looked; how alive it seemed to be as one could see it move all about. So this then was when they went to place their imitation crab there below the Cliff-Pek, below the Great Mountain-Nimaʼ Juyubʼ there in the West, known as Meʼawan: Bent-down Maize Plant; Doubled-over Milpa.

Meʼawan: Meʼoj Awan Doubled-Over Cane of Maize Bent-Down Maize; Broken-over Cane of Maize Falling Down Place of the Sun: Kajbʼal Qʼij Primordial Origin Place of Maize Western Horizon: Sipakna Meʼawan is the name given to this place known as Meʼoj Awan; Doubled-Over Cane of Maize; Bent-Down Maize; Broken-over Cane of Maize; just like the arm of Junajpu when it was hung over the embers burning in the hearth of Chimalmat; embers meant to dry-out the arm of the Maize Deity: Jun AjPu.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Meʼoj Awan is the last stage of the Lifecycle of Maize before the harvest of Maize in la Milpa. Meʼawan or Meʼoj Awan is the name of Bent-Down Maize whose cane is bent over in order that the head-aj of maize can dry downward so the birds canʼt peck at its grain and the rain canʼt feed the growth of deadly black spores of mold that ruin the mazorca of maize-jal and cause death amongst the Maize People and their domesticated animals they feed with rotten maize seed unhealthy for human consumption.

Meʼawan is known as the Place of Origin of Maize thus in is seen as the Primordial Mountain of Maize in the West at the Falling Down Place of the Sun-Kajbʼal Qʼij where maize is said to originate above and below the great ravines and canyons that are shaped by the streams and rivers that course their way down the down this mountain that appears out of the clouds of the Western most reaches of the Kʼicheʼ and Huehuetenango a place known as the Ixcan or IxKan the Origin Place-Ix of Maize-Kan: IxKan.

Meʼawan is the Mountain of Maize where Teocinte-Ajii is still found growing up and down the valley floor cut, carved, and crafted by the water winding its way down the ʼFlower- Suchitlʼ river known as the Suchiate that forms the border between Chiapas and Huehuetenango to shape the boundary line of Mexico and Guatemala. This is the Origin Place of the Maize People that the Popol Wuj is invoking through this story of Sipaknaʼs primordial hunger and ancestral appetite for that which is his in life: just fish, just crab; xa kar, xa tap.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: Meʼawan was the name of the mountain where Sipakna would be defeated by the Two Boys, Two Sons; e Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ, JunAjPu, Ixbʼalamkej were their names. This then was when the Boys, the Sons, met up with Sipakna by the waterʼs edge. There, beside the riverside they came upon Sipakna searching for his sustenance. “Where are you going, you my Son, you my Boy-At Kʼajol?” the Two asked. “I am not going anywhere; Iʼm just out searching for what is mine; my food; my sustenance, you, my Boys-Ix Kʼajolabʼ; you, my Sons-Ix Kʼajolabʼ,” said Sipakna. “So, what then is yours-awech; what then is your sustenance-awechaʼ?” asked the Two who spoke as One. “Just fish, just crab-xa kar, xa tap are what are mine; just fish; just crab are my sustenance that satisfy my hunger; that appease my appetite. But there are none to be found here so I havenʼt had a thing to eat since the day before yesterday; kabʼijir. Not one bite, nothing at all for two days now. There are no fish to be caught here; just as there are no crab to be had here either; so I havenʼt had a thing to eat; nothing to eat at all,” said Sipakna. “The day before last is when I left off eating and I donʼt know how much longer I can endure my hunger,” said Sipakna to Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. “Well there is one real Big Crab down there in the canyon below. Truly, it is One Big Crab-Jun Nimaʼ Tap. If itʼs your lucky day, if itʼs your ʼsuerteʼ you might just catch him.” “He just snapped at us when we tried to catch him. If he hasnʼt moved on you can grab him; surely someone as strong as you can nab one as big as him,” said Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. “Take pity on me Boys; come along with me to show me the way. Show me nothing more than where he stays, Ix Kʼajolabʼ, you oh Sons. Surely you know where he lays and his crab-like ways so what would it be but a chance for you to join up with me to walk down the road to find him. What do you say; will you not show me the way?” pleaded Sipakna. “No thanks, we donʼt want to; you can arrive there by yourself. Itʼs not such a lost place; itʼs not so very hidden away. Just follow along the river; just follow the foot of the water and you will find him there where he lies alongside the river.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
You will come upon this One Big Crab right there below the Great Mountain. Just listen to him clattering about there at the bottom of the ravine. Just get yourself going; youʼll arrive there just fine!” said Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. “Please, I beg of you, just help me this once! What if I donʼt find him, my Boys? Surely you can accompany me to show me where to go to show me the way to where he lays. Besides, there are plenty of birds alongside the road over there. Plenty of birds can be found up in the trees for you to test your skills with you blowguns, and I know just where you can find them,” said Sipakna.

His genuine meekness and humble pleading convinced the Boys to lead the way. And so they took off down the road walking together talking as they liked to do and was their way. Sipakna didnʼt need to say another word to persuade the Boys to come along with him once he promised to point out birds along the road. Each one shouldered a blowgun; ever at the ready; ready to blow-down the birds they spotted up in the trees. This is when they said what they had say and what they had been waiting to say was this: “You had better catch that Great Big Crab because that is the only reason we are going back there with you. We arenʼt going to try again to catch him because he bites; he just strikes out to then snap at you in a most vicious sort of violent way,” said the Boys before they continued talking as they accompanied Sipakna walking along the way: One to the left; One to the right; Sipakna in the middle with a Twin on either side. They went on and on talking about this most precious prey that lay in wait for Caiman Boy who was happy to be on his way to appease his appetite and ease his hunger for sustenance.

They never stopped talking about how enormous this One Big Crab really was; they talked as they walked to whet the appetite of Sipakna as they honed their story just to sharpen his hunger for this One Big Crab that he was afraid had already gone away.

They talked and talked about the Tap-Crab and their many attempts to catch him; all of their advice was given to provide Sipakna with the kind of counsel that would lead to their victory and his defeat.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“First we entered face-down-jupulik but that just frightened him away. Then we entered face-up-pakʼalik and almost got him, so perhaps you might begin by entering face-up-pakʼalik,” encouraging Sipakna whose hunger had got the best of him.

“Very well!” said Sipakna.

And so it was that the Boys, the Sons accompanied Sipakna. They walked until they arrived down below at the foot of the canyon.

And there, lying out to one side-tzalam was the Crab-ri Top with its shiny red back glowing like a red hot ember down there at the bottom of the canyon- chuxeʼ siwan.

Tzalam: To Lie on Oneʼs Side Tzalam: To Sacrifice One on the Side Tzalam: To Lay Down Flat Tzalam means to lay down on oneʼs side which is the way the Boys came upon Wuqubʼ Kaqix with his broken jaw and loose teeth. Tzalam or ʼto lay to oneʼs sideʼ is also the way ʼvictims of sacrificeʼ were placed on the Sacrificial Stone that was laid out on the Altar of Sacrifice so that the ʼWhite Flint-Knife of Sacrificeʼ could open the space between the ribs to then reach in to grasp the palpitating heart with Jaguar Paws-Jaguar Claws; Eagle Talons-Eagle Claws grip to then rip the pounding heart from the human chest.

Imagine the predatorial strength a sacrificial act like that takes. Yet, this is the image suggested here through the evocative mythopoetic genius that says so much with so few words that leaves one wondering if that which is said to be ʼtzalamʼ is that which shall be sacrificed? The answer is yes for anybody who ends up on their side in the Popol Wuj is going to be sacrificed on their side: tzalam. This beguiling, bewitching Crab is formed in the Imaginal Realm to be shaped in the Mythic Imagination to then be molded by this Poetic Incantation of this enchanting sort of glossy invocation of this mythic prey that takes on the attributes of a predator because of what the Hero Twins have to say about the way it tries to bite with its dangerous deadly claws that shimmers and shine so that it appears to be alive and pulsating with life.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
You can see it down below all aglow; crimson red, its living warmth pumping in the sun; its appetizing appeal; the beguiling grip of its grasp; the bewitching way it holds oneʼs attention fast; those who gazed upon its enchanting charm, its captivating pull could not free themselves from the strength of its clasp; the crush of its clutch.

The animate ensoulment of the ancestral soul has come alive through the mythopoetic magic of the Hero Twins bringing this mythic crab to life. This capacity to bring formed and shaped objects to life is the mythical essence of the myth-making genius of Popol Wuj. The Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account brings the Imaginal Realm of this Maya Myth alive through the story-telling play of that Ancient Word that makes a mythopoetic play on bringing this One Big Crab alive through the telling of this ʼMyth of the Sipakna and Hero Twinsʼ itself. This is a mythic play on animating the image within the myth-the Crab-that is in its self the animation and enlivenment of the mythic images. This is the raison dʼêtre of myth from beginning to end so the reader or viewer can participate in this transcendent experience of having ʼformed and shapedʼ beings being brought to life. Now Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are performing this magic in order to bring to life the mythic being and becoming of the ancestral soul. Now this One Big Crab as an animate being has been brought to life through the complete engagement of the divine soul of the Kabʼawil Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej and its divine ability to bring this ancestral image to life. If you have ever tried to catch crabs in a river you will know they attempt to stay motionless like the rocks and stones on the river floor or stream bed until they explode into life.

This now pulsating red creature skittered about below the cliff-kaq wakʼowoj ula rij grabbing hold of Sipaknaʼs full attention to then hold it tight while focusing his desire in the most beguiling sort of bewitching way.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Sipakna now found he was grasped by the captivating grip of this Nawal Crab whoʼs grasp would not leave him be. Now completely enchanted Sipakna knew that only by devouring his favorite food would he be set free from its hold on his predatorial soul; he wished only to swallow whole this most delectable looking form of his favorite sustenance in order to bring to conclusion this magical sort of supernatural play betwixt predator and prey; between the nawal world of the Hero Twins and their divine ability to form forms and their capacity of Kabʼawil to shape shapes in the most enchanting sorts of enthralling ways.

“Utz bʼa la! Very well!” cried Sipakna, who was now overjoyed; thankful for having finally found what heʼd been looking for, for so many days, he just wanted that crab in his mouth to swallow it whole, right then and there.

For truly Sipakna was finished off by his hunger by now; just humbled, just humiliated by his insatiable appetite for fish and crab; crab and fish; kar, tap; tap, kar.

He wanted to enter face-down-jupunik at first, so he tried just that. But the crab rose face-up-pakʼal chik, so Sipakna came right back out determined to go right back in now that he had a sense of this enchanted place and its captivating space. “You couldnʼt get him?” they asked. “Not yet. He just rose-up coming at me face-up-xa pakʼalik kaqanik. I just missed him, but I almost gotʼim; I nearly caught him. Perhaps it would be better if I entered face-up-kipakʼeʼik kinok ubʼik” he said, reconsidering his position and perhaps remembering what they told him in the first place. So then he entered face-up, little by little he made his way to where the Crab lay perfectly still; now it was just the two of them there at the bottom of the great canyon... Sipakna was by now completely inside the mountain. Only his kneecaps were showing, as if he had disappeared.

Just then the mountain came undone: it collapsed on his chest. No longer was he able to move. Right then and there, Sipakna turned into stone. The mountain swallowed him whole.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This then was the defeat of Sipakna by the Boys, by the Sons, ri Kʼajolabʼ: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. Sipakna was the one known as Bʼanol Juyubʼ which is what made him the Maker of Mountains according to the ancestral meaning of the Ancient Word, Ancestral Account.

It was he, Sipakna, the Spiny One, the Smoking One who was known as Caiman Boy, Volcano Son; it was he that was the First Born Son-Nabʼeyal Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

It was he, who was turned to stone beneath the mountain of Meʼawan, and there he continues to lie beneath this Broke-back Mountain of Maize; Bent-back Mountain of Maize, Meʼawan-Doubled-over Cane of Maize-Meʼoj Awan-Broken Cane is its name; the place where Sipakna was lured to his defeat by his own hunger and desire to meet his death laid-out on his back.

Xa Nawal: Just Magical Transformation Changing-Transforming Ancestral Divinity It was just their ancestral powers of transformation-xa nawal; that were just their magical powers of transformation-xa nawal that brought forth their ingenious capacity to bring forth their imaginative powers of deception-xa nawal that led to the defeat of the First Born Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix. It was the twinning of conceit and deception; pride and arrogance that led to Sipakna being deceived by those who conceived a most innovative plan of deadly devious deception that was inspired by the One-Jun who was known as the Mocker of Men; He who we are his Slaves; He Who forms and shapes himself; the Night Wind; the Enemy on Both Sides; He who Sees both Far and Near; the Curved Obsidian Blade known as Hail, White-Frost; and Ice; He who is the Heart of the Sky One-Footed-One; Hurricane; the Lightning Bolt Thunderer-Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja is just one of the many, many names who is never named other than Ma Jun Kʼo Taj-He Who is Not There; the Invisible One; the Invincible One who knew how to lose first in order to end up winning at last. This is the work of Tezcatlipoca who gives himself up by walking beside Sipakna as the Enemy on Both Sides; the Crab as He Who Makes Himself; and on it goes as Trickster makes the World one word at a time.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It was their nawal powers of enchantment that gave them the victory over the Second One who manifest himself as the Big Man-Nimalaj Achi through Self- Magnification-Nimarisay ribʼ who was the Second One to be defeated; to be destroyed and disappeared by the Boys.

He who was the First Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix; he who made himself out to be greater than he was through his Self-Aggrandizement-Nimarisay ribʼ this was Sipakna who was transformed into a mountain of stone; he who was left to lie where he was led to die beneath the Mountain of Maize: Meʼawan.

Second One of Three MeʼAwan: IxKan To Become a Mountain of Maize The Second One to be defeated by tricksterʼs trap set by appetite and hunger to be lured by the Boys inside a mountain to be turned to stone because of his arrogant pride; his self- inflation; self-glorification-nimarisay ribʼ that brought about the end of his days through tricksterʼs capacity to bring about the reversal of destiny which was the inevitable way Sipakna would become the Mountain he became by following his appetite to where he could satisfy his hunger. This is the Mountain of Meʼawan where the Original Cane is Bent-down and Broken- over to provide the essence of the substance from which the flesh of the First Four Fathers will be formed and shaped.

Popol Wuj is one perfectly intricate story that builds on itself both forwards and backwards because it is not a lineal story that it appears to be. Instead it is circular in nature that goes from Age to Age transforming from Sun to Sun by going round and round; year after year; day after day; Moon after Moon; month after month; changing and transforming the destiny of those who are formed and shaped by its sacred narrative.

body:
Our sacred story has taken us over to the Western Border of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom in this place known as the IxKan the Origin-Ix place of Maize-Kan on the Suchiate-Flower River on the border of Huehuetenango-Ancient, Ancient Pueblo of the Mam People; Mam Pueblo the Ancestral People-Mam who are the Ancestors-Mam. We are on the border of Mexico and Guatemala where the mountains are steep and the rivers run through deep canyon gorges. This is the place where the Boys lead Sipakna down beside a river gorge where a Great Big Red Crab is brought to life by the Nawal Powers of Transformation of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. It is ʼXa Nawalʼ it is ʼJust Transformative Powersʼ that make it so.

ONE MORE ANCESTRAL TALE THEN SHALL WE TELL, this one speaks of Kabʼraqan; Earthquake Boy; the Two-Footed One; the Third of Three; the Second of Two Sons who said they were the better than the best.

Earthquake is his name; Kabʼraqan as he known, the One who came next, the Third of Three; Kabʼraqan is he who we shall speak of now to complete the telling of their death and defeat by the Boys, the Sons, known and named; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: Earthquake or Kabʼraqan ROX Third out of Three This then is the Last of another Ancient Account of another Arrogant One of another filled with Pride and Conceit; One more False-faced Son; of the Three False-faced-Ones; Earthquake or Kabʼraqan is he who is the Second-Son the Last of the Three Arrogant and Boastful Ones. It is of He that we shall relate of those who did vociferously state that they were the Greatest of All those who were Greater than Great; the Third of the Self-Magnifying Ones; the Second Son of the First One who said he was the Light of the Sun; Light of the Moon when in fact he was the False Light of the Moon; False Light of the Sun; Wuqubʼ Kaqix was his name; Seven Scarlet Macaw. Wuqubʼ Kaqix is the One who was taken out of his Tree; the arrogant Father of the Two Arrogant Sons; Wuqubʼ Kaqix, Sipakna, and now Kabʼraqan the Second of Two Sons of Seven Macaw the First of this Three to be defeated by the Hunters; the Hunted; the Hero Twins; this then is the Last Story of all Three; here we shall tell of the Second Brother of the Big Three: the Giants of the Age of the Wooden People; the Sun of the Men of Tzʼite; the Talking Tree; the Moon of those Reed Women of Sibʼaq-Reeds that grow thick beside the Lakeshore that grew abundant with life. These are the Three Ancestral Narrative that teaches one how to be humble and courteous by showing reverence and deference; respect and regard without acting subservient and docile; submissive and weak. Popol Wuj teaches power and strength by telling these stories death and defeat that manifest the true dangers of self-deception that comes with arrogance and pride that lead to downfall and defeat; death and destruction; decline and then demise. This is the story that will be told here to be told again and again throughout the myth- making and story-telling of the Popol Wuj that taught the Noble Lords and their Descendants who were their Replacements how to reign and rule as powerful Leaders and intelligent Protectors of the People and their Pueblo.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
So realize this myth teaches the exemplary way to live out life as a Noble Rule who is called to guide and protect those people who depend upon oneʼs guidance and protection. The Maya are known to be a humble people yet their humility is based on ancestral power and noble strength that comes with the nawal powers of change and transformation that bring about the reversal of destiny through tricksterʼs power to act with humility and deference in order not to be seen as one who is born with the sovereign power and authority to rule and reign as a Noble Lord and Leader of People here on the Face of the Earth.

I am the Leveler of Mountains In yojol juyub I am the Destroyer of Mountains The Death and the Defeat Of the One Known and Named:

Earthquake-Kabʼraqan-Two-Footed-One

“I am the Leveler of Mountains-In yojol juyub-I am the Destroyer of Mountains; I am he who ʼfells mountainsʼ thus a ʼFeller of Mountainsʼ am I who takes down Mountains before the Heart of the Sky,” he said.

But it was just Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who defeated Earthquake-Kabʼraqan- Two-Footed-One, the Second Born Son of Seven Scarlet Macaw-ukʼabʼ ukʼajol Wuqubʼ Kaqix.

Those who spoke were Jun Raqan; Chʼipi Kaqulja; and Raxa Kaqulja when they spoke for Ukʼuʼx Kaj who told Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej just what to do next: “The Second Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix, the Second Son of Seven Macaw is just another one, another one who must be defeated.”

“This is just my word-xawi nutzij, for it is no good what he does there on the Face of the Earth. They wish to surpass the Sun in power and importance, strength and majesty; and this is something that just cannot be.”

“Bring him down then, just take him down when you persuade him to accompany you over to were the Sun comes up; convince him to walk East with you over to the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij-the Place of Dawn as it is known!” said Juraqan when he spoke to the Two Boys, Two Sons.

body:
“Very well then, You-Lal, oh Noble Lord; it is he, then, who must go. It is no good what we see in him. Do you not exist? Are you not the exalted one? Are you not the one who rises up higher than all the rest, you, oh Heart of the Sky-Lal Ukʼux Kaj?” said the Boys when they heard the word of Juraqan, the one known; the one named Hurricane-Jun Raqan-One-Footed One: Heart of Sky-Ukʼux Kaj- Heart of Heaven as his name is heard spoken.

And there Kabʼraqan was; out ʼLeveling Mountainsʼ across the land. It was just with the ʼSlightest Tap of his Footʼ on the ʼFace of the Earthʼ that he was able to ʼBring Downʼ Big Mountains, Small Mountains leveling them right ʼDown to the Groundʼ there wherever it was that he shook in order to shake the Earth causing it to quiver; causing it to quake as Kabʼraqan performed the task that was his to perform as the Third One; the Second Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix: Earthquake his name; the Second of Two who knew what was his to do on the Face of the Earth: Uwach Ulew where he caused the Sky to shake and the Earth to quake as Earthquakes are called to do. This then was when the Boys met up with him:

“Where are you going there, you, oh Son; you, oh Boy-At Kʼajol?” they asked Kabʼraqan. “Iʼm not going anywhere; Iʼm just bringing down mountains; just leveling them; just taking them down; down to the ground ʼfor All Time; for All Eternityʼ as it is said: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq; known as the Footpath of the Sun; Footpath of the Dawn; chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq; as Long as the Sun Rises; as Long as the Sun Dawns as Eternity is named; as Ever-Lasting Life is known,” said Kabʼraqan the Boy; the Son. For All Time: Eternally Chi Bʼe Qʼij; Chi Bʼe Saq For as Long as Dawn Comes; For as Long as the Sun Rises On the Footpath of the Sun; On the Footpath of the Dawn Raqan Qʼij; Raqan Saq Footpath of the Sun; to the Footpath of the Dawn

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The saying: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq might be translated as ʼfor as long as Dawn Comes; for as long as the Sun Risesʼ it is a Traditional Maya oath or spell that makes folks know ʼthis is what I do and I will do what I do to the End of Timeʼ. This is a salute in a toast that Elderly Maya Women and Elderly Maya Men still say when they take a ritual shot of liquor, letting their words ʼripʼ by letting their words ʼroarʼ as they thunder the salute: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq; for as long as Dawn walks the Path of the Sun; for as long as the Sun walks the Path of the Dawn; which is often heard in another version of the same sort of saying: Raqan Qʼij; Raqan Saq which signifies: to the Footpath of the Sun; to the Footpath of the Dawn as a play on the expression performed throughout this recitation of Popol Wuj: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq; ʼon the Path of the Sun; on the Path of the Dawnʼ which is to say for all time; which is to say for all eternity!

Which is to say: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq; On the Footpath of the Sun; On the Footpath of the Dawn which is what Kabʼraqan roars to make the Earth quake and the Sky shake to let the Boys know that he is right there; which means he is right here; and, he isnʼt going anywhere: chi Bʼe Qʼij, chi Bʼe Saq!

Which is a truly Nawal Way to set up the story of his own death and destruction by letting everyone know from the start that this Boy known Earthquake is as tough as his Older Brother, Sipakna, who was the Number One Son of Wuqubʼ Kaqix who went down doing what was his to do in a world where oneʼs hunger and appetite tells us who we are by telling us what is ours in life to bring to fruition; what is the essence of our sustenance that becomes the flesh of our body and the bones of eternity.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Popol Wuj, when it comes right down to it, is an Ancient Ancestral Account of Noble Lords fasting while walking on a Sacred Journey while acting and speaking in Sacred Ways in accordance with the Sacred Count of Days. Popol Wuj tells us at the end of the Noble Pilgrimage of Kʼicheʼ Nobles and their Descendants known as the Engendered Sons of Noble Lords who walk their First Four Fathers Ancient Ancestral Path to the Sacred Center of Pilgrimage known as Tolan Tzuy-Wa and named the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij while giving worship and praise to their Kabʼawil and Divine Ancestors.

All along the way they perform self-sacrifice to nourish and nurture the Kabʼawil to sustain them with their Sacred Sustenance of the body and blood of human beings; human being who were formed and shaped from the divine essence of maize and water; to form the nature and essence of human flesh and human blood. Maize and water will be used by the Former; the Shaper to form and shape the body and blood of the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Lineages in the First Generation of Kʼicheʼ Maya Nobles; Kʼicheʼ Maya Lords who were then called to perform self-sacrifice with Maguey Spines and Stingray Spines; Obsidian Blades and White Flint Blades.

So do realize the Boys are performing sacrifice that is founded in hunger for that which creates the flesh and blood of Wuqubʼ Kaqix: the Golden Yellow Fruit of Tapaʼl; the fish and crab of Sipakna-Cipacatli-Crocodile-Caiman Boy and now Kabʼraqan-Earthquake who eats Birds;; Birds that Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej will hunt for their Older Brothers and Grandmother to eat; Birds that will provide and sustain Jun Bʼatzʼ; Jun Chowen with their Sustenance! Maize will be the Sacred Sustenance of the Maize People of the Pueblo Maize and that pattern of existence and understanding is being laid down right here in these sacred stories of the defeat of those who show no gratitude; those who show no thanks for all that provides and sustains then with their Sacred Sustenance.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the sacred narrative brought forth here so we develop a sense of what is needed to live the ʼgood lifeʼ on the Face of the Earth. What is necessary to live the ʼdivine lifeʼ for the Maize People who take up the Sacred Path of their Divine Ancestors who you will come to see know just how to act and just how to speak by following the ʼfootstepsʼ of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej and their Grandmother IxMuqane and most of all their Mother: IxKikʼ.

Two-Footed One-Kabʼraqan-Earthquake: One of the Eternal Ones of the Sun One of the Eternal Ones of the Dawn

So this then was when Kabʼraqan spoke with Two Boys; the Two Sons; Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ known and named; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej asking them this:

“Where are you Boys from? I donʼt know your faces; I donʼt know your names. What do they call you? When then are your names?” asked Kabʼraqan. “We have no names; we are just hunters; we are just blowgun boys, we snare birds with our gypsum line; indeed, we are those of the Forest; we just trap up on the Mountainside. Just are just Poor Orphans-xa Oj Mebʼa. There is nothing that is ours, you, Boy, you, Son, At, Kʼajol,” said the Boys before continuing on. “We just wander along from place to place shouldering our blowguns. We just pass through the Small Mountains, the Big Mountains, just walking and wandering about shouldering our blowgun is our way,” said the Boys. “Well, for one who levels mountains like yourself, we can tell you for certain that way over there is one really Big Mountain that grows and grows all the time. That mountain just keeps growing; it just keeps rising up and up; growing taller and taller all the time; it is a real Big Mountain that Great Mountain over there,” said the Boys staring off in the direction of the Coming Out Place of the Sun; just tapping the soft silky dust making it puff-up; puff, puff.

“Over there, well, we have no luck at all; over there; over there, there arenʼt even one or two birds that weʼve snared for ourselves, you, oh Boy-At Kʼajol. Is it really true that you bring down ʼallʼ the mountains, Boy? ” asked Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej ʼas ifʼ to question the possibility of something like that being the truth; to which Kabʼraqan responded just the same. “Is it really true that you ʼsawʼ this mountain that you speak of? Where is it? I want to see it for myself. I will take it down. I will shake it down. I will just grind it right down to the ground. Where did you say you saw it?” asked Kabʼraqan-the Two-Footed-One; Earthquake as this Destroyer Mountain was known; as this Leveler of Mountains was named.

“It is just a little bit over that way, it just grows and grows up above all the rest; truly high does it climb that mountain there; it just puffs and puffs its way up into the Sky; it just climbs and climbs way up high; itʼs over there towards the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij-Place of the Dawn,” said Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. “Utz! Great! So then show me our road so we can be on our way!” he said to the Two Boys, the Two Sons; chi Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ. “Not so fast, you must just come over here to walk between the two of us. One to the left side; one to the right; after all we have our blowguns so if there are any birds to be had, then, we will be ready with our blowguns to take as shot,” they said.

Happily, contentedly they went along testing their blowguns as they made their way but when they blew on their blowguns no earthen clay shot came out of their tubes it was their puff, puffing on their blowguns that took the birds down; which left Kabʼraqan truly astounded to then leave him astonished.

They just puffed on their long wooden tubes; they just blew hard on the mouth of their blowguns and…puuj… puuj…They just blasted bursts of nawal breath through their enchanted blowpipes, and the birds fell from the limbs of the trees fluttering down to the ground; poof in the dust…chimalmat…they fell flat on their backs.

body:
This simply astonished Kabʼraqan who was truly astounded by all the Boys said and did. And so it was they went along towards the Coming Out Place of the Sun hunting all along the way, taking their time enjoying the fine day. It wasnʼt long before they had all the birds they needed to do what they were called to do by the One-footed-One there in the Heart of the Sky; Jun Raqan Ukʼuʼx Kaj.

So this then was when they went to work drilling fire and in no time their birds would be ready for roasting over the fire they drilled with clever cunning and skill.

They blanketed one of the birds with a sacred sort of soft silky soil known as ʼsajkabʼ known as ʼwhite-earthʼ which when wettened with water it becomes a curious class of calc; a gypsum coat that serves as a simple sort of plaster. But, when it is left to dry it becomes a fine, fluffy kind of divine dusty dirt similar if not the same as a tasteless, odorless, plain, pallid talc; really itʼs just deadly white earth and that is why they call it: sajkabʼ.

Once they basted the bird with sajkabʼ they placed it with the others to roast ever so slowly over the bright burning coals of their red hot fire.

“This one is for him, so that he might hunger for it, so that he might devour it. We will just whet his appetite, then, so that when he takes in the aroma it will awaken his desire for a nice piece of meat,” said the Boys. “So then it shall be the white earth-sajkabʼ with which we cover his bird that shall be his defeat; for the earth that we baste and brown his bird will be the same earth we envelop him when we throw him down in the ground before we bury him beneath the Earth.”

“Indeed, great wisdom comes to us through the Great Sages, the Great Knowers-Nima Etaʼmanel, those known; those named One Former, One Shaper- Jun Tzʼaq, Jun Bʼit.” “May it be so! May it come to pass! To the Sowing! To the Dawning! Ta Chawaxoq! Ta Saqiroq! May it come at last!” said the Two Boys, the Two Sons.

“Because it is just our heartsʼ desire to take a bite of meat. Truly, itʼs natural to enjoy a bit of roasted flesh. This is just the longing of the heart; like that of Kabʼraqan that longs for a tasty treat; Kabʼraqan who craves for nothing more than to eat a juicy piece of roasted meat,” said Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej when they spoke to one another there watching over their beguiling birds that simmered so sweet over their enchanting fire. Kabʼraqan just stood there staring; he just stood there salivating as he took in the captivating aroma that sparked his appetite that soon set his hunger on fire. The Boys just turned the birds over ever so slowly in the reddish-orange flames that glowed with the rich warm heat of their fire; those birds were just roasty-toasty, browning so easy as they cooked to perfection; juicy fat just dripped from their crispy, crackling backs; truly, the sweet smelling grease just sputtered and spattered to flame up out of that delectable fire to release an enchanting aroma of an ancient, ancestral kind of primordial desire.

Primal Power of Fire Transforming Magic of Brazing Birds over Hot Coals The Trap of Appetite; the Hankering for Meat Tricksters Tricks on the Sacred Path of Hunger

It was just because of the delicious aroma of the roasting meat and the spellbinding scent of those sweet smelling birds with their sumptuous grease that Kabʼraqan now hankered for so ravenously for just a bite of this brazed birdʼs succulent meat.

body:
If only he could just try a taste of that tantalizing treat; if only he could calm his fierce longing; his ferocious hankering hunger; for now his mouth watered for just a bite of the roasting meat with its crackling gristle and fizzling fat that fizzed and sizzled on the birdsʼ brazed and browned backs; as their golden skins crackled as the grease spattered and sputtered over the fire that now ignited a profoundly primitive flame that now burnt bright as some sort of ancient ancestral fire that ignited the hunger that was the hankering of a most primordial desire. A desire lit by the primal power of fire that now burned as an ancient ancestral desire; a desire that hungered to devour all that was within reach of Kabʼraqanʼs will to fulfill that ravenous longing for what the Boys brazed on their fire; their fire that now bloomed like a flower whose succulent scent had Kabʼraqan in the grasp of its primal power.

For now Kabʼraqan was not only caught but captured in their trap: the trap of appetite. The trap of appetite the Boys had set just for Kabʼraqan; the trap of appetite that now had Earthquake in its grip; the trap of appetite that Kabʼraqan could no longer slip.

Kabʼraqan now just swallowed his drool; he just downed his dribble, as he began to drown in his very own spittle; as the meat grilled, as the fat sizzled; the grease spat and then lit in the flames of the fire that burned in the pit over which the roasting birds were turned on the spit. Now there was no turning back; no way to quit so they kept up with the plan that had become actually quite fun as they slowly spun those birds little by little as the fire popped and fizzled; popped and fizzled so that the meat cooked and the skin sizzled.

body: So then, they, the Two Boys, the Two Sons asked Kabʼraqan something that spoke to him in a visceral sort of primal way; a question that spoke to the truth that he bore within him as the essence of his soul; a truth that now bound him to the Earth in an essential sort of elemental kind of way; a question and an answer that would identify him through a simple yet substantial sort of identification. Now it was Kabʼraqan who was destroyed by his desire to destroy the work of his older brother the Maker of Mountains; for it was now those who twin brothers who were made up of he who was the Number One Son that was the Maker of Mountains; and, the Number Two Son who was the Destroyer of Mountains should be those who would be known as Mountains. For it was they who were buried beneath the two most important Mountains by these Boys who laid those Arrogant Ones as low as low can be since they changed and transformed them into Mountains at end of the Earth: the Sowing Mountain of Maize-Meʼawan and the Dawning Mountain of the Sun-Saqiribʼal. All of this changing and transforming of oneʼs rivals into Eruption Mountains that erupted with abundance and Earthquake Mountains that dawned with transcendence had to be fully contemplated to be brought to completion by those two charming tricksters who were enchanting beguilers who bewitched those who got in their way of becoming the Sun and Moon of the New Era and its New Age; these were those Ancient Ancestral Hunters; the Blowgun Boys known as the First One and Second Son; named Blow-gun Boy and Little Jaguar Deer. It was just through their enchanting words spoken over their beguiling fire that the Boys bewitched those browned and brazed birds that were now completely cooked; the same birds they had hunted with their nawal powers of blowgunners; magical transforming powers of nawal hunters; nawal powers of magical transformation given as a gift to the Hero Twins from those who were known as los Nawales; the Former; the Shaper; the Mother; the Father; the Ancient Old White-Haired Ones; the Ancient Old Ancestral Ones....
