body:
The End of this Story-telling of Defeat and Destruction Myth-Making Narrative of the Arrogant Ones; the Proud Ones Self-Magnifying Ones; Self-Aggrandizing Ones; Self-Glorifying Ones This then was when they asked: “What then is your food; what then is your sustenance; what is it that is yours, Kabʼraqan?” The poor Boy just answered wantonly as he was now completely transfixed by his ancient ancestral appetite: “Truly delicious do I find the aroma that I smell now. That which is roasting here before me is truly what I desire to eat. Why donʼt you just give me a little taste; just a bit of this sweet smelling meat?” he replied with true humility.

Earthquake Boy, Earthquake Son was now utterly humbled by his horrific hunger; Kabʼraqan found himself to be totally devastated, destroyed by his desire; knocked down; laid low; just leveled was he, the Two-Footed-One, who was now overwhelmed by his own appetite and its craving for meat.

Kabʼraqan was definitively demolished by his false sense of superiority that had always ruled his self-aggrandizing delusion of grandeur and his grandiose illusion of power and majesty.

This, then, is when they gave Kabʼraqan that browned basted bird that they had expressly prepared for him to eat, which was his destruction and defeat as the destroyer of mountains; Kabʼraqan, the shaker and quaker of the Earth who was the maker of Earthquakes.

This then was when he finished off that whole bird without saying a word. Kabʼraqan devoured the specially brazed bird he was give to eat without ever tasting his defeat.

An Alternative Telling of the fall of Kabʼraqan He just smacked his lips; he just sucked his teeth; he just licked his fingers as he wiped his cheeks; never had he ever tasted something as delicious as the nicely coated back of that brazed bird and its roasty-toasty meat.

He took what was given just as he ate all that was offered; the bird they gave him was the one they plastered with the white earth known as sajkʼabʼ and that gypsum baste might be what gave that the rich taste to that roasted bird in white earth leaving it succulent and sweet.

body:
When they finished eating and they continued on walking until they came to the Coming Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij-the Dawning Place of the Sun, in the East; there where the Big Mountain, the Dawning Mountain stood high above all the rest of the Mountain-Plain.

This Dawning Mountain is known as Saqiribʼal or Sajribʼal. Now they stood at its feet; at the Foot of the Mountain; PaRaqan Juyubʼ is where they stood, the three of them there. This, then, was when Kabʼraqan could go no farther. This is where he felt that his strength had abandoned him; the power and strength that had always existed within his Two Feet was now brought to completion; the Two-Footed Oneʼs vigor and vitality was gone for he was turned to stone.

Just like a pile of rocks was the way he now felt in his feet, in his hands, then his knees; his ankles, well they buckled; his body just seized; then ever so slowly he began to fall as he collapsed onto the Face of the Earth. Before he knew it, it was he who was destroyed and defeated; dead and gone; just demolished; just laid low; just leveled like a Great Mountain was the One named Kabʼraqan who was knocked down to the ground without making a sound.

No longer was he capable of making his way. It was the sajkabʼ with which they blanketed his bird, the divine dirt; the sacred earth that was his downfall; the doing of the Boys that was the divine calling of their Father; their Lord and Ruler known and named Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

He who is spoken of as Heart of the Sky; Hurricane Rain; Lord Storm; Lord of the Thunderers-Tojojila; Thunderbolt-Lightening; One-Footed Rain this is the One-Footed-One who sees it all to know it all to divine it all in order to control and create the Sky-Earth through the Destruction he embodies at the End of every Sun; at the End of every Age.

body:
Kabʼraqan couldnʼt do a thing to the Great Mountain that stood before them. He did not destroy it as he wished he could. He did not demolish it like he thought he would. He didnʼt even try to level it as he thought he should. It was over; his power and strength were gone; gone for good. Just like a captive was he bound by the Boys, the Sons. They tied his arms behind his back; they coupled his hands together to then knot them at the wrists. Then they bound and tied his ankles together like a war captive; like a slave; like an offering to be offered up for sacrifice was he subjugated.

This then was when they threw him down and buried him in the ground; in the White Earth; under the Dawning Mountain: Sajribʼal.

Thus was the defeat of Kabʼraqan; it was the doing of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who did innumerable, uncountable things here on the Face of the Earth; waral Chuwach Ulew. Now we shall tell of the birth of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej; since we have first told of the defeat of Wuqubʼ Kaqix-Seven Scarlet Macaw along with Sipakna- Volcano Son, and Kabʼraqan-Earthquake Son here on the Face of the Earth; waral Chuwach Ulew.

Quotes to Feed the Myth; to Sustain the Story

“Myths do not happen all at once. They do not spring forth whole into the world. They form slowly, rolled between the hands of time until their edges are smooth, until the saying of the story gives enough weight to the words-to the memories-to keep them rolling on their own.”

E. Schwab A Conjuring of Light

body:
“The hearer of myth, regardless of his level of culture, when he is listening to a myth, forgets, as it were, his particular situation and is projected into another world, into another universe which is no longer his poor little universe of every day. . . . The myths are true because they are sacred, because they tell him about sacred beings and events. Consequently, in reciting or listening to a myth, one resumes contact with the sacred and with reality, and in so doing one transcends the profane condition, the "historical situation." In other words one goes beyond the temporal condition and the dull self-sufficiency which is the lot of every human being simply because every human being is "ignorant" — in the sense that he is identifying himself, and Reality, with his own particular situation. And ignorance is, first of all, this false identification of Reality with what each one of us appears to be or to possess.” Mircea Eliade “Our modern alienation from myth is unprecedented. In the pre-modern world, mythology was indispensable. It not only helped people to make sense of their lives but also revealed regions of the human mind that would otherwise have remained inaccessible. It was an early form of psychology. The stories of the gods and heroes descending into the underworld, threading through labyrinths and fighting with monsters, brought to light the mysterious working of the psyche, showing people how to cope with their interior crises. When Freud and Jung began to chart the modern quest for the soul, they instinctively turned to classical mythology to explain their insights, and gave the old myths new interpretation. There was nothing new in this. There is never a single, orthodox version of a myth. As our circumstances change, we need to tell our stories differently in order to bring out their timeless truth…”

A Short History of Myth Karen Armstrong

body:
Theatrical Tradition of Ritual Drama; Song and Dance Drama; Long Performance of Mythic Recitation; Long Performance of Myth and Ritual; Ancestral Practices of Initiation through Peregrination; Long Distant Warrior-Merchant Tradition.

These are aspects of Mesoamerican Civilization Myth and Religion and their Socio- Cultural Traditions found here in the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj that comes from Olmec Origins on the Gulf Coast and from Teotihuacan in the Central Highlands of Mexico and Central Highlands of Guatemala such as Kaminal Juyu and Abʼaj Takalik as well as the Lake Shores of Atitlán and Amatitlán and all along the Pacific Coast and Boca Coast of Southern Mesoamerica as well as Mixtec-Zapotec Tradition of Oaxaca.

All of these Mesoamerican Traditions will influence the Maya of Southern Mesoamerica who will adopt and adapt Social and Cultural influence they find in the Mesoamerica World through Long Distant Trade and Cultural Exchange. This is adoptive and adaptive way of the Maya continues to amongst the Maya of Southern Mesoamerica to this very day. The Popol Wuj is an expression of this cultural capacity and adaptive capability of the Maya to his very day.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu and their sons Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are those of Teotihuacan the First Ones; the Ancient Ones of Tula-Tollan; these are those of Cholula- Chollan; these are those of Chichen Itzaj and Mayapan; these are those of Palenque, Bonampak, Tikal, el Mirador, Nakbeʼ, Calakmul, Cancuen, Waxaktun; Yax Ja, Quirigua, and Copan. These are those of an Ancient Mesoamerican City of Great Splendor where the ancestral image of ancestral perfection was realized by those Artists and Artisans; Architects and Astronomers of the Splendid and Sublime City with its Rulers and those Rulersʼ Vassals and Subjects known as the Divine Daughters and Sacred Sons who worked and played with their Noble Lords to reach a state of precious perfection right here on the Face of the Earth.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These are those who are Protectors of Maize, Guardians of the Sacred Sustenance as they are named; the Father, the Uncle as they are known; One Ancient Ancestral Father of Maize, Seven Ancient Ancestral Father of Maize known from here on as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. These Two are the First Fathers of the Maize People or Ixim Winaq: Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are their names, the names of the Fathers of the Hero Twins: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who complement and complete one-an-other as Divine Twins that manifest their Divine Twinship through constant transformations of nawal genius and nawal imagination that are experienced as sacred acts of ritual play and ritual speech. These then are the names of their Parents-kikajaw-the Parents, the Primordial Pair, the Ancestral Mother-Father known as Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane; the First Father, the First Mother, the Parents-Kikajaw: Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane who are the Ancient Ancestral Pair; Divine Grandmother, Divine Grandfather of the Maize People, those of the Saq Kʼaslem-Divine Life, Sacred Life, Bright Life for they are those of the Face of the Earth; those of the Milpa and Maize; these who are those who are empowered with the magical powers of transformation and creation known as: Nawal Winaq.

These Nawal Winaq are Divine Ancestors who are Noble Ancestors who embody the transformative energies of renewal and regeneration on the Face of the Earth. They embody the ancestral powers of the mythic imagination and initiatory transformation of the life affirming forces of light and life; they are Divine Ancestors of the Living Light of the Sun and Moon; the life giving solar warmth of the Sun and lunar pull of the Moon; the constancy of the Sun and transforming essence of the ever-changing and transforming Moon.

body:
The personified image of the Sun and the Moon live on in the face of the Ancestors seen in face of their Descendants as well as their harvest of Maize and Cacao that is transformed into sacred sustenance through the work and care of the Men and Women; Boys and Girls; Grandmother, Grandfathers; Chuch-Qajaw. The ʼhard kernelsʼ of maize and ʼhard beansʼ of cacao live on as replacements of the original ʼkernels of maizeʼ and ʼbeans of cacaoʼ in a world where and in which Maize and Cacao are personified by Maize Deities and Cacao Divinities. These Divinities of Sacred Sustenance are known in Popol Wuj as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu for it is they who are reborn in the shape and form of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. These Twins may have been Maize and Cacao; Junajpu as Maize and Ixbʼalamkej as Cacao who will become the Sun and Moon of the Era and Age of the People of Sacred Sustenance: Ixim Winaq known as People of Maize; Maize People.

Their Ancestral Soul lives within the Maize Beings as an eternal connection that connects the Divine Ancestors with their Human Descendants who experience transcendence through the Ritual Drama of Popol Wuj that opens up the portals of ritual experience known as ʼParticipation Mystiqueʼ in which the participation of the Descendants in the mythic lives of their Divine Ancestors. Descendants were able to enter the Ancestral Soul by entering the Ancient Word in order to enter the Imaginal Realm of the Popol Wuj. By fully engaging their Mythic Imagination the Ancient World of the Divine Ancestors could be entered because in truth it does not die it lives on in the imagination but also in the experience created through Long Performance; Long Recitation of the Ritual Drama of Popol Wuj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Popol Wuj that was formed and shaped so that its transforming essence is experienced as their Nawal embodied in the sparkling green resplendence of a jade bead; the blood red remembrance of a Tzʼite bean; the Maize Shoot of the Sprouting Seed all of which are manifestations of the Eternal Return of the Divine Ancestors through their ʼRitual Renewalʼ as the Descendants known as ʼkʼexel-replacementsʼ as ʼketal-signsʼ as ʼkitzijel-word-spark-essence- flowerʼ all of whom will be with us all along the way.

This Ancestral Essence of Maize and Cacao; Sacred Sustenance is alive within Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu and their Boys, their Sons: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. Their essence is Life and Rebirth and so they embody the eternal return of the bright life of the Dawning and the Sowing for even if they are killed their Nawal essence, character, or nature known as the ʼbeing and becomingʼ or ʼukʼojeʼikʼ will find a way to come back to life through some sort of magical means of transformation.

Popol Wuj was the Ritual Way to bring the Divine Ancestors back to life through the Descendants who ʼbecomeʼ their Ancestors through the ʼeternal returnʼ embody in this Myth of the Maize People. Popol Wuj opens the way for the Descendants to become their Ancestors through the Transcendent Experience that is the Participation Experience of the Replacements of the Divine Ancestors becoming their Divine Ancestors. This is the magical practice of transformation known as being and becoming a Nawal; a Nagual; a Nahual.

This reveals to us as it tells to us that the sacred journey and the goal are the same when the Maya played out and performed the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj. This is the mystery of myth; the mystery of the Descendants becoming their Ancestors through the ʼtranscendent functionʼ of myth through which the Descendant who is the Replacement of the Ancestors becomes ʼone with their lineageʼ by becoming ʼone with the essenceʼ with which the First Father; First Mothers of Maize were brought into being through the forming and shaping of ground maize.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This experience of coming into being is experienced again through the Descendants full engagement in the Imaginal Realm of the Mythic Imagination. This Imaginal Realm created by the Mythic Imagination is where we are going now. We will now enter the Ancient Word; to enter the Ancestral Account of the Ancient Ones; the Nawal Ones; the Ones known as the Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu and all of their family of the Maize People; the Pueblo of Maize.

Letʼs then enter the word with our fully engaged Ancestral Soul to be able to fully engage in the Mythic Imagination of Popol Wuj. Let us enter ʼin illo temporeʼ when this all happened in mythic time and mythic space to be experienced now in mythic time and mythic space and by doing so experience mythic transcendence in a magic sort of metaphorical way where our Ancestral Soul is brought to life so that we might live again in those ancient ancestral times when the Myth of Maize was once lived out in the lives of the Maya just as they are lived out today. Jo junam jo; letʼs go together; letʼs go: Jo, jo, jo junam jo!

THIS THEN IS WHEN WE WILL NEXT NAME THE NAMES OF THE FATHERS OF JUNAJPU, IXBʼALAMKEJ; let us name the names next of their Fathers; the names of the Fathers of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

Let us drink to him; let us just make a toast to it being told; to its being spoken; to its being said; the telling of the tale that tells of the begetting of the Boys, the Sons, the Twins; the account of Jun Junajpu and his engendering of the Twins; of his begetting of his Sons: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

Just the ʼhalfʼ of it we shall tell; just a part of their ancestral story we shall tell; the ʼhalfʼ that gives an account of their Fathers is what we shall tell.

Here then is itʼs telling; here then is itʼs being told; the Ancestral Story, the Ancient Account of those who are named Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

In the darkness, in the night-chi qʼequmal, chi aqʼabʼal-were they born, the Boys, the Sons; those who were born Twins; Twin Boys, Twin Sons known as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. These Boys, these Sons were begotten to their Father Xpiyakok while being born to their Mother IxMuqane.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
So then this Jun Junajpu had just two children and the two of them were Boys, his Sons: Jun Bʼatzʼ known as One Monkey is the name of the First-born- Son; Nabʼeal, while Jun Chowen spoken of as One Artisan is the name of the Second-born Son; Kabʼal. Here then is the name of their Mother; IxBʼaqiyalo-White Egret Woman of the Great Water-Sea; IxBʼaqiyalo-White Bone Woman of the Delta-Sea; White Bone Woman of the Great Estuary Sea-Yalo-Palo; White Bone Egret Woman of the Ocean-Sea-IxBʼaqiyalo as she is spoken of, as she is named, the First Woman, the First Wife of Jun Junajpu as she is known. Now this Second Son of Xpiyakok-IxMuqane named Wuqubʼ Junajpu had no Wife, he was just a Single Man. And being the Second Born-Kabʼal it was just in his nature to remain a Young Man of marrying age; xa ulaqʼel.

Great Thinkers-E Nimaʼq AjNaʼoj-Great Sages were they; great then was their Knowing and great, too, was their Genius-Ketamabʼal-their Knowledge, for it was they who were Great Diviners-E Nikwachinel-Mid-most Seers who lived here on the Face of the Earth beneath the Sky.

They were Seers who were known to be Knowers; Seers who were seen to be Knowers who were seen and known to be Diviners; Diviners whose sight reached both far and near; for truly vast was their vision; for truly infinite was their sight so that endless and infinite was their seeing and knowing here on the Face of the Earth. They were good-natured and they were well-trained; properly instructed were they in all that they came to say and do; perform and make; act and create. They taught their arts to their Boys; they passed on their skills-nawikil-their knowledge to their Sons Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen: these who were the First Begotten Sons of Jun Junajpu known as the Older Ones; the Elder Sons. They were Flute Players; e AjSuʼ

They were Singers; e AjBʼix They were Blowgunners; e AjPu They were Scribes and Painters; e AjTzʼibʼ.

They were Carvers, Sculptors, and Mask-makers; e AjKʼot They were Jade-workers; e AjXit and Silversmiths; e AjPuwaq, as well.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is what became of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen spoken of as One Monkey and One Artisan as these Boys were known to be: flautists and singers; hunters and blow-gunners; scribes and painters; sculptors, carvers, and mask-makers; jade- workers and jewelers; silversmiths and workers of precious stones and fine gems; artists and artisans were they who were performers and dancers; magicians and musicians who loved making music to dance about the house.

This is how these Twins were known, those who were the Boys of Jun Junajpu as these first two Sons were named: Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; One Spun Thread; One Ancestor; One Howler; One Monkey, One Artisan as they are known as it is said.

Now as for Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; well, they just Threw-Dice; xa Sakʼ, they just Played-Ball; xa Chaaj; everyday they threw dice, everyday they played-ball: xa Sakʼ, xa Chaaj. Just two-on-two did they play their games; in duos as doubles, in pairs as partners, in twos as twins they played every day, day after day they played in a complementary sort of way; as balanced pairs they played; as competent companions is the way they played; as they played in harmony; competitive yet collaborative is the way they played; as they played and played; day after day.

It was the four of them that gathered together to play two-on-two; it was those who were the First Fathers of the First Sons who played together as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen to compete with one another everyday in astounding and astonishing feats of play; when they played ball on their ancestral ballcourt that they called-Jom-Ballcourt-Burial Groundsʼ pronounced just like ʼhomeʼ.

One day Wok-Laughing Falcon landed there above their Ballcourt-Jom, and seeing that they were playing he stopped to watch the way they played their rubberball game as they competed against one another ʼtwo-on-twoʼ as complementary companions- that played against ʼone-an-otherʼ in pairs; as couples; at doubles-kikʼulelaj kibʼ as it is said in Maya Kʼicheʼ

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Wok, Laughing Falcon, was a Seer-Ilol ke-making him the Worker- usamajel-the Messenger of Jun Raqan, Chʼipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja, these were those known as the Heart of the Sky; Ukʼuʼx Kaj. Now for Wok, this Laughing Falcon, it was not far for him to fly from the Heart of the Sky to the Face of the Earth; nor was it distant for him to descend there to Xibʼalbʼa: Place of Fear, Place of Intimidation, and Place of Initiation. In an instant this Messenger Wok-Laughing Falcon arrived there in the Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj where he acted as the Messenger-Samajel-Worker of Jun Raqan, Chʼipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja Wok with who he arrived with there in the Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj as a great Seer-Ilol who saw everything that went on in the land of the living and the land of the dead; on the Face of the Earth just ʼbelow the Skyʼ and in Xibʼalbʼa just ʼbelow the Earthʼ.

For Wok, being a Falcon, it wasnʼt far for him to fly from there in the Heart of the Sky to here on the Face of the Earth; nor was it far for him to fly from up here on the Face of the Earth to down there in Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa. In an instant Wok could fly up into the Sky with the One-Footed-One Hurricane-Jun Raqan; and so it was that Wok could fly back and forth from up in the Sky with Jun Raqan to then drop down to Xibʼalbʼa to be with those of Xibʼalbʼa seeing everything there was to see with the vision of a ʼSeer-Ilolʼ which was the work and way of Wok who saw all their was to see as Wok the Ilol; Wok the Seer. Now it was Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who remained on the Face of the Earth for a long time after the death of IxBʼaqiyalo-White Egret Woman, the Mother of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen, the Monkey Twins, the Artisan Twins: One Howler Monkey, One Artisan Son as they are known.

IxBʼaqiyalo: White Bone Woman of the Great Water

IxBʼaqiyalo is also known as White Bone Woman of the Great Water, in which Ya-Lake and Palo-Sea combine to create Yalo-Great Water in the form of a Lake or perhaps in the shape of an Estuary where the Snowy White Egret Ancestors live out their lives.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Their light white bodies are formed from weightless hollow bones and bodies conformed from almost no flesh; these divine ancestral birds are avian beings that live by the shores of large bodies of placid pacific water.

These birds canʼt take much wind and live almost like ghost beings because they are so light consisting of bodies shaped with puffy fluffy snowy white feathers and a yellow beak that spears minnows and fish like the true warrior women they embody as the ancestral souls of the Dead who they ensoul as white winged wanderers who move from the Highlands to the Lowlands sailing along in the wind on the white wings formed from hollow bones and bright white feathers as light as the breeze; perfectly at ease perched on the thinnest of reeds doubled- over in the rushes.

Because IxBʼaqiyalo was a Snowy White Egret she lived up on the Highland Lakes alongside the lakeshore reeds and down on the Seaside Estuaries where there was nice calm water for her to fish amongst the thick stands of reeds. These lake and estuary reeds were once teaming with a great multitude of minnows, snails, shrimp, langoustine, and crabs which is the sacred sustenance of Mesoamerican women and men; girls and boys.

It was the women in particular and old men and children who accompanied them to create ʼfish traps or corral-kokʼ amongst the reeds where the minnows and crabs and shrimpʼ

were rounded up and harvested by old men and boys in dugout canoes that drove and corralled the minnows, fish, shrimp and crabs into the fish traps or weirs or corrals formed in the reeds.

This is where IxBʼaqiyalo would go to get her fill of what the people gathered together form themselves. IxBʼaqiyalo dies but we donʼt know why but we do know she is the embodiment of sacred sustenance for she must become the white bone of white maize or some such nawal transformation of the Divine Ancestors; all of whom will be transformed into sacred sustenance by the time we come to end of our long performance and recitation of the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

body:
IxBʼaqiyalo as White Egret Woman is seen on Classic Period polychrome vases painted in calligraphic styled pictographic histories and/or myths. IxBʼaqiyalo is also seen as an avian images sculpted on exterior temple friezes that are plastered on white temple walls such as that found in el Mirador above the sculpted plaster images of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who are seen in the water beneath where White Egret Woman stands ready to spear her sacred sustenance with her long spear-like beak. But we are only told ʼhalf of the storyʼ and that doesnʼt include telling of IxBʼaqiyalo so we fluffed-up her Snowy White Egret feathers a bit here so such comes to life in the Imaginal Realm of your Mythic Imagination.

The rubber ballcourt-jom where the paired partners played as teams of Fathers and Sons was the rubberball ballcourt where the rubberball game was played on the Road to Xibʼalbʼa; this place on the Road to Xibʼalbʼa was where the ball-players played up on the Face of the Earth.

And so this was where the pairs of Ballplayers were heard playing ball all day long. This was when and where their bouncing ball was heard bouncing off the walls and bounding off the floor causing a great roar for those who were down below in the Underworld place known as Xibʼalbʼa. Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen couldnʼt help being heard down under the earth by Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame-Lord One Death, Lord Seven Death who were the Noble Lords and Rulers of Xibʼalbʼa. These were those who did not like the sound of the way the Ballplayers jumped up and down and the way they ran around while their rubberball bounced up and down on their finely finished; perfectly plastered ballcourt; known to the Men and Boys as the place they called jom; the burial place that was the sacred space they pronounced to one another as ʼhomeʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This running all around after the ball that bounced up and down was just much too much for the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who being Lords of Death liked it as still and silent as death gets but this is not what was going on over their head which is why the sent their messenger up above to invite those from the Face of the Earth to come down to Xibʼalbʼa if they really wanted to play ball.

There is a ubiquitous pun formed continuously through the ingenious mythopoetics of the original Maya Kʼicheʼ Language. This fun little pun comes to life through this formation of ʼon the road to Xibʼalbʼa-pubʼeʼel Xibʼalbʼa and the blowgun-pubʼ of the Boys written as both pubʼ and ubʼ so that the contraction that is formed by ʼon the roadʼ moves from ʼpa ubʼeʼelʼ to become ʼpubʼeʼel-on the roadʼ as in on ʼblowgun roadʼʼ which is a form of sympathetic magic says the Blowgun Boys are going to defeat those of Xibʼalbʼa to make the Road to Xibʼalbʼa become the ʼRoad of the Blowgunnersʼ which is heard as this ʼsignifying punʼ throughout the telling of the story of the Boys walking on the road to Xibʼalbʼa shouldering their blowguns as they make their way to and then through Xibʼalbʼa.

I mention this so the reader gets a taste of all that is inevitably lost in translation; all of which we will place on the table when able so you get a sense of the constant and continuous word-play that takes place throughout the endless play-on-words in this Indigenous Literary Masterpiece of Ancient Indigenous Literature that is formed and shaped from a sacred sort of secret ceremonial speech that makes the Popol Wuj one of this Worldʼs Great Mythic Masterpieces formed from Mythic Metaphorical Language to create Sacred Literature formed from Maya Mythic Metaphors and Ancient Ancestral Archetypes of the Maya Culture and the Mesoamerican Civilization.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
When you come to know the Popol Wuj you will know the Deep Structure of the Mesoamerican Worldview. This is it we are about to descend into the Ancestral Soul of Mesoamerica by descending down underground into the Land of the Dead known as Xibʼalbʼa where the Lords of Death want to control the living by defeating them with the powers of death. This is the way they play the Rubberball Game on their Ballcourt known as the Pusbʼal Chaaj: the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice. Leaving little doubt what game they really want to play which is the game of death.

Lords of Death: Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame Lords of Life; Lords of Maize: Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu Pusbʼal Chaaj: the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice

“What is going on up there on the Face of the Earth? Who are they to jump up and down the way they do; running up and down yelling and screaming causing such a racket; I just canʼt take it; I just canʼt have it! Go up there to send for them so they can come down here where they can play ball with us. Just let them be defeated by us here on our court with our play, that is all I have to say,” said those of Xibʼalbʼa. “They show no humility before us; they show us no respect, they show us no regard; they no longer humble themselves before us for who we are. They show us no deference; just as they show us no reverence for it is they who show us neither care nor consideration for who we are and what we do.” Cried the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. “Their wild ways of bouncing the ball and stomping about while yelling and shouting out on their ballcourt; the jumping up and down while run all about is no way to act or speak for those who know how to play the rubberball game on the rubberball court!” Called out the Lords Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame. “They obviously donʼt recognize our power and authority anymore with the way they beat their ball all about to then bounce it over our head,” said all of those there in Xibʼalbʼa.

This then was when they gathered together their thought; when they celebrated Council together to talk the situation over with one another; to figure out what they should do about the ballplayers that were making so much noise.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were those who were named Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; those who were the Supreme Judges of the Word; those who were they that weighed the word-e nimaʼq qʼatol tzij; those who were the ʼsupreme judges of the truthʼ as it is said. This then was when they gathered together in council to consider and contemplate their thoughts and ideas there in Xibʼalbʼa. These were those named Jun Kame-One Death; Wuqubʼ Kame-Seven Death.

It was they who were the Supreme Judges of the Word. Lord One Death, Lord Seven Death they were those who ruled over the power and authority of the Living and the Dead for it was they who judged the ways and weighed the word which gave them the sovereign power to measure the truth-qʼatabʼal tzij through their authority to evaluate the facts.

And this power to ʼweigh the word; measure the truthʼ gave them the power to punish and penalize the fallen and failed ways of those who didnʼt know how to act and speak in knowledgeable ways that were traditional ways. These Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were those who ruled over all others with their sovereign rule and ancestral power of their noble word and its ancestral weight; its ancestral weight that was the balance of power; which is to say Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame were those with the supreme power to weigh the truth with a measure of authority in order judge life and death of the destiny of those who were accused of doing wrong while not speaking the truth or knowing the proper way to act and speak; which is to say they who were those known and named Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame were those who governed their ancestral world through their noble rule and its sovereign power over their ancestral realm and its supreme rule and reign over death and disease as the lords and rulers of Xibʼalbʼa.

That is why those who were invited to Xibʼalbʼa had to be very careful about accepting an invitation to play ball with the Lords of Death on their Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice because if the Noble Lords Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame decided to judge those Ballplayers as being unworthy of continuing on living life then they would most certainly be sacrificed on their altar of sacrifice.

As for all the other Lords of Xibʼalbʼa, they were each assigned a sacred burden to bear as an ancestral cargo to be carried out as a divine obligation to fulfill as an ancestral duty to be brought to completion that was a traditional responsibility that called to be brought to fruition. These sacred burdens that were ancestral obligations of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were borne out as sacred burdens that had to be fulfilled and ancestral obligation that had to be completed by those who were the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who were the Lords of Death and Disease.

These were those who performed their duties and obligations under the power and authority of the Supreme Lords of Xibʼalbʼa One Death, Seven Death-Ajawabʼ Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; who carried the fate of the living on their shoulders in order to fulfill their sacred burden as the ʼsupreme judges of the truth-e nimaʼq qʼatol tzijʼ by bearing the inevitable fulfillment of the Truth that the Life of the Living would find its natural fruition of the Living Dying in Death and through Disease.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This was the rule and reign of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa; they were the Lords of Death and Disease; each with their name and all with their own particular realm of bearing the Living to Death while showing the way of the Healthy to Disease. They were all tricksters and cheaters; these Lords of Death and Disease; they were all liars and deceivers who lured Living; the beguiled and bewitched Breathing; they coaxed and cajoled; enchanted and charmed the Living and Breathing towards Death and Disease so the Ancestral Souls ended up being held captive by the Lords of the Dead in Xibʼalbʼa. It was they, the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa, who bore upon their shoulders the burden of their ancestral responsibilities that gave life its sacred hierarchy; the sacred hierarchy that was the divine order of life and death; the divine order of life and death that was ruled over through the sacred rule and reign of ancestral rulership that was the divine office of the Lords of Death. They were who bore the sacred burden of judgment over life and death that was brought to fruition through the devious and dastardly ways of the Lords of Death and Disease; which is to say by the many Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who we are about to meet through the ʼnaming their namesʼ in perfect order and in perfect ways that reflects the sacred hierarchy of the Land of the Living and the Land of the Dead. Popol Wuj tells you none of this because the Maya knew this as being the very essence of their myth and religion; as well as the Life and Death way of Maya Culture and Mesoamerican Civilization. Life and death were thus ruled over through the sacred ordering of sovereign authority and divine rule of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa over each and every aspect of death and disease; these are the traditional realms of death and disease and those traditional realmsʼ specific dominion over particular forms of death and particular shapes of disease.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
For Xibʼalbʼa was where the Lords of Death and Disease resided until they were called up onto the Face of the Earth to do their work among the Living and Breathing Descendants and Replacements of the Divine Ancestors. These Descendants who were the Replacements of the Divine Ancestors were those who were called by Lords of Death and Disease to descend down into Xibʼalbʼa to be tested by the trials and ordeals found in the Houses of Tests and Houses of Trials of Xibʼalbʼa. And if the ʼinitiatesʼ survived the tests and overcame the trials in the Houses of Ordeal in Xibʼalbʼa then they lived life for another Count of Days.

But if those who were invited down to Xibʼalbʼa did not conquer their fears in order to triumph over the tests and trials of Xibʼalbʼa then they were immediately sacrificed on the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice. And that my friend is what is going to happen here where we are headed in this Sacred Narrative that is calling us on to the Xibʼalbʼa and its many tests and trials in its Houses of Ordeal known as the Houses of Xibʼalbʼa .

ʼName the Namesʼ of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa Lords of Death; Lords of Disease; Lords of Death and Disease

The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa that were paired in pairs and coupled in couples were called upon to fulfill their ancestral obligation and sacred burden as the Noble Lords and Rulers of Death and Disease; Lords and Rulers who ruled over the lives of the Living who existed on the Face of the Earth.

It was this ancestral power of the Lords of Death and Disease that each of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa exercised as the rule of sovereign authority over those who lived on the Face of the Earth. It was they, the Living, that came to the attention of the Supreme Lords of Xibʼalbʼa known as Ajaw Jun Kame, Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kame spoken of as Lord One Death, Lord Seven Death.

Naïve People; Innocent People Mountain People; Simple People

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Let us then ʼName the Namesʼ of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa so we can move on to their playing ball with the innocent ones who are the naive ones who lived on the Face of the Earth in the Land of the Living. These are those known as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; they are those of the Mountain Places; they of the Canyon Country; Settled and Sedentary Divine Ancestors of the Maize People. These are those Mountain People; Simple People of Simple Times and Simple Ways who know nothing of the Deadly Ways of Death.

These are Mountain People who live out their life by following their Mountain Ways that donʼt expect others to deceive and lie; trick and cheat; mislead and betray which is exactly what the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa do. But Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are ʼcountry bumpkinsʼ who know nothing about the dastardly and dishonest Ways of Others; and, the Ways of Others were not the Ways of the Good Life; the Honorable Death; and Eternal Return of Ancestor through Rebirth.

Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu are Nawal Ancestors of the Sacred Count of the Days who return to life every Two-Hundred and Sixty Days; they are Ancient Ones; they are Nawales who leave the perfect example-saqetal for their Descendants to follow as Replacements of perfect speaking and perfect acting Divine Ancestors. This then is the Ancient, Ancestral Account of the Living and the Dead in which the Dead want to harvest the warm souls of the Living to keep the Dead warm by keeping the souls of the Living captive in the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa. This is the direction we are heading so letʼs get going down this road to Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
All of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were given their power and authority over Death and Disease by being given a Sacred Burden to bear as a Divine Task to perform known as the Divine Office that they carried-out as a Lord of Death who was a Lord of Disease. Each and every Lord of Xibʼalbʼa was appointed Sovereign Rule-Ajawarem over a type of Illness or a kind Accident by those who were named Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame. Let us then ʼName the Namesʼ of the Lords of Death; who are Lords of Disease; who are Lords of Accidents; who are Lords of Assault, Attack, and Anger; Lords of Hatred, Hostility, and Enmity. The first of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa to be named were those Lords known as Xikʼiri Pat; Kuchuma Kikʼ whose Divine Office; Sacred Burden pertained to he who ʼlet-bloodʼ who was he who ʼbled-bloodʼ and his companion who was he who ʼgathered-bloodʼ who was he who ʼcollected-bloodʼ for it was they who were those whose burden it was to heal those whose blood was ill; to cure those whose blood was not well.

So then came next Ajal Puj-Lord Pus and Ajal Qʼana-Lord Jaundice; these Lords-Ajawabʼ were given the authority over the swelling up of people; they caused pus to ooze from their legs; they caused their face to turn yellow; Jaundice is the name of the disease of their domain.

That then is the rule and authority; the sacred burden and ancestral cargo of the power and sovereignty of Ajal Puj; Ajal Qʼana; Lord Pus, Lord Jaundice. The next Lords of Xibʼalbʼa named here are those known as Chʼamiyabʼaq, Chʼamiyajolom; Lord Bone Staff, Lord Skull Staff; they are the guardians and gatekeepers that act as the wardens of Xibʼalbʼa: their scepters, their staffs-chʼamiy are made of skull-jolom and bones-bʼaq.

These are the staff-bearers of Xibʼalbʼa whose cargo it is to make people grow thin; to then transform them into skeletons; these unfortunate souls just end- up skin and bones. Those who are affected by this disease just look like skeletons so that at the end of their days there is nothing left of them but ʼskull and bonesʼ known as ʼjolom, baqʼ with no meat on their bones; with no flesh on their bodies.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
When these folks died it was just their skeleton that was taken away. This then was what Chʼamiyabʼaq, Chʼamiyajolom; Lord Bone Staff, Lord Skull Staff reigned and ruled as Co-Regents; Co-Rulers who were Lords of Death and Disease; whose cargo; whose burden; whose office-upatan was that of skeletal beings: just skull and bones is what they were. Chʼamiyabʼaq; Chʼamiyajolom were the Staff Bearers of Xibʼalbʼa: they bore the Staff of Bones, Staff of Skulls for the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Ajawabʼ Xibʼalbʼa. They led the way of those of Xibʼalbʼa when it came to taking up the Road of Xibʼalbʼa that led to the Council House of Xibʼalbʼa or Popobʼal Xibʼalbʼa. These Lords of Xibʼalbʼa where known as the Staff Bearers of Xibʼalbʼa; Skull-Jolom and Bone-Baq were their emblem of office, Jolom; Baq were just the symbols of their Divine Office as the Guardians and Gatekeepers of Xibʼalbʼa; Chʼamiyabʼaq, Chʼamiyajolom were the Wardens of the Land of the Dead.

These were their positions of power and authority over Death borne out in their names Lord Bone Staff, Lord Skull Staff; Chʼamiyabʼaq, Chʼamiyajolom, as they are invoked, as they are named, as they are known as the Lords of Skull and Bone.

Those that came next were Ajal Mes; Ajal Toqʼobʼ Lord Filth-maker, Lord Back-stabber they were those known as Lord Slander, Lord Favor who created conflict wherever they were called. Their burden of office was just causing hostility and hatred; anger and enmity amongst people by digging up filth on oneʼs enemy either behind the house of an adversary or in front of the house of a rival. They were there to make a ʼmessʼ of anotherʼs life by doing some nasty ʼfavorʼ or just sowing-strife to create violence and aggression.

No matter where it was that these slanderers met they created mocking malevolence, wicked iniquity, and cruel contempt by bating friends into initiating preemptory conflict that escalates into battering brawls to end-up as bitter enemies whose coldhearted cruelty knows no limits.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These endless wars of hatred and hostility were always founded in ʼtrash-talkingʼ and ʼback-stabbingʼ activities that came to fruition in low-life fighting fed by low-life filth that called for fatal sorts of favors; favors that asked somebody to cause somebody else to ended-up laying face down in the dirt or face-up by the side the road; laying perfectly still because of being perfectly dead at the bottom of a ravine or in some out-of-the-way place like a gully or a gorge or a gulch. This is the work of these back-biting problem-makers who are the causers of conflict known as Ajal Mes; Ajal Toqʼobʼ

This is the authority given to Ajal Mes; Ajal Toqʼobʼ, as they are called. They were true Trash-Talkers completely competent and capable of completing evil-errands by doing others a fatal favor!

Next comes the naming of those rulers of death and disease known as Ajaw Xik; Ajaw Patan; Lord Hawk, Lord Wing, Lord Messenger; Lord Merchant, Lord Cargo-Carrier, Lord Tribute-Bearer-Ajaw Patan.

Ajaw Patan was just the Lord of the Pack-strap of Merchants; Patan-Tump- line of Porters, Pack-strap of Bearers, Tump-line of Cargadores, Pack-strap of the Kakaxtle of Tamemes as they are known: Aj Patan. These are those who bear cargo on their back in a merchantʼs carrying-box known as a Kok-Tortoise Shell that is spoken of a Kakaxtle which is ʼCarrying-Frameʼ of a Long-Distant Merchants known as a Pochteca. This is their Lord of Death; the One to be Feared on the Road or around the Corner; under a bridge or beside a cliff. This is that Sacred Burden of Death and Dying named here: AjPatan is his name. This name named Ajaw Patan is a Death Lord Merchants; a Death Lord of an Ancient Ancestral Cargador. This is the name that named Ajaw Patan as a Merchant Lord of Violent Death who was encountered in and upon the Road as a malicious and malevolent murderer Merchants who robbed them blind to then leave them dead or just dying in the ditch beside the road or beside the riverʼs edge.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
There were plenty of places to way-lay a Long-Distant Pochteca who couldnʼt see well to take proper precautions because of this tump-line that was stung over the crown of oneʼs head. Known as Patan this Pack-strap was the origin and fundamental reason for many a merchant death.

Ajaw Patan is the name that names those who were killed by killers while being robbed by robbers who left these unfortunate merchants with little choice in desperate situations where there is nowhere to run and nowhere to hide. These Underworld Lords were those who ruled over the deaths of travelers who died on the road from sudden death-xa rax kamik as it is known and named because of the way blood pours forth from these ill-fated merchantsʼ mouths after being laid-low on the road. These were Merchant Lords who were just ambushed from above or taken down from below; both of which are violent ways to go.

These are those who die spitting-up blood after being beaten bad by murderous thieves who take advantage of those who walk with their tumpline on the top of their head not being able to see where they are going as they walk down the road.

Ajaw Xik, Ajaw Patan; Lord Hawk; Lord Bearer of Burden or just named as they often are: Xik, Patan. These are those who are they that cause Sudden Death, like a Hawk, these Lords of Death just swoop down from above; just like a thunderbolt of sudden lightning these victimsʼ attackers are there to plunder what is carried on the merchant back by their pack-strap or tumpline thatʼs been torn asunder to then take its bearer under.

Truly there is no crueler ruler of a disease as is Xik, Patan for usually it is not poverty and need that is the seed to this sort of devious death that is as most dastardly deed. No, it is always avarice and greed that are the root of this deadly disease that feeds the need to kill Merchants like this lighting quick form of death known as Xik: Sudden Death; Raxa Kamnaq. These two, Xik, Patan, strike far from home without warning to finish off all those unfortunate Long Distant Merchants who bear their cargos with tump-lines slung over the crown of their heads.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These are those who are slain by the side of the road and then left to die in a pool of blood in the most violent form of death the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa name: Xik or Hawk because of how ʼQuickʼ one dies without ever being sick. These are those that take hard-working folk by the throat to choke them out by throttling them hard. These killers just crush the chests of merchants-warriors- ballplayers who are destined to die far from home. They make this happen either walking about or sitting-down in the middle of the road; nobody knows where their lives will be cut-short in this most brutal of all ways to go.

This then was naming of the name of the traditional power and authority that ruled those who went by the names: Xik, Patan. So then they gathered together to celebrate council with one another to consider and contemplate their thoughts. These were those who were the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who were known as the Lords of Death and Disease.

They decided to persecute Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu in order create conflict to cause trouble with those known and name Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. Those of Xibʼalbʼa wanted the Ball-playing equipment and adornment of Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu; their desire alone called them to invite the Ancient Ancestral Ballplayers down to Xibʼalbʼa to play on their Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice: Pusbʼal Chaaj.

So this then is what they did to create the problem they only they could solve by sending for their Messenger-Workers known as AjSamajel who would be sent up to send them down.

body:
Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu Fair-play vs. Deception AjPus were those of sacrifice-pus; AjPubʼ were those of the blowgun-pubʼ; AjPuj were those of weeping pustules of pus-puj; Ajpu were those ancient ancestral ones from the place of pu-reeds as in the cattail reeds and rushes; AjPuuh were those of the shamanic breathe that transformed the soul and spirit of the nawal to heal the ill, to cleanse the poisoned, the polluted, to transform the Sky-Earth and its beings with a powerful ʼpuuhʼ of breathe. AjPus those of Sacrifice-Pus for it will be Junajpus who will sacrifice the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa to end sacrifice once and for all until it begins again through the influence of Tollan Tzuy-Wa and Lord Storm known as Tojil who will call for blood when those who call for rain so that a great flood will fall when the Mountain Pueblo call for the fire they need to keep warm while their Milpa calls for rain to grow to fruition. AjPus; Junajpus: Ancient Ancestral Lord of Sacrifice. These were those spoken of as One Ancient Ancestral One of the Blowgun and Seven Ancient Ancestral Blowgun Man from the mythical Place of the Reeds thick with abundance where the Ancient Ancestors lived magical transforming lives defined by a life of acrobatic ball playing; familial contentment, and the ease of Artist and Musicians who knew where their sacred sustenance was being grown in magical milpas that provided these First People with sustenance while sustaining their soul with ease knowing they could create with ease and comfort knowing what was theirs in life.

Deception was not part of their lives in which lying had no place and cheating was pointless in play that was meant to be an divine expression of the Ancestors whoʼs movements were ʼrememberedʼ through body memory so that ball play was experience as a manifestation of divinity through the repetition of the movements of the Nawales.

body:
Same with the dice throwing that was a playful means of being and becoming one with the visualization of the dice. The excitement that comes with the seeing and knowing of the next throw that one needed to complete the throws that formed the configurations of this Game of Dice known as Saqbʼal. How fun to become one with the die that were thrown just right to bring forth the face of the divine that came with the casting of the die that was a casting of the lots. This is the good life of the Twin Fathers of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej; Twin Sons of Xpiyakok, IxMuqane. They are now going away to a distant place to play on a Ballcourt with rules and ways of its own that are not at all like those at home on the court known and named: Jom. Now Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu have awoken the anger and wrath of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame with their bouncing ball and stomping about while yelling and shouting out on their ballcourt that is said to be right there beside the Road of Xibʼalbʼa which says something about where these Ancient Ancestral Ones come from.

Now the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa want to take for their own the prized possessions of these two innocent twins; these two ball-playing brothers; these two ball-playing fathers who have what the Lords of the Underworld do not have but want very much for their own because of their ʼbad-styleʼ ways where envy and avarice are what have ignited this passionate problem of asking their newly found rivals; there newly created adversaries to bring their ʼball-playingʼ equipment with them down to Xibʼalbʼa; but Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu will not do as they are commanded to do by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu were asked to bring down to Xibʼalbʼa that which is theirs to pass down to their sons as inheritance. The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa want to take from Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu the splendid adornment and special ball playing equipment from those who the Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame are inviting down from the Face of the Earth. Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame do this because they have nothing of their own to adorn themselves as ballplayers on their ballcourt for they are nothing but skeletal beings with no clothes, no jewelry, no jade, no ball gaming equipment, or adornment to call their own.

And you know how False-face Lords are. They need adornment to show everyone they are legitimate entitled lords with insignia sovereign rule and emblems of noble investiture that identifies them as Noble Lords with the power and authority to Noble Rule. And so it is that Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu have brought their ball playing equipment to the attention of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame. And so it that the ball-playing gear; their ball- playing equipment of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu will be named here along with all of its valuable paraphernalia. The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa wanted what was not theirs yet the very source of the envy and jealousy that they now suffered; the jealousy and envy they suffered was formed and shaped by their desire to possess for themselves the beautiful ball-playing equipment and adornment that was not theirs yet had become the very object and origin of the ferocious longing and fierce desire that they now suffered as the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. And so it is that the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa now want for themselves the ball-playing equipment-ketzʼabʼal of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; for it is Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who have caught the full attention of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa with their loud stomping about and continuous running around in their endless ball-playing matches on the Face of the Earth where they yell and scream without giving a thought to the possibility that they are playing on top of the Underworld Abode of those known as Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame who are ballplayers that never take their ball playing skills out of the house and down the road.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Something is going on here with Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame but it is impossible to know until one has read the Popol Wuj multiple times . Why do the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa want the Ball- Playing Equipment-ketzʼabʼal? And why does noise and movement bother them so much as residence of the Underworld where the Ancestors go to then transform into the Stars in the Constellation above? What is going on here and how will we ever really know? Popol Wuj is ʼMythʼ and as ʼMythʼ it is meant to ʼbedazzleʼ the mind of descendant in order to awaken their Ancestral Soul to the ways of Life, Death, and Rebirth in world that is only given meaning by human beings who give it meaning through telling myth in order that ʼfires-upʼ our soul in order to get us moving towards acts of creation and destruction that are meant to ʼre-createʼ the World of the Sky-Earth. Myth confounds us on purpose in order to seek ways of participating in creating what is before or destroying what no longer serves our lives and deep desire to make sense of those lives lived here on the Face of the Earth.

This is why we live at a time when humanity has returned to myth and mythology with the knowing that has a great deal to offer our imagination and the way that imagination awakens our human consciousness to experiencing the divine through the ʼtranscendent functionʼ of myth that creates the perfect conditions for human beings to transcend time and space in order to enter ʼin illo temporeʼ of myth when and where myth takes place in our psycheʼs or soulʼs experience of myth. Myth then is about the soulʼs experience of the divine.

Myth then opens up the doors of perception through which we are able to see our lives and our world in divine kinds of ways. Myth then develops our perception in order to be able to ʼsee throughʼ reality in ways that provide deep meaning to our lives and profound understanding of our world. Myth teaches us how to live the ʼgood lifeʼ in ways that make us feel at home in this world; this world in which we belong according to myth and its myth-making; meaning- making ways of revealing the meaning of life and why we are here.

This then is the Ball-Playing Equipment-ketzʼabʼal-Ball-Playing Adornment of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu:

Kitzʼum-their animal pelt apron-armor-ri kitzʼum-their skins, their covering, their protection they wore that transformed them into Nawal Lords; Animal Companions of the Ballcourt

Kibʼate-their ball-playing yokes worn on their hips-kibʼate-the wooden yokes to ʼbeat- bʼa-hammerʼ the rubberball; hip-yokes made from the wood-teʼ-cheʼ-trees; yokes covered in puma or jaguar pelts

Kipachqʼab-their arm guards-kipachqʼabʼ to protect their arms from being bruised and broken by the heavy rubber ball and to reinforce their arms to strengthen their play when the go down to the ground to make a play

body: Kiyachwach- their penachos or coronas-kiyachwach-headdress that express the ʼface- imageʼ of their nawal-nahual-nagual that comes to life on the ballcourt as the soul-spirit- essence of the Ballplayer; the Animal Companion-Nagual-Animal Transform are embodied through these finely finished feather headdresses and embellished wooden masks Wachzut-their emblematic head-scarf and skull-protectors-wachzut-the ʼzuteʼ or ʼhead- scarfʼ that all ballplayers wore as a way of showing ʼfaceʼ on and off the ballcourt so that everyone knew their place Kikawubʼal-their gemstone adornments-kikawubʼal-jade beads that Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu wore as the essence of their lineageʼs eternal life; the eternal life embodied in these emerald gemstones and jade beads that empowered those who wore them with the power of renewal and essence of regeneration of the lineages from which the ballplayers came as the flowering fruit that grew in the limbs and branches of their lineagesʼ ancestral tree with its ancestral trunk, limbs, and branches from which flower and fruit the lineages through their multiple generations The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa are ʼdead-setʼ on taking for themselves what Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are determined not to give away and that is their fine ball-playing regalia of those whose family tradition it is to play their ancestors rubberball game over their heads. This set of ʼball-playing gearʼ that is ʼball-playing equipmentʼ that is ʼball-playing regaliaʼ was the ʼone great inheritanceʼ a Father could pass down to their Sons and Grandsons.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And this my dear reader must be well understood to be able to understand what is at stake here when Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu descend down into Xibʼalbʼa without their ʼball- playing gearʼ carried along with them! Ball-playing gear that will be left hanging-down in the rafters of their Mother IxMuqaneʼs House; ball-playing equipment that is left behind to be taken up and worn by their sons when the time comes to play the rubberball game as the inheritance of their Fathers; their Fathers Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who are the Maize Lords; Maize Lords whose adornment and embellishment is their ball-playing gear with its beautiful jade necklaces and bracelets; feather headdress and protective ʼskinsʼ and ʼarmbandsʼ and all important ʼyokeʼ with which to ʼbeatʼ the ball making it fly across the sky and through the rings that are ʼballcourt markersʼ mounted above the ʼapronʼ up on the wall of the Maya Ballcourt.

Being Summonsed by the Lords of Death The Descent Down into Xibʼalbʼa An Archetypal Descent of the Soul Let us now tell next of when they journeyed to Xibʼalbʼa to play Ajaw Jun Kame, Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kame and how they left behind Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen, the sons of Jun Junajpu.

Their mother had already died for Ixbʼaqiyalo was already dead before the defeat of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen by JunAjPubʼ, IxBʼalamKej! It was then that they, the messengers-samajel-the emissaries arrived on the Face of the Earth after being sent by their Lords, Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; One Death, Seven Death. These were those known as envoys-ajsamajel-workers who were the servant emissaries of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who sent them with a message to summons Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu with a summons that was an invitation. This summons was sent with the messengers while being told to do the following:

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Go you Messenger Warriors of the Noble Reed Mat-AjPop Achij; go with this summons to bring back Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu!” said Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame. This was when the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa said this to their messengers: “Say this when you arrive there with them: ʼCome! Kepetoq!ʼ is what the Lords say for us to say to you: ʼDown here is where you must descend; here is where you must come to play with us, so that we might liven-up our lives with you! Truly we are amazed by you; truly we are astounded by all you do; and, that is why we wish for you to arrive here to play with us!ʼ say the Lordsʼ you will say,ʼ” they said when they left their instructions with their Messenger Warriors of the Noble Reed Mat; AjPop Achij.

“You will say to them, ʼBring along your ball-playing gear; just bring along your gaming things; your ball-playing regalia so that you shall be well prepared to play on our ballcourt, just bring what is yours: bring your waist yokes-kibʼate, to beat the ball; bring your arm protectors-kipachqʼabʼ; and your rubber-ball-kikikʼ as well!ʼ say the Lords.ʼ This is what you must say to them when you arrive with them; when you arrive up there,” said the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa when they spoke to their Messengers-AjSamajel-Workers-AjSamajel.

And so these were the Messengers, the Owls-ri Tukur, the Owls were their Messengers-Kisamajel: Chʼabʼi Tukur; Arrow Owl Juraqan Tukur; Jun Raqan Owl; One-Footed Owl Kaqix Tukur; Macaw Owl Jolom Tukur; Skull Owl These Four Owls were Messengers Warriors of the Noble Reed Mat; these were those spoken of as the Emissary; Envoy of Xibʼalbʼa.

Chʼabʼi Tukur-Arrow Owl moves fast like an arrow that arrives in flash out of nowhere Juraqan Tukur-One-Legged Owl has just one leg; but he has wings, he has feathers Kaqix Tukur-Macaw Owl is colored fire-red; he has wings, just as he has feathers And then there is Skull Owl-Jolom Tukur; Skull Owl is he who has just a skull, he has no legs, he just has wings, he just has feathers; Jolom Tukur-Skull Owl is a Skull Being with no legs, only wings and feathers are what he has as a Messenger Owl of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; One Death, Seven Death, the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
There were Four Messengers-Workers known as Samajel Rajpop Achijabʼ they were of high rank known as the ʼMessenger Warriors of the Woven Reed Mat of the Noble Lords and Rulersʼ.

They had status that went with their rank so that people took notice wherever they were sent to arrive with the messages that they delivered for their Lords to be listened to as the very same voice and message as the Lords who sent them to be followed as the Lordsʼ very same orders that were sent with their Messengers who were Warriors of the Noble Reed Mat of Noble Rule and Authority: Samajel Rajpop Achijab.

These were those Messengers-Workers-Servants-AjSamajel who were respected as the ʼveryʼ embodiment of the word of the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

The Owls flew up and out of the cave underworld of Xibʼalbʼa that was down below the surface of the earth to arrive instantly over and above the Ballcourt where they perched themselves over and above the ballplayers. The ballplayers who were playing ball on their ballcourt they called Jom, ancestral place of burial, ancestral place of deceased ballplayers; dead Lords; dead and deceased Lords who were buried there beside the Ballcourt Burial Grounds: Jom.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu were playing ball on their ballcourt there; the ballcourt they called Nim Xol Kar Chaaj-Great Hollow of Fish Ballcourt that came from a previous Age and its sacrifice.

This Ballcourt of Nim Xol Karchaaj is there where there is a ʼhollowʼ on a limestone shelf that stretches out towards the road that drops down to Xibʼalbʼa; the Road to Xibʼalbʼa that drops down to the Lowland limestone caves where one finds the entrance to Xibʼalbʼa.

Nim Xol Kar Chaaj is the opening that leads down into the underworld caves of the Dead and Deceased Ancestors.

body:
And so the message of the Lords-Ajawabʼ was formed-xtzʼaq by the messengers; the message that was thrown down-xtzaq into play by their messengers, the Owls-Tukur. This ʼthrowing downʼ of their word was received as a challenge that was thrown into play by the Owls who formed their words just right so they were received as the words of the Noble Lords that were formed by the Owls to be thrown down into play by the Messengers perched above the ballcourt by the Owls-xtzaq kitzij kumal Tukur, as it is said.

This challenge that the Owls made on behalf of the Lords was thrown down on the ballcourt to the ballplayers who listened in disbelief to all the Messengers said.

“Could it be true that this was said by Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame?” asked Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. “Truly it is so-Qitzij bʼa la,” they said, said the Owls, “Oj na! Letʼs go! We are to accompany you! Bring along all of your ball-playing equipment-chikʼam uloq ri ketzʼabʼal-your ball-playing gear with all your ceremonial adornment; your ball-playing regalia! Say the Lords.” Said the Owls-ri Tukur; ri AjPop Achij Xibʼalbʼa. “Utz bʼa la! Very well then! Just wait for us since we must first take leave of Our Mother: QaChuch,” they said then to the Owls-ri Tukur-the Messengers of Xibʼalbʼa. This then was when they went back home, returning to speak with their Mother-Ixmuqane.

Their Father-Xpiyakok was already dead; Xpiyakok had already died which made their Father Xpiyakok an Ancestor; a Deceased Lord; Xpiyakok, their dead Father who had already died as it is said: xkaminaqoq kiqajaw.

body:
And so they arrived there with the Mother to take leave of her before descending with the Owls to Xibʼalbʼa on the Road to Xibʼalbʼa. IxMuqane is the name of their Mother; the Mother; the Grandmother; the Great Grandmother of the People of Maize; the Maize People: Ixim Winaq. “Joʼna! Ix QaChuch-We must go! You, Our Mother; Joʼna! Ix QaChuch. Weʼll return right away; donʼt cry Mother we will soon be back home. It is just the Messengers of the Noble Lord-usamajel Ajaw-it is just they who have come to summons us so that we might accompany them; and so weʼve been asked to ready our things so that we might return with them. It is they who have come to guide us; it is they who have arrived with us so that we may depart with them; those who our guides who now wait upon us; it is they, the Owls, who will show us the way; for it is they who have come all this way so that we might leave with them.”

ʼ“Kepetoq! Come along!ʼ say the Lords-ri Ajaw,” said those who were sent to summons us,” said Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who repeated to their Mother what was said to them. “We will leave behind our rubber ball-qakikʼ, as our remembrance, as our sign” they said, those named Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu, when they took leave of their Mother IxMuqane.

Straight-away they left their ball tied up in the rafters of the house-puwi ja.

“Qojul na! We will return! We will come back! Then we will take up our ball to put it in play again!” said Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. Then they gave instructions to their Boys; their Sons Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen before taking leave of their home:

“Just play your flutes, just sing your songs; just paint and write, just carve and sculpt. Make our home warm; our family content by warming the heart of your Grandmother,” is what they said when they left their words of counsel; when they took their leave of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen, their Artisan Sons, the Monkey Boy Twins: One Howler Monkey, One Artisan Monkey: Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen.

body:
Bitter tears did she weep-qʼusqʼus choqʼ kichuch-their Mother, IxMuqane, upon their getting-up to her alone with their Boys; their Sons who they left with instructions to warm the heart of their Grandmother who was like a Mother to them because their Mother Ixbʼaqiyalo had already died; she was already dead.

“Joʼ na! Come now! We are not going to die. Donʼt be sad-Maja bʼi kojkamik. Mixbʼisonik.” said Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu when they left.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu On the Road to Xibʼalbʼa Sacred Journey; Archetypal Path of Initiation; Path of Transformation

And so it was that Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu left. They were guided down their road by the messengers, the emissaries, the Owls-Tukur.

This then was when they descended down the ʼblowgunʼ road of Xibʼalbʼa- xeqaj kʼut pu ubʼeal Xibʼalbʼa. They dropped down the steep steps of the steep face of the steep flight of stairs there-xuluxuj uchi kumuk-and then down, down, down they went in their steep, steep descent.

When they arrived at the bottom of the steep flight of stairs the Ball-players came out to where the canyons split off from one another arriving at a place spoken of as the junction of the river canyons where they came to the turbulent river rapids of the Changing, Transforming River-Jal Ja that formed the Blowgun Canyon- Siwan Ubʼ that was there at the entrance of the two great canyon rivers; rivers that dropped underground like a ʼblowgunʼ as in a Narrow Canyon; as in an Echo Canyon-Nubʼ Siwan creating the crying call of Kʼulku Siwan the ʼqʼu-qʼuʼ cry of Quetzal Canyon-Qʼuqʼ kul Siwan.

body:
Now they must pass through the rushing-roaring rivers and their wild- whirling waters swirling down below of where Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu must go. This misty place of river spray is known and named Jal-Jal Jaʼ Simaj-the Turbulent River Rapids were a spectrum of colored light bridges the canyon void beneath the roaring river mist. This is where the river rapids roar crowned by sharp limestone spears that resemble spiny stakes the rise-up straight; just jade green spikes set sharp and pointed in their way. It was here that those spike-like spines-simaj-stood standing-up before them to halt their march; these spine-like spikes were placed just so to pierce them with their sharp, sharp blades to stop their progress; to block their way.

But the fearless ballplayers were not speared; they were not stabbed; they were not spiked, and so they moved on undaunted by these tests and trials they encountered on their way to Xibʼalbʼa where theyʼd been invited to play.

Theyʼd been summoned by the Lords-Ajaw so they did whatever was demanded of them in order to do as they were commanded; and so it was that they took up the narrow road north to then follow it to where it landed them and that is where they appeared to be stranded there before two deadly and diseased rivers that gave them no other option then to continue on to where they could make it across without giving up and accepting loss.

They came upon the side of a river, Blood River-Kikʼ Aʼ; they passed right over without drinking a drop.

They came upon another river, where pus-puj alone ran like water; they werenʼt defeated there either, they just crossed right over that lethal stuff.

It was then that they arrived at the Crossroads-pa Kajibʼ Xalqat Bʼe where Four Roads from the Four Directions met together at the Center to then cross-over one another at the Crossroads.

This is where they were defeated; they were defeated at the Crossroads where Four-Kajibʼ Crossed-Xalqat Roads-Bʼe came together at the place where Four Roads Crossed: Kajibʼ Xalqat Bʼe: the Crossroads.

There at the Center of the Crossroads the Four Roads met:

body:
One Red Road; Jun Kaqa Bʼe One, then, Black Road; Jun kʼut Qʼeqʼa Bʼe White Road One; Saqi Bʼe Jun One, then, Yellow Road; Jun kʼut Qʼana Bʼe Four Roads; Kajibʼ Bʼe This then was when it spoke; the Black Road-Qʼeqʼa Bʼe spoke; “I am the one to take up, I am the road of the Ruler; I am the road of the Noble Lord-In ubʼe Ajaw!ʼ” said the Black Road-Qʼeqʼa Bʼe.

Right there is where they were defeated; they were defeated when they took up the road of Xibʼalbʼa-ri ubʼe Xibʼalbʼa. This is the road they chose; when they chose to walk the Black Road-ri Qʼeqʼa Bʼey the Black Road of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

It was then that Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu arrived at the Council House of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa-Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa.

It was there that they were defeated again. For it was they who were deceived by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa: Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame- One Death, Seven Death.

The first seated ones there at the entrance of the Council House of Xibʼalbʼa was just a Decorated Decoy; just a Dressed-up Dummy-kawutalik Poy, kawutalik Ajam Cheʼ just a Decked-out Doll; just an Adorned Work of Wood.

This is all that these wooden decoys; wooden manikins were; Embellished Works of Wood; just Adorned Woodwork is what they were and all that they would ever be. Because those Wooden Men who were seated there at the Entrance Way of Xibʼalbʼa were just Bedecked and Bejeweled Manikin carved from the soft and knotless wood of the Tzʼite; that kind and caring Painted Tree-Tzʼajtel the Corral Tree that was a deceptive and devious as a tree could be.

body:
It was the lively Talking Wood from this always alert and attentive Whistle Tree known as the Palo de Pito that could have fooled anyone because it sure seemed like the First Seated and Second Seated Lords of Xibʼalbʼa just winked at the Ballplayers who barely raised their gaze to look upon the face of those who were seated in the principal position and place of the highest rank and order. These newly arrived Ballplayers simply assumed that these two were the First and Second Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. And so they did what anyone would do when greeting Manikin Men made of Wood who were seated to make a fool of you. Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu greeted the First and Second Noble Lords just as they believed they should be greeted despite their nature and condition being that of the wood whose essence was that of a tree.

These carved men, these sculpted men were dressed up and decorated before being set-up seated right there beside the entryway of the Council House Hall of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa-Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa:

They were just Decorated Dolls, xa Poy, xa Ajam Cheʼ, just Whittled Works of Wood placed right there at the entrance of the Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa: the Council House Hall of the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. It was they; it was just them, those Wooden Men who were greeted first and then second by Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. Who thought they knew how to act in this sort of place where they would speak with proper humility and a touch of grace in order to not look weak and ending up losing face by making a mistake to then be treated as a disgrace.

This then was beginning of the end for two of them; this first failure would be the root of their ruination; the origin of their humiliation, for it was just the sowing; just the seeding of their defeat by those of Xibʼalbʼa: Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame.
