body:
“Greetings! Good Morning One Death Qʼala! Saqarik Jun Kame!” said Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu as they greeted the First-Seated-One seated there in the first seat at the entrance hall of Xibʼalbʼa. But the Decorated Decoy; the Decorated Doll-Poy sitting there was just a Wooden Manikin who sat there silent and still; this ʼWooden-kind-of-Manʼ who sat there silent and still said nothing at all. “Greetings! Good Morning Seven Death; Qʼala! Saqarik Wuqubʼ Kame!” they saluted the second-seated-one; the second wood-worked work-of-wood: Ajam Cheʼ.

Those who were seated as the First Seated One and Second Seated One did not speak they didnʼt say a thing; no, those who Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu greeted that were seated there at the entrance of Council House Hall of Xibʼalbʼa-ri Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa did not say a word; they didnʼt say a thing; those Wooden-Works-of-Wood didnʼt make a peep because they couldnʼt speak being Works of Wood-Ajam Cheʼ and since Worked-Wood was all they were not a word was heard. This was when a roar of laughter thundered through the entrance hall as a horrendous howl resounded down through the Council House of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa.

The Lords and Rulers of Xibʼalbʼa just laughed hysterically for they had defeated Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu so very easily by besting them with this simple testing of them that ended their chances of taking one step more towards the floor of their Ballcourt; not one footstep further would they now make to take up play on the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice known and named as Pusbʼal Chaaj; for Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame defeated them-xechʼakomajik right there; right there at the entrance of Xibʼalbʼa.

One must pass through Rites of Initiation to know the Ways of the World One must learn how to be at Home in the World Sacred Stories, Ancestral Ritual provide one with a deep sense of Belonging in the World

body:
Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu were ridiculed as fools for not knowing who to greet by not knowing who was real and who was wood as anyone who was initiated into the ʼritual naming of namesʼ surely would. But these two country boys could not do what they did not know what to do. So they couldnʼt make the right decision by knowing how to determine the true from the false in order to weigh the word in order to speak the truth in order to act in the right kind of traditional way. They didnʼt know the way to act in order enter the Council House of Xibʼalbʼa by knowing how to ʼname the namesʼ of the Noble Lords of Death and Disease who bore the sacred burden of their ancestral office. How could they show these Noble Lords deep respect and high regard if they couldnʼt even name their names. Thus the Father Twins lost heart from the start for not how to speak and act smart. Their losing heart caused them to lose face which made them feel the disgrace they now felt for not knowing a single thing about place they were invited that was the place they now found themselves feeling out of place and a strong sense of estrangement for they now felt they did not belong.

So now they were filled with a deep sense of not belonging to this place that came from their not knowing anything about those who had invited them there was compounded by the humiliating position that their hosts the Lords of Death has so cheerful and deceptively placed them in caused Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu a profound sense of ignorance that came with their innocence that reassured them that the entire world was just like home and its ballcourt and the milpa and the mountain and its river and all that was found there.

But the world with its people and its place were different which is something one learned by listening to sacred stories or gazing upon pictorial histories to learn from the experience of those who had gone before and left their knowledge, experience, and hopeful some wisdom written down and painted in Ancient Ancestral Accounts. But these two ballplayers knew nothing of this thus had been easily defeated by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: Those two who had been invited to play ball in Xibʼalbʼa not been initiated into the ways of Noble Lords so there was no question they felt completely out of place in a noble sort of space like this where they were; a noble space that was traditional place where they had come; a regal sort of royal place like this where they were didnʼt allow them to feel like they belonged while reassuring the sense and sensations that they should have never come. Who were they to accept an invitation from Four Emissary Owls who were Warrior Messengers Owls of the Sacred Woven Mat of Rule and Authority? Sure they were thrilled to be invited to play but they didnʼt know what that meant for knowing something like that was something they just did not know thus could not say. No, they should have never left home but how could they have known what they did know without being initiated into the Noble Realm such as this that was the Noble Council House of the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. One would feel a deep sense of belonging in place like this if only one had participated in a Long Performance and Long Recitation of an Ancient Ancestral Myth that told about People and Place like this in order to feel at home with a deep sense of belonging by coming to a the very same kind of place told about through the Ancient Word of the Ancient Account that tells about the Noble Council House of Xibʼalbʼa and the Nawal Ajawabʼ that ruled and reigned from atop their Jaguar Throne set upon the Sacred Woven Mats of the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. The Ballcourt they played back at their Mountain Place in Canyon Country was known as their ʼjomʼ which was the burial ground of their Ancestors that made them so very much at home playing above where the ʼskull and bonesʼ of their Ancestors rested as the decomposed into the earth from which they had come such a long time ago.

body:
The Noble World of a Civilization requires that Young Men prepare themselves through Rites of Passage in which the Young are initiated by their Elders who as Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word become Masters of Ceremony who are Masters of Ritual of Transformation and Change. This is what was needed to be able to whole heartedly accept an invitation to play-ball and perform dance far from home knowing how to speak and act among others by being able to expect the tests, trials, and ordeals such as those found here in Popol Wuj. Like this little trick that is always part of the ʼNaming of Namesʼ of all Noble Lords of all Noble Council House of Noble Lords and Rulers, just like here.

It took Rituals of Initiation to accept invitation to go to places far away to play music and perform ritual and tell stories like this one here where one feels at home in the world; the world in which one belongs; the world where one belongs because of the mythic narratives that provide one with a deep sense of belonging in the world. This is the Sacred Story known as the Myth of the Maize People that is told here in the Popol Wuj. The Myth of the Maize People that is the Mesoamerican Masterpiece of Mythopoetic Genius that is being Translated and Interpreted here through the Nawal Genius of Change and Transformation that is comes to fruition in the Art of Translation and the Art of Interpretation known as Hermeneutics that flowers and fruits on each and every page of this interpretive play with myth and metaphor .

It was then that those of Xibʼalbʼa spoke and those who spoke were Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame:

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Utz bʼa la! Very well then, at least you arrived with us here, at least you have come down here below to spend time with us here in Xibʼalbʼa. Tomorrow you will have an opportunity to put into play your hip yokes-kibʼateʼ, your arm guards-ipachqʼabʼ,” they said, when they spoke to Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu there in the Council House of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa. It was then that the Lords spoke when they said: “Just take a seat then, just take a seat there upon our bench,” they were told. It was just a searing slab of stone; the seat that the Lords offered Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu was just a burning bench.

It was then that they were burnt badly; they were just seared sadly there atop that blistering bench; they just did what little they could do to move about atop that scorching seat that had been offered to them so graciously; but they just got no relief, no relief at all atop that blazing bench of Xibʼalbʼa.

When it was too much for them to bear they no longer pretended and shot straight up off the bench and into the air; for truly their bottoms were burnt and burnt badly from sitting on that burning bench of those ever-so-clever and oh so friendly Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

The flat cooking stone that was placed there with such care was just to defeat Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who now just wanted one thing only which was to get up and out of there.

Truly, these cunning trickster Lords of Xibʼalbʼa could not get enough of their deceptive ways of mocking their invited guests to make fools of those from up above on the earth who had never felt disgrace until now for they had never, ever lost face like this before; for they had never been caused humiliation through deception and trickery like this that was so cunningly crafted now to cause nothing but shame through the Noble Lords clever ʼbait and switchʼ tactics where they offered ʼone thingʼ to then give something completely ʼotherʼ to those Fathers who are Brothers. Enough was enough or was it?

body:
Brothers who were Fathers who were Ballplayers who had enough of this kind of playing around that had nothing to do with a rubberball and its bouncing around or the rubberball game where their shouting and screaming had never been as loud as the laughter of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. Their endless laughing that was the loudest laughter that the Junajpu Brothers had ever heard. Laughter that left them in tatters; they were shattered from so much laughter caused by their antics trying to stay seated on that damn bench of Xibʼalbʼa.

And that was all that seemed to matter at least to those of Xibʼalbʼa who almost ʼsoiledʼ themselves from so much laughing at the way the burnt the butts on that burning bench theyʼd been so warmly and willingly offered; and, offered as eagerly and excitedly as anything they had ever been offered. Why bother leaving home if this was what happened to those who were offered a chance to play ball when in reality you were summons to be the butt of one joke after another; jokes that were always on you who had so enthusiastically accepted this invitation with such innocent naiveté thinking while hoping it were some great honor. What a joke!

And so it was that the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa burst out laughing until they fell on the floor where they fell to pieces because they couldnʼt take it anymore; they just came undone from laughing so hard as they now laughed at the entrance hall of their Council House: Popobʼal Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They cramped up inside from their endless laughing so that it seemed they would die from the hysteric affect of endless laughter. They just writhed in pain from laughing about their laughter; their blood; their bones seized up as they laughed and laughed at anything and everything their hilarious guests came up with by the way they acted as if nothing had happened; pretending that their bottoms hadnʼt just sat on a frying pan. No matter what they did it caused the Lords laughter so they summonsed their attendants to take those two jokers out of there. “Xa jix chi ja! Just go on now; just go ahead and get yourself out of the house here so you can enter Dark House. Go then, go receive each your pine-torch and cigar there before your sleeping quarters,” they were told.

It was then that the two arrived at Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Ja-House of Darkness. Just darkness alone filled this first house of tests and trials of Xibʼalbʼa.

So then they arrived there at Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Ja; darkness alone was the inside of that House; House of Darkness its name: Qʼeqʼuma Ja. Right away those of Xibʼalbʼa gathered together their thoughts; and so those Noble Lords expressed those thoughts; those thoughts that they were thinking: “Letʼs just sacrifice them tomorrow, it is just a bad sign, it is just a wrong sort of indication; it is a mistake-labʼe-a nettle road as they say; a road of nettles is what it is. It is just a mistaken path that we have taken.”

“So let them be sacrificed straightaway with our gaming implement-ri qetzʼabʼal-our gaming equipment with which we play our game; the game we play and the way we play it. The way we play in our way of playing on our court with our ball in our way of play; which is to say the way we play our game of sacrifice.”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Let it be our way of ball-playing and our ball-playing equipment-ri qachaajibʼal-that brings them a quick and sudden death. Let us just sacrifice them tomorrow; yes, yes, let us do this,” said those of Xibʼalbʼa speaking there together in council with one another. Indeed their ball-kichaaj-was just a Round Obsidian Stone-Kʼolokʼik Cha- with its own name; the name of their Round Obsidian Stone; just as the name of their game was known as Saqi Toqʼ that was spoken of as the White Flint Knife. And so it was known that the White Flint Knife of Sacrifice was the name of their sacrificial ball, the name of their sacrificial game; so that the name of the game they played was known as Sacrifice-Pus that comes to fruition through the ʼsudden-opening of sacrifice-xaraxojʼ that is performed with the sacred knife known as Saqi Toqʼ or White Flint Knife of Sacrifice.

Ri chaaj: the rubberball; the rubberball game; the rubberball ballcourt; the play; and the name of their game which was sacrifice. Sacrifice was the game played by those who were the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

Now you know who the Xibʼalbʼan Lords are and why they issued a summons for Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu come along and descend with the Owls to come play ball with the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa on their Ballcourt name Pusbʼal Chaaj: Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice or Ballcourt Place of Ballcourt Sacrifice.

Their ball was just a razor sharp Obsidian Blade; the game of sacrifice they played was just played with a polished stone blade. And so it was that their blade made of obsidian is what would be put in play the very next day.

For their ball, the ball of Xibʼalbʼa, was just a round obsidian ball-kʼolokʼik cha that was just a sharpened, polished blade of sacrifice-xa juqʼul kichaaj; and so the ballgame of sacrifice they played and the sacrificial way they played; as well as the sacrificial ball with which they played their game of sacrifice was as a sacrificial ball of ballgame sacrifice that was a polished blade which was a sharpened blade that was a well-honed, sharp, and shiny obsidian blade of sacrifice-xa juqʼul kichaaj.

body:
This razor sharp obsidian blade of sacrifice was their ball and their game and their way of playing their game which made their game just the game of ball-game sacrifice.

And so then they entered there where they were led. Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu entered Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Ja.

It was there they were given their torches-kichäj of burning torch-pine. This is to say they were given their burning torches-kichäj tzijom-torches that were burning since Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame had lit them to then give them to their porters-yaʼol to then pass them on to Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

And so it was that they were given burning cigars to accompany their burning torches; each of them-Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu-was given a lit cigar that was already burning-kisikʼ tzijom chik-when the porters-yaʼol were given them already lit by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

These already lit cigars and already lit torches were delivered to Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu, already burning!

This then was when they were there in Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Jaʼ crouched down in a squat-chʼokochʼoj-sitting on their heels in the dark; they were just left waiting in a crouch-chʼokochʼoj like war captives; like slaves; like captives bound and captured for ritual sacrifice. This all happened when they were there in Dark House: Qʼeqʼuma Ja.

This was when the porters-yaʼol came in to give Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu their torches-kichäj along with their cigars-kisik; torches and cigars that were already lit when they were given to them already burning.

Truly, their torch-pine torches were ablaze-kajuljut; their torches were burning resplendent when the porters entered there; the porters-yaʼol entered Dark House with their torch-pine torches lit; they were just burning; they were just ablaze.

Each was given a cigar; each of their cigars was lit; they were burning; the torches they were given were just like their cigars that were given to them burning; they were ablaze-kajuljut.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Then they-the porters of the torches and cigars-spoke for the Lords: “ʼtomorrow you must return them just as they are given to you as a burning torch, as a burning cigar; so return them just as you have received them. Donʼt finish them off; donʼt burn them down because you must return them just as they have been given to you; we will gather them from you just as you have received them from us; so return them to us at Dawn just as we give them to you now,ʼ say the Lords to say to you,” they were told, those known and named Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. So then they were defeated-xechʼakataj for those two who were left in Dark House were finished off; for it was they who finished off their burning torch-pine torches-chäj just as they finished off their burning cigars-sik.

And so it was that the two of them there were finished off; they were just finished off when they went before the Lords to give them what was theirs; when they went to give their cigars and torches that were finished off; for they burned no more.

The tobacco cigars; the torch-pine torches they were all burnt up before the dawning of the sun; before the sun rose at dawn the two who were in Dark House; those who were in Qʼequma Ja were done; they were finished off.

This was when daybreak broke after watching and waiting for Dawn all night long from within Dark House where the dark of nightʼs darkness is so very dark there in that Dark House that was a House of Darkness-Qʼeqʼuma Ja.

Houses of Ordeal; Houses of Xibʼalbʼa Qʼeqʼuma Ja; Xuxulim Ja; Tew Ja; Bʼalami Ja;

Sotzʼi Ja; Chayim Ja Qʼaqʼa Ja

Thick with trials is Xibʼalbʼa-tzatz utijobʼal Xibʼalbʼa thick with tests-tzatz utijobʼal many are the trials found there in Xibʼalbʼa where one encounters heaps of tests-kʼya molaj chi tijobʼal that must be confronted as the countless tests that are trials; trials that are always an ordeal because truly one was called to overcome the great many trials and tests encountered there in Xibʼalbʼa. The first one is Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Ja; just darkness alone is there inside that dark, Dark House.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The second house of ordeal then is Xuxulim Ja-Shivering House-Xuxulim Ja is its name this Cold House-Tew Ja thick with cold is it there inside that House; unbearable cold drafts of icy winds blow there; intolerable whistling gusts of penetrating cold are met there; fearful freezing frosty gales drive through the inside of that frigid, icy abode of Shivering House-Xuxulim Ja; Tew Ja-Cold House is its name.

The third place of trials, the thirds place of tests goes by the name of Jaguar House-Bʼalami Ja as it is named-chuchʼaxik-as it is spoken of. Nothing but Bʼalam-Jaguar are there inside, tangled up, squeezed together in a rage, furious are they, closed up are the Jaguar-Bʼalam in the House of Jaguar-Bʼalami Ja; Jaguar House is its name. Sotzʼi Ja is the name of the fourth house of tests-ukaj utijobʼal-the fourth house of trials, the fourth house of ordeal. Just Bats alone are in that house: Xa utukel Sotzʼ kʼo upam chi Ja.

They screech-ketzitzotik; they shriek-ketzʼitilajik; as they bat their wings and fly around in a great swarm in their Bat House: Sotzʼi Ja.

In that Sotzʼi Ja that is a House of Bats is where Bats alone flitter as they flutter all about in that closed-up, closed-off House of Bats where Bats and Bats alone are sealed-off inside that place where Bats, and only Bats, are kept inside; just held tight to fly around and around all night; so that all-night long the Bats of the House of Bats flitter-flutter all about.

There is no place for them go; no place for them to hang, no place for them to hide; there is no way for them to get outside and fly away because those Bats are trapped inside so there is no way for them to get out; those Bats of Bat House never fly out.

body:
These are just the flittering and fluttering Bats of Bat House whose obsidian- blade fangs grow out of their obsidian-blade snouts. There is no way for those Bats to escape that Bat House that is a House of Bats-Sotzʼi Ja with no way for anyone to ever get out! The fifth house then is Chayim Ja-Obsidian Blade House is its name. There are just perfectly ordered and perfectly aligned Obsidian Blades there inside Obsidian Blade House where the Obsidian Blades all look the same. They just resound off of one another as their sound resonates off the walls where they grind and grate as they scratch and scrape across the floor of the Obsidian Blade House; Chayim Ja: House of Obsidian Blades.

Many were the tests, many were the trials of Xibʼalbʼa, but Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu never ever even entered inside there; they never entered within these houses of tests and trials that we entered here only by naming their names so that when their names were named they came to life in the Imaginal Realm of the Mythic Imagination. This is how the Houses of Xibʼalbʼa came to life and while we will enter each and everyone to spend the night to survive the ordeal that it is to enter there inside the Houses of Ordeal; Houses of Xibʼalbʼa that are named here: Qʼeqʼuma Ja; Xuxulim Ja; Tew Ja; Bʼalami Ja; Sotzʼi Ja; Chayim Ja and Qʼaqʼa Ja that is the House of Fire that is not named here.

Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu Powers of Death; Powers of Life White Flint Knife of Death; Blood the Water of Life

It was then that Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu presented themselves there before Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; this was when they came forth before the Lords in the calm, dim light of Dawn: apanoq saqnatanoj. “Where are my cigars of rolled tobacco? Where are my torch-pine torches that were left with you in the House of Dark-Qʼeqʼuma Ja-Dark House?” they were asked. “We finished them off-xqakʼiso, at Ajaw-you Oh Lord, you Oh Father, At Ajaw,” they answered.

“Utz bʼa la! Very well then!” said Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame.

body:
“So today then, your days are finished; your destiny has come to its end; now you shall die; now you shall be forgotten; your ancestral line; your ancestral lineage shall be cut-off at the trunk,” said Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame.

“Wakamik bʼa la xkʼis iqʼij, kixkamik, kixsachik, xkixqaqʼupix!”

“Here we shall end your days; here your existence shall be finished: for you will be sacrificed; your face lost, your countenance gone, vanished once and for all,” said Ajaw Jun Kame, Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kame-Lord One Death, Lord Seven Death.

Then they were sacrificed; then they were buried there in the place known as Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice-Pusbʼal Chaaj ubʼi xemuq wi.

Pusbʼal Chaaj is the name of the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Sacrifice is where they were buried; for it was they, Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who were buried there beside Pusbʼal Chaaj.

They decapitated Jun Junajpu so that only his body-nimal; the body of Jun Junajpu, the Elder Brother-nimal was buried with the body of his Younger Brother which meant that just the body-nimal of the Older Brother-unimal-was buried with his Younger Brother-uchaqʼ.

They were buried beside Pusbʼal Chaaj there in Xibʼalbʼa.

“Go place his skull in the fork of the tree planted there; the tree that is standing there beside the road,” said Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame: “Chiyaʼ ujolom xol cheʼ ri tikil pa bʼeʼ.” When they placed the skull in the fork of the tree was when the tree instantly began fruiting; never had the tree fruited before the skull of Jun Junajpu had been placed in the fork of the branches of this barren tree.

And this is why the calabash gourd-tzima is called the way it is today because of the skull of Jun Junajpu as it is said; the calabash gourd is spoken of as ujolom Jun Junajpu; the skull-head-jolom of Jun Junajpu.

When they placed the skull in the fork of the tree, the tree fruited forth completely filling the limbs with perfectly round skull-like gourds-tzima that were a marvel to look upon.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Let us provide you with another translation of this bewildering mythopoetic passage of Maya-Mesoamerican Mythos in order that you might enjoy its wonder and awe in a slightly different way. For the Calabash Tree is a true marvel to gaze upon for the way its gourd-fruit sprout out like perfectly round skull from its branches and trunk. The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa told Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu that their ʼlineage would be cut-off at the trunkʼ which is truly terrible sort of devastating thing to say to the founder of a lineage.

This is why this tree is seen as being so miraculous when the head-skull-jolom sprouts forth from its ʼtrunkʼ: the ʼtrunkʼ of the Calabash Tree. Again we have a ʼgreat reversalʼ coming to life instantly when the ʼtzima-ujolomʼ of Jun Junajpu sprouts forth from this once barren tree ʼstanding-upʼ beside the ballcourt. The tree that is ʼplantedʼ there that now is filled with the ʼreplacements-kʼexelʼ of Jun Junajpu whose descendants literally cover the entire tree: it branches and limbs but perhaps most importantly its trunk! Letʼs translate this again to listen to the way this metaphor for rebirth and the eternal return of the Divine Ancestor of the Maize People comes to life.

This is when they went over to place the skull of Jun Junajpu in fork of the tree; they placed it there in its limbs; that is when the tree sprouted forth with fruit; fruit sprang forth from the branches and trunk of this most marvelous tree; this tree that had never given fruit before.

This tree, with its branches and limbs, now sprouted forth with perfectly round gourds that looked exactly like skulls; and it was these gourd-skulls known as tzima-jolom that now completely covered the treeʼs limbs and branches; branches and limbs of a tree that had never given fruit before.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This Calabash Tree had never given fruit until the head-ujolom-the skull of Jun Junajpu was placed in the fork of the branches of this barren tree. The tree that is known as the Tzima, the Calabash, el Moro, el Guacal, the Gourd Tree; the gourd known as the skull of Jun Junajpu; the skull-jolom-head of Jun Junajpu; the Ancient One Blowgun Hunter; this fruit that is a gourd spoken of in Maya Kʼicheʼ as ujolom Jun Junajpu.

Then it was they, Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame were left astonished; for it was they who were left shocked with wonder and awe by what they saw: the skull-like fruit that now sprout forth this once barren tree; the Calabash whose branches were now filled with fruit; fruit that were gourds that bloomed as they blossomed forth from the branches of this marvelous tree; branches filled with perfectly round gourds that left them bewildered.

Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame were astounded by this gourd treeʼs skull-shaped fruit, for perfectly round was its appearance, there was no way of seeing which was the original skull of Jun Junajpu and which were all the other skull-like; gourd-like heads of fruit that grew upon the limbs and branches of this most astonishing; this most astounding tree whose fruit looked exactly alike the skull-head-jolom of Jun Junajpu. For truly the skull of Jun Junajpu looked exactly like the calabash gourd known as tzima; the perfectly round skull-like fruit that now covered this tree.

All of Xibʼalbʼa saw its perfection when they came to look upon it and marvel at the perfectly round shape of its fruit that now hung as gourd-skulls from its limbs and branches of this most mystifying tree.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so they came to behold its Nawal essence for truly amazing was the identical shape of the perfectly round fruit of this enchanting tree; this tree that now revealed itself before those of Xibʼalbʼa; those of Xibʼalbʼa who came to marvel at this tree and its magical transforming nature-kʼojeʼik that now appeared before them there-xux chi kikʼux-as its magical transforming essence sprouted forth before their hearts; as its nawal nature sprouted out before their souls as the natural marvel and ancestral astonishment that this Nawal Tree expressed to all those who had gathered there to gaze upon who were filled with wonder and filled with awe for what they felt and what they saw.

The magical way its round skull-like gourds sprouted forth from its trunk and limbs caused both astonishment and admiration in those who now gazed upon the perfect roundness of the great quantity of fruit that sprouted out of this tree now filled with gourds-tzel; this Gourd Tree; this Tzima as it is spoken of by all today.

The Tzima that now sprang forth with perfectly round fruit; the exact same size; the exact same shape of the head of Jun Junajpu; its fruit, its face, the mirrored reflections of one another; just perfect replacements of the twins; skull-gourd; face-fruit; fruit-bowl; the face of the gourd or uwach tzel of the calabash; the skull- jolom-head of Jun Junajpu that emerged from the trunk and branches when the head of Jun Junajpu was planted in the fork of the barren tree that stood beside the ballcourt; the Ballcourt of Xibʼalbʼa; their Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice known as Pusbʼal Chaaj.

Truly marvelous was its nature; its wondrous nature; the magical, miraculous nature of this tree filled with gourds that sprouted forth before them there. Magnificent then was its nature because of what it had created when the skull-jolom-head of Jun Junajpu was placed in its branches. It was just its bringing forth of skull-like fruit that led those of Xibʼalbʼa to talk amongst one another about this astonishing Calabash Tree-Tzima saying:

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“It wouldnʼt be good if one was to pick its fruit. And it also would not be so good if one were to enter there; there beneath its fruiting limbs; the fruiting limbs and branches of this Calabash tree with all its skull-like gourds; its perfectly round fruit,” they said; holding themselves back from doing so, keeping themselves from getting too close to where the tree grew; and, it grew where it stood; and, where its stood was where it was planted to stand-up straight there ʼbesideʼ the Ballcourt of Sacrifice: Pusbʼal Chaaj.

By now it was impossible to tell the difference between the skull and the head and the gourd from the original skull of Jun Junajpu for the fruit of the tree were just one and the same as all the other round gourds that sprouted forth from the limbs, from the branches, from the trunk of this most magical tree spoken of as a ʼtzima or guacalʼ as it is known today.

All those of Xibʼalbʼa talked about its marvelous nature and how fruitful that marvelous nature was. That is how a Young Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj came to hear of it; when she heard her Father speak of it; when her Father told of its wondrous ways.

Now we will tell of her arrival there to where the tree grew beside the ballcourt along the road; we will tell of the arrival of IxKikʼ there where the skull of Jun Junajpu was placed in the branches of the Tzima; in the limbs of the Calabash Tree. IxKikʼ Transforming Moon Maiden One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj Moon Maiden-Blood Woman Changing Moon Maiden Transforming Month-Transforming Moon The Story of the One Maiden She of the Rubberball-She of the Changing Moon She of Flowing Blood-She of Flowing Sap She of Flowing Incense-She of Flowing Rubber One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj-IxKikʼ-She of the Blood Moon

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Kuchumakikʼ-Blood Gatherer; Father of the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj Jun Qʼapoj-One Maiden IxKikʼ-Daughter of Blood Gatherer Kuchumaʼ Kikʼ-Gatherer of Blood-Rubber-Sap The naming of the Father of the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj is named as One Lord-One Noble-Jun Ajaw. Jun Ajaw: One Lord; One Noble Lord is a name that tells us he is a Lord of Xibʼalbʼa; Lord of Darkness; Lord of the Night; Lord of Disease. The Father of IxKikʼ is named Kuchumakikʼ known as Blood Gatherer or Gatherer of Blood, Gatherer of Rubber he is the Lord- Qajaw-Father of the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj: IxKikʼ.

This then is the announcement that announces the noble entrance of IxKikʼ the Moon Maiden who will become the Moon Mother who is the Moon Goddess known as Saq Ixik the White Woman; Sacred Woman in the Codex Dresden.

And for those Nawal Descendants with the eyes to see; the ears to hear; the touch to feel; the taste to savor; the scent to smell; the intuition to perceive; and, the genius to know this introduction of the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj IxKikʼ announces the forming and shaping of this new lineage of the Maize People.

These Peopleʼs lineage is founded in the Boys of IxKikʼ who are the Sons of IxKikʼ known as uKʼajolabʼ IxKikʼ: JunAjPu, IxBʼalamKiej. These are those who are brought into being on the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea through the twin nature of their Nawal lineage; a Nawal lineage formed and shaped by their complementary and cooperative sense of duality that balances and harmonizes itself through the its transformations of Life and Death; the movement of Night and Day; the ʼwalking and knowingʼ of the Sun and Moon.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the harmonizing of the dual natures of the Divine Ancestors of Maize People-Ixim Winaq that comes about through the Hero Twins being ʼtwinned from withinʼ which is to say they are the Grandsons of their Lowland Grandfather of the Rubber Groves of the Limestone Cave World that is the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa; and, the Highlands of Jun Junajpu who comes from the lineage of the Face of the Earth of Xpiyakok and IxMuqane. Both of whom are intimately bound to Maize since IxMuqane embodies the sowing of maize and Xpiyakok embodies the sprouting-out of Maize from the hard carapace of the tortoise that is the Face of the Earth.

The Sons of IxKikʼ known and named Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are the Hero Twin Grandsons of their Lowland Grandfather: Kuchumakikʼ or Gatherer of Blood, Gatherer of Rubber who is the Father-Ajaw of IxKikʼ or She of the Blood; She of the Rubber; She of the Moon; the Moon that changes and transforms to grow full in order to pull on the sap that runs like blood from the cuts that are scored on the trunk of the Rubber Trees known as Kikʼ or Blood. These trees are tapped for their sap that is their blood that runs thick or then depending on the state and condition of the Moon. This is how IxKikʼ is directly related to the Moon-Ikʼ and Blood-Kikʼ that runs with the Moon.

One Maiden; Jun Qʼapoj Moon Maiden; Moon Mother IxKikʼ, this One Maiden, will transform the world forever more as she stands up to her oppressors, to then defeat them through her ingenuity before climbing up and out of Xibʼalbʼa to give birth to her twin sons on the Face of the Earth.

Without many words we are guided by the Owls up and out of the initiatory darkness of the underworld. This One Maiden; this Jun Qʼapoj named IxKikʼ climbs up through the underworld to rise out of the archetypal hole of ʼemergenceʼ to sprout forth like a maize plant on the Face of the Earth.

Could this have been some sort of rite of initiation of Older Maidens on their path of becoming Young Women? Did Young Women enter a dark, cool place to gather their blood to be burnt over a fire with other flowers, herbs, tree sap, and incense?

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Who knows but this text suggest such a possibility through this metaphor of IxKikʼ creating a replica of her own heart to outsmart the Lords of Death. By escaping the Lords of Death and their determination to sacrifice her because she bears the rebirth of Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu in her womb; the Lords of Death want to terminate the pregnancy of IxKikʼ by ending her life through sacrifice. But this One Maiden of One Father-One Lord-Jun Ajaw ascends onto the Face of the Earth to begin a New Life in a New World with New Obstacles and New Ordeals. This archetypal image of IxKikʼ ʼrising-upʼ out of the Underworld is the very same as Jun Junajpu rising up out of the Tortoise Shell Face of the Earth seen on the Resurrection Plate of the Boston Fine Arts Museum. They are both embodiments of the People of Maize: one is the Mother Goddess of Maize; and on is the Father Maize God while both are embodiments of the Mother-Father of the Maize People who will life eternal lives that never end.

Certainly, this story tells of a rite of initiation that speaks to us through the symbolic language of mythic metaphor as this mythic Moon Maiden and Blood Gatherer have taken up the path of emergence to become the mythic Moon Mother and Goddess of Maize who will bring forth a Magical Harvest, as you will soon come to see, hear, and experience in this imaginal realm of myth-making created through these mythic words and their mythic metaphors. This is to say the One Maiden of Maize will sprout out of the underworld darkness of death to begin her new life there on the Face of the Earth at first as a faint memory of the dim light that illuminates the Sky-Earth at the dawn of a new day, new life known as ʼsaqnatanojʼ to then enter the bright light in a completely new life of renewal and regeneration; a life filled with hope and possibility to live the out the ʼbright life-saq kʼaslem, winaqirem-peoplingʼ on the Face of the Earth.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This ʼsaq kʼaslem, winaqiremʼ or ʼbright life of creation and the peoplingʼ of the Face of the Earth is the direction the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj has taken. It is vitally important the reader understands this as IxKikʼ emerges from Xibʼalbʼa stronger than ever before for she has ʼentered the wordʼ by finding her own voice and creative expression as a maker of incense known as AjQʼol or a Person of Tree Resin which is and was a very important traditional art of ʼincense- makingʼ in the Maya-Mesoamerican world. The text says, ʼXukiyaʼ aqʼanoq chi jul chuwi ulew-she grew up and out through the hole to climb up and out onto the earthʼ as it is said-chuchʼaxik. The text will continue to take on this metaphor of plant growth that speaks of the growth of the Moon Maiden become Moon Mother in this story of the Maize People that says: as IxKikʼ grows so grow her Boys who will sprout forth on the Mountainside as two heads of maize sprouting forth from the ʼcane-bodyʼ of their Mother: IxKikʼ So now IxKikʼ is no longer in the earth for she is above the earth just like the moon when rising full in the East when she comes up, out, above, and onto the Earth at the ʼComing Out Place of the Sunʼ known as the Relebʼal Qʼij.

The Full Moon rises full like IxKikʼ rises up and out of the hole at the Coming Out Place of the Sun with her full body completely filled out, completely round with two magical boys that will live their lives as one in and out of the womb. The Moon acts like the Sun by rising as the Full Moon exactly where the Sun rises ʼfullʼ at his Coming Out Place of the Sun in the East on the Eastern Horizon where the hole of emergence opens for the Sun and Moon to rise up and out of the watery underworld there in the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico. So here oneʼs imagination must fill out the suggestions and intimations of female initiation. Feminine genius comes to life here as this Young Woman overcomes the life and death ordeal she must face because of her own curiosity to know the unknown in the ʼface of the fruitʼ that hangs from the tree.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
IxKikʼ stands up for herself when challenged by her father and his generation of rulers. It is only her inventive and ingenious imagination that enables her to use the creative powers of making, modeling, and molding a solution for the life and death predicament she must overcome.

And so it comes to be that IxKikʼ overcomes death as she outwits the rigid authority embodied in the ʼblindʼ authoritarian ways of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. She first deceives to then defeat these insensitive and closed minded Lords of Noble Rule and Authority and she accomplishes this through the use of her powerful intuitive capacities of a Nawal Ancestors; magical capacities of transformation that are alive and well in the ingenious powers flowing through her innovative fingers and imaginative hands.

This is the genius of Young Women and their creative powers that this ancient account speaks of in beautiful metaphorical speech and acts of creativity in search of transforming the world of the Sky-Earth. Truly, IxKikʼ is a trickster heroine herself and not ʼjustʼ the mother of trickster heroes.

IxKikʼs genius, her transformative magic comes from her nawal powers that enable her to imagine ingenious solutions to her apparently disastrous and deadly dilemma. By doing so she originates the ceremonial use of incense created from nodules of tree sap. After all, her name is IxKikʼ which means She of Blood, She of Sap, She of the Red Tree, She of Rubber, She of the Ballcourt-Sacrifice, She of the Moon, She of the Month, She of Menstruation.

Is it not the ancestral office of IxKikʼ the gathering of menstrual blood that is suggested in her gathering of the coagulated blood that forms her replica heart of sacrifice? Is not the first menstrual blood of a young woman the occasion to reflect upon a womanʼs change of heart in a womanʼs life that is indelibly ʼmarkedʼ by the first blood of menstruation? This text does not speak of this in direct ways but it certainly suggests that IxKikʼ must gather her blood in order to mold and model a replacement heart she can use to defeat those of her fatherʼs generation; and, she succeeds at her task splendidly.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
IxKikʼ is a Blood Gatherer by tradition for she is a Gatherer of Blood; it is her cargo, her burden, her office this gathering of blood, sap, rubber and dye for she is a gatherer by name and lineage. IxKikʼ knows nothing of the ways of maize as the lineage of Jun Junajpu does. This is because IxKikʼ comes from the lineage of archetypal Hunter-Gatherer of the Age or Sun before the Maize People which some say is the Age of the Gourd Head People: Tzuy-Wa Winaq.

One might say that as a Moon Maiden, Moon Mother IxKikʼ is a primordial being of the night and its darkness the time of hunters; meanwhile, the day and its sun light is the time of the gatherers, IxKikʼ has both of these elemental forces of nature pumping through her heart causing her blood to pulse within lunar tides as a being who is of the Moon and Night. She emerges out of the Underworld carrying within her womb the Sun and Moon of the Age-Sun-Era-Epoca of the Maize People and their Night and Day; Light and Darkness. It is her power as the Ancestral Moon that ʼpullsʼ sap-blood from those beings that bleed, maidens very much included.

But it will take maize beings who see themselves as the direct descendants of IxKikʼ and Jun Junajpu to continue her ancestral work of ʼgathering and collectingʼ the thick aromatic resins that flow so slow from torch-pine and copal trees as well as the thick latex tapped from the rubber tree. Was this work of collecting the gourds of the scoured and tapped trees the work of maidens in the past? IxKikʼ embodies the power of transformation as she incarnates the continual movement and act of becoming other than that which one just was and is because IxKikʼ embodies the ways of the Moon and her constantly changing and transforming ways.

For IxKikʼ is just like the Moon for whom she is named, for she is the Female Lord or Ixoq Ajaw or Chuch-Qajaw known as the Mother-Father of all the dripping drops of sap, blood, resin, water, and rubber that transform the world once they are gathered together as the essence of Heart of the Earth; Heart of the Sky.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It is this essence that is being gathered up to then be used as powerful forces of nature that in turn transform the Sky-Earth by calling upon Jun Raqan Kaqulja; Chʼipi Kaqulja; Raxa Kaqulja to form the clouds and shape the winds to bring the fog, mist, drizzle, and rain that is called upon through the use of the many forms of incense and rubber that Mesoamericans used to communicate with their Kabʼawil who gathered up their strength to deliver abundance and prosperity to their people who lived there on the Face of the Earth. Oh, before we move up onto the Face of the Earth, it might be helpful to know that rubber was burnt in rituals of sacrifice to create black clouds of smoke to conjure up the dark black clouds that brought down the sustaining rains of the Maize People and their continual effort to bring forth their sacred sustenance: Maize.

Here then begins the Story of One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj

Here then begins the story of One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj, the Daughter of the One Lord-Jun Ajaw, his name is Blood Gatherer; Kuchumakikʼ ubʼi; Blood Gatherer is his name: Kuchuma-Gatherer, Kikʼ-Blood, Rubber, Sap.

This was when Jun Qʼapoj, the One Maiden heard of it, the Daughter of one of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa, Blood Gatherer-Kuchumakikʼ is the name of this Lord of Xibʼalbʼa, Father of IxKikʼ the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj and it was her Father that told her about the perfectly round fruit of the once barren tree that stood beside the ballcourt. When this One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj heard what was said about the fruit of the tree she became curious and thus excited by something that could be as marvelous as this enchanted tree could be; and so she began to think upon the marvelous way those of Xibʼalbʼa spoke about the Gourd Tree-Tzima.

This then was when she contemplated going to see this tree; an astounding tree, an astonishing tree covered in gourds; gourds as round as round could be.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
When its story-the story of this gourd tree-was told to this One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj by her very own Father she was left amazed; she was left astonished by all that he had to say about this tree full of skull-like gourds; a tree that grew full with these skull-like fruit that were gourds that looked like skulls; a tree that had sprung to life the moment the skull-head-jolom had been place in the fork of the tree for all to see.

“Wouldnʼt it be good to go see this tree that everyone talks and tells of; wouldnʼt it be good to go know what kind of fruit it really is? Is its fruit as sweet as they say it is; as sweet as I have heard it to be?” IxKikʼ said, curious to visit the tree after all she had heard people say as they spoke of this enchanted gourd-headed skull tree of Jun Junajpu. So then she went off by herself; and, before long she arrived there beneath where the tree was planted; there beneath where the tree grew; there where the tree stood where it was planted to grow where it stood beside Pusbʼal Chaaj; beside the Place of Ballcourt Sacrifice is where it stood planted to grow forth just as wondrous as one could imagine an enchanted tree to be; a tree covered with perfectly round gourds; a tree full of perfectly spherical skull-like fruit; a gourd tree that was a skull tree for all to see. “Jiyaʼ! Indeed! What sort of fruit is this that sprouts forth from the limbs of this tree?”

“Where does fruit such as this come; where does fruit such as this grow; fruit that sprouts forth from the arms and trunk of this tree that stands here planted beside the Ballcourt of Xibʼalbʼa known as Pusbʼal Chaaj?” “Could it be that its fruit is so very sweet?” asked the Maiden; ri Qʼapoj. “Would I die? Would I be lost; would I disappear? Would I end up ʼdead and goneʼ if I were to ʼpickʼ just one of its fruit?”

“Ma kikam taj, ma kisach taj, la kʼi ta xchinchʼup junoq?” Xchaʼ kʼu ri Qʼapoj.

“Would I be a ʼgonerʼ if I took just one of them? Could it be? Would I really be ʼdone-forʼ if I were to ʼcutʼ just one of them?” asked the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoja.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This was when it spoke, the bone-ri bʼaq that was stuck there in the fork of the tree; this was when the bone spoke, when the bone spoke to the Maiden:

“What do you want with just a bone; what do you want with just a round thing-kʼolokʼoxinaq-that sprouts forth from the branches of a tree-chu qʼabʼ taq cheʼ?” Asked the skull-jolom-head of Jun Junajpu when it spoke to the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj who stood there beneath its branches; there below its arms; beneath its branches-chu qʼabʼ, that is to say ʼbeneath the strength-chuqʼabʼ of the Calabash Tree: IxKikʼ is her name; the name of Jun Qʼapoj; One Maiden. “Ma karayij? Do you really want it?” “Do you long for it?” “Is this then ʼnotʼ what you desire?” asked the bone speaking from the limb of the tree. “Kanurayij! I do want it!” “Certainly I long for it!” “I do desire it; I do!” said the One Maiden when she spoke to the skull in the fork of the tree, the ʼround bone-like thing-kʼolokʼoxinaqʼ the sprouted out from its limbs; that shot forth from its branches; that sprang from its arms. “Utz bʼa la! So then, just extend your right hand so that I might see it,” said the Bone-Bʼaq; spoke the Skull-Jolom. “We! Yes! Yes, Indeed!” said then the One Maiden as she extended her right hand up and out towards the face of the bone-xulikibʼa aqʼanoq uwikiqabʼ chuwach bʼaq.

It was then when a shot-jun pitz-was made; a shot of spittle; a shot of saliva came shooting forth from the bone-uchubʼ bʼaq to land in the middle of the maidenʼs hand; in the palm of her hand; the palm of the maidenʼs right hand that stood extended before the bone-uwikiqabʼ chuwach baqʼ.

Kʼate kʼut chi pitz kabʼan uchubʼ baq; ta xpetik taqal kʼut puqabʼ qʼapoj.

Then, when she looked at the palm of her hand, looking so close as she could, she saw that there was nothing left of the boneʼs saliva. It was then that the bone, the skull spoke to her there; there beneath the tree. “Just a sign-xa retal I have given you with my spittle-nuchubʼ, my saliva- nukʼaxaj. My head, my skull-nujolom is no longer useful, itʼs just bone; no longer is it covered with flesh,” said Jun Junajpu before he continued to say what had to be said.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“It is just like the head of a Great Lord-Nim Ajaw: only the flesh-uchʼaqʼ alone gives them their fine appearance. Then when they die, the people are frightened by their bones-their skeletons-their skulls,” said the ʼround-bone-like thing-kʼolokʼoxinaqʼ that spoke to the One Maiden who listened intently to the fleshless Bone who spoke to IxKikʼ from the limb of the tree by saying:

“Similar to this and just like that are the descendants; the descendants of a Great Lord-Nim Ajaw are a Noble Lordʼs children; they are just like his saliva, his spittle; a Noble Lordʼs children embody as they ensoul the essence of the Noble Lord no matter if they are the sons of a ʼWise One-Naʼol-Sage or the sons of a Speaker-AjUchan-an Orator. They never disappear even after they are gone they will always be fulfilled; for they will never be forgotten even when their days are complete,” said Jun Junajpu.

“They will never be cut-off at the trunk; they will never be cut-off from their lineage; nor will the memory of a Noble Lords be lost; nor will be lost the remembrance of a Man of Knowledge-Achij Naʼol nor shall be lost the Man of Wisdom or the Speaker-AjUchan-the Orator, the Master of the Ancient Word: AjUchan. Their children will remain; their daughters, their sons shall remain as their replacements-kʼexel and so they will be remembered in the fine features of their descendants; the refined remembrance of their face with its mouth, its nose, and its eyes. So be it! Ta chuxoq! May it be so! May it come to pass!” said the Skull-Head speaking as the Wise Orator that he was. “Ta chuxoq! So be it! This is just what I have done with you. That is why you must climb up onto the Face of the Earth. You will not die; you will enter the word. Mawi kakamik, katok pa tzij.”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
You will not die; you will enter the ancestral way of the ancestral word. You will not die; you will enter the ancestral tradition. You will not die; you will enter the traditional way of the traditional life known to all as those who ʼenter the word-katok pa tzij-enter the wayʼ. You will not die: you will enter then the word; enter the way; enter the truth; enter the tradition found in the Ancient Word. Mawi kakamik: katok pa tzij!”

This is what they said; those who were Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who were the Fathers of the Boys; the Fathers of the Sons Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej- Kikʼajolabʼ Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej “Ta chuxoq! So be it! May it be so!” said the skull; said the head of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. These were the Fathers of the Boys; the Fathers of the Sons-Kikʼajolabʼ Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej this is the story of their generation; their being engendered; their being begot; their conception; their creation. It was just their genius-kinaʼoj that did it; it was just the word-utzij of Jun Raqan, Chʼipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja; the Heart of the Sky, Ukʼuʼx Kaj that brought it forth in and upon the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew; the Mountain-Plain; Juyub- Taqʼaj; the Face of the Earth; Uwach Ulew. Straight away her boys-ral, her sons-ukʼajol, her sprouts-ral began to grow as they sprouted forth-xwinaqir ral-as her boys, as her sprouts, as her sons that grew within her womb from the spittle-shot of pitz that landed in the palm of her right hand; the pitz-shot from the chubʼ-spittle that was the kʼaxaj-saliva that brought about the sprouting forth-kiwinaqirik of her two sons; the creation- kiwinaqirik of her two boys: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

So then the Maiden arrived home and after her completing six months, she was ʼknown-nawachil-divinedʼ by her Father; for truly this One Maiden was seen in order to be found out by her Father Blood-Gatherer who was the One Noble; the One Lord known as Blood Gatherer spoken of as Kuchumakikʼ-Gatherer of Blood, the name of her Father-Uqajaw.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It was only then that her Father remembered his Daughter when he saw that she was with child. This is to say: he remembered telling his Daughter the mysterious story about the marvelous tree that bore such magical fruit on its bountiful boughs and abundant branches. He remembered the prohibition regarding the picking of that skull-like fruit and the way the Lords One Death; Seven Death forbid all those of Xibʼalbʼa from entering beneath the Enchanted treeʼs alluring limbs and beguiling branches; limbs and branches covered with gourds filled with infinite encanto and endless enchantment. This was when the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa gathered together in council to gather together their thoughts-kinaʼoj with Blood Gatherer-Kuchumakikʼ who gathered together with Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame to say what they had to say in order to do what they had to do.

It was Blood Gatherer-Kuchumakikʼ who spoke first to One Death-Jun Kame while he addressed the Noble Lords who gathered to talk this situation over:

“You, Oh Lords, Ix Ajawab, my daughter is with child. It is just her knee scraping-ujoxbʼal-just her lust that makes it so,” said Blood Gatherer-Kuchuma Kikʼ when he presented himself before the Ajawabʼ Xibʼalbʼa, the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa; Lords of Disease of Xibʼalbʼa who were the Chief Judges, the Chief Magistrates who were the Makers of Justice. It was they who were the final measure of the truth-qʼatabʼal tzij-those who weighed the word to make the necessary judgments and traditional punishments.

“Utz bʼa la, Very well then, interrogate her, just chisel it out of her-chakʼoto uchiʼ-just carve it out of her mouth, if she doesnʼt confess then sacrifice her; take her far away from here to then sacrifice her,” said Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame when they spoke.

“Utz bʼa la, very well you Beloved Lords; you Revered Lords-Alaq Ajawabʼ,” said Kuchuma Kikʼ when he took leave of the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were those who weighed the word; they who gave the final judgment; they who were the final measure of the ancient word, ancient way. For there was no greater authority; nor was there a higher judge than that of the Lords Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame with whom fell the Sacred Burden-Patan of the Supreme Rule of the Noble Lordsʼ through whom came the noble ruling and decision; judgment and punishment of the Noble Lordsʼ final word. So then he, Kuchuma Kikʼ went over there where IxKikʼ was waiting; waiting to be questioned as the Daughter of a Lord-Rumeʼal Ajaw. A Daughter of a Lord who was required to tell who the Father of the Child was that she carried in her womb. For the womb of a Daughter of a Lord was where the Descendants were borne and begot as the Replacements of the Ancestors of each and every lineage.

The Mother and Father of these Noble Lineages were of great importance because they formed and shaped the ʼnext generationʼ of the Noble Lineage. Thus those who were the Mothers and Fathers; Bearers and Begetters were held responsible for bringing their Ancestors back to life as Bearer and Begetter of the next generation of Divine Daughters and Sacred Sons of Nobles Mothers and Noble Fathers.

Thus it was only proper to ask who was the Father ʼfaceʼ that was going to be on ʼfaceʼ of the child that IxKikʼ now carried within her womb to know what ʼFruitʼ was borne and begot within her womb. This is just as the Noble Council of Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa told him to do; and so he who was Ajaw Kuchuma Kikʼ; Lord Blood Gatherer did what he was ordered to do by asking the question that he was required to ask of his Daughter; his Daughter IxKikʼ; the Daughter of a Lord; Ajaw Kuchuma Kikʼ.

This was when he questioned his Daughter: “Who then is the father of the child that you bear within your womb, you, my Daughter?”

“Child? What child? There is no child that you speak of, you my Father; you my Lord. There is no man whose face I know; for I know not the ʼface-uwachʼ of a manʼs ʼfruit-uwach,” she said when she answered her father, Kuchuma Kikʼ known as Blood Gatherer.

“Maja bʼi wal, lal nuqajaw; maja bʼi achij wetaʼm uwach,” xchaʼ kʼut.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“There is no child, you my dear father; there is no fruit; no face of a man that I know,” she said then.

“Fine then, it is true that you really are one for skinning knees, you knee- skinner, you; you, scrapper of knees!” said Kuchumakikʼ.

“Utz bʼa la! Utz bʼa la, qitzij wi chi at joxol cheʼk.

Fine then, itʼs true-qitzij-you really are one for skinning knees-at joxol cheʼk!” said Blood Gatherer-Kuchumakikʼ.

“Just go sacrifice her, you Messenger-Warriors of the Noble Reed Mat of the Council House-Ix AjPop Achij. Bring her heart back in your sacrificial gourd bowl-tzel-so the Lords may take it up in their hands to ʼroll it over; turn it aboutʼ so that it may be examined this very day,” he told the Owls-ri Tukur.

“Chipusu Ix AjPop Achij. Chikʼamaʼ uloq ri ukʼux chi upam tzel. Chikikʼololej Ajawabʼ wakamik,” xeʼuchax kʼut ri Tukur.

There were four of them when they flew off. They gathered-up the gourd bowl of sacrifice-kitikʼem ri tzel ta xebʼek in their hands when they flew-up and away on their sacred burden of ritual sacrifice given to them to complete by the end of the day by those who were the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

They cradled the maiden in their arms-kichʼelem ri qʼapoj, just as they bore their White Flint Blade of Sacrifice-Saqi Tokʼ Pusbʼal Re-known as their Sharp- edged White Flint Knife of Sacrifice.

This is when IxKikʼ spoke to the Owls with whom she was raised as a child of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“You canʼt make good on those that are your orders to sacrifice me, you oh Messengers-Ix Samajel-you oh Workers cannot bring to completion those instructions to kill me because there is no me ʼskinning my kneesʼ; mawi nujoxbʼal. What is mine; that which is within me; does not come from lustful acts- joxbʼal of sexual longing and desire. Not me, itʼs just not my way, not ever, I am too clever for something as careless as that known as ʼthe scrapping and skinning of oneʼs knees,” she said, taking the chance; making the opportunity to speak her truth. “That which grows within me is just a making and manifestation of itself, it is just my going to marvel-numayjaj at the skull-head-jolom of Jun Junajpu; there on the skull-head-gourd tree known as the Tzima; the Calabash tree that stands growing beside the Ballcourt of Xibʼalbʼa-Pusbʼal Chaaj-Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice.” “Donʼt do it! Kʼekʼe ta kʼut! Donʼt you do it! Detain yourselves; restrain yourselves! Donʼt sacrifice me, you, oh, Envoy Owls-Ix Tukur-you, oh, Emissary Owls; fine companions of mine that you are; You, oh, Workers-Ix Samajel-You, oh, Messengers of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa,” said the Maiden when she spoke in her own defense; knowing what was the ʼrightʼ way to be taken up; and, what was wrong way to be ʼleftʼ behind. “What then should we place there as a replica, a replacement of your heart- ukʼexel riʼ kʼux-a replacement, replica of your heart?”

“Did your Father not tell us: ʼBring back her heart; that the Lords might turn it over in their hands making sure that it does not fall so that they might come to see what it is made of; so that they might roll it about so that they can make certain it is made like all the others. Quickly then, bring it back in the gourd bowl of sacrifice-pa tzel; just collect her heart, just gather it up by gathering it together at the bottom of your Gourd Bowl of Sacrifice-pa Tzel,ʼ” said the Owls speaking for their Lords.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were the words; this was the message given to the Owl Messengers of Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame; their Lords and Masters who sent the Owls out as their loyal messenger; their trusted emissaries to comply and complete this deadly duty; their sacrificial obligation that was now their burden to bear; this cruel cargo that was left for them to bring to completion as the ritual sacrifice demanded of them by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

So then ri Tukur-the Owls spoke before the gathering silence of IxKikʼ who listened rapt to what the Owls had to say:

“Is that which we said not what we were told? What then will we place at the bottom of the gourd bowl? What we want is that you should not be killed; what we desire for you is that you might then escape death; what we wish for you is that you should not be sacrificed so that you might live on the Face of the Earth,” said then the Emissary Owls; Envoys of Xibʼalbʼa-ri Tukur, AjSamajel Xibʼalbʼa; the Messenger Workers Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; who wanted the heart of IxKikʼ by the end of the day!

They wanted to roll IxKikʼs heart around in their hands to then bounce it off the walls and bounce it off the floor to see how it jumped up off the ground to watch as it bounced and bounced to then bounce a little more.

Then they would ʼthrow it down into playʼ by throwing it on their sacrificial pyre at the end of the day to watch how it burned while taking in its sweet scent which was the traditional way to divine what could be divined from this burning heart of IxKik as it roasted in their sacrificial fire which was Deathʼs way of revealing its ancient, ancestral divinatory powers.

What would this sacrifice tell the Lords of Death who lived to practice sacrifice down deep in Xibʼalbʼa where Sacrificial Death was practiced by the Lords of Death who willful and wantonly spilt the sacrificial blood of life to feed the eternal appetite and desire of the Dead who thirsted and hungered for the heart and soul of Living; the hearts and blood sacrifice, the very Essence of Life that were sacrificed under the Sun of Day and the Stars at Night with Xibʼalbʼaʼs White Flint Knife: Saqi Toqʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Utz bʼa la! That ʼthisʼ heart not be theirs! So be it! Ta chuxoq!” said the One Maiden; Jun Qʼapoja.

“Utz bʼa la! Mawi kech ri ukʼuʼxʼ ta chuxoq!” And then IxKikʼ continued, when she spoke, speaking directly to the Owls-ri Tukur: “May this place here no longer be your abode; may this place no longer be your home; and, that you no longer force people to die a sacrificial death. So that in the future those who are true knee-scraping-fornicators be yours to sacrifice as you see fit.”

“May it come to be that Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame receive sacrificial offerings of the sacrificial blood given as the blood offered through self-sacrifice.

And may they be given offerings of sacrifice of that which is known as the ʼfoamy head of incense-jolomax-artificial blood formed from the head-jolom of those who make incenseʼ which is just the fuzzy head of foam known as jolomax that comes from the creation of incense. May this ʼfalse-bloodʼ be given to Xibʼalbʼa as that which is known as jolomax; jolomax the fuzzy head of foam that forms on top of boiling clay pot used to cook-up the gathered tree sap that is tapped from the Red Incense Tree-Kaq Cheʼ known as ʼSangre de Dragon or Blood of Dragon Tree” known as the Tree Croton sanguifluus is a tree with a red sap similar to blood in color and viscosity. So you will see that IxKikʼ knows what she is talking about as she continued to specify how sacrifice would be apportioned to the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa as those would go from receiving sacrifice to those who would be sacrificed. This is the reversal carried out here by IxKikʼ that will be continued through the clever craft and cunning creativity of her sons the Hero Twins: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

body:
“It is only this left-over fuzzy head of foam known as jolomax that forms as the head-jolom of the cooked-up tree resin of the collected sap of the ʼdragon treeʼ; the gathered blood of incense shall be theirs. Only these shall be the substitute sacrificial offerings of ʼblood sacrificeʼ and ʼfalse blood-jolomaxʼ that shall be given to the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa as burnt offerings of sacrifice; nothing more than this; not one more heart shall be sacrificed to them; those known as Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame.”

“May it come to be! Ta chuxoq! May this too come to pass!” “May it only be the resin and sap of incense that smokes and smolders upon the sacrificial embers of the sacrificial fire set before them, in this way no longer will it be human hearts that will be offered up as burnt sacrificial offerings; offerings of sacrifice offered up to them on the burning embers of their altars of sacrifice: Ta chuxoq! So be it!” pronounced IxKikʼ as she affirmed her nawal powers of transformation that beat in her heart; the heart that was hers and not that which was to be sacrificed on the sacrificial fires of heart and blood sacrifice that blazed on the altars of sacrifice of Xibʼalbʼa. So be it!

“Just use the resin that flows from the cuts that scores the bark, the husk, the face of trees-uwach cheʼ to tap the ʼresinʼ or ʼsapʼ that is the blood-kikʼ of these red incense trees; red incense gathered up as sap-ukikʼ cheʼ for the making incense,” said the One Maiden: IxKikʼ. And so it was that this One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj made it so she could gather up the sticky red sap that oozed from the Red Tree-Kaq Cheʼ that she had tapped to cause it to flow with the pull of the moon that soon filled her ritual gourd bowl- tzel.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This red sap of incense soon coagulated as the thick red resin that clotted into a perfectly spherical shape at the bottom of the sacrificial gourd-tzel; the bowl of sacrifice-tzel. The coagulated sap of the Red Tree-Kaq Cheʼ just rounded itself out by taking the form of the sacrificial vessel in which it was gathered together as the precious red blood of IxKikʼ. This is to say the Jolomax Kikʼ the substitute blood gathered from the foamy suds of the fuzzy head that came from the cooking up of gathered blood; collected sap of the Kaq Cheʼ. This is how the ʼlook-a-like heartʼ of IxKikʼ was formed and shaped; molded and modeled by the Moon Maiden: IxKikʼ. This was when the replacement heart, the substitute heart-ukʼexel ukʼux-was then squeezed together tight; and when it was squeezed tight the sap of the Red Tree ran like blood: kikʼ.

This was the work of IxKikʼ who was ʼShe of Sapʼ, ʼShe of Rubberʼ, ʼShe of Bloodʼ, ʼShe of the Changing, Transforming Moonʼ, who collected all that was to be gathered from all that flowed forth from the strength of the Moon and flowed thick through the pull of the Moon. This was her domain; this was what was hers in life for she was a ʼgathererʼ as the Daughter of the Lord Blood Gatherer: Kuchuma-Kikʼ.

This would make her a powerful presence on the Face of the Earth where she would be called to ʼgather-up the harvestʼ of her peopleʼs sacred sustenance; a gathering of sacred sustenance that was shown as a ʼsign and symbolʼ of her being and becoming the ancestral embodiment of her destiny as the Moon Mother of the Sacred Sons, Divine Twins of the Maize People; for indeed, IxKikʼ held the ancestral heroes of the Maize People in her Full Womb as the embodiment of the Full Moon: IxKikʼ.

body:
This will be the sacred harvest held within the Full Moon-like Full Womb of IxKikʼ; the Full Moon-Full Womb of IxKikʼ is embodied by her ʼone big harvest net-jun nima kʼatʼ that will be filled with maize from within by placing ʼhead after head-mazorca after mazorcaʼ in the ʼOne Big Netʼ given to her by IxMuqane to fill in order to ʼfed those who must be fedʼ which is to say the Grandsons of IxMuqane. These ʼOne Big Net of Maizeʼ becomes the form and shape of the Full Womb-Full Moon of IxKikʼ where she carries Hero Twins; the Maize Twins: Jun Ajpu Ixbʼalamkej. These are those Divine Twins who in the Classic Period were the sons of the Lord of Maize Jun Ixim whoʼs sons were known as Jun Ajaw, Yax Bʼalam; Jun Ixim who is similar if not the exact same as the Post-Classic Kʼicheʼ Maize Deity known to you well as Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu who take different names for their different aspects. These Maize Deities Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu are succeeded by their sons Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who are known as Jun Ajaw, Yax Bʼalam the Classic Maya equivalents of Jun Ajpu Ixbʼalamkej or so it seems to be seen like this in a variety of Resurrection Scene of the Maize Deity: Jun Ixim the Lord of Sacred Sustenance who takes the form of Maize-Ixim and Cacao-Ixim!

So this then was when the blood-red-sap of the bleeding Red Tree-Kaq Cheʼ was made to flow as imitation blood; imitation blood that IxKikʼ gathered together there in the gourd bowl of sacrifice; the gourd bowl of sacrifice brought by the Owls to gather-up the ʼheartʼ of IxKikʼ.

The blood, the sap of the Red Tree-Kaq Cheʼ flowed forth just like blood; just like the substitute blood of the One Maiden who was there forming and shaping; molding and modeling her own substitute heart from the clotted, coagulated essence of substitute blood she used to form and shape; mold and model; craft and create a replacement heart; a replacement heart that was a replica heart; the replacement, replica heart of IxKikʼ: ukʼexel ukʼuʼx IxKikʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Resplendent crimson-red blood was gathered in the gourd bowl-tzel. So then the tree was named by the Maiden, Red Cochineal-Chʼuʼj Kaq Cheʼ-as it is called- chuchaʼxik: Sangre de Dragón is its name Croton sanguifluus.

It was just because its bright blood-red sap formed a fuzzy head of sudsy foam known as a head or jolom when incense-makers and dye-makers cooked-up the blood-red sap into a refined blood-red dye. This then was when they came to call the ʼsuds or foamʼ that rose to the top of their work of decoction: jolomax. This jolomax is that which they called ʼfalse blood-sangre falsa-kikʼ jolomaxʼ-as it is said-chuchaʼxik.

There is confusion in the original text or perhaps it was created somewhere down the line since the text speaks of two red colored dyes that are spoken of here. One, the Chʼuʼj Kaq Cheʼ or the Pungent Red Tree that is the red worm castings of the Red Cochineal from the Nopal Cactus and the other is the red sap that flows the scoring and tapping of the Dragon Tree so that the ʼred blood-like sapʼ flows from the Croton sanguifluus or Sangre de Dragón in the ʼgourd- tzelʼ that were attached to the Red Tree to ʼtapʼ the ʼsapʼ in order to ʼgather the bloodʼ from these magical trees.

And then IxKikʼ spoke to the Tukur-Owls giving them their final instructions upon her taking leave of them and the underworld cave realm of Xibʼalbʼa.

This was just before this One Maiden climbed up and out through the opening between the two worlds; this is the opening that led up and out of the cave realm of the underworld to then move out from below to climb-up above the watery limestone caverns.

This is what IxKikʼ must do. IxKikʼ must rise-up from darkness of Xibʼalbʼa down below to pass up and out into the light to then make her way across the Face of the Earth guided and protected by the Sun, Moon, and Stars.

body:
Was this an Rite of Passage that was a Ritual of Initiation of Young Women o sea; that is to say: Qʼapoja-Maidens or Daughters of their Fathers who are going to become Daughters of the Mothers of the Husbands that in English are known as Mother-in-Law and Daughter-in-Law that shows the vast difference in human relationships. There is no warmth or affection in the name ʼMother-in-Lawʼ and ʼDaughter-in-Lawʼ but this relationship of IxKikʼ is transforming in this direction. For she is escaping from the realm of her Father in order to be saved in realm of the Mother of Jun Junajpu as IxKikʼ will soon take up the road that leads to IxMuqane who is the Mother of Jun Junajpu. This is Initiation; this is Transformation; this is the essence of the Popol Wuj as it reveals the Traditional World of the Maya and the human relationship lived through in this Imaginal Realm of Myth that the mirrored reflection of the Cultural and Natural Realm of Maya Culture and Mesoamerican Civilization.

But before IxKikʼ could escape from Xibʼalbʼa she had to take leave of her allies the Owls, ri Tukur. This then is when IxKikʼ said what she said to the Owls: ri Tukur. This is when she provides them with ancestral advice that is cultural counsel to help them understand where they are going and what they should expect up there above on the Face of the Earth.

“Over there, on the other side, all of you will be well loved; there on the Face of the Earth you will find what is yours; you will find your luck and lot in life which will be the destiny that is yours and yours alone known to us as our Genius; our Nawal; our Way of Being and Becoming in the World of the Sky-Earth; Kaj- Ulew,” said IxKikʼ to the Owls-ri Tukur.

This then was when the Owls took leave of IxKikʼ giving her their last and final instruction before guiding and protecting her until she was safely up and out of the cavernous cave world of Xibʼalbʼa.
