source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Utz bʼa la, At Qʼapoj! Very well now, you our beloved Maiden! Xqabʼe bʼa-Letʼs get ourselves going now Qawabʼa aqʼanoq-We will guide you to where you can climb up above Xa qabʼin apanoq- We must continue on our way Oj na qayaʼixtaj uwa- We must go to present the sustenance; the sap Ukʼexewach akʼux- of your substitute heart, your look-a-like heart chi kiwach Ajawabʼ-before the face, before the presence of the Lords Xechaʼ kʼut ri Samajel-Said then the Messenger-Workers of the Noble Lords Aj Samajel-Ajawabʼ Xibʼalbʼa-Messengers of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa “Utz bʼa la! At Qʼapoj! Very well then, you oh beloved Maiden!

“We are going to guide you to where you must continue up and then on your own; up and up upon the steep stairs that lead above. You must keep going by yourself from there, while we return to leave the imitation image of your substitute heart, a replica of your maiden heart. For it is us who must just present your falsified heart before the Lords; before the Rulers of Xibʼalbʼa,” said then the Ajsamajel Xibʼalbʼa; ri Tukur, the Messenger-Workers of Xibʼalbʼa; the Owls.

When they arrived there before the Lords-Ajawabʼ it was those very same Lords who were there waiting with great expectation; great anticipation for the Owlsʼ to return with their sacrificial bowl; for it was all of Xibʼalbʼa who was waiting there for the return of the Owls-ri Tukur with their sacrificial bowl-tzel- ritual gourd that held the heart of this One Maiden: Jun Qʼapoj.

“Is it not finished?” asked then Jun Kame-One Death. “Indeed, it is finished, you, oh Lord. Here then is her heart at the bottom of the ritual bowl-tzel; her heart is here at the bottom of this sacrificial gourd-tzel,” said the Tukur. “Utz bʼa la! Letʼs have a look then,” said Jun Kame.

So then the Great Lord took up her heart in his hands; resplendent red liquid dripped just like blood when he held it up; the perfect sacrificial gift; the very thing they had longed for; those who were the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. “Stir up the coals, make them good and hot so we can set this on the burning embers of our sacrificial fire,” said Jun Kame.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so they roasted the Maidenʼs heart atop the red-hot coals that burnt warm and bright where the sweet smelling scent of their sacrificial fire rose up to fill the Lords of Xibʼalbʼaʼ with pure contentment. So they all rose-up to take in the pleasant perfumed fragrance of the sacrificial offering. This was when they leaned over the fire to take in its alluring aroma. Truly pleasing did they find the sweet smelling smoke of the sacrificial offering given on behalf of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

This was when the Lords all stood to lean in over the fire; the sweet smelling smoke left them spellbound in a sort of trance and this is when the Owls and Maiden took their chance. The Messenger-Warriors showed the way up by guiding the Maiden up and away to make their escape through the hole and on their way up onto the Earth and into the light. This then was when the Owls took flight to then turn around to go back down to where the Lords were still standing around their sacrificial altar where the magical incense continued to smoke on the hot coals of the sacrificial fire.

This is how the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were defeated by the One Maiden; IxKikʼ was her name she left them all completely blinded.

An Alternative Mythopoetic Translation

Those of Xibʼalbʼa found their sacrificial offering to give off a most pleasant sort of sweet seductive scent; truly they found it to be so very, very pleasant; they had never smelt anything quite like it so they leaned in further to take in more of the precious smoke that now filled the hall.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Before long they found themselves leaning in and over their incense altar to take in the precious perfume that rose from their sacrificial fire; the sweet, sweet scent of this sacrificial offering now filled the room with its makers magical intention which was to ease their minds and calm their desires; a beautiful bouquet rose-up from the coals to quickly captivate the focus of the Lordsʼ underworld souls; the souls of those who were the Noble Lords and Rulers of Xibʼalbʼa those who were there now leaning in over their altar and the perfumed clouds of smoke that rose to leave them completely enchanted; a bit bemused even befuddled because they who no longer knew where they were or what they had been summoned there the way they were huddled around their altar completely entranced by the mesmerizing smoke rising up from their fire. And so they bent forward a little bit more as they were pulled ever closer to the potent perfection of this sweet smelling smoke that now took them in, to then place those of Xibʼalbʼa under its spell-binding control, all of them quite content to have gathered together in their Council House to resolve this problem once and for all by weighing the truth and measuring the word to now be completely calmed and settled by the pleasing scent of this most intoxicating fragrance. This then was when the Owls, the Tukur flew off to guide the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj on her path of escape; her flight that took her up through the hole that led out onto the Earth. She never looked back as she made here get away to never see or be seen again by those who were the Noble Lords and Rulers of Xibʼalbʼa.

The Great Reversal: Day and Night; Sun and Moon; Light and Dark Rain and Wind; Flood and Drought; Image and Reflection The Great Reversal is now sown in IxKikʼ who is a curious Moon Maiden very much at home in the world. Her ʼround full-moon wombʼ will bring the Sowing and Dawning closer to fruition through her Sons who will face the tests, trials, and ordeals Houses of Xibʼalbʼa with their life and death struggles that the Boys of IxKikʼ will overcome and by doing so will change the Sky-Earth once and for all.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These Sons, who are Boys, are Twins who are Heroes that will bring forth the powers of life and death; growth and decay; coming to light and falling into darkness; hiding in the shadows and shining in the light. This is the eternal challenge that is the never-ending competition between the light and the darkness; the Sun of Day versus the Moon, Stars, Constellation, and Planets of Night; the Windy Dryness of Day and Dewy Wetness of Night; the Malevolent Trickster Powers of Night and Benevolent Trickster Powers of Day all of which come together in the Boys, the Sons, the Twins where they will be engendered in Underworld Darkness of the Cold Lunar Night that is brought together with the Over-world Light and Warmth of the Sun of Day; IxKikʼ and Jun Junajpu; bear and beget the Nawal Essence of the Sacred Sons of the Sun and Divine Daughters of the Moon; Saqil Al, Saqil Kʼajol.

Above and below; night and day; light and darkness; rubber and blood; maize and humans; underworld and over-world; life and death; generative powers of creation-renewal and the deadly powers of death and disappearance; destruction and demise that are now brought together as the essence of the Sun and Moon; Day and Night; Life and Death to form and shape these ʼSupernaturalʼ Nawal Winaq-the Hero Twins-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. These are those who will transform the Face of the Earth by Peopling-Winaqarisajxik-Populating it with Maize People after the Boys transform into the Sun and Moon at the Dawning of the Sun and the Moon with their special sort of Era and Age that is peculiar to the Maize People. Remember that rubber smells like death and decay so that those who work with rubber are those who were associated with the transformative powers of death which, is to say the Nawal Essence of Death. This is the Nawal essence of Kuchuma Kikʼ, Blood Gatherer and his daughter IxKikʼ if indeed they were seen as Rubber Gatherers as an aspect of being Blood Gatherers.

Remember that the Maya sense of Death is experienced as a very lively sort of alive and bouncy kind of Death filled with the lively sort of trickster spirit and soul of the Lords of Death.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were those who were embodied in the Noble Lords and Rulers of the Lowland Rubber Groves where gourds where used to collect the rubber from the ʼtappedʼ rubber trees; rubber that smells just like the rotting flesh of death for rubber has a sweet-sour deathly smell; the smell of death.

This then is how the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were defeated by the One Maiden- Jun Qʼapoj whose curious craft and cunning creativity brought forth a most enchanting incense known as ʼjolomax kikʼ that clouded the eyes of Xibʼalbʼa leaving their vision misty by the powers of her nawal enchantment; which is to say all of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa-Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa were blinded by this One Maiden- rumal qʼapoj xemoywachixik konojel.

Eternal Kernel of Maize

For it was they, the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa, who could not see for they were left for a time without ʼsightʼ or any other form of outer vision through the clever craft and cunning creation of this most magical maiden, IxKikʼ. IxKikʼ who fooled her foe with her curious concoction brought forth through her inspired imagination that led to her ingenious invention. For this One Maiden formed and shaped the enchanting incense from her own ingenious imagination; her own magical powers of transformation all of which brought about the defeat and destruction of those who wished to defeat and destroy her. This inventive work of crafted enchantment and creative cunning was something that the Owls knew would lead to the defeat of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa by the One Maiden: IxKikʼ.

body: For it was she, IxKikʼ who blinded the lords and rulers of Xibʼalbʼa through her deceptive trickster powers that caused the disturbance and disruption that led to a deadly sort of blinding distraction and beguiling deception that allowed the One Maiden to escape. The escape of IxKikʼ was of such vast importance because of its long-term purpose and intention to bring about the decisive downfall of Age of Xibʼalbʼa and the rise of the Sun and birth of the Age of the Maize People through IxKikʼ and Jun Junajpu who as the Mother-Father; Bearer-Begetter; Conceiver and Engender of the Maize Twins. The powers of transformation and change of IxKikʼ as Moon Maiden and the powers of authenticity of Jun Junajpu with his good-willed and good-natured ways of the Earth Nature of the Face of the Earth come together to create the Hero Twins.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: All of which is just a masterful foreshadowing of what will to come to be through Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who are Twin Sons; Twin Heads of Maize of the Moon Goddess: IxKikʼ. IxKikʼ whoʼs nawal powers of change and transformation will bring about a New Way of Life under a New Sun in a New Age of the Maize People on the Face of the Earth. This is the ancestral prowess IxKikʼ who as the Daughter of the Lord Kuchumakikʼ wants to see her Moon Lineage of Gatherers of Sap conquer their space of the Face of the Earth through the death, destruction, and disappearance of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. These are battles that are taking place in lineage wars in the Maya Culture and Mesoamerican Civilization. And this must be seen. We have come to the heart of the Popol Wuj. We have come to the revelation of the soul of the Maize People where the struggle for life and death is preparing for its great confrontation between the Lords of Life and the Lords of Death; the Lords of Light and the Lords of Darkness are going to come to a climax from which a New Order will be brought forth as these Trickster Twins redefine sacrifice and the way sacrifice will be given which means they will ʼreapportionʼ sacrifice on the Face of the Earth. This is saying everything in a world where sacrifice created divine order on the Face of the Earth where the giving of sacrifice by the Providers and Sustainers is the most important aspect of the reciprocal relationship in the reciprocal giving and taking of sacrifice. Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej will reapportion sacrifice on the Face of the Earth and Xibʼalbʼa wonʼt receive the hearts and bloods of human sacrifice as they did before. This is the foreshadowing of that massive change and transformation of ritual sacrifice that is one of the principal themes of Popol Wuj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Those who carry-out these massive changes on behalf of the Heart of the Sky are the Sons of IxKikʼ who are her Boys; who are her Twins that she now bears within her womb; Sons who continue to develop and grow as she make her ascent as the Moon Goddess from deep down below. IxKikʼ escapes the deadly grip and intentions of Jun Kame in order to emerge on the Face of the Earth undeterred by Xibʼalbʼaʼs desire to offer-up her heart on their sacrificial fire to sever any hope of her Sons ever coming to life.

The Lords of Death want to ʼcut-offʼ the possibility of the Lords of Maize ever getting the opportunity to sprout forth on the mountainside as the replacements-kʼexel of their Fatherʼs Sky-Earth Maize Lineage of the Maize People; the Sky-Earth Lineage of the Pueblo of Maize People that is borne within the heart and soul Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. This is the heart and soul passed on to their Sons; their Boys; their Twins the Maize Twins; the Maize Twins: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who will become the Sun and Moon of the Age of the Maize People; as the Sun of the Pueblo of Maize; as the Moon of the Pueblo of Maize. This is the story told at Teotihuacan where ʼHumans become Divineʼ which is precisely what is going on here in Popol Wuj. Those who follow the ʼsaqetalʼ by taking up the ʼperfect pathʼ of the Divine Ancestors will become the Divine Ancestors.

This is the very premise upon which the Popol Wuj was written where the Mother- Fathers of the Ancient Word had to leave behind a ʼSacred Pathʼ that their Descendants could follow to become Divine Ancestors; the Replacements of the Divine Ancestors; the Descendants of Divine Ancestors. This is what IxKikʼ is fighting for here; this is what this Translator and Interpreter is fighting for as well. Why else would I dedicate my entire life to bring forth such a ʼperfect pathʼ to be followed by those who will come in the future to follow this work? Why, why do something as difficult as this has been for me?

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This Eternal Kernel of Maize is as Nawal in its changing and transforming ways as are the Nawal Days of the changing, transforming Sun; and, the Nawal Nights of the changing, transforming Moon. The Nawal Sun; the Nawal Moon; the Nawal Days; the Nawal Nights that are as eternal in their ancient ancestral ways as is the Eternal Kernel of Maize with its Nawal Way of Being and Becoming by living and dying; rising and falling; changing and transforming. These are the everlasting ways of life, death, and rebirth of the Eternal Kernel of Maize that dies to be reborn again and again in an infinite everlasting life that knows no end as seed that is like a skull; an ancestral skull that is like an ancestral seed whose ancestral essence sprouts back to life through the ʼspittle-like ancestral essenceʼ of Jun Junajpu who ʼspitsʼ his one ʼpitzʼ in the palm of IxKikʼs right hand. This is the metaphor the Maya will live by as the Ixim Winaq and live by still in a world where Maize is engendered by the ʼspittleʼ that falls from the Sky that fall as dew that was once known as ʼitzʼ… This is where the Fathers of the Boys, the Sons, the Twins had come from and where IxKikʼ was now ʼheadedʼ as she ʼreturned homeʼ with her ancestral harvest of Engendered Sons ripening in her womb; Sons she conceived; Sons she desired to bring the World of the Sky-Earth as the Replacements-Kʼexel; as the Descendants-Ketal-Kitzijel who are born in the World to take their Fathersʼ place on the Face of the Earth. Fathers who are known as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; Fathers who engender their Sons Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej by shooting a ʼpitzʼ in the palm of the upturned hand of their Mother: IxKikʼ. These are Sons who change and transform in the womb of their Mother IxKikʼ where they come to fruition a Maize Twins; Maize Twins who are carried in the ʼOne Big Carrying-Netʼ of IxKikʼ who is see now as a Moon Mother with as Full Womb that is seen as the Full Moon of the Moon Maiden who changing and transforming into being and becoming the Moon Mother.

body: This is very important. I have repeated the telling of this metaphor in order that you see this metaphor; in order that you understand this metaphor; in order that you feel this metaphor; in order that you might come to know this metaphor to live this metaphor in a world where humans find meaning through the metaphors they live by. This mythic metaphor played out here in this myth of the Moon Mother and the Maize Twins is a major Maya metaphor that was lived out and is lived out still in the World of the Sky-Earth where the People of Maize live by this mythic metaphor of the Maize Twins that make them the Maize People that the Maya and always will be as long as they see themselves as Ixim Winaq. This is a major mythic metaphor in a world where we humans live by the metaphors that make us and this is why we must ʼenter the wordʼ of this mythic metaphor so that we might come to live by the metaphors such as this mythic metaphor of the Maize Twins; their Mother; and, their Father.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
What are the meaningful metaphors we live by to live a meaningful life? Human beings want nothing more in life than to live a meaningful life and in order to live a meaningful life they must live that life through meaningful metaphors that give meaning to their lives. This is what is happening here. IxKikʼ and Jun Junajpu; Junajpu and Ixbʼalamkej provide meaning in our lives through their Myth of the Maize People told here; a meaning myth made up of meaningful metaphors to provide our lives with deep meaning through our entering into their ʼimaginal realmʼ where we experience their deeply meaningful lives. Meaningful lives to be deeply meaningful must be deeply informed by the experience of transcendence that comes through the imagination of eternity through the experience of the transcendent soul that experiences transcendence through the experience life, death, and rebirth of the eternal seed of maize; the emerald green seed; the jade green been that embody to ensoul the ancestral soul in the face of the Descendant that is the ʼspitting imageʼ of the Divine Ancestor. Let us take up this myth with the idea of forming and shaping a meaningful life by entering the Ancient Word to enter the Imaginal Realm of Myth and Metaphor where beauty and meaning are found in the ethical good and mythic truth found in the aesthetic beauty of this masterful myth of the Maize People: Ixim Winaq.

These were the Sons who would come to defeat and destroy the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa by bringing about their decline that would precipitate in their downfall that eventually would lead to their death; destruction; and demise.

The story of the death, destruction, and demise of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa will be told when its time to be told comes to fruition; but until then we will continue to tell the story of this One Maiden; Jun Qʼapoj: IxKikʼ is her name.

And so it was that the Mother of One Monkey, One Artisan was there at home when a Woman-Ixoq arrived; this Woman was known as IxKikʼ; Moon Maiden; Moon Mother by name.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Are kʼute kʼo ri u-Chuch Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen ta xul ri Ixoq; IxKikʼ ubʼi. When the Woman-ri Ixoq IxKikʼ arrived there with the Mother-Chuch of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; One Monkey, One Artisan she bore her beloved sons within her womb; it wouldnʼt be long now before the birth of her begotten sons who were her engendered sons of Jun JunAjPu: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej were their names.

When the Woman-ri Ixoq arrived there with the Grandmother-ri Atiʼt; this then was when the Woman spoke; when she spoke then with the Grandmother-ri Atiʼt-the Old Woman:

“I have just arrived, I have just now come to you, Thou-Lal; you my revered Mother-Lal Chichuʼ; Thou-Lal, oh, Mother-in-law for it is I that am your Daughter-in-law-In Alibʼ La and I too am your child-In Alkʼwal La, you my revered Mother-Lal Chichuʼ,” she said when she entered there with the Grandmother-ri Atiʼt; the greatly esteemed Old Woman-ri Atiʼt who questioned her: “Where is it that you come from? Could it be there that I have Sons? Did they not die in Xibʼalbʼa? These Two Boys here are their descendants, their Two Sons; they remain here as their ancestral remembrance-ketal-their familial inheritance and its recollection.”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“These Two Youths here who are Artists and Artisans; Sculptors and Musicians; Carvers and Craftsmen; Jewelers and Silversmiths; Workers of Jade, Gems, and Emeralds are their Sons; the Boys who were just left behind as a ʼsignʼ of their Fathersʼ origin and kind; they shine with their ancestral resemblance-kitzijel; just a ʼsignʼ of their descendants-kitzijel; a recollection of their familial resplendence; for they remain as the remembrance-kitzijel of their precious memory; as a spark-tzij; as a flame-tzij; as fire that burns-tzij like a name; a name that remains here like the truth-tzij; the fire-tzij that burns-tzij like a loss; that returns like shame; like the grief from sacrificial death; the spoken word-tzij bequeathed as ritual relief; the sacred word bestowed as an ember of the truth-tzij of their ancestry; just features in the face of these two youths; for they are the replacements-kʼexel of their Fatherʼs word and its way; the essence of their lineage, the truth of their inheritance; the face of their ancestry; the continuance of their nobility and its regal grace; their ritual sacrifice and its disgrace the desire of death to leave not a trace but here they are; they live on their face the mouth, the nose, the eyes cannot be erased from Earth and Skyʼs Face.”

“These Boys, their Sons, are their descendants, their remembrance, their ancestral inheritance: Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; One Monkey, One Artisan are their names. So, yes indeed, if you saw where you came from? Go back that way!” Grandmother snarled at the One Maiden-Jun Qʼapoj who arrived there before her, the Old Woman-ri Atiʼt to present herself as the Mother of this Grandmotherʼs Grandsons; the Sons of Jun Junajpu.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“But it is true that I am your Daughter-in-Law-In Alibʼ la,” said IxKikʼ to save face; stating her case; resilient yet firm; beyond blame, resistant to shame, leaving her to say: “I was just as I continue to be: that which is of Jun Junajpu is that which lives in me; that which I carry within my womb is that which is his; that which is his in me is that which is of him, Jun Junajpu; they are alive, your sons, for their essence lives within these Boys; that which is theirs, is that which lives within their Sons who live within me!” she continued, now that she had the full attention of the Old Woman. “Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are not dead; this is just a clear sign of theirs-ukʼutbʼal ribʼ saq-a luminous sort of sacred sign that is a perfect indication of their doing, of their making, You, oh, esteemed Mother of mine; oh you, revered Mother-in-law-Lal Walibʼ. You will see them again in the beloved face of those that I bear within me,” she said to the Old Woman-Atiʼt-Grandmother, standing-up for herself as she was born to do as the Daughter of a Noble Lord; Jun u-Miʼal Ajaw. The way IxKikʼ spoke and acted caused Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen to be filled with a ʼred-facedʼ sort of rage-keqʼaqʼal-they were just furious; they were just went wild with anger about how this One Maiden spoke with their Grandmother. Could it be true all she had to say?

After all, it was they Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen who were left to warm the heart of their Grandmother; it was they who played flute like their Father and Uncle had piped on their pipes; it was they who sang the way they sang; just painting, just writing; just carving, just sculpting the way they were taught by their Father; by their Uncle; Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: They were the replacements-kʼexel of their Fathers who taught them to paint, to write, to carve, to sculpt, to sing, to drum, to play on their flutes, to throw dice, to play-ball and now a another sort of foreign mother arrived to replace not only them but their mother: IxBʼaqiyalo who as we know is dead; White-Bone Egret Woman she died. And now another Mother of soon to be born other Younger Brothers has come to disturb their familial space and their privileged place was something that just burned them up-keqʼaqʼal. Envy and jealousy were an ʼuglyʼ feeling yet that is what they felt as IxKikʼ did everything she could to make herself welcome in their home; their home; the home of the lineage where their Fathersʼ House stood there in their Grandmotherʼs patio known as a sitio where they had grown-up. The only place they ever knew. They, Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen were who they were because of who they came to be through their learning to do all they had learned to do and taught to be. It was they who were the Artisan Monkey Boys known as One Monkey, One Artisan; One Howler Monkey; One Spider Monkey who learned to work and play at everything they had come do along the way as they performed and created all the arts to warm their Grandmotherʼs heart. Everything that they were taught to do from their Father and their Uncle; Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu was what brought smiles and laughter to the house where so much death had left so much loss and grief. All of this attention they gave to the artisansʼ and musiciansʼ ways of being and becoming were the artisans ways of their Fathersʼ lineage; which, were the very essence of what warmed their Grandmotherʼs heart each and every day.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were the very things that made their Grandmotherʼs heart and soul content-Are kʼut kubʼul wi ukʼux ri Atiʼt-the Monkey Twinsʼ noble ways of being consoled the heart of IxMuqane who didnʼt want to live life any other way. So it was she, Grandmother-Chichu, who spoke; this is what the Old Woman-Atiʼt said: “I donʼt want you for my Daughter-in-law-Xmakawaj wi at ta Walibʼ. That which you carry within, that which you bear there in your womb just comes from your scuffing and scraping your knees. Xa ajoxbʼal ri kʼo chapam; ¡At Kʼaxtok! ”

“You, you are nothing but a Trickster-¡at Kʼaxtokʼ!-an imposter, a poser is what you are, a false-faced liar, is that not so? They died, the sons of mine you speak of, they are dead,” said the Old Woman-Atiʼt before she threw down an impossible challenge to IxKikʼ something she could not possibly accomplish if she did not bear the nawal essence of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu within her womb.

“So letʼs just say it is true what you say. Utz bʼa la! Very well, so you are my Daughter-in-law; if that is what I hear you say. So then go! Jat bʼa la! Go bring back our sustenance; the sustenance that is ours; the sustenance that is ours to feed those who must be fed. Go harvest ʼOne Big Net of Our Mazorcas of Maize; Our Sustenanceʼ-Ja jachʼa Jun chi Nima Kʼat Qajal; Qechaʼ-that you might come back with here; since you are indeed ʼmyʼ Daughter-in-law-Walibʼ as I have heard you say-kanutaʼo,” she said to the Maiden-ri Qʼapoj. “Utz bʼa la, Fine then!” she said. “Utz bʼa la,” was all there was to say. And so it was that the Maiden went to the Milpa-pa Abʼix-where their Maize grew. This is the Milpa-pa Abʼix-Cornfield of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen. They had cleared a wide path on the way to their Milpa-jokam ubʼeal kumal-it was just an Open sort of a Wide kind of Path that led there to their Milpa; the Maiden simply followed the road-ubʼeʼl, she just followed the path that arrived there to the Milpa- pa abʼix-where their Maize grew.

body:
There was just One Head of Maize in the Milpa-xa kʼu Ju Wi ri Abʼix-there wasnʼt Two Heads of Maize, or Three Heads of Maize; there was just One Head of Maize-xa Ju Wi ri Abʼix-but this One Head of Maize was fruiting out as it ripened; so that it was found heading up as its kernels filled in and its face filled out as its corn-silk grew golden blonde; truly the silky-hair on the One Head of Maize grew long and fine to dry-up and turn light purple-brown-xuwachelaʼm wiʼ uwach chi ju wi.

It should be ʼxa kʼo jun wi ri abʼix and xa jun wi ri abʼixʼ but the text is playing with an ancient ancestral accent meant to say something that this translator does not know other than we have returned to the ʼarchetypal imageʼ of ʼOne Head of Maize-Ju Wi ri Abʼixʼ growing on One Cane of Maize growing in the Milpa of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen that recalls the One Tree planted beside the One Ballcourt upon which the One Skull of Jun Junajpu was placed in the fork of the One Tree: Jun Junajpu or One, One Blow-gun Man-Jun AjPubʼ in a world where One is Divine such as the One Maiden, Jun Qʼapoj; Jun Raqan Kaqulja and Jun AjPu…the One of Jun Kame is the One Celestial Sphere of the Sun, the Moon, and the One Great Star or Jun Nimaʼ Chumil known as Venus.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This reminds us of the One round sphere that ʼmarksʼ the body of Jun Ajpu. So that the ʼXa Ju or the Just One gives us an Ancient Ancestral since of the One Divinity; the One since of One Spirit; the One since of the One Heart of the One People of the One Pueblo of One Head of Maize that tell us we have entered into the One Imaginal Realm of the One Myth in which all is One with the One Ancient Ancestor who is at One with their One Sky and One Earth; One Lake and One Sea. This is the One Beauty of this One Scene here that is One of my favorite scenes and might I say One the most Beloved Scene in the entire Popol Wuj because of the One Way it plays with this One kind of Sacred Secret Speech of the Ancestors. So the use of ʼju wi ri abʼixʼ instead of ʼjun wi ri abʼixʼ is a play on some sort of ancestral accent or some such idea as that being spoken of here: this One Head of Maize growing on One Cane of Maize in this One Milpa with One and only One Cane of Maize: Jun Aj. Oh but what a play on words it is to call forth the great Maize Deity who will come and save the day of this One-Jun Noble Lineage of Maize People: Jun Aj; Ce Acatl as in Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl.

This then was when the One Maiden lost heart which led her to say: “Just look at that; truly lost am I; what a loser, what a cheat; just a debtor, just a fraud; such a failure; failed and fallen. So very flawed am I. ¡Kil la in makol, in kʼasbʼol! And so it is that I am done for, done in for all time; for I am a deceiver and deceived. There is no one as lost as I. Where am I ever going to bring back one big harvest net filled with maize asked of me?” Mused the maiden who now wondered if indeed she could pull off this impossible task required from her by the Old Women-Atiʼt, the Grandmother-Iyom; her Mother-in-Law-Alibʼ.

body:
“Kil la in makol, in kʼasbʼol! Apa xchinkʼam wi ri jun kʼat echaʼ kabʼixik?” xchaʼ kʼut. Oh, beloved readers what a marvelous play made on words to form a word-play beyond oneʼs imagination and expectations all which will not be taken up here because it is as sophisticated as it is complicated: kabʼixik-that which is asked of me and kabʼixik-that which comes from the milpa and Ixik-she of the moon; Kabʼ Ixik: Two that come from the Moon!

But then an idea came to her and then another until she was doing what she was called to do and that was when she knelt down before the ʼOne Head of Maizeʼ growing on the ʼOne Cane of Maizeʼ where she invoked the names of the Guardians of the Milpa, the Protectresses of the Milpa through an invocation that cause the care-takers of all the sacred sustenance to come there to where IxKikʼ was in this Milpa formed and shaped by the enchantment of these Divine Ancestors.

And so she summoned the guardians of grains and the keepers of the kernels of maize and cacao; she called out and upon the Goddesses of Sustenance as she sung out to the Protectresses of the Milpa.

Right there, before the One-Head of Maize of Jun Batzʼ, Jun Chowen IxKikʼ called out to the providers, the sustainers of the milpa petitioning them and pleading with them that they might provide her with that which would sustain her; that is to say, to provide and sustain them, her sons who were those that she was called upon ʼto feed those who must be fedʼ the sons of Jun Junajpu:

“Come, come down; come, come down here where you are called; come, come down; come, make your presence known where you are summonsed!”

body:
“Ta tul wa uloq; Ta tul takʼaloq; Ta tul wa uloq; Ta tul takʼaloq; Ta tul wa uloq, ta tul takʼaloq IxToj; IxQʼanil; IxKakaw; IxPuTziYa! At Chajal re kechaʼ Jun Bʼatzʼ Jun Chowen,” Xchaʼ ri Qʼapoj. “Come, come down, come down here; Come; come where you are summonsed; come, come down to make your presence known; you who are named; you who are known as: IxToj; IxQʼanil; IxKakaw; IxPuTziYa!” “Come, come down, come down here; you who are the guardians; you who are care-takers of the sustenance of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; One Monkey, One Artisan as they are named; as they are known!”

IxToj; IxQʼanil; IxKakaw; IxPuTziYa Mother Goddesses of Abundance; Maiden Goddesses of Prosperity It is both important and necessary to open up this incantation and enchantment of the ʼMother Goddess Care-takers of the Milpa who are the Providers, Sustainers or Tzuqul, Kʼool of the Ixim Winaq.

While stating that I have remained well within the limits of these dense embodiments of this Ancient Ancestral Names that tell of the day Toj that is Rain, Water, and Moon; the day Qʼanil Maize, Seed, and Mazorca; Hard seeds of Kakaw and Sustaining Chocolate; Alchemical Lime and Ash of the Nixtamal Tzi Ya. These are those who are all of them who provide and sustain the People of Maize; through which are nourished and nurtured as the Ixim Winaq-Maize People with their sacred sustenance of Maize and Cacao; as those, who are they, who must feed those who must be fed.

body: Tzi Ya is the white-lime water of the nixtamal used to cook up the maize kernels through the process of nixtamalization which is the alchemical secret that was the transformative process that completely formed and transformed the Mesoamerican Civilization. This alchemical process cooked the hard kernels of maize in white-lime or wood ash to release the vitamins and amino acids in order to transform Maize into as superior form of Super-Sustenance. When this cooked and ground maize is combined with kakaw the two forms of sacred sustenance creates the essential culinary and cultural ingredient that nourishes and nurtures the Maya Culture and Mesoamerican Civilization with the Super Food that enable the People of Maize-Ixim Winaq to People and Populate the Face of the Earth like never, ever before. This need to People and Populate the Face of the Earth known as Winaqarisajxik is the Principal Purpose of the Popol Wuj. And it is here with these Goddess of Sustenance that we are shown the power of IxKikʼ to change and transform the Sky-Earth as the Moon Goddess who is She who Gathers Blood; Gathers Rubber; Gathers Sap; Gathers Copal; and Gathers her Female Allies of the Sacred World and its Sacred Sustenance: IxToj; IxQʼanil; IxKakaw; IxPuTziYa. These are who IxKikʼ as the Moon Maiden; Moon Mother calls in to help her create the magical sustenance she needs to prove that her sons; her beloved sons she bears in her womb are the engendered sons of Jun Junajpu, Wuqub Junajpu. The game is on an IxKikʼ refuses to sit down in the dust and cry and we know the reason why she refuses to sit in the dust and cry and that is because she is One with the One-Footed-One known as the Spirit in the Sky; Ukʼux Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja just as she is One with the Soul of the Earth; Ukʼuʼx Ulew who is Grandmother IxMuqane known as her Mother who closely aligned with her allies known as those summoned here to come down and help IxKikʼ. Those who are known and named of the Mother Goddess of Sacred Sustenance: IxToj; IxQʼanil; IxKakaw; IxPuTziYa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Their names are names from the Four Sacred Directions that are named in the following way that follows the opposite direction of the traditional way of naming the names that follows the spinning movement from left to right moving from the East-Red to South-Yellow to West Black to North White: This then is the Cosmic Movement of Incantation that spins to the right to bring forth Sacred Sustenance required of IxKikʼ from IxMuqane who requires IxKikʼ to harvest ʼOne Big Net of Maizeʼ which is to say ʼGather One Harvest Net of Mazorcas of Maizeʼ out of the Night where the Full Moon rises in the East. As you will come to see IxKikʼ as the Moon Goddess who is a Goddess of Sustenance must use her powers to ʼpull up and outʼ on Maize to bring its ʼheadsʼ to fruition through her Nawal Powers to pull on the Nawal Powers of Sacred Sustenance as IxKikʼ pulls on the ʼCorn Silk on the golden locks of this One Head of Maizeʼ the One Magical Mystical Head of Maize that brings forth Her Sacred Sustenance as the Moon that is His Sacred Sustenance as the Sun from Dawn to Dusk throughout the Day; and, from Dusk to Dawn throughout the Night.

IxKikʼ; IxToj; IxQʼanil; IxKakaw; IxPuTziYa

“You, you Sustainers of Sustenance; you Providers of Providence; Keepers of the Canes; Caretakers of the Corn; Maintainers of Maize; Mothers of the Milpa of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; come; come down; come down here to provide us with plenty; to sustain us with sustenance!” invoked the Maiden, IxKikʼ who was right there standing before the One Cane of the Milpa-Jun Aj rech Abʼix; palms raised up and out to this One Cane of Maize with its One Head; her eyes and face raised to the Forest that grew all around this Clearing-Jok where this One Cane of Jun Bʼatzʼ; Jun Chowen stood growing were it grew. It is there where she called upon them; they; those of Sustenance; the Goddesses of Sustenance; those who are known as the Providers; those who are known as the Sustainers: Tzuqul; Kʼool.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
IxKikʼ invoked the Guardians, Keepers, Care-takers of the Sacred Sustenance of One Monkey, One Artisan when she invoked the names; to then enchant the words: You who are the Guardians of those who are One Monkey, One Artisan: At chajal re kechaʼ Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen!” This was when she called upon their Nawal powers of magical transformation that transformed maize growing in the Milpa of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen as the ʼmountain food of the Animal People-Chikopil Winaqʼ to change and transform it into Sacred Sustenance of the Maize People-Saq Ixim re ri Ixim Winaq.

Maize People-Ixim Winaqʼ These Ixim Winaq were those who began life by suckling their sacred sustenance from the Breast of their Mother from-Ix the nipple-Im of the breast-tzʼum of their mother-uchuch who provided and sustained them with Ixim-Sustenance that ʼsprouted forth-tzuq-paʼ as the tendril hairs-wi of the hard seed-naqʼ to form-tzʼaq and shape-bʼit the Ixim Winaq: the People of Sustenance; the People of Cacao-Kakaw; the People of Maize-Qʼanil the Sacred Sustenance of the Ixim Winaq.

These are those who ʼshoot out-tzuq paʼ from the ʼtendril hairs-wi-tendril shootsʼ who sprout out of the seed that is sown-ewexibʼal in the earth; the sprouting forth of the sown seed hidden-ewabʼal beneath the ground to hide it from the Bird People like Wuqubʼ Kaqix and others such as feathery wing ancestors like the Grackle known as Chʼoʼk or Chʼaʼk. This sacred narrative is also what was suckled as the sacred sustenance of the Ixim Winaq who imbibed it from-ix the very nipple-im of their Motherʼs Breast as the Motherʼs Milk that was and continues to be the real and metaphorical essences that formed and framed, shaped and structured the Maya Soul; the Mesoamerican Spirit; the Body and the Mind of the Ixim Winaq.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This then is the real and metaphorical essence of Ixim Winaq: Maize People the motherʼs milk of the Maize People formed and shaped from words and images; ancestral archetypes and mythic metaphors that awaken the imagination in order to create the collective consciousness and its hunger for epic narratives of cosmic creation and total destruction that bring about the formation of life and the germination of death. Human beings are born into this world wanting to know the stories that tell of its being populated by the Trees and Vines; Flower and Fruit; Plants and Animals; Women and Men; Mountains and Valleys; Rivers and Streams; Clouds and Rain; Wind and Sun that People and Populate the Face of the Earth. The Sons and Daughters of Mothers and Fathers want to tell and be told these Stories of Creation that warm the Heart and sustain the Soul. This is what is going on here. The Maize People are telling their story of their Divine Ancestors and those Ancient Mother-Fathers Mother Goddess and Father Gods. This is the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj: the Sacred Narrative of the Maya.

IxKikʼ; IxToj; IxQʼanil; IxKakaw; IxPuTziYa

These are Mother Goddesses, the Matriarchs of the Maize People who IxKikʼ enchanted now with her sing-song prayers petitioning their powers of prosperity that are summonsed in the form of Divine Providence. The Magical Moon Maiden calls them in to then call them down to where she is there in the Milpa of Magical Maize where the One Head of Maize-Jun Wi Aj is waiting for her command to fill the One Big Net of Sustenance-Jun Nimaʼ Kʼat Echaʼ with the harvest that is soon at hand.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This then is when she knew just what she had to do; which she could see as clearly as a clearly seen solution could be seen; for like the other four Providers-Tzuqul and Sustainers- Kʼool of the Milpa-Abʼix, IxKikʼ was borne into the World of the Sky-Earth to embody the Mother Goddess of the Full Moon whose now completely ʼFull Wombʼ was ripe with abundance in the form of her Twins; her Two Boys; her Two Sons who were the very essence and nature; condition and quality of being and becoming the Sun and the Moon that took the form and shape of a Sacred Bundle of Sacred Sustenance-Water known as Wa-Jaʼ or Way-Ya this is the ʼCarrying Net-Kʼat-Harvest Net of the One Big Net of Maize IxKikʼ must bring home to feed those who must be fed.

This then was when IxKikʼ looked upon the corn silk-tzamiy that flowed forth from the long silky locks of this one head of maize-ju wiʼ jal growing in the milpa of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; she pulled ever so gently on ʼjust one-xa junʼ of those fine filaments; those fine golden hairs; one by one she drew forth the long yellow tresses of that one head of maize; one silken strand at a time IxKikʼ pulled so that up and out came a ʼfull head of corn-jun qʼanil-una mazorca-jun jalʼ that were whole heads of maize: the corn silk shifted its shape as it transformed into perfect ʼears of cornʼ that were precious ʼheads of maize-qʼanilʼ. These heads of maize that IxKikʼ brought forth before her were the Sacred Sustenance that she now ordered and arranged in the One Big Harvest Net: Jun Nima Kʼat that Grandmother IxMuqane; IxMuq-Qʼanil; IxMuq-Kan-Eey provided IxKikʼ so she could gather-up the Maize to feed those who had to be fed. IxKikʼ didnʼt harvest the head of maize growing on the one cane, but instead she just drew out the corn silk, one by one she pulled out the hairs and one by one out came heads of maize: the mazorca of maize came forth from IxKikʼ pulling up on the fine silky hairs of the corn silk on this one head of maize-utzamiyal uwiʼ jal.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
In this way the Maiden was able to harvest ʼOne Big Net-Full of Maizeʼ from just one head of maize-xa ju wiʼ jal. Each one the fine hairs transformed into one perfect ʼheadʼ of sacred sustenance, perfect ears of corn-ju yakaj jal came forth as perfectly formed heads of maize-jal, that were perfectly formed mazorca-qʼanil. And so it was IxKikʼ brought forth great abundance from where there was just one head of Maize; Jun Qʼanil as it is said today.

Qʼanil One Divinity; One Big Net of Our Maize Qʼanil Jun Kabʼawil: Jun Nimaʼ Kʼat qechaʼ Qabʼix Qʼanajal, Saqijal; Saqijal, Qʼanajal

Qʼanil is the name of the ʼmazorca of maize or heads of maizeʼ that are invoked to this day by Day-Keepers and Diviners in the Kʼicheʼ. Qʼanil refers to a mazorca of maize that is a fully filled out head of maize with each seed seen as a perfectly rounded, filled out golden yellow skulls of abundance; this is the shiny golden abundance of the Ixim Winaq; this is the fully filled out sense of precious perfection that is perfect perfection of this golden star-like archetype and reality of the Maize People. The Golden Yellow Maize known as Qʼanajal-Yellow Mazorca of Maize will become the essence of the flesh of the First Fathers of Maize when their time comes to ʼDawnʼ onto the Face of the Earth at the Dawning of the Sun of Maize People.

body: This Qʼanajal is paired and coupled by its primordial pair that is its complementary complement of White Maize known as Saqijal. This White Mazorca with its white skull-like seeds; white tooth-like seeds of resplendence are known here in Ancient Word as Saqijal-White Mazorca. This fullness of being; this completeness of existence is what is brought forth in the Maya Cosmos as this divine sense of affluence that comes with a ʼgreat harvest of maizeʼ this dear reader is the sense of Kabʼawil; the Mayaʼs full-kabʼal sense of completion-kabʼal that is Divinity; that is the Mazorca with each and every kernel rounded out like a skull of the Ancestors come to fruition; come to completion: Saqijal; Qʼanajal a most precious incantation in the enchantment of the Sacred World; Santo Mundo: Saq Ulew; Qʼan Ulew. The Kʼicheʼ lived to experience this divine kind of complete sort of fully filled out sense of wholeness that is the perfection of completeness experienced in this word kabʼal; where the full sense of kabʼal provides one with a complete sense of fullness. This sense of fullness fills one with a whole, full, filled-up and filled-out sense of Divinity; a complete sense of the Divine that is a bountiful sense of beneficence; the Kabʼawil that one feels here-that fills one here-is that sense of Divine Abundance experienced through this Ancestral Archetype of ʼOne Big Net of Maizeʼ that fills oneʼs desire for perfection through this mythic expression of mythical abundance that becomes a perfectly round sphere of maize; a womb filled with the potential potency of complete and utter change and transformation of this mythic masterpiece; an archetypal summons for IxKikʼ to bring her calling in life to perfection. For it is this One Full Net of Maize that will become the Sun and Moon of the Maize People; a People filled with glory and majesty; a Pueblo filled with powerful and prosperous People. IxKikʼ invokes this natural gift of bounty that creates a perfectly whole, perfectly full sense of Divinity and its ʼdivine-willʼ that is called down; called in to come to fruition.

body:
This is a divine kind of fulfillment that forms the imagination to fill the Imaginal World-Mundus Imaginalis with a complete sense of abundance that is an abundant sense of fulfillment that comes forth from this magical incantation and mystical enchantment of bountiful prosperity. Only through the invocation of these Mother Goddesses is IxKikʼ able to bring forth Natural Wealth and Supernatural Plenty that is called up and out of the Earth; to be called down from the fructifying powers of the Sky.

The Earth-Sky; the Sky-Earth is where the Kabʼawil will wait and watch to listen upon the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings to call upon them as the Providers and Sustainers to come down to the ground there where they will be in the Milpa calling out to the Kabʼawil for the Maize People with gifts of plenty as in this ʼOne Big Net Of Maizeʼ as IxKikʼ does when she ʼnames the namesʼ of those who she calls into play to bring about the fulfillment of Divinity. These are those who take the form and shape of those ʼnames namedʼ as the Kabʼawil who are called down to create abundance there in the Milpa before the One Head of Maize: Ju Wi Abʼix.

Let us hear that incantation once again:

“Ta tul wa uloq; ta tul takʼaloq IxToj; IxQʼanil; IxKakaw; IxPuTziYa. At Chajal re kechaʼ Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen.” Xchaʼ ri Qʼapoj.

“Come, come down, come in here; Come; come where you are summonsed; come, come down to make your presence known; you who are named; you who are known as: IxToj; IxQʼanil; IxKakaw; IxPuTziYa! You who are the Keepers; the Caretakers of the Sustenance of One Monkey, One Artisan.” Invoked the Maiden calling upon the Keepers; Care-takers; Guardians.

body:
So let us call down these Mother Goddess one last time: IxKikʼ: She of the Blood, She of the Moon, She of Rubber; She of the Copal and Pine Trees IxToj: She of Sacrifice, She of Rain-drop, She of Blood-drop, She of Moonʼs Moisture IxQʼanil: She of Maize, She of the Mazorca, She of Golden Resplendence; of Abundance IxKakaw: She of Sacred Sustenance, She of Wealth, She of Prosperity, She of Ritual IxPuTziYa: She of the White-Lime Sustenance, She of the Active Essence of the Maya Civilization, She of the Ancestral Place of Profuse Plenty, Bountiful Abundance

Let us remember these Mother Goddesses of the Ixim Winaq IxKikʼ: Moon, Blood, Rubber, Rubber Ball, Sap, Copal Incense, Pine-Resin, Chicle IxToj: Water-Moon-Blood-Sacrifice-Debt-Payment-Mother Goddess of Ixim Winaq IxQʼanil: Maize-Milpa-Mazorca-Golden Resplendence-Mother Goddess of Ixim Winaq IxKakaw: Cacao-Chocolate-Hard-Hard Sustenance-Mother Goddess of Ixim Winaq IxPuTziYa: White Lime-Nixtamal-Nourishment-Mother Goddess of Ixim Winaq

This was when IxKikʼ took hold of the thin threads of corn-silk; the corn-silk of the head of maize; she pulled up on the hair of the head of maize; she did not harvest the mazorca of maize. Then she arranged the mazorcas of maize in her harvest net, completely filling-out her One Big Net

Ta xukʼam kʼut ri tzamiy, utzamiyal uwiʼ jal, xubʼoq aqʼanoq, mawi xujachʼ ri jal. Chikaw kʼut ri jal echaʼ pa kʼat, xqʼaxinik ri nima kʼat.

As IxKikʼ ʼpulled-upʼ on the fine threads of corn silk ʼup-cameʼ perfect heads of maize; perfect heads of maize that she ordered perfectly in her One-Big-Net where she left the harvest she collected perfectly ordered so that her net was perfectly packed; her maize perfectly placed; her mazorcas perfectly arranged. IxKikʼ had gathered her golden-yellow and silver-white heads of maize; mazorcas of maize that completely filled-out her One Big Harvest Net of Maize-Jun Nima Kʼat.

She did it all ʼjust soʼ so that she could fill her One Net perfectly full by ʼarranging itʼ with full heads of maize; mazorcas of maize that was gathered up by IxKikʼ as the sacred sustenance to feed those who had to be fed.

body:
IxKikʼ only felt herself ready to return when she had finished gathering up the perfect heads of maize that came from her pulling up and out on the thin threads of corn silk; and she wasnʼt finished pulling out those perfect heads of maize until her one big harvest net was completely full of perfectly ordered; perfectly arranged heads of maize.

It was then that the Maiden left, and it was they, the Animals, who carried the Harvest Net for her. It was they, the Wild Animals who carried the great big load of maize when they went along the road.

When they arrived back home, the animals left the great big load there alongside the house as if it had been carried by the Maiden, or so it was seen by Grandmother like that; as if the Maiden had carried the great load on her own.

When the Old Woman saw all the sustenance gathered there in the One Big Carrying Net she immediately wanted to know where it had come: “From where did all this food of yours come? ¿Apa mixpe wi ri echa awumal? I hope you didnʼt just level the place, Iʼll just have to go see for myself!” Said the Grandmother when she saw the great harvest the Maiden had gathered up.

The Old Style Translation Corn is Maize; Cornfield is Milpa; Stalk is Cane; Ear is Head Old Woman; One Big Net

“Where did you get all of this from; I hope you didnʼt just finish-off all the maize there was to be harvested? I have to go see for myself!” said Grandmother-xchaʼ ri Atiʼt.

And so the Old Woman walked out to see the Cornfield for herself; but there was just the same single Stalk of Corn standing there; just as there was the same single solitary Ear of Corn growing on the One Stalk of Corn that grew in the Cornfield; the same Ear of Corn grew on the same Stalk of Corn that stood where it grew in their Cornfield. It was there beneath where the Corn Cane grew that the Old Woman saw the place where the net had left its imprint beneath the One Corn Stalk. It was here below the Corn Stalk where the harvest net had made its mark; the mark that was printed in the earth where the Maiden had gathered her great big load of maize in her One Big Net!

body:
And so it was that the Old Woman went to see the Milpa; but there was just One Head of Maize; there was just the same One Head of Maize that there had always been in their Milpa-Xawi xere kʼo wi ri ju wi abʼix.

This then was when the Old Woman saw the imprint made by the net in the place-ukʼolibʼal below the One Cane, the One Cane of Maize with the One Head of Maize growing in their Milpa.

Nahua speakers in the North; Maya speakers in the South One Cane; Ce Acatl; Jun Aj One Corn Stalk in the Cornfield; One Cane of Milpa; Jun Aj rech ri Abʼix

For the Old Woman could clearly see the place in the dust where the heavy load of corn had sat below the single cane of maize; this was the printed place where the Maiden had filled- out her net; her net that she filled-up with perfectly formed heads of maize; perfectly shaped ears of corn that she had arranged just so; just so they filled-up her heavy load; just so they fill-out her harvest of maize that filled up her One Big Net full of corn. Her One Big Net of Maize that left a perfect imprint in the dust there just below the One Cane of Maize; there beneath the One Stalk of Corn that stood there standing with just One Head of Maize-xa Ju Wi Abʼix-One Ear of Corn that grew there in their Cornfield; in the Cornfield of One Monkey, One Artisan which was la Milpa de Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chopin.

Quickly then did the Old Woman return, arriving there before her house that was her home. Now it was her turn to speak before the One Maiden; Jun Qʼapoj; IxKikʼ is her name:

“This is just a sign of theirs. Truly you are my Daughter-in-law-at Walibʼ! Now I will have to watch all that you do! Those grandchildren of mine are already showing their magical powers-Nawinaq; they are already showing their nawal nature as Nawal Winaq-Trickster People through their nawal ways of change; their transforming trickster ways of transformation; for they are already showing the ancestral ways of their Fathers; like their Grandfather before him who are all just Magical People; just Trickster People: xa Nawal Winaq all of them,” said then the Old Woman-Atiʼt to the Maiden-Qʼapoj.

Mythic Genius; Nawal Transformation

Let us say this all again in a slightly different way in order that we understand how this ʼsign-retalʼ that ʼsignifies-ketzijelʼ on this Ancient Ancestral Mesoamerican Myth that embodies the knot that binds this ʼsacred bundleʼ of the Nahua Tradition with the Maya Tradition and their Nawal Winaq-Magical Transforming Trickster People of the Maya Culture and its Maize People. This sacred bundle is bound together with the Nahua Culture of Tricksters and the Maya Culture of Maize Lords; Maize Deities who are knotted together in this Myth of Maize; Myth of Tricksters through this One Cane; Jun Aj; Ce Acatl that is a ʼsaqetalʼ a ʼsacred signʼ that speaks to us in truly sacred sorts of secret Nawal Ways of Transforming Tricksters. We must bring perfect order to our mythic imagination before the Boys; the Sons; the Twins of the Maize Father are born standing-up straight on the mountainside.

By ordering our mythic imagination with the imaginal realm of the Maize Deities here and now we will be able to follow the mythic beauty of the sacred history of the Maize People. We must enter the ʼancient wordʼ of this mythic metaphor of ʼone cane of maizeʼ with its ʼone head of maizeʼ to be able to appreciate the invocation of the Maize Deity Quetzalcoatl whose sacred day and day name is One Cane; Jun Aj; Ce Acatl in this masterful use of mythic metaphor by these Maya Scribes who formed and shaped this story over millennia. So it only seems respectful for us who live today to take some time to appreciate the genius of the Mesoamerican Civilization as expressed here in the genius of mythical thought and imagination of the Maya Culture. Here is where we enter into millennial genius that most certainly deserves our deepest respect and most revered attention. So please, take your time to enjoy the mythic genius of the nawal transformation that is taking place here in this text.

body:
Let us do so now so we can appreciation the mythic metaphorical imagination of the Mundus Imaginalis into which we are about to be borne into here as we enter the Imaginal Realm of Maize Twins and their Mother and their Grandmother and their Elder Brother who are all gathered together here on the Kʼiche Mountainside where the Sons, the Boys, the Twins are about to sprout up and out of their Motherʼs Womb of Emergence coming into life in as Sacred Landscape filled with Ancestral Tests; Mythic Trials; and Initiatory Ordeals. This is where we are headed to now as we leave the Milpa behind to enter Grandmotherʼs Home that is the Great House of the Maize People Lineage.

Jun Aj; Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl;

Jun Ajaw; Jun Ixim; Lord One Maize

This One Cane-Jun Aj is the calendar name of the Lord of Maize. Jun Aj and Ce Acatl are the calendar names of Quetzalcoatl-Qʼuqʼkumatz-Kukulkan who is also the Maize Deity of the Nahua World that is spoken of here in Mayan Cultural ways. This image of the ʼone net markʼ under the ʼone cane of maizeʼ is like looking down at a glyph imprint in the dust in the Milpa of the Maize Deity. This is why Popol Wuj as Sacred Secret Text is of such immense importance for it is a treasure trove of Mesoamerican imagery known as iconography through which we come to understand the Maya Culture and Mesoamerican Civilization through mythic image, mythic-metaphorical word, and mythic metaphor.

These images come in succession one right after the next. These iconic revelations do not end so we must stop in order to reveal what is going on mythically and metaphorically so we can move forwards with greater knowledge and the kind of humble confidence that knowledge and wisdom always breeds. Let is look at only ʼoneʼ aspect of the nawal genius of the nawal imagination of this ingenious mythical text. For now we are presented with the ʼOne Markʼ that is signed in the ʼdustʼ beneath the One Cane; One Head of Maize as the One Spot, the One Point, the One Dot, the One Round Sphere of the Maize Lord Jun Junajpu known as Jun Ixim-One Maize of the Classic Period.

body: This then is that One Round Circle filled in with crosshatching that signifies as it says Jun Ixim who is Jun Junajpu. This is his sign left in the dust beneath the One Cane of Maize. What genius, what beauty, what a masterful way to combine illustrated imagery and writing together in one image of maize and the Maize Lord making his mark through spherical imagery left by the Moon Maiden and her iconic ʼnetʼ printed out there on the Face of the Earth in the Sacred Milpa of the Divine Ancestors of the Maize People. This ʼOneʼ mark is also the ʼsignʼ that ʼsignifiesʼ the presence of the Lords of Death! IxKikʼ is the Daughter of Lord of the Underworld. And so it was that Jun Junajpu left his sign there with IxKikʼ below the One Cane of Maize, Jun Aj, so everyone could see the sign of abundance in the sign of the One Net-Jun Kʼat beneath the One Head of Maize growing on the One Cane of Maize which says this is the sign of the Father of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. And so it is that we find the ʼsignʼ to be speaking another language that tells us of the Maize People whose Nim Ajaw-Great Lord or the Noble Prince Lord Quetzalcoatl who in Nahuatl is known as the Great Lord; the Noble Prince of the Ancient Ancestral City of Tollan or Pu which forms the name: Nim Ajaw Jun AjPu who is the Nim Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz of Tollan Tzuy-Wa who is the Nahuatl Prince of Tula-Tollan; Cholula-Chollan Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl who is the Noble Lord; Divine Prince whose Nahuatl Myth is so very important to the Mesoamerican Civilization that it lives on today. But nowhere more than in the Sacred History of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Popol Wuj is known as Kʼicheʼ Maya Noble Lord-Nim Ajaw who is Nawal Ajaw who is also the Kabʼawil known by a variety of different names from different lineage as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. You know these well through many interpretive treatments of their names so you know this Maize Deity in Maya Culture.

body:
But there are stories of Quetzalcoatl that come from the Nahuatl Culture and its Myth Cycles or Mythic Narratives that tell of Quetzalcoatl descending down into Mictlan, the Land of the Dead to retrieve the ʼbonesʼ of the ancestors to sow as the seeds of maize.

This story is similar to Jun Junajpu who descends down into Xibʼalbʼa. And so it is that this One Big Net of Maize creates a big ʼOneʼ mark on the Earth that says: ʼhere is the sign of One-Jun Junajpu or Jun, Jun AjPu whoʼs bones are the mazorca of maize gathered by the Moon Maiden that will be cooked and ground to model and mold the First Four Fathers of the Maize People who are the Kʼicheʼ Maya People of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Pueblo. The bones of Jun Junajpu are the bones that will become the seeds of the Saqijal, Qʼanajal that will be ʼsownʼ by IxMuqane who then will ground them down to then mold and model; form and shape the First Four Fathers of Maize. This is where we are headed. This is the direction Popol Wuj is taking in these first Three Acts known as the Sowing-Ewaxibʼal of the Maize People; the Sowing- Ewaxibʼal that will move to the Dawning-Saqiribʼal of the Kʼicheʼ Sun.

This One Cane or Jun Aj is Ce Acatl that is something I simply ʼcame upʼ with by translating the name of the place where the ʼsignʼ of the ʼOne Net of Maizeʼ was found in the milpa beneath the One Cane of Maize or Ce Acatl which is the day name of Quetzalcoatl just as Ce Miquiztli is the same as Jun Kame which is the day name of Tezcatlipoca.

This One Cane of Maize as the Day Sign Jun Aj; Ce Acatl; One Cane; One Mazorca tells us so much about these Boys, these Twins who wait to be born there in la Milpa.

This ʼsignʼ left by the One Big Net says in mayúsculo: JUN JUNAJPU who is the JUN AJAW known as JUN IXIM known as CE ACATL TOPILTZIN QUETZALCOATL; the Maize Lord; the Maize Deity; the Mesoamerican Lord of Maize. Tollan Tzuy-Wa and its Supreme Ruler: Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz; Lord Quetzalcoatl the Conqueror: Nakxitl Tepew Quetzalcoatl.

body:
And it is he who is said to have returned on the Day Kajibʼ Ajaw or Four Noble Lord on the Solstice of December 21, 2012. Maya Day-Keepers tell us that we live in a very pivotal passage of time that Archetypal Psychologist tell us require myth for us to ʼpass-overʼ or ʼthroughʼ these difficult times if our lives are going to be filled with meaning and soul. Myth- making that is soul-making is what will support or returning to the Sacred Landscape of the Américas in meaningful ways.

Jun Aj rech ri Abʼix; So let us return to the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj to show our deepest veneration for the Original Lineages of Indigenous People with the specific intention of acknowledge the ʼblood dropsʼ in the ʼdustʼ found beneath the Maya Milpa; drops of blood that call to us to be invoked and remembered that we might develop as deeper sense of belonging in this world with all the Many People from all the Many Pueblos that live here in these Américas.

IxKikʼs Birth of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej Standing-up on the Mountainside Sleeping atop an Ant-bed; Sleeping atop a Spiny Brambles Shouldering Blowguns; Blowgunning Birds Protectors of the Maize; Defenders of the Milpa Home Again; Home Again

Here then next we shall tell of the birth of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. This then is where we will tell of their being born-kalaxik. We will tell of their sprouting forth on the mountainside: when the day was found for their birth, for their sprouting forth-xuriq uqʼij kalaxik; when their destiny was divined as to what would be the day that they were to be borne into the world as sons birthed-xeʼalaxik by their mother here on the Face of the Earth.

This was the day when they were made to sprout forth on the mountainside; when the day arrived that she, the Maiden-Qʼapoj, IxKikʼ gave birth to her sons on the mountain-pa juyubʼ. This was when the One Maiden- Jun Qʼapoj IxKikʼ gave birth to her sons in the wilderness-pa juyubʼ for they were just born on the mountainside-pa juyubʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Grandmother wasnʼt there to watch over her when she gave birth, the Old Woman was not present when they were born; in an instant they shot up; directly, immediately they rose-up-xeyakeʼik-they just stood-up, the two of them were born standing up straight in the mountains: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej as they are named. In the wilderness they rose-up; on the mountain they rose-up-pa juyubʼ xeyake wi; in the wild they sprouted out; emerging on the mountainside they stood- up like heads of maize; it was on the mountain that they were born erect, upright;

strong and straight-pa juyubʼ xeyake wi. This is how these Boys emerged; the way they were born into life.

They Stood-up on the Mountain; Pa juyubʼ xeyake wi Pa juyubʼ xeyake wi: In the wilderness they rose up like Yaki Warriors-xeyake wi they were born standing up ready for battle these Maize Boys; these Warrior Twins stood up straight at birth in the wild prepared to meet their future; their fortune; their fate on their birth day with its divine destiny, defined day, and its divine-deified date.

It helps sound out the original Kʼicheʼ to hear the ʼsub-textʼ of this ʼWarlordʼ culture of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Lords.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: Jun yakaj jal is an ʼearʼ of corn which is a head of maize…yake is when the wind rises up…yakoj is to rise-up…It is astounding how all past translation simply want to see the Boys ʼborn on the mountainʼ without ʼentering intoʼ the divine enchantment of the original text with its ʼdouble entendreʼ and those double-meaningsʼ rising up to create deeper meaning and much greater understanding of the ʼmultivalentʼ sense of these ʼmultidimensionalʼ mythic figures: Maize Twins; Warrior Sons; Magical Transforming Magicians; Vengeful Sons; Rulers of their Lineage; Protectors of their Ancestry; Jokers; Tricksters; Ball-Players; Hunters; Good-Boys; Grandmotherʼs Helpers; Motherʼs Beloved Sons; Fatherʼs Defenders; Protectors of the Maize growing in la Milpa; Hunters; Warriors; Cultural Heroes.. We already know who they are as those who prepare the World for the Sowing of the Maize People; We know they are going to want to take down the Killers of their Fathers who are unjustly murdered by the Lords of Death. These Divine Sons are filled with the desire for revenge. The will want to take out vengeance on the Lords of Death who sacrificed their Father; Uncle so we know that they are special but we donʼt know how they find what is theirs in life; how do they know what their calling in life is and how to bring that calling to fruition. We love these Two Boys; they are really ʼGood Guysʼ but they donʼt life ʼfalse-faceʼ liars and deceivers; trickers and cheaters. Most importantly they are Mountain-made Sons of the Wilderness who are not raised ʼsoftʼ and ʼsettledʼ in a cozy kind of cleaned-up sort of prim and primped place. No, not that, not these Two Hero Twins; Blowgun Boys; the Hunter and the Hunted. This sentence: Pa juyubʼ xeyake wi; ʼon the Mountain they rose-up as Yaki Chiefs; Yaki Warlords: Yake Wiʼ is masterful work-play to ʼsayʼ the least! And, what is kind of funny is how much more conservative I am as a Kaxlan-Foreigner instead of the Maya Day-Keepers, Maya Prayer-Makers who ʼseeʼ much more in these mythopoetic plays that reveal much more than what is brought forth here in this interpretation of the Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account!

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Truly, it is astounding what Maya Day-keepers Shamans will here when I have attempted to read the Popol Wuj out-loud since the shamanic mind is so free to make word and sound associations that a foreigner like me is able to bring to a Translation and Interpretation. Anyway, I think it is important you come to know how conservative I am in my reading of Popol Wuj even though literal interpretations would not say so but what kind of sense does it make to come up with a literal translation of a metaphorical text.

That is just ignorant; that is what that is but there they are on the internet written by folks who think that is something a translator of myth should participate in. Not here, not now, not before and not anywhere in the future. What is interesting is how my left arm began vibrating while writing this here. This twitching of nerves is of course is a ʼsignʼ that reveals ʼlightening in the bloodʼ to confirm what is written here is indeed what is meant to be written to reveal what thirsts to be revealed…oh, there it is again in my left thigh, that is weird; I havenʼt felt that all along the way of this translation and interpretation of the Ojer Tzij; Ojer Natbʼal. ʼInterestingʼ; as young people tend to say these days.

So when they-the Infant Boys-were made to enter the House-the House of IxMuqane-then they would not sleep.

“Just throw them out! Truly, they just scream their mouths off-qitzij chach kichiʼ,” cried Grandmother.

So then Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen placed them on a bed of ants; and was on that ant-bed they slept sweetly.

This was when their Older Brothers took them away from the ant-bed and placed them on-top of a bed of wild blackberries bushes with their venomous barbs. This then was when Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen wanted them to die; they just wanted the baby boys to be eaten by the ants; they just wanted the twin infants to die there on top of the deadly spines of the blackberry brambles.

They yearned for their death, they longed for their demise because of the hatred and jealousy that Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen had for them; the anger and envy they held within them for their Younger Brothers-Kichaqʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
For the Boys, the Sons; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej were not well received by their Older Brothers-Katzʼ in the house of their Father; the Younger Brothers-Kichaqʼ of Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen were not welcome in the home of their Grandmother by their Older Brothers-Katzʼ who did not want anything to do with their ʼYounger Brothers-Kichaqʼ. In fact, Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen didnʼt acknowledge the presence of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej at all in their Grandmotherʼs home and because of this the Younger Boys just grew-up wild in the mountains-xawi kʼu pa juyubʼ xekʼiy wi.

Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen These Older Brothers were Great Flautists, Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; these two play flute; truly, they were Great Pipers-e AjSu-Great Flute-Players were they, these Two Older Boys; these Two Elder Sons were Great Singers of Song-e AjBʼix; for they were Great Story-tellers of tales; they were Great Singers of Song; these Boys were born with prodigious talent: Great Flautists; Great Singers were they; these two musicians and singers who played and sang the Ancient Songs in the Ancient Traditional Way. Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen were those who quickly became exceptional in all that they that did; they brought everything they did to fruition; for truly exceptional were they in all they did as they quickly showed their excellence in all they came to do.

They grew and they excelled but only through great suffering, for it was difficult to become the Great Artists and Artisans they came to be; these two who worked so hard at all they brought to perfection; the two of them there known and named One Monkey, One Artisan; Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen.

Indeed, it was only by overcoming suffering and affliction that they became the talented artists and musicians that they came to be.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
For Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen came to be Great Masters like other Sons of Great Lords; Sons who distinguish themselves through the constant struggle and endless effort it took to be as great as they came to be; it was only by their proving themselves before others that they overcame their constant confrontation with creative expertise and the inventive ordeal it was to continue to be inspired and ingenious but this is what they faced being the Artists and Artisans they were.

In time they came to be wise, sagacious seers and genius, knowers of knowledge because of all they came to see and all they came to know through their ability to endure hardship and suffer affliction. It was their constant confrontation with creativity that made them as tough and tortured as they were anguished and agonized by their endless effort to create music and art; but that is who Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen had grown-up to be in their Grandmotherʼs home; their Fatherʼs house who had died in Xibʼalbʼa long ago.

For truly, they were talented at all they did: thus they grew-up to be Great Flautists, Musicians, and Scribes who became Great Wood-workers and Carpenters; who came to be Carvers and Sculptors, too.

Everything they did was certain to come out exceptional; all they started they brought to perfection; creating great beauty and splendor as Flute-players, and Singers; Scribes and Painters. They had talent, they were born with it; it was just through their nawal powers that they did all they came to do. It was just their magical powers of transformation-xa xenawinaq-their ancestral genius to bring about change that made it so.

For it was just their nawal way of thinking that gave them their nawal thoughts which was their ancestral way of thinking their ancestral thoughts that made them who they were. In this way Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen were Nawal Winaq.

For it was just their ingenious imagination that made them who they came to be; and, who they came to be, was who they were born to become; and who they were born to become was who they struggle and strove to be.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were those who were born to be who they became; and who they had become is who they came to be known; and who they were known to be were those who were Nawal Winaq. In this way Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen were Nawal Winaq. These Boys, these Sons, these Twins were born with their Fathersʼ nawal genius; they came into the world with this nawal gift of being born into the world as Nawinaq.

Yet is was only because of their endless patient playing music and constant work creating beauty that they came to be those who they came to be; which, was the nawal artists and nawal artisans who they now were; nawal artists and artisans that became the nawal musicians and nawal singers that they now were and always would be. In this way Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen were Nawal Winaq; which, was who they were born to be.

It just showed in their face; the face of their Fathers. Thus they knew it was they who were their Fathersʼ replacements-kʼexel, the remembrance of their Fathersʼ ways of being; their Fathersʼ ways of speaking and acting-ukʼexel kiqajaw; their Fathers who were those who had gone to Xibʼalbʼa to never return as they promised they would. This was when the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were determined to cut their lineage off at the trunk but this is not the way it turned out.
