source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: For the first time in a long time the Old Women-QaTiʼt-Grandmother is named by her proper name: IxMuqane. A subtle change is felt for we are made to feel a general sense of familial familiarity formed and framed around the ʼMaize People-Ixim Winaqʼ who are ordered and organized into a family that consists of a dead Grandfather-Xpiyakok; a deceased Wife- IxBʼaqiyalo; and, a dead Father and Uncle-Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu as well as those who make-up the living family that consists of a Grandmother, a Mother, and Grandsons-Sons known to us well as IxMuqane, IxKikʼ and Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. And let us not forget those fun-loving and only to-humorous Elder Twin Brothers who now roam the Jungle Tropics as the Monkey Twins traditional spoken of as Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen known to all as the Dancing Boys: One Monkey and One Artisan! The separation between family members is now replaced by a deep sense of familial unity and familiarity between them as an intimate family of the Maize People: Ixim Winaq. I always feel flippant when having the ʼflipʼ sort of trickster thought wanting to say: Come, meet the Maize People; those known as the Junajpu; the tried and tested Ixim Winaq who embody, who ensoul the Changing and Transforming Essence of Maya Culture and the Nawal Genius of all Mesoamerican Civilization. These are truly enchanting people who do embody the most beautiful and benevolent aspects of Mesoamerican Civilization by exemplifying the path of ethical good; the way to aesthetic beauty; the initiatory road leading to the truth while always seeking the experience transcendence as Descendants devoted to walking in the ancestral footsteps of the Ancient Ones; the Nawales; those Divine Ancestors who show us the way out of the Darkness and into the Divine Light. This is what makes the Popol Wuj the precious gift it is that is given by the Maya to Humanity and Humanityʼs need for a Mythic Path to follow; a Mythic sort of Metaphorical that is Real; that is Noble; that is Kind and Generous; Providing and Sustaining that leads to our inherent sort of innate sense of Noble Perfection.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Popol Wuj is a Path to the Good-Life and those lucky enough to take-up that Path will always be rewarded with Authentic Ancestral Knowledge and Genuine Indigenous Wisdom in Humanityʼs Divine Quest in search for the Good, the True, and the Beautiful through the Transcendent Unity of the Love and Light of the Heart of the Sky-Heart of the Earth; and the Eternal Remembrance of Return and Renewal; Rebirth and Revival of Heart of the Lake of the Lake-Heart of the Sea.

Yet for our experience of such regeneration and revitalization we must make our descent down into the sacrificial fires of death and dissolution; and this is where we are headed now. So prepare because according to the Popol Wuj life is not at all the ʼlove and lightʼ of the ʼeasy lifeʼ. No, the Popol Wuj takes us on a perilous journey of descent into the Underworld where we must face the Lords of Death and Disease and that is where we are headed now.

We are going to be getting ʼclose and personalʼ with the nasty Lords of Xibʼalbʼa again, those malicious mockers of man; those cheating tricksters who are tricky cheaters; those lame losers who are just lousy-liars; those devious and deceptive deceivers of death and disease are those who we are inviting us down into their deadly domain: the Underworld Realm of the Lords of Death. This is where ʼbait and switchʼ is the name of the game with the not so Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame and their Messengers who are vitally important to this Ancient Ancestral Account of the Ixim Winaq and their nemesis: those of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They who have much in common with the ʼself-aggrandizing-nimarisaj ribʼ likes of Wuqubʼ Kaqix, Sipakna, Kʼabʼraqan, Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen in that they are all excellent examples of how not to act in life; how not to speak; how not to treat others on the Face of the Earth but there are those who are ʼdivine examples-saqetalʼ and those are Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej into whom we are about to pour into magical powers of mythic transference in order to become those who are they known and named the Divine Twins as we twin ourselves from within. While at the same time ʼacknowledgingʼ who we are down deep inside and how we will feel the aggression Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; One Death, Seven Death just as we felt it with Wuqubʼ Kaqix, Sipakna, Kabʼraqan, and Omuch Kʼajolabʼ the Four Hundred Boys.

We canʼt help but take this family feud personal; we-the reader-feel like we are getting summonsed by Xibʼalbʼa when their Messengers arrive before IxMuqane. Which makes us think as we say to ourselves: “Not again, another invite and so soon, no way; didnʼt these Boys just start to play?”

Those Two Young Men just picked up the game after finding their Ball and what is theirs in Life; which means they just picked-up the game and all of the sudden they are extended an invitation by those Lords of Xibʼalbʼa; those Lords of the Dead are rather sensitive for being formed and shaped from skull and bone. We love myth because the narrative speeds along to contemplate its life and death issues one after then next.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And that is it; this is the point to be made about the Dead and Deceased. The dead and deceased are very delicate types and the living had to make sure that didnʼt upset them in any way! Because they were very touchy about what went on where they once lived with bodies as fleshed out as any other but now they are Dead who live amongst the Dead and that is why they are so wild about inviting those with so much life to liven up their lives in the Land of the Dead: Xibʼalbʼa. IxMuqane as Matriarch of the Ixim Winaq Tribe speaks to the Emissaries, the Messengers of Xibʼalbʼa and with their arrival one can hear the difference and feel the deference for the Mother of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who will always grieve the loss of her beloved sons who died meaningless, unnecessary deaths by decapitation in the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa: Place of Fear, Place of Intimidation, Place of Trials, Tests, and Ordeal.

IxMuqane is the Head-Woman who rules her household sitting upon her reed mats by her ʼThree Stone Hearthʼ and its benevolent life-giving; life-sustaining fire, where fire equals power and power equals authority and authority is what gives rule and rulership the Sovereign Rulers who rule and reign over their Noble Realm.

IxMuqane is the Mother who provides her people with guidance; she is the Grandmother who sustains her people with her prevailing order and traditional way of spiritual and soulful protection.

IxMuqane is a ʼKʼamol Bʼeyʼ she is a ʼSpiritual Guideʼ who helps her people find their way. We care for her because she cares for her people; her pueblo who we identify with since the reader or listener of Sacred Narrative like the Popol Wuj naturally identifies with the protagonist.

Messengers of the IxMuqane:

Uqʼ; Xpeqʼ; Nimaʼ Kumatzʼ; Nimaʼ Tzʼikin Louse; Toad; Big Snake; Big Falcon Messengers of Death

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
All the Animals that will become part of this long chain of Messengers of Grandmother are in fact Messengers of Death. The Louse, the Toad, the Snake, and the Falcon are the animal emissaries that are particular to Death for each one of them announces the arrival of Death. Each in their own way is a Herald of Death that bears their message within them that says: ʼI arrive to announce Death; Death is announced; I appear to announce Death is coming; and, it is coming your way. Death is coming to you and I am here to announce its arrival.”

So realize this because all the ʼanimals or chikopʼ that are about to appear are Messengers of death beginning with the Louse that is about to fall down from the rafters of the house where the ballgame gear and rubber ball fell from above because it is the Louse that reveals when a person has died. When human beings die the lice that are always there with them on their deathbed get up and wiggle away from the Dead. These Messengers are the Messengers of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who are buried by the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Xibʼalbʼa but have not been buried properly by their sons Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who want to ʼknow the face of their Fathersʼ whoʼs soul is held captive in the Underworld. They are calling on their sons to bring peace to their Ancestral Souls by ʼordering and arrangingʼ their ʼskull and bonesʼ so they can be invoked and remembered in Sacred Ways; in Ancestral Ways; in Ways that are Ordered by the Sacred Count of the Days that give worship to Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu on their Sacred Count of Days.

There will be a profound moment of ʼatonementʼ experienced between Father and Son which is the direction this mythic narrative is moving as it moves down into Xibʼalbʼa and everything that must happen there to ʼpay-backʼ the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa and the grief they cause IxMuqane. Now it is IxMuqane that must send the message sent by Death to the Hero Twins.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This Third Act will come to its climax when the Hero Twins go to the burial place of their Fathers where their Fathersʼ soul are held captive beside the Ballcourt in Xibʼalbʼa. This is why the Sonsʼ goal is not just to play-ball but more importantly to ʼwinʼ the right to ʼknowʼ the ʼFace of the Fathersʼ to then bury them again in proper ritual ways which is the goal of the narrative. This ʼknowingʼ the Fathersʼ Face is the principal victory that is won after overcoming all the many tests and trials in the Houses of Ordeal in Xibʼalbʼa that lay between the Boys ʼdescent and entranceʼ into Xibʼalbʼa and this most transformative experience of ʼknowingʼ the Face of the Dead Father. This is beginning of their Sacred Journey of initiation to become the Sons of their Fathers by breaking and the transcending the bonds of being the providing Son of their Mother and the sustaining Grandson of their Grandmother. Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej thus go from being ʼclever and cunning hunting boysʼ of the Mother and Grandmother to becoming ʼdaring and deadly tricksters sonsʼ of the Father and Grandfather who is none other than the Heart of the Sky. The obstacles that the Hero Twins must overcome in the Houses of Ordeal in Xibʼalbʼa are the obstacles that will bring about the transformation of the warrior soul and trickster character of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who will become the Lords and Rulers of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom as the Sun and Moon of the Age of the Kʼicheʼ Maya. But first the must ʼorder and arrangeʼ the ʼskull and bonesʼ of their Father and Uncle beside the Ballcourt of Xibʼalbʼa. It is here beside the Ballcourt of Xibʼalbʼa that will become the Sacred Burial Grounds where these First Fathers of the Maize People will be invoked and remembered.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are those who create this sacred ritual invocation and remembrance of the Fathers that is known as the ʼNaming of Namesʼ as a Dawning Ceremony to meet the Sun. Yet it is their Grandmother IxMuqane who makes them ʼhardʼ by being ʼrough and toughʼ on them in order not to ʼspoilʼ them in order not to ʼruinʼ them like she ʼspoils and ruinsʼ Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen by keeping them ʼtoo closeʼ to her ʼhearth and heartʼ so that they are never harden. Grandmother IxMuqane never sends them out to be hardened and humbled by the natural ordeals of the Mountain Wilderness like the Hero Twins are. They are those who are sent out of the house for ʼcryingʼ like ʼlittle Yaki Warriorsʼ to be put to sleep on an ant-bed to then be placed in a bed of thorns as Infant Boys. This is how an infant boy becomes a hard young man. IxMuqane is the matriarchal archetype that models the ʼmotheringʼ of both ʼsons and daughtersʼ and this is why she is so very important to our comprehension of the Popol Wuj as an exemplary text on parenting children and grandchildren.

The Hero Twins must die sacrificial deaths to be transformed into powerful Warriors of the Sun and Moon; Warriors of the Day and Night. The Hero Twins will be sacrificed in Xibʼalbʼa like their Fathers but they are vastly different from their Fathers because their Mother –IxKikʼ originate in Xibʼalbʼa like IxKikʼs Father and the Hero Twinsʼ Grandfather- Kuchumakikʼ known as Blood Gatherer who is a Lord of Sacrifice known as Blood-Gatherer. The Boys are Nawal Winaq and because of this they are empowered with the Nawal Genius to dream and imagine the Ancestral Knowledge they need to bring about the transformation of their world. Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej will now attain great powers now that they know what is theirs in life and because of this are able to transform their own souls. IxMuqane becomes the ally of IxKikʼ who is the Daughter of Lord; her Mother-in-Law IxMuqane is also the Daughter of a Lord. This makes these women Noble Rulers of their Noble Realm and so it is they order the way messages are sent and received in her Ancestral Realm which is her home.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: The Home of IxMuqane is the mythic embodiment of a Great House or Nimaʼ Ja of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom which is the Palace House of a Kʼicheʼ Lineage. These Noble Kʼicheʼ Lineages will come to life in the Fourth and Fifth Act of Popol Wuj but IxMuqane shows the way a Woman Ruler must rule her Great House with a great strength. But she must also have a great sense of humor and know how to laugh at the youth that is coming along. In this way IxMuqane must learn to respect the ʼOrderʼ of the Hero Twins and this she does when she walks behind them when they return from the River after the Boys took down their inheritance from up in Grandmotherʼs House. Grandmother wanted to keep Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej for herself so she doesnʼt pass their inheritance on to them. But now she must follow them as the next Generation of the Lords and Rulers of the Junajpu Lineage for they are the Youthful Representatives of the next Generation that will come to lead and defend; guide and protect her Lineage that will live in her Great House-Nimaʼ Ja at the Heart of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. IxMuqane shows the Traditional Maya Way to rule a Home and keep order in the House. So to recap slightly: IxMuqane is best understood as the Matriarch of the Maize People. In this sense she might best be thought of as IxMuqQʼanil: She of the Buried Mazorca of Maize. As Mother Earth IxMuqQʼanil takes in the maize seed as the buried ʼskull-seedʼ of the Maize Ancestors that sprouts out as the return of the descendant as kʼexel or replacement that comes forth from the body of IxMuqQʼanil.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Thus IxMuqane embodies the resilience and resistance of the Maize Beings; Maize Plants who must face drought, flood, heat, sun, predators, hail, frost, wind, fruit bats, thieves who decapitate their heads to steal them as mazorcas from milpa, in short these are the Houses of Ordeal as the House of Tests, Trials and Ordeal of Xibʼalbʼa. IxMuqane must make certain her ʼDescendantsʼ who are her ʼTeeth-Iweey are as hard and enduring as they are tough and resistant as they are strong, supple, giving, and resilient. IxMuqane is the ensoulment and embodiment of the People of Maize for it is she who incarnates their ways with her warm and humorous way of being while at the same time exemplifying the strength and endurance that are known to be innate and inherent characters of her People; of her Pueblo. IxMuqane is the Matriarch who is responsible for keeping the ʼembers burningʼ in her peopleʼs fire. It was ʼbad styleʼ to allow the fire to go out in the Maya Cosmos so IxMuqane is always found in her Home tending her fire or on the Mountain gathering firewood or sustenance or grinding maize at her grinding stone or ordering the lives and deaths of the men and women who live and die in her Imaginal Realm. After all IxMuqane is a Day-Keeper and Diviner; she is a Prayer-maker and a Seer known as AjQʼij-Ilol-Naʼol-AjTzʼiteʼ. IxMuqane is a Kabʼawil in every way. IxMuqane is quite quiet but there is tremendous power in her silences for she is always present in every page of this Sacred History of hers from the very sowing and rooting of the First Words of the Ancient Ancestral Account; IxMuqane is present all the way through the Popol Wuj.

This is her Sky-Earth to Form and Shape as best as she is able; and she is extraordinarily able and infinitely capable to Form and Shape the World of the Sky-Earth as Former and Shaper; Bearer, Begetter; Mother, Father.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
IxMuqane always makes sure her ʼwordʼ is brought to fruition for she is the embodiment of Creation; Creation that come to Fruition through her Forming, her Shaping; her Molding, her Modeling but, she also embodies Destruction as she brings about the total obliteration of those who get in her way: IxMuqane is the Grandmother of Warrior Grandsons. IxMuqane brings forth the complete elimination of her own formations and creations if it should support her greater goals of bringing about the multiply and growing of her People; the growing and multiplying of her Pueblo of Ixim Winaq. Her powers are balanced between the two realms of Creation and Destruction for she is seen as a Female Jaguar-IxBʼalam who is the Mother Goddess of the Mountainside. Now she has a message to send to her Grandsons-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej playing ball on the ballcourt of her Sons-Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu and she will get the message sent with her Earth-Sky messengers of Death; all of them are significant in some sort of specific sort of way for each one of the Messengers embodies the different ʼlevelsʼ of death from the Face of the Earth to the Heart of the Sky. Let us take-up the road to send the urgent message from the Lords of Death known as Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame. Let us take-up the road with the Messengers so we can begin our journey with the Twins and their transformative adventure through the Maya Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa.

Ixmuqane spoke to the Messengers of Xibʼalbʼa: “Utz bʼa la! Fine then! Very well! They shall go as they are summonsed, you, oh Messengers; they shall go as they are called you, oh Envoys of Noble Lords; you, oh Emissaries of Noble Lords.” “Let it be known that they-the Boys-shall be summoned by me as they have been summoned by you; you oh Messengers of Xibʼalbʼa,” said Grandmother. Then the Messengers left, they returned from where they had come. Grandmotherʼs heart was just finished off, “Who shall I entrust to summons my Grandsons-ri Wiy? Is this not a message for them from Xibʼalbʼa? Is this not the same as when the Messengers came before their Fathersʼ went off to die there in Xibʼalbʼa?” said the Old Woman-ri Atiʼt-Grandmother.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Sweetly she wept sadly; sweetly she wept softly; when she wept sweetly there in her house; there in her home all alone-kus choqʼ pa ja utukel. It was then that a Louse-Ukʼ fell down from above; IxMuqane saw it and picked-up. Immediately she placed in the palm of her hand. There the Louse wiggled quickly ran across the palm of her that she opened up wide for the little louse to run across: chimalmatibʼ.

“You my grandson-at wiy, you my tooth-at wiy, you my descendant-at wiy, wouldnʼt you like it if I sent you on an errand? Wouldnʼt it be good if I were to send you with this message that must be sent to my Grandsons there on their ballcourt where they play every day?” This was all she had to say to the Louse there in the palm of her hand when she said:

“ʼJust now Messengers have arrived with your Grandmotherʼ you will say. ʼYou are to come in Seven Daysʼ say the Messengers; the Messengers of Xibʼalbʼaʼ says your Grandmother, you are to say, when you leave your message with them in this way,” she said to the little Louse that dropped down from up above there in the House.

This then was when he went off running just wiggling his way down the road. Sitting there by the side of the Road was a Boy; his name was Tamasul, the Toad-ri Xpeq: “Where are you going?” asked then the Toad; the Toad who sat by the side of the Road who asked the Louse from in the House.

“My word is in my belly, I am going to leave a message with the Boys,” said the Louse to the Boy; Tamasul; the Toad that sat there beside the Road. “Utz bʼa la, but it looks like you canʼt really run very fast,” said the Toad, on the Road to the Louse from the House.

“Would you like it if I swallowed you? Then you would see just how fast we would go as we make our way hopping down the road,” said the Toad. “Utz bʼa laʼ,” said the Louse-Ukʼ to the Toad-Xpeq in the Road-pa ri Bʼey. This then was when the Louse from the House was licked-up by the Toad in the Road.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They went far with the Toad but still, they didnʼt really get very far; very fast. That was when One Big Snake-Jun Nima Kumatz came along there where Tamazul was in the Road: Saqikʼas was the name of the One Big Snake-Jun Nima Kumatz who came upon the Toad in the Road with Louse from the House who he had licked-up with the message he had swallowed in his Mouth.

“Where are you going; you, oh Tamasul, my Boy?” was asked Tamazul, the Boy Toad by Saqikʼas, the One Big Snake Jun Nima Kumatz.

“Apa katbʼe wi, at Tamasul, kʼajol?” Xuchax chik ri Xpeq rumal Saqikʼas ri Jun Nima Kumatz.

“I am a Messenger, my word is in my belly-In samajel, kʼo nutzij chi nupam,” said then the Toad, Tamazul to the One Big Snake, Saqikʼas, known as the White Sparker; Sacred Spark; Bright Life. “You are not moving very fast, that is all I can see, while I would arrive there much, much more quickly,” said then the One Big Snake-ri Jun Nima Kumatz-then to the Boy Toad Tamazul-ri Xpeq.

“Letʼs go-Katojo; Katojoq-swallow me,” said the Serpent.

Sacred Order Divine Hierarchy of Sustenance

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Snake was instructed by the Toad in the Road to be swallowed-up by the One Big Snake who was ready to carry the Toad down the Road as his Load with the Louse in his Mouth; the Louse from Grandmotherʼs House who the Boy Toad Tamazul licked-up as his Load from the Road so they could go real fast to deliver the Message to the Boys at Court that they swept out every day where they play the Rubberball game with the Rubberball in their very own way. And so would begin this Maya-Mesoamerican revelation of the sacred order of the Natural World that was and is an Animated Natural World that has its Natural Order that is a Natural Hierarchy of it ʼswallowingʼ itself as Sacred Sustenance as Insects are swallowed by Amphibians; Amphibians that are swallowed by Reptiles; Reptiles that are swallowed by Birds; Birds that are swallowed by Mammals; Mammals that swallow them All… This is the story of the ʼChikop-Animalitosʼ that swallow one another in a fine kind of Divine Order that is a Sacred Order that is Natural Hierarchy of the Natural World: Louse to Toad to Serpent to Bird to the Boys and their Blow-gun Shot and their healing rubber sheath of rubber skin of this rubber cure known as ʼSangre de Sacrificio-Lotz Kikʼ that is sliced thin to win the day by regaining the eye-sight of this One Big Bird Wakʼo, Wako it name.

That then was when the One Big Snake-Jun Nima Kumatz known as Saqikʼas-the speedster toad eater swallowed the Boy Toad whole right there in the Road, poor Tamasul.

So now it is that when snakes take their sustenance they do as Saqikʼas did when he gulped down Tamasul headfirst as is the way for Toads to be swallowed ʼjust soʼ.

Chanim, Chanim-quickly, quickly; fast, fast then did he go, the One Big Snake-ri Jun Nima Kumatz, who sped off down the road.

And then the Snake was come upon by Wak, Wak who was One Big Bird, Jun Nima Tzʼikin.

Laughing Falcon is one of his names: Wako, Wako is his cry.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
He was mentioned as the Messenger of Jun Raqan Kaqulja Ukʼuʼx Kaj. Wok or Wak is the Ilol or Seer of Heart of the Sky so he was a natural choice to perform this work of Messenger who carried the message to Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who were those that listened to the voice of Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja the Kabʼawil who was the Divine Voice of the Heart of the Sky. And just like that, this Jun Nima Tzʼikin, this One Big Bird, Wak or Wok, devoured the One Big Snake none as Saqikʼas. That is the way Laughing Falcons swallow their prey in the Mountains today, swallowing snakes from head to tail just like snakes always swallow toads without fail by beginning with the head and ending with the tail; and so it goes Snakes are swallowed head to toe. Wak swallowed the One Big Snake whole to then fly directly over to where the Boys were ʼseenʼ by Wak on the Ballcourt that Wak could ʼseeʼ was well swept. This is where Wak settled down; Wak settled atop the ornate crest of that finely adorned crown of the Ballcourt.

Wak just perched himself up there on the finely finished crown that ringed around the ornamented crest of the Ballcourt where the Boys were playing down below as content as could be; all alone; completely on their own.

Wak steadied himself easily on the crown up on the crest of ballcourt known as utzʼutzʼil jom-ʼcorn tassel-utzʼutzʼil-corn flower.ʼ

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This headdress crest was an ornate crown that was an adorned cement crest of the Classic Maya Ballcourt of the Rubberball Playing Maize People with their ʼCorn Tassel-Tzʼutuj-Corn Flowerʼ embellishment that was seen as a ʼflower-headdressʼ that crowns the Ballcourt just as it crowns the maize of the milpa as a flowering headdress: Tzʼutuj as this Corn Tassel is known. Now we are on the Ballcourt of the Face of the Earth; this is not the Underworld Ballcourt but this is Ballcourt that is directly overhead the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who are down below listening to the living; the Dead are the Ancestors are they not? Who else can they be but the Dead Ancestors so imagine what this says about how the living must ʼtake good careʼ not to annoy the Dead; to not bother the Ancestors by making a lot of noise on top of their Underworld abode in Xibʼalbʼa.

There below were the ballplayers of the Ixim Winaq known as Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who were happy and content playing ball-kekikot kechaajik not even stopping until they heard his terrifying call-Wako, Wako-and that was when they saw that One Big Bird; Jun Nima Tzʼikin.

One Big Bird; Jun Nima Tzʼikin whose cry just called out his name; his name that was his call to fame: Wako; Wako; Food is Here; Food is Here as the One Big Bird calls out letting everyone known someone is going to get eaten alive. This is the call of the Laughing Falcon who says: Wak kʼo! Wak kʼo! Here I am! Here I am! Or Wak ko! Wak ko! Here is a Hard Noble One! Here is Hard Noble One! Remember this call because the Hero Twins will be calling out their Name to be acknowledged as Noble Lords who are present before all the rest: Oj Wa! Oj Wa! We are Here! We are Here! We are Sustenance! We are Sustenance! Oj Wa! Oj Wa!

And so it was that as soon as Wakʼ arrived he began crying out his name; he just named his name again and again: Wak kʼo! Wak kʼo! Food is here! Food is here! Here I am! Here I am! Wa Kʼo! Wa Kʼo! “Who is crying? Who is calling? Letʼs get our blowguns,” cried the Boys, the Sons who instantly looked up to where Wakʼ called out from the crest that crowned the Ballcourt.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Wakʼ called out from the tippy-top of their Fathersʼ ballcourt where he was able to see all there was to see. But he never could have imagined what he never saw coming. Those two Blowgun Boys fired their blowguns at Wakʼ who was hit immediately in the eye by their dead-eye shooting of their stone hard blowgun shot; their rock-hard clay blowgun ball that was blowgun shot: puff, puff...puuj…puuj...puuh...puuh...

This One Big Bird-Jun Nima Tzʼikin was shot by one of their blowgun balls; one of their ʼhard-clay-ballsʼ of their blowgun hit Wako smack in the very center of the very pit of his eye-taqal ubʼaq wubʼ.

Which in Kʼicheʼ shapes a sonorous sound of sight and syllabic symmetry to form the sounds that makes a shamanic sort of statement that is a real revelation of a tricksterʼs signification of a translation that goes like this: ʼtaqal ubʼaq wubʼ chubʼaqʼ uwach-its blowgun bone of the blowgun shot hit the bulls-eye of the bone-hard pit of his eye. Just like the shot that hit Wuqubʼ Kaqix; just like the ʼpitzʼ that hit IxKikʼ right smack in the center of the palm of her right hand-taqal ubʼaq wubʼ Ouch! These guys are real ʼdead-eyeʼ Blow-gun Boys who will show their hunting prowess as warriors who will become Kʼicheʼ

Warriors who ʼhit their markʼ when it comes to shooting ʼBows and Arrowsʼ before the Castilians come in the Fourth and Fifth Act of Popol Wuj.

Wak just whirled around before fluttering down to eventually hit the ground in a puff of dust; Wak was down on the ground where the Boys went running to see what was there to be found.

“Where did you come from?-Jupa apetik?” blasted the Boys wanting to know from whence did this crying bird come.

Wak just respond as he knew he must: “My word is in my belly-Kʼo bʼa nutzij chi nupam-there is just a bit of my truth within me. But first you must heal my eye then I will tell you. If not, then naught; if not, then no!” he said to the Two Boys who held him down tight like another big bird of his kind.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They did not realizing they shot a Seer-Ilol-Watchman of the Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj who was this One Big Bird who swallowed the Snake head to tail; a Bird who takes his sustenance like a Snake? Could this be some sort of mythic mistake? Was the Boys shooting this Crying Bird fake; for wasnʼt Wakʼo a watchman worker of the Heart of the Sky-Jun Raqan Kaqulja who was a ʼnagual-nahual-nawalʼ of the Lords of Death-Ce Miquiztli-Jun Kame our friend who is an Enemy on Both Sides the one who goes ʼunnamedʼ as the Smoking Mirror that we known as Tezcatlipoca as a bird whose cry is the call of Death as it is said?

The Trickster Lord Smoking Mirror; Trickster Deity Tezcatlipoca lurks close by yet this is not made clear which is just fine because asking rational questions of a mythic narrative is a sort of literalist-materialist crime of the settler-colonist mind. This is one reason I ask it; to make the reader aware of this ʼforeign-kaxlanʼ kind of mind that we can bring to the seeing and knowing of Ancient Indigenous Masterpiece of Mythic Narrative formed and shaped from an ancient archaic sort of indigenous type of magical mind that is molded and modeled from a mythical sort of magical kind of mystical type of nawal soul and its seriously playful sort of thinking that is founded in the Anima Mundi or the Soul of the World that is the World Soul where the ʼserious play-serio ludareʼ come to life here in this section of Popol Wuj.

“Utz bʼa la! Very well!” they said.

“Very well, we must then heal your eye,” they said with a sigh. So this then was when they shaved a thin sheath of skin from their rubberball-ri Kikʼ.

Then they placed that thin sheath skin over the eye of Wak. This was known as Lotz Kikʼ or ʼSangre de Sacrificioʼ which they used to heal wounds, just like today when people heal their wounds with thin sheaths of thinly sliced rubber.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Instantly then was this big beautiful eye of this beguiling bird cured. Once again the vision of Wak-Laughing Falcon came out well; so that just like that Wak had his vision back which as a Seer-Ilol was everything and more because now that he was healed by these two magician healers he could see better now than he saw before.

And so it was the Boys who mused that if Wakʼ could see again then he could certainly speak again; which was precisely what they wanted him to do to reveal the message he held within him; the message that was sent for them-the Boys-to receive; the message from their Grandmother sent directly to them!

“Say it then,” they said to Wak, the Laughing Falcon; who without any further need for them to plead the One Big Bird agreed to bring-up the One Big Snake-Saqikʼas who was known for his lightning speed.

Thus this One Big Snake-Saqikʼas was released from the tight squeeze he was in there within; so that he-Saqikʼas was only too pleased to be freed from where heʼd been kept inside the One Big Bird who called out Wak Kʼo, Wak Kʼo: Here he is! Here he is! Food is here! Food is here! Wa Kʼo! Wa Kʼo! Which he repeated and repeated to the Two Hunters; to the Two Blow-gun Boys who called out: Yes indeed! Yes indeed! We ya! We ya!

“Speak; Speak Out! Kachʼawoq! Speak; Speak Out! Kachʼawoq!” they said to the Snake; Kumatz; Saqikʼas; White Spark! Bright Life! “Fine! We!” said Saqikʼas.

The One Big Snake that brought up the Toad head first and looking down the Road relieved to no longer be carried about as the inner load of the Serpent inside the Bird where he never heard all that was bestowed on the Toad and conferred on the Serpent as a gift given by the Bird to the Boys who want to known what Tamazul knew which was what was the message that he had swallowed when he licked-up the Louse on the Road not so terrible long ago.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“What is your message? Speak out-Kattzijonoq! Say it now!” Toad was told in a voice that was quite bold as if to want to scold this Boy who was the Toad of the Road and the Message that was told. “There is a short message that is the truth that I bear within me-Kʼo bʼa nutzij chi nupam-There is a little bit of truth within me this is my message!” said the Toad, Xpeq; the Boy; Tamazul. So then he tried again to spit-up what he swallowed; but he could not through-up to through-out the Louse; just spittle came from his mouth. He tried but, alas, there was nothing that came up, no matter how hard he tried he couldnʼt find the little Louse that was lost in his mouth.

So then the Boys beat it out of him: “You Trickster!-At Kʼaxtokʼ-You Cheat! You think your deceit can mislead us?” they said-xuchaʼxik and so then they kicked him hard right on his big boney buttocks. Poor Boy they busted the bones on his butt from kicking him so hard from behind looking for what they would never find; for nothing sprouted out of the poor Toad no matter how hard they hit Tamasul when the Boys did their all to dislodge that little Louse from inside the Boy Toadʼs toothy mouth.

Once again they kicked him hard on his butt making a bad bump on his boney toad rump; they thought they could knock it out of him by booting him on the bones of his buttocks but nothing came from making such a furious fuss except for a big bad bump on his protruding rumpus.

He tried even harder to do what they asked of him, but just a drop of dribble drabbled down out of him to then slide down his chin to then drip; to then drop; to drabble then drop as his spittle just dropped from his mouth like spit that trickled like dribble that just hung there as a thin thread of spittle: chuchubʼ uchiʼ.

Maybe he hadnʼt swallowed that Louse after all so Tamasul asked them to take another look inside of his mouth a bit more maybe he was lost where he could be found somewhere down in his teeth and his gums where he swallowed all the tears heʼd been crying and the constant dribble of his spittle.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Then the Boys scratched about in the depths of the Toadʼs mouth. They scratched about to then search about his wide open jaw; they looked up and down, they looked all about then they stopped; this was when they saw what they saw: that lazy little Louse had gone anywhere at all.

He was right there in Toadʼs mouth sound asleep just sleeping like a log. The Messenger was never swallowed; he was right there where you could see him in his teeth doing nothing at all other than sleeping without a worry in the world. It was just ʼas ifʼ the Louse had been swallowed by the Toad when he opened his lower jaw that formed a great maw in the mouth. In the mouth of this big mouthed Toad whose throat looked just like a dark hollow when the Boy Toad opened his mouth wide and swallowed; and that is why this little Louse wasnʼt going allow himself to be swallowed he didnʼt want to have the feeling of being devoured.

And so it was that Toad was defeated. It is not clear what they gave him as the food that became his sacred sustenance.

But since he couldnʼt run fast he quickly became the sustenance of serpents and snakes who swallowed every toad they met up with on the road.

For the toad is truly the favorite food of serpents, who, as you know, love to swallow Toads whole; right side up or upside down, it doesnʼt matter as long as they enter head-first.

When the Little Louse was ready they both said at once: “Speak it! Say it! Tell it! Katzijonoq!”

So this was when he spoke; this was when Louse gave his word; this is when he relayed their message; their message that was revealed thus:

body: “This is what your Grandmother says to say to you, you oh Engendered Sons of a Father-Ix Kʼajolabʼ: Go summons them; for Messengers have come looking for you with a message that comes from them, those of Xibʼalbʼa; a summons that came here for you from Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; a message that came from the Messengers of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa; Messengers who were sent by One Death, Seven Death as their Messengers with the message of the Lords, Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame, that says this: “In Seven Days they are to come down here so we can play ball with them down here; down here in Xibʼalbʼa. Bring all that is theirs; they are to bring their Ball-playing Equipment-Ketzʼabʼal; their Ball, Kikʼ; their Yoke, Bʼate; their Arm guards, Pachqʼabʼ; their Skins, Tzʼum.” ““Come, come liveʼn things up down here with us; with some enlivening play you will come to life here!”” say the Lords,ʼ said their Messengers,” says your Grandmother,”ʼ the Old Woman who sent me to send for you; I, who was there with her when she cried and called for you,” said the Louse. “This is why your Grandmother sent me, to send you, this message, sent to you, from the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa,” said the Louse-ri Ukʼ-Messenger of the Lords of Death.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: “Could it be true?” wondered the Boys when they heard what they heard; turning it over in their head; thinking it over in their heart. Immediately they returned, arriving there where their Grandmother was waiting for them; when they went to take council with her; when they went to take leave of the Old Women; when they went to leave instructions with their Grandmother: IxMuqane. And this then is what they said: “We will be going now; we will be on our way; You, Our Grandmother, we just wish to take leave of you by leaving you with ʼour wordʼ that are a sign of ʼour truthʼ which is this that we say: ʼEach one of us has left sown a Cane of Maize here in the Center of Our House we have left it sown. This is a sign-retal of our death when they are dried out: Could they be dead? You will say when they are dried out. Then when their sprout comes back, you might ask could they be alive once again? You will say then. You, Our Grandmother; and, you Our Mother donʼt cry; you who are the Moon. This is a sign of Our Word; Our Truth; Our Live that we shall leave with you,” they said when they went out; One was sown by Junajpu, One then was planted by Ixbʼalamkej. Just in the House did they plant them out; not in the Mountain; and not there in the Wet Earth either; just there in the Dry Earth in Middle of the House were they left planted.

This is that which is written out here below in Maya Kʼicheʼ that talks of Maize in very esoteric syllabic ways that I feel is too involved to bring about here in its entirety so let us leave you with an idea of what we are getting at with ʼsyllable by syllableʼ invocation of these Sacred Word of Departure: qakan aj-our mazorca of maize; jujun-seed by see; qatik-we plant, we sow; wa-sustenance; aj-cane, corn, mazorca of maize; chun-lime of nixtamal; ikʼ-moon; nikʼ-flower; aj jal-mazorca of maize, hard head of maize; och-small little elote; xchi-to clear the milpa for planting; kat-to burn the brush; qʼat-to cut and clear milpa; wi-head of maize; tux-sprout; kʼas- spark; kʼas-life; kam-vine…and on go the syllable to pronounced in a staccato way to bring out another sort of magical invocation of the mythical enchantment of maize as the sacred sustenance of the Maize People whose Maize Lords are about to descend down into the Underworld to begin their Initiatory Ordeal of Ritual Initiation. Letʼs enter the Imaginal Realm of Xibʼalbʼa with sufficient understanding to enter that Mundus Imaginalis with the dignity that comes with the deep respect of Maya Culture through our entering an interpretive framework that provide the Original Maya Deep Structure of the Mythic Archetypal Mind of Popol Wuj. In this way our ʼImagination of Matterʼ will be filled with the Nawal Essence of the Maize People: Ixim Winaq.

“Joʼ na, Ix QaTiʼt, xa Oj pixabʼay Iwe. Waʼe kʼute retal qatzij: ʼXchiqakanaj jujun xchiqatik chi re wa aj chunikʼajal qochoch xchiqatik wi. Are retal qakamik we chichaqijik: Ma pa xekamik? Kixchaʼ ta chichaqijik. We kʼut ta chipe utux e pa kʼaslik? Kixchaʼ kʼut. Ix Qatiʼt, Ix pu Qachuch mixoqʼik. Kʼo retal qatzij kakanajik iwuk,ʼ xechaʼ ta xebʼek; Jun xutik Junajpu, Jun chi kʼu xtikow Ixbʼalamkej. Xa pa Ja xutik wi; mana pa Juyubʼ taj; ma nay pu pa Rax Ulew taj; xa pa Chaqiʼj Ulew Chunikʼajal upa Kochoch, xkitik wi kanoq.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: Maize People Sacred Lifecycle of Maize ʼNawal Beings, Nawal Ancestorsʼ We are Maize-Oj Wa I feel important to transcribe the original Maya Kʼiche text because within it is found a ʼsecretʼ sacred sort of Ancient Ancestral Writing that when read syllable by syllable brings out the sound of this message that the Boys, the Sons, the Twins Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej leave with their Grandmother and Mother. It is here at this point that we must stop and consider what is going on in this sacred writing of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Kingdom because it is here that we find ʼmagical writingʼ that tells the entire story of the Lifecycle of Maize in ʼsecret sacred speechʼ ʼnames the namesʼ of the Stages of Transformation of Maize from sowing to growing to flowering to fruiting to drying back and dying to be reborn again. This is the also the Ritual Lifecycle of the Maize People that is ʼplayed-outʼ through their Rites of Passage; Rites of Initiation; and the Sacred Journeys of Sacred Pilgrimage that took the Kʼicheʼ Maya to those sacred citadels and temples that rose-up beside the Sea. So you can either read on here or jump over this reflective interpretation to take up the translation of this precious Mesoamerican Myth known and named Popol Wuj. This passage tells of Lifecycle of Maize in very specific ways that bring out the imagination of maize as ʼsacred matter, sacred materialʼ that are ʼnawal beings, nawal ancestorsʼ who are living beings that are sown to then grow to then flower and fruit into ʼbeautiful good- looking handsome heads of maizeʼ before dying back into ʼrotten canesʼ to be buried to then disintegrate in order to return to the earth to rise-up again reborn from the seed sown back in the milpa of maize.

body:
This lifecycle of the Maize Lords Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej is planted in our imagination as the ʼsoul of the Popol Wujʼ in order that the idea of the ʼimagination of matterʼ comes alive in our ʼmythic imaginationʼ of this Sacred Scripture of the Kʼicheʼ Maya. For this Book of Council tells us the Myth of Maize that mirrors the Yearly Lifecycle of the Maize People as acted out as Long Performances and Long Recitations that were performed and recited by their Noble Lords to be lived out by their Beloved Vassals and Loyal Subjects who gather together here in order to Celebrate Council with One-an-Other in order to write down their Ancient Word; in order to inscribe their Ancestral Account; in order to implant the Divine Word of their Sacred Story of Popol Wuj.

Above then is the Maya Kʼicheʼ incantation of the planting of maize as the embodiment mythic metaphorical lives of the Maize Twins; Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who are saying: ʼWe are Maize; Oj Wa; this is Us as We who are Maize; Oj Wa; We are Here; We are Maize; We who are the Maize that we plant in Center of Grandmotherʼs House; Grandmotherʼs House that is the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew. This is ʼOur Word that is Our Truthʼ that we leave so you know who We are as We who are the Maize Lords; the Maize Beings; the Maize Deities who transform through our ritual birth, life, death, and rebirth that are experienced through the sacred rites and rituals of initiation in Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This is it! This…is…it… this is the Ancient Ancestors become Maize by planting there essence as ʼAjʼ which is Cane of Maize; which is a Head of Maize; which is the ritual naming of the name of Maize. For this is where the Maize Deities sow their Nawal in the Center of their Mothers House. The very same House of Grandmother were Grandmother will leave Maize Planted when she eventually plants Four Sacred Sowings of Maize in here House in order to Deify Maize for all time; forever more: Saqil Amaqil. This sowing of Maize in the Center of the House of Grandmother is that which is destiny; which is identity; which is being; which is essence; which is the Nawal of the Maize Lord who is the One known as Maize: Aj. The Boys, the Sons, the Twins plant their essence as ʼAjʼ in Grandmotherʼs House as Men-Aj who are Maize-Aj each one is a Lord: Aj-Aw or He of Desire; He of Longing; He of Appetite; He of Becoming: Aj Aw. Aw is the verbal root of those that plant maize as related to us by Abbé Charles Etienne Brasseur de Bourbourg who speaks of the verbal particle Aw as something sacred; something divine; golden necklace; to sow maize; awas a command. Aj is the ʼbastón or vara or staffʼ of the Noble Office of Noble Lords and their Authority. We speak of Ajaw as Noble Lords which is proper and right yet their essence is that of those who plant the bastón of the Maize Plant that is the Cane-Aj of Maize-Aj. This is a World of Maize of those who are Maize People who are those who plant Aj to be known as Ajaw!

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is written in order that the reader understand how absolutely essential and immanent the idea that the Lords JunAjPu and IxBʼalamKej are Maize Deities who originate in this sacred act of their ʼplanting maizeʼ in the House of the Grandmother. This word ʼAjʼ is always translated literally as Cane of Maize or Head of Maize when in truth the word Aj that is the name Aj is the divine being known as Aj to become the Ajaw who is he who plants maize as the Lord of Maize or ri Ajaw rech ri Aj or the Lord of the Maize. These are Maize Men who are Men of Maize spoken of in Maya Kʼicheʼ as Ixim Acha- Hombres de Maize-Ixim Achijabʼ or Maize Men who are Maize Warriors as Rain Men known as Achi Jabʼ which is a fine sort of divine play on words that are names that are grounded in the essence of the Nawal Aj of the Ixim Winaq. This is the Maya Maize Metaphor that says Man is Maize just as Maize is Men! This is the One-Jun Cane-Aj of Maize-Aj that is planted; that is sown by each of the Boys who are the Sons of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu left with the Grandmother and Mother to be raised up as the descendants of the First Fathers of Maize known to us well as those named and known as Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

These Boys, these Sons plant their essence in Center of the Patio of the House of Maize Grandmother Ixmuqane and their Moon Mother IxKikʼ to plant in order to establish the ʼconnection and communicationʼ of the Maize Lineage that forms and shapes the ʼStaff of Lineage-Ajʼ that is the ʼTree of Lineage-Cheʼʼ that stands as the pillar-raqan that holds up the House of the Earth; House of the Sky that is the House of the Sky-Earth that is the Ancestral Home of the Maize People that is the Realm that is the Territory that is the Sovereignty of IxMuqane who is the Great Mother Earth that ʼweepsʼ and IxKikʼ the Moon that ʼcriesʼ as they prey and plead for their Sons and Grandsonsʼ life, death, and rebirth in Xibʼalbʼa so that ʼmightʼ return to the Face of the Earth to their Grandmother and Mother who are there beside their Sacred Fire that burn warm and bright at the Center of their House.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This then is the Mesoamerican-Maya mythic image and mythic metaphor of Men as Maize; Men as Ballcourt; Men as Ballplayers; Men as Road; and, Women as Home, as Earth, as Moon, as Milpa, as Hearth, as Magic Transformation, as Incense, as Divination, as Storytelling Myth-makers whose Hearts are made warm by Song and Music in Lived that are filled with Canes of Maize that are embody the Ancestral Soul of their Twin Grandsons, Twin Sons who as Maize will fill the ʼCompoundʼ or ʼSitioʼ where the Inner Patio is this Noble Place that is Ancestral Palace of Sacred Rule and Divine Authority of the Matriarch IxMuqane of the Ixim Winaq. For it is ʼShe of the Buried Mazorca of Maize or Ix-Muq-Qʼanil is She of the Buried Maize Seed or Ix-Muq-Kan-Eey who is followed in her ʼfootstepsʼ by her Grandsons who do as she does as the Grandmother of Maize who is the Mother of Maize who is Maize both Body and Soul. These are her Grandsons who do as their Grandmother does when they sow Canes-Aj of Maize that is the Nawal Essence of the Maize Lords: JunAjPu, IxBʼalamkej who are named with names that embody the Place of Origin thick with Abundance; Place of Origin thick with Maize. So let us return to the iconic and emblematic speech of the Hero Twins who speak as One to their Grandmother and Mother when they leave them with departing words that are words of left when the Boys take leave of those who they dearly love and know this is the end of their lives lived together with their Mother IxKikʼ in the home of Ixmuqane. They will leave but they will not return as they left for they are going to die an initiatory death to then ʼrise-upʼ again as Nawal Ajaw who as Powerful Transforming Tricksters will change and transform the Sky-Earth to then ascend into the Sky as the Sun and Moon. This is it; this is the great speech of the Hero Twins: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

This is a Sign from Us left for You IxMuqane A Sign of Our Journey through Xibʼalbʼa A Sign of Our Ritual Initiation through Life, Death, and Rebirth

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Let us then return to where we left off above when wished to orient the reader to this most empowering speech of ʼtaking leaveʼ of Mother and Grandmother. These words of departure that when we sound them out ʼsyllable by syllableʼ reveal the ʼchanging and transformingʼ ʼessenceʼ of the lifecycle of a Cane of Maize-Aj; a Head of Maize-Wi that is the Nawal of Maize: Aj.

“Joʼ na, Ix QaTiʼt: We are going now, you our Grandmother. We have come to say good-bye; to say farewell; for we are here to take leave of you. Here then is a sign of Our Word; here then is a sign of Our Truth; here then is a sign of Our Way of Life: QaTzij. This then is a sign of ʼusʼ that ʼweʼ are leaving with ʼyouʼ to remember ʼusʼ by as ʼweʼ take leave of ʼyouʼ. Each one of us will plant a Cane of Maize-Aj here; just One Cane of Maize will we leave sown here in Our House; we shall plant it in the center of Our House-Qochoch; we shall plant one head- xchiqatik wi-we shall sow it out right here in the Middle of the House; in the Center of the House.”

“Here then is the sign of our death when we dry-up you will say when you ask: ʼCould it be that they have died? This is what you will say then when it has dried out; when the Cane dies and dries-out; when the cane dries-out and dies. But then when they sprout back you will ask: ʼAre they once again alive? Are they alive once again?ʼ This is perhaps what you will say when you ask if they-the Canes-have sprouted back to life; when they sprout back again these Canes of Maize.

“This is what you will say, perhaps, you, oh Our Grandmother-Ix Qatiʼt and you Our Mother-Ix Qachuch-do not cry-mixoqʼik-you Woman of the Moon-Ixoq- Ikʼ, you IxKikʼ Mother of the Rubberball; Mother of Ball-players; donʼt cry at our going away; our taking leave; our saying farewell; donʼt cry at our saying good- bye.”

“This is a sign of Our Word-QaTzij-Our Truth, Our Way, Our Tradition- QaTzij that we leave with you,” they said-xechaʼ those of the ʼSacred Sustenance- Echaʼ this is what they said when they took leave of their Grandmother and Mother. Then they went about planting the maize, One-Jun was planted by Jun AjPu; One-Jun was planted by Ix-Bʼalam-Kej.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Just in the house did they plant it, they did not plant it in the mountains, nor did they plant it in the wet earth either; just in the dry ground found in the patio of their house did they leave it planted; the seeds that would become heads of maize, the seeds that would become the canes of maize; the heads on the canes of maize that each One-Jun of the Boys, each One-Jun of the Sons left planted there in the Center of Grandmotherʼs House when they left Maize planted in the Middle of their Grandmothers House.

Sowing of Maize Seed Magical Incantation; Mystical Invocation Mythical Enchantment

Let us sow within our imagination this magical, mythical, mystical incantation of the Maize People left to them by their Divine Ancestors; their Divinities; their Kabʼawil who brought their Tradition of the Sowing of Maize Seed to life by ʼplanting maizeʼ in ʼGrandmotherʼs Houseʼ which is to say within the Heart of the Earth where maize is sown to be grow and grow until it is fully grown into the flowering and fruiting heads of the Lords of Maize: Jun-Aj-Pu; Ix-Bʼalam-Kej.

This then is when it gives thousands of replacements seen as the thousands of seeds found within the husk of head of the Maize Lords; seeds that look like the ancestral teeth of Grandmother and the ancestral skull of Grandfather; teeth and skull that appear to be ʼlong goneʼ yet are never really dead.

They are never really dead because once they are buried within the womb of the Earth they come sprouting back to life to begin their sacred lifecycle once again. This is just as it has always been since ʼtime immemorialʼ when the hand of the Divine Ancestors took up this sacred sustenance to sow it in the ground to then tend it until it came to fruition in its fruiting into perfect heads of maize which is to say into the heads of the Maize Lords; the Hero Twins; as it is said: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej as they are named.

body:
Let us sound out this incantation that is a taking of leave; that is an invocation upon the Twins; the Boys; the Sons making it clear there is a way for their Grandmother and Mother to know how they are by knowing in which phase of their sacred lifecycle that they find themselves in. This is that magical story of the People of Maize told through the mythical narrative that reveals the essence of the Maya Culture through the expression, revelation, and recitation of the Mesoamerican Civilization.

This is the culture and civilization where Maize climbs up and out of the Underworld of Death to live again on the Face of the Earth to flower and fruit beneath the Sun and Moon of the Sky both Day and Night in the Darkness and in the Light.

This is that story told here; this is that story revealed here; this is the invocation recited here through this short enchantment of the Maize People when their Sacred Sustenance was first sown in Grandmotherʼs House; Grandmotherʼs Patio known as Grandmotherʼs Sacred Sitio; there at the very center of her House where the life, death, and rebirth of the Hero Twins is revealed in the mirror of existence that is experienced at the very heart of Grandmother House; the House of IxMuqane. Let us sound it out one more time before moving on.

When Knowledge is Vitally Important Maya Say Everything Three Times This is the Heart of the Maya Myth of Maize This is it; Here it is; This is the Nawal Essence

“Joʼ na, Ix QaTiʼt, xa Oj pixabʼay Iwe. Waʼe kʼute retal qatzij: Xchiqakanaj jujun xchiqatik chi re wa aj chunikʼajal qochoch xchiqatik wi. Are retal qakamik we chichaqijik: Ma pa xekamik? Kixchaʼ ta chichaqijik. We kʼut ta chipe utux e pa kʼaslik? Kixchaʼ kʼut. Ix Qatiʼt, Ix Pu Qachuch mixoqʼik. Kʼo retal qatzij kakanajik iwuk,ʼ xechaʼ ta xebʼek Jun xutik Junajpu, Jun chi kʼu xtikow Ixbʼalamkej. Xa pa Ja xutik wi, mana pa Juyubʼ taj, ma nay pu pa Rax Ulew taj; xa pa Chaqiʼj Ulew chunikʼajal upa kochoch, xkitik wi kanoq.”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“We are going now, you our Grandmother. We have come to say, good-bye; to say farewell; for we are here to take leave of you. Here then is a sign of Our Word; here then is a sign of Our Truth; here then is a sign of Our Life: QaTzij: We are leaving you with something to remember us by. Each One of Us shall plant here a Cane of Maize-Aj; a Cane of Maize is what we shall plant; we shall plant it in the center of Our House-Qochoch; we shall plant it in- xchiqatik wi-we shall sow it out. “Here then is the sign of our death when we dry-up you will ask: ʼCould it be that they have died? This is what you will say then when it has dried out; when the Cane dries out and dies. But then when they sprout back you will ask: ʼAre they alive once again?ʼ This perhaps is what you will ask when they sprout back again.”

“This is what you will say, perhaps, you, oh Our Grandmother-Ix Qatiʼt and you Our Mother-Ix Qachuch-do not cry-mixoqʼik-you Woman of the Moon-Ixoq-Ikʼ, you IxKikʼ Mother of the Rubberball; Mother of Ball-players.”

“This is a sign of Our Word-QaTzij-Our Truth, Our Way, Our Tradition-QaTzij that we leave with you,” they said-xechaʼ those of the ʼSacred Sustenance-Echaʼ this is what they said when they took leave of their Grandmother and Mother.” Then they went about planting the maize, One-Jun was planted by Jun AjPu; One-Jun was planted by Ix-Bʼalam-Kej.

Just in the house did they plant it, they did not plant it in the mountains, nor did they plant it in the wet earth either; just in the dry ground found in the patio of their house did they leave it sown when they left planted; the heads of maize, the canes of maize, the heads on the canes of maize that each One-Jun of the Boys, each One-Jun of the Sons left planted there in Grandmotherʼs House.

Down, down, down into the Depths of Xibʼalbʼa; To Defeat Death; To Bring Forth the Dawn To kneel before the Sun; to raise oneʼs eyes to the Alba

Then they left, each one shouldering a blowgun-jujun chiwubʼ chike. This is the way they made their descent down to Xibʼalbʼa; quickly did they descend down the face of steep stone stairs-kumuk that were there.

body:
And so it was they who dropped and dropped as they made their way down, down, down the steep steps of the stairs that fell through the warm wet air into Xibʼalbʼa. They crossed over Jal-Jaʼ Siwan-Turbulent Water Canyon; then they passed through a great mass of moving, migrating birds; those ones known as Molay Tzʼikin- whirling, swirling Birds of Death; a Great Gathering of Migrating Vultures, a Massive Movement of spinning, spiraling Hawks.

These migrating Vultures known as los Azacuanes and Swainson Hawks signal the coming of the rains in late April and early May and their departure October and November.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Ancient Word is telling us here exactly when and at what time of year the Hero Twins begin their ʼrite of passageʼ embodied in their ʼsacred journey of initiationʼ that takes them on a perilous passage of peregrination through the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa. This must take place at the time when the maize stands straight-up as above so below. This is the Zenith Passage of the Sun on May 3 to 10th when Arcturus is ʼplantedʼ in the center of the Night Sky as the bright Red Giant that is both the tip of the Red Tail Feather of Wuqubʼ Kaqix and the torch of Tojil as well as the tip of the cigar of the Old Man or Mam, the Year-Bearer. Holes were perforated in temple ceiling through the Zenith Passage of the Sun by day and the Moon and Stars by Night were observed from below in a ʼbowl of waterʼ to see above. Thus ʼabove and belowʼ were bound together in the Star-light and Sun-light that marked the passage of this pivotal Time of the Year with precise precision. March, April, and May are the perfect time of year for the ritual performance of the Rituals of Sacrifice and Ritual Drama-Ritual Dances of the Sowing and Dawning of the New Year. This is the time of the year when the preparation of the Milpa is finished: the hoeing for the sowing and growing of the Milpa is long finished; the seeds have sown for over Forty Days; the sprouts have been drinking dew water just as long; and, firewood is split and dried to be stored. The work of building is being brought to completion as the last of thatch-grass is harvest to thicken the roof top where this ʼtwisted-grassʼ is bundled and bound; tied and knotted to leave the tabanco-p utum ja-rafters of the house ʼhigh and dryʼ before the arrival of first storms of the Rainy Season.

The Boys pushed passed Pus River-Puj Yaʼ with its flowing waters of pus; to then quickly crossover those bloody waters of Blood River-Kikʼ Yaʼ; both of them places of defeat; both of them places of death; both of them places of traps and snares of those deadly Lords of Death.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
But the Boys were not left defeated by those rivers; they were not intimidated; they were not taken-under by the water of those rivers. No, no they just crossed right over on their Blowguns.

When they came up and out of where the river canyons ended they arrived at the Crossroads; they arrived where Four Roads Crossed-pa Kajibʼ Xalqʼat Bʼe as it is named; as the Crossroads are known:

Black road; Qʼeqʼa Bʼe White road; Saqi Bʼe Red road; Kaqa Bʼe Green Road; Raxa Bʼe

Red road-Kaqa Bʼe; Black road-Qʼeqʼa Bʼe;

Green Road-Raxa Bʼe; Blue Road-Xaraxoj Bʼe White Road-Saqa Bʼe; Yellow Road-Qʼana Bʼe

Eastern Road of the Dawn-Western Road of the Dusk Heart of the Turquoise Sky-Heart of the Jade Green Earth North Road of the North Wind-Southern Road of the Xokomil Wind

The Yellow Road is not named here which is fascinating because it is the Qʼan Bʼey the Yellow Road of the South; Road of Abundance; Road of Maize; Road of Flowers and Road of the Sacred Count of Days of Kʼat; Qʼanil, Eey, AjMaq, and Ajpu or Ajaw, known as the Road of Junajpu is not named here; yet, Raxa Bʼe is named, for the Raxa Bʼe will be the road that Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej will take. They will take Raxa Bʼey the Jade Road of Eternal Life, the Emerald Green Road of the Eternal Return, the Road of Renewal and Rebirth, the Road of Revival and Recovery; the Road of Life and the Revitalization of the Lifecycle of Maize that has no end.

It is then the Eternal Lifecycle of Maize that the Boys found by following Raxa Beʼ the Resplendent Jade Road of Rebirth that leads to the Eternal Life of the Ancestors that comes to fruition through their Descendants living in the footsteps of their Divine Ancestors which is known as walking the Emerald Green Road of Resplendence: Raxa Bʼe.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Thus Raxa Bʼe is named in the naming of the names of the Roads of Xibʼalbʼa while Qʼana Bʼe the Yellow Road; the Golden Road that is the Southern Road that leads to wealth and abundance is the Qʼana Bʼey that passes through the Land of Plenty where the Great Wealth of Sustenance Mountain is found inside the Mountains of Pan Paxil; Pan Kayala where the Yellow Maize; White Maize are found as Qʼanajal, Saqijal; Yellow Mazorca; White Mazorca of the Golden Sun; of the Silver Moon. This road is not named; it is not named yet because this is where the Fourth Act will begin when the Former; the Shaper search for the essence of the flesh of the First Four Fathers of the Maize People. This is coming but it has not happened yet; not yet.

But the Yellow Road spoken of as Qʼana Bʼe will be named as the Golden Road when the time comes for Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej to rise-up and become the Sun and Moon of the Maize People; Maize Pueblo of the Ixim Winaq: the Great Nation of Maize People: Maize Sowing; Maize Growing Maya of Mesoamerica. This then will be when the Qʼana Bʼe will be the road taken-up to be walked down to come upon wealth and abundance; plenty and prosperity.

It was there at the Crossroads that the Boys sent off a Little Animal- Jun Chikop-un Animalito; an Insect is what it was; just a Little Bug called by its name: Xaʼn. Xaʼn was its name; the name of the One who listened in on what was spoken;

to listen in on all that was said; so that he would come to hear everything that he then passed on to those who needed to know all that this Jun Chikop; this One Insect; Xaʼn-Shawn had to say. And so this is what Xaʼn did; to repeat all he heard that was said.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
He, was the One-Jun named Xaʼn-Shawn who was the One-Jun that listened in on the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa when it came time to hear and remember the ʼNaming of the Namesʼ of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. His name was Xaʼn the same sounding name as Sean or Shawn. This was when the Boys, the Sons were tested by being called upon to ʼName the Namesʼ of the Lords of Death; Lords of Disease of Xibʼalbʼa, those who were known as Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame and AjAwabʼ Xibʼalbʼa. You known them but can you name them as the ʼFather- in-Lawsʼ of Engendered Sons. Let us get ahead of ourselves with this ʼNaming of Namesʼ to understand that this is the direction the Popol Wuj is moving. These are the Fathers of Daughters of Noble Lords; these are the Fathers of the defeated Mountain Tribes who will ʼgiveʼ their Daughters to the Conquering Lords from Tula-Tollan;

Tollan-Tula; those who were known as the Chichimeca that came down to conquer the Settled and Sedentary Maize Growing People who are Ruled by the Matriarch because the Patriarch was killed in Battle in not then Sacrificed as a gift given as a Sacrificial Offering. So let me not confuse you while remaining ambiguous to force you to understand what is happening here with the Fathers of Noble Daughters who are Fathers of Engendered Sons; Fathers who are sacrificed yet who beget Noble Sons; Warrior Sons; Sons who are Conquering Warriors!

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so they-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej gave Xaʼn his instructions when they told that One Insect-Jun Chikop what to do: “One by one you must bite them, first bite the First Seated One, then bite the next one seated next to the First Seated One until you finish biting them all in perfect order; in return for this that is ʼyoursʼ will be the blood of the people out on the road,” this is what was said to Xaʼn; the Mosquito; Xaʼn who was A Biting Fly; Jun Chikop; Un Animalito. “Utz bʼa la!” said Xaʼn. “Very good then!” said Sean, Shawn. This then was when he entered upon the Black Road-Qʼeqʼa Bʼe-the Road of Xibʼalbʼa arriving directly behind the Wooden Ones, the Puppet People, th ose Wooden-Woodworks of Wood -ri Poy, Ajam Cheʼ ; those carved and sculpted Manikin Men. These were the First -Seated Ones; the First -Seated Rivals; those that were the well adorned ones; those who were the Wooden Works of Wood - Ajam Cheʼ; the Dressed-up Doll People-ri Poy the ones who were seated their first as the F irst Seated Ones-Nabʼey Kuʼlel. These were the ri Poy; Ajam Cheʼ who Xaʼn arrived with when he came up from behind them to then bite them.

Kʼulel-Rival; Kuʼlel-Seated Name them in Order Name them to Know them; Know them is to Own them Own them is to Control them; Control them to Kill them These are those who are the first seated ones, the adorned one, the first ones there at the entrance of Xibʼalbʼa. They are the ʼgatekeepersʼ who must be distinguished as the real or the replica; the factual or the fake; the genuine or the imitation; the original or the counterfeit. This is an important aspect of the Mayaʼs Merchant Cosmos in which ʼimitationʼ cacao beans will be used to falsify weights and measures of loads of cacao.

But itʼs not only in the Merchant World because it is an aspect of the Noble World of Xibʼalbʼa as well; as you know so well from the way Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are laughed into submission while being humiliated by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa because the invited Ball- players cannot ʼName the Namesʼ of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This ʼnaming of namesʼ in the Maya World continues to be of major importance among the Maya who are always making sure the know your name while wanting to know if you can name theirs. This naming of names in no small thing amongst the human race in a world where everyone enjoys hearing their name said in a proper way with respect and regard as is done here in Popol Wuj.

These are the Boys rivals or kʼulel; nabʼe kʼulel their first rival are the nabʼe kuʼlel-first seated one or nabʼe kubʼulel-first seated, who are the first enemy ones known as nabʼe kʼulel- rival, enemy, adversary.

This section plays with the homonym kʼulel who is the rival, enemy, adversary and kuʼlel that is the ʼseated oneʼ who is also a kubʼulel or ʼseated oneʼ who is the one seated next kubʼul chik on a kulubʼal is a place to sit or seated platform or bench; a word formed from the verb kuʼluj to sit down and shaped from the verb kuʼlik to sit.

This tasting the blood of the Lords of the Xibʼalbʼa is a sure-fire-way for the Boys to taste the essence of their rivals, their enemies, their adversaries. What kind of blood runs through the veins and arteries of Xibʼalbʼa? The answer will tell the Boys, the Sons, the Twins who their enemy is in essence as well as who they are up against and what they need to do to defeat them. And so it is the Hero Twins send their ally Jun Chikop to bite the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa to taste the quality of blood that runs through their veins and by doing so cause their names to be named in order to name their names in perfect order. There is a great deal at stake here no doubt as shaman healers must have named these names to control the Lords of Disease through the incantation of their names.

Xaʼn, the Mosquito was sent out to bite the Lords in perfect succession; and so it was that he soon arrived there directly behind the Adorned Works of Wood ri Poy, the Embellished Works of Wood-Ajam Cheʼ; for it was a Wooden Man who sat there as the First Seated One, Nabʼe Kuʼlel who was their First Rival-Nabʼe Kʼulel.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This first seated one was covered with adornment; he was dressed-up as a decorated doll. It was then that Xaʼn, the Mosquito, bit him, he bit him First, but this Wooden One did not speak, not a word; not a peep did this First One tweet. So then the Mosquito-Xaʼn bit the Second-Kabʼ Seated One, the Second Rival; he did not speak; he did not purr; not a word was heard so it was on to the Third-Rox. Xaʼn bit then the Third, the Third Seated One, the Third Rival that sat there on the bench where the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were seated all in a row.

There sat Jun Kame-One Death; he sat in the third position; he sat in the third place after the first two Wooden Beings who were bit but they didnʼt make a sound; they didnʼt call out so nothing was heard so Xaʼn moved on to the Third- Rox. This then was when Jun Kame-One Death was bit and bit hard.

Ajii-Teocinte Ajii-Father-in-Law Ajii-Son-in-Law The highly talented storytelling scribes will have fun here playing on the Spanish ʼAqui- Akiʼ at the beginning of this narrative to say ʼhereʼ they are.

Then they switch to crying out the exclamation Ajii as a traditional twist on a traditional exclamation of pain: ʼAy yay yay yay or Ay yiiiiiʼ.

Well, Ajii means Father-in-law and Son-in-law as well as ʼTeocinteʼ grass which is the precursor to Maize which is a kind of Cane-Aj in and of its very own self. Can it be that the Maya understood this relationship of cross pollinating the ʼTeocinteʼ Grass-Zea mays subsp.

parviglumis with the Zea mays which is the Maize we speak of here as Corn in the Cornfield which the Maize in la Milpa.

body: Today Ajii signifies ʼsugar caneʼ that looks like a Carrizo Cane-Aaj or Ajii-teocinte grass. Every single word written in the Popol Wuj is a word written out by Maya Scribes in its very own special way for special reasons which are what makes the Colonial Translators always very suspect because of the way they have always come to the Popol Wuj ʼas ifʼ they knew better than the original Maya Scribes. They now come off as humorous kinds of jokes on themselves because of how arrogant and proud they have always been when always saying that the original Maya Scribes and Copyist are the ones who make the mistakes.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This exclamation of Ajii is like the ʼword-playʼ Joli, Joli; Juki, Juki…in which and where they are not ʼjustʼ exclamations although they are that as well; yet, these exclamations are signifying significant signification that are indigenous expressions of indigenous experience in the indigenous world. The Ancient Word and Ancient Expression of Popol Wuj is a very precise organization of mythopoetic statements that say something special in order to provide pivotal clue to what the secret ʼsub-textʼ wants to say: Aki...Aqui…Ajii…Ajii… So there is something going on here with Ajii-Teocinte and Aj-Maize and Aaj-Carrizo Cane in the context of the development of the lineage of Maize as a cane with kernels that are seeds that were constantly experimented with by Mesoamericans through the creation and production of maize as a domesticated grass with ʼhuge headsʼ filled with the ʼmany teethʼ of the Ancestors who are like the Fathers-in-Law-Aji and Sons-in-Law also known as Aji which will come into play soon enough. ʼAjiʼ is then a play on words that plays on the sound that is heard as ancient ancestral ideas and images that come forth from this mythopoetic masterpiece that says these Lords of Xibʼalbʼa are the Fathers-in-Law of the Twins just as the Twins are Aji or Sons-in-Law of the Xibʼalbʼa which makes them Family. This is vital information because this is an Imaginal World where Lineages dream Lineages thought and memory! This familial relationship of the Twins Mother being IxKikʼ the Daughter of a Lord: Ajaw Kuchumakikʼ. This makes the Twins those who inherit ancestral knowledge that is the nawal knowledge of how to speak and act; trick and cheat; misdirect and mislead; lie and deceive like Xibʼalbʼa when their Fathers Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu could not. These First Fathers of the Junajpu Lineage are incapable of Underworld Ways and that is why they are sacrificed on the spot!

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: The Twins are Maize People who are Maize Beings but they are also those of Xibʼalbʼa; and as Xibʼalbʼans they are likened to a Prior Age of Teocinte People; Teocinte Beings who are the ʼAncestorsʼ of the Maize People. There are stories of Bean People and Gourd People and Chili People in this Horticultural World that existed for Ten Thousand Years at least. And these were periods of time when the Plant People spoke with Human Beings who tended them with a level of care and concern that we can no longer image. This is an animate world that is an ensouled world filled with soul. We must imagine the Anima Mundi or World Soul in the same way through this Myth of Maize; Maize who is a living being that communicates to its People who take care of all the Maize Beings that live in la Milpa. So we must develop our soulʼs engagement in the imaginal realm in this way for it is our innate human capacity and capability to engage our mythic imagination that will enable us to understand the Popol Wuj in ways that similar to the ways it was once understood. Imagination is a powerful human capability that is an inventive, ingenious, and imaginative talent that is our mythical capacity to enter into myth through our imaginative capability that is an ancestral ability. This is why we must engage the imaginative capacity of our soul to develop a true sense of what our mythic imagination might come to be again after losing it for so long! Ajii, Ajii… There is a plant lineage being spoken of here and I am very content to have ʼfound it outʼ through my many translations and those translations needs for me to ʼsound it outʼ in order understand the meaning of this exclamation through the process of my slowly coming to ʼground it outʼ in mythic Mayan way that are Mesoamerican sensibilities for horticultural aesthetics and philological sensibilities that led to my getting a ʼfeelʼ for what is going on here. Ajiii!!! It makes me so happy to begin to understand the deeper levels of the Maya Myth of the Maize People!
