source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: ʼAjiʼ is the name given to the relationships of marriage alliance where the Father-in-law- Aji and Son-in-Law-Aji are created through Noble Fathers of a ʼconquered lineageʼ who ʼgiveʼ their Noble Daughters in marriage to form Marriage Alliances. These Kʼicheʼ Conquerors of the lands of the Mountain Tribes or Amaqʼ are usurpers of the original Mountain Sovereignty. But these Kʼicheʼ Lords and Rulers know they can never hold power and control over the land they conquered without the direct cooperation of the Mountain People of the Mountain Pueblo they subjugated. So these Kʼicheʼ Maya War-Captains and their Northern Allies of Nahua Warlords ʼhappily and contentedlyʼ received gifts of these powerful ʼDaughters of the Lordsʼ to form Marriage Alliances. These Daughters like IxKikʼ will become extraordinarily powerful as translators and interpreters of power relationships. This will be the role of Malinche in México with Cortés These ʼDaughters of a Lordʼ were married to ʼSons of a Lordʼ which is the Traditional Maya way of creating cultural unity and strength that will become of greatest importance in the last parts of the Popol Wuj. So realize this is very important here with the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa calling Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej Ajii! Aji! Aki! Aqui! Here we are your Fathers in Law from the conquered land of Xibʼalbʼa as we ʼforeshadowʼ the defeat and death of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame by Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. One wonders if the Daughters of the Lords brought their own Maize Seed to be sown in the land of their Mother-in-Law and Father-in-Law to improve the selections of Maize and Bean; Chili and Cacao; Vanilla and Gourds of all shapes and sizes. But it was the cross fertilizing and cross-pollinating of Maize Lineages that create Maize Alliances by combining the collaborative and complementary powers of the cross-cultural seeds of maize to bring about cross-lineage kernels of corn.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are rooted in the powerful Nawal lineage of Maize Beings by their being formed by an Over-World lineage of IxMuqane and Jun Junajpu while being shaped by the Under-World lineage of IxKikʼ and her Father Kuchumakikʼ and her Mother who must have been Mexica-Yaki like Chimalmat. In this way the Matriarchal Horticultural Aesthetics and Ethics of IxMuqane are brought together with the Trickster Lineage of ʼhungry upstarts from the Mountain-the Wild People-Mountain Peopleʼ to create something New and Powerful from: the Sun and Moon; Maize and Cacao; Highland and Lowland; Dry Desert and Humid Valleys; Cold and Hot; Dry and Wet; Hard and Soft; Male and Female; Over and Under; Mountain and Plain; Sky and Earth; Lake and Sea; Sharp and Sweet; Red and Blue; Fire and Water...This constant desire to improve oneʼs seed is something the Maize People have been involved for thousands and thousands of years over hundreds and hundreds of generations of human and plant reproduction. How can this not be part of this Myth of Maize? This is the exclamation that the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa make when they are bit and say: ʼXa Aji!ʼ Which is their way of ʼnaming their namesʼ to ʼgive up the knowledge of who they are and where they come from which for a shamanic cultural is to give-up and take-over the power to control these Lords through the power of ʼnaming their namesʼ by saying Xa Ajii or Just your Father-in-Law which is the Father-in-Law of the Twins Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej whose Mother IxKikʼ comes from Xibʼalbʼa. You get it right, of course, but itʼs a really big deal for them to say who they are to the Boys, the Engendered Sons: Kikʼajolabʼ Junajpu; Ixbʼalamkej who will never ever fall into the trap of revealing their Xibʼalbʼan Ancestry by ʼnaming their namesʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Junajpu; Ixbʼalamkej refused to reveal their origins and its ancestry when asked to name their names even though the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa will ask them time after time. And so it is that the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa will never come to know the ʼtruthʼ about their adversaryʼs lineage until the Boys name themselves which they do it quite ʼtellingʼ ways. Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame wonʼt know this secret until the end and then itʼs too late. They wonʼt known no matter how hard the Lord of Xibʼalbʼa try to get it out of the Hero Twins. They never say who they are or where they come from.

This creates great tension throughout this mythic masterpiece with its masterful play with this shamanic power of ʼnaming the namesʼ from the very first page that comes right out with the Kʼicheʼ Maya empowering their Ancient Word with the Naming of the Names of the Kabʼawil who are the Former, the Shaper; the Mother, Father and on and on as those who are: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom; Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw; Saqinim Aq; Saqinimʼa Sis Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz; AjRaxa Laq, AjRaxa Tzel; Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo… Thus goes the ʼnaming the namesʼ of the Divine Ancestors to the very last page of Popol Wuj when the Scribal Lords Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word; Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw Chuch- Qajaw Ojer Tzij Authors of Popol Wuj who name their names by saying who they are and where they come from. This is just like the Hero Twins will do when they defeat the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Oj Wa! We are Here! Here we are! We are Sustenance! This is how they say who they are and where they are. This is when they say where they are in the world and why they are there doing what they do. All at once they come out with it in order to name themselves with great pride and integrity; with great delight and dignity after defeating their mortal enemies: Jun Kame; Wuqubʼ Kame. Popol Wuj is a true work of genius and hopefully someday human beings from around the world will be able appreciate it for what it is as an Ancient American Account of Indigenous Antiquity. Popol Wuj is formed and shaped by Nawal Winaq who are Ixim Winaq who are Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Naming of the Names Lords of Xibʼalbʼa This then was the naming of the names of the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa when they named all their names by their naming the name of One-an-Other: Kʼeje kʼut ubʼixik kibʼiʼ ri xkibʼij konojel chi kibʼil kibʼ. So Xaʼn bit him, he bit the Third Seated One Jun Kame the First Seated Lord of Xibʼalbʼa who cried out:

“Aki! …Aki!” said then this First Seated One when he was bit, “What was that, that bit me here,” said Jun Kame. “Naki? What is it, Jun Kame?” asked Wuqubʼ Kame who sat right next to him as the Fourth on the Bench; the Second Seated Lord of Xibʼalbʼa. “What could it be? Something has just bitten me?” said Jun Kame.

“Xa Aji! Just Aji!” said the Third on the Bench, the First One to be bitten in a long line of Noble Lords who Xaʼn would bite, leaving Eleven Lords to bite since they were yet to be bitten! “Aji! What has bitten me?” said the Fourth Seated One in the line of lords seated on the bench of the Popol Ja, Council House of Xibʼalbʼa. “What is it Wuqubʼ Kame?” asked the Fifth Seated One.

“Something has just bitten me,” Wuqubʼ Kame said to the Fifth Seated One. “Aji!” shouted the next, “What was that? What has bitten me? Naki la mixitiyowik?” wondered the fifth seated one, fifth one sitting on the bench.

“What-Naki is it Xikʼiri Pat?” asked Wuqubʼ Kame-Seven Death.

“What is it that has just bitten me?” asked then Xikʼiri Pat-Blood-Sacrifice, Blood-Letter!

Then the sixth was bitten; the sixth rival-kʼulel; the sixth seated one- kubʼulel: the sixth seated one-kuʼlel that sat on the bench to be bitten.

“Aji!” said the sixth seated one, Kuchuma Kikʼ-Blood-Gatherer who was seated there right next to Xikʼiri Pat. “What is it Kuchuma Kikʼ?” asked Xikʼiri Pat-Blood-Letter. “What could it be that has just bitten me?” asked Kuchuma Kikʼ-Blood Gatherer. Then the seventh was bit, the seventh seated one: “Aji!” exclaimed then the seventh seated one who cried out in pain making it known heʼd been bitten just the same.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“What is it Ajal Puj-Lord Pus?” asked Kuchuma Kikʼ-Blood Gatherer who was seated there right next to him. “Who knows what has bitten me; Alay?” remarked Ajal Puj-Lord Pus. Then the eighth seated one was bitten. “Aji! Ay!” screamed out the eighth one sitting there on the bench. “What is it? Lord Jaundice? Naki, Ajal Qʼana?” asked Ajal Puj-Lord Pus. “Who knows what it was, but something bit me,” said Ajal Qʼana-Lord Jaundice. So then it was the ninth seated one of Xibʼalbʼa who was bit when he was bitten.

“Aji!” said the ninth seated one sitting there on the bench found at the Entrance Hall of the Council House of Xibʼalbʼa known to all as: Popobʼal Ja Xibʼalbʼa. “What is it Chʼamiya Bʼaq-Bone Staff?” asked Ajal Qʼana-Lord Jaundice.

“What could it be that has bitten me-naki la mixitiyowik-who could it be that has just bitten me?” asked Chʼamiya Bʼaq-Bone Staff.

Then the next in line was bitten, he was the tenth to be bitten. This was the tenth seated one there on the bench of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who was bitten. “Aji!” called out the tenth seated one there on the bench. “What is it Chʼamiya Jolom-Skull Staff?” asked Chʼamiya Bʼaq-Bone Staff. “Who knows what it was or who it could be that has just bitten me?” said Chʼamiya Jolom-Skull Staff.

When the eleventh seated one was bitten he screamed out saying, “Ajii! Aji!” said the one seated in the eleventh place there on the bench of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

“What is it Xik?” asked then Chʼamiya Jolom.

“Who knows what has bitten me,” said Xik-Hawk-Wing. Then the twelfth seated Lord of Xibʼalbʼa was bitten; he was the twelfth Lord of Xibʼalbʼa to be bitten when he called out a cry of pain and surprise. “Aji!” called out the twelfth seated one, sitting seated on the bench of the Popobʼal Ja of the Lords of Death down there in Xibʼalbʼa.

“What is it, Pack-strap? Naki la Patan?” asked then Hawk; Wing; Xik.

“Who then was that who bit me; or what was that that stung me the way it did; the one that has bitten me here below the bench?” asked Patan, Lord Merchant Tump-line; Lord of the Merchant Pack-Strap as he is known: Ajaw Patan.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Then the Thirteenth Lord was bitten, the Thirteenth seated one-Roxlajuj kubʼulel- was bitten there on the long bench of the adversary; the long bench of rival: kʼulel, kʼulelej but also those who are companions.

These are the companions who are complements of one-an-other as these pairs are known who will come to rule the land as compañeros-kʼulukʼuj as those who are the co-regents who are co-rulers of the Fourteen Generations of the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ-Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ. That is an image and idea that takes us to the very last page of this Ancient Ancestral Account when the Fourteen Generations are numbered and named in perfect succession as the Noble Generations that are named as the successive sequence of Twinned Lords of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lineages that is invoked here in subtle suggestive ways.

“Aji!” cried the thirteenth. “What is it Bloody Teeth-Naki, Kikʼ Re?” asked Patan to Bloody Fangs who was Kikʼ Reʼ. “Naki la mixitiyowik? What is it that, that has just bitten me the way it drew blood?” roared Kikʼ Re-Bloody Teeth- Bloody Fangs ready to bite back if he found the one who suckled is precious blood. Then it was the fourteenth there in a row that was bitten and bitten hard as the last one always is. “Aji!” cried out the fourteenth seated one. “Who was that who bit me?” asked the last in line; asked the last one on the bench; the last seated one in the row; the last one who sat last in the final position on that Noble Bench of Noble Lords.

“What is it Bloody Claws; what is it Blood Talons-Kikʼ Rixkʼaq-?” asked Bloody Teeth-Kikʼ Reʼ-Bloody Fangs who asked who had bitten him who was the last in the line who was known and named as Bloody Claws-Bloody Talons-Kikʼ Rixkʼaq the very last of the Fourteen Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who had been bit by Xaʼn when he bit them all in a row.

“Something bit me,” said Rixkʼaq-Bloody Claws-Bloody Talons who began scratching that bloody bite with his sharp claws that talons bleed like they always did when he had an itch to scratch like the bite he was just given.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Now with the names named in the order that the names came by the Lords naming each otherʼs name by name Xaʼn had no reason the remain in the Council House any longer so he took off in the direction of where the Boys were waiting upon his to return with the names that were named by Lords of Xibʼalbʼa in perfect order. Jun Ajaw; Jun Chikop; Jun Nawal Jun Raqan Kaqulja; Ukʼuʼx Kaj

Xaʼn flew right back down the line so they could see who had bitten them but they could not see him since they were looking down at the ʼOneʼ bite-mark he had given them by that ʼOneʼ biting insect that left them with a remembrance of the ʼOneʼ sign made by the ʼJun Chikopʼ who had bitten them ʼOneʼ and ʼAllʼ. This ʼOneʼ is the ʼOneʼ we all know there in the Heart of the Sky to who we come from and return as ʼweʼ who are ʼhisʼ the One and Only Jun Raqan Kaqulja who can change and transform into any Nawal form needed to get the ʼjobʼ done like the ʼOne Little Animalʼ known as the ʼJun Chikopʼ who was the Nawal of the Nimaʼ Ajaw. It was he who now contemplated what had to be done next to form and shape the Providers and Sustainers to provide and sustain those who were the Kabʼawil and had already sacrificed so much to arrive where they had all arrived there down the road from the Council House; on the Black Road not far from the Crossroads where the Jun Chikop was now flying to meet up with the Boys who had a pretty good idea of what theyʼd be doing next; nevertheless, as always, theyʼd take Council with the One there at the Heart of the Sky to know for certain where they were all going while perhaps telling why but that wasnʼt likely because that wasnʼt the way of the Heart of the Sky.

Xaʼn Jun Chikop-ʼOneʼ mark; ʼOneʼ sign

Xaʼn then returned to Jun Ajpu, Ixbʼalamkej; One Blow-gun Boy; Little Jaguar Deer who were those that had sent Xaʼn to bite all those he was sent to bite that he bit making sure all the Lords were bitten with a bite that left them both bit and bitten; which left them to ask the question as to who or what had just bit them with a bite that had left them so very markedly bitten?

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This question of biting and being bitten with a stinging bite is how the names of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were named in perfect order because these Xaʼn are a type of Mosquito with a very painful bite that leaves a perfectly circular mark with a pin-point of blood in the center that leaves no doubt this is where Jun Ajpu received his inspiration for the ʼOneʼ mark; ʼOneʼ sign he wore on his skin.

When this One Chikop bites he leaves his mark on those he bits and no question in oneʼs mind and body that one has been bitten; but by what or who because no one ever sees or saw him this One Little Animal: Xaʼn.

The Lords were left bit and bitten: but who or what that was that bit them to leave them bitten would never be known. This was because not one of them knew who had done the biting that left them bitten leaving them with a ʼJun-Oneʼ mark of swollen mark with a point of blood left in the middle just like the ʼOne-Junʼ mark of Jun Ajpu! And just because nobody would say who that was who left each and every one bitten nobody could name the name of the ʼOneʼ who bit them with a bite that left each one bitten.

This one bite each left each one to ask the one question as to who it was who had bit them and by asking this one question was the question that when answered, answered the question of what was the name of each and every Lord in perfect order: which makes one wonder if the name lord comes from sacred ʼorderʼ better known as hierarchy.

And so the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa named one-an-otherʼs name in order which was a perfect way to hear the Lords naming the names of one-an-other as if they were older and younger brothers. Just like this then, were their names named; they just named one another in perfect order. That is how their names were named. It was just because of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa naming one anotherʼs names that each one of the Lordsʼ names were named when they were named in perfect order.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
ʼNaming their Namesʼ Superior; Inferior One Seated Next to One Kubʼul Chuxukut This then is how the Boys brought about the naming of the names; the naming of the names of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. These were those Lords of Death that Xaʼn bit to bite them so they would be bitten in a perfectly orderly organized fashion; so that in this perfectly hierarchical way the one who was bitten first, and who was the immediate Superior Lord, would ask what was the matter to the one who had just been bitten as the Inferior Lord who had just been bitten, when he was bit next. So that the Superior Lord would name the Inferior Lords name in a most sacred sort of order known as the ʼhierarchyʼ of naming of the Lords. So that the first bitten Superior Lord would respond to the Inferior Lord who had just been bitten ʼwhat-nakiʼ was wrong; what had just happened; to which the Inferior Lord who had just been bitten would exclaim to the Superior Lord who had just been bitten: Aji! Who is that that who has just bit me? And which point he names the Lord as a rejoinder to this perfectly repetitive question as in: “who or what was just bit me Ajaw Wuqubʼ Kame? Asks Ajaw Jun Kame. To which the one who had been bitten first-the Superior Lord-names the name of the one who had just been bit-the Inferior Lord; who was the one who had just asked the previous Lord, the one who was bitten first; the one who was bit before-Jun Kame-the one who had just been bitten-Wuqubʼ Kame-is the one who asks: what or who has just bit me?

This way the freshly bitten and the previously bit would end up asking one another who had just bit them while ʼNaming their Namesʼ in perfect order so that they were bit with a bite that hurt so much that they exclaim: “Aji! What has just bit me with a bite that has left me so very, very bitten? Aji! Aji! Aji!”

The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were named by the Lord who was oneʼs immediate Superior. Each Lord was named by the Lord seated by their side-chuxukut, as they sat there beside one another on the bench in the Council House of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were named by the Lord superior to them in the sacred order that was known as a ʼhierarchyʼ so that the Noble Lord of superior rank and order named the one who was seated beside them who was of lesser rank and order; so that the higher ranked Lord was bitten first to demonstrate the noble hierarchy of the Popobʼal Ja Xibʼalbʼa with its status and station; with its position and power.

This was the Council House where stood a great bench of rule and order upon which the Inferior Lord was named by the Superior Lord until all of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were named through their being named in the perfect order of Noble Lords who named the names of one-an- other with their precision naming founded on the precise rank and particular order of each and every Lord.

This was the Noble Way of the Council House where the Boys, the Sons, the Twins were now walking shouldering their blowgun and contemplating the ʼnaming of the nameʼ of the Great Lords of Xibʼalbʼa; the Lords of Death and Disease toward whom their footsteps were now carrying on the Raxaʼ Bʼey which was the Green Road that led to Life and its Renewal.

Nabʼe-First; Kabʼ-Second; Rox-Third; Kaj-Fourth; Ro- Fifth; Waqaq-Sixth; Wuq- Seventh; Wajxaq-Eighth; Bʼelej-Ninth; Lajuj-Tenth; Julaj-Eleventh; Kabʼlajuj-Twelfth;

Roxlajuj-Thirteenth; Kajlajuj-Fourteenth…

This is a foreshadowing of the Fourteen Generation of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Rulers that begin with the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Maya. So do realize that these Lords of Death;

Lords of Disease may very well be the Ancestors of the Kʼicheʼ Maya as seen in their Ancient Ancestral Way of understanding Death and Disease. Nabʼe; Kabʼ; Rox; Kaj; Roʼ; Waqaq; Wuq; Wajxaq; Bʼelej; Lajuj; Julaj; Kabʼlajuj; Roxlajuj; Kajlajuj… First, Second, Third, Fourth, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh, Eighth, Ninth, Tenth, Eleventh, Twelfth, Thirteenth, Fourteenth…

This naming of all the names of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa was revealed to Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej by the One they sent to do their bidding.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Not one of the Lords escaped being named; each one of them named the name of the Lord seated by their side who sat next to them until the Boys finished naming the names of all of them there; leaving all of the names of Xibʼalbʼa named. That is how their names were named in perfect order; not one name of the names of the Lords was left out; not one name was left to be lost in his naming of the names of those known as the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. This was when they were bitten by the hair plucked from the skin of Junajpuʼs shin.

But it is not a true Mosquito; not a real Mosquito-mana qitzij Xaʼn that bit them when he was sent to listen to their names that would be named by Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej when they were requested, when they were required; when it was demanded, when it was commanded that they name the names of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

This then was when those named Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej took up their road upon which they went walking; this road they walked until arriving to where those of Xibʼalbʼa sat waiting:

“Greet the Noble Lords!” Said One-Jun of them-Xchaʼ ri Jun. “The Seated Ones!” ordered the One who had summonsed them.

“Ri kubʼulik!” Xchaʼ ri Jun taqchiʼnel.

“That one there is not a Noble Lord; that one there is just a Decorated Decoy-xa Poy; that one there is just a Wooden Man-xa Ajam Cheʼ-just a Carved Creation; a Disguised Deception,” said the Boys who continued. “That one seated there is just a Deceptive Decoy-xa Poy; just a fake; just a fraud; just a playful ploy known as a Poy,” said the Boy.

“That one there that sits by the door is nothing more than a Wooden-Work of Worked-Wood; xa Ajam Cheʼ just Sculpted Wood is all it is since it is nothing more than a Wooden Man that is just a carved trunk of Worked-Wood.

body:
Poy; Ajam Cheʼ False Face Fake Fraud Just a False Face Fake Fraud is what that One is because that One there is just a Wooden Figure, a Wooden Formation akin to a Man; which makes him a Wooden Manikin nothing more than that; just a Wooden Man is what he is and that is all that he his; a crafty creation of carved wood.” Said the Boys; said the Sons who stood at the Entrance where sat those devious deceptions; those deceptive distractions; those deadly disruptions meant to disturb oneʼs concentration by looking upon those Wooden Replicas as if they were real but they werenʼt they were just those Ancient Beings from Ancient Sun and its Ancient Age of Wooden Men known as Poy; named Ajam Cheʼ.

This is what they said, the Boys, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej when they arrived there at the entrance hall of the Council House of Xibʼalbʼa before the Seated Lords-Kubʼulik Ajawabʼ who sat all in a row; who sat in perfect order on the bench in the Popol Ja; the Council House of Xibʼalbʼa. This then was when they greeted the Noble Lords; this then was when they named their names: “Qʼala Tat, Greetings Father; Jun Kame: One Death!” “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Wuqubʼ Kame: Seven Death!” “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Xikiripat: Bleeder of Blood; Bloodletter “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Kuchuma Kikʼ: Blood Gatherer “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Ajal Puj; Noble Lord Pus “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Ajal Qʼana: Noble Lord of Yellow Jaundice “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Chʼamiya Bʼaq: Bone Staff Bearer “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Chʼamiya Jolom: Skull Staff Bearer “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Xikʼ: Wing Hawk; Sudden Death on the Road “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Patan: Merchant-Strap; Crossroads Death “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Kikʼ Reʼ: Bloody Teeth, Bloody Fangs “Qʼala Ta, Greetings Father; Kikʼ Rixkʼaq: Bloody Claws, Bloody Talons This is what they said when they arrived there with the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. The faces of the Lords were just finished off; the Boys named the names of all of their names when they named their names in perfect order.

Not one name was forgotten, not one name was left out; none; not a one; the Boys named them when they named them One and All.

body:
What was desired by those of Xibʼalbʼa was that their names should not be known by the Boys, by the Sons. But that is not what happened because the Boys knew those Noble Lords by name so that when the Boys came to name them they just named the Lords name by name. And all according to who they were so that they named those Lords One after the Other as only a Twin Brother could do; from First to Last; not too Slow, not too Fast so that the powers of Lords of Xibʼalbʼa would be revealed through their names that were named by the Boys; by the Sons; by the Twins whose ritual act of ʼnaming their namesʼ was no game because the Boys; the Sons named the names of the Lords by naming the names of each deadly realm and every one of their dis-eases so they were completely exposed by those who ended up confronting the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who had invited them come down just to make fun of them but the Twins were having none of that as they named the names just as the Lords of Death ordered them to do.

Defeat of the Lords Humiliation of the Rival Humbling of the Adversary Mocking of the Enemy on Both Sides So then this was when Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej did what they were told to do when it came to their naming all these names of the Lords of Death and Disease who were the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa with their names that are named in pair; in couplets; in couples; in twos; as complementary companions who are powerful, powerful beings of the Underworld Realm known as Xibʼalbʼa. And this was when they were defeated by the Nawal Genius of these Two Boys from up above who came down to play the Lords in their game which was the humiliation of the rival through the humbling of the adversary that came with mocking of the enemy on both sides.

“Come, sit here!” they were told, knowing the Boys would want to take a seat on their bench. But they didnʼt sit down; they didnʼt sit down because they didnʼt want to sit down.

body:
“That is not our bench there, it is just a cooking stone-xa chojim abʼaj-that bench there-ri tem ri-is just a hot stone bench heated red-hot to burn our butts; itʼs just a blistering burning bench to blister our buttocks, nothing more!” said Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej as they got up to go to the door. The Boys, the Sons; they were not defeated there by Xibʼalbʼa as the Lords had thought was their destiny; the destiny of theirs was not the destiny of their Fathers; no their destiny was completely other as Twin Brothers whose Mother was a Moon Goddess from Xibʼalbʼa.

“Utz bʼa la! Well then! Just go on then; the two of you just get going; just get yourselves in that House there!” they were told. This was when they entered Dark House-Qʼequma Ja but they were not defeated there either.

This was the First House of Ordeal in Xibʼalbʼa, it was the first house of tests; the first house of trials that the Two Sons, Two Boys entered; when they entered Dark House: Qʼequma Ja.

It was there that those of Xibʼalbʼa began to feel the seeds of their defeat. It was there in Dark House that they felt like maybe they were going to defeat them; that is what they felt in their heart, they felt they would defeat them, the Boys, in Dark House: Qʼequma Ja.

First, they would have to enter Dark House-Nabʼe, xeʼok pa Qʼequma Ja. That is when they went in to deliver their pine-torches-xbʼeyaʼoq ri chäj.

Those pine torches-ri chäj of torch-pine-chaj were already burning when the Worker-Samajel went in to leave them with the Boys there in Dark House. Each one was given a cigar of rolled tobacco by the Messenger-Samajel of Jun Kame who was the Servant-Samajel of One Death; Jun Kame.

“ʼHere are your torches! Waʼe kichäje!ʼ” says the Lord; who says to say: ʼAt Dawn come out and give them back, the two of them; the torches along with the cigars. The Messengers will come to collect them from you,ʼ says the Lord,” said the Messenger of Xibʼalbʼa when he arrived there with the Boys in Dark House- Qʼeqʼuma Jaʼ. “Utz bʼa la!” they said then.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
But the torches they carried with them were not burning; for they were not real torches that burned red hot. What they carried inside with them were just replicas that were substitutes of the burning embers of true pine-torches and real tobacco cigars.

The replacement torches and replica cigars that they carried with them into Dark House were the bright red tail feathers-ujeʼxiʼk of the Scarlet Macaw- KaqKʼix or just: Kaqix. Truly, the replacements-ukexwach-replicas of their torches looked just like those they were given and made to appear as real to the Sentinels who watched all that went on there in the Dark House-Qʼeqʼuma Ja. For those brilliant red feathers of the Scarlet Macaw burned bright through the night like the very torches they were given in the dark darkness of Dark House.

Red Giant Arcturus Tip of the Red Tail Feather Tip of the Cigar Remember the Red Giant Arcturus planted directly overhead in the Dark House of the Night Sky on the zenith passage of the Sun around the pivotal period time falling between the days and nights of May 3-10 when the Sun stand straight overhead at mid-day: Tikil Qʼij.

Well now we are being reminded of this time of initiation by the long red tail feather of Wuqubʼ Kaqix that ends in the Red Giant Arcturus in the very Heart of the Sky: Ukʼuʼx Kaj. The time has come to begin the New Era; New Epoca of the New Formation; New Creation of these Young Men as they make their Rite of Passage to become the Ancestral Replacements or Kʼexelʼ of their sacrificed Fathers. The time has come for the Engendered Sons to take the place of their Dead and Deceased Fathers whose bodies are buried beside the Ballcourt there in Xibʼalbʼa. The time has arrived to liberate their Ancestral Soul and Nawal Spirit of the Maize Deities Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu who embody all the Junajpu Days; Junajpu Destinies that awaits their Sons arrival beside the Ballcourt of Sacrifice: Pusbʼal Chaaj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The time has come for the life forces of the Junajpu Lineage to be freed from their bondage in their Underworld captivity where they are kept buried beside the Ballcourt of the Lords of Death. This is where the Skull-wrack stands in all Mesoamerican Ballcourt structures where the Tree Standing beside the Ballcourt is the metaphor for the Skull-wrack that stands up their growing beside the Ballcourt with skulls that are the fruit that look exactly the same just as skull do look the same when place on the Mesoamerica Skull-wrack. Now the Sons must find, collect, and perform sacrifice over the Skull and Bones of their Fathers in order to give them a proper burial. There is always more to reveal in this interpretation of the Popol Wuj this is what we shall do in order present the span and depth of the Maya Culture and Mesoamerican Civilization.

And as for the burning embers of their cigars; how were they kept alive and burning through the night? Well they just placed lightning bugs on each tip of their cigars-xa qʼaqʼa chikop xkikojo chuwi sikʼ-so it looked like the Boys just smoked and smoked them through the night! “Have we not just defeated them here then?” cheered the Sentries who watched them there in Dark House.

“Have we not just beat them here?” jeered the Sentinels that stood watching outside of that House of Darkness where they could see the burning tips of their cigars.

Those cigars that just lit-up and dimmed-down; as they lit-up and dimmed-down because of the natural flux and flow of the Nawal Lightning-bugs; who as the Boysʼ Animal Companions gave their all to deceive the Sentinels who kept watch over them throughout the long dark night of the ancestral soul that was forced to face the darkness of disillusionment and its disenchantment in Qʼeqʼuma Ja that was truly felt to be a House of Darkness.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
But only for those who didnʼt know what the Twins knew and that was that the world was full of opportunities to deceive those who were dedicated to deceiving you; which is pretty much the truth about the deceptive ways the Boys; the Sons; the Twins had to constantly come up with in their mythic life and death battle with the Lords of Death and Disease. Lords who loved deception as much as they worshipped the practice of human sacrifice; which were enough reason for the Boys to up their game and stay on their toes; while never allowing themselves moment of sitting back on their heels like their Fathersʼ did right there in Dark House when they sunk down into a slavish squat that was a sure sign they had given up on their lost lot in life.

This was when and where decapitation was their best bet for their regenerating life on earth for their lineage through the spittle that became their Sons who were the Twins who were right here where their Fathersʼ once were only now they were the ones who were going to take it to the Man when the time came to grip the White Flint Knife in their hand and do what had to be done to pacify the land.

And so it appeared to the Sentries of Dark House that it was ʼall-overʼ for those torches and cigars; what else could be expected to happen to them?

Since those torch-pine torches just burned all-night with a bedazzling bright light; and, the cigars they just simmered real nice as fine embers that stayed lit through the night giving-off the comfy-cozy feel of home through their rich warm glow.

There would be nothing left of them by daybreak from the way they burned there before the gaze of those who kept watch over the torches and cigars that most certainly would be finished off before the dawn blossomed forth from the darkness of Qʼeqʼum Ja.

But the torches were not finished off; they were the same as when they had been given to them at dusk the night before. As for their cigars, they didnʼt even light them up, they were just the same as the cigars they were given when they entered Dark House and this is how they, the Boys, returned them when the sentinels came to collect them at Dawn.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Their torches, their cigars; the sentries, the sentinels just went right over and to return them to the Rulers-Ajawabʼ-the Nobles, the Lords of Xibʼalbʼaʼ who asked:

“And these ones, who are they?” “Of what then are they made?” “Where do they come from?”

“Who fathered them; who mothered them?”

“Who engendered them; who conceived them?” “Who then is their Father; who then their Mother?” “Truly our hearts are going to be burnt up by them; surely we are going to be finished off by them! It is just no good what they do; and, to us the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. There is something about them that is different; something about them is different indeed; different too is their nature-kikʼojeʼik-their essence!” They said when they spoke to one another; those who were they of Xibʼalbʼa. It was then that all the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa were summonsed; they were sent for to hear what the Lords wanted to do next; and what they wanted to do next is why they wanted to gather together to council to gather their thoughts and ideas together about what was to be done about these Boys.

This was when Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame called the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa together to summons the Boys; to speak with the Sons: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are their names. It was then that they said this:

“Letʼs just play ball Boys; come letʼs take up the rubberball in the ballcourt together to play ball, you, oh Sons,” said the Lords, when the said what they said when they spoke with the Boys.

“Oj ochaajoq, ix kʼajolabʼ” Xeʼuchaʼxik.

And so then they were questioned there by Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; One Death, Seven Death:

“Where did you come from? We wish you would tell us, you, oh Boys; you, oh Sons, Ix Kʼajolabʼ,” asked those of Xibʼalbʼa. “Well, we must have come from some place! But we donʼt know where that could be,” is all that they said without naming from where they came.

“Apa kixixpe wi? Chibʼij taj, Ix Kʼajolabʼ,” xchaʼ kʼut Xibʼalbʼa chike “A la bʼa xojpe wi lo! Mawi qetaʼm,” xa xechaʼ, mawi xkibʼij.

“Utz bʼa la, letʼs just go play ball then, you Boys,” said-xechaʼ those of Xibʼalbʼa. “Utz! Fine!” they said-xechaʼ.

body:
“So let us put our ball into play; let us just use our ball-qakikʼ, our blood- qakikʼ” said-xechaʼ Xibʼalbʼa.

“No way! Ma taj! We donʼt want that! We will put ours into play,” said the Boys-xechaʼ Kʼajolabʼ.

“Not to be!-Maja bʼi! Here, here is where we shall just use ours,” -said Xibʼalbʼa-xechaʼ Xibʼalbʼa. “Very well then,” said the Sons.

“Utz bʼa la,” xechaʼ Kʼajolabʼ.

“Letʼs go; letʼs play. It is just a striped one-juchʼil-itʼs just a decorated ball, a ball that hides a White Flint Knife-Saqi Toqʼ inside as they say,” said Xibʼalbʼa- xechaʼ Xibʼalbʼa.

“That just isnʼt so! It is just a disguised decorated skull with an obsidian blade inside; thatʼs all it is!” said the Boys- xechaʼ Kʼajolabʼ. “No itʼs not like that!” said Xibʼalbʼa- xechaʼ Xibʼalbʼa.

“Utz bʼa la! Very Well then,” said One Blowgun Boy-xchaʼ Junajpu.

So this then was when they threw the ball of Xibʼalbʼa down into play, landing on the hip-yoke-ubʼateʼ of Junajpu who sent the ball flying.

This was when the White Flint Knife-Saqi Toqʼ went sliding as it was sent skidding across the ballcourt while the ball of Xibʼalbʼa bounced as it bounded over the finely finished floor.

body:
White Flint Knife-Saqi Toqʼ That white flint knife just slid as it shimmied in a silent sort of slide that sent it skimming in a slid sliding to go slicing over the fine thin finish of that ancient cement ballcourt; that white flint blade was sent singing as it went zinging with not a thing to slow just nothing to slow its skidding slide as it flew forever more sideways as the stone blade careened on its side across the immense silence-chitzʼininik; chitzʼininik-as the players watched in disbelief through the silent stinging silence that now screamed out shrieking as the knife-hand blade just went spinning to begin singing strident cement sounds of shrill scraping flint skimming the surface of Pusbʼal Chaaj with shimmy, shimmy sort of searing sound of this shrill screaming silence as the white flint screeched then squeal then shrieked with its jagged edge sharp and clean…then just silent still silence as that sacrificial blade lay stock-still; completely stationary on that ballcourt floor: chi-tzin-tzin-tzin; chi-tzin-tzin-tzinʼ was heard no more for nothing more could be heard other than that white flint blade that was now lay flayed out upon its belly in the now deadly silence of Xibʼalbʼa where it was so still and so completely quiet as all eyes looked on just one Sacred Being that rested silent and tranquil there on the sacrificial ballcourt of ballcourt sacrifice.

A Second Take White Flint Knife-Saqi Toqʼ

body:
This is when those of Xibʼalbʼa saw the White Flint Knife-Saqi Toqʼ fly out of the ball to then go zigzagging its way across the finely finished surface of the ballcourt floor making its way sounding out with its ʼchi-tzin-tzin-tzin; chi-tzin-tzin-tzinʼ sound as the White Flint Blade of Xibʼalbʼa echoed the cry and call of their great desire to summons sacrifice. Their White Flint Blade sounded-out as Saqi Toq could be heard ringing as it was sent singing its sacrificial song that went zinging along its sound just rebound as it resound as the ricochet obsidian blade it was that Xibʼalbʼa has sent sailing through the air just like they had wished for their razor sharp white flint knife that seemed to shimmy as it shiny sliver of death that shook and shivered to slide on its side sounding out like screech; like a squeal; like a shriek; like a scream from below as it skimmed sailing over the sleek shiny surface of the stone hard ceramic floor of their sacrificial ballcourt where and upon which they practiced their most sacred ritual known as Ballcourt Sacrifice that was performed by the Deity known as: Saqi Toqʼ White Flint Knife.

ʼThey said-xechaʼ and ʼHe said-xchaʼ …xechaʼ…xechaʼ….xechaʼ This shows how the Two Boys spoke as One in the singular ʼhe said-xchaʼ instead of the plural ʼthey said-xechaʼ for when they spoke-xechaʼ as one the Scribe write xchaʼ-as he said which is a perfect example of how the Two Boys; Two Sons who are Twins act as One Son who ʼsaidʼ what he said: xchaʼ. You know what I saying? There is no end in finding nawal genius in Popol Wuj; where the Scribes say what they say so that what must be said is left said even when the spoken word is said by the dead.

body:
It is as if the noble scribes canʼt help but play with the sound of the ʼdialogueʼ of the Noble Lords and Hero Twins who say: they said-xecha when the Lords speak but when the Twins speak they speak as ʼXa Jun-Just Oneʼ as in ʼxchaʼ-he saidʼ even though both name Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are named. What is so beautiful about this section when read in Maya Kʼicheʼ is that the ʼverbal exchangeʼ sound like the rubber-latex ball ʼsounding-offʼ on the surface of the Ballcourt-Chaaj so that one hears xechaʼ-said the Lords…xechaʼ-said the Boys…xechaʼ-said the Lord…xechaʼ-said the Sons…xechaʼ…xechaʼ….xechaʼ and so it goes as the sound of this new written language is put to an enchanting use by the Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word.

Juchʼil: A Stripped One of Sacrifice Cuchillo to Kuchʼil Juchʼil will transform the Castilian word knife or dagger that is cuchillo to kuchʼil the word for knife heard today amongst the Maya that began with the word that sounds like it sounds here: juchʼil from juchʼ or ʼstriped onesʼ; that is to say ʼstriped one of sacrificeʼ and jun chay or one obsidian blade. For it was those who were to be sacrificed that were painted with ʼred and whiteʼ stripes known as ʼjuchʼilʼ which is what the Popol Wuj is saying here. We have already come to see Xibʼalbʼa likes to hide their ʼSaqi Toq-White Flint Knife of Sacrificeʼ inside their ʼdecorated, striped ball of sacrificeʼ and this is why they are ʼfightingʼ over whose ball they will throw down into play and what kind of game of sacrifice of sacrifice will they play anyway.

Itʼs hard to say in this Mesoamerican Empire where there are so many ways to play out rituals of sacrifice and rituals of the rubberball game. But here in Popol Wuj the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa ʼseemʼ to be asking ʼhowʼ do they want to take up the ball-chaaj to then ʼthrowʼ it down into ʼplay-chaajʼ? How shall we Play-Chaaj? With whose Ball-Kikʼ on whose Ballcourt- Chaaj and by what rules of the Ballgame; whose Ball-Chaaj shall we Play-Chaaj with are all spoken in one single way with one single word that is pronounced as it is spelled which is Chaaj.

body:
Itʼs difficult to say just exactly how this game was played since the languages that are spoken in Mesoamerica come from the Highlands and Lowland; North and South; East and West so the language that the Ball-Players speak arenʼt the same language-tzij; truth-tzij; tradition-tzij; way-tzij with which to play the game. Juchʼil was a ʼstriped oneʼ and as ʼa striped oneʼ the person who was painted with red and white strips were those who were distinguished as decorated beings who were sacrificial beings who had become sacrificial gifts of ritual sacrifice; the ʼstriped oneʼ or juchʼil was headed for the sacrificial stone to be beheaded ritual sacrifice.

The game of Xibʼalbʼa is ʼsacrificeʼ this is what they want for the Boys; they just want to sacrifice them like they sacrifice everyone who comes down to Xibʼalbʼa through the oldest most deceptive trick in the book known as ʼbait and switchʼ which is what this word-play on juchʼil is about.

The juchʼil or decorated striped ball of Xibʼalbʼa is all about sacrifice even thought they say otherwise. Those of Xibʼalbʼa are great liars; who are bold-faced liars who are shameless sorts of blameless kind of false-face liars who are deceivers who are trickster that are cheaters.

Xibʼalbʼa are those who are unashamed to use that ancient trickster tactic of ʼbait and switchʼ. Because this is most certainly an ancient ancestral case of ʼbait and switchʼ for these young ballplayers who have been invited to play with the Lords of Death better be careful or they will become the next victims of sacrifice; like their Fathers: Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

This was when the White Flint Knife-Saqi Toqʼ went sliding as it was sent skidding across the ballcourt while the ball of Xibʼalbʼa bounced as it bounded over the finely finished floor.

body:
“What could that be?” shouted Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. “Naki pa la?” xchaʼ Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej “If death is all you wanted then why send for us? Why send your messengers up there to summons us down here? Thank you very much,” said the Boys who got up quickly to go; enough was enough. “You will have to excuse us; we will just be on our way!” said the Boys to those of Xibʼalbʼa-Xechaʼ Kʼajolabʼ cheke Xibʼalbʼa.

What the Lords wanted for the Boys; what they wished for them, was that they should die right there on the ʼedge of the obsidian bladeʼ or ʼchi chaʼ as they say-xechaʼ.

ʼJusu ta xkam ri chiriʼ, chi chaʼ which is to say ʼto die in an instant on the edge of their obsidian blade; on the obsidian blade of their obsidian knifeʼ which is to say ʼjusu ta xkam ri chiriʼ, chi chaʼ which was their way of saying: to be sacrificed on the obsidian edge of their obsidian blade-chi chaʼ of their obsidian knife; which meant their being sacrificed on the obsidian edge of their obsidian blade of their obsidian knife.

This was the sacrificial obsidian blade-chi chaʼ that was hidden inside of their blade-bearing ball; their blade-bearing ball of sacrifice that was the sacrificial ball that those of Xibʼalbʼa wanted to play their game; the game that they played known as Saqi Toqʼ: White Flint Knife of Sacrifice. The Boys did not die as Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame wished for them. It didnʼt happen that way; it didnʼt happen that way because that Boys didnʼt let them get away with playing their game of sacrifice as they wished. It was just those of Xibʼalbʼa who were defeated by the Boys, ri Kʼajolabʼ; the Engendered Sons: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

Now they were going; now they were leaving the ballcourt of the Lords; the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Sacrifice: Pusbʼal Chaaj Xibʼalbʼa. “Donʼt go Boys-Ix Kʼajolabʼ, we want to play ball, letʼs just use your ball; letʼs just throw your ball down into play,” said those who spoke then with the Engendered Sons-xuchax kʼut Kʼajolabʼ.

“Utz bʼa la!” xechaʼ kʼut- they said then to them.

body:
So then it was with their ball that they began play; their ball was thrown into play; the ball of the Boys was put into play so that it was with their ball that they began to play. And this was the way they continued to play with many good plays made by both sides as it is said; both side making equal plays as they played with equal strength; when they played with the Boys ball; when they played that first day to a draw.

And so it was that after playing for a while with equal strength and equal skill the Lords suddenly stopped; they stopped because they wanted to bet something to play for. The Lords wanted to play for some sort of wager; some sort of winnings-kichʼakon to play for. And so this then is how they decided upon what would be the winnings of their wager:

“What should it be that we wager-chiqachʼako; what could it be that we win- qachʼakon?” asked those of the Xibʼalbʼa.

Xibʼalbʼa known as the Place of Fear, Place of Initiation, Place of Intimidation where the Boys now were playing ball with those who had sacrificed their fathers! “Well now, why donʼt you choose,” was all that the Boys said-xechaʼ knowing what they knew about the ways of Xibʼalbʼa. “We would just like to win four bowls each-kajkaj tzel-four gourds a piece of Flower Petals,” said-xechaʼ those of Xibʼalbʼa.

“Utz bʼa la! Very well! What kind of Flower Petals-Kotzʼijal would you like to play for?” asked the Boys of Xibʼalbʼa. To which the Lords responded with kind and considerate words:

“One big handful of Red Petals; Ju tiqʼabʼ Kaqa muchit One big handful of White Petals; Ju tiqʼabʼ Saqi muchit One big handful of Yellow Petals, Ju tiqʼabʼ Qʼana muchit, One big handful of Big Ones, Ju tiqʼabʼ kʼa ri Nimaʼq,” xechaʼ Xibʼalbʼa.

“Utz bʼa la!” said the Boys, said the Sons-xechaʼ Kʼajolabʼ.

So once again then they threw their ball into play to begin another round of play; they played one another with equal strength, with the Boys making many good plays. Their hearts made sweet with their ball-playing feats-and with every good intention-but in the end the Boys gave up in defeat on this first day of ballcourt play in Xibʼalbʼa on their sacrificial ballcourt of ballcourt sacrifice.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Truly content were those of Xibʼalbʼa with their winning a sweet victory while the Boysʼ lost in defeat.

“Havenʼt we done well; arenʼt we then the first to win?” said-xechaʼ Xibʼalbʼa when they said-xechaʼ what they had to say: xechaʼ.

This then was when the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa whispered to one another: “Where are they going to go to bring back our flowers; flowers that we have won from them?” xechaʼ chi kikʼux, asked those of Xibʼalbʼa when they spoke to each other heart to heart. This then was when Xibʼalbʼa spoke with the Boys. “Truly, at dawn you will give us our flowers-qakotzʼiʼj that are the winnings of our wager-qachʼakom,” they instructed the Sons-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej- when they reiterated what the Boys were responsible for with regard to their ballcourt wager which was the winnings of Xibʼalbʼaʼs players.

“Utz bʼa la! At dawn then we will play again,” is what they said when they took leave of one-an-other; when they gave each other instructions for the following day and its serious ballgame play. It was then when the Engendered Sons-ri Kʼajolabʼ entered the House of Obsidian Blades-pa Chayim Ja, the Second House of Ordeal; Second House of Trials; Second House of Tests there in Xibʼalbʼa: Ukabʼ Tijobʼal Xibʼalbʼa. And that is when it was wished for them to be dismembered by the Obsidian-Blades; this was where the Lords just wanted the Boys to be cut to pieces by the Obsidian-Blades-xeqʼatakʼox taj rumal Cha. Those of Xibʼalbʼa wished with all their heart that the Boys, the Sons would be killed quickly; but they were not killed quickly for they did not lose heart; they did not die there in the House of Obsidian-Blades: pa Chayim Ja. This was when the Boys spoke to the Obsidian-Blades giving them their instructions: ʼThat which is yours is all that is the flesh of Animals,ʼ they said to the Obsidian Blades.

This was when they instructed the Obsidian Blades as to ʼwhat was theirs in lifeʼ when they celebrated council with them-the Obsidian Blades-in order to give their advice, their instruction, the counsel as to what ʼwas theirsʼ on the Face of the Earth. Ta xechaʼ chi re Cha ta xkipixabʼaj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
No longer did they move. All together and all at once the Obsidian Blades dropped down from above, the Obsidian Blades, all of them just dropped to the ground to lay at rest on the floor of the House of Obsidian Blades. And there they remained throughout the Night in the House of Obsidian Blades For truly, this was when they were called in; those who were just Leaf-cutter Ants and Warrior Ants who were the Conquering Ants and Cutting Ants that the Boys summoned there into the House of Obsidian Blades-pa Chayim Ja by calling them in through incantation; by calling them in through invocation that led to their captivation; that led to their enchantment. It was just by calling them in and calling them up through their singing them in and their singing them up that the Ants arrived there to enter the House of Obsidian Blades-pa Chayim Ja.

Chay Sanik; Chʼeken Sanik Obsidian Ants-Cutting Ants; Warrior Ants-Conquering Ants

This was the House of Tests and Trials that stood there beside their plantation of flower gardens and fruit trees known as their plantings-utikom; the plantings of Xibʼalbʼa; the plantation of Xibʼalbʼa: Utikom Xibʼalbʼa.

And so the Boys sang their song of enchantment as they made their incantation to invoke, to enchant the Ants so that they might file into the Lordsʼ precious plantings of flower gardens and prized plantations of fruit trees. Chay Sanik; Chʼeken Sanik known as Obsidian Ants who are Cutting Ants and Chʼeken Sanik who are Warrior Ants; who are Conquering Ants best known as Zompopo who are the Ancient Ancestral Allies of the Hero Twin Boys whoʼs lifelong relationship began with their Elder Brothers placing their Newborn Brothers on Ant Beds knowing they would sleep their best there with the Ants and that was long before those Sweet Baby Boys ever knew what an Ant was. But they know who the Ants are now so they call them in to do what must be done in the night on the limbs of fruit trees and in the flower gardens where the flowers were blooming bright with Red Petals; White Petals; Yellow Petals; and, Really Big Ones. Come, come in, come in dancing; come, come in, come prancing; come, come in …

“Chay Sanik, Chʼeken Sanik: Kixpetoq, Kixojoq iwonojel. Oj ikʼamaʼ ronojel uwach kotzʼiʼj, kichʼakon AjAwabʼ!”

For this is the spellbinding spell that the Boys have not revealed until now as their enchanting appeal to the Ants to steal away the Lordsʼ precious petals; prized petals after cutting away; all before day break. Which should be no big deal because this ancient incantation was the powerful and magic of all the powerful magical spells that there were; and so, it was a real thrill to reveal this spell because it goes like this still:

“Chay Sanik, Chʼeken Sanik: Kixpetoq, Kixojoq iwonojel. Oj ikʼamaʼ ronojel uwach kotzʼiʼj, kichʼakon AjAwabʼ!” “Cutter Ants, Conquering Ants; Come-in, come-in, come in Dancing; come- in, come in Dancing; all of you…Come! Come! Come in! Come in! Come in Dancing!”

“Come carry away their fine floral faces; Come carry away their fine flower faces; come bear away the flowery façades of their winnings; their precious petal earnings!” “Come, come carry away the blooming blossoms won by the Noble Lords who believe they are awesome! Come, come carry away the flourishing flowers of the Noble Lords who believe they have magical powers!”

This was the Boys way of enchantment as they invoked; as they enchanted the Ants to bring forth their flourishing floral winnings of their blooming blossoming ballcourt wager made to be paid to the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

“Chay Sanik, Chʼeken Sanik: Kixpetoq, Kixojoq iwonojel. Oj ikʼamaʼ ronojel uwach kotzʼiʼj, kichʼakon AjAwabʼ...” “Cutter Ants, Conquering Ants; Come-in, come-in, come in Dancing; come- in, come in Dancing; all of you: Come! Come! Come in! Come in! Come in dancing!”

“Chay Sanik, Chʼeken Sanik: Kixpetoq, Kixojoq iwonojel. Oj ikʼamaʼ ronojel uwach kotzʼiʼj, kichʼakon AjAwab”

The Cutter Ants; the Conquering Ants were instantly enchanted by the Boys who called them into the precious plantings of the Lords; to come in dancing carrying the cuttings of Xibʼalbʼaʼs prized flower petals won in the wager made between the Boys and those of Xibʼalbʼa.

Precious flower petals cut and carried away by the Ants for the Boys to fulfill the debt made with the wager they intentionally created to be paid to those whose plantations flourish with flowers filled with magical powers embodied in the blooms and blossoms of the red petals, white petals, yellow petals, and big flowers that now had to be cut from above to then be gathered from below to fill the four sacrificial gourd bowls with the precious prized petals of the Noble Lords.

“Utz bʼa laʼ!” said the Ants as they marched off to bring back the flower petals from the plantings of Xibʼalbʼa; their plantation of fruit trees and flower gardens spoken of as utikom Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame: the precious plantings of the prized plantations of Xibʼalbʼa.

The Cutter-Ants, the Conquering Ants were sent off to bring back the blossoms and blooms from the gardens and groves of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa known and named as One Death, Seven Death.

For already-the day before-it was they-the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa-who gave their instructions to the Guardians of their Blooms and Blossoms who were the Protectors of the Flowers of Xibʼalbʼa-Chajal kikotzʼiʼj Xibʼalbʼa. This is what Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame say: “You, you must watch closely; watch our flowers in our plantings! Donʼt let them be stolen now that we have defeated the Boys-ri Kʼajolabʼ-the Sons.

body:
“Where can they go to find the winnings of our wager-qachʼakon?” Asked the Lords when they spoke directly to their Guardians who were the Protectors of their Flowers; the Care-takers of their Garden: Chajal Tikoʼn. “Well, we will tell you where they will go,” said the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa, ʼThis is the place to find and take the winnings we wagered; so sleep not tonight so that you remain vigilant; lookout; keep watch; stay awake for our sake; take care of what is really, truly at stake; the color and fire that blooms from our flowers is the heart, the soul of our ancestral powers; our precious flowers that bloom and blossom in our bountiful gardens, our fruit orchards, and our flourishing groves provide us with our sacred sustenance with its divine essence comes forth from where our flowers bloom; from where our blooms blossom; from where our beloved sustenance sprouts and grows; flowers and fruits; ripens to then sweeten of the limb; on the vine. So stay wide awake through this night to protect those flower petals those tricksters will want for themselves to provide us with our winnings!”

“Utz bʼa la!” they said then-xecha kʼut-those who were the Whip-poor-will; known as Night-jars; Pu-Juyubʼ; Xpur-Pu-Weq.

The guardians of the blooming rows of flowers and blossoming groves of fruit didnʼt feel a thing when it happened to them; when it happened to them in the still silence; there in the deep dark of night; there in the garden with the flowers they were watching without ever closing their eyes. They never felt a thing when it happened to them: when the flowers were stolen from Xibʼalbʼaʼs Keepers and Care-takers of their flowering Trees and blooming Gardens: Chajal Tikoʼn.

body:
Known as the Nighthawks; known as Night-Jars: Xpurpuweq; Pujuyu; Xpurpuweq; Pu Juyubʼ; Ix-Pur-Pu-Weq; Pu-Juyubʼ who sing through the warm wet luxuriant moon-lit nights of the late Dry-Season. This is when they begin singing at dusk to call the rain when it is warm enough to stay-up through the Night to watch-over the maize sprouts-iwal abʼix shooting up in la Milpa. This is the time of the year that one says: tzuq pa abʼix; the milpa has sprouted. The Poor will and the Whip-poor-will are always there to watch the seeding and sowing; sprouting and growing of the first month Milpa being pulled up by the Moon through the night.

They just sang from the limbs of the trees while the thieves entered and exited unseen as they moved silently through the blossoms and leaves of the flowering trees.

The Sentries just spent the night jumping from branch to branch keeping watch over the blooming flowers in the blossoming gardens without ever noticing the Ants moving amongst them.

For they did not see or hear or smell a thing; neither did they taste nor feel nor think nor imagine a thing about those who came and went with what they cut and gathered as the little fleet footed Nawales they were moving about with making a sound or a stir because absolutely nothing was ever heard or seen in that night when all those many petals were gathered in bowls that were gourds known as tzel in which sacrificial offerings were always held. For it was just a silent, imperceptible force that moved through the night as they arrived and departed with what they clipped and snipped to then gather-up and carry away; which, was what those Cutting Ants and Conquering Ants were sent- out to do by the Boys who helped them cut and collect those precious petals; prized blooms; beloved blossoms that filled the Four Guacal with Red Petals;

White Petals; Yellow Petals; and the Big Ones that were there in the Flower Garden and Fruit Orchard of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa who were beginning to feel like it was time to rest as best they could and that why they gave instructions to their Care-takers who were the Guardians of all they planted around their Great House.

body:
The watchmen remained wide awake as they perched themselves on the arms of the blossoming trees that were in full flower; trees that were budding with limbs in full bloom.

There the sentinels kept watch remaining ever-so-vigilant and ever-so-ready as they kept watch over everything that was left under their protective gaze; but to fill the orchard with a definitive sense that the care-takers were alert and alive they just did what they liked to most which was to sing-out loud in the night; And so it was that they sang out through the night to stay wide awake so they could keep watch over all the blooms and blossoms they were given to protect.

The guardian were right where they were told to be; right there amongst the Lords flowering groves of blossoming trees with their flourishing flowers with their colorful petals and vibrant blooms that were falling all about as they floated down to the ground; just a calm, quiet, soft sound heard by nobody because nobody was there; just as nobody was around; in the perfect silence of the bright balmy night where row upon row of blossoming buds were being carried away; nothing seen; nothing to say; everything was in its place; where all was in perfect order as night stepped ever so lightly out of the dark and into the day… These Care-takers of Xibʼalbʼa sang their songs in crepuscular way at dawn and at dusk always on the edge of night and day in the dark; these sentries who were sentinels; sentinels who watched over the cacao where they lay their eggs right there beneath the low-lying limbs of this Grandmother trees whose ancient old breast hung down towards the ground until they were ripe enough to be taken-up to be taken away.

These Purpuweq these Pujuyubʼ were Sentries of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa known as Night- jars to this very day and it was they who just cracked their mouths wide-open to sing their songs into the starry, starry night while they kept watch over the pristine plantings of Xibʼalbʼa where flower petals now rained down from the Sky.

body:
They never saw or felt a thing when the Ants came and went throughout the long calm night gathering the Lords winnings that were so easily collected while the guardians and caretakers sang their sweet songs of solitude; their melancholic songs of longing sung through the quiet melancholy of the lonely, enchanted night.

The Ants just swarmed about there while the Night-birds sang their sad song of loss and nostalgia. What loss? Why nostalgic? It is just what is said of these birds that are said to cry over those who have died thus are those who have joined the dead in Xibʼalbʼa.

And so it is said they are Nawales of Xibʼalbʼa and why that is I have no idea, no notion, no inkling but it makes sense because they are about to enter into the great commotion that will take place all around them because of what happens on their watch under their gaze right there beneath where they sang out in the dark warm mist of the late Dry Season just before the coming of the Rainy Season. They sang with their somber tenor, sad tone filling the humid night ambiance and atmosphere with solemn enchantment; they sang as the dew covered all that it touched; they sang as the warmth of the day and its evaporation fell back to earth inundating the leaves and limbs; flowers and canes; blossoms and blooms with dew that would leave the Face of the World soaked in water like a Man-made-of-Mud.

They sang as an evocative invocation; a crying, a calling, a kind of clamoring incantation of their very own name: “Xpurpuweq! Xpurpuweq!” sang the night-criers; night-callers whose night song called as it clamored to be known by its being named its own name in the ancestral practice known as ʼnaming the nameʼ of those who named their name by singing their song so that these “Xpurpuweq! Xpurpuweq!” sang their name; which, is and always was pretty much the same. So to with the Nighthawk known and named: ¡PuJuyubʼ; PuJuyubʼ!

This is the song sung to call down the waters by naming the names of those who watch-over the magical ways; nawal magic of the transforming Mountain; of the Mountain People and their Mountain Places; Song of the Mountain Place; Incantation of the Changing Sky; Enchantment of the Transforming Mountain; Changing Place; Changing Name of the Transforming Sky; the Rain will the Song is Sung you can hear it Coming. The Song is Sung by the Guardian of the Mountain; the Caretaker who sings her Song.

The song that is sung is the Song of the Mountain. The song they sing is the song that calls for the falling of the mountain rain; the mountain rain that comes as it is called to fall upon the mountain by those who sing their song that is the naming of their names; Pujuyu, Pujuyu.

This is a kind of singing that is sung as a song that is sang as the sacred singing of the call of the mountain that sings the song: Pujuyu, Pujuyu, the song that is heard as a call and a cry on the warm and windy, balmy breezy nights by the feathery winged ones who are the singing ones who sing their soft song that is a cry and call for the coming rain that when it comes will fall as the sweet soft song of the voice of the mountain; breath of the mountain of the people of the mountain that sing the song that calls the rain that names the name: Xpurpuweq, Xpurpuweq…Pujuyubʼ, Pujuyub!

Xpurpuweq, Xpurpuweq…Pujuyubʼ, Pujuyub! Xpurpuweq, Xpurpuweq…Pujuyubʼ, Pujuyub!

This is their song sung all night long to call on the rain to fall as the sacred sustenance that is that which is theirs of those who are the sprouts shooting up in the milpa; that which is theirs is that which reveals what is their sacred sustenance that tells their ancient, ancestral truth; the truth of their ancient word that is the water and rain of the milpa and the maize that sprouts from the Face of the Earth. This is the song that one hears at night when the sprouts in the milpa are calling out for rain by crying out their name of those who are the ʼbreath of the mountainʼ Pujuyubʼ, Pujuyubʼ.

This is that which is their truth and that which is their truth is the water and rain that will quench their thirst; the thirst of the dusty dry parched mountain-plain where maize sprouts shoot up and out of the ground on the now scorching day-time mountainside.

But dusk has come as night has fallen when and where wet dew descends to begin falling and filling the little cups formed by the maize leaves that shape the little cups of ʼtwistedʼ leaves of maize known as: utum ja.

body:
These cups formed by these ʼhardʼ enduring maize sprouts withstand the strong mid-day heat of the Milpa; the Milpa with its mythical Four Hundred Boys who stand straight-up at attention like ʼlittle warriorsʼ with their heads upright in the direction of the Old Man, the Sun who rises up and over their heads while beating down on the ʼyoung initiatesʼ standing right side up with their heads facing their Father, the Sun, with his scorching mid-day heat.

These sprouts surviving in the Milpa are the ancestral descendants of the First Fathers of the Maize People.

These descendants are the embodied replacements-kʼexel that sprouts forth and grow through this initiatory period of the lifecycle of maize surviving in the Milpa as the return of the ʼyoung menʼ of the Ancestral Maize Lineage.

These are those with their ancestral faces and enduring, hard traits who come back to life after being buried at death to be born again and survive as the eternal return of the jade green seed that will never die because its essence, its nature, and its condition-kʼojeʼik.

This is the internal essence; the inherited genius borne within that skull-like kernel of maize that will live on no matter how difficult, defeating, and deadly the tests, trials, and ordeals the maize descendants must face in its young life in the Milpa.

The Young Life of the Milpa experienced in the initiatory life as Young Noble Lords who want to be and become the noble replacement of their noble Fathers and Grandfathers who lived and died before them to be born again in lives of the young noble lords who are the replacements of their ancestors and renewal of the life of the lineage that lives again through them and their beautifully enduring ways.

Their Father the Sun is ʼhardʼ on them in the ʼheatʼ of the ʼbattleʼ to survive by Day; but by Night their Grandmother and Mother water them with their qʼebʼal-tinajas in the dewy light of the Moon. The Moon and the dewy light of Mid-night will draw down the evaporated waters of the day will fill-up the maize sprouts water cups-utum ja so they can drink-in the cool fresh water of dew that drenches the Face of the Earth all-night long.

The Mother-Father; the Grandmother-Grandfather will help guide and protect all of those many formed beings, shaped beings who have been formed and shaped by the Former, Shaper; the Bearer, Begetter; the Mother, Father; Grandmother, Grandfather; the Mid-wife, Match-maker; the Shelterer, Protector there on the Face of the Earth.

This is what is happening in the nighttime in the plantings of those who live to bring their seeds to fruiting fruition.

This is the song that is sung to name the names of those who call the rain to water the milpa to ensure its survival right here on the Mountain-Plain.

Xpurpuweq and Pujuyubʼ were the two guardians, the two sentinels who watched-over the garden plantings of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame. Yet they never felt a thing when the Ants entered there to steal away what they were given to protect.

No, no they never knew the Ants were there carrying away all that was theirs to keep from being borne away in the long silent lines of Chʼeken Sanik-Zompopo Ants who cut and carried away their burden of flower petals in a magnificent nighttime movement of Ants who marched through the plantings of Xibʼalbʼa.

Those Cutting Ants; Conquering Ants moved through plantation lands of Xibʼalbʼa without ever being heard or seen. This was just the way of rebel kinds of guerrilla forces that learned to take what was theirs to take that was there to take from the oppressive Lords and Rulers who never gave a flower petal no matter how many precious prized petals were grown by their slaves in their vast plantations of blooms and blossoms of flowering fruit and fruiting flowers. Those Lords of Xibʼalbʼa never had enough and what they grew in great excess they just kept to trade with others for emeralds and jade; colorful feathers and precious metals like silver, copper, and gold.

That is just the way it was and would always be as long as the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa ruled the Canyon Country and Mountain Places like they always had and always would. Unless of course these Hero Twins who were Cultural Heroes would do as their Mother had done with was to stand-up to the Lords of Death through cunning craft and clever creativity with which to cut- down these Lords and Rulers like the Ants were doing now with the precious flower petals that were now raining down on the ground of the fruit orchard and garden plantation like flowers had never fallen from the Sky before yet there it was flower petals now covered the Face of the Earth ʼas ifʼ it had rained colored petals from colored flowers all night long.

All the Ants just tumbled over one another as they swarmed all about the garden floor harvesting the winnings of the Noble Lords. Those insatiable Ants moved all about gathering their colorful cargos of petals, enchanted by the song they heard being sung all-through the night; these Ants became bearers of blooms and blossoms; these Ants became pilferers of bright colored petals who ran about gathering up the tribute to be paid as the winnings of wager that had become the Boys debt to be settled that the Ants paid in full with effort to collect the winnings the Boys had lost on purpose to defeat the Lords at their own game; in their own court; with their own wealth and riches collected and now to be paid in full.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They climbed up into the flowers on the tree branches to cut them away. Then they gathered up the petals that fell fluttering to earth from above; down below the flowering trees blooms and blossoms were trimmed so the petals floated down without making a sound to then be gathered up and carried away by the Ants who were ready and waiting on the ground below.

All of it was done in one night by the Cutter-Ants; by the Conquering Ants; Chay Sanik, Chʼeken Sanik who were the Obsidian-Blade Ants; these, the ancestral allies of the Sons, the Boys since birth; and it was they, the Ants, who gave the Boys victory by carrying out the Lordsʼ defeat. Meanwhile the guardians sang out at the top of their lungs, splitting open their mouths doing so. They didnʼt feel a thing when their tails where trimmed and their wings were clipped.

It was a great collection of flowers: of those that were cut, of those that fell, of those that were gathered to be carried away in the jaws of the Ants, in the middle of the night; work that was finished, work that was complete before the coming of day-break.

They filled the four bowls full of flower petals, the four gourds known as raxa tzel; precious bowl, precious gourd bowls of sacrifice are what the Boys carried to the Lords at Dawn; just resplendent sacrificial bowls filled with flower petals; just blooms; just blossoms of their chosen colors: Red, White, Yellow, and those Big Ones.

So it was then that the Messengers-Samajel arrived, as those who were they that summons-taqonel others; as Messengers they arrived to summons the Boys, the Sons, who were summoned by the Messengers:

“ʼCome along thenʼ say the Lords, ʼRight-away, we want that they should bring our winnings-qachʼakon,ʼ say the Lords,” they told the Boys, the Sons, ri Kʼajolabʼ. “Utz bʼa la! Very well then!” they said then-xechaʼ kʼut. They arrived bearing four bowls of flowers cradled in their arms; with four bowls of petals they entered; with four bowls of flower petals they presented themselves there before those of Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Boys brought flowers to pay the wager the Lords had won playing ball. Sweet smelling flowers and flower petals are what they brought to the Lords; the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. This is how they, the Boys, defeated Xibʼalbʼa; they just let them win to watch them lose. It was just the Ants that the Boys sent; in just one night the Ants gathered together all the tribute that was won in the wager bet in the ballgame they played; these were the winnings of the Lords; the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

And so they delivered the four sacred gourds-tzel-four sacrificial bowls filled with the blooming blossoms and collected flower petals. That is how those of Xibʼalbʼa were defeated; they were cut down like their flowers.

The Lords just turned white, all of those of Xibʼalbʼa, deathly pale did their faces become because of the Flower Petals: Red, White, Yellow and the Big Ones.

So then they sent for the guardians of the flowers:

“Why did you give them our flowers to be stolen away? Canʼt you see that these are our flowers that are here, just look?” they demanded from the Caretakers, the Guardians-Chajal Kotzʼiʼj-the Protectors of their Flowers.

“We didnʼt feel a thing, you oh Lord, not even did we notice them trimming our tails,” they said. And just like that Xibʼalbʼa split their beaks as punishment for what had been collected under their watch; this was the price they paid for not protecting what was harvested by others under their care: the Flowers of Xibʼalbʼa. This is the origin of why these birdsʼ beaks are split. The beak, the mouth- kichiʼ of the Purpuweq, the Whip-poor-will, is this way today; a split-beaked bird is the Purpuweq.

ʼOn the Edge or Chi Cha of the Obsidian Bladeʼ Noble Warriors of the Obsidian Blade Jaguar and Eagle Warriors
