body: This is the Ancient Ancestral Place where the First Sun and First Moon were brought to life and into movement through their self-sacrifice which meant throwing themselves on the sacrificial fire. This is the Myth of the Sun and Moon in which the humble Nanahuatzin and arrogant Tecuciztecatl or Tecciztecatl immolate themselves on the sacred fire that burned in Teotihuacan. This becoming of the Sun and Moon is identical to the sacrifice of JunAjPu, IxBʼalamKej who immolate themselves by throwing themselves on the Sacrificial Fire burning there in Xibʼalbʼa to become the Sun and Moon of the Age or Era of the Ixim Winaq. Teotihuacan is where Humanity is said to have transformed into Divinity which perhaps means that it was the Sacred Place of Transformation or Divine Heart of Initiation where Human Descendant became the replacements of their Divine Ancestors. Just like in the Popol Wuj Kʼicheʼ Maya Initiates once made this Ancestral Peregrination to Tollan Tzuy-Wa so where Young Noble Lords took up their Divine Ancestorsʼ Paths of Initiation just as described here in Popol Wuj. By learning the Dances and Singing the Songs; Playing the Ballgame and Practicing Blood Rites of Self-Sacrifice the Kʼicheʼ Maya Youth became Kʼexel or Replacements of their Divine Ancestors.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Thus we must recognize in order to realize that the Popol Wuj is a Book of Counsel that shows the way to carry out Rites of Initiation that were carried out through Rituals of Transformation. Thus the name of the First Hero Twin Junajpu; the Ancient One from the Reeds and Rushes of Teotihuacan: AjPu or XJunAjPu: He the Ancient Ancestral One from Tollan Tzuy- Wa. JunAjPu thus is well understood as the Ancient Ancestral One of the Ancient Ancestral Place of Abundance-Pu-Place of the Reeds but he is also the One Blow-gun Boy, Lord of the Hunters, Lord of the Warriors, Lord of the Ballplayers, Lord of Transformation, Creation, and Destruction as his is complementary, collaborative, and cooperative Younger Brother Little Jaguar Deer who is his ʼsavior-protector-healerʼ spoken of always as the Second of Two who is the Twin Brother of Junajpu known always as named always as Ixbʼalamkej Ixbʼalamkej: Little Jaguar-Deer; Lord of the Hunter and Hunted; Lord of the Mountain, Lord of the Wild; the Second One of Two who heals and resuscitates the First One; Junajpu whenever he becomes wounded by being dismembered. Junajpu is the Guide of his Young Brother Ixbʼalamkej who is the Protector of his Older Brother Junajpu; the ʼTwoʼ who work together as the ʼOneʼ: the ʼTwoʼ in the ʼOneʼ Hero Twins who are the Cultural Heroes of the Maize People.

These are the Two Maize Deities who are the one face of the Maize Lord, their Father Jun Junajpu; the First Father of the Maize People. Jun Junajpu begets his ʼEngendered Sonsʼ Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej in the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa who grow upon the One Cane-Jun Aj that is the body of their Mother IxKikʼ who, like One Cane of Maize-Jun Aj, sprouts-up and out of the Underworld to grow and grow before flowering to fruition on the Face of the Earth. In this way these Boys who are the Sons of their Father-Jun Junajpu are born from their Mother-IxKik who bears them up and out of the Underworld carrying them to safety in her womb. This womb of IxKikʼ becomes ʼone big net of maizeʼ that IxKikʼ must harvest just as she bears her Boys-the Maize Twins on her back until they are born.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
IxKikʼ is a Cane of Maize who bears her Sons-the Replacements of their Father the Maize Lord on her back as the Moon Mother of Maize-IxKʼik who carries her twins as two swaddled heads of maize that grow on her as the ʼengendered sonsʼ of the First Father of Maize: Jun Junajpu. This is their story; the story of Maize Deities; the story of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej the Sons of the Maize Lord-Jun JunAjPu that is the Sacred Narrative of the Maize People: Ixim Winaq.

Before any of this happens these Two Cultural Heroes of the Ixim Winaq must ʼorderʼ the Sky-Earth to ʼprepareʼ it for the coming of the Maize People. This is the work of blowgun boys who are the primordial hunters of birds who are the primordial enemies of the Ixim Winaq in a world where maize is the preferred food of the birds. This is why Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej must take Wuqubʼ Kaqix down from his throne that sits in his Great Tajpal Tree that stands above and over his Great Kingdom of the jungle forest that the Maize People wish to take for themselves in order to settle down beside it along its lakeshore and waterways in order to grow their Milpas of Maize and their Milpas of Cacao as it is said. This struggle between Wuqubʼ Kaqix and the Hero Twins Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej is the central part of the Popol Wuj introduced to you here. It symbolizes the eternal struggle the Maize People have with the Bird People who are happy to eat the food the Maize People have apparently grown for them.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Maize People must control the Bird People through superior magic and so it once was that the Kʼicheʼ Maya who knew themselves as Ixim Winaq performed this Ancient Ancestral Account as Ritual Drama at the time of sowing their Milpas with Maize. The Maya performed this ritual drama as a magical means of controlling the birds and animals who like nothing more than eating the sweet canes of maize to then devour the sweet kernels of corn. This then is the story of that eternal struggle between Maya maize growers and the wilderness that surrounded their fields. This will play itself out in beautiful ways as you will come to experience for yourself. A story that begins with this very dramatic line: “This then is when it begins; here then is where it begins; the story of the defeat of Wuqubʼ Kaqix by the Boys, the Sons: Jun Ajpu, IxBʼalamKej.”

The imaginal mythical realm we are now about to enter is an Ancient Ancestral World that is remembered here in deeply nostalgic ways; ways that recall remembrances when the Hero Twins of the Maize People ʼordered and preparedʼ the Face of the Earth for the Creation of the Maize People. The Popol Wuj is the story of the defeat of the Animal People; the creation and destruction of the Clay People, and now the last of the Wooden People who do not know what it takes to rule as a Noble Lord; Noble Lords who learn how to act through the ways and words of Junajpu and Ixbʼalamkej. The sacred narrative of these Divine Twins begins here so do realize this story taught the way of being and becoming a Noble Lord through the forming and shaping of the ways and words of the Hero Twins.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They knew their death; they knew it well; they knew it when they left them their instructions while taking leave of Xulu, Pakʼam; they knew of their departure, they were advised of its arrival; the Boys were given counsel; they knew of their death and disappearance; it was clear to them; they could see it; they knew of their dying for they saw the way of their sacrificial death. Ta xepixabʼik, xketamaj kikamik. This then was when those of Xibʼalbʼa made their great stone oven to make the sweet drink; this is the kind of stone fireplace-chojibʼal-oven that Xibʼalbʼa made.

They used the really big leaves; these were the big leaves they used: nimaʼq xaq, the big leaves they used to ignite a big burn ablaze-nimaʼq xaq-to set a great fire to burning there in the stone oven of the sweet drink, the bitter drink known as: nima chojim abʼaj kiʼ.

Nimaʼq Xaq There is some sort of double entendre and word-play going on with the Big Leaves- Nimaʼq Xaq they use to build their sacrificial stone oven where they ʼsetʼ a great fire ablaze to create a Big Burn-Nimaʼq Xaqʼ in this fire place chojibʼal where the traditional sweet drink-ki is drunk when the performance of ritual sacrifice takes place. This is the sweet drink-kiʼ of the big maguey leaves-kiʼ from which comes the alcoholic beverage known as Kiʼ. I am the first to admit this is another one of those places in the Ojer Tzij that I know I am incapable of writing some sort of definitive translation; yet, I am more than content to venture an alternative reading of this most ʼbeguilingʼ passage that no doubt is placed here to ignite our mythic imagination.

Mesoamerican People and their Pueblo made alcoholic beverages just as they are spoken about here in the making of these ceremonial stone ovens where the text tells us those of Xibʼalbʼa are preparing to become ritually inebriated at the time of their sacrifice of XJunajpu, XBʼalamKej. Mesoamerican people drank alcohol during the ritual performance of sacrifice otherwise drink alcohol and becoming intoxicated outside of the ceremonial intoxication was a religious and cultural offense that was punishable by physical punishment and even sacrifice if this practice persisted.

body:
So do realize the Maya are not getting drunk all the time but they do drink in ritual ways; ways that are indicated here in this passage Here then is an alternative translation of the passage: Are kabʼan ri nima chojim abʼaj, kʼeje ri chojibʼal ki xkibʼan Xibʼalbʼa, Nimaʼq Xaq xkikojo. A passage one is left wondering if the Nimaʼq Xaq are indeed Big Leaves of Agave used to make their sweet drink-ki that was a bitter drink-ki because why are they using big leaves here at all?

Perhaps it is in context of some cultural context we no longer understand or simply because I as a translators like the other translators are clueless when it comes to understanding the depths of Kʼicheʼ Maya religion prior to the Castilian Conquest and Colonization.

Perhaps it is because the text is not talking about leaves-xaq at all but the setting a big fire ablaze-nimaʼq xaq xkikojo or is it the placing of a big fire-nimaʼq xaq to make a big burn-xaq that is to say to make a great fire in the stone oven. because what is certain something else is going on here that past translators simply want to fly right over on their way to a making a translation more concerned with North American cultural equivalents instead of seek to understand the ritual performance of ceremony and their subtleties that are reflected in the Original Maya Kʼicheʼ text of the Popol Wuj.

So then they made their great stone oven of sacrifice; the fireplace carved out beneath the earth, this was the dugout oven-chojibʼal that those of Xibʼalbʼa made; it was in here that they set a great fire ablaze-nimaʼq xaq xkikojo; this was the kind of stone oven that those of Xibʼalbʼa made their sweet drink-Kiʼ-bitter drink in which ʼbig leaves-nimaʼq xaqʼ were used; big leaves of agave known by their name: Kiʼ.

The Messengers arrived to accompany the Boys and so it was that the Boys accompanied the arriving Messengers of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame.

They came for the Boys; they came to show them the way to the Great Stone Oven-Nima Chojim Abʼaj of Xibʼalbʼa, this is what the Messengers said to the Boys when they said what the Lords sent them to say.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This then is what they said: “You are to say to them: ʼKepetoq! Come along then! We have come to show you what we are cooking up in the great stone oven,ʼ say the Lords to say to you; you, the Two Sons-Ix Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolab” said the Messengers. “Utz bʼa la, very well indeed,” said the Boys.

Quickly, they went walking so that quickly they arrived beside the round stone circle that formed the stone oven-chuchiʼ choj. And there it was that the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa hoped to tempt them with a little game.

“Letʼs jump over our sweet-drink that sits cooking in the oven; just four times each, back and forth, each one of us, in turn, you oh Boys-Ix Kʼajolabʼ,” they were told then by Jun Kame. “You canʼt pull that one on us, donʼt we know our death, you oh Noble Lords-Ix AjAwabʼ? Watch this!-Chiwila na!” They said! Then, they paired off face to face to then take hold of one-an-other by the hands; and then, the two of them dove ʼhead-firstʼ into the sacrificial fire of the stone oven: e pu jupujuj ta xebʼek pa choj. There in the fire the two of them died.

Sun and Moon Nanahuatzin and Tecciztecatl Pu Jupujuj What an exquisite play on e pu jupujuj: the two jumped head-first, into the stone oven: e pu jupujuj ta xebʼek pa choj in which the ʼaspirationʼ of the blowgun-ju-pujuj as the last ʼexhalationʼ of life is experienced as the release from life to then dive ʼhead-first or jupujujʼ into the sacrificial fire to extinguish the life of the Boys in order to be transformed into Young Men.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This then is a mythic memory and ritual remembrance of a rite of passage and ritual of initiation that was twinned with this Maya Myth of the Men of Maize. This is one of the principal mythic images of the Kʼicheʼ Maya. Through the sacrificial fires of ritual death and rebirth acted out in ritual drama and ritual sacrifice the Mayaʼs mythic imagination is able to feed the Mayaʼs ancestral soul with these mythic images and archetypal imagery that provide and sustain the burgeoning Maya identity of Young Maya Initiates with mythic metaphors that are necessary and even required for the Young Maya Male Initiates to transform through the fires of ritual sacrifice leading to the nawal transformation of Wild Older Boys who donʼt know what is theirs in life to Young Men who come to know what is theirs in life through ritual transformation found in this rite of passage. These are Young Men who know their destiny and given what they need by their families to bear the burden that is theirs to bear in life. This ʼmagical transformationʼ takes place in the sacrificial stone oven of sacrifice. In the Quetzalcoatl Myth of Tula-Tollan Lord Quetzalcoatl dives into his sacrificial fire to become the Morning Star as do Nanahuatzin and Tecciztecatl in the Nahua Myth of the Creation of the Sun and the Moon that tells of two divinities who throw themselves onto the sacrificial fire to become the Sun, Nanahuatzin-the One Pustule Pus dripping One and Tecciztecatl the Beautiful Conch Shell One who becomes the Man in the Moon. In other words the Popol Wuj is replicating this Mesoamerican Mythic Metaphorical Motif of ritual death and rebirth through immolation on the ritual fire in which is extinguished the immature identity in order that the mature identity comes forth from the ashes. This is the transformation of Older Boys who were hunter-providers that fed those who needed to be fed by those who were the sustainer-protectors of Grandmother and Motherʼs Milpa. These Older Boys are transformed through their ritual sacrifice into Young Men who will become Kʼicheʼ Warriors, War-Captains, and Warlords as you will come to see right here in this sacred narrative of the Popol Wuj.

body:
For now realize the depth of the resonance that come from this ritual of immolation or ritual sacrifice through fire spoken of so poetically in this myth as the Boys, the Sons jumping ʼhead-first-into the fire of the stone oven of sacrifice: e jupujuj pa choj.

Now this mythic history will instantly transform into a bedazzling and beguiling magical mythical play of the mystical Maya Soul in which the human imagination is taken far beyond the limits of the natural world and its material limits. Now everything and anything becomes possible for these two dancing magicians which makes our mythic imagination explode up and out of the fire to become the mythical heroes our souls yearn to be deep down within us where these mythical images resound and reverberate with a heroic sense of life, death, and rebirth. We human beings find this kind of hero myth narrative irresistible because we all wish we had superhuman kinds of divine sorts of powers to set the world right. These divine human powers of warriors who fight for justice are right on the threshold divinity and humanity as our soul takes up the epic road of this mythical journey.

This is the journey we are on now beyond all the normal limits of our limiting thoughts and those limiting thoughts limiting our possibilities to set the world right by defeating and destroying the tyrants to ready the Face of the Earth for the Divine Ancestors who will take over the governance of the Sky-Earth once all the terrible Earth and Sky Monsters are slain and the False-face Rulers and Lords are taken down off their thrones.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the work of the Cultural Heroes like Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej have performed all along beginning with Wuqubʼ Kaqix to move to his Two Sons Sipakna and Kabʼraqan. Then we watched and listened to the Age of the Wooden People be put in order by the Heart of the Sky and his animating the pots and comals; the three hearth stones and the pots on the fire; the bowls and utensils; the domesticated dogs and turkeys; the houses the collapse, the caves that cave-in; the sticks and stones of the forest; all of which take down the soulless heartless Wooden People; that comes to conclusion with Wooden People being transformed into the Kʼoy as were the Twins Older Brother Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen who were transformed into the ʼchikopil-animalsʼ they always were: Kʼoy the Spider Monkey.

The Boys find out what is theirs as they take up their Ball-playing equipment to begin playing on the ballcourt of their Fathersʼ that they sweep-out every day to play and play and play for they are Noble Lords and Noble Lords play ball as Noble Lords play ball today but they start out as poor orphan or meebʼa. It is this story of the poor orphan becoming the great ballplayer that lives on to this day as it will live on here on the Face of the Earth as long as there are rubber balls and boys who want to follow their fathers in their play of the rubber ball game. And now we are in Xibʼalbʼa with the Boys really taking it to the Lords of Death and the back and forth ballgame playing during the day and Houses of Ordeal through the Dark of Night; the Freezing Cold; the Brawling Jaguars; the Burning Fire, and the Killer Death Bats. We have arrived folks with the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa because we have been summonsed once again by the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa to play their game. But the Boys play their own game by jumping head first into the sacrificial fire of ritual and its performance; the sacrificial fire of initiation and transformation… Letʼs get back in the myth and stay there from now on for the Boys have finally given themselves up for Dead to Death in the Underworld Land of the Lords of Death: Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Great euphoria erupted throughout Xibʼalbʼa as the Lords of Death burst forth with the pure unadulterated joy they now felt; for truly delirious were those of Xibʼalbʼa with the defeat and demise of the Boys.

Finally those of Xibʼalbʼa found themselves to be the victorious ones upon the death of the Boys; the death and defeat; destruction and demise of the Two Boys: Kaʼibʼ Kʼajolabʼ.

Xibʼalbʼa went mad whistling wildly with their hands; as they gathered together howling horrendously with their cries of ecstatic enchantment that overcame them and their Lords who were now utterly overjoyed by this definitive defeat and destruction of these beguilingly belligerent tricksters.

“We have defeated them! We have defeated them but they did not give themselves up easily,” cried the Lords. And so it was that they did next that which was theirs to do.

They summoned Xulu, Pakʼam. It was with them, Xulu, Pakʼam that the Boys had left their word; their word that was their instructions for those who asked what should be done with the bones.

Those of Xibʼalbʼa summonsed those known by the name of Xulu, Pakʼam who were just the ones to divine what they-the Lords-were to do with the bones of the Boys.

Xibʼalbʼa is an orderly lot, as you well know, from the naming of names to playing of games they do what they are told to do and this is what they did; which was just as they were instructed to do with the bones of the Boys that they gathered up from the ashes there in the stone oven of sacrifice.

They ground the bones down and then took them to the river where they scattered them in the water. But they didnʼt go far for they dropped straight down to the bottom of the river; to the bottom of the water; to the bottom of the river water.

This is when they transformed themselves into sharp, good-looking Young Men-e chaʼom kʼajolabʼ xeʼuxik. They became well-built; good-looking;

handsome Young Men; that is who they became; those who were the Two Boys transformed into beautiful Young Men.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is how they showed themselves when they showed themselves again to the people there up above. And so it was that when they showed themselves again they looked exactly the same as they looked before; and how they looked before was how they showed themselves to be again which is how they appeared now which was as two strong handsome, good-looking Young Men. This is all a play on how the Young Maya Maize Deity looks after he dies and goes into the Underworld to then rise up again just exactly the same as before. This is the quintessential idea of the kʼexel: the exact replica and replacement of the one who went before.

They transformed into sharp, good-looking youths-e chaʼom kʼajolabʼ; they appeared to be well-built young men with good looks whose appearance was just the same as it was before; this is the way they showed themselves when they showed themselves again as sharp good-looking youths who were equal, if not exactly the same as before; that was the way they made themselves to appear now; when they appeared again just exactly the same as they appeared before. But then on the Fifth Day they reappeared; this was when they were seen in the water on the waterʼs edge by the people who saw them there. The two of them looked just like Fish Men-xa Winaq Kar.

This then was when their faces were seen by those of Xibʼalbʼa who were out searching for them alongside the river. They were searching for them there because the people had seen them there at the waterʼs edge alongside the river. The next day, the Boys ʼdressed-xchuweqa-adornedʼ themselves to appear as Two Orphan Boys, Kaʼibʼ Mebʼa:

With rags they dressed themselves;

With rags they covered themselves;

With rags they bundled themselves up.

Nothing about these Boys looks made an impression on those of Xibʼalbʼa; in no way did their appearance call the attention of the Noble Lords: Ajawabʼ Xibʼalbʼa.

What the Boys did now was different from what they did before; they changed, they changed from what they were before; they transformed, the Boys acted differently; their way of being changed; their way of acting changed. Their way of being now was different from the way it was before.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Those of Xibʼalbʼa watched everything that they did and everything they did was the origin, the root, the source, el principio-uxeʼnajik of the downfall and defeat of Xibʼalbʼa by them; the dancers, the performers, the magicians; who were these Boys who had changed from what they were before into what they had now become. And so it was that word of their dancing arrived to the ears of the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame. So that those who came before them spoke passionately of what they heard and what they heard was from those who had seen and experienced the marvels of magic that these Two Orphan Boys enjoyed performing; or the dances they danced; or the sacrifice they performed as ritual sacrifice.

“Who are these Two Orphan Boys that everyone is talking about?” asked Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame. “Is it true that everything they do is so sweet? Is it true that their dancing is so beautiful?” asked the two Lords. “It is true that their dancing is sweet for it is truly beautiful; everything they do is something special to see!” said the one who brought the news to the Noble Lords; the Noble Lords who were made content just hearing the wonderful news of these Orphan Boys who danced and did all they came to do; those Poor Orphan Boys who performed all they came to perform.

Truly, all the many stories that arrived with the Lords were received with delight while at the same time their curiosity obliged them to ask the one who came with the news: “Could it be true that they really do all the things it is said they do?”

Immediately the Lords sent for their Messengers so they could be sent to summons the Boys to come entertain the Lords with their dancing of their dances; their making of their magic; their performing of their sacrifice.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
those who are so enthusiastic about our dancing our dances? What would we tell all of them; all of those who havenʼt seen our dancing yet; yet patiently await our arrival to entertain them?” “The dances we do canʼt be done before the Lords. We canʼt dance like that before the Lords. We canʼt do the kinds of dances we do when we are asked to dance before a Lord in the House of a Lord. So that is why we donʼt want to go dance for the Lords. Nope, not for us; it just isnʼt something that we would like, or even want, to do. So thank you but we wonʼt be going with you, oh Messenger- Workers, Ix Samajel,” said Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej content they had made themselves well understood by the Messengers of the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa. They went anyway, by punishment alone did they go; only under pain and threat of pain did they go; as they left walking afoot between their escorts. And this is how they found themselves moving as the moved ever so slowly along with those who were sent to summons them.

Only when they were forced to walk did they walk; only when forced to move did they move. Many times they resisted. They just went back and forth, side to side, wandering about; meandering around here and there is the way they went when they went walking towards where the Lords where; there to Xibʼalbʼa is where they were headed as they went walking accompanied by the Messengers- Samajel-Workers of Ajawabʼ Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame.

Those Messengers of Xibʼalbʼa kept them moving; they knew how to keep people moving who wished not to move where they were summonsed.

Many times those of Xibʼalbʼa pressed the Boys forward and many times the Boys resisted. The Messengers were forced to go back and forth to keep them moving in the right way. They constantly were after the Boys to keep them walking in the direction they were headed.

They were headed towards Xibʼalbʼa; that is the way they went; and the way they went was dragging their feet. The Orphan Boys were determined not to go where they were summonsed but in the end they arrived there anyway.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Before they knew it the two of them found themselves right where they wanted to be: obedient subjects; devoted vassals invited in to the House of the Lords. The Lords brought them before them; the poor Orphan Boysʼ eyes cast down ʼas ifʼ suffering from some sort of shameful sort of disgrace. With great humility they humbled themselves before the Noble Lords. This was when they entered showing profound reverence; with profound deference they doubled themselves over as they bowed down deep to those who invited them as part of the poor, pitiable populous brought to entertain their proud, powerful Lords.

This was when they entered humbling themselves before the Lords by laying prostrate before those of Xibʼalbʼa; the Orphans, Mebʼa, placed themselves face- down to express their full obedience to the Noble Rulers of Xibʼalbʼaʼ.

They showed themselves to be the very image of dutiful subjects of their Noble Lords because they truly appeared to be the poor Orphans that they were said to be; the very same Orphans that lay prostrate before these Noble Lords who now looked upon the Mebʼa as the ʼBoysʼ they appeared to be.

It was then that the Lords asked them about their mountain places-juyubʼal; their wild places in the mountains that was their home. They were asked about their People; who were their Pueblo-Amaqʼ to whom they were born.

They were questioned about their Mother-Chuch, their Father-Qajaw asking them: “So then, where do you come from?” “¿Apa kixpe wi!” Xeʼuchaʼxik.

“We donʼt know, you oh Noble Lord-at Ajaw-you oh Noble Ruler. We know not the face of Our Mother-QaChuch; we know not the face of Our Father- QaQajaw. We were just small children when they died,” they said as they spoke there before the Great Lords; Nim AjAwabʼ Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They said nothing; nothing that would reveal who they were; nor who their Mother was neither who their Father was when they answered the questions of Xibʼalbʼa. “Utz bʼa la! Just do a little bit; just a bit for us to see,” said the Lords. “What would you like? Your payment, what shall it be? What is it that we might give you for your fee, for we didnʼt invite you here to dance for free; so what will it be for us to see your dance, for your sing songs, there must be something we can give you that you might perform a bit more contentedly?” they were asked then, the Boys, by those of Xibʼalbʼa. “We donʼt want anything! For truly we are afraid to perform here for you,” they said then to the Ruler when they spoke to the Lord. “Donʼt be afraid! Donʼt feel intimidated! Donʼt be embarrassed! Donʼt feel humiliated! ¡Mixibʼij iwibʼ! Mixxobʼik!”

“Dance; dance that you might just dance all the many dances that you dance.” “First dance the one where you sacrifice yourselves.”

“Then do the one where you burn down my house.” “Donʼt be embarrassed! Whatʼs to fear now that your here! Donʼt feel afraid; donʼt feel ashamed! ¡Mixibʼij iwibʼ! Mixxobʼik!”

“Do all that you know; show us all you can show! To watch you dance is all that we want; that you should dance is all that we long for; just to liven up our lives here in Xibʼalbʼa is why sent for you to be invited over here. So show us what you know by your dancing all of your dances and performing all you magical enchantments. That is all that we want; that is all that we ask for,” said the Noble Lords to the Orphan Boys.

“So have no shame! This was our heartsʼ desire when we summonsed you here, you poor orphans-ix mebʼa. Please, we wish to give you your pay for your dancing today!” they were told then when they were spoken to by the Lords; when they arrived there prepared to perform before those of Xibʼalbʼa.

It was then that they began their song-kibʼix; it was then when they began their dance-kixajoj. Then they all came in, all those of Xibʼalbʼa they crowded in tight so all could see them-the Meebʼa-perform their dances; this then was when they danced their dances:

They danced the Weasel Dance-xkixaj Kux;

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They danced the Whip-poor-will-xkixaj Pujuy;

They danced the Armadillo-xkixaj Ibʼoy. Then the Ajaw-Lord-Ruler said to them: “Sacrifice my dog, then bring him back to life,” they were told-xeʼuchaʼxik.

“Fine!” they said. “We!” xechaʼ. When they sacrificed his dog then they brought him right back to life. Really, truly was he content, the dog; the dog of the Lord was made quite content when he was brought back to life; wagging his tail the way he did when he jumped back to life! Then the Lord said to them: “That you just might burn-up my house then a bit if you wouldnʼt mind!”

That is when they set fire to the House of the Ajaw-rochoch Ajaw Xibʼalbʼa- the house of the Lord of Xibʼalbʼa was set ablaze with all the Lords packed inside; but they didnʼt burn up, nobody died.

Instantly, everything was just exactly as it was before; immediately, the Lords were perfectly fine again, nothing was lost; nothing was destroyed in the Noble House of the Noble Lord One Death: Ajaw Jun Kame.

All of the Lords where simply amazed by all that the Boys did; Boys who they now admired as these dancing Orphans that they were but also for their miraculous transforming powers that were ancestral powers to do the impossible which the Lords had never seen nor experienced anything like it before; the way they could do what they could do that they did as that which had never been done before.

Their dances too left the Lords as content as could be as they watched with joy all there was to see. Whichever dance the Boys performed the Lords enjoyed it greatly; truly content were they with every dance the Boys danced.

But then they desired another sort of dance and they all knew what that was because it was the very reason those Orphan Boys had been summoned by the Noble Lords to come dance their dances and perform their performances; because what their hearts most desired was that they should perform their dance of sacrificial death.

So this then was when those Ancient Ancestral Dancers from the time of the Ancient Ancestors were told by the Lords:

“Now then, put ʼA Person-Jun Winaqʼ to death! Sacrifice him without him dying dead!” was the next challenge put to them.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Chikamisaj na kʼu Jun Winaq! Chipusu, ma ta kʼu chikamik!” Xeʼuchax kʼut.

“Utz bʼa la!” said the Boys when they said, “Muy bien!”

This then was when they looked upon the great crowd and grabbed hold of a person; this ʼOne Person-Jun Winaqʼ they were to dispatch right there.

This then was when they sacrificed him. They sacrificed him by making his beating heart burst forth from his chest, to then extract it before holding it up high for all to see to then show its perfect roundedness there before the Noble Lords before presenting it to them to turn about in their hands with infinite glee.

Truly awesome was what they saw, truly amazed by it all, were Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame; One Death, Seven Death, as they are known, as they are named: the ruling Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

So then immediately they brought this ʼOne Person-Jun Winaqʼ back to life again. Great was the contentment that filled his heart; the heart of this Jun Winaq; this One Person; greatly did his heart rejoice when he was brought back to life again. Filled with admiration were the Lords; they were left deeply astonished by what they had just seen. And then one of them had an idea. “Sacrifice yourselves in turn, so that we might see it ourselves. Truly our hearts wish for nothing more than to see this dance of yours,” said the Lords- Ajawabʼ.

ʼUtz bʼa la, very well then, you, our Lord-at Ajaw,” they said.

And so then they sacrificed one another; XJunajpu was sacrificed first by XBʼalamke. Kʼate puch xkipus kibʼ: are kʼu xpus ri XJunajpu rumal XBʼalanke.

One by one his legs came off, his arms as well; his head came off and fell to the floor to then roll, it rolled pretty far.

His heart was cut-out and dripping wet it was set atop a flat green leaves of maize-tzʼalik-as these flat green leaves of maize are called!

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Drunken with ecstasy were all the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa, intoxicated with delight were all of them who were now filled with awe by all they saw those dancing Orphan Boys could do. Only one of them went dancing about: Ixbʼalamkej-Little Jaguar-Deer alone spun all around; dancing while spinning and spiraling about now completely unbound did Ixbʼalamkej go dancing round and round when he danced his dance of sacrifice to the drum that was pound to make the sound of sacrifice: tun, tun; tun, tun; tun, tun.

“Katwalijoq! RISE-UP!” he shouted then. Joyously did he, Junajpu, come back to life; for it was he who survived the cutting-edge of the sacrificial knife!

Great was the contentment of the Boys for having performed their sacrificial dance there before the Lords. And just like the contentment of the Boys so was the contentment of the Lords for the Boys to have performed their dances there before them the Lords; for it was ʼas ifʼ the Lords had danced those dances of sacrifice themselves.

And so then the Lords suffered a keen eager yearning from within; a yearning that they felt as a deep desirous longing in their hearts; for now the Lords hungered to dance the dance of XJunajpu, XBʼalanke when they danced their dance of ritual sacrifice. This then was when these words sprang out of Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame: “Do it to us! Sacrifice us!” when they cried out: “Chibʼanaʼ chiqe! Kojipusu!” “Sacrifice each one of us, one by one, both the same-Junal taj kojipusu!” said Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame to XJunajpu, XBʼalanke. “Utz bʼa la! Very well then! Certainly you will come back to life; could there be death for you? Can Death be killed?”

Utz bʼa la; chi kʼastaj iwach; ma pa ix kʼo kam?

“We have only come to entertain and amuse you; you, our Sovereign Lords and Rulers; you, oh Noble Lords of divine daughters, sacred sons; devoted vassals, dutiful subjects-Ix pu Rajawal iwal, ikʼajol.” they said then to their Lords of Xibʼalbʼa.

The First Lord they sacrificed was the ʼHead Ruler-Jolom Ajaw-la Cabecera known as Jun Kame, named One Death for he is the Sovereign Lord and Ruler of Xibʼalbʼa-Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The first lord they sacrificed by lopping off his head, decapitating him just as he suggested, precisely as he requested; and that was that Ajaw Jun Kame was finally dead; the Jolom Ajaw the Head Lord have succumbed to Death.

Seeing this happening there before their eyes, those of Xibʼalbʼa ran for their lives; afflicted by fear, filled with dread, all of them fled seeing that their Noble Lords and Rulers were now deader than dead. And so it was that the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa lay there lifeless; just as the Lords of Death lay there dead the two of them had each given up their head.

In the original text it appears that the two lords are sacrificed together but then the authors return to Wuqubʼ Kame-Seven Death to tell of his humbling himself before the Boys to beg for his life but they sacrifice him in a ritual ways spoken of here as xaraxoj and xaraxoxinaq which is explained below. So do realize as a translator I am following the original text and its authors that we must assume are communicating to the reader in meaning ways of communication that are purposeful ways of communication even they that might appear to be otherwise.

Once Jun Kame had met his death; once One Death, Jun Kame was dead, the Boys, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej quickly grabbed hold of Wuqubʼ Kame-Seven Death, for it was he who was next. They didnʼt bring them back to life-Mawi xkʼastaj chi kiwach.

They sacrificed-e xaraxoj the first of them and then they left his companion sacrificed-xaraxoxinaq as well. They did this to punish them. Straight-a-way they sacrificed the First Lord-Jun Ajaw who was the Head Lord-Jolom Ajaw but they didnʼt bring him back to life.

The other Lord tried but he could not escape and so he went before the dancers and humbled himself. He knelled before the dancers and wept calling out: ʼToqʼobʼ nuwach! Have mercy on me!ʼ as he begged and beseeched them to show him mercy for all that he felt towards those who now held him captive; but it was too late for that. All the Sons and Daughters; the Subjects and Vassals of the Lords went running to save themselves by descending down into the deep canyon there where they sought refuge and safety.

¡Xaraxoxinaq!

body:
¡Aj Xaraxoj Aj Xaraxoj Winaq! ¡Aj Raxa Laq, Aj Raxa Tzel! It was then that the chests of the Lords were cut-open and their hearts torn from their chests to then be held up high. Both of them, the two of them, those who had begged for their own sacrifice, now had their beating hearts extracted from their open chests.

This ritual act of Heart Sacrifice spoken of as Xaraxoj obtains its name from the Blue- Green Bowl of Sacrifice. This is the blue-green bowl-raxa tzel or blue-green gourd-raxa tzel that was used to gather up the sacrificed heart and blood during the ritual performance of ritual sacrifice. This ritual sacrifice of decapitation, dismemberment, and heart extraction was performed by very specialized temple priests known and named as Aj Xaraxoj Winaq. Those who performed this practice of Heart Sacrifice-Xaraxoj were spoken of as Sacrificers of the Blue- Green Plate, Blue-Green Bowl-Aj Raxa Laq, Aj Raxa Tzel; making them Aj Xaraxoj that molded and modeled their names to become Xaraxoxinaq or Sacrificers of the Blue-Green Plate, Blue- Green Bowl of Ritual Sacrifice!

This short section of naming the names of heart sacrifice is only mentioned here as Xaraxoj even though this sacrifice will be performed by the Makers of the Blue-Green Plate, Makers of the Blue-Green Bowl; AjRaxa Laq, AjRaxa Tzel as the Sacrificial Priests of Ajaw Nakxitl Quetzalcoatl from Tollan Tzuy-Wa. These are those who are Makers that are Modelers and Molders of the Blue-Green Plate of Sacrifice, Blue-Green Bowl of Sacrifice; AjRaxa Laq, AjRaxa Tzel known as Jun Raqan-Ukʼux Kaj; Ukʼuʼx Ulew-Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz. In which these Primordial Deities of the Creation and Destruction of the Ages and Eras of the Suns and Moons of Mesoamerican Civilization are called upon as Jun Raqan Kaqulja and his precious twin rival and adversary is also his collaborative and complementary companion of creation known as Sovereign Plumed Serpent-Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz is also known as Ukʼuʼx Choʼ-Ukʼuʼx Palo, Heart of the Lake, Heart of the Sea thus Heart of the Water; Quetzalcoatl: the Precious Twin of Mesoamerica and its Ancestral Tradition of Sacred Twinship.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This short naming of the names Xaraxoj and Xaraxoxinaq apparently says so very little when in reality these names that speak of ʼritual sacrificeʼ speak as they suggest the principal concern of the entire last third of the telling of this sacred history that is the mythic history of Popol Wuj in which sacrifice will be spoken of in hidden yet revealing ways. The Spanish Inquisition must have been very present in the hearts and minds of the Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw who as highly trained Maya Scribes were concerned about survival of this literary masterpiece that they dedicated their lives to writing thus risking their lives for writing it. So they had to be very careful how they presented sacrifice. The better it was hidden the more likely their legacy left in writing would be protected.

Perhaps what is most important here is the legitimization of human sacrifice as heart extraction or Xaraxoj performed by Xaraxoxinaq who are named as Being of the Blue-Green Bowl; Blue-Green Gourd of Sacrifice who are known as no other than Twin Deities or Kabʼawil known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuxʼ Ulew Juraqan Kaqulja and Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz Ukʼuʼx Choʼ- Ukʼuʼx Palo; AjRaxa Laq, AjRaxa Tzel. The Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw scribes are very secretive here in order to protect their Ancestral Account of their Ancestors past.

As soon as they killed the First Noble Lord-who no longer was brought back to life-did the Second Lord come trembling before the dancers.

“Have mercy on me; Toqʼobʼ nuwach!” he cried out when he realized what was about to happen to him.

“Pardon me; have mercy on me; I beg you; I beseech you; mercy me Boys: Toqʼobʼ nuwach! Toqʼobʼ nuwach!” was all he could say; these were his only words now that he felt his grave situation. Those of Xibʼalbʼa ran for their lives trying to escape, the daughters, the sons; the subjects, the vassals; kal, kikʼajol of the Noble Lords fled to the Great Canyon: Nima Siwan. Just One-Xa Jun was how they ended up piled on top of one another in the deep gorge known Nima Xolobʼachan; the Great Abyss.

body:
It was there that they piled on top of one another; then there came a great swarm of Ants, countless quantities of swarming Ants flooded over the canyon as if theyʼd been driven there by an unseen force. It was only then, because of the Ants that those of Xibʼalbʼa were driven out of there; it was only because of the swarming Ants did the vassals and subjects; the daughters and sons of Xibʼalbʼa give themselves up to the new rule and authority of the realm; delivering themselves over to the new lords of the land.

They bowed down low, they wept and they wailed as they came back to give themselves up to those who subjugated them.

Those of Xibʼalbʼa who tried to escape were those who now returned to prostrate themselves before the Boys as sign of obedience; as act of submission.

Those of Xibʼalbʼa returned in mass as show of respect; they returned to show humility; to show reverence and regard for those who conquered them there in Xibʼalbʼa.

Thus then were they defeated, the Noble Lords of Xibʼalbʼa-Rajawal Xibʼalbʼa. It was just their astonishing performance of magic; it was just their astounding powers of transformation that gave them their ancestral ability to do all they came to do to become the Nawal Winaq that they were born to be by saying and doing all they came to say and do. And so this then was when they named their names-xkibʼij kibʼiʼ to reveal their origin in order to let everyone know who they were and from where they had come. They named their names of noble entitlement-xkikobʼisaj kibʼ-noble ancestry; they named their names before all of those of Xibʼalbʼa to reveal their noble roots; their noble lineage.

For these Boys were not poor orphans known as mebʼa; no, no they were indeed Engendered Sons of Noble Lords-Kikʼajolabʼ whoʼs Mother; IxKikʼ was the Noble Daughter of a Noble Lord of Xibʼalbʼa: Kuchuma Kikʼ. And so they ʼnamed their namesʼ which is where this Ancient Ancestral Account began with the first ʼNaming of the Namesʼ as the invocation of the Divine Ancestors and Kabʼawil at the very beginning of this recitation of Popol Wuj.

body:
“Hear our names that we shall now name! Just as we shall name the names of our Fathers; for it is the names of our Fathers who we shall now name!”

“Oj Waʼ! We are here! We are Sustenance! Oj Waʼ! Here We Are-Oj Wa! We are Present! ¡Presentes! Oj Waʼ! We who are XJunajpu, Xbʼalanke by name! We, who are those named JunAjPu and IxBʼalamKiej. We are here! We who have won the day! Oj Wa!”

“Oj Wa! Oj Wa! We-Oj who are Here-Wa! We who are Present! We-Oj who are Sacred Sustenance-Wa; Oj Wa! We-Oj who are the Heads-Wa of our Pueblo; Oj Wa! We who are they who are here to lead our Pueblo: Oj Wa!”

And these are the names of our Fathers who you killed: Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are their names.”

¡Oj Wa!

We are here!

We who are Maize! Oj-We and Wa-Here Oj Wa!: We are who we are! But also Oj Wa! Oj-Ancient, Oj- Ancestral, Oj-We, Oj-We the Ancestors, Wa-Sustenance; Oj Wa-We the Ancient Ancestral Sustenance! ʼOj-Weʼ and ʼWa-Sustenanceʼ: Oj Wa. Oj Wa: We, the Sacred Sustenance of the Ixim Winaq: Maize People, Oj Waʼ! Oj Wa, We-Oj the Head-Wa; It seems that the Scribes are also saying that they are present at the end of this definitive death of the Lords of Death. So that the Scribes say ʼWeʼ the storytellers of this Ancient Ancestral Account are present in our presentation of this Sacred History, Sacred Narrative that constitutes the sacred sustenance of the Mayaʼs Mythic Soul which is the Mythic History of the Kʼiche Maya: ¡Oj Wa! ¡Presente! We are here! This is the Sacred Sustenance to feed those who must be fed and who hunger for the divine essence of their Divine Ancestors: Oj Wa! We the Ancient Ancestral Essence of Maize; We-Oj the Head-Wa of Sustenance-Wa: Oj Wa! We-Oj are present; we who are the essence of the Sacred Flesh of Maize-Wa of the People of Maize: Ixim Winaq! We are who are Maize; we whoʼs bodies are formed from Maize so that We-Oj are Maize as Maize is Sustenance-Wa; Oj Wa and so it is that We are the People of Maize-Oj Wa; Ixim Winaq.

body:
We-Oj who will go on being formed, shaped; modeled, molded to be made in the knowing, feeling, intuitive, insightful, and ingenious hands of IxMuqane, Grandmother and Mother of the Ixim Winaq and all of her replacements from one generation to the next of Mothers and Grandmothers of the Ancestral Lineage of the Ixim Winaq; People of Maize: Oj Wa!.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are their names, the names of the First Fathers of the Maize People who are the Fathers of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. It was their Gourd-Head; their Gourd-Skull; their Gourd Head, Tzuy Wa; their Gourd-Skull, Tzima-Jolom that was the head of the skull that was the gourd that was the head that was the jolom of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu that was the spit; that was the pitz; that was the spittle; that was the kʼexaj; that was the spit; that was the chʼubʼ that was the engendering essence of their replacements or kʼexaj that came from the skull-jolom to engender-kʼojolaj the engendered Boys-Kʼajolabʼ-Engendered Sons in which the skull-jolom is the seed-ijatz within which is the engendering essence-kʼojeʼik of the ancestors; the essence that engenders the Sons of the Moon Mother IxKikʼ who are the Grandsons of Earth Mother Ixmuqane. It will be in the ʼcenterʼ of the House of IxMuqane that the Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej will plant canes of maize; canes of maize that will grow and transform in order to live and die to be sown again to sprout forth with life as maize plants who are the Twin Heads of Maize that were sown in the Center of the House of IxMuqane as you will soon come to see.

body: This will be how this first half of the Popol Wuj ends with the Sowing of Maize in the Center of the House of IxMuqane. Is IxMuqane then not the Earth within which is buried the sown seeds of maize? Is not the House of IxMuqane the Face of the Earth? Is not IxMuqane the Face of the Earth within which is sown the sacred sustenance of the Maize People? But nobody is going to tell you this in a literal materialist rational analytical world in which a mythical figure cannot be a manifestation of a natural reality. To understand the Imaginal Realm of Myth one must enter the word in imaginative ways that open up a mythic world in which mythic truths transform the natural world into a mythic reality. Can we read myth as a literal truth to reveal material reality that was originally expressed as mythical realms through the mythic imagination? No, no one must imagine myth as the mythic imagination that comes to life through the thought of the heart which is to think mythically; which is to think metaphorically; which is to think by engaging oneʼs mythic imagination in order that the mythic world is brought to life through oneʼs mythic imagination. If you have learned anything in this book I hope it is that you have learned to engage your mythic imagination so you can begin to think through the thought of your heart in order to feel through the heart of your heart to know through the engagement of the human soul and its divine way of knowing oneʼs thoughts as the feeling of. This is the way one must enter the word of Popol Wuj to understand it as the Sowing of the Seed and the Dawning of the Sun of the Ixim Winaq: Maize People.

body:
To understand the Popol Wuj similar to the way the Maya once understood it requires us to engage our soul in the mythic imagination that is known as the ʼthought of the heartʼ that is understood as the ʼfeeling of oneʼs soulʼ through the mythic imagination that calls upon us to engage ourselves heart and soul in the forming and shaping of an Imaginal Realm that can only come to life through our soulsʼ engagement in the mythic words and mythic images that are sown in our imagination the secret sacred speech of the Ancient Word that reveals as it recites the Ancestral Account.

To understand the Popol Wuj similar to the way in which it was once understood asks a great deal from us humans yet there is nothing that is human that cannot be understood to us human beings and this is why we have done all we have do to translate and interpret the Ancient Word of the Popol Wuj so that the audience can understand its Ancestral Account in magical kinds of transformative ways that awaken our hearts and souls through our engagement with the mythic imagination and its ʼnawal wayʼ of forming and shaping ancient images of the Ancestral World of the Sky-Earth.

This is what we are engaged with here as bring to fruition the expression; the revelation; and the recitation of the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of the Popol Wuj. It has only been through our effort to bring to life the Popol Wuj that we have awakened our understanding of the Maya Culture in the context of the Mesoamerican Civilization.

It has only been through our engagement of our mythic imagination that we have come to experience the Sowing, the Dawning; Ewaxibʼal, Saqiribʼal as the revealing of all that was hidden in the shadows to be brought forth in the light. It has only been our desire to bring forth the knowledge and insight of the past in the present in order to transform our lives in a transformed world in the future that we have made the effort we have since the very first footstep with took on this mythic path we have walked upon from the very first page of this Translation and Interpretation of this Sacred Narrative of Popol Wuj.

body:
This is the mythic narrative of the Sowing of the Maize People in the Towns and Citadels of the Mountain Places and Canyon Country. This is the Sacred History of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Lineages that begins with the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Sun and its light bringing to life the First Men; First Women known as the First Mothers; First Fathers. They are those who formed and shaped the Great Houses that were established throughout the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom where marriage alliance with Kʼicheʼ Lords were gifted the Noble Daughters of Noble Mountain Lords to create Great Houses throughout the Mountains and Canyons that were conquered and settled by Kʼicheʼ Maya Warlords and War-Captains. We have traveled a long, long way on this Mythic Journey of Transformation that has been brought to life as a Long Performance of the Perfect Life; Precious Existence spoken of as Saq Kʼaslem; Winaqirem.

When we finish this section with the Sowing of the Seed in the Great House of IxMuqane we will move on to the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Sun as the Sun of the Ixim Winaq. We will soon move into the Dawning part of the Popol Wuj as we come to understand just exactly what the Ancient Word; Ojer Tzij means by the Sowing and Dawning in a World where Ojer signifies Ancient and Ancestral as well as We and Us in the sense that Oj signifies We the Ancestors who are the Ancestral Sustenance-Oj Wa-Ancient Sustenance.

This then is the divine lineage of those who ʼName the Namesʼ of their Ancient Ancestors who are the Divine Ancestors of the Ixim Winaq: Oj Wa; Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane; Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; Ixbʼaqiyalo, Jun Bʼatzʼ, Jun Chowen; Jun Junajpu IxKikʼ Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej. Oj Wa!

These are those who are spoken of as Kabʼawil who will be followed by the Divine Ancestors of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq: the First Fathers known and named Bʼalam Kiʼtzʼe; Kaqa Palama; Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ; the First Mothers named and known as Chomi Ja; Majukutaj Tzʼununi Ja; Ikʼi Bʼalam Kaqixa Ja who will give birth to the First Mothers; First Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Maya and their Thirteen Lineages of Twin Kʼicheʼ Noble Lords and Rulers as they will become named when the time comes for the ʼNaming of the Namesʼ of these lineages. Popol Wuj is also saying Oj Wa suggests the idea that those who are the ʼOj-Weʼ who enter the Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij are those who enter the Wa-Sacred Sustenanceʼ of the Maya Soul known through the Imaginal Realm of this Ancient Account that is the Mythic Metaphor of Maize told through the sacred narrative of the victorious Cultural Heroes known as the Hero Twins: Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who defeat Death in the House of Xibʼalbʼa to transform through initiation to be reborn as sharp good looking Young Men-e Chaʼom Kʼajolabʼ who are well- spoken handsome Young Men.

These Young Good-Looking Young Men are the Maize Deities yes but they are also those who are at the cutting edge of destiny as the Men of the Obsidian Blade-Chaʼom. These are the ʼsharp-lookingʼ Kʼicheʼ Warriors who are also Sacrificial Priests who perform human sacrifice known as AjKajbʼ AjKʼixbʼ who we will come to know exceedingly well as we enter into the Kʼicheʼ Maya Mythic History that tells of the Dawning-Saqiribʼal of the Kabʼawil of Tollan Tzuy Wa and the First Father Warlords who must feed them in order that the Kabʼawil feed those who must be fed: Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼiche Amaqʼ.

body:
We are just now coming to the end of the Sowing-Ewaxibʼal aspect of Popol Wuj that tells of the Divine Maize Ancestors with their ʼNaming of Namesʼ while saying: Oj Wa-We are Maize; We are Sustenance; We are Here to be planted as the Boys were planted; as the Sons were sown by their being engendered by the Divine Ancestor of the Maize People: Jun Junajpu the son of the Maize Father Xpiyakok who is he who sprouts forth from the tortoise shell earth; and, son of the Maize Mother IxMuqane who is she of the buried tooth-seed of maize! Oj Wa! We are here who will expand the Kʼicheʼ Territory to leave the earth sown with the sacred seed of the Ixim Winaq; the People of Xpiyakok, IxMuqane.

We are about to hear when and where IxMuqane deifies the sacred sowing of maize in the sacred milpas of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom and its Great Houses. IxMuqane as the Matriarch of the Maize People will have her Boys; her Sons sow her divine seeds in her Ancestral Realm in order to transform it into the Sacred Territory of the Ixim Winaq-Maize People of Maize. IxMuqane will deify her Sacred Realm of Maize by deifying maize through the sacred act of ʼnaming the namesʼ of maize at the moment of sowing maize within the womb of the earth which is to say in the body of the Divine Grandmother of Maize: IxMuqane.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
You will see and hear this acting deification of maize through the sacred speech of IxMuqane who will name the names of the names of maize while naming the names of the sacred place where she will seed-ewexibʼal and sow-ewaxibʼal in this sacred act where she will hide- ewabʼal, and bury-muqubʼal her peopleʼs sacred seed within her ʼearth-wombʼ to grow the Yellow Maize-Qʼanajal, White Maize-Saqijal from which she will form and shape the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo; Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ while their women-ixoqil-wives will come forth from their ʼdreaming them into lifeʼ: Bʼalam Kiʼtzʼe and Kaqa Palama Red Sea Turtle House of the Red-East; Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ and Chomi Ja Shrimp or Prawn House of the White-North; Majukutaj and Tzʼununi Ja Hummingbird House of the Black-West; Ikʼi Bʼalam and Kaqixa Ja Scarlet Macaw House of the Yellow-South. Oj Wa! Finally these mature Older Boys have become mature Young Men and they have the right to name their names and proclaim who they are and where they come from so that everyone comes to know who their Fathers are and what happened to them and why they-the Young Men-have defeated the Lords of Death as a pay-back and debt-payment for their sacrificial deaths.

Here we go; this is it, the end where the judgment and condemnation are articulated by the Engendered Sons of Fathers who were sacrificed in the most unjust and mean-spirited way imaginable. For the Fathers of the Hero Twins were first deceived to then be humiliated by being laughed at truly shameful and degrading ways. Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame did everything they could to make their invited guests to feel shame and disgrace. This was gave their Sons the right to take out revenge on those who caused their Fathers to experience the dishonor and humiliation they were made to suffer; and so it was that Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej were driven to vengeance in search of retribution as a pay-back for what their Fathers were made to suffer.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These Cultural Heroes of the Maize People will now manifest the maturation and transformation of these once young and naïve Blowgun Boys who hunted birds for their Older Brothers. Now they are Nawal Winaq in every ways since that are those who are now known as Warrior-Priests who have earned the power and authority to sacrifice those who must be sacrificed to bring forth the necessary retribution and reprisal to create harmony and balance through reciprocal violence on the Face of the Earth.

Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are those who have survived the less than fair play of the Ballgames played out on the Underworld Ballcourt of Pusbʼal Chaaj to then face and overcome the tests, trials, and ordeals of the many Houses of Initiation in Xibʼalbʼa. These Young Noble Lords of their Grandmother and Grandfatherʼs Mountain Place-Juyubʼal are those who have become sovereign Noble Lords who are also powerful Warlords that act as Sacrificial Priests of Tolan Tzuy-Wa who practice ritual dance of sacrifice known as Xaraxoj. This is the ʼResplendent Deathʼ of ʼHeart Sacrificeʼ that they perform on the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa: Jun Kame, Wuqub Kame.

“We are those who came to avenge the suffering and affliction you caused Our Fathers-QaQajaw. We are those who came to take vengeance for the torturous deceit and torment you caused our Fathers Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; we are those who came to collect the ancestral debt that is the blood debt-pakʼol owed to us for the horrific loss caused and created by those of Xibʼalbʼa; they the Lords of Death; those who caused the agony and anguish suffered by Our Lord, Our Noble Father: Qaqajaw.”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“And it is only because of their pain and suffering that we were able to bear the pain and suffering you caused us; because you did cause us suffering and affliction as well. Now we must sacrifice you; we must finish you off; we must bring death to you. There will be no survivors amongst you; not one of you will be saved!” they said to them. And so it was that those of Xibʼalbʼa begged for mercy, all of those of Xibʼalbʼa just wept while they begged for mercy: “Toqʼobʼ qawach-Have mercy on us, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej!” called out those of Xibʼalbʼa: “It is true that we acted with cruelty against your Fathers; truly we have wronged your Fathers; just as you say, so it is so. They are buried beside the Pusbʼal Chaaj-Sacrificial Ballcourt; Ballcourt of Sacrifice,” they said.

“Utz bʼa la! Very well then! This then is our word-qatzij-our truth; our command, our orders given to you.”

“Listen up all of you from Xibʼalbʼa-Ix Xibʼalbʼa, because no longer shall your lineage be of any consequence, nor the vocation of your descendants be of any importance; no longer will your ʼdaysʼ be celebrated as they once were; neither will be the sacrificial offerings given to you be significant.” “Now all that will be yours is a bit of ʼfalse blood-kikʼ jolomaxʼ”

…just red nodules of incense, just the red foam that forms on the head of the cooked up sap, the extract from the croton tree-árbol de grana-this froth, this foam, this fuzz, these suds from this ancient ancestral work of making red dye from the croton tree will be the ʼthe head of foam or jolomaxʼ from which your sacrificial offerings will come; these red nodules of incense will be yours, but nothing more…

“No longer will it be ʼclean blood-chʼajom kikʼ-that will be given to you as burnt offerings. This is to say: no longer will pure blood; the clean-blood of blood sacrifice be the sacrifice that is offered to you.”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“The only thing left for you will be just the round clay tortilla comals broken to pieces, just busted old pots, just shattered shards of smashed pottery, just all those burnt and broken things made of clay will be yours; for that is what will be used to form, to shape your humble mounds that will become your altars of sacrifice.” “Everything that you were entitled to will be taken away, just as you will be brought down low. Just the offspring of the grasslands and just the offspring of deserted places will be your sustenance. It will be nothing more than insects; nothing more than serpents; nothing more than small winged creature that will be your sacrificial gifts, your sacrificial sustenance. Everything else shall be kept safe, kept secure, and kept protected, guarded from being offered up as sacrifice to you and your lineage. So be it!” “No longer will yours be the Saqil Al, Divine Daughters of the Dawn; no longer will yours be the Saqil Kʼajol, Sacred Sons of the Sun; Saqil Al-they who are the Dutiful Daughters of the Dawn; Saqil Kʼajol-they who are the Soulful Sons of the Sun who are known and named the Devoted Vassals and Loyal Subjects who are the Providers-Tzuqul and Sustainers-Kʼool of those who are the Noble Lords.” “No longer will these be those who provide and sustain you with your sacred sustenance; for no longer will you receive worship and adoration from the Daughters of the Dawn; Sons of the Sun; Vassals and Subjects of this Realm; Daughters and Sons of this Kingdom”

This is to say no longer will you receive any human sacrifice from the lineages of human beings that are to come!

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
“Only the destitute will bow before you. Just the lost ones, just the fallen ones will give you your sustenance. Just those who fight, the heartbroken ones, the afflicted ones, those who are bound to vice will be the one who enter there with you to give sacrifice to you.” “No longer will you just take anyone you want for whatever it is you want them for, enslaving the people of the mountain places and taking captives in the canyon country for your own needs of self-magnification and self- aggrandizement!” “For now you will only be invoked through offerings of false blood, the nodules of incense bled from the dragon tree, the sap tapped from the croton tree, known as the kikʼ jolomax,” this is what Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej said when they address those of Xibʼalbʼa who received their proclamation with their heads bowed but their hearts set free; their souls released from their ancestral burden that they no longer wished or wanted to bear or carried carry any more: the sacrificing others instead of their sacrificing of themselves.

It was over. The Ancient Ancestral Ways of Blood Sacrifice were over for those of Xibʼalbʼa. And that was the beginning of the end of their being called upon through invocation, incantation, and enchantment for no longer would the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa be called upon to kill and disappear others while causing people to suffer through deadly disease, damning disasters, and violent accidents.

No longer would their place be of any significance anymore; no longer were their days of worship of held to be of any great importance like they once were in ancient times.

For they were just dedicated to creating conflict and waging war these Ancient People-Ojer Winaq; continuous quarrel and constant combat were what these Old Style People most enjoyed instigating on the Face of the Earth.

And so it was that all the malicious malevolence that had been slowly creeping to an end had now come to an end with the uncompromising words of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Truly their names that were the names of Xibʼalbʼa were not divine names, nor were their Deities-Kabʼawil-Divinities seen as sacred any longer, no more were they held in high regard and thought to be powerful and potent anymore; there only capability and capacity was to frighten others by causing fear with their ugly frightening faces.

After all creating fear and dread by wearing terrifying masks and headdress was no great power for it brought nothing but disease and disharmony in peopleʼs lives.

It was they who were those that caused conflict; it was they who were known as AjTza-War People; tyrannical traitors one and all along with the AjTukur Winaq-Owl People.

The Owl People who found contentment in causing conflict and discord, pain and suffering, calamity and confusion for themselves and others. They were gifted at the art of hiding the true intentions of their heart. Just hypocrites, evil minded, and deceptive; they were just oppressors of others; that is who they were and continue to be for those who carry-on their ways by speaking and acting like them by following in their footsteps.

This is who they truly were; as it is said about these who were those who painted their faces to cause fear-susto-fright; just fear xawi xibʼal was the origin of Xibʼalbʼa. And it was they who were stripped of their grandeur and power. They were done for because nobody would tolerate folks acting that way any longer.

There was nothing left on their cheeks that could hide their lack of greatness and glory, nor was their dominion over others of any importance anymore.

All this was done by XJunajpu, Xbʼalamkej; they who had won the day by conquering the Lords of Death for they defeated fear and intimidation and now they were here to shine their light to show the way.

Grandmother of Ixim Winaq: IxMuqane Ancient Old Woman: Rilaj Ixoq Our Ancestral Grandmother: Qatiʼt

This then was when she wept; when they, the Boys, were invoked by their Grandmother; there before the Cane of Maize-ri Aj.

This is where they, the Grandsons, were called upon, beseeched before their Cane of Maize-ri Aj; the Cane of Maize that the Boys, the Sons had left planted-ri xkitik kanoq.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Sprouts of maize sprouted out; Xpe utux ri Aj; they grew, they flowered, they fruited, and then they dried back again-kʼate xchaqij chik. That was when they-the Boys-were burnt up in the stone oven: xekʼat pa Choj.

Sprouts came again-xpe chik utux ri Aj; and again Grandmother burnt offerings, she burnt copal incense before the Canes of Maize, as a remembrance of them; the Boys.

Grandmotherʼs heart was made content when for a second time the maize sprouts sprouted out; this is when Grandmother deified them-Ta xkabʼawilax rumal katiʼt; this was when she sanctified them. This was when she transformed them into Holy Lords of Maize; Divine Maize Deities; Divine Maize Ancestors as she made them Kabʼawil: Divinity.

Grandmother Blessed the Maize of the Pueblo IxMuqane Deified the Maize of the Ixim Winaq Deification-Kabʼawilax-of Maize Grandmother blessed the maize; Grandmother consecrated the maize to sanctify the maize to make the maize sacred; to make the maize divine by naming its name in the place it was planted. This naming of the maize is what made the maize divine-xkabʼawilax by sanctifying the maize and deifying the divine places it was sown to be known by its being named by the IxMuqane; Grandmother of the Ixim Winaq who sanctified the sowing of maize in order to deify the divine ancestry of maize in the place of its Sowing; and, by deifying the sacred space of their sacred lineage the Old Woman established the divinity of the Maize Peopleʼs divine ancestry who divine essence was embodied in the soul and spirit of maize.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so we have arrived; we have arrived at the Sowing of Maize as Divinity in its divine place with IxMuqane in her House. We are about to step into the ʼnaming of the namesʼ of these sacred space; divine places but first let us take a moment to reflect on what has just happened in this sacred scripture to understand how we will bring to fruition by bring this side of the Sowing and Dawning to completion as we make our way ever so carefully and cautiously through the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj known as the Sowing, the Dawning of Life with it Peopling and Populating the Face of the Earth. It will be Grandmother who names the sacred places where Maize was deified; the sacred spaces where Maize was sanctified when she established the divinity of the sacred canes of maize. This deification-kabʼawilax-of maize by the Ancient Old Woman IxMuqane was brought about by her naming the names of the canes of maize with the divine names of the divine places where their sacred seeds were sown that led to their sacred canes being grown.

These were the divine names given as the names of the sacred spaces where the sacred canes of maize were grown that were named with the sacred names given to them by their being named by the sacred names of the sacred places, sacred spaces they were sown.

This is the way Grandmother deified her Grandsons-the Boys- the Sons-the Hero Twins as the Holy Lords who were Maize Deities; Holy Lords who were Divinities of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq-Maize People. Grandmother sanctified as she deified the Maize Divinities through the ʼnaming of their namesʼ as the sanctification of their divine remembrance that was established by naming their names according to where the Maize Lords-Holy Lords were sown and grown as the Ancestral Deities of the Ixim Winaq: the Maize People.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These Ixim Winaq worshipped their Ancestral Maize Deities-Kabʼawil Ixim as the deities of their Sacred Sustenance-Kabʼawil Saq Ixim that were named by IxMuqane who was the Divine Ancestress; Divine Grandmother of the Ixim Winaq and their Sacred Sustenance White Maize; Yellow Maize; Silver Maize; Golden Maize; Lunar Maize; Solar Maize: Saq Ixim, Qʼan Ixim; Saqijal, Qʼanajal.

This is their story; the story of IxMuqane as: Ix-Muq-Qʼanil; She of the Buried Maize; Ix- Muq-Kan-Eey; She of the Sown-Maize-Seed-Teeth-Descendant. For it is IxMuqane now manifests as Kabʼawil as Divinity in the form and shape of the Great Mother of Maize who will now name the names of maize to deify it by naming the name of the sacred space in which it is sown.

This then is the Sowing in the divine relationship Twinship in the telling of the Ancient Ancestral Account of the Sowing Kʼicheʼ Maize and the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Sun. This then will bring the Sowing to fruition to prepare us for the Dawning to come.

This then is the naming of their names; the naming of the names of the Maize Deities; sacred names that were named by their being known as the names of the sacred spaces; divine places where the sacred seeds of maize were sown; where their divine canes of maize were grown:

Nikʼaj Ja: Middle of the House, Nikʼaj Bʼichoqʼ: Middle of the Harvest;

Kʼasam Aj: Living Cane of Maize Chʼatam Ulew: Flat-bed of Earth, were the names they were given.

This then was the naming of the names:

Nikʼaj Ja: Middle of the House Nikʼaj Bʼichoqʼ: Middle of the Harvest These were their given names because it was just in the Center of the House; it was just in the Middle of the House that the Maize-Aj was sown-rumal xa chunikʼajal upa kochoch xkitik Aj. This then is the naming of the Flatbed of Earth-Chʼatam Ulew and the Living Maize-Kʼasam Aj since it was on top of the Flatbed of Earth that was sown the living plants of maize known as Living Maize; Living Mazorca. It is said that the name Living Maize-Kʼasam Aj was the name given to this maize because the Boys planted this maize and it sprouted again when they came back to life as Kʼasam Aj: Living Maize.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Kʼasam Aj came to be known by its name, Living Maize-Kʼasam Aj, because the maize sprouts sprouted out-xpe utux aj-which is to say, ʼitʼs maize sprout comes-outʼ as they shoot-up, to rise-up and out of the Earth, as in the shoots of Maize that sprout out from the Living Earth.

These are the names that were placed by la Abuela IxMuqKanEey on the Maize that was left sown by the Boys, the Sons, the Twins: JunAjPu; IxBʼalamKej Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu These are the names of the First Fathers-Nabʼe kiqajaw of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej and of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq.

Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

These are their First Fathers who died long ago in ancient times; those ones known as Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu. These are their First Fathers who were killed long ago in antiquity; their names are Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

Are kʼu ri nabʼe kiqajaw xojeroq kekamoq ri Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

Are kʼu ri nabʼe kiqajaw xojeroq kekamoq ri Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

They saw then their faces, the faces of their Fathers, they saw them there in Xibʼalbʼa. Xkil chi kʼu uwach ri kiqajaw chilaʼ chi Xibʼalbʼa.

Their Fathers spoke with them there once they had defeated those of Xibʼalbʼa. Xchʼaw chik kiqajaw chi ke ta xkichʼak Xibʼalbʼa.

And since the Boys, their Sons, rose-up victorious over the Lords of Xibʼalbʼa they went directly to where their Father; their Uncle known as their Fathers who were buried to arrange their bones in order to adorn them so they could be affectionately revered; benevolently honored; highly respected; deeply venerated; shown eternal thanks and given everlasting praise through simple rituals of sacrifice and genuine acts of devotion.

None of which was possible unless their bones were properly prepared in the ancient ancestral way through rites of remembrance and recollection to then begin what would become an endless celebration of loving admiration and perpetual adoration. This then was what came to pass as the Maize Deity and his worship has continued through continuous change and constant transformation to be remembered today in truly astonishing ways.
