source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Here then is the ʼadornment and arrangementʼ of their Fatherʼs bones by them-uwiqik chik kiqajaw kumalʼ the Boys, the Sons which is to say they gave their Fathers their proper burial while arranging an altar-place upon which to receive burnt offering of sweet scented incense there beside Pusbʼal Chaaj.

Wa kʼute uwiqik chik kiqajaw kumal. Are xkiweq ri Wuqubʼ Junajpu: chila xbʼekiwiqa wi chi pusbʼal chaaj.

They ʼadorned and embellishedʼ as they ʼarranged and dressedʼ the remains of Wuqubʼ Junajpu. They went over there where he was to them put-him-together- xbʼekiwiqa wi- in the place known as Pusbʼal Chaaj-Altar of Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice.

Pusbʼal Chaaj is where Wuqubʼ Junajpu was ʼput back togetherʼ to then be properly ordered and adorned; arranged and embellishedʼ by his descendants.

Just his ancient face with its transforming essence was that which they wished to bring forth; so this is what they did; they brought forth the essential nature reflected in his face. In order to bring forth the fundamental nature of his face Wuqubʼ Junajpu was asked to name the names of everything that formed the essential nature of his face and so it was Wuqubʼ Junajpu who named the names of the essential aspects of his countenance; the names of the essential features of his face he was asked to name and so it was those that he named: His mouth-uchiʼ-his mouth His nose-utzaʼm-his nose His eyes-ubʼaq uwach-his eyes At first he found the names to then say them but then it was only this little bit that he was able to express; his mouth, his nose, his eyes; he was just able to name everything above the ʼlipsʼ of his mouth above his jaw; that is to say the ʼfleshʼ that once formed the fine features of his face were no more; all that was left was the hard bone of his skull with its mouth, nose, and eyes.

The ʼday-signʼ of the Sacred Count of Days of the Divinatory Calendar day Junajpu known also as Ajpu and Ajaw are universally illustrated with a mouth, a nose, and eyes, these alone are a remembrance of the original face of the First Father of Maize: Wuqubʼ Junajpu or Chicome Xochitl in Nahuatl: Jun Ajaw known here as this twin Wuqubʼ Ajaw.

body:
And even though his mouth could no longer name the names of each and everything, at least he was able to name all that was up above the lips of his mouth and thus he was heard again by his Sons who heard him name the names of his face with its mouth, nose, and eyes.

So this was when they showed Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu deep respect and great regard in order to honor him through the veneration of their Fathersʼ remains; their skull and bones. These they left properly buried and perfectly adorned to form and shape an ancestral altar place that finely finished and properly embellished that now stood there firmly planted beside the Pusbʼal Chaaj: Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice.

And so it was that they left their Fathers to be worshipped right beside the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballcourt Sacrifice by being remembered there through that which they left in this place: the ancestral heart of maize-wi kanajoq ukʼux-the ancestral soul of maize.

This is beautiful play on words pertaining to the remembrance of maize as the heart and soul essence of their Father that was left behind-wi kanajoq ukʼux-as the heart and soul of their Fathersʼ Nawal Essence as Maize Deities-wi-kan-aj-joq-head-body-cane-husk of maize as it is said in the secret sacred speech of the Ancient Ancestral Word. This is entire section makes serious play of words that are metaphors of the burial that is the ʼseeding and sowingʼ of the ancestral ʼbones and skullʼ that are ʼleft-behindʼ as the ʼseeds sownʼ of those First Fathers of the Ixim Winaq who are the Maize Deities: Jun Junajpu; Wuqubʼ Junajpu.

It was they, the Sons, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej who left the heart and soul of the Fathers right there beside the Pusbʼal Chaaj: “Here you shall be remembered; here you shall be invoked! This is how it shall be! Chuxik!” their Fathersʼ were told by their Sons.

This then was when they brought their ritual act of consolation to fruition, when they consouled their heart-xkʼubʼax ukʼux-when the heartened their soul there beside Pusbʼal Chaaj.

body:
“You will be the first to be worshipped by the subjects and vassals known as the Divine Daughters borne the Light; Sacred Sons begotten in the Light: Saqil Al, Saqil Kʼajol. Your names will never be forgotten by your ancestral descendants who will always be your Loyal Subjects and Devoted Vassals: Saqil Al, Saqil Kʼajol. So be it! Ta chuxoq!” This is what they said to their Fathers when they comforted them; when they consoled them; these then were their words of remembrance at the time of their return; at the time of their commemoration when they remembered their Fathers; when they celebrated council together to bring reconciliation and resolution to their lives for all they were made to endure in their noble hearts and ancient souls.

“We are here to make right the wrongs caused by your death and disappearance; we are here to remember all the pain and suffering the Lords of Death did to harm and humiliate you!”

This is the way they took leave of their Fathers, Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu, there beside the altar they formed, the shrine they shaped for their Fathers there beside the Burial Altar of the Sacrificial Ballcourt of Ballgame Sacrifice- Pusbʼal Chaaj.

It was then when the Boys, the Sons-ri Kʼajolabʼ rose-up victorious by defeating Xibʼalbʼa definitively-xchʼakatajinaqoq and what was most important was that they left Jun Kame, Wuqubʼ Kame sacrificed so that they would remain dead and disappeared, lost forever. Those two Lords of Death were gone for good, their lineage cut off at the root!

This was when they-the Boys, the Sons, the Twins-climbed up here into the bright light. Straightaway they ascended into the Sky: ʼOneʼ of them became the Sun and the ʼOtherʼ became the Moon.

It was then that it dawned, when it brightened, the vault of the Sky, the Face of the Earth.

There in the Sky is where they are now; up there in the great vault of the Sky. And up into the Sky then did climb the Four Hundred Boys-Jobʼ Much Kʼajolabʼ those who were killed by Sipakna.

body:
And so they became the Boysʼ companions; the stars of the Sky are what they came to be and they are there still shining in the darkness of the night, burning bright as the eternal essence, undying embers, the resplendent starlight of the Divine Ancestorsʼ Ancestral Soul.

Sowing of Maize-Ixim;

Dawning of the Sun-Qʼij;

Origin of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq In other words this was the beginning of the New Age of the New Sun, the New Moon, and the New Star-Venus that marked the New Era, the New Epoch of the Ixim Winaq on the Face of the Earth so the Former, Shaper need to complete their work so the People of Maize would be ready to meet the New Sun in order to greet the Dawn as they welcomed in the New Age of the Ixim Winaq.

This will be the Sun and Moon of the Maize People that will reign over the Sky-Earth and the Divine Time within which it will exist now that the Preparatory Age of the Hero Twins has come to a close. The Boys, the Sons, the Hero Twins, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are ready to enter the Sky as the Sun and the Moon and their Father Jun Junajpu as Morning Star-Venus Matutina and their Uncle Wuqubʼ Junajpu as the Evening Star-Venus Vespertina.

These are the Sun, Moon, Star passing overhead of the Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; the Former, the Shaper of the Maize People. These Celestial Deities will soon begin their walking over and across the Face of the Earth to transform the Face of the Earth as they move up and down its Mountains and Plains as they move across its Canyons and Valleys; Forests and Ravines; as you will soon come to see.

The time and space of this mythic narrative overlap as the time and space of the Ages; the Suns; the Eras overlap as mythic beings and natural beings from past Suns continue on as remnants of past Eras; past Ages like the Kʼoy or Spider Monkeys and the Constellations in the Night Sky that continue on above just as the Natural World continues on below much the same as it has always been.

body:
But it will be the Dawning of the Sun of the Maize People that will transform the Face of the Earth dramatically. This is cosmogonic moment of the highly anticipated arrival of the “Dawning of the Sun” that this Ancestral Account has already mentioned a great deal to create a profound anticipatory desire to know and experience the Dawn.

This then is the first annunciation of the Dawn of the Ixim Winaq; the Dawn of the Sun of the First Four Fathers; the Dawn of the Sun of the Age of the First Four Principal Kʼicheʼ Maya lineages; the Dawn of the Sun of the Age of the Era of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Kingdom; the Dawn of the Sun of the Age of the Era of the Epoch of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Kingdom becoming One with the Great Empire of Tula-Tollan Tzuy-Wa of the Great Lord and Ruler: Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz This building up of desire and anticipation is brought about through statements such as this one that is placed here that says: “There was just a little bit more to go before the Sun, Moon, and the Star-Venus passed over the heads the Former; the Shaper.”

This creates a close kind of contact with the imminence of the mythic moment while entering an euphoric sense of mythic transcendence in which one has the ecstatic experience of oneʼs soul transcending historical time and the ʼterror of historyʼ by entering the mythic time of ʼin illo temporeʼ that one experiences as time out of mind by entering ʼin those timesʼ of myth that never were yet always are experienced by the human soul and its imagination as the profound experiences we have when our hearts and minds; spirits and souls enter the Imaginal Realm of Myth: Myth that are said to be those things that never were but always are! Let us enter into this place of deep belonging where we enter the word and its world of being and becoming.

Quotes to Provide the Understanding; Quotes to Sustain the Knowledge

“A myth is a way of making sense in a senseless world. Myths are narrative patterns that give significance to our existence.” Rollo May

body:
“It helps to regard soul as an active intelligence, forming and plotting each personʼs fate. Translators use ʼPlotʼ to render the Ancient Greek word ʼMythosʼ in English. The ʼPlotsʼ that entangle our souls and draw forth our characters are the Great Myths. That is why we need a sense of myth to gain insight into our epic struggles, our misalliances, and our tragedies. Myths show the imaginative structures inside our messes, and our human characters can locate themselves against the background of the characters of myth.” James Hillman

“We may be closest to hearing the call when we feel alone or in trouble, for genius hides behind the wound and one of the greatest wounds in life is to not know who we are intended to be or what we are supposed to serve in life.” Michael Meade Genius Myth

“It is easy to understand why the memory of that marvelous time haunted religious man, why he periodically sought to return to it. In illo tempore the gods had displayed their greatest powers. The cosmogony is the supreme divine manifestation, the paradigmatic act of strength, superabundance, and creativity. Religious man thirsts for the real…through the annual repetition of the cosmogony, time is regenerated…the ritual recitation of the cosmogonic myth plays an important role in healing, when what is sought is the regeneration of the human being….thus the cosmogonic myth serves as the archetypal model for all creations, on whatever plane-biological, psychological, spiritual. But since ritual recitation of the cosmogonic myth implies reactualization of that primordial event, it follows that he for whom it is recited is magically projected in illo tempore, into the “beginning of the World” he becomes contemporary with the cosmogony What is involved is, in short, a return to the original time, in order to begin life again…”

The Sacred and the Profane Mircea Eliade “I will tell you something about stories…They arenʼt just entertainment. Donʼt be fooled. They are all we have, you see, all we have to fight off illness and death.” Leslie Marmon Silko “Language shapes the way we think, and determines what we think about.”

Benjamin Lee Whorf

body: “Our approach to imagining is predetermined by our idea of it. Disciplines of the imagination turn into a disciplining of the images. Insidiously we become biased against the world we wish to enter. And active imagination becomes subverted into mind control, gaining knowledge, strength, and wisdom at the expense of the images of the soul…I cannot raise my voice strongly enough against these methods. In them lies the abuse of the abuse of the soulʼs first freedom-the freedom to imagine…If we are willing to accept internal controls upon the imagination, will have succumbed already in soul to the same authoritarianism that would dominate the body politic. The connection between submission to technical manipulation of imagination and submission to external controls is subtle, but it is real… sin against the imagination whenever we ask an image for its meaning, requiring that images be translated into concepts.” James Hillman UKAJ FOURTH Ixim Winaq Maize People as Kʼicheʼ Winaq Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ The Sowing of a Culture; the Dawning of a Civilization Maize People: Ixim Winaq Maize, the Flesh of the Ixim Winaq: People of Maize Here then is its beginning; the beginning of the thinking about the forming; the beginning of the imagining of the shaping of the People of the Pueblo; the People of the Pueblos that will populate the Face of the Earth. This then is beginning of the telling of their story of the forming; of the shaping; of the molding, of the modeling; of the crafting, of the creating of the People of the Pueblo, who would be formed by the Former; who would be shaped by the Shaper: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol. This then was when they began the Ancient Ancestral Quest to find the sacred substance that would be used as the flesh to Form the Formed People; to Shape the Shaped People. This is the telling of their search for the essence of the material that would be used to Mold and Model the People of the Pueblo who would become the People of Maize; the Maize People known as the Ixim Winaq.

body:
Here then was its being sown; here then was when it was thought about; when its being thought about was contemplated; when its being contemplated was imagined; when its imagined to be searched for to be sought out in their quest to find the essence of the substance that would be used for the flesh of Human Beings: Winaq.

So then they spoke, and those who spoke were:

Alom: Bearer of Children; Mother of Sprouts; Mother of Descendants Kʼajolom: Better of Children; Engenderer of Sons and Daughters Tzʼaqol: Former, Maker, Molder; Constructor, Maker of Tzʼaqon, Tamales Bʼitol: Shaper, Finisher, Modeler, Creator, Refiner; Ceramicist, Sculptor Tepew Qʼukumatz-Sovereign Plumed Serpent, Majesty Feathered Serpent, Lord Quetzalcoatl, Conqueror Kukulcan; these are their names, kibʼi.

“Dawn approaches: our creation remains unfinished despite the time being right for their appearance; it is time they come out for the time is ripe for their emergence!”

“May they appear: the Providers, the Sustainers, Tzuqul, Kʼool; the Feeders, the Maintainers, Tzuqul, Kʼool; the Nourishers, the Nurturers, Tzuqul, Kʼool; those that Sustain Life, those that Maintain Life: Tzuqul, Kʼool.” “May they appear; may they be revealed as the Saqil Al; Divine Daughters of the Dawn; Precious Ones born in the Clear Light of the Sun; Beloved Daughters of the Dawn; Devoted Vassals of the Realm; Women and Girls: Saqil Al.”

“May they appear; may they be revealed as Saqil Kʼajol; Sacred Sons of the Son; Precious Ones begotten in the Clear Light of the Dawn; Beloved Sons of the Sun, Loyal Subjects of the Kingdom; Men and Boys: Saqil Kʼajol.” This is what they said when they spoke; those known as:

Alom, Kʼajolom;

Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol;

Tepew Qʼukumatz. “May people appear; may people come forth to populate the Face of the Earth,” they said, Mixqʼale winaq, uwinaqil uwach ulew!

body:
“May human beings appear; may human beings reveal themselves; may their faces shine like the Sun, may it begin; the peopling of the Face of the Earth; the populating of the Face of the Earth with the forming and the shaping of the Providers, Sustainer; Tzuqul, Kʼool” “May the molding, may the modeling begin; may the creating, the crafting commence of the Divine Daughters of the Dawn, the Sacred Sons of the Sun; Saqil Al, Saqil.” May this then be its origination; may this then be its generation; may this then be its creation; the origination, the generation, the creation of the People, Winaq; the Populating of Humanity, Winaqil here on the Face of the Earth.”

Divining the Essence Nawal Condition Nature; Substance; Flesh; People of Maize In council, as one, they gathered together in the Darkness of Night-Chi Qʼequmal; in the darkness before the Dawn-Chi Aqʼabʼal to bring to light the scattering of the seeds; the scattering of the beans to then form and shape the formation; the creation of their divination to find what was would be the essence of the substance used to form body by shaping the flesh of humanity. There in the darkness before the Dawn-Chi Aqʼabʼal they gathered together to divine the question they asked to be revealed through the forming and shaping of their divination as to what would be the nature of the substance that would be used as the native soul and natural spirit of human flesh. They searched for it now in their quest to bring forth those who would be their Providers; of those who would become their Sustainers that would take the form of the Human Formation; that would take the shape of the Human Creation here on the Face of the Earth. It was just a matter of scattering the golden seeds along with the corral red beans to then move their hands over their divinatory seeds; it was just by invoking while enchanting their divinatory beans that they would then be able to form the five seed hillocks to then shape the five bean mounds of their forming and shaping of the diving with which to order the sacred shape and divine count of their divination.

body:
This then was when they would see in order to find in order to known what it was that they were looking for there in the revelations found in dark silent quietude of Night; there in the dark darkness before the dawn their answer was found; there before the rising radiant rays of the revelatory light of Dawn that their answer was revealed to them in the calm white light that came to them out of the Dark Night.

There is where their quest ended when the answer was revealed to them in the bright dawning light of the rising Sun: Saqnatanoj; Saqnatanoj; the nostalgic remembrance of the bright shining light that sprang forth from the House of Dawn known as Saqnatanoj.

Thus they formed, thus they shaped their divination to know what would be the essence of the flesh with which to bring forth their creation of the Formed Beings-AjTzʼaq; of the Shaped Being-AjBʼit. It came to them in the Dark Darkness before the Dawn; it was revealed to them in the calm cool light of Dawn: Saqnatanoj.

The answer came to tell them what would be the substance-kʼojeʼik; what would be the character-kʼojeʼik, the condition-kʼojeʼik, the nature-kʼojeʼik, the essence-kʼojeʼik of the flesh- tyoʼjil that would be formed into the Formed People-AjTzʼaq Winaq; that would be shaped into the Shaped People-AjBʼit Winaq.

This was when they searched; this was when they sifted; when they sought it out as they thought it out by gathering together their divine minds seeking the revelation of their ancestral divination. What would they use as the substance to form the flesh of their forming; what would they use as essence of the flesh of their shaping?

body:
What was this essential substance that was also the sacred sustenance they searched for in their quest to find what they sought out for its nawal essence that would be used to form the flesh of their Providers; what then was the nawal nature of the sacred substance would be used to shape the sacred sustenance of their Sustainers there on the threshold of the dark of night and the light of day at the end of Night and the start of Day; there in the Dark before the Dawn with its first rays of light that struck down the Stars in the Night Sky as the piercing arrows of fierce bright light of the warrior Sun at the break of day with its luminous light and promise of warmth and nurturance to come.

What then was it there to found in the revelation that would surely be revealed in the light that now sprouted forth out of the dark shadows of Night and into the brilliant light of Dawn?

Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol Tzuqul, Kʼool Poqʼol, Kirol They sought to divine the essence of the substance by moving and mixing their divining beans and sacred seeds to find out what would be used to form and shape the flesh and blood; body and bones of the formed beings, shaped beings that would multiply and grow to people and populate the Face of the Earth.

These would be those that would be known as the Providers; those known as the Sustainers who would continue with the forming and the shaping as the Formers, Shapers; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol. These would be those who would continue providing; those who would continue sustaining as the Providers, as the Sustainers; Tzuqul, Kʼool who were and always would be the beloved descendants of the Former, Shaper; Bearer; Begetter; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom.

What then was the essence of the sacred substance that would bring the Sky-Earth to fruition by its being peopled and populated with the Formed Beings that were the Shaped Beings who would bear the burden of the Forming; of the Shaping that lead to the ʼProviding and Sustainingʼ of the ʼMultiplying and Growingʼ of all that existed on the Face of the Earth?

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Known in Maya Kʼicheʼ as: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Tzuqul, Kʼool; Poqʼol, Kirol all of which maintain the balance and harmony of the reciprocal relationships embodied in the natural movement of the Kaj-Ulew; Cho-Palo; Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj; Siwan-Pek; Chuch-Qajaw; Saqil Al-Saqil Kʼajol; Ixoqil, Achajil… This question of the essence of human flesh they planted there in the Dark-chi Qʼequmal before the Dawn-chi Aqʼabʼal when they gathered together in council to sow the seed of their divination so that their divination would reveal the answer of their divinatory revelation that would sprout forth to tell them what would be the essence of the sacred substance that would be used as the flesh to form and to shape the formed beings and the shaped being to be formed and shaped by the Former, the Shaper: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol.

This was when they hunted it for it as they stewed upon it; when they turned it over and over in order to chew upon it.

This was when they thought upon it in contemplation; when they pondered it in meditation to reflect upon their imagination that revealed just what it was and just where to find it. Just like that, in an instant, ancestral insight came to them; a lucid revelation of the answer to their question appeared to them; the end of their quest came as the substance was revealed to them as to what would be the essence of the flesh that showed itself to them in a flash; now it was only a matter to find where its keepers where keeping it in order to enter the place where its guardians were protecting it by hiding it. Once they found it they would then pick it up to then carry it away. Then it was just a matter of shelling it; to then clean it before they cooked it in ash or lime; to then rinse and wash it as soft nixtamal when they then could grind it; to then form it; to then shape it.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
First Four Fathers Formed Beings; Shaped Beings Molded Ones; Modeled Ones The revelation was now shown to them as it shined its light on them as daybreak broke on the Sky-Earth to open the door of the House of Dawn so the Sun could come out to shine up and over the World where everyone now watched and waited to hear the answer to the question of the quest asked of their divination that came together in council to contemplate and consider; to ponder and wonder through the silent stillness of dark and the calm quiet of the dawn while divining their question with the inner light of their ancestral might.

It came to them, crystal clear, shining bright; it came to them, out of the darkness into the light; it came to them, at first vague, in fact blurred, but now fully within sight; it came to them, out of the shadows and into the light; it came to them, a definitive knowing of ancestral insight; it came to them, out of the dawn in this long dark night.

The answer was revealed to them; it came to them, they now knew where they could find the sacred substance to be used as the essence of the flesh of the formed beings; the flesh of the shaped beings that were soon to be brought forth out of the imagination and into existence.

They now knew where they would find the little skull-like, teeth-like seeds that would provide them with the divine substance that would soon become the firm flesh to the First Four Men made of molded and modeled maize. Formed Beings that were Shaped Beings whoʼs flesh and bones that would be formed and shaped from the golden yellow grains and pearl white kernels of the sacred sustenance that would be found where they were safely hidden away. These yellow grains and white kernels would be the perfect substance with the ideal essence to be used as the flesh of those formed beings, those shaped beings that would soon be formed and shaped; molded and modeled into the first four maize beings to people; to populate the Face of the Earth: Uwach Ulew.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They knew what it was; and, now, they knew where to find it. For the sacred place where they would find what they needed was revealed to them through the insights and answers that their divination provided them as it guided them in the right direction; divination that came from the One that confide in them what needed to be supplied them in the form of ancestral intuition required to bring their work to fruition.

For now they knew just how to bring their divine burden to completion through their divine connection with the One that now guided and protected them in their forming of the Formed Beings; in their shaping of the Shaped Beings.

This then is the telling of the Ancient Ancestral Account of those known and named Ixim Winaq: Maize People; the People of Maize formed and shaped from golden yellow mazorcas-qʼanajal and silver white mazorcas of maize-saqijal; known together as emanations of the Day; of the Night that were expressions of the Sun; of the Moon: Qʼanajal, Saqijal. There was just a little bit longer to go before the appearance of the Sun, the Moon, the Star and their passage overhead of the Former, the Shaper.

Pan Paxil; Pan Kayalaʼ are their names: Split-Mountain-Pan Paxil-Cleft- Mountain; Bitter Water Place-Pan Kayalaʼ-Sour Water Place as they are known to all as the Mountains of Sustenance that were spoken of as Jun Juyubʼ Wa: One Mountain of Sustenance.

From here came the Yellow Heads of Maize-Qʼana Jal: from here came the White Head of Maize-Saqi Jal: Qʼana Jal-Yellow Maize, White Maize-Saqi Jal. This is it; this is the Sacred Sustenance of the Maize People: Qʼana Jal-Saqi Jal Yellow Mazorca; White Mazorca; Golden Maize, Silver Maize the true wealth of the Maize People: Ixim Winaq.

These are the ancestral names of the sacred substance used as the essence of the flesh; the very substance, the very essence that would become the body and bones; teeth and eyes that were formed and shaped from this sacred substance that was the sacred sustenance of the Maize People.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
But it was not so very easy to find this treasure of the Qʼana Jal-Saqi Jal; Golden Maize, Silver Maize; where was it hidden in the Maize Mountains of Pan Paxil; Pan Kayalaʼ known as Split Mountain Place; Bitter Water Place; both of them Sustenance Mountains; both of them Mountains of Maize.

Here they are; here are the names of the Animal Companions of Sustenance- Chikop Waʼ these are those known as the Animal Guides, the Pathfinders of Sustenance-Kʼamol Rechaʼ:

Yak- Grey Fox but known as a ʼGato de Monte-Mountain Catʼ: Yak love to eat maize; just as they love eating all those that love eating maize. Utiw: Coyote eats as much sweet and mature maize as she-he can get his-her sharp clawed paws on; all ʼCanines-Tzʼiʼ love maize as well as eating all those that eat maize in the dark shadows of long tropical nights. Kʼel: Parakeets fly in flocks; flocks that fly in search of milpas fruiting with elotes-qʼanil to eat everywhere they flock to feed on maize everywhere they flock.

Joj-Crow smartest of them all; these are those who always feast on any and all unattended cornfields or milpa either up in the Highlands or down in the Lowlands they feast on maize everywhere the fly.

These then are the four animal guides that brought word of the maize; the four animals that brought forth the knowledge of what it was and the knowing of where to find that which was known, that which was named the Yellow Ears of Golden Maize; White Ears of Silver Maize: Qʼana Jal, Saqi Jal. These animals, they came from Pan Paxil and so it was they showed the way to Pan Paxil: Split Mountain Place; Broke-back Mountain Place; Cleft Mountain Place.

Qʼana Jal; Saqi Jal. Pan Paxil; Pan Kayala Pan Paxil was explained to me by an elderly Kʼicheʼ Maya Day-Keeper-AjQʼij as mountain of treasure that is like a ʼpiñataʼ that as a Juyubʼ Wa; Sustenance Mountain that had to be ʼbroken-openʼ from inside where the maize pours down from up above inside this split mountain that is a cleft mountain.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The maize is said to have been stored up above inside the mountain like the rafters of a Great Mountain House so that the maize is made to flow down from up inside of this Broken- open, Split-open Mountain of Maize that is a Cleft-Mountain of Sustenance; that is a Broke-back Mountain of wealth and riches.

Pan Paxil then is a true Sustenance Mountain-Juyubʼ Wa-Tonacatepetl where the sacred essence of the Maize Beings falls down from above ʼas ifʼ falling down from a treasure chest up inside this Broken Open-Paxil-Split Open Place that is seen as a Ancestral Mountain Palace spilling-down with a great bounty of wealth and prosperity; overflowing with a great harvest of profuse plenty; bursting forth with a bountiful abundance of source and supply; riches and resource: Pan Paxil.

It was there that they found their sustenance; from this great abundance of sustenance came the flesh of the Formed People; the Shaped People. Areʼ kʼut xok utyoʼjil Winaq Tzʼaq, Winaq Bʼit.

Water then was their blood; the blood of humans came from it.

Jaʼ kʼut ukikʼel; ukikʼel Winaq xuxik.

This is how the Heads of Maize-Jal-Mazorca were used by Alom, Kʼajolom; Bearer, Begetter; Conceiver, Engenderer This is how they-Alom, Kʼajolom-made use of the mature heads of maize; la mazorca; ri jal as it is known. Are xok kumal Alom, Kʼajolom ri jal.

Alom, Kʼajolom; those of Sprouts-Al; those of the Descendants-Al; those of Skull-Jolom those of Replacements-Kʼexel; those of Sprouts-Al; those of Twin Skulls-Kʼajolom as these are known as Alom, Kʼajolom; Bearer; Begetter of Kʼexel-Replacement; Conceiver-Alom, Engenderer-Kʼajolom of Descendants-Kʼexel-Exchange-Change-Replacement-Jaloj-Kʼexoj Change within Change on the Outside on the Husk-Jaloj; on the Inside within the Husk-Kʼexoj. Ijaʼl: Descendant-Descendent of a Class, Generation, or Race to be known. Ijaʼ: Seed-Ijatzʼ, Wi- Head; Kernel-Naq; Winaq-Person-Twenty Being; Descendant-Eey-Tooth; Awex-Maize; Abʼix- Milpa; Ijatz-Seed to be sown-Ijaʼ; the Seed Sown; the Kernel Grown; the Sprout-Al; the Descendant-Al-Eey; the Tooth-Eey; the Skull-Jolom; the Replacement-Kʼexel nothing more needs be known.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
So then they were made content for they were made happy; pleased upon finding such a beautiful mountain-utzilaj juyubʼ with such abundant stores of sweet-kus, full-bodied kinds of thick-tzatz Heads of Maize: Yellow Maize, White Maize; Qʼana Jal, Saqi Jal.

This plentiful place was thick-tzatz with Small Pods of Cacao; Peq and Large Pods of Cacao; Kako.

Immeasurable loads of sweet fruit were found there inside Sustenance Mountain: Peq: Small Pods of Common Cacao-Pataxte Peq Kako: Large Pods of Superior Cacao-Kakawa: Kakaw or Kokowf Immense amounts of Sweet Fruit-Kʼilaj Echaʼ was hidden away their inside those Sweet Mountains of Sustenance:

Tulul: Zapote Kʼawex: Guanabana-Anona Qʼinoom: Jocote Tapaʼl: Nance Ajacheʼ: Sour-sop Kabʼ: Honey.

All this sweet sustenance-kʼi laj echaʼ-was found there inside the Citadel- Tinamit-by the name of Pan Paxil, Pan Kayalaʼ known as: Split-Mountain Place, Biter-Water Place.

It was just completely filled with tasty greens that were growing there in plenty; truly there were many classes of edible herbs that grew in these Mountains of Sustenance that were truly Sustenance Mountains; for it was true that every variety of edible herb was found there growing in great plenty:

Chʼuti echaʼ: Plantations of Small Greens were growing there thick with edible greens Nima echaʼ: Plantations of Large Greens were growing there thick with edible greens Chʼuti tikoʼn-Small beds of planted vegetables were growing there thick with produce Nima tikoʼn-Large beds of planted vegetables were growing there thick with produce The way to this place of plenty was shown by the Animals-Chikop; it was just the Animals-Chikop that led the way to where great abundance lay inside these mountains of plenty; the animals opened the path as they opened the way to where great loads of sustenance were found there thick and sweet to be gathered up as a great bounty.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
For truly these were Benevolent Bountiful Mountains-Utzilaj Juyubʼ that would bring prosperity to the Ixim Winaq for all that was found there to be gathered up and carried away as the burden of those who were guided there in their quest to find the substance with which to form the flesh of the men that would soon be made from the essence of this most sacred sustenance: Qʼanajal; Saqijal. This then was when it was ground down; when the Yellow Maize, the White Maize were ground down; nine times was the maize ground down; nine then were the grindings that were made by IxMuqane when she ground down the Yellow Maize, the White Maize on her grinding stone; when the maize was ground down nine times by Grandmother IxMuqane. IxMuqane Qatiʼt Ixim Winaq Kamul Iyom; Kamul Mamom Nabʼe Qatiʼt-Qamam Nabʼe Chuch-Qajaw IxMuqane as you known so very well is the principal mythic figure who acts as the narrative link between all the evolutionary ages of this Sacred History of the Ixim Winaq for these are her people; this is her pueblo who is brought forth into existence by her as the Great Grandmother-Kamul Iyom who is Twice a Mid-Wife-Kamul Iyom that is to say Twice a Matriarch-Kamul Iyom.

IxMuqane was been with us all along the way as the Great Mother-Great Grandmother who acts and speaks as the Great Matriarch-Great Mid-Wife of this Sacred History. She has been with us since the opening page that has been sown to be grown as the Ancestral Account-Ojer Tzij that begins with the ʼnaming of the namesʼ as the invocation of the Ancient Ancestors- Ojeroq Winaq and Kabʼawil on the very first page. This was and is the seeding and sowing of the First Mother-Fathers; Nabʼe Chuch-Qajaw; Our First Grandmother-Grandfathers-Nabʼe Qatiʼt- Qamam of the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo. And now we have arrived at that Mid-most Place when these Sacred Seeds of Sustenance will be ground down upon the grinding stone of IxMuqane. Once ground down these sacred seeds of sacred sustenance will be used as the sacred substance embodied essence of the ancestral flesh of the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Lineages of the Four Directions of the Kʼicheʼ Cosmos with their Four Corners, Four Sides.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Those Kʼicheʼ Lineages known as the Great Houses will begin with the Forming, the Shaping of the First Four Fathers who will be formed; who will be shaped in the molding and modeling hands and imagination of the Former, the Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol: IxMuqane, Xpiyakok. Only Xpiyakok is the skull-shaped seed of skull-shaped heads of the skull-shaped teeth that will become the ʼdescendant-teethʼ of their Divine Ancestors: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom: IxMuqane, Xpiyakok.

Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Former, Shaper are those whose creative crafty hands are the divine hands of IxMuqane: Mid-Wife of the Ixim Winaq. Molder, Modeler; Crafter, Creator of the Formed Beings, Shaped Beings of Maize known as the First Four Fathers of Kʼicheʼ Maya Lineages of the Ixim Winaq: Bʼalam Kʼitzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam and their women, their wives Kaqa Palama, Chomi Ja, Tzʼununi Ja, Kaqixa Ja. These First Four Mother- Fathers spoken of as Chuch-Qajaw will people and populate the Four-fold Cornering, Four-Fold Siding of the Face of the Earth.

This then was when she ground the Yellow Maize, the White Maize nine times; nine then were its grindings; nine times did IxMuqane grind the Yellow Maize and White Maize when IxMuqane ground the maize to form and shape the First Four Men.

Ta xkeʼx kʼut ri Qʼana Jal, Saqi Jal. Bʼelejebʼ kʼu ukaʼl xubʼan Ixmuqane.

Nine grindings of maize were the nine times that Grandmother IxMuqane ground her maize when she ground down the Yellow Maize, the White Maize on her grinding stone-uka; when IxMuqane ground her maize nine times with her nine grindings on her grinding stone: bʼelejebʼ kʼu ukaʼl.

Ta xkeʼx kʼut ri Qʼanajal, Saqijal; bʼelejebʼ kʼu ukaʼl xubʼan IxMuqane.

For it was IxMuqane who made nine grindings-bʼelejebʼ ukaʼl on her grinding stone-uka-when the Old Woman; Grandmother ground down the Yellow Maize, White Maize nine times on her grinding stone.

This was when the Yellow Maize of the Sun and the White Maize of the Moon were ground down nine times on the grinding stone of IxMuqane when the Old Woman made nine grindings of the yellow and white maize.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Ground maize was the substance used along with the water of ʼnixtamalʼ to bring forth the strength of their strong supple bodies as well as the stretch; the strength of their flexible arms and legs that were set aglow with the radiant warmth of their golden complexion.

Echaʼ xokik, rukʼ Jaʼ ropenal xwinaqir uqʼabʼcheʼal, uqʼanal winaq xuxik.

This is when it was done by those named:

Alom, Kʼajolom-Bearer, Begetter Tepew Qʼukumatz-Sovereign Plumed Serpent;

Majesty Quetzalcoatl; Precious Twin as they were known.

This then was when Our First Mother-Fathers-Nabʼe Chuch-Qajaw were brought to life; when they were said to have entered the word; when they say they entered the way; entered the word: xkikojo patzij when they were placed in the word; placed on their way; when they were placed in the truth; placed in the tradition of the Ixim Winaq.

This was when they were made to come to life; those who were Our First Mother Fathers; Nabʼe Chuch-Qajaw when they say the became the word; when they say they became the way; when it is said the became the truth; when it is said they became the tradition of being and becoming Ixim Winaq; those who were formed; those who were shaped from their sacred sustenance Saqijal; Qʼanajal.

Saqijal; Qʼanajal; this is what was used for its being formed-utzʼaqik; for its being shaped-ubʼitik at the time of its forming; at the time of its shaping; the forming; the shaping of Our First Mother, Our First Father; our First Mother- Father: utzʼaqik, ubʼitik QaNabʼe Chuch-Qajaw.

This was when Our First Mother-Father; QaNabʼe Chuch-Qajaw ʼentered the wordʼ as it is said; when they entered the truth as they say; when they entered the tradition as it is said; when they were brought to life as they say through the ancestral word and its ancestral way of the ancestral truth of the ancestral tradition; known as Ojer Tzij: the Ancient Word; the Ancient Way; the Ancestral Truth; the Ancestral Tradition.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is what they say; just as this is what was said when they were placed; when they were put in their Ancestral Place when they entered the Way; when they entered the Word to be placed in the Truth; to be placed in the Tradition. This is what they said; this is what they say of the word and its way; of the Truth and its Tradition of Our First Mother-Fathers; QaNabʼe Chuch-Qajaw.

Kʼate kʼut xkikojo pa tzij utzʼaqik, ubʼitik QaNabʼe Chuch-Qajaw.

This is the Way of the Word just as it is the Word of the Way that tells of the Truth just as it tells of the Tradition of Our First Four Mother-Fathers who were brought to life in the Word that is the Way that is the Truth that is the Tradition of those who are the Ixim Winaq.

These were those who were formed; these were those who were shaped from Sacred Sustenance that was used as the essence of the sacred substance from which was formed the flesh of the Ixim Winaq: Saqijal, Qʼanajal.

Just Yellow Corn; just White Corn were its essence; just Yellow Maize, just White Maize were its flesh: Xa Qʼana Jal; Xa Saqi Jal utyoʼjil. Just sustenance alone was used to form the legs and shape the arms of the maize beings. Xa echaʼ raqan, uqʼabʼ winaq.

Here then, are our First Fathers-QaNabʼe Qajaw. There were four of them who were formed into beings of maize; e kajibʼ chi winaq tzʼaq; four of them formed into human beings who were men.

It was they who were formed; it was they who were shaped from sustenance alone; just sustenance alone was used to form; to shape their body. It was sustenance alone that ʼentered inʼ as their flesh; the flesh of the First Four Fathers of Maize was just sustenance-echaʼ. For it was just sustenance alone that entered in as their flesh; the flesh of the Maize People was just sustenance- echaʼ. Xa echaʼ okinaq kityoʼjil.

The First People were formed and shaped this way by IxMuqane who put in; who placed in ground maize as the essence of sustenance that became the substance that she ʼusedʼ as the flesh of the Formed Beings, the Shaped Beings.

Here are the names of the First People; Nabʼe Winaq who were formed; who were shaped with the ground maize. Waʼe kibʼi Nabʼe Winaq xetzʼaqik, xebʼitik.

body:
These are the First Being; Are Nabʼe Winaq. Here are the names of the First Maize Beings who were formed; who were shaped from maize; these then are their names:

First Noble Person; Nabʼe Winaq; First Ancestor who was named as a Jaguar Lord of the Mountain who was known as a Jaguar Ruler of the Mountain;

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ is the name of the Noble Lord Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ known as Jaguar Sweet Smile; Jaguar Sweet Laughter; Jaguar Lord of Great Contentment; Jaguar Lord of Great Laughter.

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ is of the East there in the place known as Relebʼal Qʼij; the Coming Out Place of the Sun; Red is his color.

He, Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ Sweet Laughter; Laughing Jaguar; Smiling Jaguar has a great big smile with great big teeth; there are images of him that were formed and shaped using molds of clay to model and mold his distinctive face with a great big smile and full set of great big teeth like Tojil who is his Divinity-Kabʼawil and perhaps this is why they should look so similar for they are happy and content their before the Rising Sun where they meet to greet the Sun and Dawn.

The Second Jaguar Lord and Noble Ruler is the Second Lord known as Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ Lord Jaguar Night, Lord Jaguar Dark Night: Ukabʼ Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ. The second of the First Four Fathers of Kʼicheʼ Winaq then is Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ; Jaguar Night is of the North; White is his color just as Death is his domain.

The Third Jaguar Lord then is Majukʼutaj: No One Is Here, Invisible One; Just Nobody Here; Majukʼutaj is of the West; the Third of the First Four Noble Lords is known as Majukʼutaj which is to say ʼNobody is Hereʼ or the ʼInvisible Oneʼ as in the Black Jaguar of the West, the direction of Black-Blue Darkness of Night. Falling Down Place of the Sun-Qajbʼal Qʼij as is known his Western Realm; this is the Western Place of the Invisible One; the Third Lord is the Invisible One: Rox Majukʼutaj.

body:
Majukʼutaj is the Black Jaguar that cannot be seen at night which makes him invisible like Lord Tezcatlipoca who we might best think these rulers are aspects of since Tezcatlipoca was the titular guide and protector of Noble Rulers and known as Tepeyollotl or Heart of the Mountain and was seen as the Night Sun emblematic of Majukʼutaj.

The fourth then is Ikʼi Bʼalam from the South where there is abundance in all shapes and forms; kinds and classes; and so too with Ikʼi Bʼalam as in the Many Jaguar, or maybe it could be Iqʼi Bʼalam as in the Wind Jaguar; Ikʼi Bʼalam or Moon Jaguar; Eqʼ Bʼalam or Black Jaguar but more than likely it is Many Jaguar as in Ikʼi Bʼalam which is a well known expression denoting a great Many Jaguar.

Bʼalam KiʼTzeʼ; Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ; Majukutaj; Ikʼi Bʼalam This Ikʼi Bʼalam reminds us of the House of Jaguars for it were Jaguar Moon-Bʼalam Ikʼ or Jaguar Wind-Bʼalam Iqʼ then the name would be Bʼalam Ikʼ as in Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ or Bʼalam KiʼTzeʼ yet the Kʼicheʼ Maya Scribes write Ikʼi Bʼalam-Many Jaguar that seems to signify the Great Many Jaguar of the abundant South Coastal Plain of la Costa Sur del Pacífico; land of golden yellow and Dry Tropical Forest where all the Trees and Vines flower and fruit forth in great abundance. Yet, many translators prefer Ikʼi Bʼalam or Moon Jaguar while many more prefer Eqʼ Bʼalam or Black Jaguar of the Merchant Canoe that paddle the Pacific Littoral looking for opportunity all along the Costa Sur.

And this is why I read Ikʼi Bʼalam as Many Jaguar because there were so many jaguars living on this wide open Pacific Coastal Plain known to this day as a place of great abundance and supernatural plenty. Yet, many translators prefer Ikʼi Bʼalam or Moon Jaguar while many more prefer Eqʼ Bʼalam or Black Jaguar of the Merchant Canoe that paddle the Pacific Littoral looking for opportunity all along the Costa Sur.

body:
And this is why I read Ikʼi Bʼalam as Many Jaguar because there were so many jaguars living on this wide open Pacific Coastal Plain known to this day as a place of great abundance and supernatural plenty. These are the names of Our First Mother-Fathers-QaNabʼe Chuch-Qajaw as they are named, as they are known when they are invoked; when they are enchanted; when they are summonsed by Prayer-makers and Day-keepers.

“Just Formed; Just Shaped,” as they say.

“Xa Tzʼaq; Xa Bʼit,” keʼuchaʼxik.

These First Fathers had no Mother, they had no Father; their Mothers remain unnamed, their Fathers remain unnamed as well, because they came into existence without a Mother; without a Father for they were: ʼJust Formed; Just Shaped; Xa Tzʼaq; Xa Bʼit.” We shall only speak of the men; we shall only tell of the men. No woman gave them birth; no man engendered these First Four Men: First Formed Men, First Shaped Men; Nabʼe AjTzʼaq, Nabʼe AjBʼit. No woman bore them in their womb; no man engendered them with their seed, with their spittle; for it was just the doing of those named:

Ri AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit: Former; Shaper Ri Alom Kʼajolom: Mother, Father These are those who are the Former, Shaper; Mother, Father who formed and shaped the First Four Fathers from maize; from ground maize they were formed; from ground maize they were shaped by Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Former, Shaper known as AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit; She of the Forming; He of the Shaping spoken of as Alom, Kʼajolom; Bearer, Begetter; Mother, Father. Xa Pus; Xa Nawal:

Xa Pus: Just Sacrifice; Just Surrender to Ritual Death Xa Nawal: Just Magical Transformation; Just Ancestral Transformation Xa Pus; Xa Nawal: This was what brought forth these First Four Fathers Xa Pus; Xa Nawal: This is what brought the First Four Men into the World of the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew.

It was just their ritual performance of sacrifice-xa pus; it was just their ancestral practice of sacrifice-xa pus;

It was just their ancestral powers of transformative magic-xa nawal;

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is that which brought forth the First Four Fathers who would come to people and populate the Face of the Earth. This is what molded them; this is was what modeled them; kitzʼaqik, kibʼitik; when they were formed, when they were shaped by those known and named as: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom; Tepew Qʼukumatz.

This was when creation gave fruit when humans came into being: xeʼuxik.

They talked together and they spoke to one another too: xechʼawik

They looked out and could see well, their vision was good: xemukunik

They listened and so they heard well, their hearing was good: xetaʼon.

They heard all there was to hear; they could hear all that was heard: xetaʼon.

They walked well so they walked wherever they wished, they wanted to walk; they walked in rites of passage; the walked in rituals too: xebʼinik.

They grasped everything they touched; they understood all they picked-up; their grip was strong so they held tight to all they caught: xechapanik

They were truly fine humans, truly handsome were they; their mannish faces gave them their masculine good-looks which provided them with their strong strapping manly appearance: e utzilaj winaq, e chaʼom

They could take a deep breath and so it was that they could breathe; their breathing came forth as inspiration for truly they could breathe: kʼo kʼuxlabʼ

They were filled with ancestral heart for they were ancient, old beings formed from nawal spirit; shaped from nawal soul so they came to celebrate council with care and concern to contemplate the Sky-Earth through the thought of the heart, in the seat of the soul; and so it was that these First Four Fathers were Ancient Ones filled with heart and soul: kʼo kʼuxlabʼ

These men, they looked out on and upon the world and straightaway their vision extended as far as their sight could see which was a far as their sight reached: kemukunik.

Their sight reached as far as their eyes could see to contemplate everything that was there to be seen with their vision that saw everything: kemukunik.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Seeing everything gave them a complete understanding of all that existed beneath the Sky as they contemplated all there was to see upon the Earth and all there was to be seen in the vast vault of the Sky; for nothing escaped their vision; their vision that reached easily across the expanse of the Sky; just as it moved with ease across the Face of the Earth: Kemukunik

When they looked, then immediately they saw everything that was there to be seen in order to reflect upon and know all that was there to be seen in the vast vault of the Sky and upon the flat plane of the Earth.

Nothing cut-off their vision; nothing got in the way of their sight; nothing, nothing at all. At first they didnʼt have to walk to see what there was below the Sky, they could just look out from wherever they were to see all there was to see.

Excellent was their vision; perfect was their understanding; vast was their all-knowing sight as it moved over everything there was to see and understood. And so it was that they soon became those who were thick with genius understanding as their knowledgeable sight and insightful knowing penetrated all that surrounded them to see and thus know the world in which they lived.

For truly their sight saw everything there was to see in order to known everything there was to know: Pa Cheʼ: Among the Trees, in the Forest Pa Abʼaj: Among the Stones, in the Rocks Pa Cho: Upon the Lake, in the Water Pa Palo: Upon the Sea, in the Ocean Pa Juyubʼ: Upon the Mountains; in the Wilderness Pa Taqʼaj: Upon the Plains, in the Valleys, on the Savannas

Truly, they were most Sacred People-Loqʼolaj Winaq-Holy People is who they were for truly it was they who were known as a most Beloved People; Noble Men; Gracious Men; Dignified and Genuine were they who would be known as Jaguar Lords of the Four Cardinal Directions and their Mountain-Plain-Juyub-Taqʼaj; Lake-Sea-Cho-Palo.

Noble Rulers is who they were that were guided by ancestral power and authority. Theirs was the power and authority of Noble Lords that was their destiny and its burden to bring to fruition.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
For it was just theirs in life to govern and rule the people of the pueblo they were formed and shaped to guide and protect; defend and direct as Holy Lords who were there to show their people to well-being and prosperity by providing and sustaining their Kabʼawil with sacrificial gifts of sacred sustenance given through ritual sacrifice.

This was their destiny in life that they now were called to bring to perfection by perfecting their ancestral ways and words that would bring their lineage to flowering fruition by entering the truth; by entering the tradition to bring their lives there in and upon the Sky-Earth to its greatest flowering and fruiting fulfillment.

These then are their Noble Names:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ: Jaguar Sweet Laughter; Jaguar Sweet Smiles Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ: Jaguar Night, Dark Jaguar of Night, Night Jaguar Majukʼutaj: Invisible One, Nobody Is Here, Black Panther Ikʼi Bʼalam: Many Jaguars, Moon Jaguar, Wind Jaguar

All four of these Noble Jaguar Lord were there together; and, this then was when they were questioned by their Formers, their Shapers-AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit:

“What do you feel about your existence?”

“Juchaʼlik kikʼojeʼik kinaʼo?” “What do you have to say about the condition of your life?” “Can you not see?”

“Can you not hear?”

“Is it not good the way you speak, the language that you use?”

“Is it not excellent the way you can walk all about?”

“Look then at all you can see; all you perceive beneath the Sky; can you not see clearly the Mountain-Plain that stands before you?”

“Try it now then!” they were told. So this then was when they saw all there was to see beneath the Sky. And so then they gave thanks to Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Former, Shaper:

“Truly then we give you thanks two times, we give you thanks twice; we just give you thanks three times, we give you thanks thrice; we give you thanks for your forming and shaping of us; for our being molded and modeled by you: Thank You. Thank You. Thank You.”

“Thanks to you we have been given our mouths and our faces so that we might speak-kojchʼawik; so that we might hear-kojtaʼonik; so that we might be able to contemplate-kojbʼisonik; so that we may move about-kojsilabʼik.”

body:
“Truly we feel quite well-Utz kaqanaʼo; truly we feel quite content to have come to know all that which is to be known both far and near.” Utz kaqanaʼo xqetamaj naj, naqaj. “Just as we have seen what is big and what is small in the Sky and on the Earth.”

“Mi pu xqilo nim, chʼutiʼn upa Kaj, upa Ulew.” “Thanks then to you weʼve been created by you, Our Formers, Our Shapers.

“Thanks to you weʼve just been created: We the Shaped Ones; We the Formed Ones.” “Kʼamo kʼut chi, mixojwinaqirik: Oj Tzʼaq, Oj Bʼit!” We the Formed Ones: Oj Tzʼaq! We the Shaped Ones: Oj Bʼit!

You who have just brought us forth into being. Mixojuxik. You Our Grandmother: At QaTiʼt! You Our Grandfather: At QaMam!” they said. And so it was that they gave thanks for their being formed; for their being shaped by the Former; by the Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol who formed them as the Formed Ones; who shaped them as Shaped Ones; AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit.

These are the Formed Beings they were; these are the Shaped Beings they came to be. And who they became were all-knowing beings that ended up knowing all; all-knowing beings that ended up understanding everything.

This is who these all seeing; all knowing beings were. They were those who understood everything they saw and knew.

And, because they ended up seeing everything, they ended up knowing everything; and because they ended up knowing everything they ended up understanding everything they saw and knew.

They saw the Four Corners-Xkimukuj Kaj Tzʼuq.

They saw the Four Sides-Xkimukuj Kaj Xukut;

The Womb of the Sky-Upam Kaj; the Center, the Middle of the Sky The Womb of the Earth-Upam Ulew; the Center, the Middle of the Earth

But this did NOT sound good to AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit: Former, Shaper; Molder, Modeler who said:

“It is just no good what it is that they say; Those who are known as Our Former-QaTzʼaq;

Those who are known as Our Shaper-QaBʼit;

Those who are known as Our Molder-QaTzʼaq; Those who are known as Our Modeler-QaBʼit; For is it not they who have said to us: ʼWe just understand everything; Big and Small.ʼ

This is what they said, when they said: “Mixqetamaj ronojel Nim, Chʼutiʼn!”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Then they came together to celebrate council with one another to gather their thoughts; these were those known as Alom, Kʼajolom:

“Now what shall we do with them? What must we do so that their sight only reaches near, so that they only see what they should see, so that they see just a little of all that there is to see on the Face of the Earth?”

“It is truly not good what they say they see. Are they not just Formed Beings; are they not just Shaped Beings, is that not how they are named: just Formed Beings, just Shaped Beings: xa Tzʼaq, xa Bʼit, kibʼiʼ?”

“This is just a sign that they will soon become Deities like us; Kabʼawil chik. Truly, this is just a sign of sorts; an omen that indicates how they will soon become Kabʼawil, Divinities like us is what they will become. This is what will happen to them next- xa labʼe e Kabʼawil keʼuxi chik! And they havenʼt even multiplied and grown very much yet.”

“Ta Chawaxoq! ¡Ta Saqiroq! To the Sowing! To the Dawning!”

“Yes, yes, let us be done with it now; now that they havenʼt grown to be so very many.” “So be it! ¡Ta Chuxoq! ¡Qué así sea!” “Let us just undo our work a bit, nothing more; this is what we must do. Because it is just no good what we know now; now that we know what we know about them. They will just become the same as us, doing as we do since their knowing; their understanding reaches so far; since their vision sees everything there is to see,” said those known as:

Ukʼuʼx Kaj: Heart of the Sky Jun Raqan: One-Footed Hurricane Rain Chʼipi Kaqulja: Misty-Rain Thunder-Lightning Raxa Kaqulja: Resplendent Green Thunder-Lightening Tepew Qʼukumatz-Sovereign Plumed Serpent Alom: Mother of Descendants Kʼajolom: Father of Descendants Xpiyakok: Grandfather of the Maize People IxMuqane: Grandmother of the Maize People Tzʼaqol: Former-Molder-Maker Bʼitol: Shaper-Modeler-Creator as they are called; keʼuchaʼxik This is when they transformed its nature-ukʼojeʼik-its character of their creation; this was when they changed the essence of their formation, known as their Forming; their Shaping: KiTzʼaq; KiBʼit.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Their eyes were just misted over by the Heart of the Sky: Ukʼuʼx Kaj. Their vision was just made misty like breathe on a mirror, their eyes were just veiled, their vision just a blur compared to what it was before. They could only see what was near; their vision was clear just as long as they looked at what was close; at what was near.

Xa kʼu xwabʼax ubʼaq kiwach rumal ri Ukʼuʼx Kaj. Xmoyik kʼeje ri xuxlabʼix uwach lemo, xmoyomobʼik ubʼaq kiwach. Xa naqaj chik xemukun wi.

This is how they lost their knowledge as well as their understanding. It was just lost, the insight and genius that had been gained by the First Four Fathers: the First Four Beings: Kajibʼ chi Winaq. All of it was just forgotten; their wise knowing-ketamabʼal and intelligent feeling-kinaʼobʼal; their clever gift of wisdom; their ingenious sense of intelligence was gone; puuh-puuj it was just misted over!

This then is just the root, just the beginning, just the origin of the sowing, the seeding of the original creation of the First Grandfather, First Father: Nabʼe QaMam, Nabʼe QaQajaw.

This then is the beginning; just the origin of their being formed, their being shaped: Our First Grandfather, Our First Father-Nabʼe QaMam, Nabʼe QaQajaw by the Heart of the Sky; by the Heart of the Earth-Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew.

And then there were their companions-kikʼulel-their partners; who were the first women-kixoqil who would become their wives-kixoqil-their wives-kixoqil who were their women-kixoqil.

It was just a Kabʼawil that thought them up so; it was just a Deity that imagined them so; it was just a Divinity that dreamed them up so-Kabʼawil xnaʼojin chik.

It was just a Divinity that imagined how they would come into being. It was a Deity that was a Kabʼawil who dreamed them up in his sleep; he who was and is known as Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj.

It was the Kabʼawil known as Ukʼuʼx Kaj who brought forth the Women who were the Companions of the First Four Men; he brought them into being out of his sleep.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Out of Sleep into the Dream These First Women are known as Kaqa Palama-Red Sea-Turtle; Chomi Ja-Shrimp House-Prawn House; Tzʼununi Ja-Hummingbird House; Kaqixa Ja-Scarlet Red Macaw House. These Divine Ancestors will be brought to life through the Dreaming of the Ancestral Dream in a world where dreaming will be of vast importance when its mythic images and soul experience will bring forth knowledge and insight from the Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Earth; Heart of the Lake; Heart of the Sea. Dreams are experienced by the Maya as the Ancestral Soul moving through the Sky-Earth in order to make contact with the Divine Ancestors who will take on Nawal Forms; Nawal Shapes to Guide and Protect the Great Houses-Nima Ja of the Kʼicheʼ Lineages.

The First Four Women will not come from material reality that is physical reality; the First Four Women will come from the Ancestral Soul through its Ancestral Imagination that Dreams the Ancestral Dream in what is known as ʼdreaming the dream onʼ through the Nawal expression, revelation, and manifestation of these Divine Ancestors as Nawal Women who form and shape the Nima Ja known as the Great House that are experienced by the Wondering Soul of the Dream World as the Imaginal Realm of the Nawales where Dream and Myth reflect one-an- other as words echo images and images reflect words. This is the Way of Dreams Forming and Shaping of the Ancestral Soul as the Popol Wuj tells us here.

These First Four Mothers will be formed and shaped through the highest aesthetic potential that bring forth the beauty of these beautiful and powerful women that come into being through the ancestral soulʼs capacity to bring forth the ancestral imagination whose strength and beauty is to bring forth dream images out of the imaginal realm and into material reality.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is that story of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Lineages of Divine Women and Divine Men that will begin now and continue on to this day were dreaming is an ancestral path to finding lost aspects of ancestral memory, forgotten knowledge and extinguished wisdom that is sought to solve unsolvable problem and find solutions to impossible situations. Dreams are the path to finding all that was lost and destroyed through the many years of wanting to forget what is now desirous to remember. The Descendants of the Divine Ancestors must communicate with their Formers of the Future Fortunes and Shapers of Destiny through prayers of gratitude and petitionary pleas in order to ask for what is needed from the Divine Ancestors and Kabʼawil who will manifest themselves through signs given in nature and ways shown on paths revealed in Nawal Dreams. Dreams are what will reveal just what is needed to be known to do just what is needed to be done when the time comes to do what needs to be done to bring the destiny of life to fruition for those who live walking in the footprints of their Divine Ancestors who formed and shaped the way of their Descendants by their walking across the Face of the Earth on the Sacred Path of the Sun.

This is why the Sun is greeted everyday at Dawn to be asked for guidance and protection by Maya Day-Keepers and Prayer-makers who have taken up their Divine Ancestorsʼ Sacred Staff in order to lead the People of their Pueblo through life and its many tests and trials. This is the story that is told here.

This was the Divinity known as Heart of the Sky who was the Kabʼawil Ukʼuʼx Kaj that imagined them so.

It was just a Deity known as a Kabʼawil who on his own, all alone imagined the Women of the First Four Men. These were the Women who would become the Wives who would be the Companions of the First Four Men. These Women were brought into being through the sleeping-dreaming of Ukʼux Kaj who was a Deity known as a Kabʼawil that was named Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were those known as the Women-Kixoqil-the Wives. This Divinity known as the Heart of the Sky-Ukʼuʼx Kaj was the Divinity-Kabʼawil that conjured them up while he slept to dream; when he dreamt in his sleep his imagination brought these truly beautiful women-qitzij jebʼel chi ixoq into being who were Wives-Kixoqil who would be the First Four Menʼs Companions-Kikʼulel; their Companion Wives who were the Women; who were the Companions of the First Four Men.

These Women who were Wives who were Companions sprouted forth in the imagination of Ukʼuʼx Kaj who dreamt sleeping to imagine these beautiful Women while he slept dreaming.

For the First Four Women came into being out of sleep; from sleep came the dreams that formed the Women in the imagination of Ukʼuʼx Kaj; Women who were shaped into the Wives who were brought forth into being as the First Four Menʼsʼ Companions; the Companions of the First Four Grandfathers-Nabʼe Mam; First Four Fathers-Nabʼe Qajaw.

And so it was that the Divinity Heart of the Sky who brought forth out of sleep these truly beautiful women that were the Companions of the First Four Men:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam;

Our First Grandfathers; Our First Fathers Nabʼe QaMam, Nabʼe QaQajaw.

Truly beautiful were the Women of those First Four Fathers: Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ: Jaguar Sweet Laughter of the Red Dawn of the East.

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ: Jaguar Night of the White Wind of North.

Majukʼutaj: Invisible One of the Black Dusk of the West.

Ikʼi Bʼalam: Many Jaguar of the Yellow Abundance of the South.

Truly beautiful were the Women who were with:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ

Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ

Majukʼutaj Ikʼi Bʼalam

Qitzij jebʼel chi Ixoq kʼo rukʼ Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam.

It was only with their women by their sides that these First Four Men became fully alive; for these First Four Men came fully to life when the First Four Women were there by their sides. With their Compañeras-Kikʼulel-Companions by their side they came to life; wide-awake; completely alive.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Just like that they were as content as could be; all at once their hearts were made sweet; it was just because of their Companions-Kikʼulel who were their Women-Kixoqil-their Wives.

Kʼo chi kixoqil ta kʼi xekʼastajikʼ; anim xkikot chik kikʼux rumal kikʼulel.

These then are their names, the name of the Houses of the Women Lords-e Ixoq Ajawabʼ in which they brought their children of their lineage into the world, like IxMuqane who has her Great House so too are named the First Four Women:

Kaqa Paluma Ja: Red Sea Turtle House was the name of the woman-ubʼi rixoqil-wife of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ

Chomi Ja: Shrimp House was the name of the woman-ubʼi rixoqil-wife of Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ. Tzʼununi Ja: Hummingbird House was the name of the woman- ubʼi rixoqil- wife of Majukʼutaj. Kaqixa Ja: Macaw House was the name of the woman-ubʼi rixoqil-wife of Ikʼi Bʼalam.

Or is it Jaʼ meaning Water since Mesoamerican People named themselves from ʼWaterʼ that was the vital essence of their lives in the form of rivers, lakes, oceans, seas, estuaries, streams, and springs. Or is both Water; Jaʼ and House; Ja since both signify on the People of the Pueblo who came from Nima Ja or a Great House while living ʼbeside- chaqʼa jaʼ or Chaqʼa Nima Jaʼ or Beside the Great Water. It makes no sense to reduce the meaning to either House or Water when we can easily entertain both meanings to this elemental and essential Maya word of Ja and Jaʼ; House and Water.

Kaqa Paluma Ja: Red Sea Turtle House ubʼi rixoqil Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ Chomi Ja: Shrimp-Prawn House ubʼi rixoqil Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ. Kaqixa Ja: Macaw House ubʼi rixoqil Majukʼutaj. Kaqixa Ja: Macaw House ubʼi rixoqil Ikʼi Bʼalam.

These are the names then of their Women-Kixoqil-their Wives those who became the Ixoq Ajawabʼ the Women Rulers, the Women Lords, Women Warriors, the First Noble Women Lords of Kʼicheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They were the First Mothers to multiply the many descendants of the Small Villages, Great Villages; they were the First Mothers who gave birth and multiplied the Small Tribes of People, Great Tribes of People known as: Chʼuti Amaqʼ, Nima Amaqʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ; Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo. This then is the origin, the foundation, the root of Kʼecheʼ Winaq who are spoken of here as ʼWe the Forest People; We the Many Trees People; Oj Kʼiche Winaq; known to all as the Kʼiche People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo; Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ. This then is the origin and the foundation of who we are as Kʼicheʼ People Kʼicheʼ Pueblo; Winaq Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ also spoken of as: Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ Here then is the beginning of the story that tells of who we are as the Forest People; Mountain People; Oj, Kʼecheʼ Winaq: Oj, Kʼicheʼ; We, the Kʼiche People; We, the Kʼicheʼ Nation; Oj, Kʼicheʼ Winaq.

For this is the root of the Ancient Ancestral Account that is the Sacred Story telling of who we are as a People that tells of who we are and where we came from as the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ; Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo.

From the Hearth of IxMuqane and IxKikʼ

to the Ceremonial Fires of Tula-Tollan Immediately their women, their wives made these first men content; for it was their women-kixoqil-their companions-kikʼulel who made the First Four Men fully awake, fully alive; awake, alive, content with life because they were content with their women. These were their ʼwomen companionsʼ who were their ʼwomen wivesʼ that they would live out their long ancestral lives.

These are the First Four Women who the Kʼicheʼ Maya will look back on as the Fist Four Matriarchs who will be the Nabʼe Alom or First Bearers of the First Sons-Nabʼe Wal or Nawal of the Lineages. These Women, these Wives will become the replacements-kʼexel of IxMuqane who will now fade away without a word said as she simply dissolves into dust as she disintegrates into the narrative ground of the Ancient Word.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is so very important yet we donʼt get the real sense of the departure of the Great Mother Matriarch IxMuqane with this most simple Introduction to these Women, these Wives who will become the Matriarchs of the Four Principal Lineages of the Kʼicheʼ Nation, Kʼicheʼ Kingdom, Kʼicheʼ Civilization that will rise and fall by the end of the telling of this Mythic History of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaq.

The Cultural Heroes, Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej have opened our understanding of Kʼicheʼ Maya Culture with its traditional ways of speaking and acting and so too has IxMuqane and IxKikʼ who are their Grandmother and Mother who do the same as mythic archetypes that teach by guiding and protecting their people through their mythic example.

Many became those who practiced ritual sacrifice as Sacrificial Priests who were Blood-letters; Blood-letters AjKʼixbʼ who ʼletʼ their blood; blood-letters who bled their blood with maguey spines-kʼix and stingray spines-kʼix.

These AjKʼixbʼ were those of the Maguey Spine, those of the Stingray spine, the sacrificial spine of blood-sacrifice who bled themselves as an ancestral form of practicing self-sacrifice.

The AjKajbʼ gave blood sacrifice with Obsidian blades for they were those who bled themselves to feed the stone deities with the blood they gave with sacrificial obsidian blades of ritual sacrifice.

AjKʼixbʼ; AjKʼixbʼ These were those who were known and named as Blood-letters that will go by their name AjKʼixbʼ; AjKʼixbʼ who are those of the spine-kʼix; those of the thorn-kʼix; the spine-kʼix, the thorn-kʼix used to bleed the blood that was dried on paper to be burnt as burnt offerings of sacrifice.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Many became those who practiced the practice of blood sacrifice on the altars of sacrifice by Sacrificial Priests known and named: AjKajbʼ. AjKajbʼ ʼthrew downʼ the sacrificial victims from up on top of the steep temple stairs-kumuk to the round altar place waiting down below on the great plaza where itʼs perfectly round sacrificial altars that lay there below awaiting the sacrifice to be ʼthrown downʼ to be divined by the way they landed upon the perfectly round altar place that were placed perfectly down below those steep temple stairs of the temples of the Kabʼawil.

Kabʼawil that were the Deities who were sustained; Divinities who were gifted sacrifice by the First Four Mother-Fathers whose burden it was to nourish and nurture their Ancestral Deities. Deities who were the Divinities presented to the First Four Fathers when they went to Tollan Tzʼuy Wa to receive their Kabʼawil who they would bear on their backs as their sacred burden who would protect and guide the lineages of the Kʼicheʼ to this very day and the writing of this translation-interpretation of Popol Wuj.

Each deity had its own mountain-plain; each divinity lived upon their own mountain-sea; each kabʼawil existed in and upon their very own mountain-lake that were the temple-mountains; plaza-seas where sacrifice was given to them as sacred sustenance by being burnt-up and thrown-down in perfect practices of blood sacrifice by those known as AjKʼixbʼ; AjKajbʼ.

No longer were they just Four; for now there were many more. Yet this is a remembrance of these who are Our First Four Mothers-Kajibʼ Qachuch who became Our Mothers-QaChuch.

This is a remembrance of Our Four First Mothers; Kajibʼ Qachuch of We the Kʼicheʼ People-Oj Kʼicheʼ Winaqʼ; We the Many Tree People-Oj Kʼicheʼ Winaq; We the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo-Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

We the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo who are known as el Pueblo Kʼicheʼ spoken of as Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ as those who came from the First Four Fathers, First Four Mothers of the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Different were the names of each one of them when they multiplied into many when they came forth from there at the Relebʼal Qʼij, the Coming out Place of the Sun; there in the East, en el Oriente at the Place of the Rising Sun; Relebʼal Qʼij: Place of the Dawn. Many were the ʼNamesʼ of the different ʼPeopleʼ there at the Relebʼal Qʼij- Coming Out Place of the Sun; different were the ʼNamesʼ of the many ʼPeopleʼ there before the House of Dawn.

This then is the naming of their names of those who were there when they bent down-low before the Dawn at the Coming up Place of the Sun: Tepew Oloman: Sovereign People of the Land of Rubber Kʼojaj: People of the Puma of Mexico; Masked People of the Puma Kʼenech Ajaw: Sun-Faced Lord; People of Palenque These were the first three names of the many people gathered there at the Relebʼal Qʼij, when they burst forth-xpoqʼotajik-to multiply into many at the Coming Out Place of the Sun; Place of the Dawn known as the Relebʼal Qʼij.

This then is the knowledge-retaʼm-the knowing of the origins of the Tamubʼ known as the Great Trunk People; and, the Ilokabʼ the Seer People, People of Vision People; the ʼHoney Hunters; the Honey Finders: Ilol Kabʼ. We were ʼJust One-Xa Junʼ when we came away from there; when we came away from the Coming-Out Place of the Sun. Xa Jun xpe wi chilaʼ Relebʼal Qʼij.

Xa Jun xpe wi chilaʼ Relebʼal Qʼij: Relebʼal Qʼij; Dawning Place in the East known as the Coming-Out Place of the Sun: They became ʼJust One-Xa Junʼ when they came away from there at the Coming-Out Place of the Sun. Xa Jun xpe wi chilaʼ Relebʼal Qʼij: They were ʼJust One-Xa Junʼ when they came away from the Coming-Out Place of the Sun; there in the East at the Place of the Dawn is where they were made Just One-Xa Jun.
