body:
The name of the Great Lord of Sacred Sustenance there was: Rajawal Aj Relebʼal Qʼij-Noble Lord and Ruler of the People and Pueblo of the Dawn; they went straight to him there when they arrived then at the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij They arrived before the Noble Lord and Ruler who was there before them and known by the name: Ajaw Nakxit; Nim Ajaw: Lord Four Footed Deer; Nakxitl Traveler; Conqueror; Voyager for he was a Great Four Footed One who walks on four feet like the wind he is strong and moves across the Face of the Earth without anyone or anything to stop him or slow him down; a Great Lord who is a Powerful Warlord; a Great Ruler who is a Just Judge; a Noble Lord and Supreme Ruler; known as the Balanced One; the Harmonious One: Nima Ajaw Nakxit was his title; his sovereign name.

Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl was the Name of the Great Lord and Highest Authority of the Realm known as the One who Weighs the Word-Xa Jun Qʼatol Tzij; the One who Measures the Truth-Qʼatol Tzij thick with the power and authority of rule is his majesty; his sovereignty; thus the ʼnaming of his nameʼ Ajaw Nakxit.

Ajaw Nakxit: Lord of the Four Feet; Noble Lord Deer; Noble Traveler; Noble Knower of the Kingdom; like maize his flesh is the original sustenance of the First Animal People; the flesh of deer was formed and shaped by the Former; the Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol who forms and shapes the Deer from the essence taken from the Four Cardinal Direction; Four Colors of the Four the Four Roads; Great Strength and Balance of the Four Hoof of Deer; Powerful Leader; Strong Leader.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Ajaw Nakxit was Rajawal Aj Relebʼal Qʼij which made him the Noble Lord and Ruler of the Coming Out Place of the Sun; Relebʼal Qʼij who was himself invested with the names of entitlement bestowed upon him as the supreme authority who is thick with power and strength of rulership and majesty-tzatz rajawarem of all the lands giving him great sovereignty-tzatz rajawarem. For thick was his power and strength of the Four Corners; Four Sides where he ordered and balanced the harmony and strength of his divine power over the People; noble authority; sacred authority over the Pueblos who lived upon those lands that were his to rule as a benevolent Ruler.

Nakxit Quetzalcoatl was the Noble Lord who was the caring and kind benevolent Ruler; the Just Judge of all those who came before him in quest of his great power-qʼaqʼal and authority-tepewal that would provide and sustain them with his noble ways of rule through sovereign command and supreme control that made him the very embodiment of splendor and majesty in Rulership-Ajawarem- Nobility. Truly, Nakxit was a Noble Lord; a Majestic Sovereign; the Supreme Lord of the Realm. For it was he Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl who bestowed rule and authority upon the Young Noble Lords who came before him to receive that which they traveled far and wide by walking while suffering and self-sacrificing along the way to acquire; to attain that which were signs of sovereignty and insignia of rulership that entitled and empowered them with the power and authority to rule as rulers in his majestic realm of noble sovereignty with its sacred ways of divine rulership.

body:
These were the signs and symbols of all their Sacred Offices: Aj Popol who was the Highest Noble Lord and Ruler of the Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule; and AjPop Kʼamjaʼil who was the Lord Counselor of the Reception House Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule; Second-in-line to the Noble Lord and Ruler: AjPop. So then they brought forth the images that embodied the essence of rulership and this is what they were: the signs and symbols of power and authority that were seen as the emblems of investiture that symbolized and signified the supreme sovereignty of the AjPop who was the Noble Lord and Ruler of the Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule; and, the AjPop Kʼamja known as the Noble Lord and Ruler of the Reception House Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule; he who was second in line to receive the rulership of the Noble Reed Mat of Council and Rule.

Those were the names of the Noble Lords who ruled over the People of the Pueblos with supreme power and sacred authority.

The Great Lord; Nim Ajaw was there; he was the Noble Lord of the Kingdom known as, Ajaw Nakxit. It was Ajaw Nakxit who gave out all of the symbols and insignia of Nobles, Lords, and Rulers: Wachinel Ajawarem-the Emblems of Rule and Rulership of Noble Lords.

It was Noble Lord himself Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl who fulfilled the task of bestowing power and rule upon the Young Lords of Kʼicheʼ who were the replacements of their Noble Fathers; the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl provided them with the sacred sustenance that would sustain them with power and sovereignty of Noble Rule and Divine Authority through his bestowal upon these Noble Sons of Noble Fathers with their signs and symbols, emblems and insignia of Nobles, Lords, and Rulers.

This is who they were now recognized to be as Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ through all they received in the form of emblems and shape of insignia that manifest their Noble Rule while it expressed their Sovereign Authority.

body:
These sacred insignia and noble emblems were acknowledged by Lords and Vassals alike just as they were recognized by Rulers and Subjects as the sacred symbols of these Young Noble Lords Divine Rule and Noble Authority spoken of as: Wachinel Ajawarem.

These are the names of the Wachinel Rajawarem-the Symbols and Emblems of Rulership and Authority that embodied and imbued these Named and Entitled Lords with the power to rule as a Noble Lords; Noble Rulers. These then are the names of the symbols of Noble Rulers and their Noble Rule:

Muj: Canopy, Paladin-Throne; Bearer of Noble Lord as Sacred Burden Qʼalibʼal: Jaguar Pelt Throne and Woven Reed Mat of Rule and Authority Tzam-baq: Nose-bone driven through the septum as a sign of initiation Subʼaq; Tzu bʼaq: Eagle Bone Flute of the Noble Lord and Ruler Cham-Cham: Ceremonial Drum or Gourd Rattle of Ruler Tatil: Resplendent black body paint-mineral dust; for ritual dance Qʼanabʼaj: Gold Beads-Amber Beads-Yellow Beads; Gold Bead Necklace Tzikwil Koj: Puma Fang Necklace, Puma Claw Necklaces; Canyon Tzikwil Bʼalam: Jaguar Fang Necklace, Jaguar Claw Necklace; Mountain Jolom: Owl Skull; Messenger of the Lords of Death; Ancestors Pich Kiej: Deer Hoofs; Signs of the Nawal of Lord Four-Foot Deer-Nakxitl Makutax: Deerskin, Jaguar-pelt Armband; Ballcourt-Warrior Insignia Tʼotʼ tatam: Snail Shell Bracelet; Dance Costume; Ukʼuʼx Cho-Ukʼuʼx Palo Kʼus bʼus: Tobacco Gourd for Ceremonial Tobacco Dust Kaxkon: Ritual Bowl for Sacred Count of Days for Incense Chiyom: Macaw Feather or Parrot Feather Crest; Headdress of Holy Lord Astapulul: Royal Crane Panache or Headdress of Quetzalcoatl Noble Prince

They carried all this away with them on their return; all of this they bundled- up to then bear it all away from where they were there beside the Sea. It from there that they carried away the writings of Tulan; it was from there beside the Sea that they brought the written books of the painted histories known as their Writings of Tulan; Utzibʼal Tulan which is spoken of as Tzibʼal Tulan.

Cargo boxes-Kok; Carrying-frames-Kakaxtle;

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Tortoise Shell-Kok; Merchant Boxes-Kakaxtle Once it was all given as gift and received in ritual the Young Lords bundled and bound it together to pack it away in their cargo boxes: kok.

They packed it tight in their carrying-frames: kakaxtle borne on the backs of porters and warriors; ball-players and merchants; lords and vassals alike known as kakaxtle in Nahuatl spoken of as kok in Mayan languages. These are wooden boxes or frames to be carried upon oneʼs back like ʼturtle shells-kokʼ they are emblems of merchants.

This is the tightly woven reed burden-bearing box; kok that these transformed Young Lords picked-up to place on their back to be borne with a tump-line slung over the crown of their skull-jolom-head. This is how they came away from the place there known as: ʼBeside the Sea- Chʼaqa Paloʼ.

Kok or Kakaxtle are merchant carrying boxes often represented by a turtle or tortoise shell that the Maya and Nahua people used to carry and protect perishable items like feathers and cacao, polychrome ceramic vases, plates, cacao cylinders, and everything of great value to nobles that are named above.

This is a sacred history of merchant alliances as it is a native chronicle of sacred tribute. This one image of the Young Noble Lords quickly placing their signs and symbols, emblems and insignia of noble investiture in their kok-kakaxtle is emblematic of the trade and tribute agreed upon with Ajaw Nakxitl that is spoken about with just one word: kok.

They also brought back the Writing-Tzibʼal-Painting of Tulan known as Utzibʼal Tulan.

Utzibʼal Tulan-Utzibʼal These were the Books of Sacred Writing; the Books of Precious Painting of Tulan that were highly prized and coveted Screen-fold Books of Writing; precious Books of Painting known as Utzibʼal Tulan; Tulan Writings; Tulan Paintings.

These are the Pictographic Histories; these are the Pictorial Histories known as the Ilbʼal that the Maya Scribes of the Popol Wuj lament not having to consult for their writing of the present exemplum of that Mesoamerican Genre of Literature known as Ilbʼal: Places of Vision; Place of Sight; Places of Imagination.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These are the books the Young Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ carried away with them when they bore them away bundled up in their kakaxtle. These are Writings of Tulan that these fearless young men carried with them when they left Tulan with the Books of Tulan-Utzibʼal Tulan neatly packed-up to be carried away in their kok.

They gathered their Books of Tulan with their Painted Signs and Symbols spoken of as Utzibʼal Tulan-Utzibʼal; the Ancient Writing, the Ancestral Writing of Tulan; Utzibʼal Tulan as they are known by those who are said to have entered the Truth of the Tradition by entering the Way of their Word: xechaʼ chire kiokinaq chi upam kitzij.

They picked themselves up to bear themselves away from the place Beside the Sea; carrying their sacred burden in their merchant boxes; kakaxtle and carrying frames; kok and then they began their journey of home.

And so then they returned back to the place where they had begun; they returned with the many symbols of rule and rulership that gave them the power and authority to govern the Mountain Pueblos with their Mountain People and Mountain Places.

So then they arrived back to where they started out when they returned to their citadel city-kitinamit-their walled city of Jaqawitz as it is named.

There is where they gathered together. Those who gathered together were those known as the Tamubʼ who were assembled there with the Ilokabʼ.

They gathered together to celebrate the return of the Young Noble Lords:

Kʼo Kaʼibʼ, Kʼo Akutek, Kʼo Ajaw. Their hearts were made sweet while giving thanks for their arrival and return with the symbols of noble investiture and emblems of noble authority that gave them the power to rule over the Pueblos as Noble Lords: AjPop; AjPop Kʼama Ja; Lord of the Noble Mat; Lord of the Noble Reception House Mat. The Three Young Kʼicheʼ Lords returned home to their Mountain Citadel with the Sovereign Rulership-Ajawarem that Nakxitl bestowed upon them as symbols and signs of the favor that they received from the his as the Nim Ajaw AjRelebʼal Qʼij-Great Lord of the People of the Dawn-Rajawal AjRelebʼal Qʼij; Lord of the People of the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Nim Ajaw Rajawal Relebʼal Qʼij.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Mountain People and the Canyon People of the Mountain Pueblos; Canyon Pueblos now received their Lordship-Ajawarem, just as they accepted their Rulership-Ajawarem as Subjects; as Vassals; as Daughters and Sons-Saqil Al puch Saqil Kʼajol of the Great Lord of Coming Up Place of the Sun; ri Nim Ajaw Tulan Tzuy-Wa with whom they were now the most kindly aligned friends who were the most friendly kinds of allies.

Those who were made content were those who were named; those who were known as: Rabʼinalebʼ; Qʼaqʼchekelebʼ; Aj Tzʼikina Ja who were shown the supremacy of their new condition before the ʼfaceʼ which is to say before the ʼcountenanceʼ of all the other Tribes; which was experienced as a sense of superiority and supremacy that was now felt as a novel source of power and pride.

These are those who spoke slightly different languages as the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords for the Rabʼinalebʼ spoke Achi; the Qʼaqʼchekelebʼ spoke Kaqchikel; and the Aj Tzʼikina Ja spoke Tzʼutujil. But did the nobility speak a Noble form of Kʼicheʼ such as that suggested here in the Ojer Tzij of Popol Wuj that has many Tzʼutujil and Kaqchikel words and phrases as well as Achi forms of myth-making; story-telling language?

The returning Noble Lords enjoyed nothing more than showing the People of the Pueblos their insignia of power; their rights of investiture that were seen as symbols and signs of authority that by extension manifest their sovereign power with all of its grandeur of rule and majesty rulership-unimal ajawarem.

All of which taken as a whole further demonstrated the hallowed importance of their divine leadership of the People that secured the protection and guidance of the Pueblo.

For truly, the divine dignity of their noble power and regal decorum that the Kʼicheʼ People now felt for themselves as Noble Pueblo was what would make them a Powerful Kingdom founded upon the Divine Power of its Nawal Rulers. This was the sublime sense of superiority they now enjoy with the newly gained Majesty of the Noble Sovereignty that they now benefited from upon their return from the Tulan Tzuy-Wa.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
For the Kʼicheʼ now experienced as sense of dominion over their realm that they had never known before making good on their promise to their Fathers to take up the road to kneel before Nakxit Quetzalcoatl of Relebʼal Qʼij there at the Coming Up Place of the Sun; there at the House of Dawn where the Nim Ajaw Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz ruled upon the Noble Reed Mats of the Popol Ja rech ri Tulan Tzuy-Wa.

They last a long time there on top of that Mountain of Jaqawitz; by then there were many of them all together there on the mountain top growing all the time.

Their new condition as sovereign Lords of a sovereign Pueblo was what came to manifest their superiority before the other Tribes which made them more than content-kikotik because of the signs and symbols that they could now show all the other Pueblos.

These were the emblems of rule and investitures authority that were brought back by their Three Young Lords that gave them sovereign power and divine rulership over all the Pueblos.

The sweet success of their ancestral quest was an important revelation to be shown to all the People of the Pueblos of the Mountain Places and Canyon Country who came before their Young Noble Lords to see emblems of power and insignia of rulership; they were shown to all the People of the all Pueblos upon their return from the Nakxit Quetzalcoatl Rajawal AjRelebʼal Qʼij.

Nakxit Quetzalcoatl Rajawal AjRelebʼal Qʼij What is important to understand that the Supreme Deity Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz; Ukʼuʼx Cho; Ukʼuʼx Palo is always with us throughout this myth-making performance of Popol Wuj. Yet, the Nima Ajaw; Great Lord spoken of here as Nakxit Quetzalcoatl Rajawal AjRelebʼal Qʼij known the Great Lord and Ruler of the Coming-Up Place of the Sun that is another name for Tulan Tzuy-Wa is not the same as Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz who is a Kabʼawil of the most supreme proportions as the Light and Life aspect of the twinship of Creator-Destroyer Deities who is twinned to his Darkness and Death aspect of twinship of Destroyer-Creator Deities known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja Ukʼuʼx Kaj; Ukʼuʼx Ulew.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These are Deity not Great Lords despite the fact that Nakxit Quetzalcoatl Rajawal AjRelebʼal Qʼij appearing to be divine which he most certainly is because he is the one who gives the First Four Fathers their Kabʼawil Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz, Nikʼaj Taqʼaj. But there are ʼdegreesʼ of hierarchy that are only suggested through the Ancient Word; Ojer Tzij which are never clarified so I believe it is important to organize this a bit despite my feeling that the Kʼicheʼ Maya Scribes wanted to create ambiguity between all the categories that the rational, analytical, materialist, lineal sort of academic mind wants to place in all the tiny boxes of empirical thought to keep it all straight. Qʼuqʼkumatz; Quetzalcoatl; Kukulkan are all divine names worm by Noble Lords and we will meet another Lord Quetzalcoatl; Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz soon enough to heighten the intended sense of confusion created between divinity as Kabʼawil and divinity as Nawal and divinity as humanity in the case of humans that embody nawal powers of divinity as ancestors who transform and change at will as Nawales are said to do yet are not said to be Kabʼawil.

These emblems and insignia embodied the sacred burden of rule and responsible now borne on the backs of the Young Noble Lords. For it was they who were now responsible for the well-being of their People and the prosperity of their Pueblo; now these Young Lords of Noble Fathers were the all-powerful sovereigns of the Kʼicheʼ People; of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo who by extension were made responsible and accountable to the Great Lord and Ruler of the Relebʼal Qʼij in the East; he who was named Nima Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl; known as Rajawal AjRelebʼal Qʼij Nima Ajaw Nakxit Quetzalcoatl; the Nima Ajaw Relebʼal Qʼij. This then was when they realized that with the new power they received was plenty of reason and cause for them to live in a new condition of existence-kikʼojeʼik as Noble Rulers of their People who were responsible for finding a place for them to live as an ever growing and multiplying People and expanding Pueblo.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so it was that the Young Noble Lords were made to bear the burden of responsibility for the power and authority of the all the many Pueblos and People they were now responsible for as the Tzuqul, Kʼool-Providers, Sustainers who they now provided with protection and sustained with guidance through their position as Sovereign Rulers of their Mothersʼ and Fathersʼ Ancestral Realm which meant much more responsibility for them as Noble Lords who led their People and Pueblos as Beloved Rulers who now exercised the Sovereign Rule of a Powerful Kingdom: Nimal Ajawarem

That was when they lived on top of the Mountain of Jaqawitz along with all the others who were there with them at the Coming Out Place of the Sun known as Relebʼal Qʼij. They lived there for a long time and so it was that together they made for a great many People atop the Mountain of Jaqawitz.

Here is where their wives died; the wives; the women of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj they died on Jaqawitz.

The First Men were dead, they had already died but now their Women died, their Women who were their Wives died there on Jaqawitz so now they were also dead.

The First Four Women:

KaqaPaluna Ja: Red Sea Turtle House Chomi Ja: Shrimp House Tzʼununi Ja: Hummingbird House Kaqixa Ja: Scarlet Macaw House

First Four Men:

Bʼalam Kiʼtze: Lord Jaguar Sweet Laughter; Lord Jaguar Sweet Smile Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ: Lord Jaguar Night; Lord Jaguar Dark Night Majukʼutaj: Black Panther; Invisible One; Not One is Here; No One at All Ikʼi Bʼalam: Moon Jaguar; Wind Jaguar; Many Jaguars; Lord Jaguar Moon

These were the Divine Ancestors; these were the Ancient Ancestors-Ojer taq Winaq of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ of the Many Tree People, Many Tree Pueblo. And so it was that these were the First Four Fathers who engendered the many Kʼicheʼ Maya lineage to sprout-forth from their seed; from their spittle. This is where their wives died; the wives, the women of Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ; Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ; Majukʼutaj; it is they who died; it is they who were now dead the Fist Mothers; First Fathers; Divine Ancestors; Ancient Ancestors; Old People: Ojer taq Winaq Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Just then, just like that the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ came away from there, they abandoned their mountain of origin; their ancestral mountain of emergence-Jaqawitz is the mountain they left abandoned when they got up from upon Chuwi Juyubʼ to leave it behind just as had been abandoned Kaqa Ja-the abandoned Red Temple House of Sacrifice so too did they leave the Mountain Top-Chuwi Juyubʼ abandoned when they left Jaqawitz they just left it behind.

This is the way of the people; this is the lay of the land; this is the sacred play of the sacred rounds of night and day; twenty years pass and then one day they say the time has come to abandon the mountain we were once guided to establish ourselves as a Pueblo on a Livable Mountain; a Habitable Mountain chosen by their Kabʼawil: Jaqawitz. Now they were summoned again; now they were called to take council to hear they were to abandon Chuwi Juyubʼ Jaqawitz.

That was it the Kabʼawil had spoken and they had listened and so it was time to go; and so they got going. They were going now and soon they would all be gone when they abandoned Jaqawitz; not one was left behind; like Majukʼutaj nobody was there on Jaqawitz because everyone had packed up their kakaxtle; their kok to the bear what little they had when they left Jaqawitz abandoned; nothing was left behind; only the Kaqa Ja stood there on the flat open plain on top of Jaqawitz that was cleared-off and clean-up to leave Jaqawitz abandoned.

They sought another mountain; they sought another more livable mountain; a more suitable mountain is what they sought; and there they prospered, on innumerable mountains they prospered when they came away from Jaqawitz in search of other mountains to settle and establish their lives.

And so it was they found and settled on one mountain after the next; and where they came to live their lives was on prosperous mountains; fruitful livable mountains upon which to settle to live their lives as the Kʼicheʼ People; as the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo: Winaq Kʼicheʼ, Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ.

And so it was that they named them; they named the mountains they settled, the mountain places they found and settled where the mountain places they named.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They named those mountain places where they came together; the mountain places they settled is where the suffered punishment together; where they performed sacrifice together there on the mountains they settled. That was the life experience of those First Mothers; First Fathers-Nabʼe Chuch-Qajaw who experienced life on their newly settled mountains as a difficult punishing existence; that was the way life was experienced for those who sought out and settled truly fine, livable mountains; they just suffered great hardship; they just endured suffering there on those mountains they settled.

Uncountable were the number of mountains that they settled where they gathered together to endure great hardship; many were they mountains where they bound and bundled themselves to one-an-other to overcome ordeal; to survive everything they were made to endure to live prosperous, abundant lives on one mountain after the next. They gathered together with one another to endure all they were made to endure Our First Mothers; Our First Fathers overcame suffering and sacrifice. Xemolomanik, Xechʼijomanik; eNabʼe QaChuch, e Nabʼe QaQajaw.

They gathered together in order to persevere together; they gathered together in order to endure together to become a strong enduring People that became a strong enduring Pueblo; so that together as a People they endured; so that together as a Pueblo they survived to become who they were and who they came to be: a strong and hard, enduring People, who became a strong and hard enduring Pueblo.

This is what the Ancient People said-Ojer taq Winaq xechaʼ-when they told these stories; when they recounted their tales telling of when they abandoned their fortified mountain citadel Chuwi Juyubʼ; Jaqawitz its name. So then they left it; they just deserted it; they just left behind their first town, they left it abandoned, the one they called Jaqawitz. This was when they arrived there to begin their work of establishing a new town. Chi Kʼix-Beside the Thorns was the name of their new town that they went to found as their new citadel on the habitable mountain where they went to sow their seed there in the ground of Chi Kʼix to found their new town.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is what they did when they began again on a habitable mountain; on a good mountain to then found and form a new fortress settlement; Chi Kʼix was its name; Beside the Brambles; Beside the Thorns was its name; the name of the place Beside the Spines where they gave sacrifice. They made it there a long time; for a long time they made a good life together there as they built their stronghold together from a handful of smaller groups of clans and families.

Chi Kʼix was a fortified citadel-tinamit that was formed from a handful of smaller groups of people: juchʼobʼ tinamit.

They had daughters, and they had sons so that over time they became many vassals and many subjects; and so it was that they became a great populace once again. And like before they multiplied and grew to eventually people the face of the earth by peopling and populating the Mountain-Plain-Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj as they were formed and shaped to do.

There were Four Mountains of Sustenance there that were known as Kajib Juyubʼ Waʼ. But only one of them, just One Mountain was taken as the name of the Four Mountains.

They married their daughters; they found companions for their sons; companions who became the wives of their sons; these women who they found for their sons were their partners for life: kʼulel.

Many of their daughters, many of their sons they just gave away. Just as favors, just out of respect for one another did they do it; they just gave their daughters and sons away to one another out of communal respect; out of personal regard for one another.

The bride price they asked was the bride price they received, making their lives there quite good; quite comfortable.

They lived the good life there on that mountain they found and settled together as a Pueblo formed and shaped from groups of People.

They lived a fine life there on that mountain by accepting the gifts given to them out of respect; and, by doing so they lived in gratitude and this is what made their way of life a good hospitable way of existence.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is when they supervised and inspected the groups of towns of Chi Kʼix that were the fortified towns grouped together in a handful of towns known as Chi Kʼix. This is when they passed through on inspection of each one of these towns in this group of towns where people were able to live out good lives. They came to supervise each one of the groups that made-up this citadel city-jutaq chʼobʼ chi tenamit-that is to say they came to visit in order to inspect each group of the one main citadel; the name of that fortified citadel was: Chi Kʼix.

These then are their names of the Tinamit; the names of the Pueblos of Chi Kʼix: E Chi Kʼix-Beside the Thorns; Beside the Brambles; Beside the Spines Chi Chaqij-Beside the Dry Place; Beside Parched Place Chi Chʼaq-Beside the Wet Place, Beside the Soggy Place Jumeta Ja-Alder Bark River; Alder Dye, Orange Dye Vats beside River Kulubʼa-Kolubʼat-Boundary markers; Border-line that mark the boundary Kawinal-People of Second Winal, People of Forty-Years beside Chi Xoy These were the names of the Mountain Citadels where the Kʼicheʼ Lords stayed to visit their People of the Pueblos; Winaq, Amaqʼ. These were small towns within which they stayed in order to know what it was like to live within those small fortified settlements. This is where they visited to know what it was like to live in one of those tiny mountain strongholds.

These are the names of Fortified Mountain Towns known as Mountain Citadels that the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords spent time inspecting to see if they could not find other mountains similar to these to establish themselves and their people in order to keep multiplying and growing as a Pueblo.

For it was they, the Noble Lords, who were those that went out in the mountains wandering about looking for a Livable Mountain-Ulaj Juyubʼ upon which establish themselves in order to live a calm, contented, comfortable life on a hospitable mountain on a fertile and fecund mountainside.

They were looking for a fruitful mountain where they would settle new towns in which capable hard-working people could establish themselves and settle down to a successful life on a fructifying mountainside.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They were searching for mountain places where strong enduring people could prepare the land to sow the seed and grow the milpa. And so it was that they sought out a Livable Mountain-Ulaj Juyubʼ to live out peaceful prosperous lives.

They were seeking a livable mountain to flourish on as in the past because in those days there were many People there who were seeking a hospitable sort of welcoming place to live their life.

They Left it Abandoned This then was when the spoke to one another; they took council with one another when they thought and when they pondered what to do next. This then was when they came away from there; this then was when they left their Mountain Place abandoned; the Mountain they lived on for a long time was the Mountain they now left; they left it behind; they left it abandoned; they left no one behind. Their journey of becoming had then just begun as they broke away from where they come; they broke from their Fathersʼ past to create; to craft their new lives on their new mountains; mountains of their own choosing in lives of their own making with its molding and modeling; with its forming and shaping on the Mountain Place they would come to live when they came to the place that they found that was a livable mountain; a mountain they could live on with their wives and their children.

This is how it was with them the Young Noble Lords whoʼs new condition as Rulers who were given their power and authority they felt the ancestral burden of responsibility for the People of the Pueblos as their Providers; as their Sustainers. And so the decided it was time to find a Mountain Place where they could lives of abundance and prosperity; and so, the abandoned their homes and left from there where they had made their lives upon the Mountain- top of Jaqawitz known as Chuwi Juyubʼ. They left it abandoned; they walked away and never looked back. Our First Mother, Our First Father became hardened people who were made strong through their surviving the difficult lives that were theirs to live.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This then was when they gathered together on the mountain to endure the difficult lives of theirs that were their lives to live as those who lived their lives as founders of settlements. They were those who went out finding and founding mountain settlements. They were those kinds of people who knew what was theirs in life and what that was; was searching and settling themselves on small mountain settlement as strong People who came from a hard kind of all-enduring Pueblo.

These were a People who at first lived to survive; to then lived to thrive; to then live-out blessed lives as a bountiful People who existed as a prosperous Pueblo on ancient, ancestral mountains like that of Jaqawitz.

Jaqawitz was an ample open mountain where prosperity was cultivated throughout the many years of sowing and seeding the abundance they harvested there year after year until there was nothing left for the mountain to give to those who at first lived just to survive but then began to thrive by living magical sorts of plentiful kinds of bountiful lives.

These were the lives of Our First Mother-Fathers who lived beautiful blessed bountiful lives up on top of Jaqawitz.

Ulaj Juyubʼ Livable-Fertile-Earthy-Rich Mountain This Ulaj Juyubʼ which is a Livable Mountain-Fertile Mountain-Rich sort of Earthy Mountain was a mountain molded and modeled from good workable earth-ulew not too much stone; not too much clay; not too much sand; not too much shade; not too dry; not too wet; some breeze but not too much wind; not too many gophers; not too many deer nor a great abundance of rabbits; not too many birds; not too many jaguar or puma and this is what they were out looking for to live-out lives on a mountain where there werenʼt too many animals to defend the milpa from with oneʼs planting stick and blowgun. Most of all a mountain where one could play ball and have some fun if not out hunting with oneʼs ancient ancestral blowgun.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the sort of land they sought when the Young Noble Lords went out walking and searching for a livable place to live their lives with their people who went out exploring all over their mountains and canyons in quest of the perfect place to establish a new settlement that began with the Young Lords walking across the face of the earth looking for signs in the trees and traces in the dirt that told of what kind of possibilities were held within the earth and its sacred soil.

Eventually they would find mountain places-juyubʼal just like the kind of livable mountain places they were looking for. And so it was that when they found places like those ones they settled them and established themselves by sowing the seeds of their milpa to begin growing the canes of their maize this is the traditional way to establish the living the good life on a fine mountain; on a fertile mountainside.

There on the mountainside on some nice sunny ridgeline is where they could place their houses that were homes in the morning light and evening sun where there was a spring for water and good rich soil to sow their milpa.

This is what the Young Noble Lords were out on their quest in search of new livable mountains to form and shape new settlements that would grow into an ever expanding group of houses and milpas that enveloped one another in the mountains and canyons of this one great big mountain citadel known as a tinamit in this forested mountain place known as the Kʼicheʼ.

It was then that some of the Older People began dying; they reached the end of their lives. Those who died were those who had brought the Sovereign Rule of the Noble Lords from the Coming Up Place of the Sun: Ajawarem Relebʼal Qʼij.

They had died, those who had been bestowed the status of Ruler and Authority; and those who had received noble entitlement and named to the office of Noble Lords there in Tulan Tzuy-Wa were those who were dying if not already dead.

These were those who lived as the sovereign rule and authority over the Pueblos who were growing old and dying out little by little; day by day.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It was they who had made the long difficult journey to the ʼPlace beside the Seaʼ known as Relebʼal Qʼij and it was they who were those that had died; it was they the ancient old ones who were already dead.

These were those who had gone to Tulan Tzuy-Wa on the advice of their Fathers, the First Fathers who had given them instruction on their remembrance that was a commitment to their promise to return from where their rule and authority originated there beside the sea at the Coming up Place of the Sun.

They were already quite old when they took up the road searching for a Livable Mountain-Ulaj Juyubʼ-Habitable Mountain; a Fertile Mountain; a Fruitful Mountain from which would come the harvest and abundance from which to live a Life worth living; a Life lived on a Mountain worth living it: Ulaj Juyubʼ.

It was they in their old age who passed from one mountain to the next on their way across the Great Mountain-Plain-Nim Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj on their quest that was a difficult journey searching and surveying; exploring and examining; investigating and evaluating these Mountain Places where they would settle and establish a Mountain Top Citadel known as a Juyubʼ Tinamit.

These were those who were dying. It was they who had brought back the Noble Rule from the Coming Out Place of the Sun.

These were those old of age who brought back the Sovereign Rule of the Named Lords; the Entitled Lords from the East.

This was the Sacred Rule of the Noble Lords from there where the Sun rises up and out of the Sea at the Coming Out Place of the Sun: Relebʼal Qʼij. These Grandfathers were already White-haired, White-whiskered Old Men when theyʼd passed by this way awhile ago.

So these First Grandfathers-Mamaxel; these Old Men-Nima Winaq who brought back the power to rule over other Pueblos never became accustomed to the places where they passed through on their journeys of inquiry and inspection.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
So they moved-on despite suffering great ordeal; they survived only by overcoming many afflictions as they made their way through the world looking for a mountain place to live a life worth living in a chosen place worth living that life; that life of suffering and affliction that must be endured to establish a settlement on a ʼbountiful mountain; on a plentiful mountainʼ where one comes together with others to form a built town and shape its wooden walls to mold and model a settlement that is the establishment of a Mountain Citadel; a Mountain Stronghold; Jun Juyubʼ Tenamit to be formed; to be shaped; to be settled; to be established on the Face of the Earth. Chi Ismachi, this is the name of their town, the town that the Ancestral Grandfathers, Ancestral Fathers-Mamaxel, Qajawixel founded and established after searching to find a Mountain Place-Juyubʼal upon which to found their One Mountain Citadel-Jun Juyubʼ Tinamit.

Chi Ismachi; Beside White Whisker Tree; Mimosa Blanca Only after a long time of searching did they find a Mountain Place-Jun Juyubʼal to establish and build their One Fortified Town-Jun Juyubʼ Tinamit-their One Mountain Citadel which became their very own Great Walled City: Chi Ismachi; Beside the Old Manʼs Whisker; Beside the Beard of the Old Man; Beside the Sunʼs White Whiskers; known as Beside the Old Manʼs White Whiskers; White Whiskers of the Sun or just Beside the White Whiskers Tree spoken of as Ismachi; known as the Sunʼs Beard or the Sunʼs Whiskers: Chi Ismachi Beside the Whiskers; Whiskers of the Old Man; Old Man the Sun. This is a plant that once played a principle role in the lives of initiates ʼentering the fireʼ of the Sun by taking the ʼessenceʼ of tree to obtain the vision of seers who were said to ʼenter the fire-enter the flamesʼ of the Sun.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Ismachi known as White Mimosa; Mimosa hostiles a tree that grows ʼBeside the Forestʼ where the land has been cleared and cleaned on Mountain Tops where the land has been disturbed allowing these trees to thrive on Mountain Places disrupted by fire where Milpa is sown; where Milpa is grown. Chi Ismachi is literally Beside the Fine Hairs or Peach Fuzz that grows around of Ones Face, Cheeks, and Mouth; the Hairs of Oneʼs Face: ismal-chi or rismal chi; a beard; un bigote!

Once again a name has been chosen that when turned in the rays of the Sun begins to form and transform in meaning more than a metaphor could ever wish for and then a wee bit more. This Ismachi may well be pointing to a ritual plant used in the transformation of one vision by igniting the vision of initiates in order that receive knowledge of their destiny or the answer to a question that calls to be known.

Chi Ismachi: Place of the White Whiskers; Beside the White Beard;

There beside the Old Menʼs Tree: Mamaxel; Beside the White Mimosa: Ismachi Chi Ismachi: Place of the Whiskers or Beside the Whiskers is the name of the mountain and the town where the Old Men-Mamaxel came to settle and rule beside the Nawal Tree that would be the remembrance of their search to find a place that reflect their Old Manʼs nature with their Sons, Grandsons-the Hummingbirds darting all about them suckling the nectar, the essence of the Sunʼs heat; the Sunʼs light found in the plenitude of white whisker-like flowers that cover the White Mimosa Tree known as: Ismachi!.

This is a foundational word-play on this Ancestral Place and these Ancestral People since Chi Ismachí is named by the Grandfathers-Mam and Fathers-Qajaw after the Ismachi Trees growing there with their White Whiskers that are taken to be the very Whiskers of the Sun, this is the White Mimosa Tree, the White Whiskers of the Old Man; the Sun.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This Ismachi Tree; this Whisker Tree is seen as the Nagual of the Sun brought to life on the Face of the Earth its heliotrope leaves and flowers open and close according to the rising and falling of the Sun-the Old Man-Mam-the Ancestor. This is heat and light; warmth and luminescence of the Old Man-Mam, the Sun-Tat-Father, as he makes his way on his daily walk walking over and across the Face of the Earth; and, yearly walk back and forth along the horizon line in the East, in the West; the Rising, the Falling creating a moving left to right, right to left on the sides, on the edges of the Face of the Earth.

This is the tree of the Sun, the Nawal embodiment of the Old Man himself who calls in his Sons the Hummingbirds to feed by darting about him cleaning his beard suckling his nectar in the First Rays of the Dawn: Saqnatanoj. Tojil suckles the nectar of his flowery gifts and so too the hummingbirds chattering about taking the precious essence of their sustenance the ʼwhite dustʼ of the Sun. Chi Ismachi: Beside the White Whiskers of the White Mimosa Tree is the name of the newly germinated town that shoot up as it sprouts out of the ground just like the super fertile and fecund seed of this super abundant flower forming; seed shaping tree.

Ismachi Tree assuredly assured the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords this would be a fine place to live by establishing themselves in the ambient of and below the shade of this trees whose tiny perfectly aligned leaves open and close according to rays of the Sun. This White Whisker Flower Tree or White Mimosa gives the name to this Ancient Ancestral Tree that gives the name to the town that is remembrance of the Old Men who founded it long, long ago.

This treeʼs seeds germinate in great profusion to then begin growing and growing in a great confusion of invasive trees like an invasive people who look to seed themselves to spread out and take over a territory they wish to call their own by naming it as the tree that tells of their essential nature: Ismachi the White Mimosa Tree.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
For like the form of the People and the shape the Pueblo takes so are their Nawal Trees that manifest as the sign and symbol of where they come to life to spread and spread covering the land with leguminous ways of peas in a pod that pop open in the heat of the Sun after being drenched in dew through the night.

So like the seed so do the people fall off a great sprawling trunk of many strong and enduring limbs. Wherever the seed of this tree should fall then instantly it will sprout out and grow; which is everywhere making this tree the incarnation of the idea of ʼPoqʼol, Kirolʼ or ʼgo forth and multiply to then grow and grow and grow.

Saq rismal chi: White Hairs of the Mouth; White Whiskers of the Face or White Beard or Saq Ismachi-White Whiskers of the Sun or Ismachi Qʼij is the name of this tree that is the House of the Sun where his Sons and Grandsons the Hummingbirds come and go from this White Whiskered Tree that becomes Humming Bird House that is the House of the Sun where the Tzʼunun-Hummingbird comes and goes making it a true delight to behold in the warm rays of the Sun and the sweet breeze of the Mountainside where this Mimosa Tree thrives on the edge of mountain slopes where the heat is most intense and the soil dry and parch because the howling wind and scorching sun. Ismachi then is an enduring tree that thrives in affliction while surviving any and all suffering.

Know as Mimosa hostilis or Tepezcohuite in Nahuatl and Ismachi in Maya Kʼicheʼ this plant was used to treat skin disease so it may well have been part of the ʼwarriorsʼ pharmacology. The plant also is rich source of the psychoactive agent DMT and may have been used in rites of initiation.

In the Dry Season months this Ismachi Tree become Heaven on Earth when its flowers- leaves-limbs and halo of pollen become a genuine Paradise of the Sun and Terrestrial Throne of the Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Earth when the Great White Beard of the Sun call in the Wasps, Bees, Hummingbirds, and Butterflies and those who are out chasing them.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the perfect emblematic place for the Old Men-Mamaxel to establish and ʼbring forthʼ their final home in which the Old Men are rejuvenated by being brought back to life by watching while participating with their Sons and Grandsons who must buzz about their new town that is like the Mimosa tree that comes alive with the birds and bees; wasps and butterflies; hummingbirds and tiny stingless bees that are busy all day long in the ʼwhite beard-like flowersʼ of the Ismachi tree just as the Daughters and Sons; Vassals and Subjects; Sons and Grandsons are busy all day long working to create and craft a new colony of humanity; that now are forming and shaping this spectacular Citadel City; the Tinamit of Ismachi.

Like a ʼBusy Bee-Hiveʼ becomes this White Whiskered Citadel of the Old White-Haired Ones; the Old White Eye-Browed Ones known as the Mamaxel of Ismachi of the Mamaxel. It is they who come tell us the story of the hard-working Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo in the secret sacred language of this magical myth. Its every word and every name call us as they beckon us on to a deeper relationship with the words of remembrance that are here to be discovered as the mythic words and mythic metaphors that form the mythic names that shape the mythic images calling for our attention to be discovered through their meaning becoming uncovered. So that our hearts and souls are awoken by the beauty that waits within to provide us today with the heat and warmth of our own ancestral soulʼs flowering forth as we experience for ourselves some unforeseen blooming and blossoming of narrative beauty found in some blossoming and blooming meaning of some deeper more flourishing; flowering meaning of this subtly adorned text.

Time, patience, care, and attention to this sacred Indigenous text of these mountains and canyons natural world that speaks in natural ways of Old Men as white bearded flowers on trees swarming with bees at work as an enduring people, enduring pueblo to make and mold a ʼSplendid Cityʼ whose origins are found in the white whisker flowers of a helio-tropical tree.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The hidden message of the trickster messenger deity enters our interpretive translation, our hermeneutic, to coax us blooming heart and blossoming soul into more floral, florid meanings by going beyond the call of convention to seek out in order to find the essence and origin of the Maya imagination by entering the imaginal realm of the mythic imagination like a butterflies seeks out its sacred sustenance in the nectar that the hummingbird misses by going so fast in order move on to the next flower; the next word; the next metaphor calling out to be known and acknowledge by us in the Age we live in where transcendent beauty is all that matters because of the way aesthetic leads to transcendent truth in the Sky-Earth that all that matters is the truth and the culture good that come from that truth that leads to deeper understanding of the Indigenous People here in Indigenous America.

This is the power and glory of these Maya scribes in their creation of this mythic illumination of magnificent white bearded tree; Ismachi of the Mamaxel the Old Men and our Ancestral Remembrance of them of the Grandfathers of the Kʼicheʼ Maya and their Ancestral Past sought and found through the names of their trees with their transforming leaves and flowers of the Old Man the Sun that magically tells of the Kʼicheʼ Citadel created and crafted on a ʼlivable mountainʼ in an Ancestral Place named by trees and their flowers that speak of the Sun there in the Heart of the Sky.

The Sun acts like a seed when it buries itself beneath the Earth so that this sun-like is a buried being that we watch and wait for its sprouting that is a rising up and out of the Earthʼs surface. This is a story that began at the beginning with the sowing and dawning life and creation that started long ago with articulation of the sacred most name: Ulew.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Ulew that is the root of the name of a Habitable Mountain Ulaj Juyub that was the kind of Livable Mountain Place that the Noble Lords looked for when they went out looking for the perfect place to live the good life in a livable place amongst the trees and vines; the streams and rivers; the pine groves and cypress groves beside the White Mimosa Trees: Chi Ismachi!

Chi Ismachiʼ is the name of their mountain just as Chi Ismachiʼ is the name of their town that the Kaweq founded and settled up there in the mountains when they were already Old Men: Mamaxel. It was they, the Old Men; the Grandfathers-Mamaxel, who settled this place, forming their village, shaping their town. This is where they established their power to then test the strength of their noble sovereignty-tepewal-reign over their kingdom; their divine rule-ajawarem-noble rulership; their power-qʼaqʼal-strength; their dominion of realm-nimal-grandeur of position: tepewal; ajawarem; qʼaqʼal; nimal.

They were great builders-tzʼaqol; for it was they who raised stone walls- tzʼaq of lime and mortar-cal y canto to build-tzʼaq their temples-tzʼaq and temple walls-tzʼaq.

They continued on with their foundational project of building buildings in the fourth generation of the Lords Kʼo Nacheʼ known as Ajaw Kʼonacheʼ and Belejebʼ Kej-Nine Deer who was the Lord Chancellor, Lord Magistrate when those who governed were Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Jaʼ known as Ajaw Kʼotuja Lord Sweatbath and Istayul known as Ajaw Istayul. It was they who were those that were named Aj Pop-Noble Lord of the Council House Mat of Noble Rule and Authority.

The second ruler beside him was known by the name Aj Pop Kʼama Jaʼ Noble Lord and Ruler of the Reception House Mat of Rule and Authority. Noble Lord reigned second beside AjPop who was the first to reign and rule over those Noble Palaces of the Kʼicheʼ spoken of a Council Houses known as Popol Ja.

The two of them ruled there at Chi Ismachi that became the stunningly Beautiful City that they brought forth; a truly Splendid City it became under their sovereign rule-Utzilaj Tenamit xuxik-it came forth into being as a Elegant Citadel City of the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo known as the Kaweqibʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so it was that Chi Ismachi became a truly Gracious City-Utzilaj Tenamit that was a truly Splendid City-Utzilaj Tenamit. This is what Chi Ismachí became because of everything they did; those that were named the AjPop, Ajaw Qʼalel, and AjPop Kʼama Jaʼ Noble Sovereign and Ruler; Chancellor and Magistrate of the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo.

These were all revered Old Men; Mamaxel; for they were truly Old Men; adored Ancianitos; venerated Viejitos beloved by their Daughters and Sons; cherished by Granddaughters and Grandsons. One and all these were good men who were fine men, men who brought forth the Great Walled City Chi Ismachi that was known as the place Beside the White Whisker Tree of the Sun and named after the White Mimosa Tree and Old Men-Mamaxel-the Grandfathers that thrived there under the nurturing warmth and light of the Sun. Ismachi spoken of as the White Whiskers of the Old Man-Mam with his Long White Beard of Flowery White Whiskers. There was only Three Great Houses-Nim Ja that came forth from this finely finished Mountain Place known as Chi Ismachi. There was not yet the Twenty- Four Great Houses because at the time there were only Three Great Houses-Oxibʼ ri Nim Ja that were there at Chi Ismachi. There was Xa Jun-Just One-Xa Jun Nim Ja-Just One Noble House; Just One Long House of the Noble Lords; Just One Great House of the Kaweqibʼ; Kaweq Winaq; Kaweq Amaqʼ.

Kaweq Winaq, Kaweq Amaqʼ; Kaweq People, Kaweq Pueblo Kaweq is a name that has a great variety of etymological possibilities that all come into play in the many opinions as to what the name Kaweq actually means; a name that means many different things to many scholars. Nevertheless, none of those scholars involved in the study of Popol Wuj has brought forth a definitive definition and understanding of the signification of this ʼobscureʼ and ʼadornedʼ name. Again, the ʼPeople Adornment or the Adorned Peopleʼ is another folk etymology that was given as an answer to my insistence to find the ʼmeaningʼ behind this name so once again realize my desire to understand how the Traditionalist Maya understand the names of their ancestorsʼ Popol Wuj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And this is why I prefer not to add to the confusion by leaving this perfectly beautiful Maya-Mesoamerican name Kaweq to remain as it is and untranslated. While bringing forth an understanding of the name Kaweqa of this most important name of the principal lineage of the Kʼicheʼ lineages in an effort to bring out everything I have found with regard and with respect to this ancient ancestral Kʼicheʼ Maya name with the intent and purpose to bring to out some of the irony in which this name is ʼadornedʼ which ironically is what ʼkaweqaʼ signifies as ʼadornmentʼ in the sense of ʼaddingʼ on to ʼrenewʼ or ʼembellishʼ a sacred image or effigy such as a Kabʼawil that is adorned and embellished with special dress and adornment of those who are his or her Tzuqul, Kʼool; Providers, Sustainers.

To speak in specific terms there is a ritual known as ʼweqa Mamʼ the dressing or adornment of the image of the ʼOld Manʼ known as the Mam; the Ancestor. The adornment of the Mam comes on the evening of the day before he will be seated on his throne to rule the following year as the Year-bearer or Mam. ʼKaweqa Mamʼ is ʼtheir adorning of the Mamʼ which seems to be a fine beginning to the understanding of this name of the Kaweq lineage; after all the ʼadornment and dressingʼ of the Divine Ancestors is one of the principal themes that runs through the Popol Wuj. For those of us interested in etymology the name Kaweq is a name that speaks to the day name Kawoq, the nineteenth day name of the Chol Qʼij or Sacred Count of Days in which Kawoq signifies storm, thunder, and lightening which makes a great deal of sense since the Kabʼawil of the Kaweq is Tojil.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
But the Kaweq are a People who may well come from the Kanekʼ or Kan Ekʼ or Black Serpent People of the Northern Lowlands of the Gulf of Mexico, la Laguna de Términos, and the Yucatan Peninsula. The Kaweq may well be connected etymologically to the Qʼeqʼchi or Black Faced People who are the neighbors of the Kʼicheʼ in Alta and Baja Vera Paz as well as the Petén and Belize and this is exactly the area where Xibʼalbʼa is so this may also be a root to the understanding of the name Kaweq. It is important to read the work of Ruud van Akkeren Xibʼalbʼa y El Nacimiento del Nuevo Sol provides his reader with a complete understanding of the Kaweq. According to van Akkeren the Kaweq lineage spoken of her are connected through salt and the trade routes of salt to the Kanekʼ Winaq; Kanekʼ People. The etymology of the name Kanekʼ as Kan Ekʼ or Qʼan Ekʼ the Bright Star, Shining Star of Venus that transforms into Morning and Evening Star which makes for another interesting understanding of the Kaweq as a People of the Great Star that is the planet Venus: Raxal Chʼumil. The Popol Wuj is bound deeply to the Star-Planet giving us good reason to the think of the Kaweq as the People of the Planet Venus. As stated above kaweq could also, and easily, signify ʼthe Adorned Onesʼ since the Kaweq are those who adorn-kaweq-the wood-worked puppet people to defeat the Pueblos at Jaqawitz. And since this narrative makes a ʼgreat dealʼ of the ʼadornment-embellishment- ornamentationʼ of the Puppet People and Wood-worked Beings or Poy-Ajam Cheʼ at Jaqawitz then I am inclined to think of the Kaweq as those whose magical use of adornment bring about the world of the Maize People; Ixim Winaq.

This is a people who see the changes and transformation of the maize place as the adornment of their Maize Deity. He must be well dressed and well-adorned when it comes time for the Maize Deityʼs flowering and pollination, when he must dance in the breeze with the birds and the bees and dance in the wind to bring about an abundance of sustenance.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Kaweq then are those who adorn the Maize Lord, Jun Junajpu son of Xpiyakok, when he ʼsprouts forthʼ from the tortoise shell carapace of the surface of the Earth. Remember Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej ʼxkiweq-they adornedʼ the ʼface-imageʼ of their dead Fathers Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu beside the Pusbʼal Chaaj just as the Ancestor, Mam, is ʼdressed and adornedʼ in the town of Santiago Atitlan during Holy Week to ʼrenewʼ the Face of the Earth.

The Kaweq Maya are a people who adorn, dress, decorate, and ornament their Ancestors who reciprocate with rain and wind; clouds and warmth to cause the Face of the Earth to be renewed with a new set of clothes while being bejeweled with blossoming embellishment and blooming adornment. This is the new green growth that dresses and adorns the Face of the Earth; la Milpa and its Maize Deity who was taken infinite forms and shapes as the ʼoneʼ divinity come back to life to carry out his-her lifecycle as the many ʼgood-looking, well-builtʼ young man.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: The Kaweq are ʼthose who adorn the ancestorsʼ as least that is the way I have come to think of them as a people concerned with ritual and its need for embellishment. Just like the words written here; the beautiful words, images, and metaphors of the Ojer Tzij that adorn and embellish our lives with their majesty and magnificence. The Kaweq are the primary lineage of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq spoken of here in Popol Wuj and it appears that they are tied to the Yucatan Peninsula and the Gulf Coast of Mexico where they have gone to their place of origin to bring back their symbols and signs of authority and rule from Lord Quetzalcoatl known as Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl of Tollan known here as Nakxitl who scholars tell us was the founder of Mayapan and reestablished the sacred city of Tula Tollan by the divine turquoise waters of the Great Cenote Itzaj known as Chi Chen Itza which means Beside-Chi the Cenote-Chen of the Itzaj; perhaps known as the sacred place ʼBeside the Water-Chaqʼa Jaʼ of the completely parched limestone shelf of the Yucatan where water is stored beneath the Earth. Yucatan where the deity known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja gave the world the name Hurricane which is a kind of Storm that Tojil is said to form beside the water. Let us begin this section again now that we have faced the difficulty of providing you, dear reader, with an understanding of the name Kaweq and its possible meaning and place of origin beside the water where the Olmeca-Xicalanca People developed beside the water in the Tabasco-Campeche area of the Gulf of Mexico. Olmeca; Rubber People and Xicalanca; Gourd Head People known as the Tzuy-Wa who migrated up into the Highlands of Chiapas and Guatemala to mix with the Mountain People who are the Kʼicheʼ speaking people who had always existed in the Mountain Place and Canyon Country spoken of here as where the First Mothers of Engendered Sons are said to have come from in this ancestral quest to discover the original tree from which oneʼs lineage branched off from to become the Kaweq People of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Kaweq were most probably the primary community of the three Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw or Kʼicheʼ Maya Noble Scribal Lords who organize the transcription of the original painted and written hieroglyphic codex-style hieroglyphic version of the Ojer Tzij we now know as Popol Wuj, the Book of Council that is translated and interpreted here.

Let us move on as we appear to step into a much more ʼhistoricalʼ telling of the Ojer Tzij as the Ancient Word becomes an apparently Historical Account of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ by making ʼfactualʼ sorts of statements in its story-telling prose as you will soon see is written out here by the Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw lineage of Maya Scribes known as the Chuch-Qajaw Ojer Tzij; Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account. Nevertheless, this may just be as ʼmythicʼ a ʼhistoryʼ ever is as it is written by the Kaweq Lineage who wish to be seen by Castilian King Filipe el Segundo who is ʼKing of the Worldʼ when the Popol Wuj was written which reflects the concerted effort to participate in the Castilian Empire of Philip II as the Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom-Kʼicheʼ AjAwarem.

Here begins the Kʼicheʼ Myth of Grandeur with which to prove their worth of ʼincalculable, immeasurableʼ importance as allies of the Castilian King Philip II as they had always been for the Great Lord Quetzalcoatl: Nim Ajaw Nakxit Qʼuqʼkumatz Rajawal AjRelebʼal Qʼij Tolan Tzuy-Wa.

Here begins the narrative that seeks to bind the Ancestral Past of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ with the present moment of the Castilian Conquest and Settlements of Dominican and Franciscan Orders among the Highland and Lowland Maya in the ʼNew Worldʼ of ʼNew Spainʼ. This the New World into which the Kʼicheʼ Maya Scribes want to make their presence known by telling of their glorious past that was an epic past that was a heroic past. That past is what lead up to what was then the present day of the 1550ʼs when the Ojer Tzij of Popol Wuj was written.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It is vital to remember this particular Ojer Tzij of Popol Wuj was written by Kʼicheʼ Maya Scribes who were trained and educated by Dominican Friars that lived with the Kʼicheʼ Maya in el Quicheʼ during this most pivotal point in history that is threshold across which we can cross on bridge created by the Popol Wuj and its ability to connect the Ancestral Kʼicheʼ Past as the Before and the After of the Kʼicheʼ Descendants Future.

This is it; this is the bridge across which to connect us with the origins of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. This is the written word that binds the thriving Indigenous World of Kʼicheʼ Maya Descendants of today with its thriving Indigenous World of the Kʼicheʼ Maya of their Ancestral Past. Let us begin again with the Maya Scribes telling of the Three Great House of the Nim Ja Kaweqib!

There was only Three Great Houses-Oxibʼ ri Nim Ja that came out of this place known as Chi Ismachi. There was not yet the Twenty-Four Great House because at this time there were only Three Great Houses-Oxibʼ ri Nim Ja that were there at Chi Ismachi. There was Just One Great House-Xa Jun Nim Ja; Just One Nobel Abode- Just One Palacio de los Señores Kaweqibʼ those who are known as the Kaweq People, the Kaweq Pueblo; Kaweq Winaq; Kaweq Amaqʼ. Just One Great House-Xa Jun Nima Ja existed there at Chi Ismachiʼ of the ʼPeople of the Great Houseʼ or Nima Jayibʼ or ʼGreat House Peopleʼ as they are known: Nijaʼibʼabʼ or Nima Jaʼibʼabʼ ʼPeople of the Great House, Pueblo of the Great Houseʼ as they are known. There was Just One Great House of the Lord Kʼicheʼ People-Xa Jun Nim Ja Ajaw Kʼicheʼ; Ajaw Kʼicheʼ Winaq-Lord Kʼicheʼ People. These were a true Great House People: Nim Ja Winaq; Lord Kʼicheʼ People as they are known: Ajaw Kʼicheʼ as they are known with Xa Jun Nim Ja Ajaw Kʼicheʼ.

There were two Great House People that embraced one another there. These Two Great Houses lived there embraced one another there as two together-xa kaʼibʼ kumatzil-just two wrapped around one-an-other; just two enveloped one another there-xa kaʼibʼ kumatzil-just two embraced one another at Chi Ismachi;

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
these Two Great Houses were intertwined with one another there Beside the White Mimosa Tree; the White Beard of the Ancient Ones; the Old Ones; ri Mamaxel Chi Ismachi.

As you known only to well this is the Mimosa hostilis the bright white flower of the White Beard of the Sun; White Head; White Skull of the Sun-Saq Ismachi Qʼij; Saq Awi Qʼij; Saq Ajolom Qʼij; Great Grandfather of the White Bearded Sun; the White Mimosa Tree who bears a most sacred substance in its roots that was once imbibed by warriors who suckled its essence before battle to become fearless of Death by being shown where they would go upon dying to this world to then enter into the Paradise of the Sun with its hummingbirds, butterflies, and flowers on Flower Mountain; the Primordial Flower Paradise of the Sun.

There were two groups in town that were made one when they were there at Chi Ismachi. Their hearts were made ʼOne, Only One-Jun, Xa Junʼ through their happy harmonious; quiet contented lives they lived with one another there at Chi Ismachi and this made them Just One; Xa Jun with the other as it is said: ʼJust One was their Heart-Xa Jun Kikʼuxʼ with one-an-other so that they lived in great contentment-kikotik; kikikʼux. Bitterness was not part of their life for evil-doing played no part of their way of life; their Rulers lived out ʼsweet hearted-kiʼ kikʼuxʼ ways of being and becoming peaceful Noble Lords; they were just all around ʼGood Styled, Good Waysʼ People: Utzilaj Winaq.

No fighting went on there either, nor were there quarrels; there were no up- risings; nor were there revolts. Chi Ismachi was just a peaceful harmonious place of balance and accord where calm contentment reined among the kind and content People of a very harmonious sort of tranquillo Pueblo-Xa Saq; Xa Amaqʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Xa Saq; Xa Amaqʼ; Harmony and Embrace This was the precious way of life for those of Chi Ismachi who lived as a contented Pueblo woven together as a sacred reed mat of interwoven ways of being and becoming a people who were said to embrace one another as ʼserpentsʼ so that they were a Pueblo of People who were enveloped together-kumatzil-a Pueblo of People that embraced one another as in the word kumatzil which is mythic metaphor that invokes the embrace of Lord Quetzalcoatl as the noble foundation of the Pueblo who lived together as an interwoven-kumatzil-intertwined People who lived together as one braided and bound to another as a sacred bundle of like-minded People who were a kind-hearted People that existed as unified People that lived as a united Pueblo. Chi Ismachi is a Mountain Citadel thought of as a Precious People-Saq Winaq created a Perfect Pueblo-Saq Amaqʼ who were a People and a Pueblo that was completely enveloped with one another in an ancestral embrace spoken of as being of just one heart-xa jun kikʼux.

Chi Ismachi then was made-up of flourishing People that formed and shaped themselves into a prosperous Pueblo who lived together as a Perfect Precious People that was a Calm Contented People who lived with one another as a Happy Harmonious Pueblo known as Xa Saq; Xa Amaqʼ. And as the precious sort of perfect kind of sweet-hearted Pueblo it was; the Pueblo of Chi Ismachi lived in a peaceful sense of perfection because of its type of tranquil tolerant People; just a calm quiet composed People; just as happy and harmonious as a Pueblo could be that was made of kind considerate caring People:

Xa Saq, Xa Amaqʼ! Xa saq, xa amaqʼ kʼo chi kikʼux; Xa Saq, Xa Amaqʼ!

They just shared one contented heart; they just shared one contented soul as One Ancestral Pueblo formed and shaped from One Ancestral People that were known to live together as a Perfect Peaceful People who lived as ʼone heartʼ in a Happy Harmonious Pueblo that was spoken of as: Xa Saq, Xa Amaqʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Only light, only warmth was what was in the hearts of the Pueblo who lived as a People intent on forming and shaping a Pueblo with a communal heart formed from the ancestral soul of peace and contentment; and shaped from the ancestral heart of ancestral remembrance. Truly, these were people who lived in peace; those who lived together here lived gathered together in harmony and accord with one another as a Pueblo filled with People who showed care and concern for themselves as a Pueblo by showing kind, caring consideration for their People.

There was no evil-eyed sorcery; no ill-willed malicious maneuverings- majabʼi moxwachinik; no jealousy; no resentment; no desire to take from another; nor were there any ʼleft-handedʼ ways of causing pain and suffering for the daughters and sons of the Mother-Fathers of the Pueblo. There was no evil-eyed sorcery; no ill-willed malicious maneuverings- majabʼi moxwachinik; no jealousy; no resentment; no desire to take from another; nor were there any ʼleft-handedʼ ways of causing pain and suffering for the daughters and sons of the Mother-Fathers of the Pueblo. No rage, no burning red-faced anger; majabʼi kaqa wachinik; no ugly angry mean-hearted ways were ever expressed amongst the bright-minded People of that light-hearted Pueblo.

The power of those who lived there remained a small power; they never became a Pueblo of great strength or dominance; they were never seen as being empowered and important enough to cause others to take notice; and, because of this they never grew proud; nor were they arrogant in their ways. They were a modest people who lived peaceful, contented lives. And this is the way they lived for a long time there on their Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj-Mountain-Plain surrounding Chi Ismachi. This all took place at and upon their Mountain Place-pa Juyubʼal. But that was not how their lives would remain; at least for not much longer; a new warrior way of being was coming their direction that would end the perfectly peaceful harmonious ways of Chi Ismachi.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Chi Ismachi: Precious Tree; Perfect Tree; Tree of Flower Mountain Ancestral Tree of the Old Men-Mamaxel; Flourishing Wealth; Flowering Abundance Chi Ismachi, it was just like a low-lying sprawled out tree full of white fluffy flowers that were visited by hummingbirds, honey-bees, butterflies, and tiny stingless bees who lived the good-life suckling nectar from the heart of the blossoms and the blooms while forming and shaping a happy hive with the pollen collected from the bright white beard-like flowers that look like tiny brooms. This is the Precious Tree; the Perfect Tree; Xa Saq-Xa Amaqʼ. This Ancestral Tree was the very image of contentment and abundance that was achieved by gathering-up the sweet harvest of great quantities of golden flower dust known as pollen- puqbʼal cheʼ to then effortlessly transform it into sweet tasting honey and soft molten wax with which to form the ʼnestsʼ from which the next generation of bees would be deposited to grow in order to become many.

This was the bright life lived on Flower Mountain of Chi Ismachi where the Sun brought forth the good-life on the Face of the Earth in the form of white beard-like flowers to provided the bees with pollen to sustain the next generation with the wax to craft the hive to create the honey to provide and sustain the Great Mother and Matriarch of the hive who ʼburst forth-poqʼol with many replacements-kʼexel who grew and grew into many, many descendants of the original face of the Ancestral Bee.

This was the way of the precious perfection of Chi Ismachi where the Tribe that was the Hive lived in peace and harmony. This was the very embodiment of the ancestral image of the perfect life that was naturally found in the perfect ways of nature that were found to be known and beloved by the People of the Pueblos here on the Face of the Earth.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is what one looked for when looking for the beauty and perfection of a harmonious community that hummed harmoniously and buzzed busily while singing along as song of contentment harvesting in order to transform the natural abundance that was sought to be suckled on Flower Mountain where lived those Perfectly Peaceful People in the Precious Prosperous Pueblo of Chi Ismachi. This was that Place; those were these People who formed and shaped this Pueblo of Chi Ismachi; Xa Saq, Xa Amaqʼ.

So if harmony and balance were to be found anywhere in the land it was found in the peaceful perfection of the people that formed and transformed the natural balance and harmony that existed amongst this Pueblo that grew thick with the natural abundance of the wealth and riches that came flowering and fruiting from the many flourishing trees of this flowering Forest where the birds and bees lived in perfect peace and precious harmony.

The contentment they enjoyed when they lived on their Mountain Place where ancestral perfection was sown to sprout forth as the peaceful ways of the People that led to the harmonious ways of the Pueblo would soon be nothing more than a longing for the good-life in their remembrance of the past.

This is why Chi Ismachi was known as an Utzilaj Juyubʼ; Ulaj Juyubʼ which was a most Bountiful Mountain; a most Inhabitable Forested Wilderness.

These were those of little strength and no power; they were those who were not admired by others; those who were yet to be strong and powerful. But then a new way of being was brought forth; a new way of acting came into the land that was known as strengthening oneself up in order to harden oneself up as warriors; warriors who decided to ʼgrip their shield in their fistʼ to take war to those who had more.

This fisting of the shield that was a gripping of the shield was so these warriors at Chi Ismachi could ʼwield their shieldʼ like never before which is one way to say: that those who were once weak were those who know wished to wage war.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This taking up the shield to wield it on the field of battle was something very new to the Kʼicheʼ world where war had always been practiced as a form of defense where as now ʼto wield the shieldʼ was to pursue capturing other for sacrifice and slavery. This all begins at Chi Ismachi.

This was the way of war that entered there amongst those of Chi Ismachi; a once peaceful People that was a peaceful Pueblo who were a People; a Pueblo that would never be the same again.

This warrior way of life was the new warrior way of living life. And this warrior way of living life that was a life lived like a warrior would eventually change the way of living life for all those People that lived their lives as a Pueblo that would now come to live life as warriors there on their Mountain Place in their Mountain Citadel known and named Chi Ismachi.

Ilokabʼ: False-Face People Their ancestral ways of life would be transformed by those known as the Ilokabʼ who while out looking for honey ended up looking for trouble like all honey hunter always do when out looking to take something from another that was not theirs to take.

So that the trouble they went looking for was the trouble they found; so that the trouble they found was the trouble they would confront in conflict that was waged in battles in wars that wars created from nothing more than self-aggrandizing rulers wanting to be greater than ever before. This is the story of the self-magnifying rulers of the Ilokʼabʼ who were ʼhoney-huntersʼ or ʼilol kabʼ who went out looking for trouble.

It wasnʼt long before the lives of those living Chi Ismachi were lived in a place thick with trouble brought about because of the warrior ways instigated by those honey hunting Ilokabʼ People of the Ilokabʼ Pueblo: the Honey Hunters who lived their lives as warriors who hunted the abundance created and crafted by others that they saw was theirs for the taking.

These were those who thought nothing of harvesting what others had gathered through suffering and sacrifice to be taken by hunters and gathers who had become warriors who raided and pillaged the wealth of others.
