body:
It would be their warrior ways that began to change the lives of all those People who had lived lives of peace and tranquility; in Pueblos formed and shaped on the principals of balance and harmony.

Those peaceful ways of living and those tranquil lives they had lived had now come to the end as those of Chi Ismachi began showing their strength and power through their dominion and rule over all those people and pueblos that lived around them.

This then was when they tested as they tried their hand at the warriorʼs art of taking-up the shield there at Chi Ismachi: xkikowisaj pokobʼ chiriʼ Chi Ismachi. This was when they tested their warrior skill and ability of ʼwielding the shieldʼ to harden themselves before all the other Pueblos to then show their supremacy and superiority in the art of war.

So that the life of the Pueblo would be changed and transformed like never ever before to become the life of the People that was lived in constant and continuous war. It didnʼt take long for those of Chi Ismachi to grow so strong that they no longer had to yield to others either in the forest or out on the field especially before those who had no idea how to ʼwield the shieldʼ on or off the battlefield.

And so it was that they found themselves to be excellent warriors who excelled at the art of war by entering the violent and vicious field of battle by practicing what was known as palming the shield-pokobʼaxik to quickly make their rivals submit to their powerful and punishing warrior ways of making war with its bows and arrows; spears and shields.

And so it was that where the other Kʼicheʼ People of the other Kʼicheʼ Pueblos saw opportunities for creating more abundance and opportunity by expanding out into ʼfertile mountainʼ where they dedicated themselves to produce more prosperity and abundance the Ilokabʼ could only see opportunities for taking the abundance and prosperity of others through the art of wielding the shield that was their way of making war.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Flowery Fields of the Flowery Wars Their proving grounds were right there on the flowery fields of the flowery wars were there was ample opportunity to test their sovereign strength and warring ways of wielding the shield as this way of war was known in those days.

This was the wielding of war-shields that were inlayed with serrated obsidian blades that transformed the defensive shield into mythic monsters from ages long past that allowed the warrior to shred and thrash their way through the enemy on both sides by swiping and slicing; grating and grinding their way through the battlefield like a jaguar and puma; hawk and eagle whoʼs fangs and claws; beak and talons shredded as they thrashed their way through the battlegrounds leaving their rivals torn to pieces; ripped limb from limb; to be dismembered in the most mythic of all ancestral ways of destroying the enemy to bring about their defeat and destruction; death and demise.

It is ʼas ifʼ the end of the Age of the Wooden People had come back to haunt their descendants as we reach the end of this mythohistorical epic of Blowgunning Hunters who transform into Warlords whose obsidian blade knives now turn on their enemy to draw blood to provide and sustain sacred sustenance for their Kabʼawil like never before...

There at Chi Ismachiʼ their magical way of combat was that they ʼwield their shieldʼ on the battlefield to prove their strength to everyone who watch them fight that was taken as a sign and symbol of their nawal powers inherent to noble rule- kajawarem that manifest their ancestral authority-tepewal to ʼLord-it-Overʼ on others as sovereign-tepewal warlords who were ruler-ajawarem warriors of Chi Ismachi.

This was when the Kʼiche Lords showed their power-qʼaqʼal to dominate those they ruled with their superior genius and cunning supremacy that came with their newly won powers of governance and leadership.

Those newly won powers were manifest by their physical dominion over the other Pueblos through their magical nawal powers and their sovereign authority as their total rule as Noble Lords was now expressed in the grandeur of their rulership-nimal ajawarem.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This aggrandizement of their rulership was about to be experienced by all those Mountain People; Mountain Pueblos who surrounded the Kʼicheʼ of Chi Ismachi.

It was then that the Mountain People of the Mountain Pueblos who lived in their Mountain Places-Pa Juyubʼal and Canyon Country-Pa Siwan were about to feel the power and strength of the sovereign rule and authority of these indomitable Kʼiche Warlords who were well prepared to bring what was theirs in life to fruition.

Their time had come for the Kʼicheʼ Warlords and War Captains to lead their vassal warriors into battle by taking up their bows and arrows; spears and shields in order to go to war like never before.

When this was seen by the Ilokabʼ was when the Ilokabʼ began their war, for it was they who now wished to wage war on their enemy.

They wished only to defeat those of Chi Ismachi by killing their Lord known as Noble Sweat House: Kʼotuja; Kʼo Tuj Jaʼ.

They wanted to have an ally help them do their work of finishing off this one Noble Lord of Chi Ismachi known as Ajaw Kʼotuja: Lord Noble Sweat House.

This was when they began causing disruption to create dissent in order to take over the realm they wished to govern and wanted to command to satisfy their insatiable hunger for total rule through their indomitable will for power and control.

And so it was that the Ilokabʼ decided to assassinate Ajaw Kʼotuja of the Nijaʼibʼabʼ through the help of a Noble Lord of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ named Istayul just because they, the Nijaʼibʼabʼ the lineage of the Great House People, Great House Pueblo were practicing the ʼart of warʼ known as ʼpalming the shieldʼ that was their ʼway of doing battleʼ known as ʼfisting the shieldʼ that was the ʼwar- making-wayʼ of those who came to ʼwield the shieldʼ who were those of Chi Ismachi: xkikowisaj pokobʼ chiri Chi Ismachi.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They wanted just One Lord-xa Jun Ajaw to come over to their side; they wished to ally themselves with One Noble Lord and this Jun Ajaw was Ajaw Iztayol or Iztak Yolot or White Heart, Bright Heart, or perhaps, something like: Precious Heart; Perfect Heart. It was the Ilokabʼ who tried their best to convince Ajaw Iztayol to kill Ajaw Kʼotuja-Lord Sweathouse for them; for the Ilokabʼ were those who only wished death for Ajaw Kʼotuja of the Great House People of the Nijaʼibʼabʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq.

They wanted to teach Ajaw Iztayol how to kill; the Ilokabʼ wished to show Ajaw Iztayol how to slay; how to assassinate the One Lord-Jun Ajaw they envied most; the One Lord-Jun Ajaw who had created so much in his life.

Ajaw Kʼotuja; Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja was the One Lord-Jun Ajaw who had brought forth a powerful and productive realm, that others now wished to take for their own by killing this One Lord who built it with his peaceful People who lived as a harmonious Pueblo that lived a Sacred Life; a Precious sort of Perfect Blessed Life: Xa Saq; Xa Amaqʼ pa Saq Kʼaslem.

But this plan of the Ilokabʼ to rule over the rest of the Kʼicheʼ by killing Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja-Noble Lord Sweat House did not turn out as it was first imagined; as it was first intended. No, it was not like that; the murder of Lord Sweat House-Ajaw Kʼotuja did not turn out as it was planned.

Their plan indeed ended in failure; their plan ended in reversal; because their plan ended in the death and defeat of those who wished the death and defeat of another.

The Ilokabʼ were destroyed by their own deceptive; destructive left-handed ways; for the deceit and deception of Ilokabʼ sorcery ʼfellʼ on those who rose-up again Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja. And so it was that the Noble Lord Sweat House-Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja who the Lords of the Ilokabʼ wished to murder did not die; for he was not killed; he survived their attempt to finish him off. It was just later on when that happened; it was later on that he; Lord Sweatbath House-Ajaw Kʼotuja was killed by the Ilokabʼ, but not at first; at first they could not slay him; for the plans they made to bring about his demise could not be realized.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They, the assassins did not kill Ajaw Kʼotuja; he was not assassinated by the Ilokabʼ who at first tried to bring about his death and disappearance.

And so it was that the Ilokabʼ could not do what they wished to do; they failed to kill Ajaw Kʼotuja even though they made every effort to do so; they could not do so because he was much too much for them to bring down; Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja was a strong and powerful Kʼicheʼ Lord.

And thus began the quarrels-yujuj-struggles; the disturbances-chʼakimal-the uprisings; the wars-labʼal-the battles. They entered by force and attacked the first town; the conquering warriors-ajlabʼal; assassins-kamisanel who attacked and then invaded their Great House Citadel-Tinamit to conquer those who lived there, the Great House People-Nijaʼibʼabʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq the People; the Pueblo of Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja- the People of Lord Sweathouse.

What the Ilokabʼ wanted was to annihilate the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, they just wanted to wipe them out, one and all. This is what the Ilokabʼ wanted; the Ilokabʼ

wanted to defeat and destroy those who lived all around them to capture and enslave them. This what the Ilokabʼ wanted but it did not work out this way. What they, the Ilokabʼ wanted was to rule by themselves; that was what they wanted, that is what they bore in their hearts, that is what they willed for themselves and their remembrance; and it was just because of their desire to rule the land that they invaded the lands of those they wished to rule by killing the Kʼicheʼ Winaq-the Kʼicheʼ People.

But it was they who were killed; for it was they who came to die; it was they who were taken prisoner-xetelechexik to be kept as captives; to be kept as slaves- xekanabʼix. In the end it was the Ilokabʼ who ended up being killed-xeʼulkʼamoq; it was they who were captured-xetelechexik; it was they who were enslaved-xekanabʼix.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is what their destiny was. That which they wished for others is what they were made to endure which was to be taken captive to then be enslaved; to be taken as the fruits of war to be offered up as gifts of sacrifice on the altars of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ. This is what the Ilokabʼ brought upon themselves for want what was not theirs.

Those warriors who came to kill the Kʼicheʼ Lords and make prisoners of their Kʼicheʼ subjects and vassals were those who were taken captive and made prisoners to be humiliated and then sacrificed as they wished to do to the Kʼicheʼ Winaq.

Few were saved; fewer still survived; those who wished death for others were those who ended up amongst the dead.

This was when their sacrifice began. They just laid them out to then open them up; the Ilokabʼ became the sacred sustenance of the Kabʼawil of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq.

The Sacrificial Priests, the Sacrificers of Sacred Sustenance known as the AjKʼixibʼ, AjKajbʼ sacrificed them; they lay them down to then slay them to then flay them; the Providers-Tzuqul, the Sustainers-Kʼool were blessed with the providence and sustenance to provide and sustain those who were there to be provided for and sustained by those known and named AjKʼixbʼ; AjKʼajbʼ.

The Ilokabʼ were made to pay their debt-tojbʼal with their own flesh; with their own blood for the sin; for the transgression; for the offence; for the wrongdoing committed against Ajaw Kʼotuja; he the Noble Lord; he who is known as Lord Noble Sweat House as he is named: Ajaw Kʼotuja; Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja.

They were made to be slaves as soon as they came in; they became subjected vassals once they came in to give themselves up; when they saw they were defeated and were sure to die they came before the Noble Kʼicheʼ Warlords to deliver themselves up. It was then that they became subjects of the Noble Lords who received them there as their enslaved subjects; the vanquished vassals. For it was the Ilokabʼ who were enslaved; they were made serfs just as they were made subjugated slaves by those who they wished to defeat and destroy; to capture and enslave; to take prisoners in war to sacrifice to their Kabʼawil.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Because after all, it was they, the Ilokabʼ who waged war against the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords; Kʼicheʼ Lord to who they-the Ilokabʼ-became slaves; serfs; subjects; and vassals who were enslaved for the rest of their days as those who labored and worked for their Kʼicheʼ Lords; Kʼicheʼ Lords to whom they were enslaved forever more as subjects; as vassals; as slaves who came to know nothing but sweat and toil.

The Ilokʼabʼ created conflict with those of the Canyon Country; for it was they who invaded the lands of the Kʼicheʼ Territory driven by the desire to conquer the Kʼicheʼ Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblos of the Kʼicheʼ Canyons; where they attacked the Kʼicheʼ Towns there in the Kʼicheʼ Ravines; just as the assaulted the Kʼicheʼ Citadels with their Kʼicheʼ Villages that lay within the palisade walls of Kʼicheʼ Strongholds where there were Kʼicheʼ People living as part of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblos: chirij Ajaw, chirij Siwan, chirij Tinamit. What the Ilokabʼ wanted was to have annihilated in order to have eradicated and eliminated the Kʼicheʼ Lords-Kajawal Kʼicheʼ; this is what came from their heart; what came from heart was their desire to be supreme; their drive to be superior over the rest was the root, the origin of their own death and destruction.

What they wanted was to end their noble reign; the noble reign of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq. What the Ilokabʼ wanted was to end the power and authority of the Lords of Chi Ismachiʼ; this is what the Ilokabʼ wanted for the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ.

But, it did not happen that way, no, it most certainly did not. What happened next was the opposite of what they had planned when the Ilokabʼ initiated what they could never have imagined was about to begin; and what was about to begin was the reversal of the destiny of the people and pueblo known as the Ilokabʼ; the reversal of their Noble Lordʼs ambitions when what was began had finally begun. This was when the War of the Shields began; this was the beginning of the conflict known as the Pokobʼ Labʼal-War of the Shields.

This then was when it began; the beginning of the sacrificial payment of the sacrificial debt created by the ever so clever and cunning: Ilokabʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Now is when it began; the sacrifice of their subjects; the sacrifice of their vassals of the Ilokabʼ before the divinity of their enemy who were the Kabʼawil of the Kʼicheʼ; it was they who were provided for with the sacred sustenance that came from the Ilokabʼ coming into give themselves up; just as it was they; the Kabʼawil who were sustained and supported by the vassals and subjects known as the daughters-al and the sons-kʼajol of the Ilokabʼ.

The Kabʼawil of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ were fed with sacred sustenance that came from the hearts and blood of those who were deceivers, liars, and cheats known and named Ilokabʼ.

The subjects, the vassals of the Ilokabʼ were sacrificed before the Kabʼawil of the Kʼicheʼ there in the towns and villages of Chi Ismachi; this was the outcome of the War of the Shields: Pokobʼ Labʼal.

This then was the origin of their defensive preparation against invasion; the rulers of Chi Ismachi began their protective shielding of their towns as a result of the War of the Shields. For this was when they began building barricades as protective palisades to shelter and shield their villages from imminent invasion.

And so too began their construction of the barrier that stood as the defenses of their great walled cityʼs fortifications; fortifications that they formed and shaped from timber stakes, split log posts and wood planks.

This was the very root of Kʼicheʼ Lords project of the forming of fortifications and the shaping of the shield that surrounded the stronghold of Chi Ismachiʼ where the power-qʼaqʼal-authority and noble rule-tepewal-divine sovereignty of these Kʼicheʼ Lords began to show itself in every way.

What became of Chi Ismachi was truly great in the way it developed into a mighty strategic center, for it was extraordinary the way it became empowered like never before with the further empowerment-qʼaqʼal of Kʼicheʼ Lords and their Noble Rule and that Noble Ruleʼs Rulership-Ajawarem over the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom- Ajawarem.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Everything they did was the cause of further grandeur and greatness; dominion and dominance; superiority and supremacy of the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo. So that everything they brought to fruition was further cause of the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼiche Pueblo to prosper and prevail in order to know and experience the blessing and bestowal of abundance so that they came alive to thrive like never before.

Everything that came their way was the cause for even further satisfaction and contentment founded in the power and authority that was theirs to rule as Sovereign Lords of the People and Pueblos; as Noble Lords who only had thoughts of care and concern for their creative People and productive Pueblo. It was only through pain and suffering that they became truly powerful and invincible rulers known as Nawal Ajaw who appeared before all as the Nawal Magicians they came to be; for truly the gratification they felt for all they received was quickly transformed into gifts of sacrifice; offering of sacred sustenance to pay the debt they always acknowledged as gifts from the Divine Ancestors who had gone before to open the way to the wealth and success that was theirs to receive to then give away.

It was only because others wanted defeat, death, and destruction for them that they became stronger, more intelligent, more imaginative, and much more ingenious than their enemy who focused only on the death, defeat, and downfall of their enemy instead of the forming and shaping of a better life in a more fruitful place. Those who wanted only death and destruction for them were repaid as was the way of those who placed themselves as obstacles on the path of the Nawal Ajawabʼ Kʼicheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
But they did not die; they were not dead; they were not destroyed; they were not defeated; nobody brought about their downfall and so it was that they became superior kinds of Nawal Ancestors whose supremacy over all others was no longer in question; no longer was their superiority in doubt for the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ who were the Lord Kʼicheʼ now ruled and reigned supreme over all other People; all other Pueblos of all the Territories; of all the Lands; of all the Realms: the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ where the most powerful and precious of all those who were found anywhere around.

There no longer were those who were able to humble and humiliate them now. There was no longer a conquering force that could enter there where they were to cause them trouble; for no longer could anybody invade their mountain top citadel. And so it was that their reign and rule over all the other Pueblos was now complete.

And so it was with the Kʼicheʼ Maya Lords of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ People; Ajaw Kʼicheʼ Pueblo was nothing that came to them that was not the cause of further grandeur and greatness for them as a people; there was nothing that came to them that did not make them a more powerful Pueblo; for there was nothing that did not caused their rule and rulership to become even more magnificent; even more extraordinary than before because every ordeal they were made to face became an opportunity for them to further the power and glory there on the Face of the Earth. Therefore, there wasnʼt anything that came towards or against them that wasnʼt reason enough to cause them to create more power and superiority to do all that they were called to do to bring their destiny to fruition by knowing what was theirs to bear as their sacred burden amongst the many People and Pueblos in the Mountain Places and Canyon Country that they were now about to bring into their very own dominion and reign known as el Reino Kʼicheʼ; Ajawarem Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Kʼicheʼ Lordsʼ ability to rule as powerful sovereigns and noble rulers was already there at the beginning; their destiny to become great warlords who were strong leaders was already there at Chi Ismachi; it took root there for it was sown there by the Mamaxel-the Old Men of Chi Ismachi the Mountain of White Mimosa Flower; the Flower Mountain of White Mimosa Trees: Saq Ismachi. And the power of their Kabʼawil grew in step with their ascendency to power and rule; and, so too the Noble Lordsʼ responsibility to both their People as the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo and their Kabʼawil as guide and protector of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords and their People; their Pueblo.

In this way the Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ strengthened more and more as the Sovereign Rulers of the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo-Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ who became stronger and stronger as they provided and sustained one another more and more to grow and grow to become stronger and stronger. The worship and adoration that was received by the Kabʼawil was given as the sacred sustenance that was provided by their keepers; by their sustainers, the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords who kept and sustained their Kabʼawil there through ritual sacrifice-chiri xnimar wi ukʼixik Kabʼawil.

The Kabʼawil of the Kʼicheʼ received the sacred sustenance of sacrifice that was theirs to receive as the gifts of sacrifice that provided and sustained them as the Providers and Sustainers-Tzuqul, Kʼool of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ. And so it was that the power and strength of the Kabʼawil grew and grew as their ability to provide and sustain their daughters and sons; vassals and subjects with all they needed to grow and grow as the Tzuqul, Kʼool-Providers; Sustainers of the Kabʼawil of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords-Nim Ajawabʼ Kʼicheʼ.

This caused fear among all the Tribes, all the Pueblos; ronojel Amaqʼ. The Small Tribes, the Great Tribes-Chʼuti Amaqʼ, Nima Amaqʼ-the Small Pueblos, the Great Pueblos were terrified as they watched them enter; when they watched the entrance of the captives of sacrifice; those known and named: ʼTeleche Winaq; Captive Peopleʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Pueblos were terrified as they looked on; terrified as they watched the captives being led by the Kʼicheʼ warlords and warriors into the plaza to be left before the temple upon which they would be sacrificed; those captured, those bound for sacrifice; these were those who were sacrificed as sacrificial gifts exchanged for the power and rule; dominance and control bestowed upon the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords known and named Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja; Ajaw Kʼotuja and Ajaw Iztayol.

Tepewal; Qʼaqʼal Only they, the Noble Lords, enjoyed the right of conquest-ki tepewal which was the right of subjugation. This was the ʼdominion-qʼaqʼalʼ that was the ʼpower-qʼaqʼalʼ of the Noble Lord and Ruler Ajaw Kʼotuja and Noble Lord and Ruler Ajaw Iztayol together with the Great House People; Nijaʼibʼabʼ and the Lord Kʼicheʼ People; Ajaw Kʼicheʼ in all their majesty and supremacy they now experienced as those who had conquered those who had tried and failed to conquer them.

Ajaw Kʼo Tuj Ja and Ajaw Iztak Yolot of the Nim Jaʼibʼabʼ and Ajaw Kʼicheʼ were those who brought about the great reversal so that it was now clear they were Nawal Ajawal; truly they spoke and acted as Nawal Winaq in ways that manifest their power and capacity to reverse destiny and the power and rule behind those who wanted only defeat, death, and demise for them. But it was not this way because it did not turn out the way their enemy had planned their plan of death for them Ajaw Kʼotuja; Ajaw Iztayol of the Nijaʼib and Ajaw Kʼicheʼ.

There were only three family lineages-xa ox chʼobʼ chi Tinamit xkʼoje-that were there at the town Chi Ismachi where the Ismachi Tree, White Mimosa grew like an Old Manʼs Beard; White Whiskers of the Ancient One, the Mam, the Ancestor.

Chi Ismachi was the Ancestorsʼ fortified town, just as it was the Ancient Oneʼs citadel that was the seat of authority and throne of power of the Old White- Haired Whiskered Ones who founded this ancestral city of these three Kʼicheʼ lineages amongst the Ismachi Trees.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Chi Ismachi: Hummingbird Son of the Sun Chi Ismachi the White Whiskers of Old Man-the Old Man in the Sky-the Old Man the Grandfather Sun, Mamaxel; the Ancient One who opens and closes the flowers and leaves of this Ismachi; White Mimosa tree with the light; with the heat of the Sunʼs vitality and strength.

Chi Ismachi this is the Old Manʼs tree with the power to open and close the leaves and flowers of the Tree who communicates with the Sun; the Sun who enchants the hummingbirds, bees, wasps, ants, butterflies, birds, and insects of all kinds.

Chi Ismachi this is the place of vitality and growth of pollen, the honey, the nectar, the flowers, pods, seeds, potent potential of the essence of growth and reproduction of the lineage of the line of the ancestors and descendants and their eternal return with no end; no beginning; just white flowers; sacred flowers.

Chi Ismachi is the place where the flowers call in the hummingbird to perform his playful work of fertilizing the flowers dripping wet with nectar that flows from the flower as the essence of natures power to replicate in order to re-make and re-create itself through the celestial movement of the Sun that opens the flowers at dawn to begin the pull and flow of nature and its power to bring about the sprouting of the shoot and the blossoming of the bloom. This is the place: Chi Ismachi. Chi Ismachi this is this mythic metaphorical place of the Ancient Ancestors of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ; this is the place of remembrance and recollection of the ancient beauty of the past and the knowing there is always the next Mountain Place to conquer and settle like Chi Ismachi. Chi Ismachi; Beside the White-Beard Tree that is the Nawal of the Sun just as he opens the way to the flowering flow of the eternal play of destiny. This the sacred place of the Old Man known as the Mam and Old Men Mamaxel who the next generation came before his here at Chi Ismachi to open their road to their destiny as is the work and the way of the Mam; the Ancestor who is Lord of the Road; Lord of the Way; Lord of the Eternal Play; Lord of the Dawn of Day.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
So there began their feast in honor of their daughters-kimial who they asked to be married well. This is the way the tribes came together as one in the Three Familial Lineages; the Three Great Houses-Oxibʼ Nima Ja.

So there they drank their sweet drink-kukaj wi kukyaʼ where they received their sustenance; these were just gifts given to them for the gifts they made of their sisters; the gifts of their daughters.

It was just happiness that reigned in their hearts when they did it; when they feasted, when they gathered together to share their abundance at the banquets there in the Great Houses when they said:

“It is just a symbol of our gratitude; just a sign of our thankfulness for our children; our descendants known as our sign, our spark-qetal, qatzijel; retal qatzij the soul; the symbol; the emblem; the mark of our word, of our life; just a sign, just a symbol as it is said in our ancestral tradition the flame, the fire that has passed on to our descendants who are our replacements.” “May this be a blessing for their marrying as our daughters, as our sons who shall be named for their status and entitled for their stature as positioned members of the sacred order of Our People; of Our Pueblo,” they said at the feasts that were the marriages of their daughters and their sons; their vassals and their subjects; subjects and vassals of the Noble Realm of the Noble Lords of the Three Great Houses braided together as One at the Stronghold Citadel City of Chi Ismachi.

Just by naming alone and in its power of entitlement were they able to designate one from the other; when they made distinctions as to who was who amongst those of the Pueblos; it was just through naming only that deference was made amongst one another through the power came with the status and position of noble entitlement: xkʼobʼwi uloq.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This was the naming of the Seven Pueblos-Wukʼ Amaqʼ; these were the allied towns, the allied villages: “Let us marry together, let us make alliances together. We who are the lineage allies; we who are ancestral companions: we the Kaweqibʼ, we the Nijaʼibʼ, we the Lord Kʼiche; Ajaw Kʼicheʼ” they said, the Three Principal Lineages-Oxibʼ Chinamit, the Three Great Houses-Oxibʼ Nima Ja.

This is the way they lived for a long time there at Chi Ismachi. They lived this way together for many generations, until they sought out another livable; inhabitable; hospitable mountain upon which to establish another peaceful harmonious town; another well protected walled citadel; another Tinamit that was a contented place to live the good life; another fortified palisade mountain top village. When they found their mountain to live on they established a town there.

This was when they abandoned Chi Ismachi leaving it deserted. This was when they deserted Chi Ismachi leaving it abandoned. They just pulled themselves up and left Chi Ismachi. And so the Kʼicheʼ Lords rose up from where they were to arrive at the Citadel City of Qʼumaraq Aaj; it was there where they came to be when they arrived at the town of Qʼumaraq Aaj.

Qʼumaraq Aaj: Rotten Cane; Decayed Cane; Decomposed Cane This is the place known in the Kʼicheʼ language as Qʼumaraq Aaj; spoken of as Rotten Cane; Decayed Cane; Decomposed Cane; a sign, a symbol of the End of an Era; a Fallen Sun; a Buried Cane that is a Dried-up, Dried-out Cane the Nawal of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom; the Nawal of the Kʼicheʼ Rulers who never died dead; who never disappeared forever for their Replacements are here in the Face of the Kʼicheʼ Rulers of the Kʼicheʼ Villages, Towns, and Cities that are all ruled by Kʼicheʼ Rulers. Qʼumaraq Aaj known as Rotten Cane once translated as Broken Cane which is a name rooted in this epoch ending name that signifies the end of the Noble Kʼicheʼ reign of this Kʼicheʼ Highlands Mountain Citadel known for a long, long time as el Quicheʼ the Principle City; Capital City of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom; el Reino Kʼicheʼ as it is named: Qʼumaraq Aaj or Qʼumar Kaaj-Dried-Up, Dried-Out Desiccated Cane thus the name of Rotten Cane.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is a name that might as well be known as the Disintegrated Cane; Decomposed Cane; Decayed Cane that turns to Dust when returned to the Ground to become Soil once again; to become the Dirt of the Earth from which will arise the sprouting out of the shoot of the sprout of the sown seed planted in the Earth.

Qʼumaraq Aaj was where the fire of Tojil was ʼput-outʼ when it was extinguished by the Tlaxcalteca allies so that the Castilian Conquistadors could then ignite the power that was the fire embodied in the Sun Face Lord of the Castilians Adelantado Don Pedro de Alvarado know as Kinich Ajaw Tonatiuh or the Sun-faced Lord Tonatiuh; the Sun Lord of the Castilians and their Tlaxcalteca and Cuauhquechollan allies.

This is the Dawning of the New Sun that reigns over the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom with it Noble Rulers and Regal Leaders of the Kʼicheʼ People of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo that lasts until 1992 when begin a twenty year period of change of rule and authority in all the many Indigenous Villages, Towns, and Cities of Highlands and Lowlands Guatemala. In the Year of 2012 known as Oxlajuj Baqtun; Thirteen Baqtun the New Sun of the Kʼicheʼ rose again to inaugurate the installation and investiture of a New Era of a New Sun that returned the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom once again to the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo after Five Hundred Years of violent subjugation and de facto slavery all of which has come to an end.

This newly won freedom of the Maya Guatemala created the possibility for the uncompromised writing this Translation and Interpretation of the Popol Wuj in the Highlands of Guatemala on the very boundary line of el Reino Kʼicheʼ to the West, to the North, and to the Northeast; el Reino Kaqchikel to the East and Southeast; and, el Reino Tzʼutujil to the South towards el Lago Atitlán and beyond to their cacao groves of the Boca Costa and Costa Sur. This Translation and Interpretation was written where the original Popol Wuj was transcribed from the Painted Lienzos of Ancestral Mapas of Pictorial Mythopoetic History.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Qʼumaraq Aaj was one of the many places I returned to time and again to ignite the fires of my imagination in my quest to bring out the spell of the Sacred Landscape that one feels inhabits the mythic words and mythic metaphors that form and shape this Mythohistorical Religious Text. Letʼs go it is time we walk on to the end.

So these are the names of the Lords of the Kʼicheʼ who arrived there at Qʼumaraq Aaj, the Lords names there are: Ajaw Kʼotujaʼ and Ajaw Qʼuqʼ Kumatz.

This is the Noble Lord of the Kʼicheʼ known as Qʼuqʼkumatz the one known as Lord Quetzalcoatl of the Kaweq.

The Kʼicheʼ arrived there at their new home with the other Noble Lords- Ajaw-Chiefs and Rulers of the Mountain Tribes; Mountain Pueblos: Juyubʼal Amaqʼ. They arrived there together in their new home of Qʼumaraq Aaj: Broken- down Cane; Dried-up; Dried-out Cane.

Qʼumaraq Aaj:

Rotten Cane of Maize, Decomposing Dried out Cane Death of the Lifecycle of Maize Annunciation of the Eternal Return Call for the Emerald Green Earth of Rebirth Call for the Turquoise Blue Water of Renewal Summons of the Jade Green Feathers of Quetzal Summons of the Lovely Blue Cotinga Plumage Imagine your life that is lived as one with the sacred milpa whose sacred seed has been passed down to you to sow and grow; tend and defend to then harvest in order to select and protect as the sacred seed of the sacred sustenance of your divine lineage. This is the seed of maize that you will seed at the Sowing at the four corners and four sides of your milpa that will be brought to life through the ritual fire known as the Dawning.

The Sowing and the Dawning will happen within twenty days of one another once you along with all the other Men and Boys have cleared and cleaned to then burn before sowing your familyʼs seed. If you are a women reading this in our contemporary age known that Kʼicheʼ Women often did all of this work in the Milpa in the Horticultural Age of Ixmuqane when women tended the milpa while the Men were off hunting or off trading your surplus in distant markets.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The idea that maize is the work of men is found here in Popol Wuj while remembering Ixmuqane is the Great Mother who ʼdeifiesʼ maize to then chose which is seed is planted where. The Maize People are Mother-Father; Chuch-Qajaw People of a extraordinarily ʼtransgenderʼ culture that defines Male and Female roles to then live beyond boundaries of definition. This is important to know. These seed will be harvested to feed those who must be fed so your work is not just work; your work is a lifecycle that will lead to your victorious harvest of abundance or your defeat that leads to your death and demise. So this lifecycle of maize that is told in the sacred mythic- history of your people; your pueblo is of vast importance to you because you know your people; your pueblo will only live for Thirteen Generation when it break-down to be bent low after drying up as a People to die out as Pueblo.

But now you must sow the seed of your Divine Ancestors whose very teeth and skulls you plant in the earth in order that they sprout out with life. Then once the milpa is perfectly prepared its seeds are sown in ʼhandfuls of fiveʼ of ʼLord Fiveʼ ʼGreat Starʼ ʼVenusʼ known as the Lord of Five Days. Then once the seeds are sown begin the watching and waiting for the sprouts to shoot up through the earth as the many, many sprouts that you will tend in your milpa; sprouts that you look upon as the Four-Hundred Boys-Jobʼ Much Kʼajolabʼ or Five Eighty Sons- Omuch Kʼajolabʼ and it is they who will provide your body and blood with abundance while sustaining your heart and soul with meaning and pride for the existence you lead on the Face of the Earth-Uwach Ulew.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This milpa of yours is not just maize plants growing in a field. This milpa of yours is the manifestation of your body and soul come to life on the Face of the Earth beneath the benevolent gave of the Heart of the Sky and the Three forms of Lightening-Thunder known as the Call of Rain-Kaqulja: Jun Raqan-Nabʼey Kaqulja; Chʼipi Ukabʼ Kaqulja; Raxa Rox Kaqulja. This is the story that is coming to its climax with the annunciation that we are headed off to Qʼumaraq Aaj. This is massively important announcement because it says: ʼwe are coming to the inevitable end to this lifecycle of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq and their Sacred Sustenance-Ixim-Awex-Abʼix.

Once the seeds are sown and the sprouts sprout out then begin the Days and Nights of continuous sheltering and protecting of the Milpa-Abʼix for the Milpa cannot be abandoned ever because it must be tended of weeds and defended from the birds, animals, and the elements, while praying for the perfect sustenance of warmth and light from dawn to dusk; mist and dew from dusk to dawn.

The milpa grows and grows as the rain pours and pours while the sun shines to warms the supple cane body of these bisexual corn plants: female cane and male heads. The cane mother of maize must fill out as the maize plants grow thick to then begin to tassel up and out as two ʼgood-lookingʼ handsome young menʼ who are soon to be adorned with the splendid crown headdress crest that sways in the breeze.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Then the Milpa goes hyper-sexual as the nascent heads of maize-ʼxpax ochʼ break-out for all the maize in the milpa has just ʼbroken-openʼ from the body of the cane. The long golden hairs begin flowing forth to soon be dusted by the gold dust of this mythic maize deity- ballplayer. Once these heads grow on these strong good-looking canes the corn silk flows from these growing heads of the Hero Twins Jun Ajaw known here as Junajpu and his twin Yax Bʼalam spoken of here as IxBʼalamkej. These heads of maize of the Hero Twins fill out and thicken as the canes harden and the tassels begin drying back after releasing all their pollen. It is then that the Boys, the Sons, the Twins are visited by their allies: the wasps and ants, hummingbirds, bees and breeze to pollinate the flowers of the corn silk and corn tassels as the insects ascend and descend; descend and ascend to pollinate every corn silk with the pollen from the headdress tassel of Maize Deity who dances in the wind while overcoming ordeals night and day in order to bring forth the flowering and fruition of five seeds in which each seed will give two heads of eight hundred seeds to create 1,600 kernels in a bunch of five canes with the potential of producing 8,000 replacements.

This is why maize is seen as a Magical Transforming Ancestor-a Nawal Winaq capable of truly miraculous transformation. But it takes a tremendous amount of care and concern by those workers of the milpa who truly love their maize as the very sons and daughters of a very ancient line of ancestors...These is the story told here that is coming to the end at Rotten Cane- Qʼumaraq Aaj-Broken-Down; Bent Over Cane This miraculous plant known as a maize growing in a milpa awex, abʼix, and awan has not been mentioned except in metaphorical ways and then one can say this is what the entire Popol Wuj talks about in its own ingenious way. It is difficult for us moderns to understand that maize was the very soul of Maya life in a life that was understood as the way of maize.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Now we have come to the end of that life cycle of Maize that has come to be Rotten Cane that is the drying desiccating kind of drying where the termites to turn the maize cane into tiny cane pellets of maize dust that become one with the dirt and dust; grit and grind of the cane that becomes the earthen soil it came from and shall return to rise as a sprout again and again. It makes sense. It makes sense to title the last citadel of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Sacred History Dried- Up, Dying-Out Cane that is Decomposing, Decaying where the end of a People comes with the end of the Lifecycle of Maize in a People who see themselves as Maize Plants and their Pueblo as a perfectly formed and shaped Milpa with its Four Corners; Four Sides. The Ancient Maya Myth-makers knew just how to bring out the ʼMythic Metaphor of the Maize Peopleʼ in this ingenious indigenous work of sacred literature. The end is coming, from the sowing and rooting to the drying and dying; decomposing and decaying we have come to the end of the lifecycle of maize for the cane is drying out to fall apart into dust.

The ancestral narratives of Popol Wuj were once played out here and with some active imagination this sacred space comes to life. Qʼumaraq Aj, Qʼumaraq Aaj is known as Rotten Cane in English which it is but it is a drying up and a drying out that comes to cane at the end of their lifecycle before being buried in the earth or burned into ash to feed the soul of the earth, to feed the soil of the earth with ash into which seed may be sown or space be opened up for new cane to sprout forth.

This is the essence of the naming of the name Qʼumaraq Aj. In this place of Qʼumaraq Aaj the Kʼicheʼ Maya Day-keepers, Diviners, Seers, and Knowers threw their seeds and beans on their divining tables-mesas to count out, divine, see, and know just exactly how the end of their age would come to end. To then see what would be the essence of the New Sun and its newly formed and shaped people would be made.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The name Qʼumaraq Aaj also speaks of all the Carrizo Cane that surrounds this citadel that itself is surrounded by a rounded ravine that is a deep, deep barranco that encircles this Citadel of Qʼumaraq Aaj where this Carrizo Cane burst forth to grow and grow until it falls over itself to then begin rotting to by drying-up to then dry-out before turning to dust; thus the name: Rotten Cane-Qʼumaraq Aj. The place we are moving to now to end this recitation and revelation of the Ojer Tzij-Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

The end of the lifecycle came to this Sacred Site of Qʼumaraq Aj with its destruction and demise; decomposition and decay in the Sixteenth Century with the construction of the New Age New Sun of Christianoil during the times of Word of God that was built in Santa Cruz del Kʼicheʼ where the Sacred Maize Plant became the Holy Cross and Junajpu became Jesukristo while Ixbʼalamkej became Thomas-Didymus the Patron Saint of Chichicastenango celebrated on December 21sth the Solstice when the Dawning of the Sun is celebrated before the harvest of the current years maize can be taken up.

The Maya took in the Catholic Saints and Martyrs; Mothers and Virgins to then transform them into Maya Santos who transformed as Nawales always do and that is perhaps why the Popol Wuj died out over a long period of assimilation. It only makes sense that the Ojer Tzij of Popol Wuj should come back to life today as the Kʼicheʼ Maya move towards radical decolonization of their Traditional Maya World and its Mythic Figures that seeks to rid itself of ʼKaxlanʼ influences in often severe and even militant ways.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
After all the Kaxlan were quite severe in their destruction of the Maya World during the five centuries that followed the Conquest and Colonization of the Kʼicheʼ Maya world especially when it came to Citadels like Qʼumaraq Aj whenever cut stone was needed to provide for a Catholic construction or provide for a State building project. Little by little the original stone was hauled away to build in Santa Cruz del Quicheʼ until today when Qʼumaraq Aaj or Qʼumaraq Aj has almost no stone except in its magnificent ballcourt that is exceedingly well preserved. But no matter what the situation is with stone or no stone this once decayed and decomposed citadel has come back to life in the most astonishing and awe-inspiring ways with visitors arriving everyday of the year to perform ritual upon its altars or in its cave of Xibʼalbʼa; or, simply to take young and old Maya and Mestizo adults and children on an adventure of initiation to the very center of the Kʼicheʼ Maya world before the arrival of the Kaxlan Winaq.

Today Qʼumaraq Aaj has been reborn as one of the major ritual centers of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Pueblo. The Temple of Tojil and Awilix in particular now known as Templos but spoken of here in Popol Wuj as the God House of Tojil-Rochoch Kabʼawil Tojil; the God House of Kabʼawil Awilix-Rochoch Awilix, the Ballcourt-Jom, and the Cave Path into the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa still exist. These sacred spaces continue to exist as places of divine exchange and ritual communication between the Ancestors and their Descendants; the Contented Living and the Grateful Dead. As we approach the end of that story it is important you know it is to this sacred space that is a real physical place that we are moving in this myth that is becoming more and more grounded in physical realities like this Ancient Kʼicheʼ Citadel known as Qʼumaraq Aj.

So there at Qʼumaraq Aaj the Lords and Rulers known as: Ajaw Kʼotuja; Lord Sweatbath and Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz; Lord Quetzalcoatl are recognized as the Fifth Generational Change of Rulers-X-Ro-Kʼexoq-X-Ro- Leʼa which is the fifth dynastic change of generational rule by:

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Those born in the light, as the Daughters of the Dawn; Saqil Al Those begotten in the light, Sons of the Sun; Saqil Kʼajol Those of the First Four Mother-Fathers at Tulan Tzuy-Wa The Fifth Generational Change of Rulers; Xrokʼexoq; Xroleʼa These were those known as the Daughters; the Sons; Ixoq Al; Achij Al Those who were born in the perfection of the light; uxeʼ Saq, Those who were begotten at the origin of the Pueblo; uxe Amaqʼ Those who were born as the origin of human existence; uxe Kʼaslem, Those of the peopling; populating of the Face of the Earth; uxeʼ Winaqirem Xrokʼexoq; Xroleʼa uxeʼ saq, uxe amaqʼ uxe kʼaslem, uxe winaqirem

This is the Fifth Generation of People; Ro leʼa Winaq who were the Noble Lord Rulers: Nim Ajaw; Nawal Ajaw; Nawal Winaq From the beginning of the Light; Uxeʼ Saq From the sprouting forth of the Dawn; Uxeʼ Saq From the origin of the Pueblo; Uxeʼ Amaqʼ From the origin of the Peopling of the Pueblo; Uxe Kʼaslem, Winaqirem Uxe Saq, uxeʼ amaqʼ, uxeʼ kʼaslem, winaqirem This is their story; the story of those known as Kʼo Tuj Ja; Lord Sweathouse and Qʼuqʼkumatz, Quetzalcoatl.

These are the Noble Lords who come to build the Citadel of their ancestors and descendants the Citadel City known as Qʼumaraq Aaj.

It was there at Qʼumaraq Aaj that they built their Houses; Rochoch. And it was there too that they built their House of Divinity; Rochoch Kabʼawil. They arrived there; they established themselves within the natural defended Citadel; Qʼumaraq Aaj surrounded by a steep ravines where cane grew in abundance. Here in Rochoch Kabʼawil their Kabʼawil lived there in their House with his Nawal Priests; Ancestral Priests.

This is where their Kabʼawil lived with their AjKʼixbʼ, AjKajbʼ; the Kabʼawil lived with their Sacrificial Priests; those who performed human sacrifice lived in the House; Rochoch with their Kabʼawil.

The House of the Kabʼawil; Rochoch Kabʼawil were built at the heart of town; this is where they placed the House of the Kabʼawil: Rochoch Kabʼawil; they placed them at the center of the city. This was a naturally defended city with a steep ravine surrounding it on all sides where carrizo cane grew and thrived.

body: The Burning of Qʼumaraq Aj Qʼumaraq Aj or Qʼumaraq Aaj will be burnt just a Tula was burnt and Tenochtitlan and Teotihuacan were burnt to the ground just as Tula was burnt when Quetzalcoatl threw himself on his funeral pyre to transform his life through his immolation in his Nagual form as ʼOne Cane- Jun Aj-Ce Acatl-Jun Aajʼ Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl will be burnt in order that the golden seed-shining star rises up into the sky, just as the golden seed of maize sprouts forth as a sprout to stand-up as a new green cane as the lifecycle of maize and humans mirror one another. Yet now Popol Wuj suggests that each Sun of each Age mirrors this cycle of rooting to rotting; sowing to burning the maize metaphor is maintained that begins in creation to move to destruction to be reborn in re-creation.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This is what Popol Wuj calls us towards in our own existence; day after day; year after year; life after life in a world of the Sky-Earth where we die to be reborn to grow and mature to flower and fruit to die back, decompose and decay to be burnt back in order to be sown again in perfectly prepared land upon which the axe and hoe and fire have cleared and cleaned it to begin the cycle again and again and again. The Lords of Kʼicheʼ will be burnt by the Spaniards who may well have asked how we shall finish off these Lords so they do not come back. The Old White Haired, White Whiskered Ones may well have told them to burn them and then grind their bones to then sprinkle them in the river. Oxibʼ Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi are known as the Last Lords of the Kʼicheʼ but that just is not so. Oxibʼ Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi like the Hero Twins just keep transforming themselves because they were and are Nawal Winaq whoʼs ancestral soul is an eternal fire, eternal spark, eternal ember, eternal heat of the Sun that cannot be extinguished as long as it is remembered through performing fire ceremonies as the Maya continue to do every day of the year. That is endless naming of the names of the days is exactly the same as the ancestral soul of the First Four Fathers being passed on as seed that contains the original spark of life within it that constitutes the eternal return of the Maize People. Death is the prerequisite for rebirth which is what this last section of this narration of Popol Wuj is doing its best to bring forth as it name the names of the lineage holders who will be replaced by their descendants just as Jun Junajpu past on his essence that he spat forth as the spitting image of him and his twin Wuqubʼ Junajpu to bring the sacred count of days to completion.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is what is happening here so heads up as we take this story to its inevitable ending to begin again. Just like Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej entering the Sky to be accompanied by the Four Hundred Boys which is to say: Junajpu becomes the Sun just as Ixbʼalamkej becomes the Moon of the Age of the Ixim Winaq who are embodied by the Four-Hundred Boys in the Southern Night Sky where the Two Cross Stand-up in the Night Sky surrounded by the Milky White Atole of the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds to provide and sustain the Nawales of the Sun and Moon with their sacred sustenance while that hang on their Santa Cruces of the Southern Cross and the False Cross where these Divine Twins await being sown again to begin the Sacred Lifecycle of the Sowing and Dawning again; Ewaxibʼal; Saqiribʼal. We have almost come full circle; is that not exciting. Because we have arrived at the Naming of the Names of the Lords of Kʼicheʼ at Qʼumaraq Aaj: Oxibʼ Kej; Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi.

So these are the Lords of the Kʼicheʼ at Qʼumaraq Aaj, the Lords names there are: Lord Ruler Ajaw Kʼotujaʼ and Lord Ruler Ajaw Qʼuqʼ Kumatz-Qʼukumatz-Quetzalcoatl. Those who arrived at Qʼumaraq Aaj-Rotten Cane, Dried Crushed Carrizo Cane Dust is the idea of the Ancient Name of the Last Town of the Ixim Winaq, the Maize Peopleʼs last home also known as Qʼumaraq Aj-Broken down Cane; Dry Cane turning to dust. This will be the end of the Maize Story, the Dry Cane, Rotten Cane turned to dust in Qʼumaraq Aaj is where the ancestral line of the Kʼicheʼ Maya who live in direct line to the First Four Fathers-First Four Mothers of Ixim Winaq is broken; the sacred lineage is broken at Broken Cane.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: This is the end of the line for Noble Ancestral Rule of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ at Dried out Cane. The Ojer Tzij as Ancestral Language of Popol Wuj will begin invoking a greater sense of loss until the end when the Last Lords of Kʼiche are burnt in Qʼumaraq Aaj which is a way of saying their ancestral soul will always return as ʼgood-looking, well builtʼ Young Men when Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are burnt upon the Stone Oven of Xibʼalbʼa. The Kʼicheʼ Maya are a strong people; they are an enduring people who continue to people and populate the Face of the Earth with their divine daughters and sacred sons. Soon Guatemala will elect an Indigenous President and more than likely she will be the replacement of IxMuqane. She would have already won had she not be ʼdisqualifiedʼ by the most corrupt government in the entire Americas in 2023 exactly 500 years after the conquest. The Doctrine of Christian Discovery and Domination are as much in place to control Indigenous America as they ever have been and this is we must all do our part to bring forth the change and transformation needed to live with dignity and integrity in this world, in our lifetime. Qʼumaraq Aaj; Qʼumar Kaaj or Rotten Carrizo Cane is the perfect this naturally defended citadel because it is surrounded by a ravine of broken down and rotting Carrizo Cane, thus Rotten Cane, the name of the place even before there was a beautiful little capital city of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom: Qʼumaraq Aaj, first came the name of the Place then the name of the City. This is the way of place names among the Kʼicheʼ in which the Place is named after a natural aspect first to then become the name of a built town or walled city so that the original ʼnaturalʼ sense of the space maintains an archetypal effect on the built city. This was the cane-aaj the Kʼicheʼ build their turkey coops-kok as well as waddle and daub mud and cane houses-xlabʼ ja. The carrizo cane was split to be used in basketry as well as many different constructions for gourd and squash and bean trellises.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The carrizo cane that surrounded Qʼumaraq Aaj did indeed become extraordinarily dry and brittle which made it unbelievably flammable. The ravine surrounding this Maya Citadel is said to have been burned to defend Qʼumaraq Aaj from attack which maybe how the town received its name from the ʼRotten Caneʼ.

The Kʼicheʼ used cane for arrows that flew straight and true. Cane flutes were fabricated from the cane to play the music that spoke secret sacred sort of ancient language known as tzijola. Carrizo cane was of vital importance to the Maya and continues to play a major role in agriculture to this day.

This is where their Kabʼawil lived with their AjKʼixbʼ, AjKajbʼ; the Kabʼawil lived with their Sacrificial Priests; those who performed human sacrifice lived in the House; Rochoch with their Kabʼawil. Here at the center of the citadel is where they came to the temple altar places where the Kabʼawil awaited them in their Houses-Rochoch to receive their sacred sustenance with which they were provided; with which they were sustained so that they grew in strength and valor. And so it was that their power to rule increased; their lordship, their rulership, it grew in size and strength. There they became many; the population grew thick; the city grew thick there with people as they, the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ grew and grew to become the great many People of this thickly populated Pueblo.

Because of this there were those who began thinking upon the Great Houses- Nim Ja and how they were organized; the way they the people were gathered together within them; and, the way they split apart when they became too many.

It was the way the Great Houses;-Nim Ja were created that caused the fighting that led to the warring between one another that originated in the organization of the Nim Ja-the Great Houses of Qʼumaraq Aaj.

The Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ became angry; they just became red- faced with envy; they became jealousy of one another because of the bride-price of their sisters and the bride-price of their daughters.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
No longer was there the great abundance that there once was for marriage feasts; feasts that once established and secured the alliances between the lineages.

No longer were there any ceremonial tamales known as tzaqon; the large ritual tamales that were eaten at their marriage banquets; no longer was there the ritual drinking of the ʼsacred waterʼ kukʼya to toast one another during the performance of ritual during their marriage celebrations of their chosen marriages; of their selected marriages that led to the forming and shaping of the familial alliance; the chinamit alliances.

This great lack of plenty was the root of their separating from one another; and so it was that those of Qʼumaraq Aaj separated again. For now they turned on one another using sorcery: just throwing the bones and skulls of the dead to ʼdisgrace the memoryʼ of the Ancestors; just evil-eyed sorcery was what they performed; it was by invoking their ancestral bones and skulls alone that they became skillful at performing witchcraft; again.

This was the way and means they fought one another causing more resentment and anger; causing more division and derision; disdain and disrespect to then create great distance between the traditional lineages that could no longer be held together as they once were.

Eventually they divided up into the Nine Lineages and even so they continued to enter into conflict with one another; quarreling constantly over their sisters; their daughters. Their constant quarreling and endless arguing put into question the decisions that they made with regard to their understanding of their rule and the formation of their power and authority.

And so it was that the Pueblos divided once again into the Twenty-Four Great Houses-Veinte-Cuatro Casas Grandes-Juwinaq Kajibʼ chi Nim Ja. These Great Houses-estas Casas Grandes-these Nim Ja that came to be there were those that made of those who had ʼcome forthʼ from ancestral times-xojeroq, for these Nim Ja were formed from those who had arrived at the citadel of Qʼumaraq Aaj long ago.

This was what completed the Twenty-Four Great Houses now as they were formed from those groups who were there for a long time.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so it was that the Twenty-Four Great Houses Juwinaq Kajibʼ Nima Ja pa Qʼumaraq Aaj were now complete.

So then they finished the naming of the Twenty-Four Great Houses here in the town of Qʼumaraq Aaj. It was blessed by the Señor Obispo, after it had been abandoned; it was a lost place that had been forsaken.

Qʼumaraq Aaj had become an abandoned place that was a deserted place that had become a forgotten place that was an altogether lost place that came to be known by those who abandoned it as a forsaken place; but it is not like this anymore; no, no Qʼumaraq Aaj is not an abandoned place as it once was when el Señor Obispo Francisco Marroquín came to bless it in 1539.

It was then at that point that the Dominicans began moving its cut-stones to build the near-by city of Santa Cruz del Quicheʼ where the Popol Wuj was written according to the last sentence of this Book of Council spoken of today as Popol Wuj yet seems to have been known to its original Maya Scribes as Ojer Tzij; Ancient Word; Ancestral Account written by the Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw right outside of Qʼumaraq Aj in the New Citadel named and know as Santa Cruz del Quicheʼ which is New City formed from ancient stones and shaped from ancient ways of molding and modeling a temple walls and plazas.

But Qʼumaraq Aaj was not always like that; it was not an abandoned place; a deserted sort of desolate place. It was there in Qʼumaraq Aaj that they the Kʼicheʼ once grew strong as a People; a powerful People; a strong and powerful Pueblo. This is then is an account of when and where the power of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ grew strong; when they enjoyed splendid thrones; where they had their order and place on their benches with their ceremonial cushions; truly this was a grand place with a fine palace; always clean; always well swept.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They had divided up into Great Houses according to their power; they divided up according to the dominion over others; each with their own rounded stone altar place, each with its fire, each with Noble Lords with his source of power, each of the Nima Ajawabʼ with their sovereign rule. Each of the Noble Lords; Noble Rulers; Ajawabʼ of the Nine Lineages of Qʼumaraq Aaj settled there among one another in the following way:

Nine Noble Lords of the Kaweq Nine Noble Lords of the Nijaʼibʼ

Four Noble Lords of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ

Two Noble Lords of the Saq Iqʼib-White Wind-Ajaw Saq Ik-White Moon These people grew to become a great multitude of people; thick with people was this populous, and many more were just the vassals, just the subjects that followed each of the Noble Lords. Thick with descendants were they, the people of the lineages; the peopled populous of the towns.

And so it was that a great many children were born as the engendered daughters and sons of the many Noble Lords there; these were begotten descendants of the many Noble Lords and their noble lineages. There were many there who followed the Great Lords there; many were those who lived as subjects and vassals of each of their respective Great Houses-Nim Ja.

And it was these vassals and these subjects who were the first among many, first among the many children that were engendered by them, the Noble Lords. These children were born to them; these were those children born to the Mothers of a Great House; and, many more were those that were children born of Fathers of a Great House.

So that it came to be that there was a great multitude of family members of each of the Noble Lords; truly there was a massive population that came to be there at Qʼumaraq Aaj. These were those who made-up the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ known as the Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ, these were the Subjects; the Vassals; the Daughters; the Sons who were engendered by to be born to the Kʼicheʼ Lords of the Great Houses; these were the Lords that ruled the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom that was now thick, thick; tzatz, tzatz with vassals and subjects of each of the Lords-Ajawabʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These are the Noble Lords and Rulers; Nim Ajawab-Noble Lords who ʼstoodʼ before the Great House of the Kaweqibʼ; these are those who ʼsatʼ upon the Pop that was the Ancestral Reed Mats of Noble Rule and Authority. These were the Woven Reed Mats of the Council House of the Noble Reed Mat: Popol Ja of the Nine Lords of the Kaweqibʼ each with their individual Great House placed all around the Council House of the Mat; Popol Ja of the Kaweqibʼ, each of which grew to give more fruit to become many more ʼfacesʼ of the Kaweqibʼ.

Naming of the Names:

Three Principal Lineages Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ So then next are named the Names of the Titles of the Noble Lords and Rulers before the Great House People; Ajawabʼ wa chuwach Nijaʼibʼabʼ these are the titles of the Noble Lords and Rulers before the NimaJayibʼabʼ-the Great House People, this then is their First Lord:

Ajaw Qʼalel: Lord Magistrate; Judge of the Word; He of Clear Vision Ajaw AjTzik Winaq: Speaker of the Word; Crier of the Word; Announcer Qʼalel Kʼaʼm Ja: Judge of the Reception House; War Captain; Magistrate Nima Kʼaʼm Ja: Noble Receiver of the Reception House Mat Uchuch Kʼaʼm Ja: Women Receiver of the Reception House Mat Nim Chʼokoj Nijaʼ ibʼ: Master of Ceremony of the Nija ibʼ, Speaker, Scribe, Performer; Master of Marriage Ceremony of Ritual Cacao; Mother-Father of the Ancient Word; Master of the Long Performance of Ritual Drama Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw Awilix: Chief Narrator of Awilix; Master of Ritual Performance of the Ceremony of Kabʼawil Awilix; Master of Ceremony Yakolatam uTzam Pop Saq Latol: Chief of Maintenance and Clearer of the Edges of the Roads; Cleaner of the Surroundings of the Citadel and the Roads entering and exiting the Citadel; He Opens the Road Nima Lolmet Yeoltux: Chief Tribute Collector; Chief Director of Tribute Labor; Labor Contractor and Organizer of Labor for Maintenance of Roads These then are the Nine Lords that stood before the Pueblo of the Nima Jayibʼab; these then are the Nine Principal Lords of the Great House People; Belejebʼ kʼut chi Ajawabʼ chuwach NimaJayibʼabʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These then next are the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ; these are the Names and Titles of the Lord Kʼicheʼ Lineage-Ajaw Kʼicheʼ the Pueblo known as the Lord Kʼicheʼ Lineage: Ajaw Kʼicheʼ Aj Tzik Winaq: Chief Speaker of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ; Crier of Summons Ajaw Lolmet: Lord Collector of Tribute of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ Ajaw Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw Kʼicheʼ: Lord Chief Master of Ceremonies, Lord Master of the Performance of Ritual Drama, Ritual Dance, and Ritual Recitation of Ojer Tzij; Lord Chief Master Scribe of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ

Ajaw Jaqawitz: Head Priest of the Kabʼawil Jaqawitz of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ Pueblo; Noble Lord Provider; Sustainer of Sacred Sustenance for Jaqawitz Kajibʼ Ajawabʼ chuwach Ajaw Kʼicheebʼ: These are the Four Noble Lords presented as rulers before the Lord Kʼicheʼ Lineage; Four Rulers of the Lord Kʼicheʼ Lineage Kajibʼ Ajawabʼ chuwach Ajaw Kʼicheebʼ: Four Great Houses of stone and mortar; post and beam; bundled and bound thatch roof; Four Great Houses set around the Center of Ciudadela; Four Crossroads of the Four Lords as the supreme authority before the Ajaw Kʼicheʼebʼ-Lord Kʼicheʼ People Kajibʼ Ajawabʼ Ajaw Kʼicheʼibʼ known as the Four Lords of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ People; Ajaw Kʼicheʼ Pueblo; Four Houses; Four Mothers; Four Fathers; Four Rulers of the Four Corners, Four Sides of the Kajib ʼAjaw Kʼicheebʼ: Perfectly Ordered Lords of a Perfectly Ordered Great House

And there are two lineages more, two towns more to add here:

Saq Iqʼibʼ Ajawabʼ: Lords of the White Wind House Saq Ikʼibʼ Ajawabʼ: Lords of the White Moon House Tzʼutuj Ja: Lords of the Maize Flower; Maize Tassel House Qʼalel Saq Ikʼ: Judge; Warlord; War Captain of the White Moon House There was just one Great House for these Two Lords. Xa Jun chi Nim Ja e kaʼibʼ chi AjAwabʼ.

Thus is completed the Naming of the Names of the Twenty-Four Lords; Twenty-Four Rulers-Juwinaq Kajibʼ chi Ajawabʼ and the Twenty-Four Great Houses-Juwinaq Kajibʼ Nim Ja of the Three Main Lineages and their Branches of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

Continuation of the Story of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It was then when increased the power-qʼaqʼal and majesty-tepewal of Kʼicheʼ sovereignty, when their noble rule and noble dominion increased. For it was their noble sovereignty that was theirs to increase in strength and importance amongst the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords as well as with their vassals and subjects who they guided and protected through their noble rule and its sovereign authority grounded in the autonomous rule embodied in the Great Houses-Nim Ja.

This was when they plastered their many houses and patios. They just went to work with their lime and cement plastering their houses; cementing the fines faces of their thin-walled ballcourts; and, finely finishing the refined façades of their temples all with a burnt lime mortar-chunaxik and white-wash-sajqabʼix.

It was with white-lime mortar and white-wash that the Great Houses finished their work of covering the walls and patios with bright white lime of all the towns and countryside constructions found out there in the canyon country. This is what was known as working on the entire kingdom by saying siwan; tinamit to mean canyon country-siwan and citadel town-tinamit as the elegance of ʼcountry and townʼ also known as ʼtown and country-pueblo y paisajeʼ is known still.

Truly grand, truly great were the many projects of construction that were commenced and completed with lime and mortar-cal y canto by these people known as the Great House Peoples of the Kʼicheʼ Maya Pueblo who built the Great Houses that were given their names. They all came forth as they all came together when they arrived there: the Small Tribes, the Big Tribes-Xul Chʼuti Amaqʼ, Nima Amaqʼ of the Kʼicheʼ and it is they who formed and shaped the strength-qʼaqʼal-majesty and the authority- tepewal-control of the Kʼicheʼ Lords.

The Kʼicheʼ Lords who together with the Small Tribes and Big Tribes would bring about the power-qʼaqʼal-might; sovereignty-tepewal-dominion of a Mountainous Realm of Canyon Country that the Lords and Vassals together would form and shape into a Kingdom of truly magnificent splendor.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
There was a Lord who increased the strength and sovereignty of the Kʼicheʼ. This was when they began the construction, the creation of Houses of the Kabʼawil of the Kʼicheʼ People by the Kʼicheʼ Lords who were those that constructed and created the Houses of their Deity-Rochoch Kabʼawil-Dwellings of Divinity was what these Stone and Plaster Temples were for the proper housing of the Kabʼawil. This is why they were built. They were built to house the Kabʼawil of the Kʼicheʼ.

They also built the Houses of the Lords-Kochoch Ajawabʼ but it wasnʼt they who built them; the Lords, they didnʼt do the work; they didnʼt make the houses they built themselves.

The reason they didnʼt build their Houses of the Lords-Rochoch Ajawabʼ was because of the great many descendants who were born to them who were their Daughters and their Sons. It was they who built the Houses of the Lords-Kochoch Ajawabʼ.

It was their Sons-Kikʼajol and Daughters-Kal who became their Subjects and Vassals who loved their Lords as a Son-Kʼajol loves his Mother; as a Daughter-Al loves her Father so did the Vassals and Subjects love their Lords; the Subjects and the Vassals; the Daughters and Sons loved their Lords as their beloved Fathers.

There was no need to bribe or beg them to do their work.

There was no need to steal them away and enslave them.

There was no need to knock them down, to then take them by force; the Lords did none of this to their People; for they, the People, were truly devoted vassals of their Noble Lord: Ajaw. And so it was that they belonged to one another just as the Lord belongs to the Vassal so the Vassal belongs to the Lord who in turn through the love and care for one-an-other so did they belong to their Kabʼawil and this is why they were happy to build their Houses.

This was when they worked together as a People of a Pueblo so that wherever there was one there was soon to be another.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so it was that many came forth who were their Older Brothers and many more who were their Younger Brothers; and it was they who gathered together in council with one another and took responsibility to attend to the petitions made by their Ajaw for that which was needed to be completed in the work of their building and construction.

For truly the Lords were well loved by their Vassals who treated their Lords with high regard and deep respect; for Lord and Vassal never lived in neglect of one-an-other. It was not like that they worked together to bring forth all they brought to fruition when they brought their work to completion.

Their day of birth of the Lords was the day of their Nawal; the Day of their Destiny that was of great concern to his Subjects; to his Vassals; his Daughters; his Sons. The day the Noble Ruler was born on was a day of celebration that was celebrated by both his vassals and the engendered sons born to him.

For the destiny of the Pueblo was embodied in the destiny of their Noble Lord and so it was that his children and his vassals alike took care to celebrate the sacred day of their Lords destiny; the Day of the Nawal of the Noble Lordʼs birth and its destiny was of tremendous importance to the Pueblo.

So then the people of the canyon grew and so then did the people of the towns grow with them: the Canyons-Siwan and Fortified Towns-Tenamit grew together to become the many dutiful daughters and devoted sons; faithful, obedient subjects; respectful vassals of the Lords who ruled the People.

It was the Lords who guided and protected their Pueblos who formed and shaped the many Tenamit-Citadels that protected the many Pueblos with their wooden fortification built around their Citadels-Tinamit in their Canyon Country- Siwan. These were Palisade Pueblos-Tinamit that existed in the Canyon Country- Siwan and Mountain Places-Juyubʼal. The Kʼicheʼ Winaq-Many Tree People peopled and populated themselves as a People; as a Pueblo in their Canyons and in their Strongholds.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so it was that they became a great many people living in the defensive citadels that constituted the fortified towns and made-up the many sheltered outposts yet there were many more others who lived in their ancestral Mountain Places-Juyubʼal as ancestral Mountain People-pa Juyubʼ.

For there were those Pueblos that existed who wished to live as their ancestors lived when they lived upon their Mountain Places-Pa Juyubʼal as Mountain People-Pa Juyubʼ.

Those mountain people of the mountain places didnʼt just come in to give themselves up to the noble word and noble way of the Noble Lords. No, the people of the mountains were not like that; they didnʼt just walk in to give themselves over to the sovereign rule of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ. It was not like that; not at all. It was not like that because there were plenty of people from plenty of pueblos of the canyons and towns that did not come in to be ruled by the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords.

And so it was that only through waging war with its conflict and conflict did the Canyon Country and their Protective Strongholds bend and then break before the power and might of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords and Warlords who where Nawal Winaq who were Nawal Ajaw.

A Sense of the Mountain People These were times when the leaders of pueblos and their vassal people were guided by dreams and protected by the voice of their Kabʼawil that spoke to them in order guide and protect one another through mutual support and shelter; with ways and words to inspire and encourage; through intuitions to lead towards power and lure away from danger; through dreams that came to warn and caution the guides and protectors of the people of the pueblos as they made their way over land, through the many pueblos found on the ways, and across the sacred landscape as well as in and out of the wilderness.
