source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And so it was the Kabʼawil were made content so the Lords of the Mountain and the Ukʼuʼx Kaj; Ukʼuʼx Ulew were made content to bring the rain and wind; warmth and sun; clouds and dew to make the Maize in the Milpa content.

And so the People of Maize of the Pueblo of Maize were made content with their great harvest nets filled with great loads of big heads of maize. With the harvest nets full the Noble Lords were made content and so they gave more and more sacrifice to their Kabʼawil in their Rochoch Kabʼawil. This is their story being told here.

They showed veneration to their Kabʼawil by invoking the ancient ancestral essence of stone that was the flesh of these Kabʼawil. The People worshipped them by naming their names and by doing so gave them praise and adoration.

They ʼKept the Daysʼ of their Divinatory Calendar and its ʼSacred Count-of- Daysʼ that told them what to do and say next to form and transform the lives of the People of the Pueblos through their Kabʼawil that was provided for and sustained in their Rochoch Kabʼawil, the House of their Deity. The People of Pueblos entered first in the Rochoch Tojil to burn offerings before Tojil; then they provided and sustained the AjPop and AjPop Kʼaʼma Ja through ritual sacrifice that was brought forth through the invocation, incantation, and enchantment brought about through the ancestral practice of Naming of Names of the Nawal Ancestors and Kabʼawil of those who were AjPop and AjPop Kʼaʼma Ja-the Noble Lords of the Council House of the Woven Reed Mat of Rule and Authority.

It was then that they came before the Noble Lords to give their quetzal feathers-kiqʼuqʼ which were their way of providing tribute before the Lord; it was he who they provided for and sustained as both AjPop and AjPop Kʼamja.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It was through nourishing and nurturing the Kabʼawil of Stone in the Stone House of the Kabʼawil that the Noble Lords of the Council House Mat were venerated as the Great Lords and Magical Transforming Ancestors that they were; those who were known as Nima Ajawabʼ; Nawal taq Winaq these were those whose names were those known as Great Lords-Nima Ajawabʼ who were those known and named as: Ajaw Qʼuqʼumatz; Kʼo Tuj Ja. It was they who through their nawal powers were able to change and transform the Face of the Earth for truly they were: Nima Ajawabʼ; Nawal taq Winaq.

Many towns were subjugated by these Great Lords that were Nawal taq Winaq, and it was they, the Nawal Winaq who were known and named as the Great Nawal Lords-Nim Nawal Ajaw: Nawal Ajaw ri Qʼuqʼumatz was one and the Nawal Lord Kʼo Tuj Ja was the other.

The two Nawal Ajaw known as Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj were another divine duo who were co-regents that ruled together as a pair of Noble Lords and Rulers who ruled ʼas ifʼ they were divine twins.

Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj were those who ruled as collaborative and cooperative companions to govern the People of the Pueblos of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Kʼiqʼab-Nabʼey; Kawisimaj-Ukabʼ First came the strength subjugation of Kʼiqʼab and his ʼstrong armʼ of conquest that opened the road for his complement who came to settle the land. This was he who was Kawisimaj with his ability to establish settlements on the land by planting milpa after clearing the mountainside and valley floor with the axe and hoe to then set fire to clean the earth of the many obstacles and obstruction for the proper seeding of the maize seeds that were sown in the rich forest soil and ash of cleared and cleaned land. It was Kawisimaj who came with his ʼsimaj-planting stickʼ with which he inseminated the earth with the sacred seed of the Ixim Winaq that sprouted forth as the descendant replacements-kʼexel of the ancestor whoʼs seed like ʼspittle-kʼexajʼ was just like that of Jun Junajpu. It was then that the tortoise shell earth sprouted forth with the milpa in the form and shape of all the many sprouts that came up and out of the ground. This is the story suggested but not told when the names of Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj are named.

It was these who were known as Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj that knew whether or not war was to be made; because everything was revealed before them clearly; they saw before them all that was to be seen; whether it was death; or, whether it was famine; or, whether they had go to battle in order to make war on another.

No matter what it was they knew what it would take place because they had a place to see it-Ilbʼal; there was a Council Book-Popol Wuj was its name.

This was their Book of Council that they consulted to know what needed to be done to bring their worked to completion by bring their lives to fruition through the seeing and knowing of the knowledge they looked for and found in their Book of Council that was their Council Book: Popol Wuj was its name.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They were not like any other Lord; for great was their essence; immense their nature; vast their character. What was theirs in life was their ability to fast; they fasted there for a long time in their ancestorsʼ sacred buildings; for truly sacred was their burden of fasting; sacred was their self-sacrifice that was carried out by them in their Sacred Temple; in their Sacred Realm; for their Powers of Creation; for their Power of Sovereignty: Loqʼbʼal Tzʼaq, Loqʼbʼal Ajawarem.

This was their ancient ancestral way of being in the world; this was their Nawal Way of becoming Nawal Ajaw through the change; through the transformation that comes through self- sacrifice that was their way of being and becoming Nawal Ajaw; Nawal Winaq in and upon the Face of the Earth-Uwach Ulew; there in and upon the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew.

For a long time they fasted when they humbled themselves; when they prostrate themselves before their Kabʼawil to suffer through self-sacrifice. They just punished themselves; they just gave sacrifice as penance; sacrifice as payment; sacrifice as tribute offered; tribute paid.

Xekʼajbʼik: they sacrificed themselves; they punished themselves; they brought themselves low to humble themselves before their Deity; their Kabʼawil.

And this then was their fast, 180 days they fasted and 180 days they prostrate themselves and burnt offerings-kekʼatonik-before their Kabʼawil.

This then was when they fasted there before their Kabʼawil for 260 days Oxlajuj Winaq; the Fast known as ʼThirteen Twenty-Oxlajuj Winaqʼ is the name of the Fast they fasted, Oxlajuj Winaq-Thirteen times Twenty days did they sacrifice themselves; they lay face down; they prostrate themselves while they sacrificed their burnt offerings; burnt offering of sacrifice that they burnt before Tojil; they burnt their sacred offerings there before their Kabʼawil Tojil.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Xa Munil-Only Fruit; Xa Tulul-Just Zapote; Xa AjAche-Just Matasanos; Xa Qʼinoom chikilo-Just Jocotes fruit did they suckle; they ate no sustenance molded and modeled from Maize; no Sacred Sustenance formed and shaped from ground maize did they take; just fruit was all they ate; that is all they took; they just suckled fruit. When they practiced sacrifice for Three-hundred and Forty days they humbled themselves through punishment-kʼajbʼik; though penance-kʼajbʼik; through blood-letting-kʼajbʼik sacrifice upon their altars of sacrifice before their Kabʼawil there in the House of their Deity-Rochoch ri Kabʼawil.

They did not eat for Three hundred and forty days-Wuk lajuj Winaq-just Seventeen times Twenty days did they prostrate themselves face-down before the Earth before the Sky. This was their fast known as Wuklaj-Seventeen, this is when they took it slow when they made their fast; this was when they did not eat anything but fruit; for the fast of Wuklaj-Seventeen they just suckled Jocote- Qʼinoom Chikilo.

Truly-qitzij they carried out great vows; this was the sign of their intentions before the Kabʼawil as the Noble Lords of the People who were the Pueblo; this was an indication of the spiritual essence of the Holy Lords.

They didnʼt sleep with any woman then; they kept to themselves by staying alone; just keeping themselves company by staying all alone with themselves; they fasted while remaining in the house of the Kabʼawil.

They gave sacrifice, the performed acts of worship and adoration every day; they just burnt offerings-xa kʼatonik, and they just lay themselves down upon the ground as they prostrate themselves before their Kabʼawil. This was all they did when they made the fast known as Wuklaj-Seventeen.

They just stayed there in the dark of night; they just stayed there in the light of day. Their hearts wept just as their bellies wept when prayed and petitioned for the light and life of their daughters-kal and of their son-kikʼajol; for the blessing- usaq and health-ukʼaslem. This was when they prayed and petitioned for: usaq, ukʼaslem, kal, kikʼajol.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
They made prayers of petitions for their Rule as Noble Lords of their People; they made petitionary prayers for the Sovereignty that was theirs to Govern over their Kingdom; to Rule over their Realm: Ajawarem.

This was when they raised their Face to the Heavens; this was when they lifted their Eyes to the Sky above-Chi Kaj-and the Heart of the Sky: Ukʼuʼx Kaj. This then is their petitionary prayer that they performed as they pleaded for their beloved People, precious Pueblo; the Sons, the Daughters; the Vassals, the Subjects to satisfy all their hunger and need made known through their plea; their petition; their appeal presented here before the Heart of the Sky; Heart of the Earth.

Aqʼaroq! At Oobʼ uQʼij, at Juraqan, at Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ulew

“!Aqʼaroq! At Oobʼ uQʼij, at Juraqan, at Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ulew!

At yaʼol rech qʼanal, raxal, at pu yaʼol miʼal, kʼajol!” “Chatziloj, chamaqʼij uloq a raxal, a qʼanal!

Chayaʼ taj ukʼaseʼik, winaqirik wal, nukʼajol.”

“Chipoqʼ taj, chiwinaqir taj, Tzuqul awe, Kʼool awe, Sikʼi awe pa bʼe, pa jok, pa bʼe yaʼ, pa siwan, Xe cheʼ, xe kʼaʼm;

Chayaʼ kimiʼal, kikʼajol!

Ma ta ja bʼiʼ il, tzʼap, yan, kʼexo.

Ma ta chok kʼaxtokʼonel chikij, chikiwach!” “Me pajik, me sokatajik, me joxowik, me qʼatowik.

Me qajik rekem bʼe, rajsik bʼe;

ma ta ja bʼik pakʼ toxkʼom chikij, chikiwach.”

“Keʼayaʼ taj pa raxa bʼe, pa raxa jok!

Ma ta ja bʼi kil kitzʼap akʼwil, awitzmal!” “Utz taj kikʼojeʼik tzuqul awe, kʼool awe chachi, chawach.”

“At Ukʼuʼx Kaj, at Ukʼuʼx Ulew, At Pisom Qʼaqʼal, a puch Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz;

Pam Kaj, upam Ulew, Kaj Tzʼuq, Kaj Xukut.” “Xa ta Saq, Xa ta Amaqʼ upam chachiʼ, chawach, at Kabʼawil!”

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Kaj Tzʼuq, Kaj Xukut; Four-fold Cornering, Four-fold Siding You of the Four Corners; Kaj Tzʼuq You of the Four Sides; Kaj Xukut May there be Peace, Xa ta Saq;

May their be Divinity, Xa ta Saq; May there be Perfection, Xa ta Saq; May there be Clarity, Xa ta Saq; May there be Tranquility in Community, Xa ta Amaqʼ May there by Peace, Xa ta Saq;

May their be Harmony, Xa ta Amaqʼ You Resplendent Divinity of the Sacred People of the Harmonious Pueblo, May Radiant Peace shine in beside and before your Eternal Name: Kabʼawil Xa ta Saq; Xa ta Amaqʼ upam chachi, chawach; at Kabʼawil

Aqʼaroq! At oobʼ uqʼij, at Juraqan, at Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ulew!

At ya-ol rech qʼanal, raxal, at pu yaʼol miʼal, kʼajol!” Chatziloj, chamaqʼij uloq a raxal, a qʼanal!

Chayaʼ taj ukʼaseʼik, winaqirik wal, nukʼajol.

Chipoqʼtaj, chiwinaqirtaj, tzuqul awe, kʼool awe, sikʼij awe pa bʼe, pa jok, pa bʼe yaʼ, pa siwan, xe cheʼ, xe kʼaʼm;

chayaʼ kimiʼal, kikʼajol!

Ma ta ja bʼiʼil, tzʼap, yan, kʼexo.

Ma ta chok kʼaxtokʼonel chikij, chikiwach!”

Me pajik, me sokatajik, me joxowik, me qʼatowik.

Me qajik rekem bʼe, rajsik bʼe; ma ta ja bʼik pakʼ toxkʼom chikij, chikiwach. Keʼayaʼ taj pa raxa bʼe, pa raxa jok!

Ma ta ja bʼi Kil, kitzʼap, akʼwil, awitzmal! Utz taj kikʼojeʼik tzuqul awe, kʼool awe chachi, chawach.

At Ukʼuʼx Kaj, at Ukʼuʼx Ulew, at Pisom Qʼaqʼal, a puch Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz; pam kaj, upam ulew, kaj tzʼuq, kaj xukut. Xa ta saq, xa ta amaqʼ upam chachiʼ chawach, at Kabʼawil.

This was when the Lords fasted after they invoked their Kabʼawil in order to pray out their petition; this was when they begged and pleaded their needs when they sowed and seeded all the many thing they needed as they raised their face to the Sky and their eyes to the Heavens.

The Noble Lords and Rulers fasted for nine times twenty days-Bʼelej Winaq- 180-Days; this was when they fasted for thirteen times twenty days-oxlajuj winaq- 360-Days, and when they fasted for seventeen times twenty days-wuklajuj winaq- 340 Days too! Great was there fasting, so great that they cried out with all their heart for the divine providence that brought forth the success and prosperity of their daughters and sons.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This was when they wept for all of their women and for all of the children when they felt the weight of their responsibility when they carried out their ancestral cargos of their sacred burden of power and authority. This was when they wept for their rule and sovereignty that was their divine office that was theirs to carry-out and perform on behalf of the People; on behalf of the Pueblo; that which was the destiny of each of their Noble Lords; Noble Rulers: Ajawabʼ.

This was in the Sacred Light of the Sacred Life-Loqʼbʼaʼl Saq Kʼaslem recognized by the Noble Lords and Rulers that had come down to them from the very beginning at the sowing; the rooting of the Forming; the Shaping.

This was the precious life; precious light of the Noble Lordsʼ that was shown appreciation from the beginning; from the origin of their Sacred Rule; Divine Sovereignty: Loqʼbʼal AjAwarem. This was the Lordship that was the Rulership of the Kingdom: AjPop, Aj Pop Kʼamja, Qʼalel, AjTzikʼ Winaq.

body: They entered there as Co-Regents as Co-Rulers who were companions; they came in two-by-two as twin rulers-kakabʼ. So it was that they came in there as coupled companions; two-by-two-kakabʼ as pairs when they took turns governing the Pueblos of the Kʼicheʼ so that they as came to their Noble Rule two-in-two when they substituted one another as Rulers of the Pueblos. This is how it was when they began to rule as Co-Regents who were Co-Rulers who were Twin-like Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ. This was when they sacrificed themselves to the goverance of the Pueblos and all the Kʼicheʼ People. These rulers gave of themselves completely for the support and maintaince of the Kʼicheʼ People of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblos. There was only one origen from which their rule came forth; it was just from one begining that originated thier ancestral truth that was their ancestral tradition of those who provided the sustenance to maintain the Kʼicheʼ Lords; just one root of origin was the one way of providing sustenance and support; just one root of origin was the one word of humility and obedience of those who were the Providers and Sustainers of the Peopleʼ when they gave sacred sustenance and ritual sacrifice to maintain the Noble Rulers and their Kabʼawil. There was just one root to the one word; of the one way of those who were the Providers and Sustainers of the support and maintance of the Kabʼawil for it was they who feed and sustained their People, their Pueblos; those who had to be fed were fed by those who were their Kabʼawil.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This One Root of the One Word, One Way; the One Root of the One Truth, One Tradition came from the Many Trees People; Many Trees Pueblo known as the KʼicheʼWinaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ who were sown and rooted in the Place known as Kʼicheʼ it was only from here did their origin branch out to the other lineages. And so it was that from under the power and authority of the sacred word was it done since it came from the Lord Kʼiche-Ajaw Kʼicheʼ; and, likewise was it done by the Tamubʼ and Ilokabʼ together with the Rabinal, Qʼaqʼchikel, AjTzʼikin Ja, Aj Tujala Ja, Uchʼabʼa Ja. Thus began the tradition of providing sacred sustenance as well as the support for the Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ by providing and sustaining them with the care and concern that comes with their being provided with their sacred sustenance while being supported with the necessary support and maintance.

This is how it began there when it then became the tradition and way of everywhere else in the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom: the Noble Lords were both provided for and sustained by the Kʼicheʼ People of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo. For it was said this came from the very origins of their Sovereign Rule; of their Noble Reign.

Each group arrived there to serve their month in Kʼicheʼ; that was when it was done by all of them; that is how the Kʼicheʼ came to rule and govern those who they came to rule; for those who they ruled were obliged to provide for them as their Noble Lords who in turn provided them with Noble guidance and Noble protection for the People of the Pueblos they governed as Sovereign Rulers.

Those Kʼicheʼ Lords happily received those who were appointed to be their providers, sustainers-tzuqul, kʼool-nourishers, nurturers of their Kabʼawil for they had done so much for them. Tzuqul, Kʼool were those who gave blood sacrifice to nourish, nurture the Kabʼawil; they were those who sacrificed blood to be given as sacred sustenance.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Their fasting was a punishment that was a penance made by the Noble Lords so that it was not in vain that they ruled over all others. For it was they who gave sacrifice as payment for the debt of their power; the power theyʼd been given in exchange for the sacrifice given by them; the power they were given was the fire-sovereignty they received from the Kabʼawil of Tulan Tzuy-Wa and that fire- rulership they now possessed to rule with power and authority over the People- Winaq of the Pueblos-Amaqʼ.

The punishment they suffered in their fasts showed they had not won their rule through sorcery with its beguiling and bewitching of others through conjuring in the shadows; through bewitching in the darkness; they did not steal away their rule-ajawarem-sovereignty; nor their power-qʼaqʼal-strength because they came with a cost; majesty-tepewal-glory was won through suffering pain and the punishment of blood sacrifice; it was just suffering and sacrifice that the Noble Lords attained their rule-ajawarem and power-qʼaqʼal and majesty-tepewal-glory.

It wasnʼt for nothing that they went down to subjugate the citadels in the canyons and fortified villages of the Small Pueblos, Large Pueblos to collect tribute from them.

And a great tribute they collected because a great payment they were made to pay; those of the Siwan, Tinamit; those of the Chʼuti Amaqʼ, Nim Amaqʼ they came bearing their tribute so that there came turquoise-xit and silver-puwaq; and there came handfuls of jade beads-kajqʼabʼ raqan-jade beads by the handful that were measured by the handful; handfuls of gold beads tuwik raqan-gold beads by the handful that were measured by the handful; and there came precious jade jewelry-chi kuwal and along with all of this came the fine emeralds-yamanik- precious stones that became finely crafted jewelry that the Noble Lords wore as their adornment and embellishment.

There came penachos that were beautiful feather crest worn on the head; feather headdress known as crests that were formed and shaped from lovely turquoise-blue cotinga feathers-raxon and bright green resplendent quetzal plumes.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This finely crafted quetzal plumage framed the feathers of these highly prized headdresses; this was the precious feather work of the Small and Large Pueblos of the Canyon Citadels. These feather crests were created and crafted so that they stood straight up on the crown their Noble Lords heads; it was all delivered up as Tribute: Patan.

The tribute of all the tribes came before the twin rulers who ruled as couples; two-in-two-kakabʼ that was spoken of as Co-Regents; Co-Rulers: Nawal Ajawabʼ Qʼuqʼumatz, Kʼo Tuj Ja or Kʼotuja.

And so too did the Tribute-Patan come before Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj and those who ruled with them through the power and authority given to these Noble Lords through the titles they received and the names they were given with the rule that comes with those noble names and titles.

These were the Noble Rulers of the Mat, Noble Rulers of the Reception House Mat along with their Judges, War Captains, Magistrates, Speakers, Criers; and many others not named here by title.

So that those who are named are named by their titles: ri AjPop, AjPop Kʼamja, Qʼalel and AjTzikʼ Winaq. These were all noble positions of entitlement; these were the names of nobility that were given to show dignity and deference; distinction and difference between the Vassals and Lords; Subjects and Rulers.

These were those who formed and shaped the hierarchy of the People of the Pueblo through the naming of the names of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

And so it was that the Kʼicheʼ Lords did what all entitled Lords are called to do. It was not just a little that they came to do those who were the Kʼicheʼ Lords.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
It was not just a few more Tribes-Amaqʼ that they, the Noble Lords, went out and conquered; because it was not such a very long time that passed before many more groups of People and divisions of the Pueblos were brought into the service of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq. It was they who were those of the Mountain Pueblos who were brought in to serve the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ. It was they, the People of the Tinamit who were the Pueblos of the Siwan that came in to Kʼicheʼ bearing the sacred burden of the Nobleʼs tribute in their kakaxtle. Those of the Siwan; Tinamit that bore on their back the tribute they carried in their merchant carrying-frames-kok which was the tribute required; the tribute requested from them by the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ. It was the Siwan; Tinamit-Canyon Country; Outlier Towns who were ordered to have their great loads delivered as Patan-Tribute to the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords. It was they, the branches of the Pueblos, who received great suffering and it was they who were persecuted by their power and majesty; the splendor and supremacy that was the greatness and grandeur of the Kʼicheʼ Lords of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

The grandeur and greatness of the Kʼicheʼ did not come all at once; it didnʼt sprout forth all of the sudden; their power was created through the sacrifice and suffering of the Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ. Their power and glory that was their sovereign majesty came with a One Great Lord: Jun Nim Ajaw.

Their great growth and aggrandizement was created by a Nawal Ajaw known as: Nim Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz he who is known and named: Great Lord Quetzalcoatl. Thus was the beginning of the remarkable growth and development of the Kʼicheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Ajaw Qʼuqʼkumatz was the root and origin of their grandeur; of their greatness through his service to the Sacred Burden of Rulership and the responsibility that he took as the sovereign rule over the Pueblos and their People. So let us then name the names of the Kʼicheʼ Lords and Kʼicheʼ Nobles as if one were naming the names of a Sacred Bundle of Noble Lords and their Noble Entitlement with the dignity and decorum; deference and distinction that comes with the naming of the names of their ancestral names while naming the names of their noble titles.

So here is where we shall innumerate; here is where we shall name the names of the generations of the Noble Lords.

We shall innumerate the names by naming the names of all the Noble Lords, names that we shall name here by naming each of their names in order, until all of their names named. This is how we shall Name the Names of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Lords; Generation by Generation; Lineage by Lineage until all the Names are Named.

This then, is the descent of order, of the orderly descent of Noble Rule, of the Noble Lords:

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ, Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ, Majukʼutaj, Ikʼi Bʼalam These are the First Grandfathers-Nabʼe Qamam and the First Fathers-Nabʼe Qajaw, when they stood before the Dawn at the Coming Out Place of the Sun; there at the emergences of the Sun; the Moon, and the Star.

This was when the Our First Grandfathers-Nabʼe Qamam and Our First Fathers-Nabʼe Qaqajaw watched and waited for the appearance that was the emergence of their Sun; their Moon, and their Star: Ikʼoqʼij.

This was when the Sun, the Moon, and the Star showed their face to make their appearance at the Place of Emergence there Beside the Sea in the East.

This then is the descent that is the order of the Lordship, Rulership that we shall begin here, right at the root, as the lords entered to rule as Companions- Kʼulukʼuj-Complementary Collaborative Lords as Twin Lords; Coupled Lords; Paired Lords of the People of Maize: Kʼulukʼuj Ajaw.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were the Divine Ancestors who were the First Grandfathers that were the rulers of Great Walled Cities-Tinamit-Finely Finished Fortified Towns. These Co-Rulers who were Co-Regents succeeded one another as Noble Lords in perfect succession; one after the next the Kʼicheʼ lineages ruled as Sovereign Lords with noble power and divine authority; each one of the Noble Lords entering in perfect order as Sovereign Rulers who manifest as the Noble Lords of the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo..

This is how they appeared in succession as Noble Lords of Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ: Ajaw Kʼicheʼ.

Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ was the Root of the First Generation-Uxe Nabʼal of the Kaweqibʼ. Kʼo Kaʼibʼ also Kʼokawibʼ was the Second Generation-Uka Le after Bʼalam Kiʼtzeʼ.

Bʼalam Kʼonacheʼ became the Aj Popol of the Third Generation-Rox Le.

Kʼotuja, Istayul are of the Fourth Generation; Ukaj Le.

Qʼuqʼkumatz, Kʼo Tuj Ja is the Root of the Fifth Generation-Uxeʼ Nawal Ajaw Roʼ Le.

Tepepul, Iztayol was the Sixth Ranked-Waq Tas.

Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj was the Seventh Change-Waq Jal of Lordship of this Nawal Ajaw.

Tepepul, Ixtayubʼ are the Eighth Generation-Uwajxaq Le in the lineage of Rulers. Tekum, Tepepul were the Ninth Generation-Ubʼelej Le of Noble Lords. Wajxaqi Kʼaʼm, Kʼiqʼabʼ were the Tenth Generation-Ulajuj Le of Noble Lords.

Wuqubʼ Noj, Kawatepech were the Eleventh ranked Lord-Ujulajuj tas Ajawabʼ.

Oxib Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi were the Twelfth Generation of Lords-Ukabʼlajuj le AjAwabʼ.

Maize Lord Lineage: Jun Nal Ye; Jun Ixim; Jun Ajaw, Yax Bʼalam First Fathers: Nabʼe Qajaw; Xpeyakok, Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu;

Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej “Xchiwachin uwach jujun chu jujunal Ajawabʼ Kʼiche. This my dear reader is one last serious play-serio ludare on the Maize Lord Jun Nal Yeh which comes through the writing as a secret sort of sacred language of Tzuy-Wa that seems to say here is the appearance of the face of the First Fathersʼ Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu are being invoked in order to be made ʼpresentʼ just as we are invoking the names of the First Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ by saying we will start at the very root by naming each of their names in pairs in order of their appearance.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
And the First Lords of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq are named in pairs as: Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu sure enough the ingenious scribes write this little funny and strange little phrase that says: xchiwachin uwach jujun chu jujunal Ajawabʼ Kʼiche which translated as “their faces shall appear one by one, jujun, each one of ʼallʼ the Lords of the Kʼiche”ʼ that sounds like the Ancient Ancestral Lords Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu will appear as the One Lord Jun Ajaw the Classic Maize Deity know in the Classic Period as Jun Nal Yeh: Jujunal sounding very similar. It probably is just the way the sentence naturally appears but jujunal is also a choice the Maya Scribes make out of any number of other possibilities: serious play-serio ludare. And so you there you have it, magic nawal language of Tzuy Wa that says the Face of the Earth was ʼcleared off to seed each of the seeds of each of the teeth of the Maize Deity, known as the Maize Lord Jun Nal Yeh who has teeth like the Ground White Maize Teeth of Ground White Bone of Wuqubʼ Kaqix who was a the First False Maize Father yet is played with as a Maize Deity through his false maize teeth. Amazing people, the Maya and how they are able to pull together every last hair to bring forth the sprouting and dawning of the Maize People.

Xpiyakok merits mentioning as well because it is up through his tortoise shell back as a an Earth Deity that the Maize sprout will come shooting forth as Jun Nal Yeh comes back to life after being left for dead somewhere in Xibʼalbʼa. For it is from Xpiyakok that the rooting of this naming should begin with the Father of the Fathers of Junajpu, Xbʼalamkiej but we will leave that for you to ʼfigure outʼ so time when you donʼt have to name the names of the Kʼicheʼ Ajaw. “Xchiwachin uwach jujun chu jujunal Ajawabʼ Kʼiche”

And it was they, Oxib Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi-Three Deer, Nine Dog who ruled when the Warlord and War Captains of the Castilian Conquistadores known as el Adelantado Don Pedro de Alvarado yet known as the Sun in Nahuatl: Tonatiuh- Donadiu.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This is the Castilian Conquistador who burns to death the Two Last Lords of the Kʼicheʼ. Some say they were ʼhung-ximʼ or were they just ʼboundʼ by the Castilian People. What is importance is the Traditional Maya way of death as you know so very well would have been burning them in a great stone oven to have their ashes scattered like jade along the waterʼs edge of the Motagua River that snakes its way down through the Kʼicheʼ until it reaches the Caribbean Sea. I cannot help but think the Kʼicheʼ Maya saw a New Sunrise over their Kingdom with the fall of their Sun and the Rise of Castilian Sun-Donadiu as mention before.

Tekum, Tepepul paid tribute before Castilians. They had already been engendered at the thirteenth generation of lords.

Don Juan de Rojas, Don Juan Cortes were the Fourteenth Generation: Ukaj lajuj Ajawabʼ. They were engendered heirs of Tekum Mam and Tepepul. Oxib Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi; Three Deer, Nine Dog were the Ukabʼlajuj le AjAwabʼ

Oxib Kiej, Bʼelejebʼ Tzʼi were the Twelfth Generation of Noble Lords and they were killed-ixkamik on 4-Kʼat Marzo 9, 1524.

The perfect day to be immolated in the stone oven of sacrifice on the sacrificial fire burning their on the Archetypal Day of the Sacred Fire Kajibʼ Kʼat which Four Harvest Net but also Four Sacrificial Fire and the Four of the Four Corners, Four Sides; Four Cardinal Directions to assure the rebirth of the Kʼiche Rulers; Kʼicheʼ Lords; Ajaw Kʼicheʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq; Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

And this is the descent of the descendants, and these are the succession of the successors of the generations as well as the rank and position of Rule and Authority before the Kawiqibʼ Kʼicheʼ. The Kingdom-Ajawarem with its Rulership of the Lords is here names as those who are the Noble Lords of the Council House Mat and the Reception House Mat of the Kaweqibʼ Kʼicheʼ: ri Ajaw AjPop, AjPop Qʼamja chuwach Kawiqibʼ Kʼicheʼ; before the Kaweqib Kʼicheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Here we shall tell further of the Great Houses and their town lineages. Here they are the naming of the Great Houses-Nim Ja; these are the Great Houses of the each of the Noble Lords are the AjPop, AjPop Qʼamja. These are the names of the Nine Towns with the Nine Great Houses of the Pueblo-Chinamit of the Kawiqibʼ These are the names of the rulers of each of the Great House-Chi Nim Ja.

Ajaw AjPop: Noble Lord Chancellor; Noble Lord Councilor; He has One Great House-Jun Nima Ja that is a Holy House, Sacred House-Kʼu Ja;

Kʼu Ja-Sacred House; Holy House is the name of his Great House-Nima Ja. Ajaw AjPop Kʼaʼm Ja-Noble Lord of the Reception House Mat Tzʼikina Ja ubʼiʼ Nim Ja-Bird House is the name of the Great House of AjPop Kʼaʼm Ja-Second-in-Line to Receive Rule has a Great House Nim Chʼokoj Kaweq, Jun Nim Ja-Great Scribe; Master of Ceremonies of the Kaweq has One Great House Ajaw Aj Tojil, Jun Nim Ja-Lord Storm, Lord Thunder: Tojojila, Tojojil; has One Great House Ajaw AjTojil kʼo Jun Nim Ja; Lord Storm, Lord Thunder One Great House Ajaw Aj Qʼuqʼumatz, Jun Nim Ja-Lord Quetzalcoatl; the Plume Serpent has One Great House Popol Winaq Chi Tʼuy, Jun Nim Ja-Council Book of the People of the Noble Red Mat has One Great House Lolmet Kejnay, Jun Nim Ja-One Great House Overseer of Cotton Storage Popol Winaq pa Jom Tzalatzʼ xkuxebʼa, Jun Nim Ja-Council House People of the Ballcourt; Noble Rulers of Council Mat; Chief of the Thin Walled Ballcourts has One Great House Tepew Yaki, Jun Nima Ja-Mexican Majesty Yaki-Méxica Conqueror These were the Nine Town; Citadels; Chinamit of the Kawiqibʼ

Thick with the children of women and thick with the children of men were the children that were born there in the Great Houses that were the children born to them; many were their engendered sons that were well ordered and named after the Nine Great Houses.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Here then is the ordering of the Nijaʼibʼabʼ with their Great Houses of the Nine ʼGreat Housesʼ People; ʼGreat House-Nijaʼibʼabʼ Winaqʼ. We will first tell of the succession and sequence of the rulership that begins at the very root; the very beginning; the very origin of the sowing and dawning of the Nijaʼibʼabʼ-the very root of the very beginning of the light of Kʼicheʼ Dawn; Kʼicheʼ Sun.

This is the origin of this lineage and generation-leʼ of Kʼicheʼ People who were engendered by this First Father: Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ was the First Grandfather, Father. Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ; Nabʼe Mamaxel, Qajawixel-First Grandfather, Father; Kʼo Akul, KʼoʼAkutek, Uka Leʼ; Kʼo Chajuj, Kʼo Tzibʼaja, Rox Le; Bʼelejebʼ Kej; Ukaj Leʼ chik; Kʼotuja; Roʼ Leʼ Ajaw Bʼatzʼa; chi kʼut Uwaq Leʼ chik Istayul; chi kʼut Uwuqʼ Leʼ Ajaw; Kʼotuja; chiwi Uwajxaq Tas Ajawarem Bʼelejebʼ Kej; Ubʼelej Tas Kema, chuchax chik, Ulajuj Leʼ; Ajaw Kʼotuja; Ujulajuj Leʼ Don Christowal, chuchaʼxik, xajawarik chuwach Caxtilan Winaq. Don Pedro de Robles, Ajaw Qʼalel wakamik.

Now all of the Noble Lords come from the lineage of the War Captains and Magistrates Qʼalel Ajaw whose descendants were also Judges shall be named here.

And next we shall name the names of each name of the names of the rulers of the Great House; these are their names named here: Ajaw Qʼalel, Unabʼe Ajaw chuwach Nijaʼibʼabʼ, Jun Nim Ja.

Ajaw AjTzik Winaq, Jun Nim Ja Ajaw Qʼalel Qʼamja, Jun Nim Ja Nima Qʼamja, Jun Nim Ja Uchuch Qʼamja, Jun Nim Ja Nima Qʼamja, Jun Nim Ja Nim Chokoj Nijaʼibʼ, Jun Nima Ja Ajaw Awilix, Jun Nima Ja Yakolatam, Jun Nima Ja Are kʼut Nim Ja ri chuwach Nijaʼibʼabʼ These then are the Great House of the Great House People: Nijaʼibʼabʼ And now these are the names of the Nine Citadel of the Nijaʼibʼabʼ as it is said. Are ubʼinam wi Bʼelejebʼ chinamit chi Nijaʼibʼabʼ, chuchaʼxik. And many more were the lineages of the Lords, many were the towns of each of the Lords; we named the names of those that are named here, there are more names to name.

This is the naming of the Lord Kʼicheʼ Noble Lords, this is the naming of the names of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ of the Lord Kʼicheʼ lineage of Majukʼutaj and Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Waʼ Mam, Qajaw; Here is the Grandfather, the Father: Majukʼutaj, Nabʼe Winaq-the First Man Kʼo Ajaw, ubʼiʼ Uka Leʼ Ajaw; Noble Lord is the name of the Second Generation Lord Qʼaqʼlakan; Kʼo Kosom; Kʼo Najkun;

Wuqubʼ Aj, Kʼo Kamel, Kʼo Yobʼakojʼ;

Winaq Bʼam; Creators of Beauty, Beautifiers Are kʼut AjAwabʼ ri chuwach Ajaw Kʼicheʼ; are uleʼel, utasel puch.

These are the names of the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ and their generations of Noble Lords and their rank. These are the name of the Lords who stood before the Ajaw Kʼicheʼ. These are their generations and their ranks. And these are the names of the Noble Lords here in the Great Houses. There were only Four Great Houses. The Noblemen of the Lords-AjTzik Winaq Ajaw ubʼi Nabʼe Ajaw-is the name of the First Lord, he had One Great House: Jun Nima Jaa. Lolmet Ajaw ukabʼ Ajaw, Jun Nima Jaa-The Overseer of the Cotton Plantations of the Lords who was the Second Noble Lord, he had One Great House.

Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw, Jun Nima Jaa-Great Lord Master of Ceremonies was the Third Noble Lord and he had One Great House.

Jaqawitz was the Fourth Lord with a Great House-Jaqawitz kʼut ukaj Ajaw, Jun Nima Ja, There were Four Great House before the Lord Kʼicheʼ Lineage-Chi Kajibʼ kʼut Nim Ja chuwach Ajaw Kʼicheʼ. These are the Three Great Masters of Ritual Drama; Ritual Recitation; Ritual Performance who were honored as Fathers of all the Kʼicheʼ Lords:

Are kʼu ri e Oxibʼ chi Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw! They gathered together as just one the Three Great Masters of Ceremonies- Nim Chʼokojibʼ; these were those known as the Mother-Fathers of the Word, the Scribes; the Orators, the Storytellers, Writers, Painters, Illustrators-xa jun chikikuch wi kibʼ e Oxibʼ chik Chʼokojibʼ; these three Masters of Ceremony; Nim Chʼokojibʼ were the three Noble Lords who were the Masters of the Ancient Word and Masters of the Performance of the Ancient Word: Ojer Tzij.

They were hereditary. They were Mothers of the Word, Fathers of the Word- e Uchuch Tzij, eʼ Uqajaw Tzij. Great was their essence; great was the nature of their knowing.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
These were the three Chʼokojibʼ- Oxibʼ Chʼokojibʼ and they were those who wrote the Popol Wuj these are their names, the names of the rank and position: Great Scribal Lord of the Kaweq People-Nim Chʼokoj chuwach Kaweqibʼ Great Scribal Lord of the Nijaʼibʼ the Great House People was the Second in line of the Noble Lords of the Nim Chʼokoj then-Nim Chʼokoj chuwach Nijaʼibʼ, Kabʼ Nim Chʼokoj kʼu ri.

Great Scribal Lord of the Lord Kʼicheʼ Lineage was the Third Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw Lineage of Scribal Masters of Ceremony of Kʼicheʼ Mother-Fathers of the Ancient Word-Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw chuwach Ajaw Kʼicheʼ, Rox Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw; Uchuch-qajaw Ojer Tzij.

Chi Oxibʼ kʼut ri Chʼokojibʼ-Three Masters of the Ritual Performances of the Spoken Word; Masters of Ritual Recitation of the Ancient Word, Ancestral Story; Ojer Tzij also known as the Mother-Fathers of the Word, each in their own lineage.

Truly, this is just the essence of the Kʼicheʼ. There no longer is a place to see it; no longer is there an instrument to enliven ones imagination of the Ancient Word known as Ilobʼal re-for no longer is there a place to see the Pictorial History-Ilobʼal re that tells this ancestral story that once seen to be contemplated on a Painted Manta-Ilbʼal re-Painted Lienzo upon which to see the words and ways of the Divine Ancestors and Kabʼawil is no more; for there no longer is a ʼplaceʼ to see what is written here as the spoken word. There was the First One; there was the Ancestral Book of the Noble Lords; but it is now lost and gone.

This then is the end of our telling about all that came to pass there in Kʼicheʼ; Santa Cruz is its name.

El Fin de la Traducción del Ojer Tzij: Ancient Word, Ancestral Story; Popol Wuj March 24, 2026 PaRaqan Yaʼ Chichimuchʼ Sta. “I will tell you something about stories…They arenʼt just entertainment. Donʼt be fooled. They are all we have, you see, all we have to fight off illness and death.” Leslie Marmon Silko “A word has power in and of itself. It comes from nothing into sound and meaning; it gives origin to all things.” N. Scott Momaday “Myths are not the Truth but a Language that expresses the Truth.”

“Myths always are; but, they never were.” Sallustius 4th C. Neo-Platonist

“There can be no stronger proof of the impoverishment of our contemporary culture than the popular-though profoundly mistaken-definition of myth as falsehood.” Rollo May

“The soul of our civilization depends upon the civilization of our soul. The imagination of our culture calls for a culture of the imagination.”

James Hillman “It it is true that there is always more than one way of construing a text, it is not true that all interpretations are equal.” Paul Ricouer

body: “If a man loses anything and goes back and looks carefully for it, he will find it.” Sitting Bull Lakota Tatanka Iyotake “It is usually during the trauma of initiation that a neophyte hears the most sacred myths of his tribe for the first time. This is an important point. A myth is not a story that can be recited in a profane or trivial setting. Because it imparts sacred knowledge, it is always recounted in a ritualized setting that sets it apart from ordinary profane experience, and can only be understood in the solemn context of spiritual and psychological transformation. Mythology is the discourse we need in extremity. We have to be prepared to allow a myth to change us forever. Together with the rituals that break down the barrier between the listener and the story, and which help him to make it his own, a mythical narrative is designed to push us beyond the safe certainties of the familiar world into the unknown. Reading a myth without the transforming ritual that goes with it is as incomplete an experience as simply reading the lyrics of an opera without the music. Unless it is encountered as part of a process of regeneration, of death and of rebirth, mythology makes no sense.” A Short History of Myth by Karen Armstrong “It is easy to understand why the memory of that marvelous time haunted religious man, why he periodically sought to return to it. In illo tempore the gods had displayed their greatest powers. The cosmogony is the supreme divine manifestation, the paradigmatic act of strength, superabundance, and creativity. Religious man thirsts for the real…through the annual repetition of the cosmogony, time is regenerated…the ritual recitation of the cosmogonic myth plays an important role in healing, when what is sought is the regeneration of the human being….thus the cosmogonic myth serves as the archetypal model for all creations, on whatever plane-biological, psychological, spiritual. But since ritual recitation of the cosmogonic myth implies reactualization of that primordial event, it follows that he for whom it is recited is magically projected in illo tempore, into the “beginning of the World” he becomes contemporary with the cosmogony.

body:
What is involved is, in short, a return to the original time, in order to begin life again…”

The Sacred and the Profane Mircea Eliade

“The psyche is the inward experience of the human body, which is essentially the same in all human beings, with the same organs, the same instincts, the same impulses, the same conflicts, the same fears. Out of this common ground have come what Jung has called the archetypes, which are the common ideas of myths.” Joseph Campbell

“In imitating the exemplary acts of a God or of a Mythic Hero, or simply by recounting their adventures, the man of an archaic society detaches himself from profane time and magically re-enters the Great Time, the Sacred Time.”

Mircea Eliade

“It helps to regard soul as an active intelligence, forming and plotting each personʼs fate. Translators use ʼplotʼ to render the ancient Greek word ʼmythosʼ in English. The plots that entangle our souls and draw forth our characters are the great myths. That is why we need a sense of myth and knowledge of different myths to gain insight into our epic struggles, our misalliances, and our tragedies. Myths show the imaginative structures inside our messes, and our human characters can locate themselves against the background of the characters of myth.” James Hillman

“A myth, therefore, is true because it is effective, not because it gives us factual information. If, however, it does not give us new insight into the deeper meaning of life, it has failed. If it works, that is, if it forces us to change our minds and hearts, gives us new hope, and compels us to live more fully, it is a valid myth.

Mythology will only transform us if we follow its directives. A myth is essentially a guide; it tells us what we must do in order to live more richly. If we do not apply it to our own situation and make the myth a reality in our own lives, it will remain as incomprehensible and remote as the rules of a board game, which often seem confusing and boring until we start to play.”

A Short History of Myth by Karen Armstrong

Popol Wuj is written at a unique moment in time and historical space which gives us a unique possibility to ʼcross-overʼ the liminal space and time that exists between our Present Moment in Time in this New Century and the Time before the Conquest and Colonization of las Américas by the European Catholics. Reader, allow yourself to be transported over the Colonization of the Maya to then ʼenter the wordʼ of their Santo Mundo before it was changed and transformed by the Dominican Order and the Castilian Colonists. Popol Wuj is the Magical Mythical Bridge that enables us to cross-over this liminal space to enter ʼin illo temporeʼ when the Sacred Acts of Sacred Times formed and shaped the Maya World and all that came to pass within it as told through the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

IxMuqane who is the Ancient Ancestress of the Maize People who transforms maize with her white lime and grayish white ash on her Threes Stone Hearth where her Divine Partner burns like Old Man Sun between the Sacred Triangle of Ancient Ancestral Stones.

IxMuqane ground her maize that she cooked in lime; boiled in ashes to create the sacred substance that would become the sacred sustenance of the Maize People. The Sacred Substance; Sacred Sustenance that was sculpted and shaped; molded and modeled by IxMuqane to form and shape the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ People; Kʼicheʼ Pueblo. Popol Wuj moves to this Mythic Event known as the forming and shaping of the People of Maize; Pueblo of Maize.

This is why I have introduced you to this major mythic archetype of the Popol Wuj so you begin your Sacred Journey knowing what all Initiate knew: IxMuqane is the Great Mother Earth whose Twin Sons and Twin Grandsons will defeat the Lords of Death to prepare the Face of the Earth for ʼforming and shapingʼ of the First Four Fathers. The Maize Twins; the Hero Twin; Lords of Light and Shadow; Lords of Day and Night; Lords of the Face of the Earth victorious in their defeat of the Lords of Death in the Underworld. This is Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej are as Trickster Twins who pull-off the ʼgreat reversalʼ by transforming impossible odds into their lucky opportunity to turn the problem around to then send it all in the opposite direction. What canʼt we learn from these Two Nawal Lords who always know more than they say?

This is the Sacred Story known as the Sowing of the People of Maize and the Dawning of the Kʼicheʼ Sun of the First Four Mother-Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. This is their Sacred Story; this is their Magical Myth introduced to you right here with these mythic words and mythic phrases; mythic metaphors and mythic imagination; mythic ideas and mythic images; mythic characters and mythic figures; mythic realm and mythic world.

This is the Noble Realm of the Noble Kʼicheʼ Kingdom whose First Four Mothers-Fathers; First Four Matriarch-Patriarchs are brought forth into being the First Lineages into being with their First Generation of Descendents who are brought into the Sky-Earth by who First Mother-Fathers-Nabʼe Chuch-Qajaw who bear and beget; conceive and engender of the Kʼicheʼ People of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo; People Maize; Pueblo Maize known as the Ixim Winaq. Popol Wuj is the Mythic Masterpiece of the Maize People that tells the Mythic-History of the Maya Culture as the Familial Story of the Maize People and the Sacred History the Mesoamerican Civilization as the Sacred History of the Kʼicheʼ Maya who make their Sacred Journey to Lord Quetzalcoatl in Tulan Tzuy-Wa at the Coming Out Place of the Sun; at the Place of the Dawn were the First Four Fathers go in their Sacred Journey to find ʼOneʼ who will ʼGuide and Protectʼ them as their Divinity- Kabʼawil.

This is the Sacred Story of Initiation known as the Dawning that is told throughout Mesoamerica at this time of the Toltec Sun. So Popol Wuj is a Family Story of the Maize People that tells the Myth of the Maize People that is known as the Sowing-Ewaxibʼal. The Sowing-Ewaxibʼal is followed immediately by the Dawning-Saqiribʼal which is the story of the Forming and Shaping of the First Four Mother-Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ to then begin the mythic watching and waiting of the Kʼicheʼ Dawn at the Dawning-Saqiribʼal of the Kʼicheʼ Sun of the Age of the Kʼicheʼ Maya told here at the Sowing-Ewaxibʼal and Dawning-Saqiribʼal of the Kʼicheʼ World; Kʼicheʼ Kingdom revealed in the revelation of the Ancient Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj.

body: ʼMundus Imaginalis-Imaginal Worldʼ Nabʼe Ixoqibʼ; Nabʼe Kʼulel; Nabʼe Ixoqil Ancestral Remembrance; Ancestral Memory Dreaming Dream; Dream Myth; Mythic Dreaming First Four Mothers; First Four Companions; First Four Fathers Let us enter the word of the Ancestral Remembrance to recall and remember the Ancestral Memory of the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ that tells of the First Four Mothers who are First Four Companions of are the First Four Wives of the First Four Fathers. This that is a sacred story of the sleep of the Divinity- Kabʼawil; the Deity; the God-Kabʼawil known as Heart of the Sky-Heart of the Earth; Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Ukʼux Ulew who dream the First Four Matriarchs of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo into life. These are the First Four Women; First Four Companions-Primeras Cuatro Compañeras-Nabʼe Kejebʼ Kikʼulel who are the Women-Ixoqibʼ; the Wives-Ixoqil; the Companions of the First Four Fathers who are brought to life through dreams found in sleep. I write this in order that you consider what this means in the sense of the vast importance of Dream and that Dreams are seen and known as real Ancestral Beings in which the ʼImaginal Worldʼ communicate and connects to One through the Dreams that are dreamt in the Dreaming of Knowledge; the Dreaming of Insight; Ways of Understanding and Answers to Questions to find oneʼs way on the Path of Life and the Ordeals, Tests, and Trials found on the Way. Imagine then the importance Dream; imagine then the importance of Myth as the Communal Dream of a People; as the Mythic Imagination that Forms and Shapes the Ways of Being in the Imaginal World; Mythic World of the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo. In this sense the Popol Wuj must be understood as the Ancestral Myth that is the Waking Dream that is Walking Dream that carries the Initiate through the Communal Dream of the Maize People. This is the Dream World that is the Underworld found in Xibʼalbʼa where the Dead are the Ancestors who are the ʼJudgeʼ of their Descendants as is played out here in the Ancestral Account where the Hero Twins descend down into the Land of the Death; Land of the Ancestors.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
The Ancient Word of this Ancestral Account forms and shapes the Imaginal World of First Mothers; First Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ. This Imaginal World of the First Divine Ancestors is peopled and populated by these Dream Women and Maize Men who form the Maize People of the Sun of the Maize People; of the Age of the Maize which is the Kʼicheʼ Sun of the Kʼicheʼ Age.

These Suns; these Ages; these Eras need not become confused here in the reading and recitation of the Popol Wuj but they always will be confused because that is the baffling, bewildering of Myth especially the Popol Wuj. Yet each of the Five Acts of the Five Section build on one another both backwards and forwards in a Myth that is meant to be read over and over and over through life as was performed year after year after year. For the Kʼicheʼ the chronology of the Story- telling; Myth-making made no difference because the Kʼicheʼ Maya knew the Popol Wuj by heart as they suckled it from the breasts of the Mothers as the Sacred Sustenance that fed those who called out to be fed by the sacred sustenance that is the sacred narrative of Popol Wuj.

Like the Maize People formed and shaped by ground maize in the hands of the Former, Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol while Women were dreamt into being by the Heart of the Sky who was he who formed and shaped the Women and Men of the Third Age; Third Sun of the Wooden People. The Wooden People who were made up of Women and Men whose flesh; whose essence came from different substances with completely different essences. This is the essences of the Popol Wuj that distinguish who or what a beingʼs essence is by what they are formed and shaped from. Which is to say: ʼyou what you eatʼ and ʼyour teeth defineʼ how one will live on the Face of the Earth. Teeth is the name of the Descendants; teeth are the name Grandmother gives to her Grandchildren: iwiyʼ her grandchildren; her teeth; her descendants.

body:
And so it is that the Wooden Men are carved from the Trickster Tree; the Tzʼiteʼ Tree that is the Divining Tree; the Talking Tree that is an Ancestral Tree; the Old Man; Mam; the Old Ancient White-Haired One who speaks. Whereas the Wooden Women of the Age of the Wooden People; of the Sun of Wooden People were shaped from the ʼReeds and Rushes-Sibʼaqʼ of the Lakeshore. The Lakeshore is that Place of Origins; Place of Great Plenty; Place Thick with Abundance; Ancestral Place and Sacred Space of Maya Women where the Reeds and Rushes are teaming with Life from which the First Foods are all found: Snails; Minnows; Crabs; Turtles; Eggs; Cattail Roots; Ducks; Grebes; Coots and Fish. The Women of Reeds and Rushes are of the Third Age that comes before the Fourth Age of the People of Maize; Pueblo of Maize: Ixim Winaq.

Women and Men are not the same at all in the Maya Cosmos because Women and Men are not created from the same essence; same substance; same sustenance; same flesh and so it is the First Four Women of the Age of the Maize People are Formed and Shaped from Dreams. What then is the Divine Essence of the Divine Dreams: Divine Imagination; Divine Intuition; Divine Genius known as the Nawal Genius of the Nawal Imagination that forms and shape all being into becoming?

ʼRise and Fallʼ ʼDawn and Duskʼ

body:
First Four Mother-Fathers Men of Maize; Women of Dreams Maya Culture; Mesoamerican Civilization Natureʼs Way is Cultureʼs Way is the Way of Civilization The Ancestral Way of Maize; of Sun; of Moon; of Culture; of Civilization The First Four Women; First Four Men of the Kʼicheʼ are those known as: Bʼalam KiʼTzeʼ-Kaq Palama Ja; Bʼalam Aqʼabʼ-Chomi Ja; Majukutaj-Tzʼununi Ja; Ikʼi Bʼalam-Kaqix Ja. In which Kaq Palama Ja is the Red Sea Turtle House; Chomi Ja-Shrimp House; Tzʼununi Ja-Humming Bird House; Kaqix Ja-Scarlet Macaw this then is the origin of the First Four Great Houses of the First Four Lineages of Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. Know you know where we are headed which is to say from Mythic Narratives of Magical Transforming Hero Twins with their Trickster Mother and Grandmother Matriarch to then move to Epic Narratives of the First Four Lineages which tells us so very much about the Maya Culture and the Mesoamerican Civilization as understood by the Maya Culture and in terms of the Mesoamerican Civilization. The entire Popol Wuj is a wonder to read with surprises found every step of the way.

Women and Men are formed and shaped from different substance with different essence which gives them a different way of thinking and dreaming that causes Women and Men to develop in different ways. And so it is that the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj is molded and molded from mythic images and mythic idea of these two forms of imagining and thinking and dreaming and acting and speaking. The Maya Culture then is crafted and created from mythic figures and mythic structures.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Just as the Maya Soul; Ancestral Soul is formed and finished by mythic words and mythic metaphors so too is the Maya Culture awakened by the archetypes of this Dream World of the Maya Soul that is both ground in and inspired by the Imaginal World of the Maya Myth of Maize that through the Mythic Metaphor of the Maize Twins who are the Two Heads of Maize growing on One Cane of Maize that is the Body of their Mother IxKikʼ. It is through their Sacred Story that the Mythic Metaphor of the Maize Beings; Maize Lords brought into being through the Mythic Metaphor of the Maize People told by the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of the Sacred Lifecycle of Maize. That is it; the Popol Wuj tells this story to tell it again through the Rise and Fall of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom.

This ʼRise and Fallʼ of all life on Earth; ʼRise and Fallʼ Cultures and Ages; ʼRise and Fallʼ Civilizations and Sun; ʼRise and Fallʼ People and their Lives; ʼRise and Fallʼ Cities and their Histories all ʼRise and Fallʼ like the lifecycle of Maize. All Life on Earth follows the Sacred Lifecycle of Maize and its ʼRise and Fallʼ that begins with the death of the seed of the ancestor; the seed-skull-tooth sown as the descendent at the sowing, sprouting, growing, flowering, fruiting, maturing, doubling-over, bending-down, drying and dying to be harvested and carried in from the Milpa into the patio of Grandmotherʼs House. Here then seed ʼshelledʼ from the cob to be cooked and ground to be formed and shaped into tortilla and tamales and eaten; or, selected for seed to be sown again by being buried in the ground under the Earth.

The Earth of the Great Mother IxMuqane; the womb of IxKikʼ where the Hero Twins are engendered by their Father…And so goes the Popol Wuj the Sacred Story of Maize and the Maize Beings: Ixim Winaq. This is the Sacred World of Maize of Maya Culture of Maize; that is the Ancient Ancestral World of the Mesoamerican Civilization; that is Ancestral World of Kʼicheʼ; that is the Mythic World of the Maize People of the Pueblo of Maize; the Kʼicheʼ People of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
All of these Worlds come to life in the collective unconscious of the dreamers or the listener of myth in a world where the Ancestral Soul feeds on the sacred sustenance embodied in the Sacred Narrative of Popol Wuj. These images and ideas; figures and structures; words and metaphors activate the archetypes in the collective unconscious to release tremendous psychic energy to move our Ancestral Soul that we share with all humanity. We share the same collective memory; collective unconscious where we experience dreams in similar ways. But about Indigenous World before there were influences that came from Imaginal Realms to influence the way one dream and the way one experienced myth. This is a question that in no way be addressed in an Introduction but the point is made: when the Kʼicheʼ Maya lived lives with only one main myth of the Maize People with the Maize Lords and the story of the sacrificial fire of the Hero Twins becoming the Sun and Moon. What was the connection and communication between and betwixt Myth and Dream before the Imaginal World of the Kʼicheʼ was transformed by outer influences like the Word of God-Uchʼabʼal Tiox and Christianoil-Christianity? What then, what kind of imaginal magic of dream and myth; seeing and knowing; divination and imagination; story-telling and myth- making? What then? What happened then?

Five Suns; Five Ages; Five Days and Five Nights Five Act Performance; Five Sections Myth-Making Mythic History; Sacred Myth; Historical Myth; Sacred History Ancestral Mind; Ancestral Soul; Ancestral Mind; Ancestral Body Mid-Point of Year; Wayebʼ; Five Days Asleep; Five Nights Awake

Where a Pueblo comes together to share their Divine Ancestorsʼ Ancestral Myth through the Long Performance and Ritual Recitation of their Myth through Ritual Drama then that Pueblo will experience the Ancestral Mind; Ancestral Soul; Ancestral Mind; Ancestral Body as Unified Consciousness.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
This was once how the Popol Wuj was brought to life among the Kʼicheʼ Maya People and their Pueblos that gathered together at the Mid-Point of Year to participate in the transcendent experience of Popol Wuj as the expression and experience of Ritual Theatre. The Long Performance of the Ancient Word of the Ancestral Account of Popol Wuj brought forth the Ritual Renewal of Life on Earth.

For the Popol Wuj was once upon a time played out as the Ritual Theatre of Ritual Revival; Ritual Drama of Ritual Resurrection of Sacred Cycle of Life, Death, and Rebirth. This was how the Five Acts of the Five Sections of Popol Wuj were played out on the Five Nights of the Wayebʼ when time slept in order that Ancestral Myth could be brought to life like a dream. Myth like dream needs the enchantment of the still quiet dark of Night in order that the Imaginal World of the Mundus Imaginalis is given its sacred space to come into being. The Wayebʼ fell between the Old Year and New Year when the Sky-Earth was reborn by being seeded and sown at death to sprout back to life through the Ritual Renewal of Popol Wuj with its Long Performance and Long Recitation that formed and shaped the Ancestral Soul of the Kʼicheʼ People; Pueblo Kʼicheʼ.

The Old Year was sacrificed by being burnt in the Sacred Altar with is Divine Fire that was extinguished to then be drilled back to life as the women and men were came together in communal orgy to engender divine descendants who would be born nine months later when the corn crop; maize crop was brought in December. With corn in its crib and the descendants in theirs the Sacred World of the Maya lived in perfect order formed and shaped by the balance of ritual and myth; and, the harmony of sacrificial gifts and sacred petitions. This is the story told in the Popol Wuj so allow this be sufficient for your Introduction into this Ancient Ancestral Account of the Sacred Book of the Kʼicheʼ Maya of the Pueblo Kʼicheʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: Now here is what is fascinating about Myth; Myth carries us across liminal space and liminal time as we ʼPass-Overʼ the Threshold of the Years. This Sacred Act of Passing over Sacred Space through the Long Performance of the Popol Wuj became the Passion of Christ played-out and performed at Night. These Five Dangerous Days of the Wayebʼ; Days of Transformation; Days of the Changing Face of the Year-Bear were those Days when the Popol Wuj was brought to life in the Dark of Night when the Rituals of Renewal and Rites of Initiation were bound together in the Five Acts of Popol Wuj that begins in Creation and ends in Destruction. these Five Sacred Days and Five Sacred Nights which is that they ʼcarry the Mayaʼ over a liminal period of Time between the Eighteen Months of Twenty Days that make up a Solar Year Count. The Five Days that lay between are known as the Wayebʼ in the Classic Maya World in which a ʼWayʼ was a ʼNawalʼ or ʼAnimal Transformʼ so too are Twenty Days of the Sacred Count of Days known as Nawales. Four of these Nawales or Way of the Wayebʼ are Year-bearer or Mam Like the Maize in the Milpa so too is the Mythic Narrative of Popol Wuj. In the middle as only mythic mystery would have it the Hero Twins Flower and Fruit like ʼGood-looking Young Menʼ who are Maize Deities that have come to perfection as the elongated heads of the Mazorca with its beautiful long locks of silky hair and magnificent headdress adorning their head. This Hero Myth of the Hero Twins stands as the Highlight and Heart of the Popol Wuj is the Mythic Narratives of the Hero Twins. They will by imitated and emulated; replicated and duplicated by Noble Rulers and Warlords whose Epic Narrative with be told in the last two Acts of Popol Wuj.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body: Popol Wuj is a ʼperfectly orderedʼ Mythic History that is the Sacred History of the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo but it tells much, much older mythic narratives that all Maya People of all the Many Maya Pueblos shared with one another the Mythic Masterpiece of the Maize People that is told as the ʼsacred storyʼ of the Family of the Maize People with their Grandmother and Grandfather whose Sons take up a Sacred Journey were they ʼengender sonsʼ in a foreign land who become the Magical Maize Twins whose magical powers of transformation change the world forever as the great abundance of life floods the land with prosperity and growth where before the Lord of Death caused nothing but poverty and strife. These Maize Growing People of the Maize Family show the way to happiness and contentment in lives where those who must be fed are fed with the ʼsacred sustenanceʼ that is sown in and all around ʼGrandmotherʼs Houseʼ creating a perfect world. This then is when the ʼMaize Twinsʼ climb up into the Sky to become the Sun and Moon of the next age of the Maize People-Ixim Winaq-People of Maize. Tollan Tzuy-Wa; Reeds and Rushes ʼTwinning-Kenningʼ ʼSowing-Ewaxibʼal-Dawning-Saqiribʼalʼ Now it is time for the ʼDawningʼ of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom as People of Maize whoʼs ʼSowing-Ewaxibʼalʼ will be completed by the ʼDawning-Saqiribʼalʼ in a World that completes and complements itself through ʼTwinning-Kenningʼ of everything that exists. And so it is the Hero Twins-Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej become the Sun and Moon of the Age of the Maize People that will now begin ʼwaiting and watchingʼ for the Sun, Moon, and Star that will mark the ʼDawning-Saqiribʼalʼ of the New Sun of the New Age of the Maize People who are the Kʼicheʼ Maya People; Kʼicheʼ Maya Pueblo who have taken up the Sacred Journey to become initiated as members of the Great Empire of the Great Lord Quetzalcoatl of Tollan Tzuy-Wa; the Place of Origins that is the Place of the Reeds and Rushes that is the Place of Natural Wealth and Abundance.

source: Popol Wuj: Complete Translation & Interpretation, Vincent James Stanzione (MARCH 24 2026 master PDF)
body:
Tollan Tzuy-Wa is the Citadel City beside the Sea at the Coming-Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼij where the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom travel on a Sacred Journey in search of ʼone who will guide and protect themʼ in their lives. Which is to say they seek a ʼDivinity-Kabʼawilʼ to show them what to do and when to do it by speaking to the Kʼicheʼ in the Maya Kʼicheʼ Language. This is a fascinating idea because it manifests how Indigenous People once listened to Divine Voice that taught them their language in order to guide and protect them throughout life. Many Maya continue to live with this connection and communication with Divine Beings.

And so it comes to pass that these First Four Fathers are there to raise their Face towards the ʼComing-Out Place of the Sun-Relebʼal Qʼijʼ where and when they raise their Eyes to the Sky at the First Dawn of the Great Sun of Quetzalcoatl. This is where all the Many People of all the Many Pueblos experience ʼOne Dawnʼ together as ʼOne People, One Puebloʼ to known themselves as those of the First Dawn of Tollan Tzuy-Wa. This is experienced by all the People of the all the Pueblos as the transcendent moment of unity and perfection at the ʼoriginʼ of the New Dawn the Many Tribes who have come before Lord Quetzalcoatl to be given in order to ʼbear awayʼ a particular Divinity-Kabʼawil that they receive as their own who teaches them their ways of speech and their ways of living on their particular place on the land.

Their Deity known as a Kabʼawil will show them their particular arts and sciences that over time cause each Tribe to act and speak differently on their different Mountain Place-Juyubʼal and Canyon Town-Siwan Tenamit. Popol Wuj teaches us exactly how the Mesoamerican People understood their lives but it takes a certain amount of initiatory interpretation to ʼenter the wayʼ of the Maya Way of being and becoming in order to ʼenter the worldʼ of the Maya and their deep relationship with their Deity who ʼguide and protectʼ them though birth and life to then continue on in death and rebirth as is revealed here in Popol Wuj where once comes to understand the Maya lived with a deep sense of rebirth through the descendants-ketal who returned through their replacements-kʼexel in order that the original seed of the lineage never died out. This is the story told here in the Popol Wuj.

The way of its twinning of sound and complementing of sound and meaning by coupling its words while kenning its sounds and kenning of meanings. The ingenious way its mythic poetics plays on words and sounds that lead to word plays that create multiple meanings that are brought to life through evocating ideas while suggesting myriad meanings through the use of diverse ideas and sundry sounds that are brought forth through a great multitude of different and diverse mythic images and mythic metaphors. The Popol Wuj is graced by a massive vocabulary and I should know since I have translated and interpreted thirteen times in the last Seven Years from beginning to end over and again. Each time I have been left in complete awe in how different each of the Five Acts is which show how advanced the Maya Culture was in its participation in the Mesoamerican Civilization. I hope I made my point the Ancient Word of Popol Wuj is as astoundingly beautiful as it is astonishingly brilliant in the way it brings out the Creation of the Kʼicheʼ Maya World to bring about the Dawning of the Kʼiche Maya Kingdom.

body:
The Ancestral Account of the Kʼicheʼ People, Kʼicheʼ Pueblo is the much, much more ancient and ancestral Maya Myth of Maize that tells of the many Creations and Destruction of the many Suns; many Ages; many Eras that are lived through to their flowering and fruiting completion when they then die to be buried in the Earth to be reborn again as the ʼReplacement- Kʼexel-Descendantʼ of their Divine Ancestor.

The Divine Ancestor and their Beloved Descendants-Replacement who, like all Ancestral Life, is sown as seed beneath the ground to rise up again as a sprout that climbs up to grow out of the Heart of the Earth. This is how the original face of the original ancestor is called forth to flower and fruit as the perfect remembrance as the perfect replacement of their Divine Ancestor. The Divine Ancestor who is seen to be known in their place that shines bright there in the Starlight of the calm, quiet, darkness of Night whoʼs resplendent darkness is made to shine as the constellations of light in the Heart of the Night Sky.

The Ancient Myths found here in the Popol Wuj were once performed at night on the Great Plaza of the Citadel City Qʼumaraq Aaj-Broken-down Cane that is found at the Center of the Kʼicheʼ World; at the very Heart of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. The Night Sky and its revolving constellations revealed the stories that were recited while being performed by the masked and costumed actors who brought their Divine Ancestors and Divinities-Kabʼawil to life.

The Popol Wuj is best thought of as an Epic Myth performed in ʼFive Performancesʼ of five separate Ancestral Accounts that when told in succession tell the Mythic Narrative of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom. The Popol Wuj is Ancestral Script that tells of ʼall that was done by the Kʼicheʼ People in the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom by the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo known to you well be now as Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ. Popol Wuj is the Ancient Word-Ojer Tzij that reveals as it tells the Ancestral Account-Ojer Tzij.

body:
The Mesoamerican Civilization was and continues to be an ʼIndigenous Worldʼ where its People who make up their Pueblo love to ʼact and performʼ their myth and religion through ʼDance Dramasʼ that are ʼRitual Dramasʼ that teach as they entertain the public. We are told by the Kʼicheʼ Maya Scribes who wrote the Popol Wuj that it took a ʼlong performanceʼ to bring to completion the forming and shaping of the Sky-Earth; Lake-Sea. And so it was; and so it is that the revelation, recitation, and replication of the Original Word; Original Account of the Sprouting and the Dawning of the Bright Life of Divine Ancestors and Divine Twins and Twinned Deities is brought forth out of the Darkness and into the Light.

This is the story of the Popol Wuj with its many fallen creations and failed destructions in a World that we continue to live in known as the Sky-Earth. For the World we live in is a World where Traditional Maya live as the Descendants who are the Replacements-Kʼexel of their Divine Ancestors. The Popol Wuj must be understood as a living myth that is coming back to life each and every day as Mesoamerican People remember themselves as Beloved Descendants of their Divine Ancestors. Popol Wuj is alive.

Popol Wuj is a living being whoʼs Mythic Characters exist within all of those who enter its words; to enter its ways; to enter its world; to enter its traditions; to enter its truths: all of which are spoken in Maya Kʼicheʼ as katok pa tzij. We are entering the Ancient World of these Mesoamerican People known as the Kʼicheʼ Maya today; and we are entering that Ancestral World of the Kʼicheʼ Maya by entering into its Ancestral Word that tells the Ancestral Account known to all as: Ojer Tzij-the Ancient Word; Ancestral Account of the Ancient World; Ancient Ways of the People and Pueblo named Kʼicheʼ who know themselves to this very day as Ixim Winaq: Maize People. These are the Life Ways of the Maize People who are brought into being by the Forming and the Shaping of the Formers and the Shapers. This then is the Ancient Maya Myth of the Forming and Shaping of the Ixim Winaq-Maize People known and named here as Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Amaqʼ Kʼicheʼ.

body:
This then is the flowering of Ancient Myth; this then is the fruiting of Ancestral Remembrance that is remembered to be revealed as that which is recited here as the Ancient Word; as the Ancestral Story of Popol Wuj; the Book of Counsel that fruits; that flowers; as the flowering fruit of Ancestral Bounty; of Ancestral Plenty.

This is what is shown here to be known here as that which is sown here as the Ancestral Seed; the Ancestral Seed that sprouts forth in bountiful abundance as the Sacred Sustenance to feed the Ancestral Need of the Ancestral Soul.

Sacred Sustenance is the essence of this Ancient Story of the People Maize whose life and lifecycle of life, death, and rebirth is told over and over in myriad ways. These ways of being told to be heard over and over again never grow old since they change and transform as oneʼs life changes and transforms through the many Suns that rise and fall Day after Day as the Years and its Suns move round and round forming and shaping the Life Ways of a Person and their People. This then is the Sacred Story of the Life, Death, and Rebirth of a People; the Sacred Narrative of a Pueblo; the Myth that Forms a People; the Myth that Shapes a Pueblo. This Forming and Shaping is a Molding and Modeling that is a Sowing and Dawning of a People of Maize and a Pueblo of the Sun.

This is the Sacred Story told here known as the Sowing of the Seed and the Dawning of the Sun; the Maya Myth of Maize; the Mesoamerican Myth of the Sun, Moon, and Star that is revealed here as the remembrance and recollection of the Ancient Images of the Ancestral Mind and its Ancestral Memory that is the reflection of Ancestral Images of the Ancestral Soul that sleeps deep down in our Ancient Mind; Ancestral Soul to be brought to light by the Ancient Language known as Myth; Myth the Ancestral Language of the Soul.

Our Ancestral Soul is our Ancestral Inheritance just as our Ancestral Mind is formed and shaped by Ancestral Remembrance that watches and waits for the appearance of the mythic word that resound with mythic sound to form the mythic image that awakens our remembrance of the mythic world that slumbers within us just waiting and watching; watching and waiting for the mythic images and mythic sound to awaken the slumber of our sleeping Ancestral Soul. Myth awakens us from deep, deep, deep down inside of our Ancestral Mind that is formed and shaped from birth with images and ideas; forms and figures; acts and adventures; events and experiences known as archetypes.

This Archetypal Mind is really an Archetypal Soul that exists within as a Living Breathing Entity that hungers to be fed by the Living Breathing Entities that are Myths. Yes, Myths are alive they are not dead. Myths exit as Ancient, Ancestral Beings who we bring to life through our engagement with them. We bring myths to life just as myth bring us to life by ʼfiring us upʼ with mythic images.

These mythic images and mythic narratives release psychic energy that is held down within us as repressed energies of the soul. And their they remain causing us a great deal of pain until we release them by lighting them up with mythic images that come to life by our firing up with myth and its images, archetypes, figures, and events that create soulful experience within us so that feel life once again.

body:
Myths are magical, mystical, mythical formation that took thousands of years of human experience being reflected in the cauldron of story-telling and crucible of myth-making. Myths come to as fully formed beings and perfectly shaped entities that we eat alive to feed the hunger of our soul and appease our appetite for only that which satisfies which is the mythic body found in the written text of myth. Our souls devour myth once we develop a certain taste for a particular myth. Is not the Popol Wuj this kind of myth; is not this Book of Council this kind of risk; is this Council Book that comes from Beside the Sea this kind of story meant to awaken the Ancient Sea of Consciousness that live within you; that lives within me; that lives as relic of the past within those of known today who wish to be freed by reading and contemplating this Myth sown like a seed to grow like a tree.

It takes a certain amount of time and effort to truly enter the word of its way of revealing the Ancient Way of the Ancient World of the Maya but once you develop a taste for Ancient Ancestral Story of Hunters and Warriors; Tricksters and Jokers; Singers and Dancers; Storytellers and Performers of Ancient, Ancestral Tricks you will be hooked on its playful narrative that never lets up. For Popol Wuj is a myth so perfectly written that each and every word adds and augments the sense, sentiment, and significance of this Mythic Masterpiece of the Ancient Mesoamerican Word of the Ancient Ancestral World of the Maya that molded and modeled this Myth of Maize over many thousands of years of sowing of maize that led to this growing myth that has been the Sacred Sustenance of the Maya sense time immemorial. So let us take our time to introduce you to it by introducing you to the Purpose and Meaning of Myth.

Molding and Making of Myth Forming and Shaping of Human Beings Carving and Crafting of Culture Sculpting and Shaping of Society

body:
The primary purpose of myth which is to feed the Ancestral Soul; the Ancestral Soul that when properly fed with its sacred sustenance grows and grows into a well formed People of a perfectly shaped Pueblo. It takes myth to form the natural chaos we humans face on Earth. It takes myth to shape the confusion that comes at us in a world that constantly changes. It takes myth to organize our mind and feed our soul in order that we feel a sense of order that comes from the balance and harmony provided by Mythic Narrative that feeds our Ancestral Soul. Our Ancestral Soul that wants nothing more that to be awoken by a Mythic Masterpiece such as this that is remembered and recited here to feed the hunger of our Soul. Our Soul with its appetite for all that is said to be mythic essence; mythic in character; mythic in nature.

This then is the Beginning of the revelation of all that was left to us long-ago by the Noble Council of the Noble Scribes of the Noble Realm of the Noble Kingdom of the Kʼicheʼ Maya People; Kʼicheʼ Maya Pueblo. For is was they who were those known and named as the Noble Kʼicheʼ Maya Scribes who wrote their Divine Ancestorsʼ Book of Council spoken of today as the Popol Wuj: the Council Book; the Book of Counsel.

Popol Wuj; Sacred Book of the Maya that tells as it reveals ʼall that was done by the Many Tree People of the Many Tree Puebloʼ when they were called to do what asked of them from Heart of Sky-Earth; Heart of the Lake-Sea. This is Sacred Myth that reveals as it tells of that which was brought forth upon the Sky-Earth through the Forming and Shaping known as the Sowing and Dawning of the Sacred World molded and modeled as the Sacred Sky; as the Sacred Earth. This then is the Sowing of the Sacred Seed of Sustenance; the Sacred Seed of the People of Maize. This then is the Dawning of the Sacred Sun of Rule and Governance of the Ancient Ancestral People of Sustenance; the Ancient Ancestral Pueblo of Maize.
